title: WEEK ONE LESSON NOTE.
subject: English Language
rawText:
SS 1 ENGLISH LANGUAGE WEEK 1 SPEECH TOPIC: Intonation Pattern Rise and Fall Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice in speech or the variation in speech while speaking. It gives special meaning and emphasis to utterances. FUNCTIONS OF INTONATION 1. Grammatical function: This is used to differentiate between specific sentence types – declarative, interrogative, polar questions etc. when a speaker wants to give information, the falling tone is used. 2. Attitudinal function: The attitude can be that of surprise, doubt, sarcasm, interest, indifference, disbelief, uncertainty. For instance, when a speaker answers “Yes” in reply to a question, different shades of meaning can be inferred. If given in a falling tone means affirmation, meaning there is no doubt. But when it is given in a rising tone, it suggest some reservations (doubt) in the speakers mind. TYPES OF INTONATION a. The falling tone b. The rising tone c. The rise and fall tone A. THE FALLING TONE This is used to indicate a fall in the pitch of a speaker’s voice. In writing, we use the downward arrow to show a sentence uttered with the falling tone “↓” USES OF FALLING TONE a. To make statement. Examples;

i. We shall all pass English language ↓ ii. The teacher is coming ↓ b. To give commands. Examples; i. Shut the door ↓ ii. Stand up ↓ c. To make exclamations. Examples; i. What a pleasant surprise! ↓ ii. Oh my Goodness! ↓ d. WH-Questions. Examples; i. When are you coming? ↓ ii. Why are you late to school? ↓ B. RISING TONE This is used to indicate a rise in the pitch of a speaker’s voice. USES OF THE RISING TONE a. For asking questions requiring a “Yes or No” answers otherwise known as polar questions. Examples; i. Is this your book?↑ ii. Are you coming? ↑ b. For polite request. Examples; i. May I borrow your book please? ↑ ii. Could you tell me the time please? ↑ c. For greetings. Examples; Good morning sir↑ Complement of the season ↑ d. To indicate uncertainty Will John come to school tomorrow? ↑ Can she make it? ↑

e. For incomplete statements. Examples; While they were playing ……..↑ As I was saying …….↑ C. THE RISE AND FALL TONE USES a. This tone is used in making a list of items. The voice pitch begins listed while the last item receives a falling tone. Examples i. One↑, two↑, three↑, four↑ and five↓. ii. Go in with a pen↑, pencil, a ruler and an eraser↓ b. It is also used in tag questions. Examples, You can do it, can’t you↑ She is hardworking↓, isn’t she? ↑ Assignment Exercise on unit 13 Question 3 page 173 Read and indicate the appropriate intonation VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT TOPIC: WORD ASSOCIATED WITH RELIGION CHRISTIAN, ISLAMIC AND TRADITIONAL RELIGION Religion is the belief in the existence of a particular god or gods and the activities that are connected with the worship. The three major religion in Nigeria include; Christian religion, Islamic religion and Traditional religion.

CHRISTIAN RELIGION Christian religion is the religion based on the teaching of Jesus Christ, His death and resurrection. And the belief that He is the son of God. A believer of the religion is baptized in a Christian church, and is called a Christian. Christendom refers to all Christians in the word. Words associated with Christian religion include; communion, lent, baptism, evangelist, sin, repentance, church, Bible, Reverend father, Pastor, deacon, tithe, saints, monk, nun, priest etc. Examples of such words and their meaning. 1. Consecrate: Set aside for a religious practice (to make someone or something holy) 2. Doctrine: Set of rules and principles guiding the church. 3. Baptism: Dipping someones in water for cleasing and to become a full member in Christ by an ordained Priest or Pastor. 4. Church: A Christian place of worship 5. Bible: The Christian holy book that contains the word of God 6. Tithe: Ten percent of one’s income given to God 7. Repentance: To denounce sin and turn to God 8. Saints: People who died in Christ ISLAMIC RELIGION Islamic religion is the religion that is based on the total submission of the will of Allah and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad who is regarded as the first leader and teacher of Islam. His parents were Abdullah Ibn Abd-al mutalib and Aminah. He was one of the Quaraishi people born in Mecca (Saudi Arabia) Words Associated with Islam 1. Qur’an: A holy book that contain the revealed words of God 2. Hadith: Collection of the sayings of Prophet Muhammad 3. Mosque: Muslim’s place of worship

4. Ablution: The act of washing oneself for prayer. 5. Imam: The leader of Islamic congregational prayer 6. Zakat: Alnis giving 7. Salat: Five daily prayers 8. Id-el-malud: Celebration of the where ram is sacrificed. TRADITIONAL RELIGION Traditional/religion is the belief in gods and ancestral spirits Words associated with traditional religion 1. Shrine: A place of worship 2. Rituals: Various performances done to gain favour from gods 3. Sacrifice: Offering of anything to a god 4. Supernatural: Things beyond the forces of nature 5. Polyheism: Act of believing in mangy gods 6. Sacrilege: Act of violating something sacred 7. Ethics: Moral principles by which a person or a group is guided 8. Superstition: The practice of deep religion thoughts Assignment In your new concept English, answer the questions on unit 7 exercise 2 and unit 8 exercise 2. COMPREHENSION READING PASSAGE FOR WORD TOPIC 3: MEANING IN CONTEXT OR READING FOR CONTEXUAL MEANING Contexual meaning of a word is the meaning of a word in relation to other words in the sentence. As we read a given passage, we come across some difficult words whose meanings we do not know. However, the surrounding words can help one understand the meaning. Therefore, the meaning of such word ceases to depend on the single word but takes into consideration the context or the situation in which the word is used. Example 1. Our get-together comes by the month of August (month of the year)

2. I am expecting an august visitor (important visitor) Uses Contextual meanings are required in answering a comprehension questions that demand finding another word or phrase that means the same and can replace as used in the passage. STEPS TO UNDERSTANDING WORDS FROM CONTEXT 1. Read the passage very well to gain general understanding of the passage. 2. Pay more attention to sentences with difficult words. 3. Try to figure out the meaning of such words not in isolation but with other surrounding words. 4. Replace it with another word that can fit in such environment or the context. 5. Read through the new words to make sure it fits in grammatically. Assignment In unit 7 of your new concept English, answer the comprehension question “H” TOPIC 4: STRUCTURE TYPES OF SENTENCES IN STRUCTURE Simple, compound, complex, and compound complex sentences There are different types of sentences based on structure. They include; simple, compound, complex and compound complex sentences A. Simple Sentence A simple sentence contains one idea and one verb. It consists of one independent clause. Examples 1. Rose went to the market 2. She bought a lot of goods B. Compound Sentence

Compound sentence is a sentence which contains two or more independent clauses that are joined together by co-ordinating conjunctions like; and, but, either or, neither nor. The major feature of compound sentence is that it can contain two or more ideas. Examples 1. Rose went to the market and she bought a lot of goods 2. John came yesterday and saw his bag on the table. 3. He came, he saw and he conquered 4. She tried hard but failed in her attempt 5. We can either eat spaghetti or take some wine. C. Complex Sentence A complex sentence contains one main clause and one or more subordinate/independent clauses. Examples; 1. This is the boy who was caught stealing oranges Here, the second idea depends on the first to make a complete sense. “This is the boy” is the main clause while; “Who was caught stealing oranges” is the dependent clause. 2. When the rain stopped, the dancing competition continued. “When the rain stopped” is a dependent clause that derives its complete meaning from the main clause “the dancing competition continued”. D. Compound Complex Sentence

A compound complex sentence contains two main clauses and at least one or more dependent clauses. Examples 1. We ate the food which was kept on the dining table for us but we were not satisfied. The above compound complex sentence can be broken thus; i. We ate the food but we were not satisfied (compound sentence containing two independent clauses). ii. Which was kept on the dining table for us …. (dependent clause). Therefore, compound complex sentence contains two independent clauses. More examples: 1. While the children were sleeping, the dog stole into the room and ate the raw meat. 2. Your creditor came yesterday, when you were not at home, and asked after you but I was able to pay him. Assignment 1. Give 2 examples of simple and compound sentences. 2. Mention the features of complex and compound complex sentences 3. Mention the difference between the compound sentence and the complex sentence. TOPIC 5: SPEECH WRITING A speech is a written material meant to be presented orally to a target audience. Speeches are meant to inform, entertain, persuade, educate or motivate people to action. Kinds of speeches

A. For entertainment e.g Birthday party Weddings Dinner party etc. B. For information/to educate the audience e.g Paper presentation to impact knowledge Farewell speech. C. For persuasion Speech that its aim is to convince the audience on a particular issue D. For condolences FEATURES OF A SPEECH 1. The title: The title of a speech should contain the following; the purpose, name and title of the speaker, occasion, place, date and time e.g. A farewell speech presented by Martin Owo, the head boy of Government Secondary School Kubwa on the send forth ceremony of our dearly beloved principal, Mr Idris Kunle, at the assembly hall, on 20th April, 2024 at 10am 2. Introduction This must be carefully done to attract the attention of the audience by recognizing the special guest/audience present. It must start with salutation. Example The chairman of the occasion, the principal, the management staff, the PTA …….. Ladies and gentlemen. I feel highly honored to stand here today to deliver my speech on ……….

3. The Body This contains the main message. Start by giving your main points and then support each point with relevant details, comparisons and contrasts etc. explaining who, when, where, why, how. All should be presented in good English. 4. The Conclusion Here you summarize your main points. It is important to end in a memorable way by i. making a forceful and shocking statement ii. provide some further food for thought iii. leaving your audience with positive memories of your speech Guidelines 1. A speech is meant to be delivered to an audience, hence, the use of present tense is required. 2. It should be in four sections; headings, introduction, body and conclusion. 3. Slangs and humour should be avoided unless it is for informal situation 4. No name at the end of the speech. Assignment Prepare a speech to be delivered on the prize and award giving day of the final year students of the school.

The three major religion in Nigeria include; Christian religion, Islamic religion and Traditional religion.

CHRISTIAN RELIGION Christian religion is the religion based on the teaching of Jesus Christ, His death and resurrection. And the belief that He is the son of God. A believer of the religion is baptized in a Christian church, and is called a Christian. Christendom refers to all Christians in the word. Words associated with Christian religion include; communion, lent, baptism, evangelist, sin, repentance, church, Bible, Reverend father, Pastor, deacon, tithe, saints, monk, nun, priest etc. Examples of such words and their meaning. 1. Consecrate: Set aside for a religious practice (to make someone or something holy) 2. Doctrine: Set of rules and principles guiding the church. 3. Baptism: Dipping someones in water for cleasing and to become a full member in Christ by an ordained Priest or Pastor. 4. Church: A Christian place of worship 5. Bible: The Christian holy book that contains the word of God 6. Tithe: Ten percent of one’s income given to God 7. Repentance: To denounce sin and turn to God 8. Saints: People who died in Christ ISLAMIC RELIGION Islamic religion is the religion that is based on the total submission of the will of Allah and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad who is regarded as the first leader and teacher of Islam. His parents were Abdullah Ibn Abd-al mutalib and Aminah. He was one of the Quaraishi people born in Mecca (Saudi Arabia) Words Associated with Islam 1. Qur’an: A holy book that contain the revealed words of God 2. Hadith: Collection of the sayings of Prophet Muhammad 3. Mosque: Muslim’s place of worship

4. Ablution: The act of washing oneself for prayer. 5. Imam: The leader of Islamic congregational prayer 6. Zakat: Alnis giving 7. Salat: Five daily prayers 8. Shrine: A place of worship 2. Rituals: Various performances done to gain favour from gods 3. Sacrifice: Offering of anything to a god 4. Supernatural: Things beyond the forces of nature 5. COMPREHENSION READING PASSAGE FOR WORD TOPIC 3: MEANING IN CONTEXT OR READING FOR CONTEXUAL MEANING Contexual meaning of a word is the meaning of a word in relation to other words in the sentence. As we read a given passage, we come across some difficult words whose meanings we do not know. However, the surrounding words can help one understand the meaning. Therefore, the meaning of such word ceases to depend on the single word but takes into consideration the context or the situation in which the word is used. Example 1. Our get-together comes by the month of August (month of the year)

2. I am expecting an august visitor (important visitor) Uses Contextual meanings are required in answering a comprehension questions that demand finding another word or phrase that means the same and can replace as used in the passage. STEPS TO UNDERSTANDING WORDS FROM CONTEXT 1. Read the passage very well to gain general understanding of the passage. 2. Pay more attention to sentences with difficult words. 3. Try to figure out the meaning of such words not in isolation but with other surrounding words. 4. Replace it with another word that can fit in such environment or the context. 5. Read through the new words to make sure it fits in grammatically. Assignment In unit 7 of your new concept English, answer the comprehension question “H” TOPIC 4: STRUCTURE TYPES OF SENTENCES IN STRUCTURE Simple, compound, complex, and compound complex sentences There are different types of sentences based on structure. They include; simple, compound, complex and compound complex sentences A. Simple Sentence A simple sentence contains one idea and one verb. It consists of one independent clause. Examples 1. Rose went to the market 2. She bought a lot of goods B. Compound Sentence

Compound sentence is a sentence which contains two or more independent clauses that are joined together by co-ordinating conjunctions like; and, but, either or, neither nor. The major feature of compound sentence is that it can contain two or more ideas. Examples 1. Rose went to the market and she bought a lot of goods 2. John came yesterday and saw his bag on the table. 3. He came, he saw and he conquered 4. She tried hard but failed in her attempt 5. We can either eat spaghetti or take some wine. C. Complex Sentence A complex sentence contains one main clause and one or more subordinate/independent clauses. Examples; 1. This is the boy who was caught stealing oranges Here, the second idea depends on the first to make a complete sense. “This is the boy” is the main clause while; “Who was caught stealing oranges” is the dependent clause. 2. When the rain stopped, the dancing competition continued. “When the rain stopped” is a dependent clause that derives its complete meaning from the main clause “the dancing competition continued”. D. Compound Complex Sentence

A compound complex sentence contains two main clauses and at least one or more dependent clauses. Examples 1. We ate the food which was kept on the dining table for us but we were not satisfied. The above compound complex sentence can be broken thus; i. We ate the food but we were not satisfied (compound sentence containing two independent clauses). ii. Which was kept on the dining table for us …. (dependent clause). Therefore, compound complex sentence contains two independent clauses. More examples: 1. While the children were sleeping, the dog stole into the room and ate the raw meat. 2. Your creditor came yesterday, when you were not at home, and asked after you but I was able to pay him. Assignment 1. Give 2 examples of simple and compound sentences. 2. Mention the features of complex and compound complex sentences 3. Mention the difference between the compound sentence and the complex sentence. TOPIC 5: SPEECH WRITING A speech is a written material meant to be presented orally to a target audience. Speeches are meant to inform, entertain, persuade, educate or motivate people to action. Kinds of speeches

A. For entertainment e.g Birthday party Weddings Dinner party etc. B. For information/to educate the audience e.g Paper presentation to impact knowledge Farewell speech. C. For persuasion Speech that its aim is to convince the audience on a particular issue D. For condolences FEATURES OF A SPEECH 1. The title: The title of a speech should contain the following; the purpose, name and title of the speaker, occasion, place, date and time e.g. A farewell speech presented by Martin Owo, the head boy of Government Secondary School Kubwa on the send forth ceremony of our dearly beloved principal, Mr Idris Kunle, at the assembly hall, on 20th April, 2024 at 10am 2. Introduction This must be carefully done to attract the attention of the audience by recognizing the special guest/audience present. It must start with salutation. Example The chairman of the occasion, the principal, the management staff, the PTA …….. Ladies and gentlemen. I feel highly honored to stand here today to deliver my speech on ……….

3. The Body This contains the main message. Start by giving your main points and then support each point with relevant details, comparisons and contrasts etc. explaining who, when, where, why, how. All should be presented in good English. 4. The Conclusion Here you summarize your main points. It is important to end in a memorable way by i. making a forceful and shocking statement ii. provide some further food for thought iii. leaving your audience with positive memories of your speech Guidelines 1. A speech is meant to be delivered to an audience, hence, the use of present tense is required. 2. It should be in four sections; headings, introduction, body and conclusion. 3. Slangs and humour should be avoided unless it is for informal situation 4. No name at the end of the speech. Assignment Prepare a speech to be delivered on the prize and award giving day of the final year students of the school.

title: ARTICLE
subject: English Language
rawText: An article is a word we use before a noun (name of a person, place, thing, or idea). Articles help us know if we are talking about something general or specific. There are three articles in English: 1. A Used before a singular noun that begins with a consonant sound. I saw a dog. She has a book. 2. An Used before a singular noun that begins with a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u). He ate an apple. She is an engineer. 3. The Used when we are talking about something specific or something already known. The sun is bright. I read the book you gave me. Types of Articles ✅ Indefinite Articles: a, an (general) Definite Article: the (specific)

title: STRESS TIMING
subject: English Language
rawText: Stress Timing There are two classes of words content words and grammatical words, content words are stressed e.g. main verbs, nouns, adjectives and adverbs while grammatical words are unstressed in setences e.g. pronouns prepositions, conjunctions, articles and some auxilliary verbs. Stress timing can be defined as the distribution of stressed and unstressed words in a sentence to produce a regular rhythm in English Language. It is having a rhythm in which stressed syllables tend to occur at regular intervals of time regardless of the number of intervening unstressed syllables. Examples 1. The SHORT BLACK GIRL KILLED the DOG. 2. Let's HAVE FISH for a CHANGE. 3. They've Got a BOY and a GIRL 4. ONE WAS TALLER than the REST 5. WHAT DO their PARENTS THINK? Stress timing can help to communicate meaning because the way the sentence is said can affect meaning. Examples. 1. I asked you to buy me a bunch of red roses. 2. I asked YOU to buy me a bunch of red roses. 3. I asked you to buy me a bunch of RED roses. 4. I asked you to buy me a bunch of red ROSES.

title: RECORD KEEPING
subject: English Language
rawText: Record Keeping A record is an information about something that is written down or stored on paper, a computer, film e.t.c. so that it can be used in the future. We keep records for reference i.e. so that we can have access to the information whenever we need it. The following reasons are why we need to keep information. 1. We forget important information as human beings. 2. We may need to present some of the document at request in some places. 3. Our ability to keep record shows that we have a good education. 4. It shows that we are responsible, trust worthy and careful 5. We need to keep good records as advance in life to avoid problems and present the records when they are needed. 6. Keeping results, testimonials e.t.c. will help during job interviews e.t.c. Tips on Record Keeping 1. Keep records in a way you can easily find them. 2. You can use a diary or note book to keep records of your income and expenses. 3. Keep your records in a safe place and in an orderly manner. 4. We can also keep records electronically. 5. Use accurate and short expressions to keep records.

title: WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Expository Essay The word exposition means a clear and detailed explanation therefore an expository essays is an essay whose dluty is to explain. In writing an expository essay, the writer explains a process, a thing or an idea by carefully selecting the relevant things and arraging them in an orderly and coherent manner. In order to give a clear and detailed explanation in an expository essay, the writer must be competent and have a clear idea of what he or she is explaining. Examples of Topics of a Good Expository Essay 1. How to write an essay. 2. Why gardening is my hobby. 3. How to make Soya bean milk. Note: An expository essay is the type of essay we wrife when we want to inform, instruct and/ or explain a process. Features of a Good Expository Essay The features of a good expository essay include the following: 1. Examples 2. Illustrations 3. Explanations 4. Adequate description giving attention to details 5. Sufficient information.

title: NARRATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Narrative Essay A narrative essay is a type of essay that tells a story or gives an account of events. It is usually written from the writer’s point of view and aims to entertain, inform, or teach a lesson. --- Features of a Narrative Essay 1. Storytelling: It tells a story with a clear beginning, middle, and end. 2. Characters: It includes people (real or imagined) involved in the story. 3. title: DEBATES
subject: English Language
rawText:
Argumentative Essay 📘 An argumentative essay is a type of essay where you present your opinion about a topic and support it with strong reasons and evidence. In this essay, you: Choose a position (for or against) Give reasons to support your opinion Provide examples or facts Sometimes explain the opposite view and show why your view is better Structure of an Argumentative Essay 📝 1. Introduction Introduce the topic Give background information State your thesis statement (your main opinion) 2. Body Paragraphs Each paragraph should contain: A clear point (reason) Explanation Example or evidence 3. Counter-Argument (Optional but Important) Mention the opposite opinion Explain why you disagree with it 4. Conclusion Restate your opinion Summarize your main points End strongly ✏ Example of an Argumentative Essay

Topic: Should Students Use Mobile Phones in School? Mobile phones have become very important in our daily lives. However, many schools do not allow students to use them. I believe that students should be allowed to use mobile phones in school for learning purposes. Firstly, mobile phones help students to research information quickly. With internet access, students can look for meanings of words, solve mathematics problems, and learn new things. This makes learning easier and faster. Secondly, mobile phones help in communication. In case of emergency, students can contact their parents immediately. This makes both students and parents feel safe. Some people argue that mobile phones distract students during lessons. This may be true if students misuse them. However, teachers can make rules to control how phones are used in school. In conclusion, mobile phones should be allowed in schools because they help learning and improve communication. Proper rules can prevent distraction. rawText: *1. Define Debate* A debate is a formal discussion on a particular topic with opposing views, where participants present arguments to support their stance. *2. Analyze the pros and cons of boarding and day schools* Type of School Pros,Cons Boarding School Independence, Socialization, Access to resources, Structured environment Homesickness, Limited family time, Expensive Day School Family support, Cost-effective, Comfort of home Distractions, Limited extracurricular activities, Less independence *3. Debate for the motion "Boarding school is better than Day school"* Mr Chairman, Panel of honorable judges, Fellow debaters, Ladies and Gentlemen. Boarding school offers a unique environment that fosters independence, academic excellence, and personal growth. Students live on campus, immersing themselves in a community that encourages learning, exploration, and friendship. In boarding schools, students develop essential life skills like time management, self-reliance, and teamwork. They access state-of-the-art facilities, libraries, and technology, giving them an edge in their studies. While some argue day schools provide family support, boarding schools offer a supportive community that helps students develop crucial social skills. With qualified teachers and mentors, students receive guidance and support tailored to their needs. In conclusion, boarding school's structured environment, access to resources, and opportunities for growth make it a better choice than day school.

title: SYNONYMS
subject: English Language
rawText: Synonyms Synonyms are words that share similar meanings, offering alternative ways to express the same concept. For instance, "happy" and "joyful" are synonyms, as are "big" and "large." Examples: 1. Happy: Joyful, delighted, content 2. Angry: Furious, enraged, irate 3. Beautiful: Stunning, lovely, gorgeous 4. Smart: Intelligent, clever, bright 5. Sad: Sorrowful, melancholy, gloomy 6. Big: Large, huge, enormous 7. Small: Little, tiny, miniature 8. Fast: Quick, rapid, swift 9. Funny: Hilarious, amusing, comical 10. Good: Excellent, great, superb These are just a few examples, and there are many more synonyms for each word depending on the context and nuances of meaning.

title: ANTONYMS
subject: English Language
rawText: Antonyms Antonyms are words that have opposite meanings. They are words that express contrast or opposition to each other. For example: - Hot and cold - Up and down - Happy and sad - Big and small - Fast and slow Antonyms can be derived in several ways: 1. By the addition of Prefixes and Suffixes Adding prefixes or suffixes to words can create antonyms. Example, a. adding the prefix "un-" to "happy" creates the antonym "unhappy." b. Adding the suffix "ness" to "Lion" creates "lioness" 3. Totally different word: Identifying words with opposite meanings naturally yields antonyms. For example, "hot" and "cold" are natural opposites.

title: COMPLEX TENSE FORM
subject: English Language
rawText:
COMPLEX TENSE FORMS ⚫ WHAT IS THE MEANING OF TENSE Tense is the form of the verb used to indicate the time of the action, the continuance of the action or the completeness of the action.  COMPLEX TENSES Complex tenses are referring to sentences that have more than one verb (main and auxiliary verb) in them.  THE USE OF AUXILIARY TO MAKE COMPLEX TENSE FORM To recognize the complex tense form in English, the students should know the examples of main verbs and auxiliary verbs we have and the formation of tenses. The primary auxiliary verb  Verb To be : am, is, are, was, were, be, being, been.  V erb To have : has, have, had  Verb To do : does, do, did. The modal auxiliary verb are: can, could, may, might, shall, should, will, would , must, ought to, Types of COMPLEX TENSE FORMS 1. Present continuous tense This indicates that an action is still on at the time of speaking or writing. A primary auxiliary verb (to be) is used with the ing form of the main verb. Formation – Subject + to be + verb - ing. They are sleeping. 2. PRESENT PERFECT TENSE This shows that an action which started and was completed in the past still has a link with the present. In this case, the auxiliary verb has or have are used with the past participle form of the main verb. Formation – Subject + has/have + past participle . The man has left for Abuja. I have eaten the mango. 3. PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS TENSE This expresses an action that began in the past and it still continue. In this case, the auxiliary verb have/has + to be (been)+verb +ing . Formation – Subject + have + been + verb - ing. I have been teaching for nine years . 4. PAST CONTINUOUS TENSE This is used to express a n action that was going on in the past, at a particular time. It is also used to express an action that was going on in the past and interrupted by another action. In this case the auxiliary verb to be (was/were) + verb + ing + adverbial. Formation – Subject + was + verb - ing + adverbial. I was teaching , when the Principal sent for me. 5. PAST PERFECT TENSE

This is used to indicate that two or more actions took place in the past but one happened or was completed before the other(s). In this case, the auxiliary verb had + past participle of verb to be is used. Formation – Subject + had + past participle + a dverbial . The boy had died before help reached him. 6. PAST PERFECT CONTINUOUS TENSE This is used to show that an action had been completed at a ll)l)ll) particular time in the past that is under discussion or analysis now. To form this, we will use auxiliary verb had +to be (been) +verb+ing (verb present ing) Formation – Subject + had + been + verb - ing + adverbial. We had been praying since 1997 before God intervened in 2002. 7. FUTURE TENSE This is used to show or indicate an action that will be performed in the future. To form this, we use auxiliary to be +verb +ing (verb present) Formation – Subject + am + go + ing. I am going to church. 8. FUTURE PERFECT TENSE This is use d is used to say that something will have been completed or finished, by a certain time in the future. To form this, we use auxiliary verb will have + verb (past participle) Formation : Subject + will/shall + have + verb + ed . We will have graduated from college in five years. 9. FUTURE PERFECT CONTINUOUS TENSE This is used to show that an action has been completed or taking place at that particular time. To form this, we use auxiliary will/shall + have +been+verb (to be used ing i.e present) Formation – Subject + shall + have + been + verb (ing/en) + adverbial. The men will have been eat ing by now. IDENTIFICATION OF COMPLEX TENSE FORM. In order to identify the different complex tense form where ever you meet them in use (sentences) you have to study their formation properly, know the types and numbers of auxiliary verb and the main verb (whether present, past or past participle) that were used in the formation of the sentences. Examples : She/He comes to school everyday. You/We/They come to school everyday. When you take a look at these sentences, you will notice that they contain only the main verb come (s). This shows that the sentences are simple tense form. 2. I am coming – present continuous tense (to be +verb+ing) the sentence above is in a complex tense form. It comprises of two auxiliary verb and the main verb. 3. I have been coming – present perfect continuous tense (have +to be +verb +ing) 4. By Sunday, he will have been feeding their goats for three days (shall + have + been + verb to be + verb + ing) – future perfect continuous tense. USING THEM CORRECTLY IN SENTENCES. 1. They are sleeping early – present continuous tense 2. They have slept early – present perfect tense 3. She was phoning them – past continuous tense 4. She had phoned them – past perfect tense 5. They have been sleeping early – present perfect continuous tense 6. She had been trying to phone them before they arrived – present perfect continuous tense 7. She will buy a new house next year – future tense 8. She will be speaking at the meeting tonight – future continuous tense. 9. She will have ended the speech by 10pm – future perfect tense.

10. By 10pm, she will have been speaking for two hours – future perfect continuous tense. ASSIGNMENT Use the sentence below to form these complex tenses. I do my homework. 1. Present Continuous Tense — I am doing my homework. N/B – Number 1 has already been done for you. 2. Present Perfect Continuous Tense — 3. Past Perfect Tense — 4. Past Perfect Continuous Tense — 5. Future Tense — 6. Future Continuous Tense — 7. Future Perfect Tense — 8. Future Perfect Continuous Tense —

title: DEBATES
subject: English Language
rawText:
Debates A debate is a formal discussion where people speak for or against a topic. Each side gives reasons to support their views and tries to convince the audience or judges. Meaning (Simple) A debate is an argument with rules, where two teams discuss one topic. Common Debate Terms Motion: The topic to be discussed Example: Technology is more harmful than helpful. Proposition/Affirmative: Supports the motion Opposition/Negative: Opposes the motion Moderator/Chairperson: Controls the debate Audience: People listening to the debate Types of Debate Formal Debate – Used in schools and competitions Informal Debate – Casual discussion Parliamentary Debate – Used in government Panel Debate – Group discussion on a topic Structure of a School Debate Introduction of the topic Speakers from the Proposition speak Speakers from the Opposition speak Rebuttal (responding to opponents’ points) Conclusion Importance of Debate Improves speaking skills Builds confidence

Develops critical thinking Teaches listening and respect for opinions Example of a Debate Topic This house believes that examination malpractice should attract severe punishment.

title: INTONATION PATTERN
subject: English Language
rawText:
INTONATION PATTERN (RISING TONE) Intonation pattern refers to the pattern of changes that take place during speech production. It is also the variation in the pitch of the voice. FUNCTION OF INTONATION PATTERN 1. The grammatical function: This is the ability of voice pitch to indicate to a listener the grammatical classification of an utterances. 2. The attitudinal function: This convey to the listener information relating to the speaker's Intonation might reveal surprise, doubts or warmth. USES OF RISING TONE The rising tone is use for the following: 1. Simple polite request: e.g -please sit down. - A minute of your time please. 2. Simple greetings. E.g -good morning. -hello 3.Question that requires yes or no. E.g - must you go with them? -do you like apple? 4.Imcomplete statement: e.g - As soon as the rains,stops, I 'II.... - African countries need to .... 5.Listing items:eg -She bought carrot, pepper,peas,beans and cabbage. 6. Express surprise e.g - wow!

What a great idea!. ASSIGNMENT Exercise 3 questions 1-10. Page 172. New concept English textbook for SS 1.

title: NOUN AND ITS TYPES
subject: English Language
rawText: TYPES OF NOUN Nouns are words used to name ideas, people, places or things. A nounvis a naming words. TYPES OF NOUN 1. Proper noun: These are specific noun or particular names of people animals, places or things. Examples: John, Nigeria, January, Tuesday. Proper noun always begins with capital letters. 2. Collective noun: These are names given to a group of people, animals, places or things. Or class of individual.Examples: Fleet of cars, bunch of keys, crowd of people. They are used in singular form but gives the impression of plurality. 3.Common noun: These are general names given to group or class of people, animals, places or things. Examples: boy, girl, woman,man,town,goat, dog, table etc. 4. Abstract noun: These refers to a feeling or experience rather than physical objects. They are things or concept that can not be touched or seen. They exist in our imagination and by experience. Examples: love, hatred, hunger, wisdom,joy, sadness, honesty, happiness.etc. 5. Concrete noun: These are noun that we can touch and feel. Examples: cups, bags, tables, chairs books, pens etc. ASSIGNMENT Write short note on each of the following types of noun with examples.

subject: English Language
rawText: Structure: Noun phrase. A phrase is a group of words whose meaning is incomplete, although the group of words is part of the sentence.e.g The girl, an umbrella. etc Noun Phrase consists of a noun which is the headword and determiners or modifiers.e.g A house, The house,The tall house etc. The grammatical functions of Noun phrases. 1.Noun phrase as the subject of the verb An old man is at the door. Function: Noun phrase as subject of the verb "is". 2.Noun phrase as the object of the verb. An old man broke the door. Function: phrase as the object of the verb "broke" 3.Noun phrase as complement of an object. The man declared his wife a harlot Function: Noun Phrase as complement of an object "his wife " 4.Noun phrase as complement of a subject. Douglas is an actor . Function: Phrase as complement of a subject "Douglas " 5.Noun phrase as the complement of a preposition. An old man is at the door. Function: Noun Phrase as the complement of preposition "at" 6.Noun phrase in apposition to a noun Amusan,a renounced athlete,came here last week. Function: Noun phrase in apposition to a noun "Amusan

title: HOME AND FAMILY
subject: English Language
rawText: HOME AND FAMILY . Home is a structure or house where people live.it is one dwelling place. Family is a group of people that are related by blood. Example parents, children and their close relation. Words associated with home and family are: House, kitchen, room, dining table, sitting room, toilet, compound, back yard, store, bedroom, dinning room etc. Father, mother, brother, sister, daughter son, aunt, uncle, husband, wife, children, grandson, grandparents, siblings , nephew, niece, marriage , courtship, in low, cousin, step daughter or son etc. MEANING OF SOME WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH HOME AND FAMILY. 1. Next of kin: closest living relations. 2. Spouse: husband or wife. 3. Step brother: having the same father. 4. Nephew: son of one's brother or sister. 5. Cousin one's uncle or aunt child. 6. In low: your relations through marriage. 7. Parents: Those that gave birth to someone. 8. Marriage: A legal relationship between man and woman. 9. Uncle: Mother or father 's brother. 10. Aunt: Mother or father 's sister .

title: TRADITIONAL RELIGION
subject: English Language
rawText: Traditional religion refers to the indigenous belief systems that originated among a people before the introduction of foreign religions such as Christianity or Islam. These religions are passed down orally from generation to generation and are closely tied to the people’s culture, customs, and way of life. Key features of traditional religion: Belief in a Supreme Being who is the creator of the universe Worship of lesser gods and spirits, often seen as intermediaries Veneration of ancestors, who are believed to influence the living Use of rituals, sacrifices, festivals, and prayers Strong moral codes that guide behavior and promote harmony No written holy book; teachings are preserved through stories, proverbs, and practices Examples: African Traditional Religion Native American traditional beliefs Traditional Asian and Oceanic religions In Nigeria, traditional religion plays an important role in shaping values, community life, respect for elders, and social order.

title: READING COMPREHENSION
subject: English Language
rawText: COMPREHENSION READING FOR MAIN IDEAS. Reading comprehension is the ability to read and understand a given passage. Reading for main ideas of a paragraph is the author 's message about the topic it is often expressed directly or it can be implied. How to find main ideas: Main ideas are often found in the following ways: 1. At the beginning of a paragraph: The first sentence often explains the subject being discussed in the passage. 2. In concluding sentences of a paragraph: Sometimes it comes at the end of the paragraph. 3. At the middle of the paragraph: it is also found at the middle of a paragraph. 4. It begins with a capital letters and ends with a full stop. It's a complete sentence. 5. Remove illustration and other supporting sentences ASSIGNMENT Read the comprehension passage on page 4 of the new concept English for SSS book 1 and write out the main ideas from each paragraphs.

title: STOCK EXCHANGE
subject: English Language
rawText:
A stock exchange is a market where shares, stocks, and other securities are bought and sold. It helps companies raise money and allows investors to buy ownership in companies. Examples of stock exchanges include: New York Stock Exchange Nigerian Exchange Group London Stock Exchange Functions of a stock exchange: Buying and selling of shares Raising capital for companies Providing investment opportunities Regulating trading activities Determining prices of securities Words commonly associated with the stock exchange include: Shares Stocks Securities Bonds Dividends Investment Portfolio Broker Trading Market Equity Bull market Bear market

rawText:
A stock exchange is a market where shares, stocks, and other securities are bought and sold. It helps companies raise money and allows investors to buy ownership in companies. Examples of stock exchanges include: New York Stock Exchange Nigerian Exchange Group London Stock Exchange Functions of a stock exchange: Buying and selling of shares Raising capital for companies Providing investment opportunities Regulating trading activities Determining prices of securities Words commonly associated with the stock exchange include: Shares Stocks Securities Bonds Dividends Investment Portfolio Broker Trading Market Equity Bull market Bear market

Index Exchange Capital Finance Investors Profit Loss

title: INFORMAL LETTER
subject: English Language
rawText: An informal letter is a friendly letter written to people you know well, such as a friend, brother, sister, cousin, or classmate. The language is simple and relaxed. Features of an Informal Letter Writer’s address (top right) Date Salutation (Dear …) Friendly and simple language Closing (Yours sincerely / Yours lovingly) Writer’s name Example of an Informal Letter Email Subject How are you? 12, Olatunji Street, Ibadan. 15th January, 2026. Dear Ayo, How are you and your family? I hope you are all fine. I am also doing well by the grace of God. I am writing to tell you about my new school. The teachers are kind and the students are friendly. My favourite subject is English because our teacher explains very well. I hope to see you during the next holiday. Please greet your parents for me. Yours sincerely, Chinedu

title: SUMMARY
subject: English Language
rawText: Summary A summary is a shortened form of a passage that contains only the main ideas. It is written in your own words and leaves out examples, illustrations, and unnecessary details. Features of a Good Summary It is brief and clear. It contains only important points. It is written in your own words. It is usually written in simple sentences. It does not include examples or quotations. Steps in Writing a Summary Read the passage carefully. Identify the main ideas. Underline or note key points. Remove examples and repetitions. Write the points in short sentences. Things to Avoid in Summary Writing Copying sentences directly from the passage. Adding personal opinions. Writing long explanations. Including examples. Summary Writing (WAEC / NECO Tips) Use one sentence for one point. Write in your own words. Avoid padding. Follow the number of points required.

title: NARRATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText: NARRATIVE ESSAY A narrative essay is an essay that gives accounts of a story,an event or incident which the writer experienced or witnessed. It is an essay that tells story about a particular issue. FEATURE OF NARRATIVE ESSAY 1. It must contain an element of suspense. 2. It must appeal to the sense of smell, touch, sight, feeling and taste. 3. It requires imagination. 4. The naration must be done in a sequential order. 5. Simple past tense should be use. 6. The writer tell a story that conclude with a saying or a Proverbs. NARRATIVE ESSAY TOPICS 1. The day I would never forget. 2.My first day in school. 3. How I spent my holiday. 4. The birthday party I attended. 5. How I escaped arm robbery. ASSIGNMENT Write a narrative essay on the topic: Make a Hay while the Sun shine.

rawText: Vocabulary Associated With Home and family. A home is a place of residence or refuge.It is usually a place where Individual or family can rest and store personal property. title: SPEECH TIMING
subject: English Language
rawText: Speech Timing (Meaning) Speech timing is the ability to plan, control, and manage the time used while delivering a speech so that it is not too long or too short. Why Speech Timing Is Important It helps the speaker finish on time It makes the speech clear and well-organized It prevents rushing or unnecessary repetition It keeps the audience interested Types / Aspects of Speech Timing 1. Time Allocation Sharing time properly: Introduction – short Body – longest part Conclusion – brief and strong 2. Pace of Speech Not too fast Not too slow Speak clearly and steadily 3. Use of Pause Short pauses help listeners understand Pauses give emphasis to important points Example If a speech is 5 minutes: Introduction – 1 minute Body – 3 minutes Conclusion – 1 minute

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText: A speech is a formal talk given to an audience to inform, persuade, entertain, or express ideas and feelings. Types of Speech Informative speech Persuasive speech Welcome speech Farewell speech Debate speech Features of a Good Speech Clear introduction Well-organized body Strong conclusion Simple language Confidence and good delivery Example of a Short Speech Good morning everyone. My name is Kuburat. Today, I want to talk about the importance of education. Education helps us gain knowledge, develop skills, and become responsible citizens. Therefore, we should take our studies seriously. Thank you.

title: CONSONANT SOUND
subject: English Language
rawText: Consonant sounds:Consonant sounds/j/,/z/ #and /3/ Consonant sounds are sounds which are produced with partial or total obstruction of air at some points from the lungs to the lips during articulation. There are 24 Consonant sounds Examples /b/ /d/ / f/ /g/ /h/ bin. do. Feel. got. hair /j/ /k/ /l/ /m/ /n/ your. Cap. light. man. neat. A sound is said to be voiced when there is vibration in the vocal cord during articulation. A sound is voiceless when there is no vibration in the vocal cord Voiced consonants /b/ /d/ /g/ /v/ /z/ /3/ /n//m//r/etc Voiceless consonants /p/ /t/ /k/ /f/ /s/ etc.

title: CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText: Clause A clause is a group of words that has a subject and a verb. Types of Clauses 1. Main (Independent) Clause It has complete meaning. It can stand alone as a sentence. Examples: She is reading. The boy ran away. Adverbial Clause Modifies a verb. Shows time, reason, condition, contrast, purpose. Example: I stayed at home because it was raining. Key Points (WAEC/NECO) A clause must have a subject + verb. Not all clauses are sentences. Clauses are different from phrases (phrases have no finite verb).

title: NOUN (TYPES OF NOUN)
subject: English Language
rawText:
Noun and Types A noun is name of a person, animal, place or things. Types Noun is divided into eight types 1. Common Nouns 2. Proper Nouns 3. Abstract Nouns 4. Collective Nouns 5. Countable Nouns 6. Uncountable Nouns 7. Concrete Nouns 8. Material Nouns 1. COMMON NOUN: A Common noun is a name given in common to every person, or things of the same kind. E.g boy, woman, teacher, doctor, girls officers, poets, dramatist, merchant, travellers, city. And place. 2. PROPER NOUN: A Proper noun is the name given to some particular person or place. E.g Micheal, John, Keat, Nigeria, Togo, Japan. All proper nouns must be written in capital letter. 3. COLLECTIVE NOUN: A collective noun is a general name given to a group of things or person. E,g crowd, mob, team, block, herds, army, family, nation, and class. 4. CONCRETE NOUN: A concrete noun is a name given to a thing that can be counted, touched or seen. E.g book, table, block e.t.c 5. ABSTRACT NOUN: An abstract noun is the name of a quality, action, or state e.g freedom, liberty, thought, joy, sorrow, love, death, goodness, beauty etc. 6. COUNTABLE NOUNS: A countable noun is the name of things that can be counted or divided into singular and plural. e,g student, book, table, and pen.

7. UNCOUNTABLE NOUN: An uncountable noun is the name of a thing that cannot be counted or divided into singular or plural e.g milk, ice, rice, sand, tea. Oxygen etc. 8. MATERIAL NOUN:A material noun is the name of a material or substances out of which things are made e.g gold, silver, cooper, glass etc

title: WORD STRESS
subject: English Language
rawText:
1 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace SCHOOL FOR THE GIFTED – ENGLISH LANGUAGE CLASS: SS1 TOPIC: WORD STRESS Prepared by: Mrs. Naadzenga Mgbede Grace (Subject Teacher) 1. Introduction to Word Stress Word stress refers to the way a particular syllable in a word is pronounced with more force, louder, longer, or at a higher pitch than the other syllables. English is a stress-timed language; therefore, correct stress is very important for good pronunciation and understanding. Example • In the word teacher → TEA -cher The first syllable is stressed. If stress is placed wrongly, meaning may be unclear or may change completely. 2. Meaning of Syllable A syllable is a part of a word that contains one vowel sound and is pronounced at one beat. Words and their syllables • go – 1 syllable • Eng-lish – 2 syllables • com-pu-ter – 3 syllables • e-du-ca-tion – 4 syllables Stress always falls on one syllable only in a word. 3. Importance of Word Stress Word stress helps to: • pronounce English correctly, • differentiate between similar words, • understand spoken English easily, • speak confidently in reading and conversation, • score high marks in Oral English examinations such as WAEC/NECO in future. 4. Features of a Stressed Syllable A stressed syllable usually has: • greater loudness, • longer duration, • clearer vowel quality, • sometimes a change in pitch. Unstressed syllables are weak and often contain the sound /ə/ called schwa .

2 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace 5. Rules Guiding Word Stress in English Although English stress is sometimes irregular, the following general rules guide SS1 learners: Rule 1: Two-Syllable Nouns and Adjectives Most two-syllable nouns and adjectives are stressed on the first syllable. Examples: • TA ble • DOC tor • PRE tty • CLE ver • QUI et Rule 2: Two-Syllable Verbs Most two-syllable verbs take stress on the second syllable. Examples: • re LAX • be GIN • for GET • col LECT Rule 3: Words Ending in –ion, –sion, –tion Stress comes on the syllable before the ending. Examples: • edu CA tion • revi SI on • situa TI on • deci SI on Rule 4: Words Ending in –ic, –ical Stress falls on the syllable before –ic. Examples: • geo GRA phic • dra MA tic • eco NO mic • bio LO gical Rule 5: Compound Words i. Compound Nouns Stress is on the first part. • BLACK board • FOOT ball • CLASS room • NEWS paper ii. Compound Verbs Stress is on the second part. • over FLOW

3 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace • under STAND • out GROW Rule 6: Prefix Words In many words with prefixes (un-, re-, dis-, im-), stress remains on the root word , not on the prefix. • un HAP py • dis LIKE • im POR tant 6. Stress and Change in Meaning Some English words change meaning according to stress placement. Word Stress Pattern Meaning REcord RE -cord (noun) a written account reCORD re- CORD (verb) to keep account PREsent PRE -sent (noun) Gift preSENT pre- SENT (verb) to introduce Students must master these differences for Oral English. 7. Examples of Word Stress Patterns Three-Syllable Words • BEAU tiful – stress 1st • to MA to – stress 2nd • under STAND – stress 3rd Four-Syllable Words • exami NA tion • ge O graphy • com MU nicate 8. Weak Forms in Stress Grammatical words like to, of, for, a, an, was, were are usually unstressed in sentences. • I went to school → /tə/ not /tuː/ • cup of tea → /əv/ 9. Guidelines for Identifying Stress in Exams To answer stress questions: 1. Divide the word into syllables. 2. Listen for the louder part. 3. Use dictionary marks ˈ before stressed syllable. 4. Remember noun/verb contrast rules. 10. Summary • Word stress is the emphasis on one syllable. • English pronunciation depends greatly on correct stress. • Certain endings and compound words follow regular stress rules.

4 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace • Wrong stress can change meaning. 11. Evaluation Exercises Exercise A: Mark the stressed syllable 1. computer 2. situation 3. classroom 4. begin 5. economic Exercise B: Choose the correct option Indicate whether the stress shows noun or verb. • present • record • export • import Exercise C: Syllable Counting Break into syllables and mark stress: • examination • geographic • communication • footballer Note to Students: Regular practice in reading aloud and using a good dictionary will help you master word stress.

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT
subject: English Language
rawText:
1 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace SCHOOL FOR THE GIFTED, GWAGWALADA – FCT ENGLISH LANGUAGE – SS1 SECOND TERM TOPIC: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT Prepared by: Mrs. Naadzenga Mgbede Grace (Subject Teacher) 1. Introduction Vocabulary development is the process of learning, understanding, and correctly using new words in speaking, reading, and writing. A rich vocabulary enables students to express ideas precisely, comprehend texts easily, and perform excellently in examinations. 2. Meaning of Vocabulary Vocabulary means the stock of words a person knows in a language. It includes: • words we understand when we read or listen – receptive vocabulary , • words we use when we speak or write – active vocabulary. 3. Importance of Vocabulary Development Good vocabulary helps learners to: 1. understand comprehension passages, 2. write better essays and letters, 3. speak fluent and confident English, 4. avoid vague expressions, 5. communicate like global citizens. Students of the School for the Gifted are expected to consciously build vocabulary daily for academic excellence. 4. Ways of Developing Vocabulary a. Extensive Reading Reading novels, newspapers, magazines, and subject textbooks exposes students to new words naturally. b. Dictionary Use A good learner’s dictionary shows: • meaning, • pronunciation, • word class, • example sentences. c. Learning Word Families One root can produce many words. • act – action – active – activate – actor • nation – national – nationality – nationalism

2 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace d. Keeping Personal Word Bank Students should own a notebook where they record: • the word, • meaning in their own sentence, • synonym and antonym. 5. Methods of Forming New Words i. Prefixes A prefix is added before a root. • happy → unhappy • possible → impossible • regular → irregular Prefixes often create opposites. ii. Suffixes A suffix is added after a root. • teach → teacher • create → creation • beauty → beautiful iii. Compounding Joining two words to make one. • school + bag → schoolbag • note + book → notebook • foot + ball → football iv. Conversion Changing word class without changing form. • water (noun) → to water (verb) • phone (noun) → to phone (verb) 6. Synonyms and Antonyms Synonyms – words with similar meaning • big – large – huge • begin – start • clever – intelligent Antonyms – opposites • tall – short • early – late • success – failure 7. Learning Vocabulary through Context The context is the surrounding words that help us guess meaning. Example: • The desert is very arid ; plants hardly grow there. “arid” means dry.

3 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace Gifted students must train to infer meanings before checking dictionary. 8. Register in Vocabulary Register means words related to a field. School Register • principal, assembly, hostel, curriculum, laboratory. Hospital Register (familiar to our community) • doctor, ward, syringe, diagnosis, patient. Environment Register • erosion, pollution, climate, biodiversity. 9. Vocabulary Categories for SS1 Students should master: 1. academic words, 2. phrasal verbs, 3. idioms, 4. figurative expressions, 5. commonly confused words. Examples Commonly Confused Words • affect / effect • advice / advise • practise / practice Phrasal Verbs • give up – surrender • look after – care for • put off – postpone Idioms • once in a blue moon • a stitch in time saves nine • call it a day 10. Summary • Vocabulary development is deliberate and continuous. • Words are formed through prefixes, suffixes, compounding. • Dictionary and reading are major tools. • Register and context guide meaning. 11. Class Exercises Exercise A – Give meanings 1. diligent 2. innovative 3. pollution 4. postpone 5. hostel

4 FCT School for the Gifted: SS1 2 nd Term English Notes_Mrs. Naadzebga Mgbede Grace Exercise B – Provide synonyms • intelligent • large • beautiful Exercise C – Use in sentences • diagnosis • arid • diligent • look after Exercise D – Prefix opposites • possible • happy • regular • legal Advice to Students: Learn at least 5 new words every day and use them in your essays and conversations.

title: SIMPLE PRESENT TENSE
subject: English Language
rawText: SIMPLE PRESENT TENSE The simple present tense is used to talk about: • Things we do every day • Actions that happen often • General truths or fact Examples • I come to school early. • You come to school early. • We come to school early. • They come to school early. • He comes to school early. • She comes to school early. • It comes every morning. Rule When the subject is he , she , or it , we add –s or –es to the verb. More Examples • I play football. • She plays football. • They eat rice. • He eats rice. Uses of the Simple Present Tense 1. To show habitual actions o I read every day. 2. To state facts or truths o The sun rises in the east. 3. To show regular actions o She goes to church on Sundays. Exercise Fill in the blanks: 1. She ___ (come/comes) to school early. 2. He ___ (read/reads) his book every night. 3. They ___ (play/plays) football after school.

title: EMPHATIC STRESS
subject: English Language
rawText:
EMPHATIC STRESS DEFINITION IDENTIFICATION HOW TO ANSWER QUESTIONS ON EMPHATIC STRESS. DEFINITION : Emphatic stress is the prominence or emphasis placed on an entire word in a sentence. It is also known as sentence stress which is different from word stress. IDENTIFICATION OF EMPHATIC STRESS 1. The question itself is written in a statement format. Zainab attends a COMMERCIAL college . 2. The emphasised word is all capitalised. COMMERCIAL 3. The answer options are questions. A. Does Musa attend a commercial college? B. Has Zainab graduated from a commercial college? C. Does Zainab attend a technical college? D. Does Zainab attend a commercial school? Answer=C HOW TO ANSWER EMPHATIC STRESS QUESTIONS CORRECTLY. 1. identify the capitalised word. Here, our capitalised word is COMMERCIAL 2. Go through the options. rawText:
1 LESSON PLAN Theme: Structure Week: ……………….. Date: …………………….. Class: SS 1 ………… Period: …………… Time: …………… Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Adjuncts Lesson Topic: Adjunct of Condition Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define adjunct of condition. 2. Identify adjuncts of condition in sentences. 3. State common words that introduce adjuncts of condition. 4. Construct correct sentences using adjuncts of condition. Instructional Resource • Whiteboard • Sentence strips • Recommended text: LESSON PRESENTATION

2 Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: A couple of students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks the following questions: 1. What is an adverbial or adjunct? 2. What is a clause? 3. Can you give an example of a conditional sentence? Students’ Activities: Students respond based on their previous knowledge of clauses and sentence types. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: What is an Adjunct? An adjunct is a word, phrase, or clause that adds extra information to a sentence. It often tells us about time, place, reason, manner, or condition. What is an Adjunct of Condition? An adjunct of condition is a word, phrase, or clause that expresses the condition under which something happens. It usually answers the question: Under what condition? Common Words that Introduce Adjuncts of Condition:

3 • If • Unless • Provided (that) • As long as • On condition that • In case Examples: 1. If you study hard, you will pass. 2. You will succeed provided that you work diligently. 3. I will go with you if you invite me. 4. We shall travel unless it rains. Teacher explains that these clauses depend on a condition being fulfilled. Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively and repeat the examples. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class Teacher guides students to identify adjuncts of condition in sentences. S/N Sentence Adjunct of Condition 1 If it rains, we shall stay indoors. If it rains

4 S/N Sentence Adjunct of Condition 2 You can join us provided that you are ready. Provided that you are ready 3 Unless you apologize, I will not forgive you. Unless you apologize 4 As long as you obey, you will succeed. As long as you obey Students identify more examples from their textbook. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: A couple of students Class Activity (Fill in the blanks): 1. __________ you work hard, you will pass the examination. (If) 2. I will help you __________ you tell me the truth. (provided that) 3. We will not go out __________ it stops raining. (unless) 4. You may stay here __________ you keep quiet. (as long as) Students’ Activities: Students complete the exercise in their notebooks. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A couple of students Teacher asks:

5 1. Define adjunct of condition. 2. Mention four words used to introduce adjuncts of condition. 3. Identify the adjunct of condition in this sentence: “If you call me, I will respond.” 4. Construct two sentences using adjuncts of condition. Students respond orally and in writing. ASSIGNMENT 1. Write five sentences using different adjuncts of condition. 2. Identify the adjunct of condition in each sentence. REFERENCE MATERIAL • Oxford English Language Course Book 1 • Standard English Grammar Textbook

rawText:
SS 1 ENGLISH LANGUAGE WEEK TWO Speech: Oral Composition: Narrative Essay A narrative essay is a story, a tale, or an account of something that has happened and which one is telling to another person. It may be factual (true account) of what really happened or imaginary (made up by the narrator) Topics related to narrative 1. How I spent my last holiday 2. How I escaped being kidnapped 3. Story that illustrate the saying “It pays to be discipline. 4. Story that illustrate the saying “a stitch in time saves nine”. Features of good narrative essay 1. Title: It should have a good captivating and relevant to the event narrated 2. Introduction: It should have a good and interesting beginning 3. The body: It should have few characters that can be effectively handled. 4. Such essay must be written in the past tense. Note: for a good narrative essay, the following should be answered. a. What is the story about? b. What actions took place in your story? c. Who were responsible for those actions d. When did the action take place? e. How did the action happen? f. What were the consequences? Assignment In not less than 450 words, write a story that illustrate “a stitch in time saves nine or prevention is better than cure. Topic 2: Vocabulary: Words Associated with Advertising Advertising is a form of selling. Messages from manufacturers and advertisers reach the customers through the media. Consumers need products. Manufacturers produce goods or brands with the intention to sell them by making them available at reasonable prices.

Some relevant words are: Consumer: one who buys good s and services Advertisement : a public announcement of a product or services to call attention to it Bill-board: notice board on which information is placed Newsletter: a periodic printed report that contains news of interest to a specific group like a society or employee Discount: a reduction in the usual price of something Commercials: activity that is related to buying and selling of goods and services End-users: a person or group that is one of the consumers for whom the product was made. Advertising: Agency a company that handles clients who need their services Assignment Write ten more words related to advertising Topic 3: Structure: Types of Sentence by Functions According to function we have the following types of sentence a. The declarative sentence. This is statement or a declaration. Examples: My principal is a gentleman Kemi did not do her work. b. The interrogative sentence This is a question. Examples: How are you? Did you sleep well? c. The imperative sentence. This is a command. Example: Get out of her Do as you are told.

Note: that the subject of an imperative sentence is often not stated but it can be implied. You get out of her. d. The exclamatory sentence This is an exclamation expressing emotions such as wonder, surprise, alarm, gratitude etc. It is normal introduced by what, how and has exclamation mark at the end. What a beautiful house that is! How kind of you to have come! Volitive sentence This is used to express wish. May it be well with you. May God bless you. Assignment Give more examples of each type of sentence by function

title: ANTONYM : WORDS OPOSITE IN MEANING
subject: English Language
rawText:
1 Theme: Vocabulary Week: ……………….. Date: …………………….. Class: SS 1 ………… Period: …………… Time: …………… Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Vocabulary Lesson Topic: Antonym – Words Opposite in Meaning Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define antonym. 2. Mention at least five pairs of antonyms. 3. Identify antonyms in given sentences. 4. Form correct sentences using antonyms. Instructional Resource • Flash cards showing word pairs • Whiteboard/Chalkboard • English textbook (e.g. ) LESSON PRESENTATION

2 Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: A couple of students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students the following questions: 1. What do you understand by opposite words? 2. Give two examples of opposite words. 3. What is the opposite of “hot”? Students’ Activities: Students respond to the questions based on their previous knowledge. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: What is an Antonym? An antonym is a word that has the opposite meaning of another word. Examples: • Hot — Cold • Big — Small • Rich — Poor • Accept — Reject • Early — Late Teacher explains that antonyms help us understand contrast and improve vocabulary. Teacher also explains that some antonyms are complete opposites (dead/alive), while some allow degrees (hot/cold).

3 Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively and repeat the examples after the teacher. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class Teacher guides students to identify meanings and opposites. S/N Word Meaning Antonym 1 Honest Telling the truth Dishonest 2 Increase To make larger Decrease 3 Victory Winning Defeat 4 Present Being there Absent 5 Strong Having strength Weak 6 Light Not heavy / brightness Heavy / Dark 7 Possible Able to be done Impossible Students participate in identifying more antonyms. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: A couple of students Class Activity (Fill in the blanks): 1. The opposite of “success” is __________ (failure).

4 2. The opposite of “early” is __________ (late). 3. The opposite of “buy” is __________ (sell). 4. The opposite of “happy” is __________ (sad). 5. The opposite of “strong” is __________ (weak). Students’ Activities: Students answer in their notebooks. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A couple of students Teacher asks: 1. Define antonym. 2. Mention five pairs of antonyms. 3. Identify the antonym of “polite.” 4. Form two sentences using any pair of antonyms. Students respond orally and in writing. ASSIGNMENT 1. Write ten words and give their antonyms. 2. Construct five sentences using five different pairs of antonyms. REFERENCE MATERIAL • Oxford English Language Course Book 1 • Standard English Dictionary

title: SPEECH WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
TOPIC 5: SPEECH WRITING A speech is a written material meant to be presented orally to a target audience. Speeches are meant to inform, entertain, persuade, educate or motivate people to action. Kinds of speeches A. For entertainment e.g Birthday party Weddings Dinner party etc. B. For information/to educate the audience e.g Paper presentation to impact knowledge Farewell speech. C. For persuasion Speech that its aim is to convince the audience on a particular issue D. For condolences FEATURES OF A SPEECH 1. The title: The title of a speech should contain the following; the purpose, name and title of the speaker, occasion, place, date and time e.g. A farewell speech presented by Martin Owo, the head boy of Government Secondary School Kubwa on the send forth ceremony of our dearly beloved principal, Mr Idris Kunle, at the assembly hall, on 20th April, 2024 at 10am 2. Introduction This must be carefully done to attract the attention of the audience by recognizing the special guest/audience present. It must start with salutation. Example The chairman of the occasion, the principal, the management staff, the PTA …….. Ladies and gentlemen. I feel highly honored to stand here today to deliver my speech on ………. 3. The Body

This contains the main message. Start by giving your main points and then support each point with relevant details, comparisons and contrasts etc. explaining who, when, where, why, how. All should be presented in good English. 4. The Conclusion Here you summarize your main points. It is important to end in a memorable way by i. making a forceful and shocking statement ii. provide some further food for thought iii. leaving your audience with positive memories of your speech Guidelines 1. A speech is meant to be delivered to an audience, hence, the use of present tense is required. 2. It should be in four sections; headings, introduction, body and conclusion. 3. Slangs and humour should be avoided unless it is for informal situation 4. No name at the end of the speech. Assignment Prepare a speech to be delivered on the prize and award giving day of the final year students of the school.

title: TYPES OF SENTENCES
subject: English Language
rawText:
TOPIC 4: STRUCTURE TYPES OF SENTENCES IN STRUCTURE Simple, compound, complex, and compound complex sentences There are different types of sentences based on structure. They include; simple, compound, complex and compound complex sentences A. Simple Sentence A simple sentence contains one idea and one verb. It consists of one independent clause. Examples 1. Rose went to the market 2. She bought a lot of goods B. Compound Sentence Compound sentence is a sentence which contains two or more independent clauses that are joined together by co-ordinating conjunctions like; and, but, either or, neither nor. The major feature of compound sentence is that it can contain two or more ideas. Examples 1. Rose went to the market and she bought a lot of goods 2. John came yesterday and saw his bag on the table. 3. He came, he saw and he conquered 4. She tried hard but failed in her attempt 5. We can either eat spaghetti or take some wine. C. Complex Sentence A complex sentence contains one main clause and one or more subordinate/independent clauses. Examples; 1. This is the boy who was caught stealing oranges Here, the second idea depends on the first to make a complete sense. “This is the boy” is the main clause while; “Who was caught stealing oranges” is the dependent clause. 2. When the rain stopped, the dancing competition continued. “When the rain stopped” is a dependent clause that derives its complete meaning from the main clause “the dancing competition continued”.

D. Compound Complex Sentence A compound complex sentence contains two main clauses and at least one or more dependent clauses. Examples 1. We ate the food which was kept on the dining table for us but we were not satisfied. The above compound complex sentence can be broken thus; i. We ate the food but we were not satisfied (compound sentence containing two independent clauses). ii. Which was kept on the dining table for us …. (dependent clause). Therefore, compound complex sentence contains two independent clauses. More examples: 1. While the children were sleeping, the dog stole into the room and ate the raw meat. 2. Your creditor came yesterday, when you were not at home, and asked after you but I was able to pay him. Assignment 1. Give 2 examples of simple and compound sentences. 2. Mention the features of complex and compound complex sentences 3. Mention the difference between the compound sentence and the complex sentence.

DATE: 24th November, 2025 CLASS: SS 1 TIME: 11 : 10 – 12 : 30 DURATION: 80 Minutes SUBJECT: English Language THEME: Continuous writing UNIT TOPIC: Writing LESSON TOPIC: Article writing INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES: at the end of the lesson, the students should be able to: a. explain article writing b. state the features / format of article writing c. List and explain the useful hints on writing article. d. Write good articles INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES: Cut-out from a magazine LESSON PRESENTATION STEP1: Identification of prior ideas MODE: individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: the teacher asks the students to define essay writing. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITY: the students define essay writing. STEP 2: Exploration MODE: individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: the teacher explains essay writing further, and ask the students to say how an essay should be written. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITY: the students give their explanations. STEP 3: Discussion MODE: entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: using the instructional resource, the teacher guides the lesson as follows: Article: this is a complete piece of writing on an issue of public interest. It usually contains views or opinions of its writer on a specific issue or topic. An article is specifically for publication in a magazine or a newspaper. The audience for an article 1. The school community : an article for school magazine. 2. Local community : an article for local newspaper. 3. Foreign readers : an article for foreign magazine. 4. National community : an article for national newspaper. Useful hints on writing a good article 1. Content : the content depends on the topic you are asked to write on, but you must write on all aspects of the question to earn a good mark. Your points must be relevant to the question.

2. Organization : you are expected to write the title of the article clearly on top of the article. You are expected to write an introductory paragraph in which you are to give readers an insight to your topic. 3. Expression : your language should be formed since you are writing an article for publication in a newspaper or magazine. Write in simple straight-forward sentences and avoid using slangs. Organizing an article writing 1. Write just the title of the article and go straight to the introductory paragraph. Do not use letter writing format. 2. Choose an eye-catching title, as readers go for articles with interesting captions. 3. Go straight to the point. 4. If the article is on a controversial topic, make reference to previous articles supposed to have been contributed by others on it. 5. Write your full name and address at the end of your article. If for a school magazine, write your full name and class. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITY: the students listen attentively. STEP 4: Application MODE: individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: the teacher guide the students to write an introductory paragraph to an article. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITY: the students attempt to write an introductory paragraph to an article. STEP 5: Evaluation MODE: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher evaluates the lesson using the following questions: a. Explain article writing b. State the features / format of article writing c. List and explain the useful hints on writing article. d. Write good articles. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES: The students answer the questions. ASSIGNMENT: write an article suitable for publication in your school magazine on examination malpractices in public examinations and their remedies. REFERENCE: Essential English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Latilo T.A et al
