title: SPEECH - EMPHATIC STRESS
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH: Emphatic Stress Emphatic stress can be defined as the stress or force which is put on a particular word in a sentence for emphasizing that word or a point in the sentence usually only content words (verbs, nouns etc.) are stressed but when attention is being drawn to a particular piece of information, words other than content words such as prepositions, articles, pronouns etc. can be stressed as well. The focus of emphatic stress is exactitude. It is used to convey or show the exact particular meaning the speaker wants the hearer to have or understand. The speaker in his sentence may decide to give or convey a special meaning or message as an answer to someone’s question. It is only the particular word he stresses that will help to show, give or convey the special meaning he intends to put across to his hearer. Emphatic stress enhances the particular meaning the speaker wants to convey and makes the message very clear and easy for the hearer to understand. Example 1. Musa OPENLY disagreed with his boss yesterday. a. Did Musa secretly disagree with his boss yesterday? b. Did Musa openly disagree with his boss last week? c. Did Ali openly disagree with his boss yesterday d. Did Musa openly agree with his boss yesterday? 2. The DRIVER has taken John away a. Whom did the driver take away? b. Who took John away? c. What did the driver do? d. Where did the driver take John to? Identify the answers according to the explanation on emphatic stress. Further exercise i. My mother’s FRIEND hates pets (not her enemy or any other relation) ii. The manager SACKED the typist (not employee) iii. The PASSENGER boat docked at Calabar (not the cargo boat) 1. John scrubs the floor every SATURDAY a. Does Peter scrub the floor every Saturday? b. Does John scrub the floor every Saturday? c. Does John scrub the wall every Saturday? d. Does John scrub the floor every Sunday? 2. The officer ACCEPTED the bribe

a. Did the officer accept a bribe? b. Did the officer accept the gift? c. Did the officer reject the bribe? d. Did the recruit accept the bribe? 3. Ben’s wife is always CHARMINE. a. Is John’s wife always charming? b. Is Ben’s sister always charming? c. Is Ben’s wife always quarrelsome? d. Is Ben always charming? 4. My mother bakes bread on SUNDAYS. a. Does my mother sell bread on Sundays? b. Does my mother sell bread on Sundays? c. Does my mother make biscuits on Saturdays? d. Does my mother make biscuits on Sundays? 5. The CUSTOMER is always right a. Is the customer often right? b. Is the customer always wrong? c. When is the customer right? d. Is the seller always right? Assignment Choose the one to which the given sentence is the appropriate. 1] MARY loves brown shoes. A] What colour of shoes does Mary love B] Does Mary hate brown shoes? C] Who loves brown shoes ? D] Does Mary love brown gowns ? 2] It rained ALL day yesterday. A] For how long did it rain yesterday ? B] When did it rain all day? C] Was it dry all day yesterday ? D] Did it rain all day last week ?

Reference : New Comprehensive English Language for Senior Secondary Schools, by Martins Izuchukwu Amaechi. Oral English for Schools by Vickky Odozi.

title: CONT. WRITING - REPORT WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Continuous Writing: Report Writing A report is spoken or written account of an event or happening that has taken place. It may be an event that has been heard, seen or done or studied. It is always a narrative based on an actual experiences of the reporter and very often requires record keeping to enable the writer to give actual figures and dates. Types of Report 1. Private/informal report This is the type of reports you narrate to your parents, friends or classmates of an incident that happened to you or you witnessed. It is supposed to be a direct personal experience of the writer. 2. Official/formal report It is one that is presented as a formal document giving details of an event that occurred like a robbery incident, an accident, the proceedings of a meeting, a petition, a report of an excursion, research report of an experiment carried out etc. Guidelines for report writing 1. Pay attention to details and be accurate. 2. Note the sequence of events. It is important to report precisely which events led to another and what action caused what result. 3. Take into consideration the purpose for which you are writing the report. A police report is different from a report to your classmates. 4. The method of presenting requires short and clear sentences with detailed information like, date, time of event, people present, cause, time it ended, effort made to stop or enhance the incident etc. explain in paragraphs giving only the essential facts which will present a true picture of what happened. Assignment Write a report of an accident that occurred and which you witnessed to the police.

title: CONT. WRITING - ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText: Continuous writing: Argumentative Essay An argumentative essay is one that requires you to present a subject with a view to persuading your reader to agree with your own point of view against another one. An argument may be developed. a. to prove a point b. to present a view point c. to balance the two side of an issue The major differences between debate and argumentative essay is that in argumentative you are not seeing your audience so there will not be any need to greet. In argumentative, write your topic, and start writing your views point without addressing anybody. Useful hints on how to write a good argumentative essay 1. Content Here you look for the key words and show a good understanding of them before putting pen on paper. Female children are more beneficial to their parents than male children. The operative words here are beneficial and parents. Here you must interpret your question very well a. At least five arguments fully developed for or against a topic are enough for a good mark. b. Stop your opponent before he stops you by knocking his points with your arguments. 2. Organization In argumentative essay you should imagine having an audience listening to your argument. You should therefore start with the usual vocative and refer to your audience from time to time. After this you should take your position for or against the topic. In the body of the essay you should support your view with strong points. You can quote notable figures in the area you are arguing on. In the conclusion; reaffirm your position. Remember that good paragraphing, coherence through the use of linking words and logical sequence of ideas will be adequately rewarded. Expression: Use simple sentences and rhetorical questions to carry your audience along. Assignment Write for or against the topic “it is better to attend a school near your home than one outside your neighbourhood.

title: PHRASAL VERBS
subject: English Language
rawText:
NOTE ON PHRASAL VERBS A Phrasal Verb is a combination of a main verb and one or more particles (prepositions or adverbs) that function as a single semantic unit. The meaning of a phrasal verb often goes beyond the sum of its individual parts. The particle can change the meaning of the main verb, resulting in a new expression. Simply put, a phrasal verb is a combination of a verb and one or more prepositions or adverbs. The meaning of the combination is often different from the individual meanings of the words. Verbs: A verb is a word that expresses an action, occurrence, or state of being. It is a key element in constructing sentences and can convey various actions or conditions. Examples: come, call, go, take, bring, run, fall, walk, Preposition: A preposition is a word that shows the relationship between a noun (or pronoun) and another word in the sentence. It indicates location, direction, time, or manner. Examples: in, off, at, on, under, beneath, upon, by, of, across, etc Come, go and call Examples: 1. Come across: To find or encounter unexpectedly. Example: She came across an old friend at the market. 2. Come along To accompany or make progress. Example: Are you coming along with the project? 3. Come around: To change one's opinion or attitude. Example: He finally came around to our way of thinking. 4. Come by: To obtain or acquire. Example: Having a chat with Mr. President is not easy to come by. 5. Come down with become ill with a specific illness. Example: I think I'm coming down with a cold. 6. Go through To examine or review thoroughly. Example: Let's go through the details of the plan. 7. Go under To fail or go bankrupt. Example: The company went under due to financial difficulties. 8. Go without To lack or not have something. Example: We'll have to go without electricity until the power is restored. 9. Go on To continue or persist. Example: The meeting will go on as scheduled. 10. Go for To choose or select. Example: I think I'll go for the purple shirt.

11. Call back: To return a phone call. Example: I'll call you back as soon as I finish my meeting. 12. Call off: To cancel an event or activity. Example: They had to call off the soccer match due to bad weather. 13. Call for To demand or require. Example: The situation calls for immediate action. 14. Call in To request someone's presence or assistance. Example: We need to call in a specialist to fix the issue. 15. Call out: To shout or say something loudly. Example: The teacher had to call out the students for being disruptive. 16. Call up: To phone or contact someone. Example: I'll call up the customer to discuss their concerns. Crafted by Ewuzie Jacinta GSS Gwarimpa-Estate.

It indicates location, direction, time, or manner. Examples: in, off, at, on, under, beneath, upon, by, of, across, etc Come, go and call Examples: 1. Come across: To find or encounter unexpectedly. Example: She came across an old friend at the market. 2. Come along To accompany or make progress. Example: Are you coming along with the project? 3. Come around: To change one's opinion or attitude. Example: He finally came around to our way of thinking. 4. Come by: To obtain or acquire. Example: Having a chat with Mr. President is not easy to come by. 5. Come down with become ill with a specific illness. Example: I think I'm coming down with a cold. 6. Go through To examine or review thoroughly. Example: Let's go through the details of the plan. 7. Go under To fail or go bankrupt. Example: The company went under due to financial difficulties. 8. Go without To lack or not have something. Example: We'll have to go without electricity until the power is restored. 9. Go on To continue or persist. Example: The meeting will go on as scheduled. 10. Go for To choose or select. Example: I think I'll go for the purple shirt.

11. Call back: To return a phone call. Example: I'll call you back as soon as I finish my meeting. 12. Call off: To cancel an event or activity. Example: They had to call off the soccer match due to bad weather. 13. Call for To demand or require. Example: The situation calls for immediate action. 14. Call in To request someone's presence or assistance. Example: We need to call in a specialist to fix the issue. 15. Call out: To shout or say something loudly. Example: The teacher had to call out the students for being disruptive. 16. Call up: To phone or contact someone. Example: I'll call up the customer to discuss their concerns. title: CONT. WRITING - REPORT WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Continuous Writing: Report Writing A report is spoken or written account of an event or happening that has taken place. It may be an event that has been heard, seen or done or studied. It is always a narrative based on an actual experiences of the reporter and very often requires record keeping to enable the writer to give actual figures and dates. Types of Report 1. Private/informal report This is the type of reports you narrate to your parents, friends or classmates of an incident that happened to you or you witnessed. It is supposed to be a direct personal experience of the writer. 2. Official/formal report It is one that is presented as a formal document giving details of an event that occurred like a robbery incident, an accident, the proceedings of a meeting, a petition, a report of an excursion, research report of an experiment carried out etc. Guidelines for report writing 1. Pay attention to details and be accurate. 2. Note the sequence of events. It is important to report precisely which events led to another and what action caused what result. 3. Take into consideration the purpose for which you are writing the report. A police report is different from a report to your classmates. 4. The method of presenting requires short and clear sentences with detailed information like, date, time of event, people present, cause, time it ended, effort made to stop or enhance the incident etc. explain in paragraphs giving only the essential facts which will present a true picture of what happened. Assignment Write a report of an accident that occurred and which you witnessed to the police.

VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT : WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH MEDICINE Medicine is the study and treatment of diseases and injuries. PRACTITIONERS IN THE FIELD OF MEDICINE 1. Physiotherapist: One specialized in the treatment of children and adult disease, injuries or weakness in the joints muscles of old people’s bones through exercise or massage. 2. Paediatrician: A specialist who treats children and babies 3. Gynecologist: A specialist who treat women. 4. Obstetrician: One who specializes in the delivery of babies. 5. Medical Doctor: A trained personnel who has been given the licence to practice medicine and prescribe drugs to ill and injured persons. 6. Radiotherapist: One trained to take x-rays or other forms of radiation in the treatment of diseases. 7. Geriatrician/d ʒ eri ə ti ʃ n/: An expert in the medical care of old people 8. Opthalmologist/oculist/okj ə list/: A specialist who treat eye disease and operates on the eye. 9. Optician: A specialist who examines the eye and recommend glasses. 10. Pathologist: A specialist who performs autopsy – examines dead bodies to find out the cause of the death. 11. Dentist: A doctor who specializes in teeth treatment 12. Masseur /mses ʒ :/: A female professional for massage. Convalesce: A period or time when one recovers after an illness or a medical operation. 5. Subcutaneously: Given through the skin 6. Intramuscularly: Given through the muscle 7. title: SYNONYMS
subject: English Language
rawText:
VOCABULARY: SYNONYMS OF WORDS A synonyms is a word or phrase that means exactly or nearly the same as another word or phrase in the same language for example “shut” is a synonym for “close”. Synonyms are also words that have almost the same meaning; begin – commence, battle – conflict, tinge – stain, keen – sharp, acute etc. We should also know that no two English words are exactly identical in their meaning and usage, just as not two human faces are likely to be completely identical in their features. Some words may appear identical at first, a close examination will show differences in the usage. For example, “wealthy” and “rich” appear to mean the same thing. However, while “wealthy” is used in relation to money and property, “rich” has many other appliations e.g. rich colour, rich cake, rich decoration, rich soil etc. Again while “fragrance” is used in reference to “perfume”, its synonyms “aroma” and “odour” show differences in usage. While “aroma” is used in relation to wine or spirits, “odours” often suggests a foul smell. Some words share equivalence in meaning, précised equivalence maybe interchangeable as in. a. He has a big house b. He has a large house “Big” and “large” are interchanged here in terms size. But in, that was a big help, “big” cannot be interchange with “large” neither can “large” be interchange with “big” in, He was in a large part responsible for what happened. There is no “absolute sameness” in synonyms. It is a good test of discrimination to select or take the most appropriate word. Sometimes, one synonym is realized more than another; example: “Beautiful” has a deeper and more specific meaning than “pretty” or “a lovely”. Therefore, when we say that two words are synonyms we mean that they are similar in a specific contest and can be used to replace each other in the context. The importance of synonyms stems from the fact that it provides variety for words in English language. It helps one to know the exact words to be used in the prevailing context. Examples of words and their synonyms Words Synonyms 1. Annihilation Destruction, carnage extinction 2. Benefit Profit, revenue, yield, gain 3. Deterioration Pollution, defilement, adulteration 4. Enormous Huge, gigantic, massive 5. Fertile Fruitful, abundant, productive 6. House Dwelling, abode, domicile 7. Intelligent Clever, brilliant, knowledgeable

8. Loyal Faithful, ardent, devoted 9. Organization Institution, management 10. Partner Associate, colleagues, companion 11. Polite Cautions, cordial, gracious 12. Risky Dangerous, perilous, treacherous 13. Sleepy Drowsy, sluggish, listless 14. Vacant Empty, deserted, unhabited 15. Apex Summit, climax 16. Protagonist Hero, star, major actor How to identify correct synonyms 1. The tense of the word use; Tense in English simply means or refers to the time of an action performed by the subject and indicated by the verb. We have the present tense, past tense and future tense e.g. Begin – start Began – started Beginning – Starting 2. The part of speech which the word used belongs to; nouns, pronouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, prepositions, conjunctions and interjections. Exercise Provide the correct synonyms to these words 1. Deprived stripped 2. Career 3. Counterpart 4. Practice 5. Distinguishing 6. Heeding 7. Kinsmen 8. Odds 9. Roared 10. Monster 11. Inferno References Basic English Grammar for Schools and Colleges by Chidinma C. Nduaguibe Complete English Course for Senior Secondary Schools by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe Ph.D

title: PHOTOGRAPHY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Vocabulary Development: Words associated with Photography Define Photography Photography is the art or practice of taking and processing photographs picture film that supports the light sensitive photographic emulsion color/flash/aerial Words related with photography 1. Lens: A piece of glass or other transparent material, curved on one or both sides, which makes a beam of light passing through it to bend, spread out became narrow, change direction used in the camera. 2. Snapshot: A picture taken with a hand held camera 3. Dark room: A darkroom in which photographs can be given their proper form (developed). 4. View finder: It helps a photographer to aim and compose his picture. It is a glass hole which shows the photographer what his photograph will include. 5. Shutter: The shutter is a mechanical device that controls the length of time light allowed to enter the camera through the lens and fall on the film. 6. Focusing control: This enables the photographer to focus on objects at varying distances to create the sharpest possible image. 7. Shutter Release: This is the button that activates the shutter. 8. Diaphragm: This device control the amount of light that reaches the film by varying the size of the lens opening. The “iris” type of diaphragm is composed of a series of thin, metal leaves that over tap, leaving a variable circular opening in the center. 9. Film Advancer: This is a mechanism for moving the film through the camera so that one frame after another can be exposed in sequence on a roll of film. 10. Developer: A chemical substance used for bringing out the image on a photographic plate or film after a picture has been take on it. 11. Photograph: A picture obtained by using a camera and film sensitive to light photo, snap, pictute. 12. Blurred Photographs: Photographs that cannot be clearly seen. 13. Flash gun: A piece of apparatus for holding a flash bulb and is used at the moment when the photograph is taken. 14. Cine camera: Used to take motion pictures 15. Tripod: A three legged stand used to stability and elevate a camera, a flash unit or other photographic equipment. 16. Negative: A long narrow strip of chemically wasted plastic which is advanced so that the next image is projected onto an exposed film. 17. Aperture: A hole or an opening through which light travels

other words SLR camera, a flash, over exposed print, speed, background, lead camera with film, photographer, focus, glossy/matt prints, time exposure, out of focus, flash light. Assignment Write out ten more words that are associated with Photography and their meanings.

title: SPEECH - LISTENING TO GRASP MAIN POINTS IN A POEM
subject: English Language
rawText:
TOPIC 1: LISTENSING TO GRASP MAIN POINTS IN A POEM Poetry is an imaginative and emotional creative work of art meant to stimulate thought and to be enjoyed. It is the sum total of the use of certain devices in writing such as rhythm, rhymes, meter, figure of speech, stanza, verse, the poet’s feeling and at titude to the subject matter etc. TYPES OF POETRY 1. Narrative poem: A poem that tells a story. 2. Lyrics poem: A poem that is musical in nature 3. Dramatic poem: Poem involving characters that interact in verse form. 4. Some: A 14 lines poem. We have two types of sonnet. a. Petracchan Italian sonnet divided into octane and sestet with rhyming scheme of abba, abba, ade, ade. b. Shakespearean sonnet which has 3 set of four lines followed by a couplet. 5. Pastorial poem: Poem on a country side or rural life 6. Dirge: A poem for the dead. 7. Epigram: Poem about the deeds of great people. 8. Ode: Poem that addresses a person or thing. Others include: satire, ballad, epic, limericle, elegy etc. POETIVE DEVICES 1. Verses/stanza: Poetry is written in verses or in stanzas. A stanza may be made up of 4 lines or more 2. Imagery: Imagery is a mind picture. It is a collection of images or a mental picture called in mind by the use of concrete expression to appeal to the reader’s sense of imagination. 3. Language: The language is the writer’s choice of words. It is also called “Diction”. The writer may choose to make his language simple and sometimes difficult. Poetry makes use of rhyme unlike prose. 4. Setting: This is the time and place of the events or actions in a poem. 5. Figure of speech: A phrase or a word having different meaning than its literal meanings. ASSIGNMENT: Night rain is a poem written by John Pepper Clark on his experience as a boy. Listen carefully as the poem is read on page 230 and answer the questions on unit 5 page 66. CLASS ACTIVITIES AFRICA BY R.E.G AMARHOE

I saw a maiden dark and lovely, sitting by a wayside, sad and lovely Oh pretty maiden, so dark and comely. Why sit by the wayside, sad and lonely? I am neither sad nor lonely, she said, but living, Sir, among the deaf and dumb, Relentlessly watching these shameless dead. Makes my warm heart grow very cold and dumb. The analysis of the above poem. The poem is an elegy (a poem that expresses sadness) it talks about a pretty lady with a warm heart who later became sad because of the circumstances that surround her. Devices used in the poem 1. Setting: by the wayside – along the road 2. Rhyming scheme: AB, AB, CD, CD. 3. Imagery: pretty maiden, wayside, deaf and dumb, shameless, dead, heart. 4. Figure of speech: Metaphor Answers to the questions on the poem Pg 77 New concept English. 1. The mood of the maiden is sadness. Line 8 shows the evidence “makes warm heart grow very cold and numb. 2. The lady felt that way because she is living among people that have no feelings. Line 6. 3. The lady referred to here is a pretty maiden. 4. She is from Africa- People from dark origin. 5. Personification 6. It is a metaphor 7. Bad, dark, lonely, deaf, cold, numb.

pages.text: TOPIC 1: LISTENSING TO GRASP MAIN POINTS IN A POEM Poetry is an imaginative and emotional creative work of art meant to stimulate thought and to be enjoyed. It is the sum total of the use of certain devices in writing such as rhythm, rhymes, meter, figure of speech, stanza, verse, the poet’s feeling and at titude to the subject matter etc. TYPES OF POETRY 1. Narrative poem: A poem that tells a story. 2. Lyrics poem: A poem that is musical in nature 3. Dramatic poem: Poem involving characters that interact in verse form. 4. Some: A 14 lines poem. We have two types of sonnet. a. Petracchan Italian sonnet divided into octane and sestet with rhyming scheme of abba, abba, ade, ade. b. Shakespearean sonnet which has 3 set of four lines followed by a couplet. 5. Pastorial poem: Poem on a country side or rural life 6. Dirge: A poem for the dead. 7. Epigram: Poem about the deeds of great people. 8. Ode: Poem that addresses a person or thing. Others include: satire, ballad, epic, limericle, elegy etc. POETIVE DEVICES 1. Verses/stanza: Poetry is written in verses or in stanzas. A stanza may be made up of 4 lines or more 2. Imagery: Imagery is a mind picture. It is a collection of images or a mental picture called in mind by the use of concrete expression to appeal to the reader’s sense of imagination. 3. Language: The language is the writer’s choice of words. It is also called “Diction”. The writer may choose to make his language simple and sometimes difficult. Poetry makes use of rhyme unlike prose. 4. Setting: This is the time and place of the events or actions in a poem. 5. Figure of speech: A phrase or a word having different meaning than its literal meanings. ASSIGNMENT: Night rain is a poem written by John Pepper Clark on his experience as a boy. Listen carefully as the poem is read on page 230 and answer the questions on unit 5 page 66. CLASS ACTIVITIES AFRICA BY R.E.G AMARHOE

The poem is an elegy (a poem that expresses sadness) it talks about a pretty lady with a warm heart who later became sad because of the circumstances that surround her. Devices used in the poem 1. Setting: by the wayside – along the road 2. Rhyming scheme: AB, AB, CD, CD. 3. Imagery: pretty maiden, wayside, deaf and dumb, shameless, dead, heart. 4. title: SUMMARY WRITING - SUMMARIZING IN A SPECIFIED NUMBE
subject: English Language
rawText:
SUMMARY: SUMMARISING A PASSAGE IN A SPECIFIED NUMBER OF SENTENCES Summary can be described as a shortened form of a long passage after removing all irrelevant ideas from the main points and giving a short account of the passage using your own words. To summarize a passage in a specified number of sentences demands that one should pay attention to the instruction on the number of sentences each questions requires. Some questions demands that you summarize in one, two, or three sentences. Ensure you write as instructed. A sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. THINGS TO NOTE FOR GOOD SUMMARY 1. Brevity: Your answer must be brief and straight to the point. No use of additional information apart from the main points. 2. Relevance: A candidate answer should be relevant to the points mentioned in the passage. 3. Clarity: This means that students are expected to put down their answers clearly. 4. Originality: Your answers should be written in your own words to avoid the error of mindless lifting. 5. Identify the topic sentences: The topic sentences are the main points in the paragraphs of the passage which are mostly found in the first or last sentence of a paragraph. 6. Write your answers in complete sentences CAUSES OF LOSS OF MARK IN SUMMARY WRITING 1. Mindless lifting of words from the passage. This means copying down the exact words and expressions of the writer. 2. Phrases and incomplete sentences. In summary, your answers should be written in complete sentences not in phrases. 3. Writing more than required number of sentences. 4. Grammatical/expression errors. 5. Wrong use of preamble or the introductory statement that does not flow with the sentences. Exercise Answer the summary questions in unit 7 of your New Concept English i. In one sentence, what is the reason for the war in the passage? ii. In two sentences, one for each, explain the two types of war the writer feels could have made sense.

Reference : New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools by Ayo Banjo et al.

title: SPEECH : SIMPLE POLITE REQUEST, SIMPLE GREETINGS.
subject: English Language
rawText:
Speech : SIMPLEC POLITE REQUESTS, SIMPLE GREETINGS Request means politely asking for something when making a request either to a known or unknown person. It is always good to show some politeness. One’s expression (i.e what one says) and the manner of expression (how it is said), determine the pitch of one’s voice. Rising tone is always used in making request. Modal verbs like “can, will, would, may, could etc , are used for request. S/N Request Appropriate response 1 Can you tell me the time please? I’m sorry, my wrist watch is not functioning 2 Will you lend me your book today? No I can’t, I have a test tomorrow 3 Will you help me lift my box? Sure I will, where is it? 4 Do you mind if I use your mathematical set? Not at all, please go ahead and use it. 5 Can I borrow your pen for a minute Yes, here it is Greetings is a sign or word of welcome or pleasure when meeting somebody or receiving a guest. In our day to day activities, we meet a lot of people at home, school, neighbourhood, market, bank, social gathering etc. Every language has its own greetings. In English language, we have two main forms of greetings: formal and informal Formal greeting is used in formal occasion like birthdays, marriage ceremonies or seasons (Easter, Christmas, and new year etc.). They are also used during greetings of people much older than us, just like greetings e.g. Happy birthday, happy new year, Joe good morning sir, safe journey Gideon, goodbye uncle. Informal greetings is the greetings used for classmates friends, relations who are not much older than us e.g. Hello, Hi, how are you? – I’m okay, I am fine, fine thank you and you? Assignment 1. When parting with a friend what is the appropriate thing to say? 2. Define the concept a. greeting b. request

3. What is the intonation used for the following (a) greeting (b) request

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH INVESTMENT
subject: English Language
rawText:
Vocabulary Development: Words Associated with Investment An asset or item acquired with the goal of generating income or appreciation over time. Words related to investments Asset Stock Capital Bond Investing Diversification Mutual fund Equity Shareholder Dividend Sector Venture capital Fund Growth Broker Cash Capital Chips Finance Hedge Interest Business Income Commitment Speculation Bank Development Debt Holdings Leveraged Share Brokeage Cash flow Trade Securities Purchase Profit Loans Companies Firms Insurance Bills Arbitrage 1. Annual Return: An annual rate of return is the profit or loss on an investment over a one year period. 2. Bond: Bond are investment securities where an investor lend money to a company or a government for a set period of time 3. Hedge: Is to take an offsetting position in an asset or investment that reduces the price risk of an existing position. 4. Equity: Is the amount of capital invested or owned by the owner of a company. 5. Leverage: To using debt borrowed funds to amplify returns from an investment or project. 6. Brokeage: It provides intermediary services in various areas e.g investing, obtaining a loan or purchasing real estate. 7. Shareholder: Is a person, company or institution that owns at least one share of a company’s stock or in a mutual fund. 8. Dividend: Is a sum of money or reward paid to the shareholders for their investment in a company’s equity.

9. Arbitrage: The act of buying a security in one market and simultaneously selling it in another market at a higher price 10. Insurance: Is a means of protecting from financial loss in which in exchange for a party agree to compensate another party in the event of a certain loss, damage or injury. Assignment Write out ten more words that are associated with Investment and their meanings.

title: STRUCT. - RECORD KEEPING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Record Keeping Record keeping is the process of keeping information about something for the purpose of preserving/keeping it for future use. The information can be stored in a written form or in an electronic system for future reference. ITEMS IN KEEPING RECORDS 1. Personal diary 2. Files 3. Electronic system e.g. computer, phones, disc, recorded tapes etc. 4. Books e.g school attendance book for staff 5. Log book: This book contains records of certain events or activities that happened in the school. 6. School diary for scheme of works and after work done 7. Class registers for students attendance to school. 8. Dossiers: for students results 9. Visitors book: for important visitors 10. Black book/punishment book 11. Hospital folders 12. Minutes book on proceedings of meetings etc. Reasons for keeping records 1. Records are kept for reference purpose 2. Records are kept in order not to forget them easily 3. Records are kept for future clarifications e.g school fees receipt 4. It makes one not to get into trouble. 5. It is used for interviews or for job purposes. 6. It shows that the keeper is careful, trustworthy and responsible 7. Record keeping shows a good mark one someone’s personality. Where and how records should be kept Records should be kept in orderly manner and in a safe place. E.g a big envelope with a title or name written on it. Records are kept where they can be easily found. They are also written in brief, concise and accurate manner. Exercise a. What is record keeping? b. Give five reasons why records are kept c. Mention six items for keeping records. d. Why do you keep personal records? Assignment

Get a small diary, keep records of your activities for two weeks and submit on a scheduled date.

title: EMPHATIC STRESS
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Speech Date: ___________________ Class: SS 1 Time: ___________________ Duration: 40Minutes Subject: English Language Week: ___________________ Unit Topic: Speech Lesson Topic: Emphatic Stress Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Explain the meaning of emphatic stress. 2. Identify words that carry emphatic stress in sentences. 3. Demonstrate how emphatic stress changes the meaning of an utterance. 4. Read sentences with appropriate emphatic stress. 5. Construct sentences showing emphatic stress. Instructional Resources ● Whiteboard/Chalkboard ● Sentence charts ● Flashcards containing sample sentences ● Audio recordings (optional) LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: Identification of Prior Ideas (Engage) Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students:

● What is stress in speech? ● Do we pronounce every word in a sentence with the same force? ● What happens when we pronounce one word more strongly than others? Teacher reads: ● I bought the book. Then repeats with emphasis on different words. Students' Activities ● Listen carefully. ● State the differences they notice. ● Predict why certain words receive extra stress. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Meaning of Emphatic Stress Emphatic stress is the extra force or prominence given to a particular word in a sentence in order to emphasize its importance or to convey a specific meaning. Emphatic stress helps a speaker to: ● Correct misinformation. ● Express contrast. ● Highlight important information. ● Show strong feelings. Students' Activities ● Listen attentively. ● Take notes. ● Ask questions where necessary.

Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Teacher explains that changing the stressed word often changes the meaning of the sentence. Examples of Emphatic Stress Sentence 1: I bought the book yesterday. 1. I bought the book yesterday. ○ Not someone else. 2. I BOUGHT the book yesterday. ○ I purchased it; I did not borrow it. 3. I bought the BOOK yesterday. ○ Not a pen or a notebook. 4. I bought the book YESTERDAY . ○ Not today. Sentence 2: Mary borrowed my pen. 1. MARY borrowed my pen. ○ Not Jane. 2. Mary BORROWED my pen. ○ She did not steal it. 3. Mary borrowed MY pen. ○ Not yours. 4. Mary borrowed my PEN . ○ Not my ruler. Sentence 3: The principal praised the teacher. 1. The PRINCIPAL praised the teacher.

○ Not the vice-principal. 2. The principal PRAISED the teacher. ○ He did not criticize the teacher. 3. The principal praised the TEACHER . ○ Not the student. Sentence 4: We are travelling to Abuja tomorrow. 1. WE are travelling to Abuja tomorrow. ○ Not they. 2. We are TRAVELLING to Abuja tomorrow. ○ We are not merely planning. 3. We are travelling to ABUJA tomorrow. ○ Not Lagos. 4. We are travelling to Abuja TOMORROW . ○ Not today. More Examples of Emphatic Stress 1. HE won the competition. 2. She is VERY intelligent. 3. This is MY bag. 4. The meeting starts at TEN o'clock. 5. I said RED , not blue. 6. We need the report TODAY . 7. It was JOHN who called. 8. She ACTUALLY completed the work. 9. They arrived EARLY . 10. The food was DELICIOUS . Functions of Emphatic Stress 1. To express contrast. 2. To correct an error. 3. To emphasize important information. 4. To express surprise or strong emotion.

5. To attract the listener's attention. Step 4: Application Mode: Pair Work Teacher's Activities Teacher writes the following sentences on the board: 1. I met the governor yesterday. 2. She gave me a gift. 3. The students completed the assignment. Students are asked to: ● Read each sentence several times. ● Stress a different word each time. ● Explain how the meaning changes. Students' Activities ● Practise pronunciation. ● Demonstrate emphatic stress. ● Discuss meaning changes. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What is emphatic stress? 2. Mention three functions of emphatic stress. 3. Read a sentence using emphatic stress. 4. Explain how emphatic stress can change meaning. 5. Construct two sentences showing emphatic stress.

Students' Activities ● Answer questions orally. ● Read sample sentences aloud. Summary Teacher revises: ● Meaning of emphatic stress. ● Functions of emphatic stress. ● Effect of stress on meaning. ● Correct pronunciation of stressed words. Assignment Write five sentences. For each sentence: 1. Stress two different words. 2. Explain how the meaning changes in each case. Example: I saw the doctor yesterday. ● I saw the doctor yesterday. ● I saw the DOCTOR yesterday. Explain the difference in meaning. Reference Materials 1. F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012). New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 2 . Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. 2. Banjo, A. et al. New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools . 3. Oral English for Senior Secondary Schools. 4. WAEC English Language Syllabus. 5. Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary.

title: STRUCTURE - PHRASAL VERBS
subject: English Language
rawText: STRUCTURE: Introduction to phrasal verbs Phrasal verbs are combination of a verb and an adverb or preposition used together to have a particular meaning. Phrasal verbs can have both literal or denotative meanings as well as idiomatic or connotative meaning. Phrasal Verb Literal/ Denotative Idiomatic/Connotative meaning meaning 1. Break down to stop functioning to start crying 2. Look up to look towards the sky to check for information 3. Speak out to talk clearly or audibly to state your complaints or needs 4. Take off to remove to go into the air 5. Put away to return something or to jail or put something Remove from sight in an enclosure Phrasal verbs with double particles meaning Come out with to say or produce something Keep up with to be at the same level with someone or something Keep hold of to hold tightly Get through to to be able to influence Get on with to make progress or continue to do something Look out for to care for someone for search for something Look up to to respect or advice Look forward to to expect something with excitement Assignment Answer the questions on page 160, exercise 3, from your class text.

title: ORAL COMPOSITION ON EXPOSITORY ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Speech: ORAL COMPOSITION ON EXPOSITORY ESSAY An expository essay is one in which the writer is expected to expose or explain a given topic. It aims at explaining and describing how something is done or how something works. For example students may be asked to write on how a particular machine or equipment works or how to prepare a particular meal. To write an essay of this nature, the writer must know enough about the topic as it is designated to inform and educate the readers. It has the following outline 1. Title 2. Introduction 3. Body of the essay 4. Conclusion How to write a good expository essay i. Content to discuss at length the topic you are asked to discuss. You are expected to unfold the bad and good consequence of the topic. You will earn a good mark if your content is well developed ii. Organization: there should be an introduction and conclusion. Your points or ideas must be fully developed in the body of the essay You are expected to arrange your pints or in a logical sequence Your sentences should be a variety of long and short sentences Make u7se of phrases or word linkers to link your paragraph with one another. The conclusion which must come after the body of the essay should briefly sum up the main ideas and make a conclusive statement on the topic. iii. Expression You must make sure that you state your facts, instances and points clearly Your vocabulary should be carefully chosen for effectiveness, especially when you are writing one topic that has a formal register. Your prose, clarity of expression is important Your language should be formal, you should avoid slangs, clichés, unidiomatic expression and meaningless phrases. The oral composition can be on any topic for example it could be on identifying the major causes and suggest ways to reduce road accidents. Paragraph (i) Introduction

What caused your article to be written (ii) First major cause of road accident (iii) Second major cause (iv) Suggestions on how to curb road accidents (v) Conclusion Assignment Write and discuss on “A friend in need is a friend indeed”. In not less than 350 words.

pages.text: Speech: ORAL COMPOSITION ON EXPOSITORY ESSAY An expository essay is one in which the writer is expected to expose or explain a given topic. It aims at explaining and describing how something is done or how something works. For example students may be asked to write on how a particular machine or equipment works or how to prepare a particular meal. To write an essay of this nature, the writer must know enough about the topic as it is designated to inform and educate the readers. It has the following outline 1. Title 2. Introduction 3. Body of the essay 4. Conclusion How to write a good expository essay i. Content to discuss at length the topic you are asked to discuss. You are expected to unfold the bad and good consequence of the topic. You will earn a good mark if your content is well developed ii. Organization: there should be an introduction and conclusion. Your points or ideas must be fully developed in the body of the essay You are expected to arrange your pints or in a logical sequence Your sentences should be a variety of long and short sentences Make u7se of phrases or word linkers to link your paragraph with one another. The conclusion which must come after the body of the essay should briefly sum up the main ideas and make a conclusive statement on the topic. iii. Expression You must make sure that you state your facts, instances and points clearly Your vocabulary should be carefully chosen for effectiveness, especially when you are writing one topic that has a formal register. Your prose, clarity of expression is important Your language should be formal, you should avoid slangs, clichés, unidiomatic expression and meaningless phrases. The oral composition can be on any topic for example it could be on identifying the major causes and suggest ways to reduce road accidents. Paragraph (i) Introduction

title: INTRODUCTION TO ACTIVE AND PASSIVE TENSES.
subject: English Language
rawText:
Structure: Introduction to Active and Passive A statement is in the active voice if the subject of the sentence performs the action. Examples The man killed the goat. Here the subject “the man” is the doer of the action Passive voice A statement is in the passive voice if the subject of the sentence does not perform any action. Here the subject is passive, the subject. Example. The goat was killed by the man. In changing a sentence from active to passive voice, care should be taken to maintain the tense. More samples of active and passive Active voice 1. Present simple tense The teacher owns a school Passive A school is owned by a teacher The boy rides a bicycle A bicycle is ridden by the boy 2. Present continuous tense Active We are eating pounded yam Passive Pounded yam is being eaten by us 3. Present perfect tense Active I have finished the job We have cancelled the match Passive The job has been finished The match has been cancelled by us. 4. Present perfect continuous tense That girl has been practicing the dance I have been buying clothes The dance has been being practiced by the girl Clothes has been being bought by me

5. Past simple tense I bought the book this morning A car hit the dog The book was bought by me this morning The dog was hit by a car 6. Past continuous tense You were washing your clothes I was riding a bicycle Your clothes were being washed by you A bicycle was being ridden by me 7. Past perfect tense We had finished the job The boy had climbed the stairs The job had been finished by us The stairs had been climbed by the boy 8. Past perfect continuous tense Tony had been jumping the fence He had been clearing the forest The fence had been being jumped by Tony The forest had been being cleared by him. 9. Simple future tense The boy will buy the books Emeka will visit me The books will be bought by the boy I will be visited by Emeka 10. The future continuous tense I shall be receiving lectures They will be buying the buckets Lectures shall be being received by me The bucket will be being bought by them Lectures shall be being received by me. Assignment Write out ten sentences showing the active and the passive tenses.

title: STRUCT. - ADJUNCTS OF PLACE AND TIME
subject: English Language
rawText: Structure: Adjunct of Place and Time Define adjunct: An adjunct is used to add extra information to a sentence which creates an extra meaning and makes the sentence more specific. Adjuncts are adverbs which answer the questions how, where, when, why, under what condition, to what degree, how often, for how long. Adjunct of time Adverb or adjunct of time answers the question when in relation to the verb in the main clause. Examples 1. I went to his house yesterday 2. He wants to see his wife now 3. He has been writing here since 4. He was admitted into the college last year 5. The interview is tomorrow 6. He will arrive Lagos at 4 pm 7. Tonight is the day we have been waiting for. 8. We shall set out by down 9. Day before yesterday was Sunday 10. Week after next is Christmas. Adjunct of place/direction It answers the question where? Examples: 1. The food is on the table 2. The girl in front is my cousin. 3. I met her first in Lagos 4. Police killed two students on the campus 5. The ugly incident happened in the middle of the road. 6. The baby is sleeping in the bedroom 7. I was in the office when my wife returned 8. The pretty girl in the corner there is my sister. 9. Ring me up at my office 10. I saw the man on the campus. Assignment Answer questions on exercise page 157 of the New Oxford English language for Senior Secondary Schools book 1.

title: STRUCT. - ADJUNCTS OF MANNER AND REASON
subject: English Language
rawText: Adjunct of manner and reason. Adjunct of manner The adjunct of manner shows how something is done. This adjunct answers the questions “how”. Examples of words used to illustrate manner: slowly, happily, in a hurry, sorrowfully, proudly, swiftly, sluggishly, roughly, badly, deeply, foolishly etc. Sentence samples 1. He embraced his son proudly 2. The job was done haphardly. 3. They hurriedly left the scene 4. The players performed badly yesterday The adjunct of reason tries to justify why an action is performed. This adjunct answers the question “why?” it is introduced by words like: because, since, as, in order to, so as to, in order that. Sentence samples 1. He married early because he is the only son. 2. She was sacked since she refused to apologized. 3. The student was sent home because he has not paid school fees. 4. He came late as he was held in a traffic jam. 5. The man left home so as to get there on time. 6. She worked hard in order that she will be promoted. Exercise Some words that show adjuncts of manner and reason for students to form sentence using them: humbly, sadly, beautiful, reluctantly, wickedly. Assignment Write “Adjunct of manner” or “adjunct of reason” for each of the following sentences. 1. He answered me rudely. 2. I will do it because of you 3. Since you lied to me, I will punish you 4. You must do the job quickly 5. They were absent because they travelled 6. She spends money extravagantly 7. We left in a hurry 8. He has to pay since he pleaded guilty 9. John was punished in order to teach others lesson 10. Funke studies hard so as to pass her examination.

title: SPEECH - DEBATE
subject: English Language
rawText: Speech: Debate on Issues of current interest The use of mobile phones should be abolished in secondary schools. A debate is an interactive and positive presentation in which two or more speakers present their argument persuading others to accept their points or views. It shows skills and ability in argument. Criteria for Debate 1. Timing: The debate must be within the time limit provided. 2. Presentation: The manner you adopt in communicating your ideas and information. For example a. Sufficient information relevant to the topic b. Sequence and orderly presentation c. Human elements used as examples 3. Accuracy of point: Your points must be acceptable facts supporting your point of view. 4. Elocution: Oral delivery which involves adequate control of voice, correct pronunciation and body movement or gesture. Guidelines for a Debate 1. State your vocatives 2. Define the content 3. Make sure you are convinced about the side you are opposing or supporting so that you don’t go out of points. 4. Do not draw a general conclusion from one example or a few points to reach a convincing conclusion. 5. Raise a few weak points supposedly by a member of the opposing side and oppose them with convincing argument. 6. Use polite language and also rhetorical questions to liven up your debate. 7. In strong term, urge your audience to toe your line or argument. 8. As you end, say thank you. Assignment You are the chief speaker in a debate on the topic “Technology has made the world a better place”. Write for or against the motion.

title: NOUN CLAUSE AND FUNCTIONS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Structure: NOUN CLAUSES AND FUNCTIONS A noun clause performs the same grammatical functions as nouns and noun phrase. These functions are: 1. Subject of the verb: examples a. How Sola passed the examination beats the imagination of her teachers. Function: Subject of the verb “beats” b. Why he has refused to put in his letter of resignation is best known to him Function: Subject of the verb is “known” 2. Subject Complement: example a. The good news is that he passed his ICAN examination. The underlined noun clause refers to the “good news”. A is the same thing as “the good news” 3. Object of verb: Examples a. The authority awarded what is termed punctuality award. Function: Object of the verb “awarded” b. The suspect eventually accepted that he was guilty. Function: Object of the verb “accepted” c. The human rights activist explained why he was arrested by the police. Function: Object of the verb “explained” 4. Object complement: Examples a. The authority gave the student what is termed award for excellence. Function: Complement of the object “student” b. The robber killed the man because he did not give them what they demanded for. Function: Complement of the object “them” c. We narrated to our colleagues how we survived the ordeal. Function: “Our colleagues” is the object of the verb narrated and the underlined noun clause complements the object our colleagues. 5. Complement of Preposition. Examples a. His action resulted into what his father predicted Function: Object of the preposition “into” b. The money was restricted from the man who stole it. Function: Object of the preposition “from” 6. In Apposition to a noun: A noun clause is in opposition to a noun when the noun clause and the noun refer to the same thing. Example The news, that I was missing, spread across the village. The noun clause “ that I was missing ” is in apposition to the noun “news”

Assignment Identify the grammatical name and functions of the capitalized words. 1] I believe THAT HE IS INNOCENT 2] WHAT SHE SAID made me happy 3] the truth is THAT HE LIED 4] we are interested in WHAT YOU ARE DOING. 5] she is worried about WHAT HE DID. Reference Essential English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Latilo T. A, et al.

title: ANTONYMS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Vocabulary Development: ANTONYMS OF WORDS: Words opposite in meaning. Antonym is a word which is the opposite in meaning of another word. It shows the relationship in contrast. Antonyms and their correct usage. It is important to note that context clues help in determining the appropriate meaning of any word. e.g. Mary is fair in complexion. The appropriate antonym for “fair” is “dark” and not “black” because there is no “black” complexion. Although, “black” is the antonym of “fair”, it does not apply in this context. Therefore one should choose antonyms or opposite of words by examining the contextual meaning. Antonyms can be formed in three ways a. By adding prefixes to the root word b. By changing suffix c. By changing a word entirely a. By adding prefix un – seen – unseen able – unable do – undo stable – unstable etc. im – possible – impossible moral – immoral pure – impure mortal – immortal in – visible – invisible discipline – indiscipline active – inactive audible – inaudible il – legal – illegal legitimate – illegitimate legible – illegible dis – able – disable courage – discourage

organize – disorganize unity – disunity b. By changing suffix. Examples Useful – useless careful – careless doubtful – doubtless needful – needless merciful – merciless c. By changing a word entirely to another word. deplete – replenish smooth – rough bold – timid temporary – permanent gently – roughly dead – alive float – sink always – never friendly – hostile cheap – expensive/costly d. Formation of antonyms by changing the prefix e.g. Ascend – Descend Export – Import External – Internal Prefix – Suffix Encourage – Discourage Construction – Destruction Prenatal – Postnatal Superior – Inferior Enthrone – Dethrone Renoun – Unknown Assignment Write out the antonyms of these words : humble, eager, considerate, extravagant, flattered. Reference Basic English Grammar for Schools and Colleges, by Chidinma C. Nduaguibe Complete English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe Ph.D.

title: SUMMARY WRITING - SUMMARIZING IN A SPECIFIED NUMBE
subject: English Language
rawText: SUMMARY: SUMMARISING A PASSAGE IN A SPECIFIED NUMBER OF SENTENCES Summary can be described as a shortened form of a long passage after removing all irrelevant ideas from the main points and giving a short account of the passage using your own words. To summarize a passage in a specified number of sentences demands that one should pay attention to the instruction on the number of sentences each questions requires. Some questions demands that you summarize in one, two, or three sentences. Ensure you write as instructed. A sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. THINGS TO NOTE FOR GOOD SUMMARY 1. Brevity: Your answer must be brief and straight to the point. No use of additional information apart from the main points. 2. Relevance: A candidate answer should be relevant to the points mentioned in the passage. 3. Clarity: This means that students are expected to put down their answers clearly. 4. Originality: Your answers should be written in your own words to avoid the error of mindless lifting. 5. Identify the topic sentences: The topic sentences are the main points in the paragraphs of the passage which are mostly found in the first or last sentence of a paragraph. 6. Write your answers in complete sentences CAUSES OF LOSS OF MARK IN SUMMARY WRITING 1. Mindless lifting of words from the passage. This means copying down the exact words and expressions of the writer. 2. Phrases and incomplete sentences. In summary, your answers should be written in complete sentences not in phrases. 3. Writing more than required number of sentences. 4. Grammatical/expression errors. 5. Wrong use of preamble or the introductory statement that does not flow with the sentences. Exercise Answer the summary questions in unit 7 of your class text i. In one sentence, what is the reason for the war in the passage? ii. In two sentences, one for each, explain the two types of war the writer feels could have made sense.

title: PHRASES
subject: English Language
rawText:
Week 3 English Language Notes TOPIC: PHRASES Subject Teacher: Mrs. Naadzenga Mgbede Grace Class: SS 1 A and B ENGLISH LANGUAGE (SS1) TOPIC: PHRASES (Definition, Types, and Differences Between Phrases and Clauses) 1. DEFINITION OF A PHRASE A phrase is a group of related words that work together but do not contain a finite verb and do not express a complete thought . A phrase can act as a noun, verb, adjective, or adverb in a sentence. A phrase cannot stand alone as a sentence. Examples: • in the morning • a bunch of keys • very happy • has been working 2. TYPES OF PHRASES There are five main types of phrases commonly taught at SS1 level. A. NOUN PHRASE (NP) A noun phrase has a noun or pronoun as its headword and may include modifiers such as adjectives, determiners, or prepositional phrases.

Structure: Determiner + Adjective(s) + Noun Examples: • the tall boy • my new school bag • a basket of mangoes In a sentence: The tall boy won the race. B. VERB PHRASE (VP) A verb phrase consists of a main verb and its auxiliary (helping) verbs . Examples: • is running • has eaten • will be going In a sentence: She has finished her homework. C. ADJECTIVE PHRASE (AdjP) An adjective phrase describes a noun and may include adverbs that modify the adjective. Examples: • very intelligent • extremely tall • full of joy In a sentence: She is very intelligent . D. ADVERBIAL PHRASE (AdvP) An adverbial phrase modifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. It tells how, when, where, or to what extent .

Examples: • very quickly • quite early • too slowly In a sentence: He ran very quickly . E. PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE (PP) A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition and ends with an object (noun or pronoun) . Structure: Preposition + Object Examples: • in the classroom • under the table • beside the road In a sentence: The book is on the desk . 3. FUNCTIONS OF PHRASES IN SENTENCES A phrase can function as: • Subject – The little boy is crying. • Object – She bought a new dress . • Complement – He is very tired . • Modifier – The boy with the cap is my friend. 4. DIFFERENCES BETWEEN PHRASES AND CLAUSES Feature Phrase Clause Contains a subject ❌ No ✅ Yes

Feature Phrase Clause Contains a finite verb ❌ No ✅ Yes Expresses complete meaning ❌ No Sometimes Can stand alone as a sentence ❌ No ✅ (if independent) Example in the house when he arrived 5. WHAT IS A CLAUSE? (For Comparison) A clause is a group of words that contains both a subject and a finite verb . Examples: • She is reading. • because he was late • when the bell rang 6. PHRASE vs CLAUSE (EXAMPLES) Phrase Clause after the match after the match ended a beautiful girl the girl is beautiful in the classroom they are in the classroom 7. SUMMARY • A phrase is a group of words without a finite verb . • A clause has a subject and a finite verb . • Phrases help to add meaning and detail to sentences. • Common phrase types include noun, verb, adjective, adverbial, and prepositional phrases . 8. EVALUATION / CLASS EXERCISE

1. Identify the type of phrase in each sentence: a. She wore a beautiful dress . b. The boys ran very fast . c. The cat is under the table . 2. State whether the underlined group of words is a phrase or a clause : a. when the rain stopped b. in the evening

It tells how, when, where, or to what extent .

Examples: • very quickly • quite early • too slowly In a sentence: He ran very quickly . E. PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE (PP) A prepositional phrase begins with a preposition and ends with an object (noun or pronoun) . Structure: Preposition + Object Examples: • in the classroom • under the table • beside the road In a sentence: The book is on the desk . 3. FUNCTIONS OF PHRASES IN SENTENCES A phrase can function as: • Subject – The little boy is crying. • Object – She bought a new dress . • Complement – He is very tired . • Modifier – The boy with the cap is my friend. 4. DIFFERENCES BETWEEN PHRASES AND CLAUSES Feature Phrase Clause Contains a subject ❌ No ✅ Yes

Feature Phrase Clause Contains a finite verb ❌ No ✅ Yes Expresses complete meaning ❌ No Sometimes Can stand alone as a sentence ❌ No ✅ (if independent) Example in the house when he arrived 5. WHAT IS A CLAUSE? (For Comparison) A clause is a group of words that contains both a subject and a finite verb . Examples: • She is reading. • because he was late • when the bell rang 6. PHRASE vs CLAUSE (EXAMPLES) Phrase Clause after the match after the match ended a beautiful girl the girl is beautiful in the classroom they are in the classroom 7. SUMMARY • A phrase is a group of words without a finite verb . • A clause has a subject and a finite verb . • Phrases help to add meaning and detail to sentences. • Common phrase types include noun, verb, adjective, adverbial, and prepositional phrases . 8. EVALUATION / CLASS EXERCISE

1. Identify the type of phrase in each sentence: a. She wore a beautiful dress . b. The boys ran very fast . c. The cat is under the table . 2. State whether the underlined group of words is a phrase or a clause : a. when the rain stopped b. in the evening

title: SPEECH - THREE SYLLABLE WORDS WITH STRESS
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH: WORDS OF THREE SYLLABLES STRESSED ON THE 2ND SYLLABLE Stress is the degree of force by which a word is pronounced. Words are broken into tiny units called syllables. A syllable is the pronounced unit of a word. It is on a syllable that stress is placed. Stressing a syllable therefore means giving it more force, such that it is louder, longer and higher in pitch than other syllables. A stressed syllable like in the dictionary is indicated by placing a stroke at the beginning of the syllable, but here, a stressed syllable should be written in capital letters. THREE SYLLABLE WORDS Three syllable words are parts of polysyllable words which have their different stress patterns with some guiding rules. These rules help us to identify when to stress the word on the first, second, third or fourth syllable. For three syllable words stressed on the second syllable, the rule guiding it says a. Stress the second syllable from the end of a word if it ends in : - cient, - ion, - ic, - ial, - ian. Examples suf-FI-cient ef- FI-cient ic stra-TE-gic dra-MA-tic -ion o-CCA-sion pro-JEC-tion dis-CU-ssion con-VIC-tion in-JEC-tion star-VA-tion con-VER-sion con-STRUC-tion fru-STRA-tion o-VA-tion -ial co-LO-nial

of-FI-cial com-MER-cial -ian ci-VI-lian Examples of the three syllable words in a sentence 1. The fru-STRA-tion in that job is too much 2. She is at the venue for col-LA-tion of results 3. The people in overalls are con-STRUC-tion workers 4. Something dra-MA-tic happened yesterday 5. I am a ci-VI-lian not a soldier Assignment Mention ten (10) words of three syllables stressed on the 2nd syllable

title: READING COMPREHENSION 1
subject: English Language
rawText: READING COMPREHENSION Passage: The Importance of Reading Reading is one of the most important skills a student can develop. It helps learners to improve their vocabulary, spelling, and understanding of English. A student who reads regularly finds it easier to understand lessons taught in class and performs better in examinations. Reading also exposes students to new ideas and cultures. Through books, newspapers, and magazines, learners gain knowledge about events happening around the world. This knowledge helps them to think critically and express their opinions clearly. In addition, reading builds confidence. When students read often, they become familiar with different sentence structures and correct usage of words. This makes it easier for them to speak and write good English. Reading can also be enjoyable, especially when students choose books that interest them. In conclusion, reading is not only for passing examinations but also for personal development. Every student should develop the habit of reading daily to become successful in school and life. Comprehension Questions 1. According to the passage, why is reading important to students? 2. Mention two ways reading helps students in school. 3. What does reading expose students to? 4. How does reading build confidence in students? 5. Suggest a suitable title for the passage. Answers 1. Reading is important because it improves vocabulary, understanding of English, and academic performance. 2. It helps students understand lessons better and perform well in examinations. 3. Reading exposes students to new ideas, cultures, and world events. 4. It helps students become familiar with correct sentence structures and word usage. 5. The Importance of Reading .

title: CON. WRITING - NARRATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText: WEEK TWO Speech: Oral Composition: Narrative Essay A narrative essay is a story, a tale, or an account of something that has happened and which one is telling to another person. It may be factual (true account) of what really happened or imaginary (made up by the narrator) Topics related to narrative 1. How I spent my last holiday 2. How I escaped being kidnapped 3. Story that illustrate the saying “It pays to be discipline. 4. Story that illustrate the saying “a stitch in time saves nine”. Features of good narrative essay 1. Title: It should have a good captivating and relevant to the event narrated 2. Introduction: It should have a good and interesting beginning 3. The body: It should have few characters that can be effectively handled. 4. Such essay must be written in the past tense. Note: for a good narrative essay, the following should be answered. a. What is the story about? b. What actions took place in your story? c. Who were responsible for those actions d. When did the action take place? e. How did the action happen? f. What were the consequences? Assignment In not less than 450 words, write a story that illustrate “a stitch in time saves nine or prevention is better than cure.

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH MEDICINE.
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Vocabulary. Week: One. Date: Class: SS 1. Period …………………………………… .. Time: Duration: Unit topic: Vocabulary. Lesson topic: Words Associated with Medicine. Specific (behavioural) objective : at the end of the lesson, students should be able to: a) Briefly explain what health means. b) List at least five words associated with health. c) Briefly explain the meaning of those words. d) Use those words to form sentences. Instructional resource: syringe, needle, drugs. Thermometer, lab coat Lesson presentation Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR KNOWLEDGE. Teacher asks students on what they understand about the day’s lesson topic. Mode: individual. Teacher’s activities: teacher asks students the following questions: a) What do you understand about medicine? b) Can you mention any words associated with medicine? c) Where do we go when we get sick? Students’ activities: students respond to the questions asked based on their knowledge of the topic. Step 2: EXPLORATION. Mode: entire class.

Teacher’s activities: teacher briefly explains to the students what health means and differentiates between good health and ill health; as well as mentioning things to do to stay healthy: What is medicine? The science and practice of the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease. Students’ activities: the students listen, repeat after the teacher loudly and answer the class activity in their notebook. Step 3 : DISCUSSION. The teacher gives room to the students to list and state the functions of words associated with health. Mode: individual. Teacher’s activities: the teacher guides the students to list and state the functions of words associated with health. Words associated with heath, meaning and usage. S/no Words Meaning Usage in sentence 1 Cold A viral upper respiratory tract infection. I am catching cold. 2 Headache A symptom of pain anywhere in the region of the head or neck. Headache is one of the symptoms of fever. 3 Infections The invasion of organism’s body by disease-causing agents. She suffers from toilet infections. 4 Pains The physical feeling caused by disease, injury or something that hurts the body. I have pains in my legs. 5 Bruise A common skin injury that results in a discoloration of the skin. His father secured some bruises from the accident. 6 Wound An injury to living tissue caused by a cut, blow or other impact. Her arm got wounded during the fight. 7 Heart attack A serious medical emergency in which the supply of blood to the heart is suddenly blocked, usually by a blood cut. She survived the heartattack. 8 Meningitis An inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord. The child has been vaccinated against meningitis.

9 Medicine The science and practice of the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of disease. The man prefers treatment with traditional medicine to English medicine. 10 Drugs Any substance (other than food that provides nutritional support) that, when inhaled, injected, smoked, consumed, absorbed via a patch on the skin or dissolved under the tongue causes a physiological change in the body. Amina don’t like taking drugs whenever she takes ill. 11 Injection An act of putting a liquid, especially drug, into a person’s body using a needle and a syringe. He is scared of injection. 12 Tranquillizers A drug that introduces tranquility in a person and other animals. She took some tranquillizers to enable her sleep after days of sleeplessness. 13 Operation 14 Doctor A person who is trained in the science of medicine or a person who has been licensed to treat sick people, etc. His mother is a doctor. 15 Nurse A person who is trained to give care who are sick or injured. His father is a nurse. 16 Dentist An oral health doctor who is trained to diagnose, treat and prevent oral diseases, promote oral health, etc. He is dentist. 17 Midwife A person, typically a woman, who is trained to assist women in childbirth. Egyptian’s midwives feared God. 18 Surgeon A doctor who performs surgical operations. I want to be a surgeon. 19 Hospital A heath care institution providing patient treatment with specialized medical and nursing staff and medical equipment My father owns a hospital. [ Students’ activities: the students list and mention the functions of words associate with health. Step 4: APPLICATION. Mode: entire class. Teacher’s activities: the teacher engages the students in a class activity by taking them through the exercise below:

Class activity Make one sentence each with the following words associated with health: a) Health centre. b) Ward. c) Stretcher. d) X-ray. e) Test. Students’ activities: students carry out the class activity in their note books. Step 5: EVALUATION. Mode: individual. Teacher’s activities: the teacher asks students the following questions: a) Briefly explain what medicine. b) List five (5) associated with health. c) State the meaning of those Words d) Form a sentence with each of the words . Students’ activities: the students respond to the questions asked. ASSIGNMENT : students are to carry out the exercise on page 33 (health and healthcare). REFERENCE MATERIALS. title: STRUC. - PHRASAL VERBS
subject: English Language
rawText: STRUCTURE: Introduction to phrasal verbs Phrasal verbs are combination of a verb and an adverb or preposition used together to have a particular meaning. Phrasal verbs can have both literal or denotative meanings as well as idiomatic or connotative meaning. Phrasal Verb Literal/ Denotative Idiomatic/Connotative meaning meaning 1. Break down to stop functioning to start crying 2. Look up to look towards the sky to check for information 3. Speak out to talk clearly or audibly to state your complaints or needs 4. Take off to remove to go into the air 5. Put away to return something or to jail or put something Remove from sight in an enclosure Phrasal verbs with double particles meaning Come out with to say or produce something Keep up with to be at the same level with someone or something Keep hold of to hold tightly Get through to to be able to influence Get on with to make progress or continue to do something Look out for to care for someone for search for something Look up to to respect or advice Look forward to to expect something with Excitement Assignment Write out ten phrasal verbs with their meanings and form sentences with them.

title: CONT. WRITING - COMPOSITION ON ARTICLE WRITING.
subject: English Language
rawText: Continuous Writing – Composition on Article Writing An article is a complete piece of writing on an issue of public interest. It usually contains views or opinions of its writer on a specific issue or topic. USEFUL HINTS ON HOW TO WRITE A GOOD ARTICLE. 1. Content: The content depends on the topic you are asked to write on, but you must write on all aspect of the question or topic to earn a good mark. Your points must be relevant to the question or topic. 2. Organization a. Writing an article is not the same as writing a letter to the editor of a newspaper. You are not expected to write a letter to the editor when you are asked to write an article for publication in a newspaper or magazine. b. You are expected to write the title of the article clearly on top of the article. c. You are expected to write an introductory paragraph in which you are to give your readers an insight to your topic. d. Consider the interest of your reader also and the effect you want to create on the readers. e. Present your points in a logical order and develop your paragraphs adequately. f. Write your name and class below at the end of your article, if it is for a school magazine. But if it is for a national newspaper or magazine, you write your name and the name of the town you are writing from. 3. Expression a. Your language should be formed since you are writing an article for publication in a newspaper or magazine b. Topics for article calls for expository prose and clarity of expression. write in simple, straight – forward sentences and avoid using slangs c. Your vocabulary should be carefully chosen for effectiveness Assignment Write an article meant for publication in one of the national newspapers on the Dangers of vandalizing petroleum pipelines in your country

title: CONT. WRITING - CREATIVE WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Continuous writing: Creative Writing Creative writing refers to the literary work produced by a student himself. It can be a short story, a drama piece or a poem. A question like “write a story which ends with the saying “one good turn deserves another”. “All that glitters is not gold” “oh had I known” demands a short story writing. Short stories are meant to be centered around proverbial themes. Here, you are required to weave a story that would illustrate the truth of the proverb. Features of a short story. 1. Theme: A short story must have a central point from which a story is developed. Examples “A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush”. Uneasy lies the head that wears the crown. 2. Plot: It must have a storyline. This means the order the story follows to develop the theme. The plot of a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush must feature a good character that uses opportunity as it comes to better life other than waiting for an opportunity that he has not seen or loosing an opportunity he has because of the one he has not seen. 3. title: STRUCTURE - PHRASES AND TYPES
subject: English Language
rawText:
STRUCTURE - PHRASES TYPES OF PHRASES A phrase is a group of words that do not contain a finite verb. A phrase cannot stand on its own to make meaning. It only forms part of a sentence. Types of phrases 1. Noun phrase: This is the phrase that does the work of a noun or pronoun in a sentence. Example: a. John the driver is dead. b. The big ugly girl is quarrelsome. 2. Adjectival phrase: This is the phrase that describes a noun or a pronoun in a sentence. Examples: a. The coat made of cotton is very lovely. b. The girl with dirty hands ate the food. 3. Adverbial phrase: this is the phrase that modifies a verb in a sentence. It answers the question “why, where, when, how? e tc. Examples: a. The head boy lives near the church. b. The old man walked slowly across the road. 4. Prepositional phrase: This is a phrase that begins with a preposition. Examples a. Sani was beaten with a cane. b. The woman drowned in the river. Identification of phrases 1. If the verbs in the expression given is preceded by ‘to’ that verb is no n-finite, therefore the expression is a phrase. Example a. He is always ready to fight anybody. b. To pass examination involves hard work. 2. If the verb in the expression functions as an adjective, it is a non-finite verb and therefore the expression becomes a phrase. Example a. I have boiled yam in my pot. b. He has replaced the broken bottle. 3. If the verb in the expression is in the ‘ - ing’ form, the verb is no n-finite and the expression becomes a phrase. Example a. I saw the boy going to the library. b. Eating supper late is what I don’t like . 4. If the expression underlined in the sentence cannot make meaning when standing alone. Example a. She is sleeping in the room. b. They are standing outside the gate. Assignment

Write out ten sentences to show the types of phrases you have been taught, underline such phrases.
