title: CONT. WRITING - DEBATE
subject: English Language
rawText: TOPIC 4: CONTINUOUS WRITING : DEBATE A debate is an argument between two persons or group of persons over an issue or a topic. It is an argumentative essay where the writer is expected to argue logically in support or against a topic. It aims at convincing the audience or the reader to share the opinion or view points of the writer. A debate could be written or delivered orally. FEATURES/FORMAT OF A DEBATE 1. The Topic: The topic should be clearly stated and should be underlined if written in small letters 2. The Vocatives: This is the greetings to acknowledge the presence of the members of the panel and the audience. Examples: The Moderator/Chairman, Panel of Judges, Accurate Time Keeper, Co-Debaters, Fellow Students/The audience 3. The Introduction: The speaker/writer is expected to introduce himself (if it is oral debate) .State the topic and take a stand whether in support or against the motion. The key words in the topic could be defined, quoting from a reliable source. 4. The Body: The speaker/writer should state at least three strong points in favour of his stand to persuade the judges and win them to his side. Also a paragraph should have one point well explained. It is good to counter the opinion of the opponent with good reasons. 5. The Conclusion: Summarize the points raised to re-affirm your position earlier taken by stating that your view points are better than your opponent. CLASS ACTIVITY You are the Chief speaker representing your school on a debate topic. Technology has done more harm than good. Write in support or against the topic. This should be not less than 450 words.

title: ADJECTIVAL CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText: Structure: Adjectival Clause An adjectival or relative clause: Is a subordinate clause that performs the function of an adjective. It describes or tells more about a noun or pronoun. The following subordinating conjunctions usually introduce adjectival clause : who, whom, whose, that, which, where, when. This qualifies the noun or pronoun that precedes it in a sentence. Examples i. I released the project to somebody who appears to be reasonable in the class. Function qualifies the pronoun “somebody” ii. It was he who slapped me. Who slapped me” qualifies the pronoun “he” iii. The landlord whose house was burgled has reported to the police. Function: It qualifies the noun “landlord” iv. The lady whose car was stolen is crying Function: It qualifies the noun “lady” v. The dress which my husband bought for me suits my shape. Function: It qualifies noun “dress” vi. The house which has been renovated looks very new. Function: It qualifies the noun “house” vii. The government ha equipped the hospital where the renowned doctor works. Function: It qualifies the noun “hospital” viii. She has visited the place where he was born. Function: It qualifies the noun “places” ix. The teacher gave a specific time when he would meet with the students. Function: It qualifies the noun “time” x. He does not remember the day when he was born. Function: It qualifies the noun “day” Assignment Identify and underline the adjectival clause in the following sentences and state their functions 1. The car that was stolen has been found 2. That is the goat that ate my yams 3. The woman whose husband bought a new house has won the election. 4. The government has equipped he hospital where the renowned doctor works 5. The teacher gave a specific time when he would meet with the students.

rawText: COMPREHENSION READING PASSAGE FOR WORD TOPIC 3: MEANING IN CONTEXT OR READING FOR CONTEXUAL MEANING Contexual meaning of a word is the meaning of a word in relation to other words in the sentence. As we read a given passage, we come across some difficult words whose meanings we do not know. However, the surrounding words can help one understand the meaning. Therefore, the meaning of such word ceases to depend on the single word but takes into consideration the context or the situation in which the word is used. Example 1. Our get-together comes by the month of August (month of the year) 2. I am expecting an august visitor (important visitor) Uses Contextual meanings are required in answering a comprehension questions that demand finding another word or phrase that means the same and can replace as used in the passage. title: STRUCTURE - CLAUSES : DEPENDENT AND INDEPENDENT
subject: English Language
rawText: Structure- CLAUSES – DEPENDENT INDEPENDENT A clause is a group of words with a finite verb, forming part of the sentence. Note: the major difference between the phrase and the clause is the finite and non-finite forms of the verb. Therefore, if the verb in the expression given does not have any of the characteristics of a non- finite verb, in phrase, the expression should be considered a clause. There are two types of clauses – main or independent clause and subordinate or dependent clause. a. The main clause: This can stand on its own to make a complete sense or sentence e.g. I am going home now The choir came and ministered b. Subordinate clause: Before the teacher arrived, the students were seriously fighting. The three types of clauses: Noun, Adjectival / Relative and Adverbial clauses i. It is a group of words ii. It always has a finite verb iii. It does not express a complete thought; it needs the main clause to make it complete sense or sentence. iv. It only forms part of the sentence. e.g of subordinate clauses are a. As soon as the boy saw the teacher, he took his heels b. Unless he passes the examination, he will not travel abroad. c. The landlord whose house was burgled has reported to the police d. How he knew my name still remains a mystery. e. Exercise: underline the dependent clauses 1. As soon as the bell rang, all the students ran to their various classes. 2. We bought the land which he sold. 3. They have not been in school since we resumed 4. When the police arrived, the students were seriously fighting

title: STRUCTURE - ADVERBIAL CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Structure: Adverbial clause An adverbial clause tells us more about the action of the verb in the main clause. It tells us when, how, where, to what extent, under what condition the action in the main clause takes place. Types of Adverbial clause The type of adverbial information supplied on the verb is the basis for naming adverbial clauses. A. Adverbial clause of time: This tells us when the action of the main verb takes place. It is usually introduced by while, when, whenever, before, until, after, since as soon as. Examples While watching the television news I saw the boy being interviewed Before you start answering the questions, read the instructions B. Adverbial Clause of reason: This state why the action of the main clause takes place. It is usually introduced by as, since, because. Examples He succeeded in the interview because he prepared for it. We left his office since he was not ready to pay us. C. Adverbial clause of purpose: It shows the motive behind the action of the main clause. It is usually introduced by so that, in order that. Examples I gave him the money so that he could buy the goods in order that peace will reign he was released. D. Adverbial clause of concession: Clauses of concession indicates that what happens in main clause is contrary to what one expects in the light of the information in the subordinate clause. They are introduced by although, though, if, even if, even though, when, whereas, while, despite, inspite of, irrespective of, regardless of, notwithstanding. Examples Although he is poor, he is very intelligent. She is very pretty even if she is dark in complexion E. Adverbial clause of place: It tells us where the action of the main verb takes place. It is often introduced by wherever, where, anywhere, etc. Examples Anywhere you go, I will follow you Children can play wherever they like F. Adverbial clause of manner. It tells us how the action of the main verb is performed. It is introduced by as, though, as if Examples. She was crying as if somebody died The man was talking as if he owns the whole world. G. Adverbial clause of result: It shows the outcome of the action of the man verb. It is usually introduced by so, therefore, so that, as a result, hence. Examples I worked so hard, that I had a breakdown I took the umbrella so that rain will not beat me

H. Adverbial clause of condition: This states the condition necessary for the action of the main verb to take place. It is usually introduced by; on condition that, if, unless, while, provided, as long as. Examples I will go for the party if they invite me I will not leave you, unless you bless me.

title: ORAL ARGUMENT/DEBATE.
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Speech Week: ............. Date: …………………, 2026. Class: SS 1 Period: …………... Time: ……………………. Duration: …………. Subject: English Language Unit topic: Speech Lesson topic: Oral Argument/Debate. Specific (behavioural) objectives : At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: i. Briefly explain what debate is. ii. Identify the structure of a debate. iii. Identify the current trends in debate. iv. Make (write) debate on a chosen topic. Instructional resource: a banner showing opening greeting (vocatives). Lesson presentation Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS. Teacher asks students on what they understand about the day’s lesson topic. Mode: a couple of students. Teacher’s activities: teacher asks students the following questions: i. What is a debate? ii. How would recognize a debate question? iii. List three rules guiding debate. iv. Can you mention one new trend in debate? Students’ activities: students respond to the questions asked based on their knowledge of the topic. Step 2: EXPLORATION. Mode: entire class. Teacher’s activities: Teacher guides the students to explain what debate is and cite an example of a debate question. What a debate? Debate is an argument that is orally presented. In other words, debate is an oral argument.

Example of debate question includes, “It is better to attend the school that is near your environment than the one outside your environment.” Students’ activities: the students listen and read a passage. Step 3 : DISCUSSION. Mode: entire class. Teacher’s activities: the teacher guides the students to identify the structure of a debate and the new trends in debate. The structure of a debate The following is the structure of a debate: 1) Introduction (one paragraph): (a) Opening greetings (vocatives): study your environment to know those present and greet them appropriately: example, Mr. Chairman, Panel of Judges, the Moderator, Accurate Time Keeper, Co-debaters, My Fellow Students, Ladies and Gentlemen. (b) Introduce yourself: example, my name is Abiola Abiodun. (c) Mention your stand in the motion you are debating on. Example, I am here to propose the motion that states, “It is better to attend school that is near your environment than the one outside of your environment” with the following points backing up my argument. (d) Define key words if necessary. Example, before I proceed, permit me to define some key words, … 2) The body paragraph (three paragraphs). The body provides detail in support of your stand in the argument: (a) Give your reasons to support your stand. (b) Counter your opponent’s points. Imagine the points your opponent is like to raise. Raise each of these points and tell your audience that it is wrong, you can then go ahead and place your opinions upon the one you have disapproved. Example, some people may say, without doctors sick people will die because there will be none to treat them medically. But if l may ask, will there be doctors without teachers, in fact, the greatest sickness in life is ignorant, which can only be cured by teachers and not doctors … 3) The conclusion (one paragraph). This should comprise the following: (a) Call on all present by their names. Example, the Chairman, Distinguished Guests, Fellow Students, Ladies and Gentlemen, and (b) Conclude by saying, I believe with these points of mine, you will agree with me that “It is better to attend the school that is near your environment than the one outside your environment.” Thank you.

New trends (parliamentary) in debate Co-debater - Friends in argument. I am here to support the motion that states – in this house we agree that … I am here to oppose the motion that states – in this house we disagree that … You can raise point of information. You can use newspaper (or any literature) and electronic devices like projector to support your argument. Students’ activities: students listen attentively, participate in the discussion and take note. Step 4: APPLICATION. Mode: group. Teacher’s activities: Teacher guides the students to explain what debate is and cite an example of a debate question. What a debate? Debate is an argument that is orally presented. In other words, debate is an oral argument.

Example of debate question includes, “It is better to attend the school that is near your environment than the one outside your environment.” Students’ activities: the students listen and read a passage. Step 3 : DISCUSSION. Mode: entire class. Teacher’s activities: the teacher guides the students to identify the structure of a debate and the new trends in debate. The structure of a debate The following is the structure of a debate: 1) Introduction (one paragraph): (a) Opening greetings (vocatives): study your environment to know those present and greet them appropriately: example, Mr. Chairman, Panel of Judges, the Moderator, Accurate Time Keeper, Co-debaters, My Fellow Students, Ladies and Gentlemen. (b) Introduce yourself: example, my name is Abiola Abiodun. (c) Mention your stand in the motion you are debating on. Example, I am here to propose the motion that states, “It is better to attend school that is near your environment than the one outside of your environment” with the following points backing up my argument. (d) Define key words if necessary. Example, before I proceed, permit me to define some key words, … 2) The body paragraph (three paragraphs). The body provides detail in support of your stand in the argument: (a) Give your reasons to support your stand. (b) Counter your opponent’s points. Imagine the points your opponent is like to raise. Raise each of these points and tell your audience that it is wrong, you can then go ahead and place your opinions upon the one you have disapproved. Example, some people may say, without doctors sick people will die because there will be none to treat them medically. But if l may ask, will there be doctors without teachers, in fact, the greatest sickness in life is ignorant, which can only be cured by teachers and not doctors … 3) The conclusion (one paragraph). This should comprise the following: (a) Call on all present by their names. Example, the Chairman, Distinguished Guests, Fellow Students, Ladies and Gentlemen, and (b) Conclude by saying, I believe with these points of mine, you will agree with me that “It is better to attend the school that is near your environment than the one outside your environment.” Thank you.

title: SUMMARY WRITING - INTRODUCTION TO SUMMARY
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- SUMMARY UNIT TOPIC:- SUMMARY WRITING LESSON TOPIC:- IDENTIFYING KEY WORDS THAT AID SUMMARY OF SPEECHES AND LECTURES. TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES :-At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to….. 1) explain summary writing 2) identify and explain the qualities of good summary writing. 3) read the given passage correctly 4) answer summary questions from the passage. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES:- A cardboard paper containing a paragraph where a topic sentence is underlined; passage from students ’ text book. PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to explain what they understand by main ideas. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question that the main idea in a passage is the subject matter. It is the nucleus. The chief point the writer is making. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to give the synonym for the word ‘brevity’ STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resource guides the students on the following: Summary expresses in few words what has been said in very many words. It calls for brevity, ie being brief. Summary involves writing down a brief and concise account of long passage. In other words, it can be described as a shortened form of a long passage after removing all irrelevant points from the main points and giving a short account of the passage using your own words. A topic sentence contains the main idea in a paragraph. Usually but not always the topic sentence in the first sentence in the paragraph. The topic sentence gives a

sense of direction, directing the attention of the reader to what is to be discussed in a particular paragraph. USING HINTS USED IN ANSWERING SUMMARY QUESTIONS INCLUDE: a) In summary questions, there is no room for examples, repetition and illustrations. b) Analogy and flowery language (ie figures of speech) have no place in summary writing. c) The use of link words or connectives is not part of summary writing eg . Also, moreover, however, furthermore etc. d) Use a preamble which when read together with the numbered points would makes complete sentence. e) Write one sentence for each point f) Avoid any grammatical or expression error in each sentence. g) Do not lift word for word from the passage. h) Use roman figure in numbering. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students read through a passage and identify the topic sentences in each paragraph. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to use the main points and the hints given to answer the summary questions STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the topic with the following question; 1) What do you understand by summary? 2) What are the useful hints used in answering a summary question? 3) What is a topic sentence? 4) Do exercise 1 page 22 of your class text book on summary writing. ASSIGNMENT Do exercise 1 page 22 of your class text book on summary writing. REFERENCES: 1) New Concept English bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) Complete English Course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011) 3) Essentials of English by Latilo T. A et al (2008) 4) Oxford Advanced Dictionary of English 7 th edition.

title: POLITICS
subject: English Language
rawText: VOCABULARY: POLITICS Politics is the process of making collective decisions, managing public affairs, and exercising power within a society or group. It involves negotiations, conflict resolution, and the allocation of resources. Nigeria has practiced the presidential democracy where the president has executive powers. In order to eliminate despotism, there are checks and balances through the exercise of power by the judiciary and the legislature. The member of the legislative houses and the president are duly elected during the general elections. Some relevant words are Ballot – box: Box into which voters put their ballot – papers. Constituency: Voters in an area or district democracy government that is run by all the people, directly or through representatives. Despot: Ruler who does what he likes and oppress people Nomination: Act of naming a candidate for a post or office Political party: Group of persons or an association formed for the purpose of practicing politics Voting age: Minimum age at which one is eligible to vote. Enfranchise: One’s right to vote in election Electoral college: Group of people who have already been voted in as members of the house, who now may vote in the presidential election. Form sentences with some of the words that are associated with Politics. Assignment Write out ten more words that are associated with Politics and their meanings.

title: CONSONANT SOUNDS FOLLOWED BY /KW/
subject: English Language
rawText: Consonant Sound followed by /kw/ Consonant Sound /kw/ The sound /kw/ is a consonant blend made up of /k/ + /w/ . It is commonly represented in spelling by “qu” . Examples of Words with /kw/ • queen /kwiːn/ quick /kwɪk/ quiet /ˈkwaɪət/ question /ˈkwestʃən/ • quarter /ˈkwɔːtə/ quality /ˈkwɒlɪti/ quantity /ˈkwɒntɪti/ quarrel /ˈkwɒrəl/ • quench /kwentʃ/ Words Showing /kw/ Clearly at the Beginning • quake quilt quit quiz quack Note • In most English words, “qu” = /kw/ • Exception: queue , unique (do not have /kw/ sound) Class Exercise 1. Underline the /kw/ sound in the following words: quick, quality, queen, quiet, quarrel 2. Use three /kw/ words in sentences.

title: ORAL COMPOSITION (STORY NARRATION)
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN: ORAL COMPOSITION (STORY NARRATION) Theme: Speech Topic: Oral Composition (Story Narration) Class: SS 1 Duration: 40 Minutes Date: ____________________ Period: __________________ Week: ___________________ Specific Behavioural Objectives By the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Explain the meaning of story narration. 2. Identify the elements of a good story. 3. Narrate a simple story clearly and logically. 4. Use appropriate voice modulation, facial expressions, and gestures while narrating. 5. Demonstrate confidence in oral storytelling. Instructional Materials ● Picture cards ● Story prompts ● Whiteboard/Chalkboard ● Flashcards showing story elements ● Audio recording of a story (optional) Previous Knowledge Students are familiar with informal storytelling such as folktales, personal experiences, and family stories. Teaching Method ● Inquiry-Based Learning (IBL) ● Discussion Method ● Demonstration Method ● Oral Presentation

LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: Set Induction (Engage) – 5 Minutes Teacher's Activities ● Asks students: ○ Have you ever told a story to your friends or family? ○ What made them enjoy your story? ○ What makes a story boring? ● Narrates a short interesting story. ● Asks: ○ What made the story interesting? ○ How was the story organized? Students' Activities ● Respond to questions. ● Listen attentively. ● Suggest features that make stories enjoyable. Step 2: Exploration (Discovering the Concept) – 10 Minutes Teacher's Activities ● Guides students to discover the meaning of story narration through discussion. ● Records students' responses on the board. Meaning of Story Narration Story narration is the act of telling a story orally in a clear, orderly, and interesting manner. Students' Activities ● Participate in discussion. ● Suggest meanings based on prior experiences. ● Take notes. Step 3: Discussion and Explanation – 15 Minutes Elements of a Good Story

Teacher guides students to identify and explain: 1. Characters – The people or animals involved. 2. Setting – The place and time of the story. 3. Plot – The sequence of events. 4. Conflict – The problem encountered. 5. Resolution – The solution to the problem. 6. Moral Lesson – The message learned. Features of Good Oral Narration 1. Clear voice. 2. Correct pronunciation. 3. Logical sequence of events. 4. Appropriate facial expressions. 5. Suitable gestures. 6. Eye contact with the audience. 7. Confidence and fluency. Step 4: Teacher's Model Story Topic: Honesty Pays One day, a boy named Tunde found a wallet on his way to school. He looked around to see if anyone had dropped it, but there was no one nearby. Curious, he opened the wallet and saw a large amount of money along with an identity card. For a moment, Tunde was tempted to keep the money. He thought about all the things he could buy. However, he remembered what his parents had taught him about honesty. He decided to do the right thing. When he got to school, he took the wallet to his class teacher and explained how he found it. The teacher checked the identity card and contacted the owner, who turned out to be a trader in the community. Later that day, the owner came to the school looking worried. When he saw his wallet, he became very happy. He thanked Tunde sincerely and offered him a reward, but Tunde politely refused. The teacher praised Tunde before the whole school for his honesty. From that day onward, he became a role model to other students. Moral Lesson: Honesty pays.

Teacher Demonstrates ● Voice variation. ● Proper pronunciation. ● Facial expressions. ● Appropriate gestures. ● Logical sequencing. Step 5: Guided Practice (Elaborate) – 10 Minutes Group Activity Teacher provides story prompts such as: 1. A Day I Will Never Forget. 2. The Lost Phone. 3. An Unexpected Visitor. 4. My Most Memorable Holiday. 5. The Day I Helped Someone. Students' Activities ● Work in pairs or groups. ● Identify: ○ Characters ○ Setting ○ Conflict ○ Resolution ● Prepare a short oral narration. Step 6: Independent Practice (Evaluate) – 10 Minutes Teacher's Activities ● Invites students to narrate their stories before the class. ● Assesses students using the following criteria: ○ Clarity ○ Organization ○ Fluency ○ Expression ○ Confidence

Students' Activities ● Narrate stories individually. ● Listen to classmates' presentations. Evaluation Teacher asks students: 1. What is story narration? 2. Mention four elements of a good story. 3. Why is voice modulation important in storytelling? 4. State two features of effective oral narration. 5. Narrate a short story in five to six sentences. Assignment Oxford English Language Course Book 1 New Concept English Language Book 1 Assignment Prepare and narrate a story on the topic: "Honesty Pays" The narration should: ● Contain at least three characters. ● Have a clear beginning, middle, and ending. ● State the moral lesson.

Students’ activities: students respond to the questions asked based on their knowledge of the topic. Step 2: EXPLORATION. Mode: entire class. Teacher’s activities: teacher guides the students to define a phrase: In the following sentences, indicate What is a phrase?

A phrase is a group of related words that does not contain a subject and predicate (verb). Examples: on the table, in the kitchen, the boy. What is a clause? A clause is a group of related words that has both a subject and a predicate (verb). Every complete sentence is made up of at least a clause. E.g. He came. Students’ activities: the students listen, repeat after teacher loudly and carryout the class activity. Step 3 : DISCUSSION. Mode: entire class. Teacher’s activities: The teacher gives opportunity to students to state the types phrases and clauses with examples, and differentiate between a clause and a phrase. What is a phrase? A phrase is a group of related words that does not contain a subject and predicate (verb). Examples: on the table, in the kitchen, the boy. Types of Phrases with examples 1. Noun Phrase : A phrase that acts as a noun. It contains a noun and may include modifiers. Examples: a. The black dog barked loudly. b. A bunch of fresh roses sat on the table. c. My younger brother ate the food . d. The tall, elegant woman is a doctor. e. Mr. Sam, the tall teacher, teaches English. 2. Verb Phrase : A phrase that includes the main verb and its auxiliaries. a. She is singing beautifully. b. They have been waiting for hours. c. We will meet them at the park. d. He has completed his homework. e. The children were playing in the rain. 3. Adjectival Phrase : A phrase that functions as an adjective, modifying a noun or pronoun. a. The car covered in mud belongs to my uncle. b. The girl, extremely tired from the journey, fell asleep. c. A house built of bricks is durable.

d. He is someone fond of adventure. e. The movie, too boring to watch, disappointed everyone. 4. Adverb Phrase : A phrase that functions as an adverb, modifying a verb, adjective, or adverb. a. She spoke with great confidence. b. He drives in a very reckless manner. c. The team worked harder than expected. d. We will meet after the concert. e. He completed the task in just a few minutes. 5. Prepositional Phrase : A phrase that starts with a preposition and includes its object and modifiers. a. The cat is hiding under the bed. b. She walked through the crowded market. c. He left the keys on the kitchen table. d. The gift is for my best friend. e. They went to the top of the hill. 6. Infinitive Phrase (Bonus): A phrase that starts with "to" followed by the base form of a verb. a. I want to learn French fluently. b. She plans to visit her grandparents next week. c. He came to fix the leaking tap. d. They are determined to win the competition. e. It’s time to leave for the airport. Students’ activities: the students state the types of clauses explain them with examples and differentiate between a clause and a phrase. Step 4: APPLICATION.

Mode: entire class. James spoke as though he was a born orator. 2. They felt that the farmer must be commended. 3. When at last he returned to the village, the told him his father had died. 4. The few books that were produced in the Middle Ages were written by hands. 5. When the world was young, artists drew their pictures on stones. Students’ activities: students carry out the class activity in their note books. Step 5: EVALUATION. Mode: individual. Teacher’s activities: the teacher asks students the following questions: ● Define a Phrase, ● state its features.. ● Differentiate between a clause and a phrase. ● Cite some examples of phrases. Students’ activities: the students respond to the questions asked. ASSIGNMENT : students are to list ten sentences containing the main and subordinate clauses. REFERENCE MATERIALS. title: SIMPLE POLITE REQUESTS AND SIMPLE GREETINGS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Speech Week: ____________________ Date: ____________________ Class: SS 1 Period: ____________________ Age: 13 years and above Sex: Mixed Time: ____________________ Duration: ____________________ Unit Topic Speech Lesson Topic: Simple Polite Requests and Simple Greetings Specific Behavioural Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define polite requests and greetings. 2. Give examples of simple polite requests. 3. Give examples of simple greetings. 4. Use polite requests and greetings appropriately in communication. Instructional Resource Charts showing examples of simple polite requests and greetings. Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Knowledge Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities

The teacher asks students the following questions: Orientation Stage ● How do you greet your teacher or parents in the morning? Conceptualization Stage ● Why is it important to use polite expressions when speaking to people? Investigation Stage ● Can you identify the polite request in this sentence: “Please, may I borrow your pen?” Discussion/Reflection Stage ● How can greetings and polite requests improve relationships in school and at home? Conclusion Stage ● What is the difference between a greeting and a polite request? Students’ Activities Students respond to the questions based on their previous knowledge and experiences. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities The teacher guides students to define polite requests and greetings and gives examples. What is a Simple Polite Request?

A simple polite request is a respectful way of asking someone to do something or give something. Examples of Simple Polite Requests 1. Please help me with this assignment. 2. May I borrow your pen? 3. Could you open the window, please? 4. Kindly close the door. 5. Please, may I come in? 6. Can you explain the note again, please? 7. Please give me some water. 8. Could you help me carry this bag? 9. May I ask a question? 10. Please lend me your notebook. What is a greeting? A greeting is a word or expression used to welcome someone or show politeness when meeting people. Examples of Greetings 1. Good morning. 2. Good afternoon. 3. Good evening. 4. Hello. 5. Hi. 6. How are you? 7. Nice to meet you. 8. Welcome.

9. How was your day? 10. Goodbye. Students’ Activities Students listen attentively, repeat after the teacher, and take notes. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities The teacher explains the importance and uses of polite requests and greetings. Importance of Simple Polite Requests 1. They show respect. 2. They promote good manners. 3. They encourage cooperation. 4. They make communication friendly. 5. Importance of Greetings 6. Greetings show courtesy. 7. They create friendliness. 8. They make people feel welcomed. 9. They promote peaceful relationships. Dialogue Examples Simple Greetings 1. A: Good morning, Musa. B: Good morning, Esther. How are you today?

A: I am fine, thank you. 2. A: Good afternoon, class. B: Good afternoon, teacher. 3. A: Hello, Jane. B: Hello, Grace. Nice to see you. 4. A: Good evening, Dad. B: Good evening, my son. 5. A: Hi, David. How was your day? B: It was fine, thank you. 6. A: Welcome to our school. B: Thank you very much. 7. A: How are you this morning? B: I am very well, thank you. 8.

A: Nice to meet you. B: Nice to meet you too. 9. A: Goodbye, friends. B: Goodbye. See you tomorrow. 10. A: Have a nice day. B: Thank you. Same to you. Dialogue Examples on Simple Polite Requests Dialogue Examples Simple Greetings 1. A: Please, may I borrow your pen? B: Yes, you may. 2. A: Could you help me with this exercise, please? B: Certainly. 3. A: Please open the window. B: Alright.

4. A: May I come in, sir? B: Yes, come in. 5. A: Kindly lend me your notebook. B: Here you are. 6. A: Could you repeat the question, please? B: Yes, I will. 7. A: Please give me some water. B: Okay. 8. A: Can you show me the way to the library, please? B: Yes. Follow me. 9. A: Please help me carry this bag. B: No problem. 10. A: May I ask a question? B: Yes, you may.

Students’ Activities Students practice greetings and polite requests in pairs and groups. Step 4: Application Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities The teacher guides students through the following class exercise. Class Activity Complete the following expressions correctly: 1. __________ morning, teacher. 2. Please, may I __________ your ruler? 3. __________ afternoon, everyone. 4. Could you __________ the window, please? 5. How __________ you today? Students’ Activities Students complete the exercise in their notebooks and practice orally. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities The teacher asks students the following questions: 1. What is a simple polite request and greeting? 2. Mention five examples of simple polite requests. 3. Mention five examples of greetings. 4. State two importance of greetings.

Students’ Activities Students answer the questions individually. Assignment Students should write ten examples of polite requests and ten examples of greetings used at home, school, or in the community with appropriate responses. Reference Materials 1. Oxford English Language for Senior Secondary Schools Book 1. 2. NERDC English Language Curriculum 3. Macmillan English for Senior Secondary Schools

title: SUMMARY WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
SUMMARY WRITING DEFINITION: A Summary is a brief or concise account of an event that gives only the main point and not the details. This means that summary must be shorter than the original text. GUIDELINES FOR WRITING A SUMMARY 1. Read the passage carefully. 2. Extract the main ideas from the paragraphs through the identification of topic sentences if any. 3. Paraphrase the extracted ideas into required number of sentences. 4. Use synonyms. 5. Never exceed the required number of sentences. 6. Answer must be in sentences and not in phrases unless there is a preamble. NOTE: in summary there is no need for the following; a. Examples and illustrations. b. Analogy: comparison between two situations or processes that seem similar. c. Repetition. d. The use of flowery language (figures of speech or literary devices) e.g. “the man is dark as charcoal” is the man dark?”. e. The inclusion of details (unnecessary or irrelevant materials) f. The use of link words (connectives- moreover, however, furthermore, as a matter of fact, etc).

Note : summary should be clear, straight forward and without blemish. E.g. “In the time of myth during the period of magic, the destiny of a great kingdom rested on the shoulder of a young boy, his name is Merlin”

title: PHRASSS
subject: English Language
rawText: WHAT IS A PHRASE? A phrase is a group of words whose meaning is incomplete, although the group of words is part of a sentence. A phrase could also be defined as a group of words without a finite verb. Phrases are usually named or identified through the head word. The head word could be a noun, verb, adverb, adjective or preposition. TYPES OF PHRASES Since phrases are usually named or identified through the head word, however, there are basically five types of English phrases namely: Noun Phrase: A noun phrase is a phrase that has a noun or pronoun as its head word. It could be pre- modified by an article, a possessive of demonstrative pronoun or an adjective. The words underlined are noun phrases: • The girl and her friends ate many oranges . • This apple is very sour. • Our teachers are hardworking. Verb Phrase: a verb phrase is a word group that indicates the predicate of a sentence. It includes a main verb and its auxiliaries ( helping verbs ). The words underlined are verb phrases: • The girl and her friends ate many oranges. • This apple is very sour. • Our teachers are going on strike. Adverb Phrase: An adverb phrase is a group of words that serves the purpose of an adverb; also known as adverbial phrase. An adverb is a word used to modify a verb, an adjective or another adverb. The adverb is the head of the phrase and can appear alone or it can be modified by other words. The words underlined are adverb phrases: • We usually go on holiday in August. • Time goes very quickly. • He behaved rudely . Adjective Phrase : An adjective phrase is a group of words that describe a noun or pronoun in a sentence. The adjective phrase can be placed before, or after, the noun or pronoun in the sentence. The words underlined are adjective phrases: • The movie was not too terribly long . • The final exams were unbelievably difficult . • Faster than a speeding bullet , Superman was finished in no time. Prepositional Phrase : A prepositional phrase is a phrase that starts with a preposition and ends with noun (or a pronoun). The words underlined are prepositional phrases: • We will be back in a few days . • We’ve got a new television with a thirty one inch screen. • I saw a wonderful painting by James. I feel sorry for you.

title: DEPENDENT AND INDEPENDENT CLAUSES
subject: English Language
rawText:
CLAUSE A clause is a group of words that has subject, predicate and a finite verb. A finite verb is a verb that can change by person, number or tense. Example: Sam is my friend Sam and Susan are my friends. Sam was my friend Note, the verb ‘is’ changed to ‘are’ in the second sentence when the number of persons increased and changed to ‘was’ in the third when the tense was changed. A subject is the person or the thing being talked about; it could be a word or a group of words. Example: Adekunle is my classmate Our noisy neighbours are generous ‘Adekunle’ and ‘our noisy neighbours’ are the subjects of these sentences while ‘is my classmate’ and ‘are generous’ are the predicates. The predicate is the part which talks about the subject in the sentence. TYPES OF CLAUSES There are two types of clauses: independent /main clause dependent/subordinate clause Independent/main clause is a clause that can stand on its own to convey meaning while a dependent/subordinate clause is a clause that depends on main clause to convey meaning. CHARACTERISTICS OF A MAIN CLAUSE It contains a subject and a finite verb It can stand alone It conveys a full meaning Example: she cooked the food happily. The trophy belongs to the champion. My father is a businessman. Ada could not talk. CHARACTERISTICS OF DEPENDENT CLAUSE It consists of a subject and a finite verb. It cannot stand alone. It is often introduced by subordinating conjunctions like: because, while, whose, that, before, how, which, who, whom etc. example:

Because he came late Which you mentioned yesterday That you gave me Which was opened yesterday KINDS OF SUBORDINATE CLAUSE Noun clause Adjectival clause Adverbial clause

Example: Adekunle is my classmate Our noisy neighbours are generous ‘Adekunle’ and ‘our noisy neighbours’ are the subjects of these sentences while ‘is my classmate’ and ‘are generous’ are the predicates. The predicate is the part which talks about the subject in the sentence. TYPES OF CLAUSES There are two types of clauses: independent /main clause dependent/subordinate clause Independent/main clause is a clause that can stand on its own to convey meaning while a dependent/subordinate clause is a clause that depends on main clause to convey meaning. CHARACTERISTICS OF A MAIN CLAUSE It contains a subject and a finite verb It can stand alone It conveys a full meaning Example: she cooked the food happily. The trophy belongs to the champion. My father is a businessman. Ada could not talk. CHARACTERISTICS OF DEPENDENT CLAUSE It consists of a subject and a finite verb. It cannot stand alone. It is often introduced by subordinating conjunctions like: because, while, whose, that, before, how, which, who, whom etc. example:
Because he came late Which you mentioned yesterday That you gave me Which was opened yesterday KINDS OF SUBORDINATE CLAUSE Noun clause Adjectival clause Adverbial clause

Theme: Structure Two: Two Date: ………….. Class: SS 1 Time: ……………………………………………………………………….. Period ……………………………………….. Duration: …………………………………………………………………… Subject: English Language Week: Six Unit Topic: Structure Lesson Topic: Synonyms — Words of the Same Meaning and Words Nearly the Same in Meaning Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. explain what synonyms are, 2. identify synonyms in sentences, 3. differentiate between words of the exact same meaning and nearly the same meaning, 4. use synonyms correctly in sentences. Instructional Resources: Whiteboard, marker, flash cards with word pairs, charts. LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students the following questions:

● What do you understand by the word's meaning? ● Can two different words have the same meaning? ● Mention two words that mean the same thing. Students’ Activities: Students respond based on their prior knowledge and give examples. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher introduces the concept of synonyms. What are Synonyms? Synonyms are words that have the same meaning or nearly the same meaning as another word. They help to avoid repetition and make speech and writing more interesting. Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively, repeat key points, and take notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains the two categories with examples. A. Words of the Same Meaning (Exact Synonyms) These are words that can replace each other in most contexts without changing the meaning. Examples: 1. Abandon — Desert 2. Acquire — Obtain 3. Amend — Correct

4. Cease — Stop 5. Conceal — Hide 6. Diligent — Industrious 7. Emerge — Appear 8. Expand — Enlarge 9. Permit — Allow 10. Reject — Refuse Sentences: ● The programme will begin/start at noon. ● She finished/ended the work early. Words Nearly the Same in Meaning (Near Synonyms) B. Words Nearly the Same in Meaning (Near Synonyms) 1. Accurate — Precise 2. Admit — Confess 3. Assume — Presume 4. Brief — Concise 5. Dangerous — Hazardous 6. Defend — Protect 7. Describe — Depict 8. Freedom — Liberty 9. Honest — Sincere 10. Idea — Notion Sentences: These words are similar but not always interchangeable in every sentence.

Sentences: ● She is slim, not thin. ● The report is accurate (not precise) and free from errors. ● The thief confessed (not admitted) his crime to the police. The teacher writes more pairs on the board and explains usage differences. Students’ Activities: Students suggest additional synonym pairs and write examples. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher gives class exercises: Class Activity: A. Give synonyms for the following words: 1. Happy 2. Fast 3. Small B. Use each pair of synonyms in meaningful sentences. Students’ Activities: Students complete the exercise in their notebooks and share answers. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students to: 1. Define synonyms.

2. Mention two pairs of exact synonyms. 3. Mention two pairs of near synonyms. 4. Use any pair in a sentence. Students’ Activities: Students respond orally and in written form. ASSIGNMENT : Write ten pairs of synonyms and use five pairs in sentences. REFERENCE MATERIALS: Oxford English Language Course Book 1. New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 2. rawText: Vocabulary: Words Associated with Advertising Advertising is a form of selling. Messages from manufacturers and advertisers reach the customers through the media. Consumers need products. Manufacturers produce goods or brands with the intention to sell them by making them available at reasonable prices. Some relevant words are: Consumer: one who buys good s and services Advertisement : a public announcement of a product or services to call attention to it Bill-board: notice board on which information is placed Newsletter: a periodic printed report that contains news of interest to a specific group like a society or employee Discount: a reduction in the usual price of something Commercials: activity that is related to buying and selling of goods and services End-users: a person or group that is one of the consumers for whom the product was made. Advertising: Agency a company that handles clients who need their services Assignment Write out ten more words related to advertising and their meanings. title: NOUN
subject: English Language
rawText:
Notes on noun and types of noun Here’s a clear set of notes on nouns and their types that you can use for study or revision: 📘 Noun and Its Types 🔹 Definition of Noun A noun is the name of a person, place, thing, idea, or quality. It answers the question What is it ? Who is it ? Examples: Person → teacher, John Place → school, Paris Thing → book, pen, computer Idea/Quality → honesty, love, freedom ✨ Types of Nouns 1. Proper Noun Names a specific person, place, or thing. Always begins with a capital letter. Examples: Ravi, London, the Ganga, Toyota 2. Common Noun Names general items, not specific. Examples: boy, city, river, car 3. Concrete Noun Refers to things that can be seen, touched, smelled, heard, or tasted. Examples: apple, dog, rain, music 4. Abstract Noun Refers to ideas, feelings, qualities, or concepts that cannot be touched. Examples: happiness, wisdom, honesty, freedom 5. Collective Noun Refers to a group of people, animals, or things taken as one. Examples: team, herd, family, bouquet, class

6. Countable Noun Things that can be counted. Can be singular or plural. Examples: book/books, apple/apples 7. Uncountable Noun Things that cannot be counted in numbers. Usually do not have a plural form. Examples: milk, sugar, information, furniture 8. Material Noun Refers to substances or materials from which things are made. Examples: gold, wood, water, cotton, iron 9. Compound Noun Made up of two or more words, joined or separate, forming a single noun. Examples: toothpaste, mother-in-law, classroom, football Tip to Remember: Every noun will fit into one or more of these categories. For example: “Ravi” → Proper Noun “River” → Common Noun “The Ganga” → Proper + Common Noun (specific river)

title: ADJECTIVAL CLAUSES AND THEIR GRAMMATICAL
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Structure Week : 7 Date: 2nd June, 2026. Class: SS 1 Time: 9:20 - 10:00am Period: 3rd Duration: 40 Min. Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Structure Lesson Topic: Adjectival Clauses and Their Grammatical Functions in Sentences Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. define an adjectival clause, and identify adjectival clauses in sentences, 2. state the grammatical functions of adjectival clauses, 3. construct sentences containing adjectival clauses, 4. use adjectival clauses correctly in speech and writing. Instructional Resources Whiteboard, marker, sentence charts, flash cards containing relative pronouns (who, whom, whose, which, that). LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual

Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What is an adjective? 2. What does an adjective do in a sentence? 3. Can you describe a noun using a group of words? Students' Activities Students respond based on their previous knowledge. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Meaning of an Adjectival Clause An adjectival clause is a subordinate clause that performs the function of an adjective by describing or modifying a noun or pronoun in the main clause. An adjectival clause usually begins with relative pronouns such as: ● who ● whom ● whose ● which ● that Examples:

● The boy who won the competition is my friend. ● This is the book that I bought yesterday. Students' Activities Students listen attentively and take notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Grammatical Function of Adjectival Clauses An adjectival clause functions as an adjective. It modifies or describes a noun or pronoun in the main clause. Examples of Adjectival Clauses and Their Grammatical Functions S/N Sentence Adjectival Clause Function 1 The girl who came yesterday is my sister. who came yesterday Modifies the noun girl. 2 The man who teaches us English is absent. who teaches us English Modifies the noun man.

3 I lost the pen that my father bought for me. that my father bought for me Modifies the noun pen. 4 The house which was painted blue belongs to my uncle. which was painted blue Modifies the noun house. 5 The woman whose car was stolen reported to the police. whose car was stolen Modifies the noun woman. 6 The students who studied hard passed the examination. who studied hard Modifies the noun students. 7 This is the village where I was born. where I was born Modifies the noun village. 8 The day when we met was memorable. when we met Modifies the noun day. 9 The reason why he left early is unknown. why he left early

Modifies the noun reason. 10 The teacher whom the principal praised is diligent. whom the principal praised Modifies the noun teacher. Additional Examples The boy whose father is a doctor won the prize. Function: Modifies the noun boy. The phone which I bought last month has developed a fault. Function: Modifies the noun phone. The woman who lives next door is a nurse. Function: Modifies the noun woman. The book that is on the table belongs to me. Function: Modifies the noun book. The athlete who won the gold medal was celebrated. Function: Modifies the noun athlete. How to Identify an Adjectival Clause Ask: ● Which one? ● What kind of person? ● What kind of thing? Example: The girl who is wearing a red dress is my cousin. Question: Which girl?

Answer: Who is wearing a red dress. Therefore, the clause modifies the noun girl. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Class Activity Identify the adjectival clauses and state their functions. 1. The boy who broke the window has apologized. 2. The car that was stolen has been recovered. 3. The woman whose bag was missing reported the case. 4. The school where I studied is very old. 5. The day when the event took place was rainy. Students' Activities Students identify the clauses and state the nouns being modified. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What is an adjectival clause? 2. Identify the adjectival clause and state its grammatical function in: 3. The man who called me is my uncle. 4. Construct two sentences containing adjectival clauses.

Students' Activities Students respond orally and in writing. ASSIGNMENT Construct ten sentences containing adjectival clauses. Underline the adjectival clauses and state the nouns or pronouns they modify. REFERENCE MATERIALS F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012). New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. Banjo, A. et al. New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools. WAEC English Language Chief Examiners' Reports. Comprehensive English Grammar Textbooks.

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH PHOTOGRAPHY
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Vocabulary Date: ___________________ Class: SS 1 Time: ___________________ Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Week: ___________________ Unit Topic: Vocabulary Development Lesson Topic: Words Associated with Photography Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Explain what photography is and identify words associated with photography. 2. State the meanings of photography-related terms. 3. Use the words correctly in sentences. 4. Demonstrate understanding of photography vocabulary. Instructional Resources ● Camera ● Photographs ● Photography magazines ● Mobile phone camera ● Whiteboard. LESSON PRESENTATION

Step 1: Identification of Prior Ideas Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities Teacher asks: 1. Orientation How do people capture and keep pictures of important events such as birthdays, weddings, and graduations? 2. Conceptualization What questions can we ask about how pictures are taken and the tools used in producing them? 3. Investigation What tools, equipment, or processes are involved in taking and producing clear pictures? 4. Conclusion What important words or terms are commonly used in the process of taking and producing photographs? 5. Discussion How can the words you have identified be correctly used in sentences to describe picture-taking activities? Students' Activities Respond based on their experiences.

Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities: Teacher guides students to explain photograph. What is Photography? Photography is the art, science, and practice of creating images by recording light through a camera. Students' Activities Listen attentively and take notes. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Group Teacher's Activities: Teacher guides students to identify words associated with photography and use them to form sentences. Words Associated with Photography S/N Word Meaning Sentence 1 Camera Device used to take photographs. The photographer bought a new camera. 2

Photograph A picture taken with a camera. I kept the photograph in an album. 3 Photographer A person who takes photographs. The photographer covered the wedding ceremony. 4 Lens The glass part of a camera used for focusing light. The lens was carefully cleaned. 5 Flash A bright light used when taking pictures. The flash illuminated the room. 6 Album A book for keeping photographs. She arranged the pictures in an album. 7 Portrait A photograph of a person. The portrait was displayed in the office. 8 Studio A place where photographs are taken. They visited the studio for a family photograph.

9 Snapshot A casual photograph. He took a snapshot of the playground. 10 Exposure The amount of light reaching the camera sensor. The exposure was adjusted properly. 11 Focus The sharpness of an image. The camera was in focus. 12 Zoom To make a subject appear closer. She zoomed in on the bird. 13 Background The part behind the main subject. The background of the picture was attractive. 14 Image A visual representation captured by a camera. The image appeared clear. 15 Negative The reversed image used in traditional photography.

The negative was developed in the laboratory. 16 Film Material used in traditional cameras. The film was processed carefully. 17 Tripod A three-legged stand for supporting a camera. The tripod prevented camera shake. 18 Frame The border or composition of a photograph. The frame contained beautiful scenery. 19 Digital Camera An electronic camera that stores images digitally. He uses a digital camera for his work. 20 Selfie A self-taken photograph. She took a selfie with her friends. Step 4: Application Class Activity 1. List ten words associated with photography. 2. State their meanings. 3. Use five of them in sentences.

Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Group Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What is photography? 2. Mention five photography terms. 3. State the meanings of: Lens Flash Portrait Studio 4. Use any three of the words in sentences. Assignment List ten additional words associated with photography, state their meanings, and use each in a sentence. Reference Materials F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 2. New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools. Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary. Photography magazines and journals

Vocabulary on Home and Family. (page 5) Home: This can be defined as a house or flat or apartment that we live in especially with our family. Family: This can be seen as a group consisting of one or two parent and their children. It can also be defined as a group of people who are related by blood, marriage or adoption. There are two types of family namely: Nuclear family and extended family. Some words associated with home and family are: Kinsmen, nieces, domestic chores, relatives, cousins, living room, uncles, household, well- wishers, aunties, courting, oldest daughter, nephews, fiancé, kith and kin, engagement ceremony. Family relations refer to; ancestor, siblings, distant relatives, next of kin. Things in the home are; kitchen ware, hearth, utensils, upholstery, rug, wardrobe, Parlour, sitting room, store, pantry, lobby, foyer. Activities within the family: courtship, marriage, divorce, burial, family life, naming ceremony. Meaning of some of the words listed are: Hearth: this means the floor at the bottom of a fire place ( the space for a fire in the wall of a room) Foyer: this is a large open space inside the entrance of a house where people can meet or wait. Lobby: means an entrance hall in a private house or flat/apartment where people can meet or wait. Pantry: This means cupboard or closet or small room in a house used for storing food. The synonym for pantry is Larder. Fiance: means the man that a woman is engaged to. Courting: This means to have a romantic relationship before getting married. title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT-RELIGION
subject: English Language
rawText:
VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT TOPIC: WORD ASSOCIATED WITH RELIGION CHRISTIAN, ISLAMIC AND TRADITIONAL RELIGION Religion is the belief in the existence of a particular god or gods and the activities that are connected with the worship. The three major religion in Nigeria include; Christian religion, Islamic religion and Traditional religion. CHRISTIAN RELIGION Christian religion is the religion based on the teaching of Jesus Christ, His death and resurrection. And the belief that He is the son of God. A believer of the religion is baptized in a Christian church, and is called a Christian. Christendon refers to all Christians in the word. Words associated with Christian religion include; communion, lent, baptism, evangelist, sin, repentance, church, Bible, Reverend father, Pastor, deacon, tithe, saints, monk, nun, priest etc. Examples of such words and their meaning. 1. Consecrate: Set aside for a religious practice (to make someone or something holy) 2. Doctrine: Set of rules and principles guiding the church. 3. Baptism: Dipping someones in water for cleasing and to become a full member in Christ by an ordained Priest or Pastor. 4. Church: A Christian place of worship 5. Bible: The Christian holy book that contains the word of God 6. Tithe: Ten percent of one’s income given to God 7. Repentance: To denounce sin and turn to God 8. Saints: People who died in Christ ISLAMIC RELIGION Islamic religion is the religion that is based on the total submission of the will of Allah and the teachings of Prophet Muhammad who is regarded as the first leader and teacher of Islam. His parents were Abdullah Ibn Abd-al mutalib and Aminah. He was one of the Quaraishi people born in Mecca (Saudi Arabia) Words Associated with Islam 1. Qur’an: A holy book that contain the revealed words of God 2. Hadith: Collection of the sayings of Prophet Muhammad 3. Mosque: Muslim’s place of worship 4. Ablution: The act of washing oneself for prayer. 5. Imam: The leader of Islamic congregational prayer 6. Zakat: Alnis giving 7. Salat: Five daily prayers

8. Id-el-malud: Celebration of the where ram is sacrificed. TRADITIONAL RELIGION Traditional/religion is the belief in gods and ancestral spirits Words associated with traditional religion 1. Shrine: A place of worship 2. Rituals: Various performances done to gain favour from gods 3. Sacrifice: Offering of anything to a god 4. Supernatural: Things beyond the forces of nature 5. Polyheism: Act of believing in mangy gods 6. Sacrilege: Act of violating something sacred 7. Ethics: Moral principles by which a person or a group is guided 8. Superstition: The practice of deep religion thoughts Assignment In your new concept English, answer the questions on unit 7 exercise 2 and unit 8 exercise 2.

title: EXPOSITORY ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Continuous Writing Two: Six Date: ………….. Class: SS 1 Time: ……………………………………………………………………….. Period ……………………………………….. Duration: …………………………………………………………………… Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Continuous Writing Lesson Topic: Expository Essay Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. explain what an expository essay is, 2. mention the features of an expository essay, 3. organise ideas into introduction, body, and conclusion, 4. write a simple expository essay on a given topic. Instructional Resources: Whiteboard, marker, essay charts, sample essay handout. LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students: 1. What is an essay? 2. Have you ever written an essay to explain something?

3. What do you do when you want to teach someone how something works? Students’ Activities: Students respond based on their previous knowledge and experiences in essay writing. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher introduces the concept of an expository essay. What is an Expository Essay? An expository essay is a type of writing that explains, informs, or describes a topic clearly using facts, examples, and logical arrangement of ideas. It does not express personal emotions but focuses on giving information. Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively, repeat key points, and take notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains the features and structure of an expository essay. Features of an Expository Essay : ● Clear explanation of ideas ● Use of facts and examples ● Simple and formal language ● Logical arrangement of paragraphs ● No emotional or biased expressions

Structure : ● Introduction – Introduces the topic. ● Body Paragraphs – Explain the topic with facts and examples. ● Conclusion – Summarises the main points. Sample Topic: “ The Importance of Clean Water” The teacher writes a short model paragraph on the board and explains paragraphing and linking words. THE IMPORTANCE OF CLEAN WATER Clean water is one of the most essential resources for human survival. Every living thing depends on water to live, grow, and remain healthy. Firstly, clean water is necessary for drinking and cooking. When water is pure and safe, it prevents diseases such as cholera and typhoid. In addition, it helps the body to function properly by aiding digestion and maintaining body temperature. Secondly, clean water is important for sanitation and hygiene. People use water to bathe, wash clothes, and clean their environment. As a result, communities with access to clean water often experience fewer outbreaks of illness. Schools and hospitals especially require a steady supply of safe water to maintain cleanliness and protect lives.

Furthermore, clean water supports agriculture and food production because farmers need it to grow crops and raise animals. Finally, clean water contributes to economic and social development. When people spend less time searching for water or treating water-borne diseases, they can focus on education, work, and community growth. In conclusion, clean water is not just a basic need but a foundation for a healthy and productive society. Therefore, governments and individuals must work together to protect water sources and ensure that everyone has access to safe and clean water. Students’ Activities: Students suggest points, copy notes, and ask questions. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class / Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher gives a class writing task: Class Activity: Make an outline of an essay with the topic, “Why Education is Important.” Students’ Activities: Students write individually in their notebooks using correct paragraph structure. Step 5: EVALUATION

Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students to: 1. Define an expository essay. 2. Mention two features of an expository essay. 3. State the three parts of an essay. 4. Read their written paragraph aloud. Students’ Activities: Students respond orally and present their written work. ASSIGNMENT : Write an essay of not less than 300 words on “The Effects of Social Media on Students.” REFERENCE MATERIALS: Oxford English Language Course Book 1. New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 2. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. Comprehensive English Grammar Textbooks.

title: SPEAKING TO PERSUADING/CONVINCE (DEBATE)
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Speech Date: ………….. 2nd June, 2026. Class: SS 1 Time: 8:40 - 9:20 am. Period: 2nd. Duration: 40 Min. Subject: English Language Week: 7 Unit Topic: Speech Work Lesson Topic: Speaking to Persuade/Convince (Debate) Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. explain the meaning of debate, and identify the features of persuasive speaking, 2. present logical arguments to support a position, 3. use appropriate expressions for persuading and convincing an audience, 4. participate effectively in a debate. Instructional Resources: Debate topic chart, flashcards containing persuasive expressions, whiteboard, marker. LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual

Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students: 1. Have you ever convinced someone to agree with your opinion? How did you do it? 2. What strategies do speakers use to make people accept their point of view during an argument or discussion? 3. What is the difference between merely expressing an opinion and persuading others to accept it? 4. How can you use facts, examples, and logical reasons to convince your classmates that your position in a debate is correct? 5. Which argument in today's debate was the most convincing, and why did you find it persuasive? Students’ Activities: Students respond based on their experiences and prior knowledge. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: What is Debate? A debate is a formal discussion in which two opposing sides present arguments for and against a motion in order to persuade an audience or judges. What is Persuasive Speaking? Persuasive speaking is the act of presenting ideas, facts, and arguments in a manner that convinces others to accept a viewpoint or take a particular action.

Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively, repeat key points, and take notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains the features of persuasive speaking and debate. Features of Persuasive Speaking ● Clear statement of position. ● Logical arguments. ● Supporting facts and examples. ● Confidence and fluency. ● Appropriate voice projection. ● Respect for opposing views. ● Strong conclusion. Useful Expressions for Persuasion Introducing an Argument ● I strongly believe that... ● It is evident that... ● There is no doubt that... ● It is important to note that... ● I wish to state clearly that…

Giving Reasons ● Firstly,... ● Secondly,... ● Furthermore,... ● In addition,... ● Moreover,... Refuting an Opponent's Argument ● My opponents failed to consider that... ● Contrary to their claim,... ● Their argument is misleading because... ● The facts clearly show that... ● I respectfully disagree with that position because… Concluding a Debate ● In conclusion,... ● Based on the evidence presented,... ● Therefore,... ● For these reasons,... ● I urge you to support this motion. Sample Debate Motion " Social Media Does More Good Than Harm." Proposition (For the Motion) Social media promotes communication. 1. It provides educational resources.

2. It creates business opportunities. 3. It helps people stay informed. Opposition (Against the Motion) 1. It encourages distraction among students. 2. It can spread false information. 3. It contributes to cyberbullying. 4. It may lead to addiction. Students’ Activities: Students identify persuasive expressions and contribute arguments on both sides. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Group Work Teacher’s Activities: Class Activity Divide the class into two groups and assign the motion: "School Uniforms Should Be Compulsory in Secondary Schools." One group speaks for the motion while the other speaks against it. Students’ Activities: Students prepare and present arguments using persuasive expressions. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students: What is a debate?

1. What is persuasive speaking? 2. Mention five features of persuasive speaking. 3. State five expressions used in persuasion. 4. Present one argument for or against a given motion. Students’ Activities: Students respond orally and participate in a short debate session. ASSIGNMENT Write five arguments supporting and five arguments opposing the motion: "Students Should Be Allowed to Use Mobile Phones in School." Use at least five persuasive expressions in your presentation. REFERENCE MATERIALS F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012). New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 2. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. Oral English for Senior Secondary Schools. WAEC and NECO English Language Recommended Texts.

Instructional Resources: Qur’an, picture/chart of a mosque, prayer mat. LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students the following questions: 1. Can you explain the meaning of Islam? 2. Can you mention any words associated with Islam? 3. Can you state the meanings of those words? Students’ Activities: Students respond to the questions asked based on their knowledge of the topic.

Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains to the students what Islam is. What is Islam? Islam is a religion based on the teachings of Prophet Muhammad (Peace Be Upon Him) and the holy book called the Qur’an. Muslims believe in one God (Allah) and follow the principles and practices outlined in Islam. Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively, repeat key points after the teacher, and jot down notes in their notebooks. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Using the resource materials, the teacher guides the students to list and state the meanings of words associated with Islam thus: S/NO WORD MEANING SENTENCE 1 Qur’an The holy book of Muslims. He reads the Qur’an every evening. 2 Mosque A place where Muslims worship.

The mosque is near our house. 3 Imam A leader who leads prayers in a mosque. The Imam delivered a sermon on Friday. 4 Salah (Salat) The five daily prayers observed by Muslims. She performs Salah five times a day. 5 Fasting (Sawm) Abstaining from food and drink for a period for religious reasons. Muslims fast during Ramadan. 6 Ramadan The ninth month of the Islamic calendar dedicated to fasting. Ramadan begins with the sighting of the moon. 7 Zakat Charity given to the poor as a religious duty. He paid his Zakat to help the needy. 8 Hajj The pilgrimage to Mecca performed by Muslims. My uncle travelled to Saudi Arabia for Hajj. 9 Allah

The Arabic word for God. Muslims worship Allah. 10 Hadith Sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad. The teacher quoted a Hadith in class. Students’ Activities: Students mention other words associated with Islam, state their meanings, and form sentences with them. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher engages the students in a class activity by taking them through: Class Activity: List five words associated with Islam and make a sentence with each of them. Students’ Activities: Students carry out the class activity in their notebooks. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students the following questions: 1. Explain what Islam is. 2. List at least five (5) words associated with Islam. 3. State the meanings of some words associated with Islam. 4. Form sentences with them. Students’ Activities: Students respond to the questions asked.

ASSIGNMENT : List ten (10) words associated with Islam, state their meanings, and form a sentence with each of them. REFERENCE MATERIALS: The Holy Qur’an New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 2. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. TeachingBanyan.com

title: ORAL COMPOSITION OF A DESCRIPTIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Continuous Writing Date: ___________________ Class: SS 1 Time: ___________________ Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Week: ___________________ Unit Topic: Continuous Writing Lesson Topic: Oral Composition of a Descriptive Essay Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Explain the meaning of a descriptive essay and identify the features of a descriptive essay. 2. Describe a person, place, object, or event orally. 3. Use vivid and appropriate descriptive expressions. 4. Organize ideas logically in an oral presentation. Instructional Resources Pictures of people, places, and objects Flashcards containing descriptive words Whiteboard Charts showing the structure of a descriptive essay. Entry Behaviour Students are familiar with describing people, places, and objects in everyday conversations.

LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: Identification of Prior Ideas (Engage) Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: How would you describe your best friend to someone who has never met him or her? If a visitor asks about your school, what would you tell the person? What details make a description interesting? Students' Activities Respond to the questions. Share personal experiences. Mention descriptive words they know. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Teacher guides students to discover the meaning of descriptive essay through discussion. Meaning of a Descriptive Essay A descriptive essay is a type of composition that gives a detailed account of a person, place, object, animal, or event so that the reader or listener can easily imagine it.

The writer or speaker uses descriptive language and sensory details to create a clear picture in the mind of the audience. Students' Activities Listen attentively. Participate in discussion. Take notes. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Teacher explains the features of a descriptive essay. Features of a Descriptive Essay Clear description of the subject. Use of vivid and specific details. Use of sensory expressions (sight, smell, sound, taste, touch). Logical organization of ideas. Use of adjectives and descriptive phrases. Introduction, body, and conclusion. Useful Descriptive Expressions Describing a Person Tall and elegant Dark-complexioned Friendly and cheerful Hardworking and intelligent Neatly dressed

Describing a Place Beautiful environment Well-arranged buildings Peaceful atmosphere Crowded market Clean surroundings Describing an Object Smooth surface Bright colour Attractive appearance Heavy weight Shiny texture Teacher's Model Oral Composition Topic: My School My school is one of the most beautiful schools in my community. It is located in a quiet environment surrounded by green trees. The school compound is spacious and clean. There are several classroom blocks painted in bright colours. The teachers in my school are hardworking and friendly. They teach us diligently and encourage us to excel in our studies. The students are disciplined and respectful. One of the things I like most about my school is the library. It contains many interesting books that help students learn more. We also have a large playground where we play football and other games. In conclusion, my school provides a good environment for learning and character development. I am proud to be a student of this great school.

Teacher Demonstrates Correct pronunciation. Appropriate voice modulation. Clear organization of ideas. Eye contact and confidence. Step 4: Application Mode: Pair Work / Group Work Teacher's Activities Teacher provides oral composition topics such as: My Best Friend. Our School Library. My Favourite Teacher. A Market in My Community. My Favourite Pet. Students are guided to identify: Introduction Main descriptive details Conclusion Students' Activities Discuss ideas in pairs. Prepare short oral descriptions. Present before classmates. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual

Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What is a descriptive essay? 2. Mention four features of a descriptive essay. 3. State five descriptive expressions. 4. Describe your classroom orally in five to six sentences. Students' Activities Respond to questions. Present short oral descriptions. Assignment Prepare and present an oral descriptive essay on: "My Favourite Place in My Community." Your presentation should contain: An introduction. At least three descriptive details. A conclusion. Appropriate descriptive expressions. Reference Materials F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012). New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1 & 2. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools. WAEC English Language Syllabus. Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary.
