title: INTONATION PATTERN - RISE AND FALL
subject: English Language
rawText:
WEEK 1 SPEECH TOPIC: Intonation Pattern Rise and Fall Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice in speech or the variation in speech while speaking. It gives special meaning and emphasis to utterances. FUNCTIONS OF INTONATION 1. Grammatical function: This is used to differentiate between specific sentence types – declarative, interrogative, polar questions etc. when a speaker wants to give information, the falling tone is used. 2. Attitudinal function: The attitude can be that of surprise, doubt, sarcasm, interest, indifference, disbelief, uncertainty. For instance, when a speaker answers “Yes” in reply to a question, different shades of meaning can be inferred. If given in a falling tone means affirmation, meaning there is no doubt. But when it is given in a rising tone, it suggest some reservations (doubt) in the speakers mind. TYPES OF INTONATION a. The falling tone b. The rising tone c. The rise and fall tone A. THE FALLING TONE This is used to indicate a fall in the pitch of a speaker’s voice. In writing, we use the downward arrow to show a sentence uttered with the falling tone “↓” USES OF FALLING TONE a. To make statement. Examples; i. We shall all pass English language ↓ ii. The teacher is coming ↓ b. To give commands. Examples; i. Shut the door ↓ ii. Stand up ↓ c. To make exclamations. Examples; i. What a pleasant surprise! ↓

ii. Oh my Goodness! ↓ d. WH-Questions. Examples; i. When are you coming? ↓ ii. Why are you late to school? ↓ B. RISING TONE This is used to indicate a rise in the pitch of a speaker’s voice. USES OF THE RISING TONE a. For asking questions requiring a “Yes or No” answers otherwise known as polar questions. Examples; i. Is this your book?↑ ii. Are you coming? ↑ b. For polite request. Examples; i. May I borrow your book please? ↑ ii. Could you tell me the time please? ↑ c. For greetings. Examples; Good morning sir↑ Complement of the season ↑ d. To indicate uncertainty Will John come to school tomorrow? ↑ Can she make it? ↑ e. For incomplete statements. Examples; While they were playing ……..↑ As I was saying …….↑ C. THE RISE AND FALL TONE USES a. This tone is used in making a list of items. The voice pitch begins listed while the last item receives a falling tone. Examples i. One↑, two↑, three↑, four↑ and five↓. ii. Go in with a pen↑, pencil, a ruler and an eraser↓ b. It is also used in tag questions. Examples, You can do it, can’t you↑ She is hardworking↓, isn’t she? ↑

title: BOOK KEEPING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Continuous Writing Date: ………….. . Class: SS 1 Time: ……………………………………………………………………….. Period ……………………………………….. Duration: …………………………………………………………………… Subject: English Language Week: Six Unit Topic: Continuous Writing Lesson Topic: Book Keeping Teaching Method: Inquiry–Based Learning (IBL) Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: ● explain the meaning of Book Keeping in their own words, ● identify the importance of Book Keeping, ● write a well-organised continuous essay on Book Keeping, ● use appropriate paragraphing and vocabulary in writing. Instructional Resources: Sample cashbook/ledger, notebook, whiteboard, chart showing simple income and expenditure record. LESSON PRESENTATION (INQUIRY–BASED LEARNING STEPS) Step 1: ENGAGE (Questioning / Prior Knowledge) Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities:

● Displays a sample cashbook/ledger or draws a simple income and expenditure table on the board. ● Asks probing questions such as: ○ What do you think this book is used for? ○ Who might use this kind of record? ○ What could happen if money is not properly recorded? Students’ Activities: Observe the material. Share ideas, guesses, and previous experiences. Ask their own questions. title: CREATIVE WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Lesson Plan: Creative Writing Theme: Continuous Writing Week: .......... Date: Class: SS 1 ......... Period: ..,. Time: …. Duration: .. Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Continuous Writing Lesson Topic: Creative Writing Specific (Behavioral) Objectives: By the end of the lesson, students should be able to: I. Define creative writing. II. Identify and explain the main types of creative writing. III. Explain at least three features of a good creative work. IV. Compose a piece of creative writing, such as a short story, poem, or play. Instructional Resource : A banner displaying examples of different creative writing forms (e.g., short story, poem, and play). Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Ideas Mode: A couple of students. Teacher’s Activities: asks students: a. What do you understand by creative writing? b. Can you mention some forms of creative writing? c. Have you ever written a story, poem, or play? Students’ Activities: Students respond to the questions based on their knowledge and experience. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire class. Teacher’s Activities : Teacher defines creative writing and explains its types. Definition of Creative Writing: Creative writing is the ability to use imagination and originality to compose literary works such as stories, poems, plays, and essays. It involves expressing ideas, emotions, or experiences creatively.

Types of Creative Writing: 1. Prose :this iIncludes short stories, novels, and essays. In writing prose, we focus on narration, character development, and plot. 2. Poetry: it usses rhythm, rhyme, and figurative language to express ideas. It's often shorter and more emotionally expressive. 3. Drama/Play: it's written in dialogue form for performance.It includes acts, scenes, characters, and stage directions. Students’ Activities: Students listen, ask questions, and repeat key points after the teacher. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire class. Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains features of a good creative work. Features of a Good Creative Work: 1. Originality: The work shunique and not copied. 2. Imaginative Ideas: Creativity and innovation should be evident. 3. Organization: Proper structure (e.g., beginning, middle, and end). 4. Figurative Language: Use of literary devices such as metaphors, similes, and imagery. 5. Emotional Appeal: The ability to evoke feelings in the reader or audience. Examples: 1. A short story about friendship overcoming challenges. 2. A poem describing the beauty of nature. 3. A play showing conflict between characters with a resolution. Students’ Activities : Students participate in identifying the features of creative works. Step 4: Application Mode: Individual work. Teacher’s Activities : Teacher assigns students to write their own creative piece: Activity : Write either a short story, a poem, or a short play (not more than one page). Focus on originality and creativity. Students’ Activities : Students complete the activity in their notebooks. Step 5: Evaluation

Mode: A couple of students. Teacher’s Activities : teacher asks students the following questions: a. Define creative writing. b. Mention and explain three types of creative writing. c. State three features of a good creative work. d. Write a short creative piece. Students’ Activities: Students respond to the questions. Assignment Students are to choose one of the following and write about it (not less than 150 words): 1. A short story about an adventure. 2. A poem about love or friendship. 3. A short play about a school event. Reference Materials Oxford English Language Course Book 1. F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012). New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1, Learn Africa Plc, Lagos.

title: ADJUNCTS OF MANNER AND REASON
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Structure Two: Two Date: …………... Class: SS 1 Time: ……………………………………………………………………….. Period ……………………………………….. Duration: …………………………………………………………………… Subject: English Language Week: Two Unit Topic: Structure Lesson Topic: Adjuncts of Manner and Reason Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: ● explain what an adjunct is, ● identify adjuncts of manner and reason in sentences, ● differentiate between adjunct of manner and adjunct of reason, ● construct sentences using adjuncts of manner and reason correctly. Instructional Resources: Whiteboard, marker, sentence charts/flash cards. LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students the following questions: ● What is an adverb?

● Can you give a sentence that shows how an action was done? ● Can you give a sentence that shows why an action was done? Students’ Activities: Students respond based on their previous knowledge of adverbs and sentence construction. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains the concept of adjuncts. What is an Adjunct? An adjunct is a word or group of words that adds extra information to a sentence. It often tells how, when, where, why, or to what extent an action happens. Adjuncts are not compulsory parts of a sentence but they give more meaning. Students’ Activities: Students listen, repeat key points, and write notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains the two types under consideration with examples. Adjunct of Manner An adjunct of manner tells how an action is performed. Examples: quickly, slowly, carefully, happily, loudly. Examples in Sentences: ● She answered the question confidently. ● The boy ran quickly.

● They spoke politely to the teacher. Adjunct of Reason An adjunct of reason tells why an action is performed. Examples: because of illness, due to rain, out of fear, for safety reasons. Examples in Sentences: ● He stayed at home because of the rain. ● She cried out of pain. ● The match was postponed due to bad weather. Students’ Activities: Students provide more examples and copy notes. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher gives class exercises: Class Activity: A. Underline the adjuncts in the sentences below and state their types. The girl danced gracefully. The flight was delayed because of fog. B. Construct two sentences using adjuncts of manner and two using adjuncts of reason. Students’ Activities: Students complete the exercises in their notebooks and share answers. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students

Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students to: 1. Define an adjunct. 2. Define adjunct of maanervand reason. 3. State the difference between adjunct of manner and adjunct of reason. 4. Give one sentence each using an adjunct of manner and reason. Students’ Activities: Students respond orally and in written form. ASSIGNMENT : Write five sentences using adjuncts of manner and five sentences using adjuncts of reason. Underline the adjuncts. REFERENCE MATERIALS: Oxford English Language Course Book 1. New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos. Comprehensive English Grammar Textbooks. TeachingBanyan.com.

title: INTONATION PATTERNS (FALLING AND RISING TONES)
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Speech Week: One Date: ____________ Class: SS 1 Period: 1st & 2nd Time: 8:00am – 8:40am Duration: 40 minutes Unit Topic: Speech Lesson Topic: Intonation Patterns (Falling and Rising Tones) Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define intonation. 2. Identify falling and rising tones. 3. State functions of falling and rising tones with examples. 4. Apply correct intonation in spoken sentences. Instructional Resources: Whiteboard and marker, Flashcards, Prepared sentences on chart, Audio recordings Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Knowledge Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities:

Teacher asks: 1. What is speech? 2. Have you noticed how your voice changes when asking questions or making statements? Students’ Activities: Students respond based on experience. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains: Meaning of Intonation Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice in speech. Examples: 1. You are coming. ↘ 2. Are you coming? ↗ Teacher demonstrates clearly with voice variation. Students’ Activities: Students listen and repeat after the teacher. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains the two types of intonation: 1. Falling Tone ( ↘ )

Voice falls at the end of the sentence. Uses and Examples A. Statements 1. She is happy. ↘ 2. I am going home. ↘ 3. They have finished the work. ↘ 4. My father is a teacher. ↘ B. Commands 1. Sit down. ↘ 2. Close the door. ↘ 3. Open your books. ↘ 4. Stop talking. ↘ C. WH-Questions 1. What is your name? ↘ 2. Where are you going? ↘ 3. Why did you come late? ↘ 4. How did you solve it? ↘ 5. Who is at the door? ↘ D. Exclamations 1. What a beautiful girl! ↘ 2. How wonderful this is! ↘ 3. What a pity! ↘ E. Certainty / Finality

1. That is the end. ↘ 2. I am sure of it. ↘ 2. Rising Tone ( ↗ ) Voice rises at the end of the sentence. Uses and Examples A. Yes/No Questions 1. Are you coming? ↗ 2. Is he your brother? ↗ 3. Do you understand? ↗ 4. Can you swim? ↗ 5. Did you see him? ↗ B. Requests 1. Can you help me? ↗ 2. May I come in? ↗ 3. Could you lend me your pen? ↗ C. Uncertainty / Doubt ● You are serious? ↗ ● He is coming? ↗ ● This is correct? ↗ D. Surprise / Echo Questions ● You won the prize? ↗ ● He stole your phone? ↗

● They cancelled the exam? ↗ E. Incomplete Thoughts ● If you come early, ↗ we will start. ↘ ● When he arrived, ↗ everyone was happy. ↘ ● Contrast (Important) ● You are coming. ↘ (statement) ● You are coming? ↗ (question) ● He finished the work. ↘ (certainty) ● He finished the work? ↗ (doubt). Tips for Mastering Intonation 1. Listen to correct pronunciation. 2. Practice reading aloud. 3. Observe punctuation marks. 4. Avoid flat (monotone) speech. Students’ Activities: Students practice reading examples aloud and identifying tones. Step 4: Application Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher writes sentences on the board for students to identify tones and read aloud. Class Activity

Identify the tone ( ↘ or ↗ ): 1. What is your name? → ↘ 2. Are you ready? → ↗ 3. Sit down. → ↘ 4. Can I come in? → ↗ 5. Where do you live? → ↘ 6. Do you understand? → ↗ 7. What a lovely day! → ↘ 8. You are coming? → ↗ Students’ Activities: Students carry out their class activity in their notes. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks: 1. What is intonation? 2. Mention two types of intonation. 3. Give two examples of falling tone. 4. Give two examples of rising tone. Students’ Activities: Students respond orally or in writing. Assignment 1. Write five sentences using a falling tone.

2. Write five sentences using a rising tone. Reference Materials New Oxford English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, Book One. New Concept English for SS Schools

title: CONT. WRITING - EXPOSITORY COMPOSITION
subject: English Language
rawText:
Date : 12 th May, 2025 Theme: Continuous Writing Subject: English Language Theme : Continuous Writing Topic: Expository Essay Specific Objectives: At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to: I] explain the expository essay Ii] mention some examples of expository essay topics Iii] identify the format/ steps for writing good expository essays / features iv) write good expository essays. Instructional Resource: The format / steps for writing good expository [features] essay written on a chart. Step I: Identification of Prior Ideas Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: The teacher ask the students to say what essay writing is all about. Students’ Activities : The students give their explanations. Step II: Exploration Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: The teacher explains an essay further, and ask the students to mention three types of essay they have learnt. Students’ Activities: The students mention the types of essay. Step III: Discussion Mode: Entire

Teacher’s Activities: The teacher guide the students using the instructional resource in the following: An expository essay is an explanatory essay in which the writer exposes, informs, explains, instructs, criticizes or analyses some concepts or situations to the reader. It allows the writer to show his or her capabilities for logical thought and reasoning. Examples of expository essay topics include : a) The consequences of indecent dressing b) HIV/AIDS: causes and remedies / solutions. c) Causes of Armed Robbery in our society. d) How to prepare red oil in my village e) Dangers of drug abuse Format: i) Title written in capital letters. ii) Introduction: Make an introductory statements about the topic using definitions, analysis etc. iii) Body: Discuss the whole process, exposing the causes and effects of something using logical analysis with good paragraphs, presentation of facts with examples. iv) Conclusion: Draw your conclusions and make judgements, writing out the importance and advantages or solutions. Students’ Activities: Students make some contributions in their various groups. Step IV: Application Mode: Entire Class

Teacher’s Activities: The teacher guide the students in explaining the expository essay, identifying the steps / features and mentioning some examples of topics under the expository essay. Students’ Activities: The students make some contributions on the given topics. Step V: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: The teacher assesses the students’ level of understanding of the lesson by asking these questions. I] Explain the expository essay Ii] Mention three examples of topics that are expository in nature iii) State the format for a good expository essay / steps iv) Develop the first paragraph of an expository essay on the topic: “Causes of Armed Robbery in our Society” Assignment: Write an expository essay on : Choices and Consequences. References: i) New Concept English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by F. AdemolaAdeoye et al Ii] Essential English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Latilo T. A. and Olooku A. T.

title: READING A PASSAGE FOR MEANING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Comprehension Date: ………….. Class: SS 1 Time: ……………………………………………………………………….. Period ……………………………………….. Duration: …………………………………………………………………… Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Comprehension Skills Lesson Topic: Reading a Passage for Word Meanings Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. read a comprehension passage fluently, and identify unfamiliar words in a passage, 2. use contextual clues to determine the meanings of words, 3. give synonyms of selected words from a passage, 4. use the words correctly in sentences. Instructional Resources ● Comprehension passage from New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1 ● English dictionary ● /Whiteboard ● Marker. LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS

Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What do you do when you come across a difficult word while reading? 2. Can the meaning of a word be guessed from the sentence in which it appears? 3. What is context? 4. Why is it important to understand the meanings of words in a passage? Students' Activities Students respond based on their experiences in reading comprehension passages. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Teacher explains that comprehension involves understanding a passage and determining the meanings of words from the context in which they are used. What is Context? Context refers to the words, phrases, and sentences surrounding a word that help the reader determine its meaning. Ways of Determining Word Meanings in a Passage

1. Using context clues. 2. Looking for synonyms in nearby sentences. 3. Looking for antonyms or contrasts. 4. Studying examples given in the passage. 5. Using prior knowledge. 6. Consulting a dictionary where necessary. Students' Activities Students listen attentively, ask questions, and take notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Teacher directs students to a selected comprehension passage from New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1. The teacher: Reads the passage aloud while students follow. Invites students to read portions of the passage. Guides students to identify unfamiliar words. Leads discussion on how contextual clues help reveal meanings. Explains selected vocabulary items from the passage. Illustrative Examples Teacher may use the following examples to demonstrate how context helps in determining word meanings: Passage Extract: Ade is a very diligent student. He studies regularly and completes all his assignments on time. Because of his hard work, he has become one of the

most outstanding students in his school. His teachers often commend him for his excellent performance. Although some students find their studies tedious, Ade remains focused and determined. His success has become a source of inspiration to his classmates. Word Meaning from Context Synonym Diligent Hardworking Industrious Outstanding Excellent; exceptional Remarkable Commend Praise Applaud Tedious Boring; tiresome Monotonous Inspiration Something that motivates Encouragement Additional Vocabulary Practice Word Meaning Synonym

Prosperity Wealth and success Affluence Courage Bravery Boldness Generous Willing to give Kind-hearted Scarcity Shortage Lack Abundant More than enough Plentiful Honest Truthful Sincere Fragile Easily broken Delicate Ancient Very old Antique Efficient Productive and effective Competent

Ambition Strong desire to succeed Aspiration Students' Activities Students: Read the passage silently and aloud. Identify unfamiliar words. Infer meanings from context. Suggest synonyms. Use selected words in sentences. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Class Activity Using the selected passage from New Oxford Secondary English Course, Book 1: List five unfamiliar words from the passage. State their meanings as used in the passage. Give a synonym for each word. Use any three of the words in meaningful sentences. Students' Activities Students carry out the activity individually and compare answers with classmates.

Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher's Activities Teacher asks students: 1. What is context? 2. Mention three ways of determining word meanings in a passage. 3. Explain the meanings of selected words from the passage read. 4. State the contextual clues that helped you determine the meanings. Students' Activities Students respond orally and in writing. ASSIGNMENT From the selected passage in New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1: Identify ten unfamiliar words. Give their meanings as used in the passage. Provide a synonym for each word. Use each word in a meaningful sentence. REFERENCE MATERIALS F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012). New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1. Learn Africa Plc, Lagos.

New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1. Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary. WAEC and NECO Recommended English Language Textbooks. Comprehensive English Language Textbooks.

title: SPEECH WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Continuous Writing Week: ………………… Date: …………………, Class: SS 1 Period: ………………… Time: ………………… Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Continuous Writing Lesson Topic: Speech Writing: An Address on a Prize Giving Day. Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Explain what speech writing is. 2. Identify at least three features of speech writing. 3. Read and analyse a sample speech. 4. Write a simple speech on a given topic. Instructional Materials 1. Chart showing features of speech writing 2. Recommended textbook (New Concept English Book 1) 3. Whiteboard Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Ideas Mode: Individual students

Teacher’s Activities: The teacher asks: 1. On occasions like a school ceremony, what do you think makes a speaker’s message clear and interesting? 2. If you are given the opportunity to speak on your school’s Prize Giving Day, what important ideas would you like to share with your audience? 3. What parts do you think a good speech should contain for it to be well-organized and easy to understand? 4. How should a speaker begin and end a speech in order to capture attention and leave a lasting impression? Students’ Activities: Students respond based on prior knowledge. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Whole class Teacher’s Activities: Guides students to understand speech writing. What's speech writing? Speech writing is the process of organizing ideas into a structured format for oral delivery. Gives examples of occasions for speeches: ● Prize Giving Day. ● Birthday celebrations.

● Send-forth ceremonies. ● School events. Teacher directs students to read a sample speech provided below: Sample Speech Writing A speech delivered by Miss Grace Daniel, the Head Girl of Government Secondary School, Tudun Wada, Wuse Zone 4, Abuja, on the occasion of the Graduation Ceremony held on 20th July, 2026, at the School Hall of Excellence. The Principal, Vice Principals, Distinguished Guests, Members of Staff, Proud Parents, My Fellow Graduating Students, Ladies and Gentlemen. I feel highly honoured to stand before you today to speak on the topic “Honest Labour.” This occasion marks not only the end of our secondary school journey but also the beginning of greater responsibilities in life. Honest labour is the foundation of true success. In a world where many seek shortcuts to wealth and fame, we must remember that lasting achievement comes through diligence, integrity, and perseverance. As students, we have been taught that there is dignity in labour. Whether in academics, vocational skills, or daily responsibilities, honest effort always yields positive results.

Throughout our years in this school, we have faced challenges—difficult examinations, demanding assignments, and moments of discouragement. However, it is through consistent hard work that we have reached this important milestone today. This proves that honest labour truly pays. Furthermore, honest labour builds character. It teaches us discipline, patience, and responsibility. These qualities are essential as we move into higher institutions and the larger society. We must resist the temptation to engage in malpractice, fraud, or any dishonest means of success. Instead, let us remain committed to doing what is right at all times. To my fellow graduates, I urge you to uphold the values we have learned. Let us be ambassadors of honesty and hard work wherever we go. The future belongs to those who are willing to work for it with integrity. In conclusion, honest labour is not just a virtue—it is a necessity for a meaningful and successful life. As we step into the next phase of our journey, let us carry this principle with us and practice it daily. Thank you, and God bless you all. Students’ Activities: Students listen attentively and read the sample speech. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Whole class Teacher’s Activities:

Teacher leads discussion on features of speech writing: 1. Title: ● Reflects the topic (e.g., Honest Labour) ● Should suit audience and purpose 2. Introduction ● Begins with greetings ● Captures audience attention. ● States purpose of speech. 3. Body ● Main ideas presented clearly. ● Supported with examples, stories, facts. ● Answers: who, what, where, when, why, how 4. Conclusion ● Summarizes key points. ● Ends memorably. Students activities: Students listen attentively, participate actively and take down notes. Step 4: Application Mode: Individual students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher gives class exercise: You are to deliver a speech on your school’s Prize Giving Day titled “The Joy of Finishing Well.” Outline your points.

Students’ Activities: Students write the outlines in their notebooks. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks: 1. What is speech writing? 2. Mention three features of speech writing. 3. State two things you observed in the sample speech. 4. Give an example of opening greetings in a speech. Students’ Activities: Respond to questions Assignment Write a full speech to be delivered on your school Prize Giving Day titled: “The Joy of Finishing Well.” Reference Materials Oxford English Language for Senior Secondary Schools Book 1 F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. (2012), New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1, Learn Africa Plc, Lagos (pp. 134–135).

title: COMPLEX SENTENCES
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Structure Week: __________ Date: __________ Class: SS 1 Period: Time: __________ Duration: 40 Minutes Unit Topic: Sentence Structure Lesson Topic: Complex Sentences Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define a complex sentence and identify the parts of a complex sentence. 2. Distinguish between the main clause and the subordinate clause. 3. Construct correct complex sentences. 4. Use complex sentences appropriately in speech and writing. Instructional Materials Whiteboard and marker Flashcards containing clauses Charts showing examples of complex sentences English Language textbook Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Knowledge (Orientation) Mode: Individual

Teacher's Activities The teacher asks: 1. What is a sentence? 2. What is a clause? 3. Can a sentence have more than one clause? Students' Activities Students respond based on their prior knowledge. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities The teacher explains: Meaning of a Complex Sentence A complex sentence is a sentence that contains one main (independent) clause and at least one subordinate (dependent) clause. A subordinate clause cannot stand alone because it does not express a complete thought. Examples 1. Because it was raining, we stayed indoors. 2. When the bell rang, the students entered the classroom. 3. Although he was tired, he continued working. 4. If you study hard, you will pass the examination. Students' Activities

Students listen attentively and copy the notes. Step 3: Discussion (Conceptualisation) Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities The teacher explains the components of a complex sentence. A. Main Clause (Independent Clause) This clause can stand alone and make complete sense. Examples: We stayed indoors. The students entered the classroom. He continued working. You will pass the examination. B. Subordinate Clause (Dependent Clause) This clause cannot stand alone. Examples: Because it was raining When the bell rang Although he was tired If you study hard Common Subordinating Conjunctions Time Cause/Reason Condition

Contrast when because if although while since unless though before as provided that whereas after because of the fact that in case even though More Examples of Complex Sentences 1. Because she was sick, she missed school. 2. When the teacher arrived, the class became quiet. 3. Although he is rich, he lives simply. 4. If you obey the rules, you will succeed. 5. Since the road was flooded, we delayed our journey. 6. After the match ended, the fans celebrated. Students' Activities

Students identify the main and subordinate clauses in the examples. Step 4: Application (Investigation) Mode: Group Work / Entire Class Teacher's Activities The teacher divides students into groups and gives the following exercises. Class Activity A Identify the main clause and subordinate clause in the following sentences: 1. Although she was hungry, she continued working. 2. When the rain stopped, the children went outside. 3. Because he studied hard, he passed the examination. Expected Answers Main Clause: She continued working. Subordinate Clause: Although she was hungry. Main Clause: The children went outside. Subordinate Clause: When the rain stopped. Main Clause: He passed the examination. Subordinate Clause: Because he studied hard. Class Activity B Complete the following: Although he was tired, __________. If you work hard, __________. When the assembly ended, __________. Because she was ill, __________.

Class Activity C Construct five complex sentences using: because although when after if Students' Activities Students complete the exercises individually and in groups. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities The teacher asks: 1. What is a complex sentence? 2. What are the two parts of a complex sentence? 3. Mention five subordinating conjunctions. 4. Construct two complex sentences of your own. Students' Activities Students answer the questions orally and in writing. Assignment Write ten complex sentences using different subordinating conjunctions.

Underline the main clause and circle the subordinate clause in each sentence. Reference Materials New Oxford English Course for Senior Secondary Schools New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools Banjo, Ayo et al., New English Project WAEC Chief Examiners' Reports Nigerian Educational Research and Development Council (NERDC) English Language Curriculum.

Define a complex sentence and identify the parts of a complex sentence. 2. Distinguish between the main clause and the subordinate clause. 3. Construct correct complex sentences. 4. Use complex sentences appropriately in speech and writing. Instructional Materials Whiteboard and marker Flashcards containing clauses Charts showing examples of complex sentences English Language textbook Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Knowledge (Orientation) Mode: Individual

Teacher's Activities The teacher asks: 1. What is a sentence? 2. What is a clause? 3. Can a sentence have more than one clause? Students' Activities Students respond based on their prior knowledge. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities The teacher explains: Meaning of a Complex Sentence A complex sentence is a sentence that contains one main (independent) clause and at least one subordinate (dependent) clause. A subordinate clause cannot stand alone because it does not express a complete thought. Examples 1. Because it was raining, we stayed indoors. 2. When the bell rang, the students entered the classroom. 3. Although he was tired, he continued working. 4. If you study hard, you will pass the examination. Students' Activities

Students listen attentively and copy the notes. Step 3: Discussion (Conceptualisation) Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities The teacher explains the components of a complex sentence. A. Main Clause (Independent Clause) This clause can stand alone and make complete sense. Examples: We stayed indoors. The students entered the classroom. He continued working. You will pass the examination. B. Subordinate Clause (Dependent Clause) This clause cannot stand alone. Examples: Because it was raining When the bell rang Although he was tired If you study hard Common Subordinating Conjunctions Time Cause/Reason Condition

Contrast when because if although while since unless though before as provided that whereas after because of the fact that in case even though More Examples of Complex Sentences 1. Because she was sick, she missed school. 2. When the teacher arrived, the class became quiet. 3. Although he is rich, he lives simply. 4. If you obey the rules, you will succeed. 5. Since the road was flooded, we delayed our journey. 6. After the match ended, the fans celebrated. Students' Activities

Students identify the main and subordinate clauses in the examples. Step 4: Application (Investigation) Mode: Group Work / Entire Class Teacher's Activities The teacher divides students into groups and gives the following exercises. Class Activity A Identify the main clause and subordinate clause in the following sentences: 1. Although she was hungry, she continued working. 2. When the rain stopped, the children went outside. 3. Because he studied hard, he passed the examination. Expected Answers Main Clause: She continued working. Subordinate Clause: Although she was hungry. Main Clause: The children went outside. Subordinate Clause: When the rain stopped. Main Clause: He passed the examination. Subordinate Clause: Because he studied hard. Class Activity B Complete the following: Although he was tired, __________. If you work hard, __________. When the assembly ended, __________. Because she was ill, __________.

Class Activity C Construct five complex sentences using: because although when after if Students' Activities Students complete the exercises individually and in groups. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities The teacher asks: 1. What is a complex sentence? 2. What are the two parts of a complex sentence? 3. Mention five subordinating conjunctions. 4. Construct two complex sentences of your own. Students' Activities Students answer the questions orally and in writing. Assignment Write ten complex sentences using different subordinating conjunctions.

Underline the main clause and circle the subordinate clause in each sentence. title: STRUCTURE - PRONOUNS AND TYPES
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS 1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- STRUCTURE UNIT TOPIC:- PRONOUNS LESSON TOPIC:- PRONOUNS AND THEIR TYPES TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1) define pronoun 2) identify their types and uses 3) make sentence with pronouns 4) identify their position in a sentence. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES:- A cardboard containing list of types of pronouns PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHERS ACTIVITIES:- The teacher asks the question, what is a noun? STUDENTS ACTIVITIES:- The students respond by saying that a noun is a name of a person, animal, place or thing. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHERS ACTIVITIES:- The teacher asks the students to give words that can replace names of people and thing. STUDENTS ACTIVITIES:- The students respond by giving words like he/she, it. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHERS ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resources guides the students on the following: A pronoun can be described as a replacement for a noun to avoid repetition. TYPES OF PRONOUNS INCLUDE! 1)PERSONAL PRONOUNS:- They are: i)First person: The person speaking Eg I (singular) plural/we ii)Second person: The person or thing spoken to Eg You. iii)Third person: The person or thing that is spoken about or that is being discussed. Eg He, she, it plural they. 2)DEMONSTRATIVE PRONOUNS:- These are this, that (singular) these, those (plural) * This is my father * These are my friends * Those are my brothers standing across the road.

3)POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS:- These are called possessive pronouns because they indicate possession. Eg My, mine, our, ours, yours, her, hers, his, theirs, their, its. i) The principal has refused to release our bags (noun) Our (a possessive pronoun) functions as an adjective qualifying the noun bags. ii) Her father is the new minister of education. Her qualifies the noun father. However, if there is a verb between the possessive pronoun and a noun, it will perform the function of a pronoun, as in the following sentences: a) Theirs is a unique case Theirs functions as the subject of the verb is. b) The building across the road is ours Ours functions as the subject complement. 4)INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS:- They are used to ask questions. Egs What, who, where, when, whose, whom, which. * What is your name? * Which of the building is yours? * Who sent you on this dangerous journey? 5)REFLEXIVE PRONOUNS:- They make reference to the subject in the sentence. Eg himself, herself, myself, itself, themselves, ourselves, yourselves. * My mother washes her clothes herself. Herself still refers to ‘my mother’ who is the subject in the sentence. Note: Reflexive pronouns are called emphasizing pronouns when they occur immediately after the subject in the sentence. Examples i)My mother herself washes her clothes ii)The president himself visited the scene of the crisis. 6)RELATIVE PRONOUNS:- These are the same set of pronouns under interrogative pronouns. Here the relative pronouns are used to introduce relative clause. These are who, whom, which, which, that, whose, when, where etc. Examples * The man who was detained is now president. * This is the house where I was born. * The landlord whose house was burgled has reported to the police * The dress which my husband bought for me suits my shape. 7)INDEFINITE PRONOUNS:- They do not refer to particular or specific people or things. They are used in general sense. Eg some, somebody, one, someone, no one, everybody, none, all, everyone, everything, many, several, few, more, much, any, both, either etc. * None of the students was present at the seminar * Somebody is here to see the manager * Everybody is free to go home now * Tell me more * One must remember the incident

Note: (i) A singular indefinite pronoun should not be referred to as if it were a plural. For example , it is incorrect to say: ‘Everyone must have their fair share of the blame’. The correct thing to say is that: ‘Everyone must have his fair share of the blame’. (ii) It is e qually wrong to switch from the indefinite pronoun one to another pronoun. For instance, it is incorrect to say: ‘One must not miss his chance. ‘The correct thing to say is: ‘One must not miss one’s chance.’ 8)RECIPROCAL PRONOUNS:- These indicate an exchange of an action between two or more people. These are: each other and one another. Each other refers to two people. E.g Dayo and Sola fought each other. One another refers to more than two. E.g The candidates taught one another in the hall. 9)CASE: NOMINATIVE AND OBJECTIVE PRONOUNS:- Some pronouns are nominative pronouns. They can only be used to function as subjects of verbs in sentences. Some other ones are objective pronouns; they function only as objects in sentences. Nominative pronouns are used as subjects of verbs. Examples • I walk down the road every day. • You come to visit once in a while. • He comes to visit once in a while. STUDENTS ACTIVITIES:- The students respond by making sentences with examples of the types of pronouns. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHERS ACTIVITIES:- The teacher asks the students to make sentence with the types of pronouns. STUDENTS ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teachers question by making sentences thus: Indefinite pronouns Everybody is free to go home One must remember the incident Reflexive pronouns My mother washes her clothes herself. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHERS ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the lesson with the following questions: 1) What are pronouns? 2) List out nine (9) types of pronouns. 3) Give examples of each of the types. 4) Make sentence with each of the types.

STUDENTS ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teachers questions actively. ASSIGNMENT 1) Make three (3) sentences with relative pronouns 2) Make two (2) sentences with possessive pronouns. REFERENCES: 1) New concept English Bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) Essentials of English by Latilo T. A et al (2008) 3) Complete English course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011)

title: READING FOR MEANING IN CONTEXT
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN Theme: Comprehension Date: ___________________ Class: SS 1 Time: ___________________ Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Week: ___________________ Unit Topic: Comprehension Lesson Topic: Reading for Word Meaning in Context Specific (Behavioural) Objectives At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Read a passage fluently and intelligently and determine the meanings of unfamiliar words from context. 2. Identify contextual clues in a passage. 3. Give synonyms of selected words. 4. Use the words correctly in sentences. Instructional Resources ● Comprehension passage from New Oxford Secondary English Course ● Dictionary ● Whiteboard ● Marker LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: Identification of Prior Ideas

Mode: Individual Teacher's Activities Teacher asks: 1. What do you do when you come across an unfamiliar word while reading? 2. Can a word's meaning be determined without using a dictionary? 3. What is context? Students' Activities Students respond based on previous experiences. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire Class Teacher's Activities Teacher guides students to explain context and ways to find meaning in context: Context refers to the surrounding words, phrases, and sentences that help reveal the meaning of a word. Ways of Finding Meaning in Context ● Synonym clues ● Antonym clues ● Explanation clues ● Example clues ● General sense of the passage Students' Activities Listen attentively and take notes.

Step 3: Discussion The teacher directs students to a selected passage from New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools. The teacher guides students to identify unfamiliar words and determine their meanings from context. Illustrative Examples Word Meaning in Context Synonym Diligent Hardworking Industrious Commend Praise Applaud Tedious Boring Monotonous Scarcity Shortage Lack Abundant Plenty Plentiful Students' Activities Read the passage.

Identify difficult words. Infer meanings using context clues. Step 4: Application Class Activity Using the passage: 1. List five unfamiliar words. 2. State their meanings. 3. Give a synonym for each. 4. Use each word in a sentence. Step 5: Evaluation Teacher asks students: 1. What is context? 2. Mention three context clues. 3. Explain the meanings of selected words from the passage. 4. Use the words in sentences. Assignment Read another passage from New Oxford Secondary English Course and identify ten words whose meanings can be inferred from context. Reference Materials New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools. F. Ademola-Adeoye et al. New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools. Oxford Advanced Learner's Dictionary.

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH ADVERTISING.
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN 1 Theme: Vocabulary Development Week: __________ Date: __________ Class: SS 1 Period: Time: Duration: 40 minutes Unit Topic: Vocabulary Development Lesson Topic: Words Associated with Advertising. Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define advertising. 2. Identify words associated with advertising. 3. Explain the meanings of the words. 4. Use the words correctly in sentences. Instructional Materials: ● Whiteboard and marker ● Flashcards ● Sample adverts/posters. Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Knowledge Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks:

ORIENTATION PHASE ● “When you see a message on TV or a poster that makes you want to buy something, what do you think makes it so convincing?” ● “Why do some products become very popular even when many similar ones exist?” CONCEPTUALISATION PHASE ● “What words can we use to describe the message used to promote a product and the people it is meant for?” ● “How can we describe the name, message, and strategy used by companies to attract buyers?” INVESTIGATION PHASE (An advert is given) ● “Study this advert carefully. Identify and list the key elements used to attract buyers (e.g., message, audience, product type, and appeal).” ● “Work in groups to create a short advert for a product. Identify the product, give it a name, create a slogan, and state the target audience.” Students’ Activities: Students respond based on experience.

Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher explains: What is advertising? Advertising is the act of promoting goods and services to attract buyers. Words Associated with Advertising (Meanings & Examples) 1. Advertisement (Advert): A public notice promoting a product. I saw an advertisement on television. 2. Product: Goods or services sold. This product is very effective. 3. Brand: A particular make of a product. That brand is popular worldwide. 4. Consumer: A person who buys or uses goods. Consumers prefer quality goods. 5. Market: A place or system for buying and selling. The company targets a large market. 6. Promotion: Activities to increase sales. The promotion attracted many buyers.

7. Slogan: A catchy phrase. The slogan is easy to remember. 8. Billboard: Large outdoor advert. The billboard is attractive. 9. Endorsement: Support by a celebrity. The product received endorsement from a star. 10. Target Audience: Intended consumers. The advert targets young people. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher guides students to read a passage on advertising and use the words the words associated with advertising: Examples: 1. The advertisement was convincing. 2. The product is affordable. 3. The brand is trusted. 4. The slogan attracts customers. 5. The target audience is teenagers. Students’ Activities: Students form sentences using the words. Step 4: Application

Mode: Entire class Teacher guides students through class activity: Class Activity Fill in the blanks: 1. A catchy phrase is called a _______. (slogan) 2. A buyer is a _______. (consumer) 3. Goods being sold are _______. (products) 4. A large outdoor advert is a _______. (billboard). Students’ Activities: Students complete the exercise. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks: 1. What is advertising? 2. Mention three advertising words. 3. State the meaning of those words. 4. Use “product” in a sentence. Students’ Activities: Students respond. Assignment Write five sentences using advertising vocabulary. Reference Materials

New Oxford English Course Book 1. New Concept English book 1.

title: STRUCTURE - COMPLEX TENSE FORMS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Complex Tense Forms Tense implies the use of a verb, phrasal verb or verb phrase to show the time of an action or to show the state expressed by such a verb or phrasal verb or verb phrase. It also implies using a verb, phrasal verb or verb phrase to show continuance of action or the completion of the action expressed by such verb. TYPES OF TENSES 1) The simple present tense 2) Present continuous tense 3) Present perfect tense 4) Present perfect continuous tense 5) Simple past tense 6) Past perfect tense 7) Past perfect continuous tense 8) Future tense THE SIMPLE PRESENT TENSE:- It is used to express habitual actions, general truths or statements. Examples (i) The word is spherical (ii) The students are taught by qualified teachers (iii) The pastor preaches the truth (iv) She comes to visit us every weekend. PRESENT CONTINUOUS TENSE:- This indicates that an action is still on at the time of speaking or waiting. A primary auxiliary verb is used with the – ing form of the main verb. Examples: (i) The teacher is teaching now (ii) The students are being taught (passive words) PRESENT PERFECT TENSE:- This shows that an action which started and was completed in the past still has a link with the present. In this case, the modal auxiliary verbs- has and have are used with the participle form of the main verb. Examples: (i) The boy has passed the test (ii) The have warned the teacher to mind his business. Present perfect tense also indicates that an action which started in the past has not been concluded. Examples: (i) My husband has gone to church (He left sometime in the past and has not returned as at the time of speaking or event) (ii) The plane has arrived (It is still at the airport) PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS TENSE:- This expresses an action that began in the past and is still continuing. It shows that an action has not been concluded. Examples: (i) I have been teaching for ten years (ii) He has been building his house since last year.

SIMPLE PAST TENSE:- This shows that an action started and was completed in the past. It also indicates a past habit which the person being referred to is no more involved in. Examples: (i) I was employed in 1991(passive voice) (ii) He used to travel home when he was young (has stopped travelling home). Etc The teacher guides the students in explaining the complex tense as she directs their attention to the instructional resource. The complex tense form has more than one verb. This verb will always have an auxiliary verb (helping verb) and the main verb. Auxiliary verbs include: Be – is, are, am, was, were, being, been Have – has, had Do – does, did, done These verbs can also be the main verb in a sentence, as in! • Ade is a good student • He did his homework • He had his bag The auxiliary verbs also help us to form a negative or a question. Examples – She went to school-> she did not go to school. | | | simple tense verb main verb. Did she go to school? | | auxiliary main verb verb Another set of auxiliary or helping verbs we use to form complex tenses are modal verbs, which are always used with other verbs to express possibility, ability, permission, necessity, willingness or advice or obligation. Examples: You can sit down now | | Model main Auxiliary verb I could dance for two hours some years ago. | | Pass main verb Tense ASSIGNMENT:- Complete the following sentences using the simple (present or past) and the continuous (present or past) tense forms. a) Wole Soyinka – the novel many years ago (write) b) The laundry man – the curtains when they came in (wash)

c) The new students – noise always (make) REFERENCES 1) New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools Bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye 2) New Comprehensive English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Matins Izuchukwu Amaechi 3) Essential English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Latilo T A. et.al.

pages.text: Complex Tense Forms Tense implies the use of a verb, phrasal verb or verb phrase to show the time of an action or to show the state expressed by such a verb or phrasal verb or verb phrase. It also implies using a verb, phrasal verb or verb phrase to show continuance of action or the completion of the action expressed by such verb. TYPES OF TENSES 1) The simple present tense 2) Present continuous tense 3) Present perfect tense 4) Present perfect continuous tense 5) Simple past tense 6) Past perfect tense 7) Past perfect continuous tense 8) Future tense THE SIMPLE PRESENT TENSE:- It is used to express habitual actions, general truths or statements. Examples (i) The word is spherical (ii) The students are taught by qualified teachers (iii) The pastor preaches the truth (iv) She comes to visit us every weekend. PRESENT CONTINUOUS TENSE:- This indicates that an action is still on at the time of speaking or waiting. A primary auxiliary verb is used with the – ing form of the main verb. Examples: (i) The teacher is teaching now (ii) The students are being taught (passive words) PRESENT PERFECT TENSE:- This shows that an action which started and was completed in the past still has a link with the present. In this case, the modal auxiliary verbs- has and have are used with the participle form of the main verb. Examples: (i) The boy has passed the test (ii) The have warned the teacher to mind his business. Present perfect tense also indicates that an action which started in the past has not been concluded. Examples: (i) My husband has gone to church (He left sometime in the past and has not returned as at the time of speaking or event) (ii) The plane has arrived (It is still at the airport) PRESENT PERFECT CONTINUOUS TENSE:- This expresses an action that began in the past and is still continuing. It shows that an action has not been concluded. Examples: (i) I have been teaching for ten years (ii) He has been building his house since last year.

SIMPLE PAST TENSE:- This shows that an action started and was completed in the past. It also indicates a past habit which the person being referred to is no more involved in. Examples: (i) I was employed in 1991(passive voice) (ii) He used to travel home when he was young (has stopped travelling home). Etc The teacher guides the students in explaining the complex tense as she directs their attention to the instructional resource. The complex tense form has more than one verb. This verb will always have an auxiliary verb (helping verb) and the main verb. Auxiliary verbs include: Be – is, are, am, was, were, being, been Have – has, had Do – does, did, done These verbs can also be the main verb in a sentence, as in! • Ade is a good student • He did his homework • He had his bag The auxiliary verbs also help us to form a negative or a question. Examples – She went to school-> she did not go to school. | | | simple tense verb main verb. Did she go to school? | | auxiliary main verb verb Another set of auxiliary or helping verbs we use to form complex tenses are modal verbs, which are always used with other verbs to express possibility, ability, permission, necessity, willingness or advice or obligation. Examples: You can sit down now | | Model main Auxiliary verb I could dance for two hours some years ago. | | Pass main verb Tense ASSIGNMENT:- Complete the following sentences using the simple (present or past) and the continuous (present or past) tense forms. a) Wole Soyinka – the novel many years ago (write) b) The laundry man – the curtains when they came in (wash)

c) The new students – noise always (make) REFERENCES 1) New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools Bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye 2) New Comprehensive English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Matins Izuchukwu Amaechi 3) Essential English Language for Senior Secondary Schools by Latilo T A. et.al.

title: SUMMARIZING A GIVEN PASSAGE.

LESSON PLAN Theme: Summary Week: __________ Date: __________ Class: SS 1 Period: Time: Duration: 40 minutes Unit Topic: Summary Writing Lesson Topic: Summarizing a Given Passage. Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Define summary. 2. Identify main ideas in a passage. 3. State rules of summary writing. 4. Summarize a given passage correctly. Instructional Materials: Whiteboard and marker Photocopies of summary passage Lesson Presentation Step 1: Identification of Prior Knowledge Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks: What is a summary?

Why do we summarize passages? Students’ Activities: Students respond. Step 2: Exploration Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Meaning of Summary Summary is the act of reducing a passage to its main ideas using your own words. Students’ Activities: Students listen and repeat. Step 3: Discussion Mode: Entire class Teacher’s Activities: Steps in Summary Writing Read the questions first. Read the passage carefully. Identify main ideas. Write in your own words. Use correct number of sentences. Avoid lifting. Proofread your work. What to Avoid Copying directly Writing irrelevant points

Using phrases Exceeding sentence limit Students’ Activities: Students discuss and explain steps. Step 4: Application Mode: Entire class Class Activity Passage: Advertising helps companies inform people about their products. It also persuades consumers to buy goods. However, some adverts may mislead people. Questions: (a) In two sentences, summarize the importance of advertising. (b) In one sentence, state a disadvantage. Answers: (a) Advertising informs people about products. It persuades consumers to buy goods. (b) Some advertisements can be misleading. Students’ Activities: Students write answers in their notebooks. Step 5: Evaluation Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks:

What is a summary? Mention two rules of summary writing. What should you avoid? Students’ Activities: Students respond. Assignment Summarize a passage from WASSCE past questions in three sentences. title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH STOCK EXCHANGE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Theme: Vocabulary Date: ………….. Class: SS 1 Time: ……………………………………………………………………….. Period ……………………………………….. Duration: …………………………………………………………………… Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Vocabulary Lesson Topic: Words Associated With Stock Exchange Specific (Behavioural) Objectives: At the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. explain what a stock exchange is, 2. list at least five (5) words associated with stock exchange, 3. state the meanings of those words, 4. form sentences with them. Instructional Resources: Chart showing stock market activities, newspaper with stock listings, sample share certificate (if available). LESSON PRESENTATION Step 1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks students: 1. What do you understand by the stock exchange? 2. Have you heard of buying and selling shares? 3. Can you mention any word related to stock exchange?

Students’ Activities: Students respond based on their prior knowledge. Step 2: EXPLORATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher guides students on the meaning of stock exchange. What is Stock Exchange? A stock exchange is a market where shares, stocks, and other securities are bought and sold. It is an organised system that allows investors to trade financial instruments. Students’ Activities: Students listen, repeat key points, and take notes. Step 3: DISCUSSION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher guides students to learn key vocabulary: S/NO WORD MEANING SENTENCE 1 Share A unit of ownership in a company. She bought shares in a bank.

2 Stock The capital raised by a company through shares. He invested in stock last year. 3 Investor A person who puts money into business. The investor gained profit. 4 Dividend Profit paid to shareholders. The company paid a dividend. 5 Broker A person who buys and sells shares for others. The broker handled the trade. 6 Market A place where buying and selling occur. The stock market is active today. 7 Exchange A system where securities are traded. Lagos has a stock exchange. 8 Portfolio A collection of investments.

His portfolio includes many shares. 9 Trading Buying and selling of stocks. Trading continues every weekday. 10 Price The value of a share. Share prices increased today. Students’ Activities: Students mention more words, define them, and form sentences. Step 4: APPLICATION Mode: Entire Class Teacher’s Activities: Teacher gives students class activity: Class Activity: List five words related to stock exchange. Write one sentence for each word. Students’ Activities: Students complete the task in their notebooks. Step 5: EVALUATION Mode: A Couple of Students Teacher’s Activities: Teacher asks: 1. Define stock exchange. 2. List five words associated with stock exchange.

3. State their meanings. 4. Use them in sentences. Students’ Activities: Students respond orally and in writing. ASSIGNMENT: List ten words associated with stock exchange, state their meanings, and use each in a sentence. REFERENCE MATERIALS: New Concept English for Senior Secondary Schools, Book 1. Business Studies Textbooks. Newspapers (Financial pages).

title: TYPES OF SENTENCES
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON PLAN 1 Theme: Structure Week: ………………… Date: ………………… Class: SS 1 Period: ………………… Time: ………………… Duration: 40 Minutes Subject: English Language Unit Topic: Types of Sentences Lesson Topic: Types of Sentences (Continued) 1. Behavioural Objectives By the end of the lesson, students should be able to: 1. Identify different types of sentences. 2. Distinguish between simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex sentences. 3. Construct correct examples of each type. 4. Analyze sentence structures accurately. 2. Instructional Materials Whiteboard Marker/ Sentence charts Flash cards 3. Entry Behaviour Students already understand:

Basic sentence structure Clauses (independent and dependent) 4. Presentation Step I: Prior Knowledge (5 minutes) Teacher writes: The girl laughed. The girl laughed and clapped. The girl laughed because she was happy. Teacher asks: What differences exist in these sentences? Teacher introduces: Types of Sentences (Continued). Step II: Exploration (15 minutes) 1. Simple Sentence A sentence with one independent clause. Examples: 1. The boy runs. 2. She is singing. 3. We enjoyed the party. 4. The teacher explained the lesson. 5. My father works hard. 2. Compound Sentence A sentence with two or more independent clauses, joined by coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, so, yet). Examples:

1. She sang and he danced. 2. I called him, but he did not answer. 3. The sun set, and the sky became dark. 4. We can go now, or we can wait till later. 5. He was tired, yet he continued working. 3. Complex Sentence A sentence with one independent clause and at least one dependent clause. Examples: 1. I will come if you invite me. 2. She cried because she was hurt. 3. When the bell rang, the students left. 4. Although it was raining, we continued playing. 5. He failed the exam because he did not study. 4. Compound-Complex Sentence A sentence with at least two independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses. Examples: 1. I came and I saw when you called me. 2. She was singing and he was dancing because they were happy. 3. We will start the meeting and we will end early if the chairman arrives. 4. The teacher explained the topic and the students listened because they were interested. 5. He studied hard and he passed the exam although it was difficult.

6. Evaluation (10 minutes) A. Identify the type: 1. The boy kicked the ball. 2. I tried, but I failed. 3. If you work hard, you will succeed. 4. She sang and he danced because they were excited. B. Construction: Write: 1. Two simple sentences 2. Two compound sentences 3. Two complex sentences 4. One compound-complex sentence 7. Assignment Write a paragraph of 6–8 sentences and: Underline each sentence Label each as simple, compound, complex, or compound-complex 8. Summary Teacher revises: Definitions Structural differences Multiple examples for clarity If you want to take this to an exam-standard level, I can also: Add WAEC/JAMB objective questions Provide error-analysis exercises

title: STRUCTURE - NOUN PHRASE
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- STRUCTURE UNIT TOPIC:- PHRASE LESSON TOPIC:- NOUN PHRASE TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1] explain a phrase 2] define noun phrase 3] mention examples of noun phrase 4] identify the noun phrases in sentences. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCE:- A cardboard paper showing examples of noun phrases PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the question, give three(3) uses of the definite article. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question, that the three uses are ‘The’ is used for group of year e.g in ‘the eighties’ ‘The’ is used for unique items. Eg the sun, the equator etc We use ‘the’ to single out an item or a person. Eg ‘the tallest boy’ etc. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to give examples, the types of noun. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s question/ instructions. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the cardboard paper guides the students in the following: A phrase is a group of words without a finite verb. A noun phrase is a group of words with the noun as the headword. Examples; The bag The sun An orange, a goat etc. NOUN PHRASE IN SENTENCE

The driver almost hit a goat Chinwe threw an orange to her friend The sun was setting when they came back. The lady has woken up. The dog has been barking The president has just left Australia. In a noun phrase, there can be many words before the noun. Egs! The bag The Italian bag The lovely Italian bag The lovely expensive Italian bag The new lovely expensive Italian bag ORDER OF WORDS- Article, opinion (adjective) origin, noun. FUNCTIONS OF THE NOUN PHRASE 1) As the subject of the verb. Example, the old man still sings well (N oun phrase as subj. of the verb ‘sing’) 2) As the object of the verb in a sentence Example, John lost three home workbooks (Noun phrase as obj. of the verb ‘lost’) 3) Subject complement Example, Olu is the doctor (the doctor is the same person as Olu). 4) Object complement. Example, I gave Sola the money The money completes the meaning of Sola (obj. of the verb ‘gave’). 5) Complement of a preposition. E.g. The man sees beyond the ordinary The ordinary functions as the object of the preposition ‘beyond’ 6) In Apposition to a noun E.g. Nigeria, the oil- rich giant of Africa, attained independence in 1960 - The underlined noun phrase is in appositions to the noun Nigeria. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- As the teacher explains the students are actively involved. STEP IV: APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to give examples of noun phrase as the subject of the verb and as the object of the verb. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the question/ instruction given by the teacher. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the topic with the following questions.

1) What is a noun phrase? 2) Give four examples of noun phrase plus the definite article 3) Give three examples of noun phrase plus the indefinite article ‘a’ and ‘an’. 4) Give three examples of noun phrase with sentence. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students actively respond to the teachers questions. ASSIGNMENT Answer question 1 (a-d) 2) (a-d) page 13 of your English text book. REFERENCES 1) New Concept English book 1 , by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) NERDC Comprehensive English book 1, by Unoh S. O et al (2009) 3) Complete English Course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011). Essential English Language by Latilo T. A et al (2008)

title: STRUCTURE - NOUNS
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBUJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- STRUCTURE UNIT TOPIC:- NOUNS LESSON TOPIC:- TYPES OF NOUNS TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1) define a noun 2) list the types of nouns 3) explain the types of nouns 4) make sentences using the examples of the types of nouns INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCE:- A cardboard paper containing the types of noun and their examples. PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to mention six(6) words associated with home and family. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question, words associated with home and family include: aunt, nephew, uncle, grandson, grandfather, tables, refrigerator etc. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to mention the objects in the classroom. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resource guide the students as follows: A noun can simply be defined as a word used to name people or persons, things, ideas and concepts, subjects, days, months, animals etc. A noun is also a name of a person, thing, place or quality. TYPES OF NOUNS Proper noun Common noun Collective noun Abstract noun Concrete noun etc

PROPER NOUN:- This refers to the specific names of persons, cities etc. Examples, Tunde, Funke, John, Lagos, Kano, Nigeria, Africa, January, Monday, Dr. etc. COMMON NOUN:- This is a general name of things, concepts, animals, and ideas. Examples; town, girl, school, men, women, boy etc. COLLECTIVE NOUN:- This is a noun used to refer to a group of things or a class of individuals. eg. A bunch of keys, plantains A fleet of cars A flock of sheep A team of players Also; class, committee, congregation, assembly etc. ABSTRACT NOUN:- These are things or concepts that cannot be touched or seen; they exist in our imagination. We know they exist by experience and feeling. Egs. Virtue, love, idea, wisdom, joy etc. CONCRETE NOUN:- They can be seen, touched, etc. Examples; Phone, Car, ,house, boy, table, chair etc. COUNTABLE NOUNS:- All nouns are categorized into either countable or uncountable nouns. Countable nouns are those that can be counted. They have singular and plural forms eg. book – books boy - boys woman – women etc. UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS:- (non- count nouns) they cannot be counted. They have only the singular form e.g Water, blood, kerosene, rice, sand, anger, fuel etc. These can be expressed in plural form by using partitives e.g. a piece of furniture (singular) pieces of furniture (plural) COMPOUND NOUNS:- These are made up of two or more words e.g Father- in- law - fathers – in – law Passer- by - passers – by Secretary- general - secretary- generals Commander- in- chief - commanders- in- chief STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students are actively involved. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher guide the students in forming sentences with the following types of nouns- common noun, collective nouns, abstract nouns and concrete nouns and in mentioning more examples of them. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question. TYPES OF NOUNS Proper noun Common noun Collective noun Abstract noun Concrete noun etc

PROPER NOUN:- This refers to the specific names of persons, cities etc. Examples, Tunde, Funke, John, Lagos, Kano, Nigeria, Africa, January, Monday, Dr. etc. COMMON NOUN:- This is a general name of things, concepts, animals, and ideas. Examples; town, girl, school, men, women, boy etc. COLLECTIVE NOUN:- This is a noun used to refer to a group of things or a class of individuals. eg. A bunch of keys, plantains A fleet of cars A flock of sheep A team of players Also; class, committee, congregation, assembly etc. ABSTRACT NOUN:- These are things or concepts that cannot be touched or seen; they exist in our imagination. We know they exist by experience and feeling. Egs. Virtue, love, idea, wisdom, joy etc. CONCRETE NOUN:- They can be seen, touched, etc. Examples; Phone, Car, ,house, boy, table, chair etc. COUNTABLE NOUNS:- All nouns are categorized into either countable or uncountable nouns. Countable nouns are those that can be counted. They have singular and plural forms eg. book – books boy - boys woman – women etc. UNCOUNTABLE NOUNS:- (non- count nouns) they cannot be counted. title: NOUN CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText: 05-18 9:23 PM NOUN CLAUSE A noun clause is a group of words that acts as a noun in a sentence. It has a subject and a verb but does not express a complete thought on its own. * Key Features: 1. Functions as a noun 2. Contains a subject and predicate 3. Usually begins with words like that, what, who, whom, whose, which, when, where, why, how, if, whether * Functions of a Noun Clause: 1. As a Subject What she said is true. (Here, “What she said” is the subject) 2. As an Object of a Verb I know that he is honest. (“that he is honest” is the object of “know”) 3. As an Object of a Preposition She is worried about what will happen. 4. As a Subject Complement The problem is that we are late. Examples: I don’t understand why he left. Whoever comes first will win the prize. Tell me what you want. * Simple Tip: If you can replace the clause with a single noun (like something), it’s likely a noun clause. Example: I know that he is right → I know this. EXERCISE Identify the noun clause in each sentence and state its function. 1. I know that she is hardworking. 2. What he said surprised everyone. 3. We are thinking about where to spend the holiday. 4. The truth is that he lied to us. 5. Whoever wins the match will receive a prize. 6. She asked whether I was ready. 7. I cannot imagine how they escaped. 8. What you need is confidence. Notein Scan the QR code to download Notein

subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS 1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- STRUCTURE UNIT TOPIC:- NOMINALIZATION LESSON TOPIC:- NOMINALIZATION OF ADJECTIVES AND VERB TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1) define nominalization 2) identify how a verb can form nouns by addition of a suffix 3) identify how an adjective can be derived from noun by addition of suffix 4) give examples of words that can be used as both verbs and nouns in a sentence. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES:- List of words where some verbs and adjectives charged to nouns PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to define a noun STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question that a noun is a name of a person, animal, place or thing. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to give examples of adjectives and verbs. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resources guides the students in the following: Nominalization is the process of producing a noun from another part of speech through the addition of derivational affixes. Examples. VERB SUFFIX NOUN Move - ment movement React - ion reaction Refuse - al refusal Fail - ure failure ADJECTIVE Careless - ness carelessness

Difficult - y difficulty Intense - ity intensity Capable - ity capability MORE EXAMPLES ADJECTIVES NOUNS Kind kindness Wide wideness Cruel cruelty Ready readiness Honest honesty Tired tiredness VERBS NOUNS Arrange arrangement Agree agreement Add addition Inform information Sing singer Post postage Teach teacher Preach preacher IN SENTENCE CONTEXT 1a) I need a change (Noun) b) I will change (verb) 2) Fight a) They always fight each other (fight verb) b) There was a fight between the two men (fight noun) 3a) Ade is a brilliant boy (adjective) b) The brilliant will always pass (noun) STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students give their own examples changing verbs and adjectives to nouns. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to change the following adjectives into nouns. Bright, accurate, wise, intelligent STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teachers question that we can have the following nouns from the adjectives given; Bright brightness Accurate accuracy Wise wisdom Intelligent intelligence STEP V:- EVALUATION

Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the lesson with the following questions; 1) What is nominalization? 2) Give four (4) examples to show how verb can be changed to nouns 3) Give four (4) examples to show how adjectives can be derived from nouns 4) Write four (4) sentences showing how words can be used as verb and nouns in sentences STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond actively to the teachers questions. ASSIGNMENT Do exercise on page 92 (1-5) of your class text book. REFERENCES 1) New Concept English bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) Complete English Course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011) 3) Essential English Language by Latilo T. A et al (2008)
