title: CONT. WRITING - NARRATIVE COMPOSITION
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- CONTINUOUS WRITING UNIT TOPIC:- ESSAY/ COMPOSITION LESSON TOPLIC:- NARRATIVE COMPOSITION TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to: 1) define a narrative composition 2) mention examples of topics under the narrative composition 3) identify useful hints in writing a narrative composition 4) write narrative composition on any topic using the hints given. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCE:- A cardboard sheet containing list of the types of topics under the narrative composition PRESENTATION STEP I:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to mention the types of composition they have studied. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s instruction that, we have the following types: Narrative, Descriptive, Expository and Argumentative compositions. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask Joy to stand up. She asks Joy to tell the class what she did at home on Sunday? STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The student (Joy) narrated what she did last Sunday hence responding to the teacher ’ s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resource guide the students on the following: A narrative essay is a straight forward account of real or imaginary events or incidents. A narrative essay is one that requires you to narrate an event, to tell a story or relate how an incident happened. TOPICS UNDER THE NARRATIVE ESSAY/ COMPOSITION INCLUDE: 1) My first day at school 2) A day I will never forget 3) My first journey to Lagos

4) How I spent my Corona Virus shutdown of two weeks 5) How I spent my last Christmas holiday 6) The day I visited the zoo 7) The kidnapping incident I witnessed 8) The day I met an AIDS patient etc USEFUL HINTS USED IN WRITING A NARRATIVE COMPOSITION INCLUDE: a) Your essay must have a title which must be underlined b) Make use of the past tense only c) Present the events in logical/ natural sequence (ie) chronological order of presentation. d) Language used has to be simple and straight forward e) Discuss one main idea in each paragraph f) Be concerned with the incident or event, the persons involved and the time and place, when and where the incident happened g) Your story must be believable, credible and possible h) At the end of the account, comment on your pleasure, surprise, regret, anger etc. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- As the teacher explains, the students are actively involved STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode : Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students from what they have learnt today, to explain what a narrative composition is. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students explain that a narrative composition / or essay is a complete account of a story, an event or incident which the writer experienced or witnessed. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the topic with the following questions: 1) What is a narrative composition or essay? 2) List out five topics under the narrative essay 3) Mention six (6) useful hints / good qualities of a narrative essay 4) Choose a topic and decide on the points you will develop in each paragraph. STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teachers questions. ASSIGNMENT:- Write a narrative essay on any of the following : My first day at secondary school. (b) A day I will never forget REFERENCES:- 1) New Oxford English for SS1 by Ayo Banjo et al (2020) 2) Complete English course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011) 3) Essential English by Latilo T. A et al (2008)

STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHERS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The teacher articulates the sounds / O / and / & / Using the instructional resource, she guides the students on the following: To produce these sounds the tip of the tongue touches the front teeth with the tongue touching the front teeth with the mouth slightly open. While /O / is voiceless, / 7/ is voiced. / O / as in: Thin, think, thought, threw, fourth, pith, worth, three, theme, thanks, north, throat, breath, mouth, thing, author, oath, thought, earth, method, forth, theory, thief, path, bath, thigh, teeth etc / & / as in:

Then, that, those, these, breathe, booth, though, there, father, brother, bathe, rhythm, leather, either, breathing, worthy, thine, sheath, moth, clothe, southern, etc CONTRASTING THE SOUNDS / & / AND / O / / / / / Breathe breath Clothe cloth Mother method Worthy lengthy STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- AS the teacher explains, the students are actively involved. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode Individual TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher guide the students in forming sentences using some of the words listed out. STUDENT ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The students form sentence using these words thus: a) I think the wealthy man deserves a big ‘thank you’ ii) The southerners and the Northerns are thankful to Mr. President. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHER ’ S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the students ‘level of understanding of the lesson with these questions. 1) Articulate the sounds / O / and / & / 2) Mention six(6) words for each of the sounds / O / and / & / 3) Describe the sounds / O / and / & / 4) Form sentences with these words: Loathe, smooth, clothe STUDENTS ’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher ’ s questions. ASSIGNMENT:- Choose correct option 1) / / (a) then (b) den (c) something (d) father 2) / / (a) mother (b) teacher (c) deem (d) earth 3) / / (a) thanks (b) three (c) though ((d) thief 4) / / (a) rhythm (b) other (c) these d) author REFERENCES: 1) Complete English Course for Senior Secondary School by Ukamaka C Ibe (2011) 2) Oral English for Schools by Vicky Odozie (2009)

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH INVESTMENT
subject: English Language
rawText: 05-24 6:20 PM Investment Vocabulary Notes What is Investment? Investment means putting money, time, or effort into something with the hope of gaining profit or benefit in the future. Example: Buying shares in a company Saving money in a fixed deposit account Starting a business Words Associated with Investment Word and their Meaning Example Sentence Capital Money used to start or grow a business The company raised capital for expansion. Profit Money gained after expenses are removed Investors hope to make a profit. Loss Money lost in an investment He suffered a loss in the stock market. Shares Units of ownership in a company She bought shares in a bank. Dividend Part of a company’s profit shared with investors The company paid a yearly dividend. Interest Extra money earned from savings or loans The bank gives 5% interest yearly. Risk Possibility of losing money Every investment has some risk. Return Profit or benefit from an investment Real estate gives good returns. Asset Something valuable owned Land is an important asset. Liability Debt or financial obligation Loans are liabilities. Portfolio Collection of investments He has a strong investment portfolio. Bond Money lent to government or company She invested in government bonds. Stock Market Place where shares are bought and sold The stock market changes daily. Inflation Increase in prices over time Inflation reduces purchasing power. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES: - The students respond to the teacher’s question by mentioning different items in the home such as Fan , tables, fridge, chairs, utensils etc STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: - The teacher explains home and family: A home is a place of residence or refuge. It is usually a place in which an individual or a family can rest and store personal properties. A family is a group of people who are usually affiliated by birth (biological) or marriage. A family group consist of father, mother and their children. WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH HOME INCLUDE:

Kitchen, utensils, wardrobe, living room, store / pantry, dining room, bed room, toilet, bed, chair and upholstery etc WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH FAMILY INCLUDE: Brother, sister, parents, in-laws, elders, siblings, uncles, cousins, aunts, wives, women, men, nephew, nieces, son, spouse, husband, step brother, grandson, grandfather, father in-law, daughter etc. Cousin – uncles or aunties child Aunt - father’s or mother’s sister Step brother - son of step parent Spouse - husband or wife Husband - woman spouse Grandfather - parents father Father in-law- spouses father Uncle - parents brother The teacher with the instructional resource shows the students more words on home and family thus: Nuclear family, single parent, immediate family, extended family, blood relative, chest of drawers, arm chair, television, radio, plate, pot etc STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES: - As the teacher explains, the students are actively involved. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: - The teacher ask the students the meaning of the following words and guide them in forming sentences with the words : (a) Nuclear family (b) Extended family c] Daughter d] Inlaw e] Niece. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES: - The students respond to the teacher’s question. A nuclear family is a family that is made up of father, mother and their children. An extended family is a family made up of father, mother, children, uncles, aunts, grandfather, grandmother etc. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHERS ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the students’ level of understanding of the lesson with the following questions. 1) What do you understand by family? 2) List out six words associated with home 3) Mention six words that are associated with family 4) Who is your stepbrother? title: ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Argumentative Essay 📘 An argumentative essay is a type of essay where you present your opinion about a topic and support it with strong reasons and evidence. In this essay, you: Choose a position (for or against) Give reasons to support your opinion Provide examples or facts Sometimes explain the opposite view and show why your view is better Structure of an Argumentative Essay 📝 1. Introduction Introduce the topic Give background information State your thesis statement (your main opinion) 2. Body Paragraphs

Each paragraph should contain: A clear point (reason) Explanation Example or evidence 3. Counter-Argument (Optional but Important) Mention the opposite opinion Explain why you disagree with it 4. Conclusion Restate your opinion Summarize your main points End strongly ✏ Example of an Argumentative Essay

Topic: Should Students Use Mobile Phones in School? Mobile phones have become very important in our daily lives. However, many schools do not allow students to use them. I believe that students should be allowed to use mobile phones in school for learning purposes. Firstly, mobile phones help students to research information quickly. With internet access, students can look for meanings of words, solve mathematics problems, and learn new things. This makes learning easier and faster. Secondly, mobile phones help in communication. In case of emergency, students can contact their parents immediately. This makes both students and parents feel safe. Some people argue that mobile phones distract students during lessons. This may be true if students misuse them. However, teachers can make rules to control how phones are used in school. In conclusion, mobile phones should be allowed in schools because they help learning and improve communication. Proper rules can prevent distraction. If you like, I can:

title: SYNONYMS
subject: English Language
rawText: 05-13 7:53 PM Note on Synonyms Meaning of Synonyms Synonyms are words that have the same or nearly the same meaning. They help make speaking and writing more interesting and less repetitive. Examples Word Synonyms Happy joyful, cheerful, glad Big large, huge, enormous Small tiny, little, miniature Fast quick, rapid, speedy Smart intelligent, clever, bright Important Notes About Synonyms 1. Synonyms may differ slightly in meaning Example: Slim means thin in an attractive way. Skinny may sound negative. 2. Some synonyms are formal while others are informal Example: Ask → informal/common Inquire → formal 3. Synonyms depend on context Example: “Strong tea” is correct. “Powerful tea” sounds unnatural. Sentences with Synonyms The boy was happy after the game. → The boy was joyful after the game. The house is big. → The house is large. She is a smart student. → She is an intelligent student. The car is fast. → The car is speedy. Notein Scan the QR code to download Notein

Class : SS 1 Theme : Speech Unit Topic : Consonant Sounds Lesson Topic : Consonant Sounds / j, z, 3 / Duration : 40 Minutes Time : Period : Instructional Objectives : At the end of the lesson, the students should able to : 1] articulate the consonant sounds / j , z ,3 / 2] define the consonant sound 3] mention words with the consonant sounds: / j, z , 3 / 4] form sentences with some of the word examples of the consonant sounds: / j , z , 3 / Instructional Resources : Flashcards showing the word examples of the Consonant Sounds/ j ,z ,3 /. Presentation Step 1 – Identification of Prior Ideas Mode – Individual Teacher’s Activities : The teacher ask the students to articulate the consonant sounds / j, z , 3 /. Students’ Activities : The students articulate the consonant sound / j, z , 3 /. Step 2 – Exploration Mode – Individual Teacher’s Activities : The teacher guide the students in defining the consonant sound, and ask the students to mention five examples of consonant sounds they know. Students’ Activities – The students define the consonant sounds and mention some examples they know. S tep 3 - Discussion Mode – Entire Teacher’s Activities – The teacher guide the students using the instructional resource in the lesson delivery. Consonant Sounds are sounds produced with obstruction of air at certain points between the lungs and the mouth.

/ j / is a voiced palatal which is produced with the front of the tongue raised and the lips in spread position. The sound occurs only before a vowel. It has the following spelling forms: Y – at the beginning of words as in you, youth, yeast, yes, yesterday, yam, yarn, yawn, yell, yellow, yet, yield, yolk, young, yelp, yard, etc. U – Unity, university, union, unit , use, utility, / Z / has the following spelling forms : Z – Zoo, prize, zoom, size, zinc, zip, breeze, etc, S – present, rose, nose, eyes, house [ verb], fees, was, boys, easy, lose, etc. X – exhaust , exhort, exalt, exactly, example, exhume, etc / 3 / has the following spelling forms : Si - conclusion, television, vision, illusion, provision, division, etc. Su -measure, treasure, usual, leisure, pleasure, closure, casual, visual, etc. G – garage, regime, prestige, camouflage, etc Z – seizure, etc. Students’ Activities – The students participate in the lesson. Step 4 – Application Mode – Individual Teacher’s Activities – The teacher guide the students in mentioning more word examples of the consonant sounds / j, z, and 3 /, and in forming sentences with the word examples. Students’ Activities – The students mention more word examples of the consonant sounds and form sentences with them. Step 5 – Evaluation Mode – Individual Teacher’s Activities – The teacher assesses the students’ level of understanding of the lesson by asking these questions. 1] Articulate these consonant sounds / j, z, 3 / 2] Define consonant sound 3] Choose the option that has the consonant sounds represented below : A] / j / a] union b] jug c] joke B] / z / a] boys b] scissors c] fence

C] / 3 / a] vision b] judge c] general 4] Form sentences with these words : casual, decision, university, breeze. Students’ Activities – The students answer the questions. Assignment – Write out five word example of the consonant sounds / j, z, 3 /. References – Oral English for Schools by Vicky Odozi.

title: STRUCTURE - REGULAR AND IRREGULAR VERBS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Structure – Regular and Irregular Verbs. The simplest definition of a verb is that it is an action word; it tells what a noun or pronoun does in a sentence. (It indicate action, a doing or a state of being.) Examples- sleep, dance, stop, talk etc. There are two types of verbs namely; regular and irregular verbs. REGULAR VERBS:- Thus; verbs are said to be regular if its past and past participle are formed by merely adding ed or d to the base or root form. IRREGULAR VERBS:- These verbs do not have fixed form. Their past and past participle are formed in different ways. title: INDEPENDENT/DEPENDENT CLAUSES
subject: English Language
rawText: 05-18 6:44 AM Note Clauses A clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a predicate (verb). Types of Clauses 1. Independent Clause An independent clause expresses a complete thought and can stand alone as a sentence. Examples: The baby cried loudly. My father repaired the car. We enjoyed the match. 2. Dependent Clause A dependent clause does not express a complete thought and cannot stand alone. It usually begins with subordinating conjunctions such as: because although when if since while Examples: because she was ill when the bell rang although they tried hard Example in a Sentence: The girl smiled because she passed the examination. Independent Clause: The girl smiled Dependent Clause: because she passed the examination Notein Scan the QR code to download Notein

title: STRUCTURE - DEFINITE ARTICLES
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- STRUCTURE UNIT TOPIC:- NOUNS LESSON TOPIC:- THE DEFINITE ARTICLE AND ITS FUNCTION WITH THE NOUNS. TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1) define nouns 2) identify the use of countable nouns with indefinite article 3) identify the use of countable nouns with the definite articles. 4) answer questions on nouns and the definite article/ indefinite article INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES :- A cardboard paper containing examples of words with the definite articles. PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students this question- mention five types of nouns you have studied. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s question that we have: proper nouns, common nouns, collective nouns, abstract nouns and concrete nouns. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to mention examples of countable and uncountable nouns. STUDENTS ACTIVITIES:-The students respond to the teacher’s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resource guide the students on the following: A noun is a name of a person, animal, place or things. It is a naming word.

All nouns are categorized into either countable or uncountable nouns. Countable nouns are nouns that can be counted. They have singular and plural forms eg chair, table etc. Uncountable nouns cannot be counted and they have only singular forms eg water, rice, oil etc. Articles: ‘a’ and ‘an’ can be used before any noun to refer to a general item eg a bag, an attitude, an apple , a book, etc. ‘The’ is referred to as the definite article because it refers to something specific or unique. The definite article in referential usage with nouns. READ THE FOLLOWING CAREFULLY 1) The water you bought is warm 2) I asked for soup but the soup you brought was watery. 3) The iron I bought yesterday did not work 4) What did you do with the money I gave you? 5) Buy me the paper Tuesday,please. Each of the expressions: The water, the soup, the iron, the money, the paper contains an uncountable noun used with the definite article. The meaning of each one is different when these uncountable nouns are used without the definite article. ‘The water you bought for me’ refers to a definite amount of water presented either in a glass or a container. The same is true of each one of the examples. Some of them eg ‘the paper’ have special meanings. - Here we are talking about a particular kind of paper. Unlike ‘a’ or ‘an’, ‘the’ can precede both uncountable and countable nouns. We do not use ‘a’ or ‘an’ with plural or uncountable nouns. ‘The’ is used for unique items ie when there is only one of such items eg the sun, the equator, the President, the Duchess of Cambridge. Items shared by a group of people are: Preceded by ‘the piano, the door, the broom, the’ floor etc. Exception We do not use ‘the’ for the groups of items below: Abstract nouns. Eg. Love, Art etc Illness/ skin, problems eg. malaria, pimples Proper nouns- Ahmadu Bello University, Port Harcourt Direction- north, night

Planets eg. Jupiter, Mars etc. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- As the teacher explains, the students are actively involved. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students from what they have learnt to give two(2) instances where the use of definite article ‘the’ is possible. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s question, that we use the definite article ‘the’ to single out an item or a person using adjectives, as in ‘ the tallest boy’ We can also use ‘the’ with only adjectives to refer to people and things. Eg Kehinde is the most handsome boy. We use ‘the’ for groups of years as in ‘the seventies’ Eg. Those shoes were popular in the, eighties, proper nouns can actually take ‘the’ when we want to show a difference. Eg The Kano I used to know was better than the present one. It is now very noisy. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher evaluates the lesson with the following questions: 1) What is a noun 2) What are countable and uncountable nouns? 3) Mention with examples four ways where the definite article ‘the’ can be used with nouns. 4) Mention with examples; Exceptions to the use of definite articles STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s questions. ASSIGNMENT:- The teacher ask the students to answer questions on (page 27) 1-3 and complete the dialogue on the same page by putting ‘the’ where necessary. REFERENCES: 1) New Concept English Book 1, by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) NERDC Comprehensive English by Unoh S. O etal (2009) 3) Complete English Course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011)

title: WRITING - MECHANICS IN WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- WRITING UNIT TOPIC:- MECHANICS IN WRITING LESSON TOPIC:- MECHANICS IN WRITING TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1) define mechanics in writing 2) identify and explain the components of writing mechanics. 3) correctly apply the components in writing. 4) write short essays / stories to demonstrate proper mechanics. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES:- List of major punctuation marks and their examples / students’ notes / text books . PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS. Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to read a poorly punctuated and uncapitalized sentences. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students read the sentences with difficulty in understanding it. STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher discusses the difficulty in understanding the sentences with the students, and ask the students to mention the reasons for the difficulty . STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students mention some of the reasons. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resources guide the students in the lesson . Mechanics in writing refer to the technical rules used to make writing clear, readable, and meaningful. They include : capitalization, punctuation, spelling, spacing, indentation,

handwriting, and paragraphing. These mechanics ensure good communication between the writer and the read. Components of Writing Mechanics. 1] Capitalization : Capital letters are used : a] to begin every sentence. b] for proper nouns [ names of people, places, days, months, etc. ] c] for the pronoun ‘I’ d] for titles [ Mr., Dr., Chief, Mrs., etc.] Examples : a] Mr Ade lives in Lagos b] She said, ‘’I will travel tomorrow’’. 2] Punctuation Marks : This helps to clarify meaning, show pauses and organise written ideas. Examples of punctuation marks include : A] Full stop or the Period [ . ] : Ends a statement and is used after abbreviations and initials. B) Question mark:- (?) We use the question mark to end sentences that ask for a reply and direct questions. Examples: Will you give me the book? Will he come? Many questions are signaled by question work like ‘who’, ‘which’, ‘whose’, ‘whom’, when, where, why, and how? Whose clothes are these? Which is the old woman’s house? C] Exclamation Mark [ ! ] : Is used after interjections and exclamatory sentences. Eg. Hello !, Wow !, What a beautiful dress ! D) Semi- colon/;/ : Is used to join together independent clauses when a conjunction is not used. Eg. Man proposes; God disposes. E] Apostrophe [ ‘] : This is used to indicate possession or ownership. Eg. John’s father, the boy’s books. F] Quotation Marks [ or inverted commas] : [ “”, `’] This is used to enclose a direct speech. Eg. “ this is our house’’, said the boy. 3] Spelling : Correct spelling enhances clarity 4] Paragraphing : Paragraphs help to organise ideas. 5] Handwriting and Legibility : Handwriting should be neat, consistent, properly spaced and easily readable. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students copy the notes.

STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher give the students a passage which is not punctuated and ask the students to copy the passage and put correct punctuation. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s instruction. STEP V:- EVALUATION Mode : Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the topic with the following questions : 1) What do you understand by punctuation marks? 2) List out four examples of punctuation marks you know 3) Give examples of each 4) Use correct punctuation here: Have you seen him’ Yinka enquired STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond actively to the teacher’s questions. ASSIGNMENT:- The teacher ask the students to answer questions on page 51 of their class text book. REFERENCES: (1) Complete English Course by Ukamaka C Ibe (2011) (2) New Oxford Secondary English Course by Ayo Banjo et al (2007) (3) New Concept English bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013)

title: ACTIVE AND PASSIVE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Structure – Active and Passive Structures. When the subject of a sentence represents the doer of an action, the verb of the predicate is in the active voice. When the subject of a sentence represents the sufferer of the action, the verb of the predicate is in the passive voice. More often than not, verbs are used in the active, and less frequently in the passive Examples Active Passive Chikebroke the plate The plate wasbroken by Chike The workers swept the streetsThe streets were swept by the workers. Nkechiate the food The food was eaten by Nkechi When changing Active to Passive, the following must be noted: Only transitive verbs (i.e. verbs that receive objects can be used in the passive). This implies that the active sentence has an object that becomes the subject of the passive sentence The tense of the transitive verb in the active sentence determines the tense of be in the passive sentence. The preposition ‘by’ is introduced in the passive sentence. (not in all

cases except when absolutely necessary). Note that not all active sentences can be changed to passive because the passive form has its proper place and function in English. Consider the following Sentences with transitive verb: Ada travelled with Obi to Enugu She slept for a whole day. Sentences with linking verbs. He became a lawyer You friend seems a very nice person. Sentences with special transitive verbs like the following: They have a new house. The new dress fits the girl. She resembles her mother. The passive form should not be seen simply as an alternative to the active form. The main reason for using the passive is used To give due emphasis to the verb activity rather than the active subject: Coal is mined at Enugu. ‘Things Fall Apart’ was written in the 1950’s

When the doer of the action is not known. He was killed during the war.

title: STUDENTS SUMMARY NOTE
subject: English Language
rawText:
STUDENTS SUMMARY NOTE SPEECH Speech is the expression of thoughts and feelings through spoken words. Oral Composition Oral composition is the act of presenting ideas clearly through speaking. Expository Speech Expository speech is used to explain, inform or describe a topic clearly to listeners. Examples of expository topics: Importance of education Effects of examination malpractice Uses of modern technology Discussion Discussion is the exchange of ideas between two or more people on a particular topic. Debate Debate is a formal argument where speakers support or oppose a topic. Rules of Debate Speak clearly and confidently. Respect opposing opinions. Present logical points. Avoid abusive language. Importance of Good Speech Improves communication skills Builds confidence Encourages critical thinking Helps in public speaking

VOCABULARY Vocabulary refers to the words used in a language. Words Associated with Investment Speculator A person who buys and sells goods or shares hoping to make profit. Profit Margin The difference between cost price and selling price. Bullish A market condition where prices are rising. Bearish A market condition where prices are falling. Dividends Money paid to shareholders from company profits. Bankruptcy A condition where a person or company cannot pay debts. Sentence Examples The company paid high dividends this year. Many investors became worried during the bearish market. The trader was declared bankrupt after heavy losses. COMPREHENSION/SUMMARY Comprehension is the ability to read and understand a passage. Summary is the shortening of a passage by stating only the main points. Note Making Note making involves writing down important points from a passage. Steps in Note Making

Read the passage carefully. Identify the main ideas. Underline key points. Write short and clear notes. Importance of Note Making Makes revision easier Saves time Improves understanding Helps memory STRUCTURE Adjectival Clauses An adjectival clause is a group of words that describes a noun or pronoun in a sentence. It usually begins with words like: who whom whose which that Examples The boy who won the prize is my brother. This is the bag that I bought yesterday. The teacher whose car was stolen reported to the police. In the examples above, the underlined clauses describe nouns. Functions of Adjectival Clauses They give more information about nouns.

They make sentences clearer and more meaningful.

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH HOME AND FAMILY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Home-Related Vocabulary Parts of a House Rooms: living room, bedroom, kitchen, bathroom, dining room, study, garage, basement, attic Furniture & Appliances: sofa, armchair, bed, wardrobe, dresser, table, chair, fridge, oven, microwave, washing machine Outdoor Areas: garden, yard, balcony, porch, driveway, patio, fence, gate House Types: apartment/flat, cottage, bungalow, villa, townhouse, mansion Common Expressions Make yourself at home – feel comfortable as if you were in your own house. There’s no place like home – home is the most comfortable place. Home sweet home – expression of comfort on returning home. 🧑🧑🧒🧒 Family-Related Vocabulary Family Members Immediate Family: mother, father, parents, son, daughter, brother, sister, children, siblings Extended Family: grandparents, grandfather, grandmother, grandchildren, grandson, granddaughter, uncle, aunt, cousin, nephew, niece In-laws: mother-in-law, father-in-law, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, son-in-law, daughter-in-law Types of Families Nuclear family – parents and children only. Extended family – includes relatives beyond the nuclear family. Single-parent family – one parent raising children. Blended family – formed when parents remarry and combine children. Common Expressions

Like father, like son – children often resemble their parents in character or behavior. The black sheep of the family – a member who is considered different or an outsider. Runs in the family – a characteristic shared by family members.

title: SUMMARY WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE: 29 th October, 2024. CLASS: SS1C, 1A and 1D TIME: 8:00-8:40, 8:40-9:20, 10:30- 11:10 PERIOD: 1 st , 2 n and 4 th periods DURATION: 40minutes SUBJECT: English Language THEME: Summary UNIT TOPIC: Summary LESSON TOPIC: Introduction to summary writing. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES: At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to: 1. Explain what summary means 2. State some basic guidelines to summary writing 3. Read a selected passage. 4. Answer the summary questions by writing the answers in their notebook. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCES: A selected passage: New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools, page 89-90, a lab top. LESSON PRESENTATION: STEP1: IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEARS MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher asks the students to explain what summary is. Summary is giving a brief and concise account of a longer passage, leaving out illustrations and examples. STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The students explain what summary is based on their previous lessons on summary writing. SEP2: EXPLORATION MODE: The entire class

TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher guides the students to state some basic guidelines to summery writing. 1. Brevity: Summary answers should be short. 2. Conciseness: It should be straight to the point, avoiding irrelevances, preferably using simple sentences. 3. Avoid lifting the exact words of the writer. 4. Use your own words as much as possible. 5. Write only the required number of sentences. 6. Avoid writing multiple points in one sentence. STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The students state the guidelines to summary writing. STEP3: DISCUSSION MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher present the selected passage to the class and asks the students to read while she guides them where necessary. STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The students read the selected passage. Step4: APPLICATION MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher engages the students to answer the summary question by writing the answers in their notebook. She guides them to mention the first answer as an example; 1.Children should learn to do things by themselves. STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The students carry out the exercise. STEP5: Evaluation MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher asks the students to: 1. Explain summary writing 2. State the guides to summary writing 3. Read a selected paragraph from the passage and summarise in one sentence.

4. Mention the summary answers to the questions. STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The students answer the questions. ASSIGNMENT: REFERENCES 1. Ayo Banjo; New Oxford English Course for Senior Secondary schools. 2. Ukamaka Ibe; Complete English Course.

title: VOCAB. DEVELOP. - WORDS ASSO. WITH AGRICULTURE
subject: English Language
rawText:
DATE:- CLASS:- SS 1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT UNIT TOPIC:- Register LESSON TOPIC:- WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH AGRICULTURE TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to…. 1) define agriculture 2) mention words associated with agriculture 3) identify the meaning of such words 4) form sentences using some of the words mentioned. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCE:- A cardboard containing list of words associated with agriculture and their meaning. PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to mention four words associated with home and family. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s instruction/ question that four words associated with home and family include: HOME: utensils, sofa, living room, arm chair. FAMILY: brother, uncle, nephew, stepsister . STEP II:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher explains some of the words associated with the home and family further, and ask the students to mention some farming implement they know. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode : Entire class

TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resource guide the students on the following: Agriculture is the science or practice of farming, including the growing of crops and raising of animals for food, fiber and other products . [ The cultivation of land and the rearing of animals to provide food, wool and other products for human use.] WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH AGRICULTURE INCLUDES: CROPS:- grains (rice, maize, millet etc) seeds, seedlings, tubers, cassava, cocoyam, yam, carrot, onions etc ACTIVITIES:- bush clearing, planting, pruning, manure, fertilizer, weeding etc IMPLEMENT :- tractor, hoe, axe, cutlass, bulldozer, harvester, wicker basket etc OTHERS :- bumper harvest, a bad harvest, famine, crop rotation, a good harvest, drought, conservation, arable, fallow, humus, depletion, subsistence farming, irrigation, fodder etc ARABLE :- Land that is fit for cultivation, land that is being tilled CONSERVATION:- Planned preservation and management of natural resources to prevent exploitation FALLOW:- Land left uncultivated to regain its fertility and rejuvenation of its minerals. DEPLETION:- The process of draining land of its fertility value FODDER:- Coarse food for cattle, horse and sheep eg hay or corn. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- As the teacher explains, the students are actively involved. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher guide the students based on what they learnt today, to explain the following words: Subsistence farming and weeding. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s questions thus: Subsistence farming is the type of farming where by the farmer produces just enough food for his family consumption. Weeding is the process of removing unwanted plants from crops. STEP V:- EVALUTION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher evaluate the topic with the following questions 1) Define Agriculture 2) Mention ten (10) words associated with Agriculture 3) What is irrigation?

4) Form sentences with fertilizer and manure STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond actively to the teacher’s questions. ASSIGNMENT:- The teacher ask the students to do the exercise on page 27 of their class text book. REFERENCES: 1) New Oxford Secondary English Course for Senior Secondary Schools 1, by Ayo Banjo et al (2013). 2) NERDC Comprehensive English 1, by Unoh S. O et al (2009) 3) Oxford Advanced Learner’s Dictionary 7th edition.

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT
subject: English Language
rawText:
Students’ Summary Note Subject: English Language Topic: Vocabulary Development – Medicine Meaning of Medicine Medicine is the science and practice of diagnosing, treating, and preventing diseases to maintain good health. It also refers to drugs or substances used to cure illnesses. Items Found in a Hospital Stethoscope Thermometer Syringe Bandage Wheelchair Hospital bed Drip (IV fluid) Gloves Face mask X-ray machine Activities in a Hospital Examining patients Diagnosing illnesses Giving injections Performing surgery Dressing wounds Conducting laboratory tests Admitting and discharging patients Providing emergency care

Hospital Personnel Doctor: Diagnoses and treats patients. Nurse: Cares for patients and assists doctors. Pharmacist: Prepares and dispenses medicines. Surgeon: Performs operations. Laboratory Scientist/Technician: Conducts medical tests. Radiographer: Operates imaging equipment such as X-rays. Receptionist: Attends to patients and keeps records. Paramedic: Provides emergency medical care. Examples of Medical Vocabulary in Sentences The doctor used a stethoscope to listen to her heartbeat. The nurse gave the patient an injection. He was taken to the hospital for surgery. The pharmacist dispensed the prescribed medicine. The laboratory technician carried out a blood test. Importance of Medical Vocabulary Helps students communicate effectively in health-related situations. Improves understanding of hospital environments. Builds vocabulary for academic success. Promotes health awareness.

title: POETRY
subject: English Language
rawText:
WEEK THREE TOPIC 1: LISTENSING TO GRASP MAIN POINTS IN A POEM Poetry is an imaginative and emotional creative work of art meant to stimulate thought and to be enjoyed. It is the sum total of the use of certain devices in writing such as rhythm, rhymes, meter, figure of speech, stanza, verse, the poet’s feeling and attitude to the subject matter etc. TYPES OF POETRY Narrative poem: A poem that tells a story. Lyrics poem: A poem that is musical in nature Dramatic poem: Poem involving characters that interact in verse form. Some: A 14 lines poem. We have two types of sonnet. Petracchan Italian sonnet divided into octane and sestet with rhyming scheme of abba, abba, ade, ade. Shakespearean sonnet which has 3 set of four lines followed by a couplet. Pastorial poem: Poem on a country side or rural life Dirge: A poem for the dead. Epigram: Poem about the deeds of great people. Ode: Poem that addresses a person or thing. Others include: satire, ballad, epic, limericle, elegy etc. POETIVE DEVICES Verses/stanza: Poetry is written in verses or in stanzas. A stanza may be made up of 4 lines or more Imagery: Imagery is a mind picture. It is a collection of images or a mental picture called in mind by the use of concrete expression to appeal to the reader’s sense of imagination. Language: The language is the writer’s choice of words. It is also called “Diction”. The writer may choose to make his language simple and sometimes difficult. Poetry makes use of rhyme unlike prose. Setting: This is the time and place of the events or actions in a poem. Figure of speech: A phrase or a word having different meaning than its literal meanings.

ASSIGNMENT:Night rain is a poem written by John Pepper Clark on his experience as a boy. Listen carefully as the poem is read on page 230 and answer the questions on unit 5 page 66. CLASS ACTIVITIES AFRICA BY R.E.G AMARHOE I saw a maiden dark and lovely, sitting by a wayside, sad and lovely Oh pretty maiden, so dark and comely. Why sit by the wayside, sad and lonely? I am neither sad nor lonely, she said, but living, Sir, among the deaf and dumb, Relentlessly watching these shameless dead. Makes my warm heart grow very cold and dumb. The analysis of the above poem. The poem is an elegy (a poem that expresses sadness) it talks about a pretty lady with a warm heart who later became sad because of the circumstances that surround her. Devices used in the poem Setting: by the wayside – along the road Rhyming scheme: AB, AB, CD, CD. Imagery: pretty maiden, wayside, deaf and dumb, shameless, dead, heart. Figure of speech: Metaphor Answers to the questions on the poem Pg 77 New concept English. The mood of the maiden is sadness. Line 8 shows the evidence “makes warm heart grow very cold and numb. The lady felt that way because she is living among people that have no feelings. Line 6. The lady referred to here is a pretty maiden. She is from Africa- People from dark origin. Personification It is a metaphor Bad, dark, lonely, deaf, cold, numb.

The poem is an elegy (a poem that expresses sadness) it talks about a pretty lady with a warm heart who later became sad because of the circumstances that surround her. Devices used in the poem Setting: by the wayside – along the road Rhyming scheme: AB, AB, CD, CD. Imagery: pretty maiden, wayside, deaf and dumb, shameless, dead, heart. The lady felt that way because she is living among people that have no feelings. Line 6. The lady referred to here is a pretty maiden. She is from Africa- People from dark origin. Personification It is a metaphor Bad, dark, lonely, deaf, cold, numb.

DATE:- CLASS:- SS1 SUBJECT:- ENGLISH LANGUAGE THEME:- VOCABULARY UNIT TOPIC:- VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT LESSON TOPIC:- WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH FISHING AND ANIMAL HUSBANDRY TIME:- DURATION:- PERIOD:- INSTRUCTIONAL OBJECTIVES:- At the end of the lesson, the students should be able……… 1) define fishing and animal husbandry 2) list out words for fishing and animal husbandry 3) identify the meaning of such words 4) make sentence with such words. INSTRUCTIONAL RESOURCE:- A cardboard paper showing list of words for fishing and animal husbandry. PRESENTATION STEP 1:- IDENTIFICATION OF PRIOR IDEAS: Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVIES:- The teacher ask the students the question, list five(5) words associated with Agriculture. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s question. STEP:- EXPLORATION Mode: Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students to mention five(5) examples of domestic animals they know. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s question. STEP III:- DISCUSSION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher with the instructional resources guide the students on the following: Fishing has to do with the sport or job of catching fish.

Animal husbandry is the agricultural practice of breeding and raising of livestock. WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH FISHING INCLUDE: Spawning, bait, lure, shoal, fish hook, ripple, float, fish monger, fishing, fishery, angling, trawl, trawler, fishing rod, gaff etc Spawning- To cause fish to lay eggs in large quantities together. Angling- The art or sport of catching fish with a hook and line Trawl- A large open- mouthed fishing net with a wide mouth that is drawn along the sea bottom. Gaff- A stick with a hook at the end, used to pull big fish out of water. Ripple- A very small wave or waving movement. Shoal- A large group of fish swimming together. Fish monger- Someone who sells fish in a shop. WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH ANIMAL HUSBANDRY0 INCLUDE: Breeding, raising, livestock, ranches, milk, artificial insemination, herds, pen, cattle, veterinary doctor, piggery, poultry, dairy, farmer, pasteurized, pest etc STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- As the teacher explains the students are actively involved. STEP IV:- APPLICATION Mode : Individual TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher ask the students from what they have learnt to explain the meaning of these words : Veterinary doctor, dairy farm and gaff. STUDENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teachers question that; Dairy farm is a farm where milk is kept and where butter and cheese are made. Veterinary doctor- Is a doctor concerned with caring for the health of the animals. While Gaff- Is a stick with a hook at the end, used to pull big fish out of water. STEP V:- EVALUTION Mode: Entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITIES:- The teacher assesses the topic with the following questions: 1) What do you understand by fishing? 2) What is animal husbandry? 3) List out six (6) words for fishing and animal husbandry 4a) Who is a fish monger? b) What is angling? STUDENENTS’ ACTIVITIES:- The students respond to the teacher’s questions actively.

ASSIGNMENT:- Make a list of ten(10) domestic animals and their young once. REFERENCES:- 1) New Concept English Book 1, by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) Complete English Course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011) 3) Oxford Advanced Learners Dictionary 7th edition.

title: ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Students’ Summary Note Subject: English Language Topic: Vocabulary Development – Medicine Meaning of Medicine Medicine is the science and practice of diagnosing, treating, and preventing diseases to maintain good health. It also refers to drugs or substances used to cure illnesses. Items Found in a Hospital Stethoscope Thermometer Syringe Bandage Wheelchair Hospital bed Drip (IV fluid) Gloves Face mask X-ray machine Activities in a Hospital Examining patients Diagnosing illnesses Giving injections Performing surgery Dressing wounds Conducting laboratory tests Admitting and discharging patients Providing emergency care

Hospital Personnel Doctor: Diagnoses and treats patients. Nurse: Cares for patients and assists doctors. Pharmacist: Prepares and dispenses medicines. Surgeon: Performs operations. Laboratory Scientist/Technician: Conducts medical tests. Radiographer: Operates imaging equipment such as X-rays. Receptionist: Attends to patients and keeps records. Paramedic: Provides emergency medical care. Examples of Medical Vocabulary in Sentences The doctor used a stethoscope to listen to her heartbeat. The nurse gave the patient an injection. He was taken to the hospital for surgery. The pharmacist dispensed the prescribed medicine. The laboratory technician carried out a blood test. Importance of Medical Vocabulary Helps students communicate effectively in health-related situations. Improves understanding of hospital environments. Builds vocabulary for academic success. Promotes health awareness.

A syllable is a part of a word that contains a single vowel sound and that is pronounced as a unit of word. A stress is the emphasis placed on a particular syllable in a word in a phrase or sentence. The stressed is pronounced louder higher than the other syllables. Word of four syllable are also known as quadra syllabic words. Quadra syllabic words can either be stressed on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd or 4th syllable. title: WRITING OF REPORTS
subject: English Language
rawText: STUDENTS’ SUMMARY NOTE Topic: Writing of Reports – Technical/Scientific Reports Definition of a Report: A report is an organized written account of an event, experiment, investigation, or situation. Technical/Scientific Report: A scientific report is a written account of an experiment or research carried out in the laboratory or field. It helps to record observations, results, and conclusions in a clear and logical manner. Features of a Scientific Report: Title – Name of the experiment or research. Introduction – Brief background or explanation of the experiment. Date of Experiment – When the experiment was carried out. Purpose – Reason or objective of the experiment. Materials/Equipment Used – List of items needed. Method/Procedure – Steps followed to carry out the experiment. Outcome/Result – Observations or findings. Conclusion – Summary of what was learned or achieved from the experiment. Important Points to Remember: Main details: Introduction, Purpose, Outcome/Result, Conclusion Supporting details: Date, Materials, Procedure Reports should be written in a logical and organized order. Clear and precise language makes reports easy to understand. Tip: Always follow the proper format when writing a scientific report to ensure clarity and completeness.

title: STRUCTURE - NOMINALIZATION OF ADJECTIVES AND VERBS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Structure – Nominalization of Adjectives and Verbs Nominalization is the process of producing a noun from another part of speech through the addition of derivational affixes or by using suffixes. Examples. VERB SUFFIX NOUN Move - ment movement React - ion reaction Refuse - al refusal Fail - ure failure ADJECTIVE Careless - ness carelessness Difficult - y difficulty Intense - ity intensity Capable - ity capability MORE EXAMPLES ADJECTIVES NOUNS Kind kindness Wide wideness Cruel cruelty Ready readiness Honest honesty Tired tiredness VERBS NOUNS Arrange arrangement Agree agreement Add addition Inform information Sing singer Post postage Teach teacher

Preach preacher Nouns can be formed from other nouns. Examples : A] Ship added to noun gives another noun : Friend + ship == Friendship Court + ship == Courtship Leader + ship == Leadership B] Noun + hood gives another noun. Examples : Adult + hood == Adulthood Brother + hood == Brotherhood Child hood == Childhood C] Noun + ish gives another noun. Example: Boy + ish == Boyish Child + ish == Childish. IN SENTENCE CONTEXT 1a) I need a change (Noun) b) I will change (verb) 2) Fight a) They always fight each other (fight verb) b) There was a fight between the two men ( fight, noun] ASSIGNMENT Do exercise on page 92 (1-5) of your class text book. REFERENCES 1) New Concept English bk 1 by F Ademola Adeoye et al (2013) 2) Complete English Course by Ukamaka Chioma Ibe (2011) 3) Essential English Language by Latilo T. A et al (2008)

Collective Noun: This is a noun used to refer to a group of things and class of individuals. Examples a team of players, congregation of worshipers, a group of things, a bunch of banana/keys. Other collective nouns include: committee of, swarm of bees, class of students, family of lions, company of actors, herd of cattle, host of Angel etc. 4. Abstract Noun: They are things or concepts that cannot be touched or seen. They exist in our imagination. We feel and experience them. Example hatred, love, beauty, death, sadness and joy etc. 5. Concrete Noun: Concrete noun can be seen and touched. All other types of nouns except abstract noun are concrete nouns. 6. Countable Nouns: Are those that can be counted. Countable nouns have singular and plural. Example table-tables, box-boxes, man-men. 7. Uncountable Nouns: These are nouns that cannot be counted. They can be expressed in plural forms by using partitives e.g. a piece of furniture, a litre of kerosene, a bottle of wine, a cup of water. Exercise Page 37 Exercise 3. What is the chief point the writer is trying to make? Sometimes the main idea is not explicitly/clearly stated. They can be inferred/gotten. That does not mean that it lacks main idea.

title: NOUN PHRASE
subject: English Language
rawText: GSS KUBWAENGLISH LANGUAGE SS 1 NOTES ON TOPICS 2024FIRST TERM 10 Note: The issues of finite and non-finite verb is the major factor that distinguishes the phrase from the clause. Therefore, for an expression that has a verb to be identified as a phrase, you must establish the following: a. If the verb in the expression given is preceded by ‘to’, it means the verb is non-finite. Therefore, the expression is a phrase. Example To pass the examination involves hard work. b. If the verb in the expression given is in the – ing form, the verb is non-finite, hence the expression is a phrase. Example Giving to the poor attracts God’s blessing c. If the verb in the expression given is made to function as an adjective, it is a non-finite verb and the expression is a phrase e.g. He told me to replace the broken bottle. Note: broken is a verb (past participle of break), but in the sentence above, it is qualifying the noun “bottle” which is the function of an adjective. Types of Phrase – Noun Phrase There are three types of phrase namely: Noun phrase, adjectival phrase and adverbial phrase. A. Noun Phrase: In a noun phrase, the head word must be a noun or pronoun. A noun phrase can be replaced by a pronoun Examples i. I saw the village head master ii. The man at the gate is my father iii. The old woman sleeping in the room has just been discouraged from the hospital. iv. Sola told me to replace the broken bottle v. I gave the money to the most brilliant student in the class. vi. To sleep without light is frightening Functions of Noun Phrase Like noun, noun phrase has six different grammatical functions 1. Subject of Verb: When the noun phrase occupies the first position in the sentence, it functions as the subject of the verb that follows it. Examples i. Sleeping without light is not something I enjoy. Function: Subject of the verb “is”

title: WORDS OF TWO SYLLABLES WITH STRESS ON THE SECOND S
subject: English Language
rawText:
WEEK 1 TOPIC: SPEECH: WORDS OF THREE SYLLABLES STRESSED ON THE 2ND SYLLABLE Stress is the degree of force by which a word is pronounced. Words are broken into tiny units called syllables. A syllable is the pronounced unit of a word. It is on a syllable that stress is placed. Stressing a syllable therefore means giving it more force, such that it is louder, longer and higher in pitch than other syllables. A stressed syllable like in the dictionary is indicated by placing a stroke at the beginning of the syllable, but here, a stressed syllable should be written in capital letters. THREE SYLLABLE WORDS Three syllable words are parts of polysyllable words which have their different stress patterns with some guiding rules. These rules help us to identify when to stress the word on the first, second, third or fourth syllable. For three syllable words stressed on the second syllable, the rule guiding it says Stress the second syllable from the end of a word if it ends in : - cient, - ion, - ic, - ial, - ian. Examples suf-FI-cient ef- FI-cient ic stra-TE-gic dra-MA-tic -ion o-CCA-sion pro-JEC-tion dis-CU-ssion con-VIC-tion in-JEC-tion star-VA-tion con-VER-sion

con-STRUC-tion fru-STRA-tion o-VA-tion -ial co-LO-nial of-FI-cial com-MER-cial -ian ci-VI-lian Examples of the three syllable words in a sentence The fru-STRA-tion in that job is too much She is at the venue for col-LA-tion of results The people in overalls are con-STRUC-tion workers Something dra-MA-tic happened yesterday I am a ci-VI-lian not a soldier Assignment Mention ten (10) words of three syllables stressed on the 2nd syllable

title: SUMMARY
subject: English Language
rawText:
TOPIC 3: SUMMARY: SUMMARISING A PASSAGE IN A SPECIFIED NUMBER OF SENTENCES Summary can be described as a shortened form of a long passage after removing all irrelevant ideas from the main points and giving a short account of the passage using your own words. To summarize a passage in a specified number of sentences demands that one should pay attention to the instruction on the number of sentences each questions requires. Some questions demands that you summarize in one, two, or three sentences. Ensure you write as instructed. A sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop. THINGS TO NOTE FOR GOOD SUMMARY Brevity: Your answer must be brief and straight to the point. No use of additional information apart from the main points. Relevance: A candidate answer should be relevant to the points mentioned in the passage. Clarity: This means that students are expected to put down their answers clearly. Originality: Your answers should be written in your own words to avoid the error of mindless lifting. Identify the topic sentences: The topic sentences are the main points in the paragraphs of the passage which are mostly found in the first or last sentence of a paragraph. Write your answers in complete sentences CAUSES OF LOSS OF MARK IN SUMMARY WRITING Mindless lifting of words from the passage. This means copying down the exact words and expressions of the writer. Phrases and incomplete sentences. In summary, your answers should be written in complete sentences not in phrases. Writing more than required number of sentences.

Grammatical/expression errors. Wrong use of preamble or the introductory statement that does not flow with the sentences.

rawText: STUDENTS’ SUMMARY NOTE Topic: Writing of Reports – Technical/Scientific Reports Definition of a Report: A report is an organized written account of an event, experiment, investigation, or situation. Technical/Scientific Report: A scientific report is a written account of an experiment or research carried out in the laboratory or field. It helps to record observations, results, and conclusions in a clear and logical manner. Features of a Scientific Report: Title – Name of the experiment or research. Introduction – Brief background or explanation of the experiment. Date of Experiment – When the experiment was carried out. Purpose – Reason or objective of the experiment. Materials/Equipment Used – List of items needed. Method/Procedure – Steps followed to carry out the experiment. Outcome/Result – Observations or findings. Conclusion – Summary of what was learned or achieved from the experiment. Important Points to Remember: Main details: Introduction, Purpose, Outcome/Result, Conclusion Supporting details: Date, Materials, Procedure Reports should be written in a logical and organized order. Clear and precise language makes reports easy to understand. Tip: Always follow the proper format when writing a scientific report to ensure clarity and completeness.

title: PHRASE
subject: English Language
rawText:
TOPIC 2: PHRASES TYPES OF PHRASES A phrase is a group of words that do not contain a finite verb. A phrase cannot stand on its own to make meaning. It only form part of a sentence. Types of phrases Noun phrase: This is the phrase that does the work of a noun or pronoun in a sentence. Example: John the driver is dead. The big ugly girl is quarrelsome. Adjectival phrase: This is the phrase that describes a noun or a pronoun in a sentence. Examples: The coat made of cotton is very lovely. The girl with dirty hands ate the food. Adverbial phrase: this is the phrase that modifies a verb in a sentence. It answers the question “why, where, when, how? etc. Examples: The head boy lives near the church. The old man walked slowly across the road. Prepositional phrase: This is a phrase that begins with a preposition. Examples Sani was beaten with a cane. The woman drowned in the river. Identification of phrases If the verbs in the expression given is preceded by ‘to’ that verb is non-finite, therefore the expression is a phrase. Example He is always ready to fight anybody. To pass examination involves hard work. If the verb in the expression functions as an adjective, it is a non-finite verb and therefore the expression becomes a phrase. Example

I have boiled yam in my pot. He has replaced the broken bottle. If the verb in the expression is in the ‘-ing’ form, the verb is non-finite and the expression becomes a phrase. Example I saw the boy going to the library. Eating supper late is what I don’t like. If the expression underlined in the sentence cannot make meaning when standing alone. Example She is sleeping in the room. They are standing outside the gate.

title: CREATIVE WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
CREATIVE WRITING Meaning of Creative Writing Creative writing is a type of writing that allows a writer to use imagination, creativity, and original ideas to express thoughts, feelings, and experiences. It is not limited to facts; instead, it involves storytelling, description, and artistic expression. Creative writing is used to entertain, educate, and sometimes pass moral lessons to readers. Characteristics / Features of Creative Writing Creative writing has the following features: 1. Imagination The writer creates ideas, events, places, and characters, even if they are not real. 2. Originality The work must be original and not copied from another writer. 3. Creativity Creative writing uses interesting expressions and unique styles. 4. Emotional Appeal It appeals to the reader’s emotions such as happiness, sadness, fear, or excitement. 5. Use of Literary Devices Literary devices like simile, metaphor, personification, imagery, and symbolism are used to beautify the writing. 6. Free Expression The writer has freedom to express ideas without strict rules. Types of Creative Writing 1. Story Writing Story writing involves telling an imaginary or real-life story in an interesting way. It usually has a beginning, middle, and ending. Examples:

Short stories Folktales Myths and legends 2. Narrative Writing Narrative writing tells a story or recounts events in the order in which they happened. Examples: An unforgettable day My first day in secondary school 3. Descriptive Writing Descriptive writing gives a vivid picture of a person, place, object, or event using the five senses (sight, sound, smell, taste, and touch). Examples: My school compound A market scene 4. Poetry Poetry expresses thoughts and emotions using rhythm, rhyme, and figurative language. Examples: Poems Songs 5. Drama Drama is written to be acted on stage. It is written in dialogue form. Examples: Plays Skits Elements of Creative Writing

1. Plot The plot is the arrangement of events in a story. 2. Characters Characters are the people or animals in a story. Major characters – main characters Minor characters – supporting characters 3. Setting Setting refers to the place, time, and environment of a story. 4. Theme The theme is the main idea or message of the story. 5. Conflict Conflict is the problem or challenge faced by the characters in a story. 6. Style Style is the writer’s unique way of using language. Importance of Creative Writing Creative writing is important because: 1. It develops imagination and creativity. 2. It improves vocabulary and writing skills. 3. It helps students express thoughts and emotions freely. 4. It entertains and educates readers. 5. It builds confidence in writing. Tips for Good Creative Writing 1. Understand the topic very well. 2. Plan your work before writing. 3. Write clearly and neatly.

4. Use simple and correct English. 5. Avoid unnecessary repetition. 6. Ensure your story has a proper beginning and ending. 7. Proofread your work for spelling and grammatical errors.

title: SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS
subject: English Language
rawText:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE NOTES TOPIC: SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS Class: SS1 Subject: English Language INTRODUCTION In English Language, words can be related in different ways. Some words have similar meanings, while others have opposite meanings. These relationships are known as synonyms and antonyms. Understanding them helps students improve vocabulary, comprehension, and writing skills. SYNONYMS Definition Synonyms are words that have the same or nearly the same meaning as another word. Note: Synonyms may not always mean exactly the same thing in every situation, but they are close in meaning. Examples of Synonyms Word Synonym(s) Happy: glad, joyful Big: large, huge Small: little, tiny Fast: quick, rapid Begin: start, commence End: finish, stop Angry: annoyed, furious Brave: bold, courageous Easy: simple Clever: intelligent, smart

Synonyms Used in Sentences 1. The children were happy (glad) to see their teacher. 2. Nigeria is a big (large) country. 3. The exam was very easy (simple). 4. He is a clever (intelligent) boy. Uses of Synonyms To avoid repeating the same word To make essays and speeches more interesting To improve vocabulary To express ideas more clearly ANTONYMS Definition Antonyms are words that have opposite meanings. Examples of Antonyms Word Antonym Hot cold Tall short Old young Happy sad Rich poor Early late Open closed Clean dirty Strong weak Light heavy

Antonyms Used in Sentences 1. The soup is hot, not cold. 2. My elder brother is tall, but I am short. 3. The classroom is clean, not dirty. 4. She arrived early, not late. Uses of Antonyms To show contrast in meaning To explain ideas clearly To improve comprehension in reading passages DIFFERENCE BETWEEN SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS Synonyms Antonyms Have similar meanings Have opposite meanings Example: big – large Example: big – small Used to avoid repetition Used to show contrast. SUMMARY Synonyms are words with similar meanings. Antonyms are words with opposite meanings. Both help improve vocabulary and writing skills. CLASSWORK / EXERCISE A. Give one synonym for each word: 1. Fast 2. Angry 3. Begin

4. Small 5. Happy B. Give one antonym for each word: 1. Early 2. Clean 3. Strong 4. Rich 5. Hot

title: REPORT WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
REPORT WRITING Meaning: A report is a formal written account of an event, investigation, or situation. It presents facts, findings, and sometimes recommendations. TYPES OF REPORT WRITING 1. Incident Report Meaning: A report written to explain what happened during an unexpected event such as an accident, fight, theft, or fire. Features: Written in past tense Answers what, where, when, how, and who Clear and factual Example Topics: Report on a fight in school Report on a fire outbreak 2. Accident Report Meaning: A report that gives details of an accident and its effects. Features: Past tense Gives cause and result Includes injuries and damage Example Topics: Road accident

Laboratory accident 3. Investigation Report Meaning: A report written after examining a problem to find its cause and solution. Features: Formal language Logical arrangement May include recommendations Example Topics: Investigation into poor academic performance Investigation into lateness in school 4. School Report Meaning: A report about school activities or events. Features: Simple formal language Factual and well-organised Written by a student or prefect Example Topics: Report on Inter-House Sports Report on Cultural Day 5. Eyewitness Report Meaning: A report written by someone who personally saw an event happen. Features:

First-hand information Past tense Clear sequence of events Example Topics: Eyewitness report of an accident Eyewitness report of a robbery 6. News Report Meaning: A report written for newspapers, radio, or television. Features: Headline Short paragraphs Answers the 5Ws and H (What, When, Where, Who, Why, How) Example Topics: Flood disaster in a community School competition victory 7. Committee Report Meaning: A report written by a group appointed to carry out a task. Features: Formal tone Includes findings and recommendations Often ends with conclusion Example Topics: Report of sanitation committee

Report of disciplinary committee FORMAT OF A REPORT 1. Title 2. Introduction 3. Body 4. Conclusion 5. Signature 6. Date LANGUAGE FEATURES OF REPORT WRITING Formal language Past tense Clear paragraphs No slang or abbreviations

title: PHRASAL VERBS
subject: English Language
rawText:
PHRASAL VERBS Meaning of Phrasal Verbs A phrasal verb is a combination of a main verb and one or two particles (a preposition or an adverb) which together form a new meaning different from the original verb. Formula: Verb + Preposition / Adverb = New Meaning Examples Verb Particle. Phrasal Verb Meaning look after look after to take care of give up give up to stop trying turn on turn on to switch on break down break down. to stop working Types of Phrasal Verbs 1. Transitive Phrasal Verbs These phrasal verbs require an object. Examples: She called off the meeting. I will pick up the book. Some transitive phrasal verbs can be separated: She turned off the light. She turned the light off. ￿ If the object is a pronoun, it must come between the verb and the particle: Correct: Turn it off. Incorrect: Turn off it.

2. Intransitive Phrasal Verbs These do not require an object. Examples: The car broke down. He woke up late. Separable and Inseparable Phrasal Verbs Separable Phrasal Verbs The verb and particle can be separated by an object. Examples: Put on your shoes. Put your shoes on. Inseparable Phrasal Verbs The verb and particle must stay together. Examples: She ran into her teacher. We are looking for the keys. Ran her teacher into (Wrong) Common Phrasal Verbs and Meanings Phrasal Verb Meaning bring up to raise a topic carry on to continue come across to find by chance find outto discover look forward to to be excited about put off to postpone

set up to establish take off to remove or to fly Importance of Phrasal Verbs They are commonly used in spoken and written English They help improve fluency and comprehension They are frequently tested in examinations Summary Phrasal verbs consist of a verb + particle They may be transitive or intransitive Some are separable, others are inseparable Their meanings are often idiomatic Practice Exercise Underline the phrasal verb in each sentence: 1. The teacher called off the test. 2. Please turn off the fan. 3. She ran into an old friend.

subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON NOTE: WORDS OF THREE SYLLABLES STRESSED ON THE FIRST SYLLABLE Subject: English Language Topic: Stress Sub-topic: Words of Three Syllables Stressed on the First Syllable Duration: 40 minutes INTRODUCTION In English Language, stress refers to the extra force or emphasis placed on a syllable when a word is pronounced. In words with more than one syllable, one syllable is pronounced louder, longer, or more clearly than the others. This lesson focuses on three-syllable words that are stressed on the first syllable. DEFINITION OF STRESS Stress is the emphasis placed on a particular syllable in a word during pronunciation. THREE-SYLLABLE WORDS A three-syllable word is a word that can be broken into three distinct sound units (syllables). Example: BEAU-ti-ful (3 syllables) WORDS OF THREE SYLLABLES STRESSED ON THE FIRST SYLLABLE In these words, the first syllable is pronounced more strongly than the other two. The stressed syllable is often shown in capital letters. EXAMPLES Word Syllable Division Stressed Syllable Beautiful BEAU-ti-ful First Family

FA-mi-ly First Cinema CI-ne-ma First Saturday SA-tur-day First Possible PO-ssi-ble First Customer CUS-to-mer First Yesterday YES-ter-day First Vegetable VEG-e-ta-ble First Animal A-ni-mal First President PRE-si-dent

First RULES GOVERNING THREE-SYLLABLE WORDS STRESSED ON THE FIRST SYLLABLE Most nouns and adjectives of three syllables are stressed on the first syllable. VEG-e-ta-ble BEAU-ti-ful Words ending in -er, -or, -ly, -ence, -ance often carry stress on the first syllable. CUS-to-mer FA-mi-ly Many common everyday words have first-syllable stress. IMPORTANCE OF CORRECT STRESS It helps in clear pronunciation It improves listening and speaking skills It prevents misunderstanding in communication It helps students perform better in WAEC oral English CLASS ACTIVITY Pronounce the following words correctly and identify the stressed syllable: Saturday Cinema Animal Clap once on the stressed syllable while pronouncing each word. EVALUATION Define stress. Mention three words of three syllables stressed on the first syllable. Underline the stressed syllable in this word: vegetable. ASSIGNMENT

Write five words of three syllables and indicate the syllable that is stressed.

subject: English Language
rawText:
SUBJECT: English Language TOPIC: Phrases SUB TOPIC: Adjective Phrase ADJECTIVE PHRASE Definition An adjective phrase is a group of words that functions as an adjective in a sentence. It describes or modifies a noun or a pronoun by giving more information about its quality, quantity, size, age, colour, origin, or condition. The main word in an adjective phrase is called the head adjective Structure of an Adjective Phrase An adjective phrase may consist of: 1. An adjective alone The tall girl won the prize. 2. An adjective with modifiers (intensifiers) She is very intelligent. 3. An adjective with complements He is proud of his achievements. 4. Multiple adjectives working together It was a dark, cold night. Examples of Adjective Phrases in Sentences Adjective Phrase. Sentence very beautiful. Shewore a very beautiful dress. full of water The bottle is full of water. extremely difficult Theexam was extremely difficult. afraid of dogs The child is afraid of dogs. rich in minerals The soil is rich in minerals.

Position of an Adjective Phrase An adjective phrase can appear in two main positions: 1. Before the noun (Attributive position) She bought a highly expensive phone. 2. After the noun (Predicative position) The phone is highly expensive. Functions of an Adjective Phrase An adjective phrase functions to: Describe a noun Give more details about a pronoun Make meaning clearer and more specific Example: The students eager to learn arrived early. Difference Between Adjective and Adjective Phrase Adjective Adjective Phrase happy very happy strong extremely strong angry angry with him How to Identify an Adjective Phrase To identify an adjective phrase: 1. Look for a noun or pronoun in the sentence. 2. Ask “What kind?” “Which one?” or “How many?” 3. The words answering the question form the adjective phrase. Summary An adjective phrase modifies a noun or pronoun.

It contains a head adjective and may include modifiers or complements. It can appear before or after the noun it describes.

title: INFORMAL LETTER
subject: English Language
rawText:
INFORMAL LETTER Meaning of an Informal Letter An informal letter is a letter written to people we know very well. These people include friends, parents, brothers, sisters, cousins, and classmates. The language used is simple, friendly, and relaxed. Features of an Informal Letter 1. Writer’s Address Written at the top right corner of the letter. Example: 15, Unity Street, Ibadan. 2. Date Written below the address. Example: 10th March, 2026. 3. Salutation Friendly greeting. Examples: Dear Mum, Dear Tunde, My dear friend, 4. Body of the Letter Contains the main message of the letter. Written in paragraphs. Uses simple and friendly language. 5. Complimentary Close

Friendly ending of the letter. Examples: Yours sincerely, Yours lovingly, Your friend, 6. Signature / Writer’s Name The writer’s name comes after the complimentary close. Language Used in Informal Letters Simple and clear words Friendly tone Contractions can be used (e.g. I’m, don’t, can’t) No strict formal rules Example of an Informal Letter 15, Unity Street, Ibadan. 10th March, 2026. Dear Ayo, How are you and your family? I hope you are fine. I am writing to tell you about my new school. My new school is very big and beautiful. The teachers are friendly and I have made many new friends. I enjoy my classes, especially English and Mathematics. I hope to see you during the next holiday. Please greet your parents for me. Yours sincerely, Bola. Uses of Informal Letters

To share personal news To invite friends or relatives To congratulate someone To express feelings and experiences

rawText: TOPIC 2: Writing: Report Writing A report is spoken or written account of an event or happening that has taken place. It may be an event that has been heard, seen or done or studied. It is always a narrative based on an actual experiences of the reporter and very often requires record keeping to enable the writer to give actual figures and dates. Types of Report Private/informal report This is the type of reports you narrate to your parents, friends or classmates of an incident that happened to you or you witnessed. It is supposed to be a direct personal experience of the writer. Official/formal report It is one that is presented as a formal document giving details of an event that occurred like a robbery incident, an accident, the proceedings of a meeting, a petition, a report of an excursion, research report of an experiment carried out etc. Guidelines for report writing Pay attention to details and be accurate. Note the sequence of events. It is important to report precisely which events led to another and what action caused what result. Take into consideration the purpose for which you are writing the report. A police report is different from a report to your classmates. The method of presenting requires short and clear sentences with detailed information like, date, time of event, people present, cause, time it ended, effort made to stop or enhance the incident etc. explain in paragraphs giving only the essential facts which will present a true picture of what happened.
