title: SUMMARY
subject: English Language
rawText: Points to note in summary writing Summary is a brief, clear statement giving most important facts about something. It is a shortened account of any piece of writing. HINTS ON SUMMARY WRITING (a) Detect the main points of the text as required. (b) state it precisely,clearly and briefly. (c) Rephrase the text using your own words with the main points in the text. (d) the summary answers must be written in sentences. (e) don't engage in mindless lifting or copying from the passage. (f) inclusion of any irrelevant or extraneous material should be avoided (g) make sure that your sentence is grammatically correct (h) ensure that you do not make two points in a sentence. (I) Smooth blending of words and satisfactory coverage.

title: DEBATE
subject: English Language
rawText:
SUBJECT: English Language TOPIC: Debate Meaning of Debate A debate is a formal discussion or argument on a particular topic in which two opposing sides present their views. One side supports the motion (the proposition), while the other opposes it (the opposition), with the aim of persuading the audience or judges. Types of Debate 1. Formal Debate – Conducted under strict rules, time limits, and moderation (e.g. school or parliamentary debates). 2. Informal Debate – A casual argument or discussion without strict rules. 3. Parliamentary Debate – Common in legislative houses, following parliamentary procedures Structure of a Debate 1. Introduction of the Motion – The topic to be debated is presented. 2. Proposition Speakers – Speak in support of the motion. 3. Opposition Speakers – Speak against the motion. 4. Rebuttal – Speakers counter the arguments of the opposing side. 5. Conclusion – Final summary and persuasion. Features of a Good Debate Clear and logical arguments Proper use of language Evidence and examples to support points Respect for opposing views Confidence and clarity of speech Rules of a Debate Speakers must speak within the allotted time. No interruption while a speaker is speaking. Arguments must be relevant to the topic.

Speakers must address the chairman/moderator Importance of Debate Develops critical thinking skills Improves public speaking and confidence Encourages research and logical reasoning Promotes healthy exchange of ideas Conclusion Debate is an important form of communication that helps individuals express ideas logically and confidently while respecting differing opinions.

title: EXPOSITORY ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
EXPOSITORY ESSAY Meaning of Expository Essay An expository essay is a type of essay that explains, describes, or gives information about a topic in a clear and logical way. It does not involve storytelling or arguing. The writer only presents facts and explanations. Purpose of Expository Essay The purpose of an expository essay is to: Explain an idea or topic Give information Teach or inform the reader Features / Characteristics An expository essay: Is written in simple and clear language Uses facts, examples, and explanations Does not include personal opinions or emotions Is usually written in the present tense Is well arranged in paragraphs Types of Expository Essay 1. Descriptive Essay – describes a person, place, or thing 2. Process Essay – explains how something is done 3. Definition Essay – explains the meaning of a term 4. Cause and Effect Essay – explains reasons and results Structure of an Expository Essay 1. Introduction Introduces the topic Gives a brief explanation of what the essay is about

2. Body Paragraphs Each paragraph explains one main point Facts and examples are used Ideas are arranged logically 3. Conclusion Summarizes the main points Ends the essay neatly Examples of Expository Essay Topics The Importance of Education How to Prepare a Good Meal Uses of the Internet Causes of Examination Malpractice Important Tips Write clearly and neatly Avoid storytelling Avoid personal opinions like “I think” Go straight to the point

title: EXPOSITORY ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText: WEEK FIVE EXPOSITORY ESSAY A expository essay expects the writer to explain in detail the topic in question for better understanding by the reader. The writer is expected to have adequate information about the topic in question as it is designed to inform, instruct, explain, criticize or analyze some concepts or situations to the reader. Topics related to expository essay Dangers of drug abuse. The dangers of premarital sex. The future of the Nigeria youth. How my favourite food is prepared. Causes of indiscipline in Nigeria secondary schools. The consequences of dressing indecently. My English teacher, how I saw her/him. Controlling HIV AIDS in Nigeria. A friend in need is a friend indeed. To write an expository essay, you are expected to have adequate information about the topic in question as it is designed to inform and educate the readers. E.g you may asked to explain the origin, causes and effects of acquired immune deficiency syndrome (AIDS).

title: ADJUNCT OF MANNERS AND REASONS
subject: English Language
rawText: WEEK SIX Adjunct of manner and reason. Adjunct of manner The adjunct of manner shows how something is done. This adjunct answers the questions “how”. Examples of words used to illustrate manner: slowly, happily, in a hurry, sorrowfully, proudly, swiftly, sluggishly, roughly, badly, deeply, foolishly etc. Sentence samples He embraced his son proudly The job was done haphardly. They hurriedly left the scene The players performed badly yesterday The adjunct of reason tries to justify why an action is performed. This adjunct answers the question “why?” it is introduced by words like: because, since, as, in order to, so as to, in order that. Sentence samples He married early because he is the only son. She was sacked since she refused to apologized. The student was sent home because he has not paid school fees. He came late as he was held in a traffic jam. The man left home so as to get there on time. She worked hard in order that she will be promoted.

title: THREE WORDS SYLLABLE
subject: English Language
rawText:
SS1 Words of Three Syllables Stressed on the Second Syllable Introduction In English pronunciation, word stress refers to the emphasis placed on one syllable in a word. This emphasis is usually shown through a louder voice, higher pitch, and longer duration. Correct word stress is important because it affects clarity, meaning, and natural speech. Three-Syllable Words A three-syllable word is a word that contains three distinct beats or sound units when spoken. In some three-syllable words, the stress falls on the second syllable, also known as middle-syllable stress. Stress on the Second Syllable When the stress is on the second syllable, that syllable is pronounced more strongly than the first and third syllables. This stress pattern is common in certain categories of words in English. Stress pattern representation: weak – STRONG – weak Examples of Three-Syllable Words Stressed on the Second Syllable Word Syllable DivisionStress Pattern important im-POR-tant weak-STRONG-weak computer com-PU-ter weak-STRONG-weak remember re-MEM-ber weak-STRONG-weak developde-VEL-op weak-STRONG-weak consider con-SID-er weak-STRONG-weak adventure ad-VEN-ture weak-STRONG-weak attention at-TEN-tion weak-STRONG-weak discover dis-COV-er weak-STRONG-weak Common Features Three-syllable words stressed on the second syllable often include:

Verbs (e.g. remember, consider, develop) Longer everyday vocabulary Words with prefixes such as re, de, con, ad. Importance of Correct Stress Using correct stress: Improves intelligibility Prevents misunderstanding Makes speech sound natural and fluent Is essential in spoken English and examinations Conclusion Understanding three-syllable words stressed on the second syllable helps learners speak English more accurately and confidently. Regular listening and practice are essential for mastering this stress pattern.

title: INTONATION
subject: English Language
rawText: INTONATION Intonation is the ability of the voice to rise and fall while talking. The degree or extent of the rising and falling is called pitch. Intonation patterns are (1) Rising tune (2) falling tune, (3) fall - rise tune (4) rise - fall tune. (1) The falling tune :- is the fall in pitch, it indicates that the voice pitch has descended from a higher level to a lower level. The arrow shows the direction of the movement of the pitch. e.g. (1)statements (a) l love fried plantain (b) she could not see the doctor. (2) WH-Questions e.g (a) what is wrong? (b) who is your father? (3) commands (a) shut up (b) keep going! (4) Advice (a) Eat enough food (b) Buy a blood tonic for yourself.

subject: English Language
rawText:
WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH HOME AND FAMILY MEANING AND USE IN CONTEXT 1. Kitchen - A room where food is prepared and cooked. Example: The aroma of freshly baked bread filled the kitchen. 2. Living room - A room in a house for general and informal everyday use. Example: The family gathered in the living room to watch a movie together. 3. Bedroom - A room used for sleeping and resting. Example: The cozy bedroom was adorned with soft blankets and fluffy pillows. 4. Dining table - A table where people eat meals together. Example: The family sat around the dining table, sharing stories from their day. 5. Garden - A piece of land used for growing flowers, fruits, or vegetables. Example: The vibrant garden was filled with colorful blooms and lush greenery. 6. Pet - An animal kept for companionship or pleasure. Example: The playful puppy quickly became the family's beloved pet. 7. Sibling - A brother or sister. Example: The siblings played happily in the backyard, enjoying the sunny day. 8. Parents - A father or mother. Example: The parents worked tirelessly to provide for their children's needs. 9. Grandparents - The parents of a person's father or mother. Example: The children visited their grandparents, listening to their fascinating tales. 10. Sofa - A long, soft seat with a back and arms, for two or more people. Example: The family relaxed on the cozy sofa, enjoying each other's company. 11. Curtains - Piece of fabric hung to cover a window. Example: The colorful curtains added a touch of elegance to the living room. 12. Lamp - A device for giving light, often consisting of a bulb and shade. Example: The lamp on the bedside table provided a soft, warm glow in the bedroom. 13. Family photos - Photographs of family members, often displayed in a home. Example: The family photos on the wall told the story of cherished memories. 14. Backyard - An area behind a house, often used for outdoor activities. Example: The children played soccer in the spacious backyard, laughing joyously.

15. Blanket - A large piece of fabric used for keeping warm, especially while sleeping. Example: The soft, knitted blanket provided comfort during the chilly night. 16. Stove - An appliance used for cooking food. Example: The aroma of the delicious stew wafted from the sizzling pot on the stove. 17. Toys - Objects designed for children to play with. Example: The room was filled with colorful toys, sparking the children's imagination. 18. Dining chair - A chair used for sitting at a dining table. Example: The comfortable dining chairs made the family meals more enjoyable. 19. Bookshelf - A piece of furniture used for storing books. Example: The bookshelf in the living room was filled with a variety of literary classics. 20. Television - A device used for receiving broadcast programs. Example: The family gathered around the television to watch their favorite show together. 21. Nuclear Family: A family unit consisting of parents and their children. Example: The nuclear family, consisting of a father, a mother, and their two children, lived happily in a cozy house. 22. Extended Family: A family unit that extends beyond the nuclear family, including grandparents, aunts, uncles, and cousins. Example: During the festive season, the extended family gathered at the grandparents' house, sharing laughter and creating cherished memories together. 23. Father: A male parent. Example: The father worked diligently to provide for his family's needs. 24. Mother: A female parent. Example: The mother lovingly prepared a delicious meal for her children. 25. Son: A male child of the parents. Example: The son played soccer in the backyard with his friends. 26. Daughter: A female child of the parents. Example: The daughter read her favorite book quietly in her room. 27. Grandfather: The father of a person's father or mother. Example: The grandfather told stories of his youth to his attentive grandchildren. 28. Grandmother: The mother of a person's father or mother. Example: The grandmother baked fresh cookies for her grandchildren.

29. Uncle: The brother of a person's father or mother, or the husband of an aunt. Example: The uncle taught his nephew how to ride a bicycle in the park. 30. Aunt: The sister of a person's father or mother, or the wife of an uncle. Example: The aunt helped her niece with her school project. 31. Cousin: A child of one's uncle or aunt. Example: The cousins had a fun playdate together at the family gathering. 32. Brother: A male sibling. Example: The brother shared his toys with his younger sister. 33. Sister: A female sibling. Example: The sister braided her sibling's hair with great care. 34. Niece: A daughter of one's brother or sister, or a daughter of one's brother-in-law or sister-in-law. Example: The aunt bought a special gift for her niece's birthday. 35. Nephew: A son of one's brother or sister, or a son of one's brother-in-law or sister-in-law. Example: The uncle took his nephew to the park for a fun afternoon outing. 36. Father-in-law: The father of one's spouse. Example: The father-in-law shared his wisdom with his son-in-law. 37. Mother-in-law: The mother of one's spouse. Example: The mother-in-law cooked a traditional meal for the family. 38. Brother-in-law: The brother of one's spouse. Example: The brother-in-law helped his sister-in-law with household chores. 39. Sister-in-law: The sister of one's spouse. Example: The sister-in-law and her sibling enjoyed shopping together. 40. Siblings: Brothers and sisters considered as a group. Example: The siblings played together in the backyard, enjoying the warm sunshine and each other's company. title: TENSES
subject: English Language
rawText:
1 . TENSES What are Tenses ? Tenses show the time of an action or state of being. They tell us when something happens. Examples: I eat → present time I ate → past time I will eat → future time In English, there are three main tenses: Present Past Future Each of these has different forms. One important group is called Simple Tenses. What is the Simple Tense Form ? The simple tense is used to talk about: Daily habits General facts Completed actions in the past Actions that will happen in the future There are three simple tenses: Simple Present Tense Simple Past Tense Simple Future Tense Simple Present Tense Use: Daily routines Habits Universal truths

3 . Form: Subject + base verb (Add –s / –es with he, she, it) Examples: I play football. She plays the piano. The sun rises in the east. Sentences: We go to school every day. He likes ice cream. 2. Simple Past Tense Use: Actions completed in the past Form: Subject + past form of verb Examples: I watched a movie. She wrote a letter. They won the match. Sentences: We visited our grandparents yesterday. He ate an apple. Simple Future Tense Use: Actions that will happen in the future Form: Subject + will + base verb Examples: I will study tomorrow.

She will help me. They will travel next week. Sentences: We will complete our homework. He will become a doctor. Examples of One Verb in All Simple Tenses (Verb: to read) Tense Sentence Simple Present I read books daily. Simple Past I read a book yesterday. Simple Future I will read a book tomorrow. Class Exercises Exercise 1: Fill in the blanks (use the correct simple tense form) She ___ (play) tennis every evening. We ___ (finish) the work yesterday. I ___ (go) to the market tomorrow. He ___ (write) a letter last night. They ___ (eat) lunch at 1 p.m. every day. Book References New oxfords English book 1 Essential English Grammar – Raymond Murphy

title: RELIGION
subject: English Language
rawText:
RELIGION What is Religion ? Religion is a system of beliefs, practices, values, and rituals through which people relate to what they consider sacred or divine. It often explains life’s meaning, moral rules, the origin of the world, and how humans should live. Definition of Traditional Religion Traditional religion refers to the indigenous belief systems that originated within particular communities or cultures and were passed down from generation to generation through oral tradition, customs, and rituals. These religions are closely connected to ancestors, nature, and community life. (Examples include African Traditional Religion, Native American religions, and Aboriginal belief systems.) Words Associated with Traditional Religion Ancestors Deity Supreme Being Spirits Shrine Sacrifice Ritual Worship Priest Priestess Divination Oracle

Totem Taboo Festival Incantation Offering Libation Myth Sacred Community Initiation Medicine man Sacred objects Belief system Nature Moral laws Afterlife Cleansing Protection Meaning of Ten of the Words Listed Ancestors – Dead family members believed to guide and protect the living. Supreme Being – The highest god, believed to be the creator of the universe.

Spirits – Supernatural beings believed to influence human life and nature. Shrine – A sacred place where worship and rituals are performed. Sacrifice – Offering animals, food, or items to gods or spirits. Ritual – A set of traditional actions performed during worship or ceremonies. Divination – The practice of seeking knowledge or guidance from spiritual sources. Taboo – An action forbidden by religious or cultural laws. Libation – The pouring of drink as an offering to ancestors or spirits. Initiation – A ceremony marking entry into a new stage of life or group. Class Exercises and Answers Exercise 1: Fill in the Blanks a. A sacred place of worship is called a ________. b. The pouring of drink to honor ancestors is known as ________. c. The highest god in traditional religion is the ________ ________. Book References on Traditional Religion Mbiti, J. S. African Religions and Philosophy

title: COMPREHENSION
subject: English Language
rawText:
Reading to Comprehend Main Idea or Storyline 1. Understanding the Main Idea The main idea is the central thought or the most important point the writer wants to communicate. Everything else in the passage (examples, details, explanations) supports the main idea. It can usually be found: In the topic sentence (often the first or last sentence of a paragraph). Through repeated words, phrases, or ideas. By asking: “What is the author mostly talking about ? ” 2. Identifying Supporting Details Supporting details explain, prove, or expand the main idea. Look for facts, examples, descriptions, or reasons provided by the author. Distinguish between essential information (supports main idea) and extra details (interesting but not central). 3. Comprehending a Storyline (Narrative Texts) To understand the storyline of a novel, play, or short story: Characters – Who are the main people in the story ? What are their traits ? Setting – Where and when does the story take place ? Plot – What events happen ? Identify beginning, middle, and end. Conflict – What problem do the characters face ? Resolution – How is the problem solved ? Theme – What lesson, message, or idea does the story convey ?

4. Strategies for Better Comprehension Preview the text: Read titles, subheadings, or summaries first. Skim and scan: Skim for the gist, scan for key details. Highlight or underline important ideas while reading. Take notes in your own words after each section. Ask questions: Who ? What ? When ? Where ? Why ? How ? Summarize the passage or chapter to check if you captured the main idea. 5. Tips for Exams or Assignments Always read the questions before reading the passage (for comprehension tests). Watch out for distractors—details that are true but not the main idea. Pay attention to transition words (however, therefore, in conclusion) that signal key points. For literature, focus on how events are connected rather than memorizing every detail.

title: CONSONANT SOUNDS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Consonant sounds What is Spoken English ? Spoken English is the use of the English language through speech for communication. It focuses on pronunciation, stress, intonation, fluency, and correct use of sounds so that speech is clear and easily understood by listeners. Consonant Sounds Followed by /KW/ The sound /kw/ is a consonant cluster made up of two sounds produced closely together: /k/ – a voiceless velar plosive :w/ – a voiced bilabial glide When pronounced, the /k/ sound is released immediately into the /w/ sound, almost as one unit. This cluster often appears at the beginning of words, especially those spelled with “qu”. Example of pronunciation flow: queen → /kwi ː n/ The /k/ sound is followed immediately by the /w/ sound. Ten (10) Words with Consonant Sound /KW/ Queen Quick Quiet Quite Quarrel Quarter Question Quilt Quench Quarry

(All the words above begin with the consonant cluster /kw/.) Five Sentences Using Five of the Words The queen addressed the nation on television. 1.He gave a quick response to the question. 2.The classroom became quiet when the teacher entered. 3.We bought a loaf and cut it into a quarter. 4.The workers get stones from the quarry. Class Exercises on /KW/ Exercise 1: Identify the Sound Underline the words that contain the /kw/ sound. a. Queen b. Cat c. Quiet d. Boy e. Question Pronunciation Practice Write the phonetic transcription of the underlined words. queen quick question Book References New oxfords English book 1 O’Connor, J. D. Better English Pronunciation

title: READING A SHORT PASSAGE ON SMALL POX
subject: English Language
rawText:
Comprehension Reading a short passage in small pox What is Smallpox ? Smallpox is a serious viral disease caused by the variola virus. It mainly affected humans and was very contagious. Smallpox has been eradicated worldwide since 1980 due to vaccination. There are no natural cases today. How Smallpox Spreads Smallpox spread from person to person, mainly through: Airborne droplets When an infected person coughed, sneezed, or talked closely to others. Direct contact Touching the infected person’s skin or body fluids. Contaminated objects Clothes, bedding, or towels used by an infected person. It usually required close and prolonged contact to spread. What Happens to an Infected Person ? After a person was infected, the disease followed stages: Incubation period (7–17 days) No symptoms Person did not feel sick yet Early symptoms High fever Headache Body aches Extreme tiredness Sometimes vomiting Rash stage A rash appeared, starting on the face, then spreading to the body Rash changed into fluid-filled spots over time Spots later dried and formed scabs

Recovery or complications Scabs eventually fell off Many survivors were left with permanent scars In severe cases, smallpox could be fatal Prevention and Control The smallpox vaccine was very effective. Global vaccination programs led to complete eradication. Routine vaccination is no longer needed today. Symptoms: Fever → rash → scabs Status: Eradicated Prevention: Vaccination

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH AGRICULTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: Words Associated with agriculture. Agriculture is the science or practice of farming. Some words associated with agriculture are: Crops; grains, seeds, seedlings, tuber-yams, cassava, coco yams, okra, potatoes, onions, spinach. Farming implements: Cutlass, hoe, rake, axe, watering can, spade, shovel, hand fork, hand trowel, garden fork, head pan, digger, tractor, silo barn, bulldozer, harvester. Etc. Farming Activities: Bush-clearing, planting season, ridge making, staking, weeding, pruning, manuring, fertilizer. Etc. Other related words are: bumper harvest, famine, crop rotation, a bad harvest, etc. Some relevant words include: = Arable Farming- Farming done on a piece of land good for tilling. = Barn: A building for storing farm produce especially yams and coco yams. = Cash crops: Crops grown for sale rather than for consumption. E.g. Palm nuts, cocoa, groundnuts. Etc. = Fallow Land: A land allowed to stay without cultivation for a while. = Mechanized Farming: Working on the farm with machines. = Nursery: A place where young trees and plants are raised for transplanting or sale. Other words related, for example: Harvest, tillage, mixed farming, irrigation, pasture, fruits, mulching, vegetables, ploughing, planter. Etc ASSIGNMENT. Explain the following: Arable farming. nn English Consonant Sounds There are 24 consonant sounds in English. Each sound has its phonetic symbol, examples, and transcriptions. 1. /p/ – Voiceless bilabial plosive Examples: pen → /pen/, people → / n pi n p n l/, cup → /k n p/ 2. /b/ – Voiced bilabial plosive Examples: boy → /b nn /, baby → / n be n bi/, cab → /kæb/ 3. /t/ – Voiceless alveolar plosive Examples: tea → /ti n /, table → / n te n b n l/, cat → /kæt/ 4. /d/ – Voiced alveolar plosive Examples: dog → /d n g/, door → /d nn /, bad → /bæd/ 5. /k/ – Voiceless velar plosive Examples: cat → /kæt/, cook → /k n k/, kick → /k n k/ 6. /g/ – Voiced velar plosive Examples: goat → /g nn t/, game → /ge n m/, bag → /bæg/ 7. /f/ – Voiceless labiodental fricative Examples: fish → /f nn /, coffee → / n k n fi/, leaf → /li n f/ 8. /v/ – Voiced labiodental fricative Examples: van → /væn/, give → /g n v/, seven → / n sev n n/ 9. / θ / – Voiceless dental fricative Examples: think → / θ nn k/, thank → / θ æ n k/, thief → / θ i n f/ 10. /ð/ – Voiced dental fricative Examples: this → /ð n s/, those → /ð nn z/, father → / n f nn ð n / 11. /s/ – Voiceless alveolar fricative Examples: sun → /s n n/, snake → /sne n k/, bus → /b n s/ 12. /z/ – Voiced alveolar fricative Examples: zoo → /zu n /, rose → /r nn z/, noise → /n nn z/ 13. / n / – Voiceless palato-alveolar fricative Examples: shoe → / n u n /, sheep → / n i n p/, nation → / n ne nnn n/ 14. / n / – Voiced palato-alveolar fricative Examples: measure → / n me nn /, television → / n tel nn v nnn n/, usual → / n ju nn u n l/ 15. /h/ – Voiceless glottal fricative

Examples: hat → /hæt/, house → /ha n s/, behind → /b nn ha n nd/ 16. /t n / – Voiceless palato-alveolar affricate Examples: church → /t nnn t n /, cheese → /t n i n z/, teacher → / n ti n t nn / 17. /d n / – Voiced palato-alveolar affricate Examples: judge → /d nn d n /, jam → /d n æm/, village → / n v n l n d n / 18. /m/ – Bilabial nasal Examples: man → /mæn/, summer → / n s n m n /, time → /ta n m/ 19. /n/ – Alveolar nasal Examples: nose → /n nn z/, name → /ne n m/, dinner → / n d n n n / 20. / n / – Velar nasal Examples: sing → /s nn /, long → /l nn /, ringing → / n r nnnn / 21. /l/ – Alveolar lateral approximant Examples: leg → /leg/, little → / n l n tl n /, yellow → / n jel nn / 22. /r/ – Alveolar approximant Examples: red → /red/, river → / n r n v n /, around → / nn ra n nd/ 23. /j/ – Palatal approximant Examples: yes → /jes/, yellow → / n jel nn /, yard → /j nn d/ 24. /w/ – Labio-velar approximant Examples: we → /wi n /, water → / n w nn t n /, queen → /kwi n n/ Assignment: Write each word that contains these Consonant Sounds.

Ritual: A set of traditional actions performed during religious ceremonies. 3. Totem: A sacred object or animal believed to represent a group or family spiritually. 4. Shrine: A sacred place where spirits, gods, or ancestors are worshipped. 5. Divination: The act of seeking knowledge or guidance from spiritual forces. 6. Sacrifice: Offering of food, animals, or other items to appease or honor spirits. 7. Deity: A god or spirit believed to have supernatural power. 8. Oral Tradition: Stories and beliefs passed down verbally from generation to generation. 9. Taboo: A forbidden action or behavior in a community due to spiritual beliefs. 10. Libation: Pouring liquid as an offering to spirits or ancestors. 11. Charm: An object believed to carry protective or magical powers. 12. Priest/Priestess: A religious leader who performs rituals and communicates with spirits. 13. Festival: A celebration held to honor gods, spirits, or ancestors. 14. Spirit Medium: A person believed to communicate with spirits. 15. Cosmology: A belief about the structure and origin of the universe.

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: Types of Noun 1. Proper Noun: Names of specific people, places, or things. Example: Nigeria, Ahmed, Lagos. 2. Common Noun: Names of general people, places, or things. Example: city, girl, book. 3. Collective Noun: Names of groups of people or things. Example: team, herd, class. 4. Abstract Noun: Names of ideas, feelings, or qualities that cannot be touched. Example: love, honesty, bravery. 5. Concrete Noun: Names of things that can be seen, touched, smelled, heard, or tasted. Example: table, dog, perfume. 6. Countable Noun: Names of things that can be counted. Example: apples, cars, books. 7. Uncountable Noun: Names of things that cannot be counted. Example: water, sugar, rice.

Spelling is the rendering of speech sound(phoneme) into writing. Example of words commonly misspelt and their correct spelling. Wrong Correct Agument Argument Clearify clarify Greatful grateful Occurance occurrence Occasion occasion Separate separate Queue qur Plain plan Dye die One won Flu flew Flare flair Bury berry Blue blew iii. CONTINUOUS WRITING: NARRATIVE ESSAY An essay is a piece of writing usually short and in prose form, on any subject or topic.

A narrative essay tells astory of what happened. It may be factual or imaginary, a narrative essay narrates a story, an event or the life of a person. It uses description to present vivid mental picture of scene and events. For a good narrative essay you should ask and find answers to the following questions. a. what is the story about? b. what action took place in your story? C. who were responsible for those actions? d. when did the actions take place? e. how did the action take place? f. what were the consequences of the actions? GUIDELINE FOR A NARRATIVE ESSAY 1. The title. 2. The introduction: this introduces the topic and helps to provide enough information for proper understanding of the topic. 3. Body of the essay. a. discuss one main idea in each paragraph. b. use the past tense for events that happened in the past. c. present the event in a logical sequences. 4. Conclusion: it should be brief and logical. Examples of a narrative essay 1. My first day at school. 2. My first journey to Lagos. 3. A day I will not forget. 4. How I spent my last holiday. 5. The day I visited the zoo. 6. My first birthday celebration. 7. The car accident I witnessed.

rawText:
Theme: Speech Unit topic: speaking to persuade, Convince and sway opinion. Lesson Topic: Cultism In Speaking to persuade, Convince and Sway opinion, the speaker has to be very eloquent, logical and Know the subject matter of the topic in question, Cultism for instance is a topical issue m this country in colleges and universities which is having adverse effects on everybody within the community where it exists to bo able to persuade the listeners, the speak must make use of Idioms, figure of speech and other vocabularies that one powerful as to win your audience.. Causes of Cultism 1. Corruption in the society leads student to Cultism. 2. Broken homes can lead students to Cultism 3. Harsh economic situation in the county encourage cultism Effect of cultism 1. Destruction of lives and property of Students and university. 2. There increase in malpractice due to non-Seriousness of cultist in their study. 3. Cultist engage in nefarious activities like armed robbery, prostitution etc. to meet up with their extravagant lifestyle. Theme: Grammar Unit Topic: Verb Le sson Topic: Auxiliary verb. An auxiliary verb is a verb used with the Lexical main verb to show tense etc and to form questions and negatives. Auxiliary verbs are classified into two types

a. primary Auxiliary - be, do, have b. Modal Auxiliary - may, shall, can. Primary Auxiliary verbs are not used exclusively as auxiliary.They have four main functions. 1. They function as main verb eg we were here They have some grapes Ngozi did her job well. 2. Used to form tense of the verb. Eg: They had gone home He was Coming home when I see him. 3. Theme: Speech Unit Topic: Sibilants - the plural markers. Lesson Topic: The’s’ and es suffixes, In English, the form of a word may be changed to indicate certam grammatical relationships in number. Such relationships exist between Singular and plural forms of regular nouns. pluraity is therefore Indicated with the suffix or Inflectional marker, ' s' or es which is also known as pulural markers. This letter’s’ has three forms of pronunciation which is realized as/s/, /z/ and /iz/. This however, depends on the sound that ends the Word (root word) before the plural’s’ is added. Sibilant is an’s’ sound or letter at the end of a word. It can be a letter or a group of letters added to the end of a Lexica / l root word to form plural or to change It into a new grammatical meaning. Types 1. 's suffix 2. es' suffix 3 ies' suffix 4. ves' suffix 1. Formation of plural using the’s’ suffice Examples: boy-boys day-day donkey-donkeys roof - roofs Key - keys Toy-toys. 2. Formation of plurals using the 'es' suffix Eg. Tomato- tomatoes

class - classes bush - bushes axis - axes basis - bases box- boxes fish- fishes match- matches Criss - Crises hypothesis - hypotheses- 3. Formation of plurals using the 'ies' suffix eg: Cuty - Cities Country - Countries. assembly - assemblies daily - dailies dairy dairies diary diaries 4 Formation of plurals using the 'ves' suffix Eg: thief -thieves. life - Lives self - selves Knife - Knives wife - wives Leaf - Leaves. 5. pluralization by either 's' suffix or res Suffix: scarf - scarfs/scarves

hoot-hoofs/hoves wharf - wharfs/ wharves. Plural marker's- S Z iz Ways of forming plural maker. A. pronounce the plural marker as "s' if the Sound before the plural element is any of the Following Voiceless Consonants / p, t, k, f, q/ Eg Coughs. Sits ropes tops. Parks. Light Cots. Spots. Stuffs books. Rakes B. pronounce 's' as 'z' If the sound before the plural element is a vowel or any of the following voiced Consonants /b, d, g, v, l, m, n, q Eg. logs/Logz/ Lords/ld:dz/ hangs/hredz Films/filmz/ C. pronounce’s’ as 'iz' if the sound before the plural element is any of the following Consonant. /s, z, d, s, ts/ Eg. Is rages. buzzes matches fishes. church tosses. batchs. dances judge. teases /s/. /z/. /iz/ maps. cabs. catches

ropes. robes. fences mats. Card's. teases parks. tongues. ashes hoofs. wings. wages mobs. hears. bushes. ete. Theme: Structure Unit Topic: Types of sentences. Lesson Topic: The simple, compound, Complex an d Compound complex sentences A Sentence is a is a group of words expressing a statement, a question or an order usually Containing a subject and a verb. A Sentence Start with a capital letter and ends with a full-stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark Features of a sentence A sentence contains two necessary part Subject and predicate. The subject points to or names the person (s) thing(s) the sentence talks about ie who or what is being discussed. Eg. The boy dances well chioma died. The predicate indicates what is said on discussed about the person or thing. It includes the verb, auxiliary, adverb and adjective which say something about the subject. Eg: They suffered Babies eat. Subject may have marker like" my, the, a etc while the predicate may have auxiliary like "will, could has etc .

Eg the game must be going on now my Parents are Leaving . Types of sentence 1 . Simple sentence 2. Compound sentence 3. Complex senten ce 4. Compound complex sentence 1. Simple sentence: this contains one subject and one predicate or verb unit. It is made up of one main clause. Eg. a. the woman ran b. The thief has been caught. 2. Compound sentence: This contains two main clauses Linked by co-ordinating Conjunction Like "and, but or etc Eg a. the work stopped but the tools were kept inside. b. Ngozi found the goat and she took it to her mother 3. Complex sentence: This contains one main clause and one or more subordinate clauses. It is linked by the following who, which, as before, although, because, as If, unless, even though, when etc Eg: a. when it rains, he does not go to work. b. John did not do the assignment which the teacher gave him. 4. Compound complex sentence: This is made up of two or more main clauses and on or more Subordinate clauses. Eg: a. She Informed her parents that she was travelling to Lokoja to visit her uncle , tout she Changed her plans and went to kaduna where she stayed with some friends for a week. b. He came in (and) told us to leave the class, though he did not tell us the reason.

The air escape through a narrow opening in the Center of the tongue. Se as in Increase, loose /S/ is silent in tense words aisle, Corps, an rendezvous. /Z/ is a voiced alveolar fricative, is realized in the same manner as /s/ except That there is a vocal Card vibration The spelling symbols of/z/ sound Z-as in Zebra, Zero, breeze, zoo Zz -as in Puzzle, embezzle S as in thousand, rise, eyes, scares ss as in scissor x as in exact, axalt, exhibits se as in nose. mimal pairs for /s/ and /z/ /S/ /z/ advice advise

They are both Palate-alveolar affricate. /ts/ is a voiceless Palate. Alveolar affricate, is articulated with the front of the tongue is raised towards the roof of the mouth for the gradual release of the trap air because the vocal Card are wide apart. The spelling symbols for/ts/ "ch' as in catch, butcher, wretched tu as in question, Ingestion, digestion. te as in righteous. /dz/ is a Voiced palate-alveolar affricate. Jar

Question tags are short responses at the end of sentences in Speech. Question tag are not used for asking questions but for The confirmation of what the speaker already knows. There are Six (6) ways of forming Tag question 1. Positive statement + nagatine tag: positive response. When you require a yes answer, use a positive statement and a negative tag. Examples: a. I can do it , Can't I? b. We are right, aren't we? c. she is going, Isn't she? 2. Negative Statement attract positive tags. a. He is not here, is he? b. No you are not hungry, are you? 3. The finite auxiliary or helping verbs are usually repeated in the tag. Examples a. He is eating the food, isn't he? b. we shall not die, shall we? c. They can do it, can't they? 4. the mam or lexical verbs uses do, does or did in the tag. Examples

a. you don't care about her, do you? b. I didn't do that, did I? c. The girl cried bitterly, didn't she? 5 The subject in the tag question is a pronoun Example. a. musa didn't do that, did he? b. mary called you yesterday. didn't she? c. The sun is bright, isn't it? 6. The choice and tense of the auxiliary ( operator) are determined by the verb phrase in the main clause of statement. Examples a. David Jumps over the fence, doesn't he? (Present) b. David jumped over the fence, didn't he? (past) Special forms. I am your friend, aren't I? The above form is only possible when the statement is positive, the fag remains am I?.. eg a. I am not your friend, am I? Note, using need, let us rather, used to, example. a. We need to know, don't we? b. We need to ask him first, needn't we? c. You had rather say, wouldn't you? d. He used to lie , didn’t he?. Theme: summary Writing. Unit topic: How to write summary answer. Lesson Topic: Using simple sentences in Summary writing

Lesson according the summary page titled "war on honest man" unit 11 Theme: Continuous writing Unit Topic Essay writing Lesson Topic: Argumentative Essay-features An argumentative essay is like a debate in which the writer is expected to argue logically in support or against a given topic. It aims of convincing the audience or the reader to share the view point of the writer. It could be written or delivered orally as a debate. In a debate, a format is followed, while in ordinary argumentative essay the vocatives may not be necessary. In argumentative essay, the writer raises Points both "for" and against' and balance. While in debate, the writer takes a stand. Features / Format of Argumentative essay 1. The Topic: State the topic on the question. 2. The vocatives: This is the greeting to acknowledge the presence of members of the panel and the audience. Example: The chairman or the moderator, panel of Judges Accurate Time keeper, Co-debaters, Ladies and Gentlemen. 3. The introduction: In the Introductory Paragraph, the writer is expected to introduce him/herself and take a stand while stating the topic example." My name is.......a student of...... I am here to propose the motion which says that.......if there are certain key words in the topic, they have to be defined or explained quoting from a reliable source. 4. The body: The writer must state or give at least three strong points in favour of his/her stand to convince the Judges and the audience and win them to his/her side Also, good paragraphing is very Important and one points should be explained in paragraph. It is equally good for the writer to raise one or two points expected from the opponent and Counter them with good points

5. The Conclusion: the concluding paragraph requires the writer to reaffirm his position earlier taken. Example?" I once again state without fear of Contradiction that................ Thanks for Listening. Assignment . You are the mam speaker in a debate on the topic: children of literate rate parents perform better in school than those of illiterate Parents. Write your argument for or against the motion.

title: VELAR SOUNDS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Subject: English Language Class : SS2 Topic: Consonant Sounds – Velars Sub Topic : The /k/ and /g/ Sounds 1. What are Velar Sounds? Velar sounds are consonants produced when the *back of the tongue touches the soft palate*, which is the soft part at the back of the roof of your mouth. The two velar sounds in English are */k/* and */g/ 2. How to Produce /k/ and /g/ /k/ sound - *Voiceless* – your throat does not vibrate. - *Place*: Back of tongue touches soft palate. - *Manner*: Plosive – air is blocked briefly, then released with a small explosion of air. - *Sound*: A puff of air comes out. - *Examples*: *k*ite, *c*ar, s*ch*ool, ba*ck*, qui*ck* /g/ sound - Voiced* – your throat vibrates when you say it. - Place*: Back of tongue touches soft palate. - Manner*: Plosive – air is blocked briefly, then released. - Sound*: No puff of air; your voice is heard. - Examples*: *g*oat, *g*ame, bi*g*, *gu*ard, *gg*uest 3. How to Feel the Difference Put your hand on your throat and say: 1. */k/ /k/ /k/* – You feel no vibration. 2. */g/ /g/ /g/* – You feel a vibration. That vibration is the difference between voiceless /k/ and voiced /g/. 4. Common Spellings Sound Letters/Combinations Examples **/k/** k, c, ck, ch, qu **k**ey, **c**at, ba**ck**, s**ch**ool, **qu**ick **/g/**g, gg, gh, gu **g**oat, bi**gg**er, **gh**ost, **gu**ard

*Note:* In words like _knife, knight_, the *k* is silent. In words like _high, light_, the *gh* is silent. 5. Minimal Pairs for Practice These words sound almost the same except for /k/ and /g/: 1. *cat* /kæt/ – *gat* /gæt/ 2. *coat* /kəʊt/ – *goat* /gəʊt/ 3. *call* /kɔːl/ – *gall* /gɔːl/ 4. *key* /kiː/ – *gee* /giː/ Say them slowly and feel the difference in your throat. 6. Tongue Twister for Practice _Give Greg a green goat._ Say it slowly, focusing on the /g/ sound. Remember: - /k/ = no vibration, puff of air. - /g/ = vibration, no puff of air. - Both are made at the back of the mouth.

title: ANALYSIS OF CHAPTER 1-3 TO KILL A MOCKING BIRD
subject: English Language
rawText:
SUBJECT: Literature in English CLASS: VEI2/SS2 TOPIC: Detailed Analysis of Chapters 1 to 3: "To Kill a Mockingbird" Chapter 1 1. Introduction to Narrator: Scout Finch introduces herself, narrating from adulthood about her childhood memories in Maycomb, Alabama. 2. Setting: Maycomb is portrayed as a small, sleepy Southern town with its own traditions and social dynamics. 3. Family Background: Scout mentions her father, Atticus Finch, a lawyer, and her brother Jem. Their mother died when Scout was young. 4. Dill Harris: Dill, a summer visitor, is introduced — he's curious and becomes friends with Scout and Jem. 5. Boo Radley: The mysterious Boo Radley, a recluse, sparks curiosity and rumors among the children. He's hardly seen outside his house. 6. Themes: Establishes themes of childhood innocence, curiosity, and the peculiarities of small-town life. Chapter 2 1. Scout Starts School: Scout begins first grade. She’s eager but faces challenges adjusting because she already knows how to read from learning at home with Atticus. 2. Miss Caroline: Scout’s teacher, Miss Caroline Fisher, is new to Maycomb. She’s unaware of local customs and reacts sternly to Scout’s literacy. 3. Conflict: Scout gets reprimanded for knowing how to read; this shows a clash between Scout’s home education and school norms. 4. Character Insights: Shows Atticus’s supportive parenting — he encourages Scout’s learning. 5. Humor and Perspective: Narrated with Scout’s childlike viewpoint, bringing humor and innocence.

Chapter 3 1. Continued School Troubles: Scout faces more difficulties at school with Miss Caroline over explaining things about Walter Cunningham, a poorer classmate. 2. Walter Cunningham: Represents the economic differences in Maycomb. Walter’s family doesn’t have money for lunch — highlighting poverty aspects. 3. Atticus’s Advice: Atticus counsels Scout on understanding others’ perspectives (“You never really understand a person until you consider things from his point of view”). Key empathy lesson. 4. Calpurnia: The Finches’ African American housekeeper, Calpurnia, plays a significant nurturing role — showing interracial relationships in the household. 5. Themes: Empathy, social class differences, and childhood learning experiences are emphasized. Overall Insights for Chapters 1-3 1. Narrative Style: Scout’s narration blends childlike innocence with retrospective wisdom. 2. Character Development: Introduces key characters like Atticus showing moral grounding, and the enigmatic Boo Radley. 3. Themes: Highlight childhood innocence, empathy, social distinctions, and the ambiance of a Southern town. These early chapters set the stage for exploring deeper issues of morality, race, and growing up in the narrative of "To Kill a Mockingbird".

title: NOUN CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Subject: English Language Topic: Structure – Noun Clause Sub Topic: Types and Functions of Noun Claauses 1. Definition of a Noun Clause A *noun clause* is a dependent clause that does the work of a noun in a sentence. It has a subject and a verb but cannot stand alone as a complete sentence. Example: *What he said* is true. Here, _What he said_ is the subject of the sentence. 2. Types of Noun Clauses a. That-clause Introduced by _that_. Example:_ I know *that he is honest. b. Wh-clause* Introduced by _wh-words_ like _what, where, when, why, how, who_. Example:_ Tell me *where you live. c. Nominal Relative Clause* Introduced by _whoever, whatever, whichever, whoever_. Example:_ I will help *whoever asks. 3. Functions of Noun Clauses A noun clause can function as: a. Subject of the verb* That she lied* surprises me. b. Object of the verb* She said *that she was tired*. c. Complement of the verb* The problem is *that we are late*. d. Object of a preposition* I am interested in *what you said*. 4. How to Recognize a Noun Clause

1. It begins with _that, what, who, where, when, why, how, whoever, whatever_. 2. It has a subject and a verb inside it. 3. You can replace it with _it_ or _something_ and the sentence still makes sense. _Example:_ *What he said* is true → *It* is true. 5. Quick Check *Fact to remember:* A noun clause answers the questions _What?_ or _Who?_ in the sentence. _Example:_ I know ***_. → _What do I know?_[what] Key Point: A noun clause looks like a sentence but works like a single noun in another sentence.

title: PREFIXES
subject: English Language
rawText:
PREFIXES A prefix is a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning. A prefix cannot stand alone; it must be joined to a root word. Examples: happy → unhappy agree → disagree write → rewrite Common Prefixes and Their Meanings Prefix Meaning Example 1. un-- not. e.g: unhappy 2. dis---opposite / not. e.g: disagree 3. re---again. e g: rewrite 4. pre-.--+ before. e g: preview 5. mis---wrongly. e g misunderstand 6. inter----between. e.g: international i7. m- / in---not. e g: impossible / incorrect How Prefixes Change Meaning Prefixes change the meaning of words by: * Showing opposite meaning (legal----- illegal) * Showing repetition (write-+---- rewrite) " Showing time or order (view ----( preview) * Showing wrong action (understand → misunderstand)

Importance of Prefixes Prefixes help students to: 1. Understand the meanings of new words 2. Increase vocabulary 3. Improve comprehension and writing skills 4. Spell words correctly Examples in Sentences She was unhappy about the result. Please rewrite the essay. The two countries signed an international agreement. He misunderstood the .instructions

title: AFRICAN POETRY
subject: English Language
rawText: SUBJECT: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH Topic: Introduction to African Poetry Poetry according to Shakespeare is the spontaneous overflow of powerful emotions captured in tranquility. Poetry is a really enjoyable and beautiful aspect of literature. Its use of language is usually more figurative than prose and drama. It is written in lines and stanza. African poetry is a rich and diverse literary form that reflects the continent's history, culture, and experiences. It encompasses various styles, themes, and forms, often blending traditional oral traditions with modern influences. FEATURES 1. Oral Tradition: African poetry has its roots in oral storytelling, with griots (West African oral poets) playing a significant role. 2. Diversity of Themes: African poetry explores themes such as identity, culture, colonialism, and social justice. 3. Use of Imagery and Symbolism: African poets often employ vivid imagery and symbolism to convey meaning. Notable African Poets A poet is a person who writes poems while an African poet is a poet who writes about African themes, setting, language, symbols and images. 1. Wole Soyinka: Nigerian poet and playwright, Nobel laureate in literature. 2. Léopold Sédar Senghor: Senegalese poet and philosopher, key figure in the Negritude Movement. 3. Okot p'Bitek: Ugandan poet, known for his work "Song of Lawino." 4. Niyi Osundare Nigerian poet known for his poem “Not my Business” culled from his collection “Season of songs” Importance of Studying African Poetry 1. Cultural Understanding: African poetry provides insights into the continent's diverse cultures and histories. 2. Literary Appreciation: Studying African poetry enhances appreciation for literary diversity and creativity. 3. Critical Thinking: Analyzing African poetry develops critical thinking and analytical skills.

title: SPEECH WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: SPEECH WRITING Speech : this is a formal talk about a particular subject, given to a group of people. Types of speech may include; welcome or farewell address, valedictory speech, inaugural speech, funeral oration, or any other speech or address delivered in an occasion. Parts of a speech 1. Introduction : this includes the title, speaker’s name, audience, occasion, place and date. The introductory part of a speech should be captivating and like an arrow point towards where you are going. Example: A WELCOME ADDRESS PRESENTED BY THE PRINCIPAL OF GOVERNMENT GIRLS’ SECONDARY SCHOOL, DUTSE, MRS.NASIR BINTA, ON THE OCCASION OF THE SCHOOL’S 2018 ANNUAL INTERHOUSE SPORTS COMPETITION ON THIS 2 ND DAY OF FEBRUARY 2018. The Permanent Secretary, Ancopss Chairman, All Principals Present, Special Guests of Honour, My Noble Colleagues, Staff and Students, Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen, 2. Body: the body of the speech should be written in good paragraphs with each paragraph discussing a definite but important aspect of the subject. All the rules of grammar should be strictly observed and the language well polished. Everything in the speech must be related to the topic. You should make use of idioms and proverbs. 3. Conclusion: the conclusion of the speech, should as much as possible, be a summary of what has been said. It should also include closing greeting. Full name and designation. Examples: Mrs. Binta Nasir (Principal)

title: ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE Class: VEI2/ SS2 Topic: Argumentative Essay Definition: An argumentative essay is a type of essay that requires you to present a subject with a view to persuading your reader to agree with your point of view against another. It's all about arguing a point and convincing your audience. Features of an Argumentative Essay - Heading: Write your essay title in bold letters. - Introduction: Introduce your topic and state your position clearly. - Body: Present at least three well-developed paragraphs, each with a topic sentence that supports your argument. - Conclusion: Summarize your main points and reaffirm your position. Steps to Write an Argumentative Essay 1. Understand the topic: Know what you're arguing about and take a clear stance. 2. Research and gather evidence: Collect facts, statistics, and expert opinions to support your argument. 3. Plan your essay: Organize your ideas and structure your essay logically. 4. Write persuasively: Use emotive language, rhetorical questions, and repetition to convince your audience. 5. Conclude strongly: Summarize your points and reiterate your position. Tips for Writing a Good Argumentative Essay - Use simple and clear language: Avoid jargon and complex sentences. - Use persuasive techniques: Ask rhetorical questions, use emotive language, and appeal to your audience's values. - Organize your ideas: Use transitional words and phrases to link your paragraphs. - Use evidence: Support your argument with facts, statistics, and expert opinions.

Topic: 1. "Should Mixed Secondary Schools be Dissolved in Nigeria?" Topic: 2. Uniforms should be abolished in Secondary schools. - Introduction: Hook your audience, state your position, and preview your main points. - Body Paragraph 1: Argue that mixed schools promote distraction and immorality. - Body Paragraph 2: Argue that single-sex schools improve academic performance and reduce teenage pregnancy. - Body Paragraph 3: Argue that dissolving mixed schools would reduce societal problems like rape and harassment. - Conclusion: Summarize your points and reiterate your position. Evaluation Criteria - Content: Relevance, depth, and coherence of argument. - Organization: Logical structure and linking of paragraphs. - Language: Clarity, persuasiveness, and grammar. - Conclusion: Strength of summary and final thought.¹ ²

title: LISTENING COMPREHENSION
subject: English Language
rawText: SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE TOPIC: Listening Comprehension: Speeches Listening is a really important skill in English Comprehension. You need to avoid distraction and focus when listening for a purpose. Importance of Listening Comprehension 1. Critical Thinking: Listening comprehension helps develop critical thinking skills. 2. Effective Communication: Understanding speeches enhances communication skills. 3. Academic and Professional Success: Listening comprehension is essential for academic and professional success. Strategies for Improving Listening Comprehension 1. Active Listening: Focus on the speaker, maintain eye contact, and avoid distractions. 2. Note-taking: Take notes on key points, main ideas, and supporting details. 3. Contextual Understanding: Consider the speaker's purpose, audience, and tone. 4. Repetition and Review: Repeat and review key points to reinforce understanding. Key Elements to Focus On 1. Main Idea: Identify the speaker's central message. 2. Supporting Details: Recognize evidence, examples, and explanations. 3. Tone and Purpose: Understand the speaker's attitude and intention. 4. title: ADJECTIVAL PHRASE
subject: English Language
rawText: Topic: Adjectival Phrases and their Grammatical Functions Class: SS2 Adjectival Phrases An adjectival phrase is a group of words that functions as an adjective, modifying a noun or pronoun. It typically consists of a preposition, an adjective, and a noun. Examples: 1. The book on the table is mine. (Adjectival phrase: "on the table") 2. The girl with blue eyes is my sister. (Adjectival phrase: "with blue eyes") 3. The house by the river is for sale. (Adjectival phrase: "by the river") Grammatical Functions: 1. Modification: Adjectival phrases modify nouns or pronouns, providing more information. 2. Attribution: They attribute qualities or characteristics to the noun or pronoun. Types of Adjectival Phrases : 1. Prepositional phrases: Begin with a preposition (e.g., "in the garden", "with great enthusiasm") 2. Participial phrases: Begin with a participle (e.g., "written in haste", "having great potential") Exercises: 1. Identify adjectival phrases in given sentences. 2. Use adjectival phrases to complete sentences. 3. Create sentences using adjectival phrases.

title: READING COMPREHENSION
subject: English Language
rawText: READING FOR IMPLIED MEANING ‘Imply’ is when an information is not stated openly. When information is not stated openly we tend to guess, assume, conclude or infer its meaning; that is when we say it has an implied “meaning”. Tips students need to follow when reading for implied meaning 1. Keep asking questions as you read. Questions such as :- where, why, when, how - will shed more light on the content 2. Note that certain expressions are subtle but laden with deeper meaning 3. Keep linking ideas as you read on to understand the writer’s line of development. This will enable you notice when a gap is created 4. Your world view: your personal background knowledge of a topic may assist you to decipher a hidden implied meaning 5. When you notice something is amiss, you assume what has happened. This assumption may make you draw some conclusions, and this conclusions will help you locate the implied meaning Assignment Answer the comprehension questions following the passage read.

title: VOWELS: DIPHTHONGS
subject: English Language
rawText: English Language Topic: Vowels: Diphthongs /ei/ Class: SS2/ VEI 2 Definition: Diphthongs are called double vowel sounds because they are a combination of 2 vowel sounds which are pronounced in quick succession to make one sound. There are eight Diphthongs in the English language. Today we focus on only one diphthong. The /ei/ is a diphthong sound that glides from /e/ to /i/ - Examples: play, day, say, way, stay - Pronunciation Tips: - Start with /e/ sound - Glide to /i/ sound - Keep the sound smooth and connected - Practice Words: - play - day - say - way - stay - pay - bay etc

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT: ENVIRONMENT
subject: English Language
rawText: Topic: Conjunctions Class: JSS2 What are Conjunctions? Conjunctions are words that connect words, phrases, or clauses (and, but, or) etc Types of Conjunctions 1. Coordinating Conjunctions: and, but, or, so, yet Examples: I like apples and oranges. - I will meet you at the park and we will play football. 2. Subordinating Conjunctions: because, although, if, unless, while - Example: I'm tired because I didn't sleep. 3. Correlative Conjunctions: both...and, either...or, neither...nor - Example: I like both reading and writing. Uses of conjunctions: - They are used to Join words: apples and bananas. - They are used to Join phrases: in the morning or at night. - They are used to Join clauses: I wanted to go, but it was raining. Assignment Use the following conjunctions to make sentences: either…or, because, or, and.

title: CONSONANT CLUSTERS
subject: English Language
rawText: SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE CLASS: VEI2/SS2 TOPIC: Consonant Clusters Definition: Consonant clusters are groups of consonant sounds that appear together in a word without any vowel sound between them. These clusters can be found at the beginning, middle, or end of words. Types of Consonant Clusters - Initial Consonant Clusters: Clusters that appear at the beginning of words, e.g., /bl/ in "black," /tr/ in "tree," /sk/ in "school." - Final Consonant Clusters: Clusters that appear at the end of words, e.g., /nt/ in "rent," /st/ in "best," /pts/ in "depths." - Medial Consonant Clusters: Clusters that appear in the middle of words, e.g., /str/ in "street," /spl/ in "splendid." Examples of Consonant Clusters - /bl/ - black, blanket, bleed - /tr/ - tree, trip, trend - /sk/ - school, ski, sketch - /nt/ - rent, tent, lint - /st/ - best, chest, nest Importance of Consonant Clusters - Improves Pronunciation: Mastering consonant clusters helps in accurate pronunciation of words. - Enhances Communication: Clear articulation of consonant clusters aids in effective communication. - Boosts Confidence: Correct use of consonant clusters can make speech more confident and fluent.

subject: English Language
rawText:
STUDENTS’ SUMMARY NOTE Topic: Structure – Clauses A clause is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb. Features of a Clause It has a subject (the doer of the action). It has a verb (the action or state). It forms part of a sentence. It may express a complete or incomplete meaning. Types of Clauses 1. Independent Clause (Main Clause) It can stand alone as a complete sentence. It expresses a complete thought. Examples: She is happy. The boy is playing. 2. Dependent Clause (Subordinate Clause) It cannot stand alone as a complete sentence. It depends on an independent clause to make full meaning. Examples: Because she is happy Although the boy is playing Examples in Sentences When the bell rang, the students left the class. “When the bell rang” → Dependent clause “the students left the class” → Independent clause

Conclusion Clauses are important in sentence construction. Understanding them helps in forming correct and meaningful sentences.

title: COMPREHENSION
subject: English Language
rawText:
. Comprehension Listening to Poetry for Comprehension and Pleasure Comprehension means understanding what we hear or read. When we listen to poetry, we listen not only to understand the meaning , but also to enjoy the sound, rhythm, and emotions in the poem. How to Listen to Poetry Effectively  Listen carefully to the theme or message  Pay attention to tone and mood  Notice rhymes, rhythm, and repetition  Think about the feelings the poem creates  Visualize the images used by the poet Types of Poetry 1. Lyric Poetry – Expresses personal feelings or emotions Example: love poems, songs 2. Narrative Poetry – Tells a story Example: ballads, epics 3. Descriptive Poetry – Describes a person, place, or thing vividly 4. Dramatic Poetry – Written in the form of a speech or dialogue 5. Free Verse – Poetry without fixed rhyme or rhythm 2. Vocabulary Development Words Associated with Building Construction Building construction involves planning, designing, and constructing structures such as houses, bridges, and schools. Common Construction Vocabulary  Foundation – the base of a building  Brick – a rectangular block used in building  Cement – material used to bind bricks  Concrete – mixture of cement, sand, and gravel  Beam – horizontal support structure  Pillar/Column – vertical support  Roof – top covering of a building  Wall – vertical structure enclosing a building

 Plaster – material used to cover walls  Scaffold – temporary structure used by workers  Blueprint – detailed building plan  Contractor – person in charge of construction 3. Structure Preservative Prefixes A prefix is a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning. Preservative prefixes suggest keeping, protecting, or preventing damage . Common Preservative Prefixes  pre- (before) → prevent, preserve  pro- (for) → protect  con- (together) → conserve  re- (again) → restore, rebuild  anti- (against) → antiseptic Examples in Sentences  We must preserve our cultural heritage.  Trees help protect the environment.  Old buildings are restored carefully. 4. Continuous Writing Free Writing Free writing is writing without strict rules. The writer expresses ideas freely and creatively. Types of Free Writing 1. Short Story – A brief fictional narrative with characters and a plot 2. Poem – Creative writing using rhythm, imagery, and emotion 3. Play – Writing meant to be acted on stage 4. Essay – Personal thoughts or opinions written freely Tips for Free Writing

 Write without worrying about mistakes  Focus on ideas and imagination  Let thoughts flow naturally  Revise later if necessary 5. Literary Devices Literary devices are techniques writers use to make their writing more interesting and effective. Common Literary Devices  Simile – comparison using like or as Example: He is as brave as a lion.  Metaphor – direct comparison Example: Time is a thief.  Personification – giving human qualities to non-living things Example: The wind whispered softly.  Alliteration – repetition of the same initial sound Example: She sells sea shells.  Imagery – language that appeals to the senses Example: The golden sun lit the sky.  Rhyme – repetition of similar sounds Example: light – night

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: Meaning of Adjective An adjective is a word that describes or modifies a noun or pronoun by giving more information about it. Examples: happy, tall, blue, three, many. Types of Adjectives Descriptive: describe quality (e.g., beautiful). Quantitative: indicate quantity (e.g., some water). Numeral: show number or order (e.g., five students). Demonstrative: point out specific nouns (e.g., this book). Possessive: show ownership (e.g., her bag). Interrogative: used in questions (e.g., which car?). Distributive: refer to items individually (e.g., each student). Order of Adjectives Adjectives usually follow this order: Opinion → Size → Age → Shape → Color → Origin → Material → Purpose → Noun Example: A lovely small old red French wooden chair. Importance of Using Adjectives Makes sentences clearer. Adds detail and interest. Improves descriptive writing. Examples in Sentences She bought a beautiful red dress. He lives in a large modern house. They adopted a small brown puppy.

title: HUMAN INTERNAL BODY SYSTEM
subject: English Language
rawText:
Human Internal body system Internal body system are the organs inside the body that work harmoniously to keep the body healthy. Words associated with internal human body system; liver, kidney, heart, intestines, stomach, brain. 1. Liver: The liver is the largest solid organ of the body. It removes toxins from the body's blood supply, maintains healthy blood sugar levels and regulates clotting. It is located beneath the rib cage in the right upper abdomen. 2. Kidney: The kidneys are a pair of bean-shaped organs on either side of the spine below the rib. The functions of the kidney include, removal of wastes, filter the blood, control the body's fluid balance and keep the right levels of electrolytes. �  Heart: The heart is a muscular organ situated in the chest. The function of the heart include, pumping oxygenated blood to other body parts, maintaining blood pressure, pumping hormones and other vital substances to different parts of the

body.

rawText:
ADJUNCTS Adjunct is a part of a sentence that modifies the verb. However, if adjunct is removed from the sentence, we will still have a meaningful sentence. Adjunct is also called an adverb and functions as adverbials in sentences. Types of Adjuncts 1. Adjunct of Time – This shows when an action is done or happened. It answers the question ‘when’. It is placed at the beginning or at the end of a sentence. When they are at the beginning, they are often emphasized e.g (a). I phoned you yesterday (b). I saw her a few months ago (c). Last week, I saw them walking together 2 . Adjunct of Place – This shows where an action is done or performed. It answers the question ‘where’. Such adverb are placed after verb e.g (a). I live here (b). They are talking outside (c). We met her in the zoo (d). They walked along the river 3 . Adjunct of Manner – This shows how an action or something is done. It answers the question ‘how’. The adverb is a place just after the verb when it is used in a sentence (a). She cried loudly (b). He drives speedily 4 . Adjunct of Degree or Quantity – This answer the question ‘to what degree’, how much. It is usually placed before the adjectives and the adverb. (a) it is too dark for us to see anything (b). last night, it rained very heavily. 5 . Adjunct of Frequency – This answers the question ‘how often’. Adverb of frequency are very important because we often use them. Examples include never, seldomly, occasionally, sometimes, generally, usually, quick, always, already, nearly, almost, hardly etc. (a). Jane rarely late for work (b). We only write to each other occasionally. 6. Affirmative Adjunct (Yes) and Adverb of Negation (No). Examples include Yes, Surely, certainly, indeed, by any means, not at all. (a). I hope my parents just for once will say yes to my latest idea. (b). if would indeed help, if I had a bodyguard. 7. Interrogative Adjunct – it answers question when, where, how, why, how much, often etc (a). When was the last time you saw her? (b). How could you have overlooked all these mistakes.

Week 1 (Comprehension) Unite Topic :- Reading Comprehension. Lesson Topic:- Reading for main point Text: New concept English Pg4 chp…….. “Revolutionaries” The main points of any passage is the essential contents they are the main substance of what has been written. They do not contain unnecessary details. The main point, therefore is the main idea, the summary or the aspect that is gripping and essential for the desired information. The main point of the passage is the air of nonchalance put up by Agbeyegb’s conrades to foil hisrerolution plan. Key words used in the passage are:- 1. Draw back, plead, Queries, Doubs, exposed, Revolutions, simulating Assignment:- To answer the comprehension question in pg5 of their text book. A prefix is a group of letters added to a root word to form new words and new meaning or an affix attached to the beginning of a word, base ,or phrase and serving to produce a derivative word or an inflectional from. Example:- un, mis, il, in, im, dis, etc. A prefix added to a word usually does not change the word class (Part of Speech) of the word e.g material-immaterial(adjective) Behave-misbehave(verb) Personal-impersonal(adjective). Types of Prefix A Prefixes showing negation Dis Away, A part Disappear, disagree and disown Ill Not Illogical, illegal, illiterate Im Not Immodest, impossible, imperfect, immobile Un Not Unhappy, uncertainly, unfair

Anti Against Antisocial, antibiotics Mai Badly Malnourish, maltreat B prefix that show number Uni One Unilateral, unison Mono One Monopoly, monologue Bi Tow Bilateral, binomial Di Two Diphthong, dissect Tri Three Tricycle, tipped Penta Five Pentagon, pentagram, pentameter Poly Many Polysyllable, polygamy, polytechnique Homo Same Homophone, homogeneous Hetero Different Heterosexual, heterogeneous C. Prefixes showing attitude Pro For, infavour, support Pro-democrat, pro-militant, pro-war, pro-government Anti Against, opposed to Anti-social, anti-corruption, anti-clerical Co Together with Co-operate, co-worker, co-tenant, co- channel, co-editor, co-exist D. prefixes that are used to generate antonyms Un Unhealthy, untainted, unserious, unaided, uninformed, unfair, untie Mis Mislead, misquote, misspell, misunderstand Ill Illegal, illogical, illegitimate, illiterate In Indecision, inaudible, inaccessible, Im Improper, impossible, monorail, impolite, immature, immodest

Assignment:- Generate two sentences using the following words and their antonyms:- Regular Unwanted Polite Decent Agree Manage Wk Topic-; Words associated with the environment. Environment refers to our immediate surroundings in which all living and non- living component co-exist. Environment is made of the air, water and land on earth, which can be harmed by man’s activities, the people and things around you in your life. Example, the building you use, people you live or work with and the general situation you are in. Also, Environment is a natural features of a place e.g whether, the type of land it has and the type of plants tt grow on it. Environmental Problems Pollution, Bush Burning, Disposal of refuse, Pest control, Sewage System, Smoking, Drainage. Soil excavation, Environmental degradation e.t.c. All these problems are caused by man that inhabit it which in effect directly or in directly affects the life of man or animals health wise. Solutions to some Environmental problems are; 1) Sustainable Building 2) Recycle properly 3) Renewable energy 4) Conserve water and electricity 5) Replace disposable items with reusable. Words associated with natural environment.

1. Atmosphere (ii) earth (iii) gasses (iv) carbon dioxide v) sewage (vi) rain (vii) disposal (viii) climate (ix) hurricanes (x) pollution. Assignment:- Check the environment Where you live and write down at least five environmental problems you notice, prefer solutions Week 2 (speech) Speech:- Unit Topic :- Poetry Lesson Topic:- listening to poetry for comprehension pleasure Poetry is the sum total of the use of certain devices in writing such as rhyme, rhythm, figures of speech, stanza, the poet’s feeling and attitude to the subject matter poetry is an imaginative and emotional writing to stimulate thought to be enjoyed . Types of poetry 1. Narrative poem:- poem that tell a story 2. Lyrics Poem:- Poem that is musical 3. Dramatic Poem:- Poem involving characters that interest in verse form 4. Sonnet:- A 14 – line poem, we have two types of sonnet. a. Retrachan Italian sonnet divided into octave and sestet with rhyming schema of abba, abba, ade, ade b. Shakes pearan sonnet with has 3 set of four lines followed by a couplet. 5. Pastoral poem:- Poem on a country side or rural life 6. Dirge, poem for the dead 7. Epigram:- Poem about the deeds of great people 8. Ode:- Poem that addresses a person or thing others include limerick, Elegy, epigram, Ballad e.t.c Features of poetry 1. A poem in nerse form or stanza 2. A poem uses rhyme or rhythm 3. A poem makes use of figures of speech like smile, metaphor, alitrtstion, repetition, onomatopoeia e.t.c to create imagery which appeal to the senses

4. The language of poetry is usually concise when compared to a short story or drama To read the poem on page 217 of the English text titled “On the grasshopper and cricket by John Keats. To analyze the poem To analyze the poem The poem is about nature and the beauty of simple and natural things of life, it mainly talks about two insects the grasshopper and the cricket According to the poet, the earth can never be dead or silent because nature keeps it alive. The natural things objects used in the setting include insect, birds, sun, trees and weed. The poem is a petracham sonnet, the rhyming scheme used is abba abba ede ede. Assignment 1. write a short poem of your own 2. Differentiate between patriarchal and Shakespeare sonnet. 3. provide answers to the poem read in the class. Week 2 ( vocabulary development) Unit topic; Words associated with building Lesson topic; Types of building, building materials and workers. A. A building is a structure such as house, church or factory that has a roof and wall, the building have types and some are constructed for different purpose e.g for resident, hotel, church, hospital, factory, office, e.t.c. These are also different materials for building and workers. B. Types of building; bungalow, cottage, mansion, one storey building, high rise building, block of flats, dethatched or semi detected building place sky scrappers e.t.c. C. D. building materials; nails, bricks, wood, bamboo, paint, block, concrete, sand, cement, tiles, marble, stones, planks, rod, zinc, saw, hammer, e.t.c.

E. Part of the house; bedroom, kitchen, doors, window, roof, sitting room, dining room, toilet, bathroom, lobby, varanda, garage, basement e.t.c. F.
