Airways : a space between roof insulation and roof boards for movement of ar. 2. Asphalt:- This is used n building for the water proof covering of roofs, flours, and other exterior parts 3. Conduit:- A ppe used n electrical work n which wire is installed 4. The margin of a roof projecting over the wall 5. Foundation:- The supporting proton of any structure below the frst floor 6. Partition:- a wall that subdivides spaces within any story f a building 7. Rafter :_ structure designed t support the roof 8. Veneer:- than sheets f wood made by rotary cutting or slicing a log. Other words Assignment Fill in the gaps with the correct options from A – D pg 70 of their text book 1 – 10. Week 2 ( structure) Unit topic; prefix Lesson topic; preservative prefix

A prefix is a linguistic element that is not an independent word but, is attatched to the beginning of a word to modify it meaning. e.g Appear – disappear cycle – tricycle operate – co – operate A preservative prefix is a prefix or condition of a word from changing. it makes use of the prefix ;re; which means again or back. ;re; as used in preservative prefix can mean; a. To preserve the present state b. To prevent from decay c. To improve on the current state d. To prevent something from getting spoil to remove fault in something. e. to improve on it Examples; work – rework affirm – reaffirm assure – reassure consider – reconsider count – recount inform – rein form arrange – rearrange cast – recast form – reform elect – re elect apply – reapply

use – reuse adjust – readjust activate – reactivate design – redesign Assignment 1. write the preservative prefix of the following words i. call ii. construct iii. start iv. gain v. visit 2. make sentences using the words above. Week 2 (continuous writing) Unit topic; free writing Lesson topic; play drama Creative writing is a skillful and imaginative literary work produced by someone without help from another, it can be a story ,poem or drama. free writing is similar to create writing. it requires ones ability think, reason and creat a piece of literary work. it can be on your personal experience or others. Drama is a literary work which involve conversation or dialogue between characters when acting on the stage. it is called a play. Drama is written in acts and scenes Types of drama 1. Comedy; a drama full of exaggerated scene for amusement and entertainment e.g she stops to conquer, by oliver Goldsmith. 2. Tragedy; A drama full of suspense and frightful scene and in which the protagonist in constant danger. it ends on a sorrowful note e.g; Othello; by shake spear. 3. Tragedy-comedy; a drama piece in which the protagonist is faced with over bearing challenges and confrontation from his or her rivals. the suffering of protagonist provokes the sympathy of the reader. How ever, by the last minute intervention of the ;

dues Exmachina; the protagonist is rescued, thus bringing the play to a happy resolution e.g lord of the files by William Golding. 4. straight play; A serious non conic drama 5. Poetic drama; A drama written in poetic verses. 6. Mime; A play in which the character uses gesture and other body languages (action) to express their thought instead of verbal communication. 7. Opera:- A drama work in which all the actions are accompanied by music 8. Passion Play:- A Christian play in which the trail, Crucifixion death and resurrection of Jesus Christ is enacted 9. Masque or mask:- A drama in which poetry, music, dance, song, lavish costumes and costly stage, effects are used in an indoor performance. Characters in Drama 1. Hero/ Heroin:- The main character, male or female respectively who usually attains extraordinary fact and a mass fame through bravery and determination 2. Tragic Hero:- A character who rises to a noble height by his/ her extraordinary trait but is ruined by an inherent human flow 3. Protagonist:- The main character who under takes a lot of risk and face a lot of antagonism in other fight for survival and to ensure that the truth and other legitimate course is ensured and presented in a literal work 4. Antagonist:- A charater who is a close rival of the protagonist. Features of drama 1. Acts:- A major section of the action in a play which may contain one or two scenes. It marks a progressive stage in the plot of the play. 2. Cast:- The complete list of all actor scheduled to perform in a play Assignment 1. List five type of drama 2. In not less than three (3) pages write a drama pieces on the ” Game of thrones” Week 3 (Speech) Unit Topic-;Listening Comprehension (oral) Lesson Topic-; Listening to summarize speeches.

Listening is the ability to pay attention to and effectively interpret what other people are saying. While A speech is written material meant to be read to a group of listeners importance of developing listening skill 1. Listening encourage empathy 2. Reduces misunderstanding 3. Builds relationship 4. Improves thought process 5. Conflict resolution The students listen as the teacher reads, the listen in comprehension Appendix 3 page 259 on the Adventures of Solomon Assignment Provide the answers to the text on page 228. Week ( structure) Unit Topic:- Figurative expression lesson topic figure of speech Figures of speech are special expression used to covey clear and brief impression than when expressed in ordinary works colourful, forceful, powerful and impressive. 1. SIMILE: It compares one thing with another using the words like or ‘as’ the two things in comparison are not similar but have similarity in the area being compared example : i. he is as dirty as a pig ii. she talks like a parrot 2. METAPHOR: a metaphor is a figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that is not literally true but helps to explain an idea or idea or make comparison . Example: i. Emeka is a tiger ii. She has a hear of stone 3. HYPERBOLE: it is an exasperation of fact for the sake of emphasis or to lighten effect. Example i. All the water in the ocean cannot wash the dert in his clothes. ii. I ate a mountain of food 4. PERSONIFICATION: It is giving of life and human attributes to inanimate objects or abstract things e.g i. The leaves are dancing to the tune of the wind ii. Evil walk in the shadow of night 5. OXYMORON: This is placing side by side two words that are contradict each other i. Etuk is a holy sinner

ii. It is an open secret that Odo is an armed robber iii. Ada is an honest liar 6. ANTITHESIS: It is pairing of two opposite ideas in a sentence in order to heighten a sharp contract between the ideas example: i. Man proposes, God disposes ii. United we stand, divided we fall iii. To err is human, to forgive is divine 7. SYNECDOCHE: This is when a part used to represent a whole things or a hole car be used to represent a part . Example: i. All fingers are not equal ii. The st best brains are in my class iii. Two heads are better than one 8. METONYMY: It is the act of referring to something by the name of something else that is closely connected or associated with it example: i. The crown has summon elders for a meeting ii. All the speakers must get the chair iii. Judgments will start from the pulpit 9. EVPHENISM: It talks of harsh and unpleasant things in a mild or pleasant way. Eg i. Mr. Sunday kicked the bucket last night ii. The man of the underworld sent him to the world beyond iii. He fought with his better half 10. ONOMATOPOEA: It is the ability of words to echo their meaning e.g (i) The bell of the chock jingles (ii) The student hissed 11. Rhetorical question:- It is when a question that does not need an answer is asked just for the purpose of persuading and appealing to the mind of the audience (i) E.g My people, will I like myself for you (ii) Can a kettle call a pot black? (iii) Who will say that his mother soup is bitter. 12. APOSTROPHE:- this is addressing an about person (abstract now) as if it were present, heving life and listening to the speaker. Example:- a. Oh! Death where is thy sting? b. O! WAEC, why are you treating me badly. c. Hear me, O earth, hear me, O hills 13. PARADOX:- it is a self contrary statement which seems to appear meaningless and unreasonable in the first thought but if closely examined, it contains an element of truth e.g i. The best way to learn a subjects is to teach it.

ii. Cowards dies many times before their death iii. For whosever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel shall save it. Assignment Make sentence to show the following figure of speech (2 sentence for each) (1) (i) Simile (ii) metaphor (iii) personification (iv) hyperbole (v) Oxymoron Week 3 ( Comprehension) Unit Topic :- Reading for structural pattern Lesion Topic:- “Chimere in search of her roofs” Page 205 – 206 unit 17 Structural pattern is the overall form organization of sentences something in this case we look at the structure of sentence in a passage and identify those that are simple sentences or compound sentences e.t.c e.g the first sentence in the 1 st paragraph is a complex sentence because it as two subordinate clause and one simple sentence Second sentence is a compound sentence, the 3 rd is a complex sentence e.t.c The main points include 1. Chimere travelled to umueze in search of root I father 2. She has not being to Umueze before 3. She did not know the Umueze that she was going to 4. The driver tried to help her by stopping her at a convenient place 5. Chemere stopped at church in order to bring her quest Assignment Provide the answers to all the comprehension questions (a – g) Week 3 (continuous writing) Unit Topic :-Speeches Unit Title:- writing speeches (An address given on a prize given day) A speech is a written material meant to be read to a group of listeners. Speeches are meavit to entain, educate and inform people Features of a speech It is also meant to motivate people to action 1. The title there should be a title for the speech you are to deliver. The title should indicate the mark of identification such as the - The purpose - Name and the title of speaker - Occasion

- Place - Date and time An Address give on a prize giving day, by Joy Okoli the Head girl of government secondary school, Kubwa, the school Assembly Hall this day with September, 2017. 2. The introduction: this must be interesting and captivating so as to elicit the interest of the listeners. It must start within salutation e.g Good morning the chairman, the principal, the school management, the P.T.A, ladies and gentlemen . I feel highly honoured to stand here today to deliver my speech on ............... 3. The body:- this is the stage that contains the actual message. Start by giving. Your main points and then support each point with relevant details, comparisons and contrasts e.t.c explain who, where, why, how. The ideas must be stated in good clear sentences 4. The conclusion:- here you summarize your main points . it is important to end in a memorable way by: - Making a forceful and shocking statement - urging your audience to follow a certain line of action or thought e.t.c - Ending in an interesting and captivating manner. Guidelines Required for speech written 1. A speech is meant to be delivered to an audience. Hence the use of present tense is require 2. A speech should be in four sentence viz, heading introduction, body and conclusion 3. Slangs and humour should be avoided since the speech is meant to be delivered to an audience superior to the writer. The use of humour is appropriate only in an informal situation like party. 4. No use of name (s) at the end of the speech since it would have been introduction at the heading. Assignment Prepare a speech to be delivered on the prize and award giving day of the final year students of the school. - Application of knowledge of first aid before going to the hospital - Preventive health care i.e preventive measures or steps to put in place to avoid sickness and diseases. - Nutrition education; these are the things to avoid or consume. - Skills and knowledge to form life long habbit. Features 1. The topic 2.The nocatives 3. The introduction 4. The body 5. The conclusion Points to consider (proposing) Health education is the understanding of how to maintain personal health. -Health education helps an individual to be more proactive in health The steps points to oppose application of knowledge of first aid before going to the hospital. The necessary things to avoid or consume. - First Aid: Application of knowledge of first aid before gong to hospital - Preventive health care: i.e preventive measures or steps to put in place to avoid sickeness and deases. - Nutrition education: those are the things to avoid to consumer - Skills and knowledge to form long life habits: sklls and knowledge to from life long habits. Assignment

Write your speech for against the motion Week 4 (Structure) Unit topic; Suffixes Lesson Topic; Suffixes ( able, age, action, en e.t.c.) Suffixes are added at the end of a word to form another word, In actual fact, many of the words, either prefixes or suffixes, If you are able to add a suffix to a word, it becomes easier to identify the word classes ( parts of speech). Nouns, adjectives, adverb are easily identifiable in words bearing suffixes. Example; Able; Laugh – laughable Wash – washable Loud – loudable Age Bond – bondage Waste – wastage Drain – drainage Mile – miieage Dose – dosage Ant Assist – assistant Serve – servant Depend – dependant Aspire – aspirant En Loose – loosen Dead – deaden Tight – tighten Quick – quicken

Full Month – monthful Sorrow – sorrowful care – careful Hope – hopeful Week 4 ( vocabulary development) Unit topic; Words associated with law and order Lesson topic; order in the court, legal action e.t.c. law is the whole system of rules that people in a particular country or area must obey. Order means a situation in which rules are obeyed and authority are respected,The dictionary interpretes the law of the nation which must be obeyed to maintain order in that nation. Words associated with law and order. 1.Accuse; To say that somebody has done wrong 2. Aquit; To give a legal decision 3. Adjournment; To postpone proceeding in a law court. 4. Adjudicate; To give official judgement or decision upon somebody ( usually lawyer) 5. Advocate; A lawyer who speaks in favour of somebody in the court of law 6. Appeal; Taking the decision of a lower court to higher court. 7. Bail; To secure the release of somebody accused to higher court 8. Client; A person who gets help or advice from a lawyer. 9. Contempt of court; Breach or act of disloyalty or disrespect to a court. 10. Councel; Advice, (also a lawyer). 11. Court; A person who commit crime. 12. Damage; Money paid by person or company for cousing injury to another. 13. Defendant; A person against who a legal action is brought. 14. Equity; fairness, right, judgement 15. Legal action Assignment 1. List atleast ten words associated with law and order. 2. Use those words in sentence. Week 4 (Summary)

Unit topic; Reading to pick out topic sentence. Lesson topic; Summary passage – The unafraid lover unit 15 chapter 176. Summary is a brief form of writing a long passage, after removing irrelevant information from the main points using ones own words Useful tips in writing good summary i. Briefy (ii). Relevance (iii). Clarity (iv). Identify the topic sentence (v). Originality (vi). Write answers in complete sentence Topic sentence is a sentence that epresses the main idea of the paragraph in which it occurs.A topic sentence reveals the writer direction and tell the reader where the writers thoughts are leading to. Facts about un afraid lover - Nylepha is ready to leave the throne for the sake of the man she loves - People are usually jealous of the love that is unafraid. - Nylepha convinced her people about the choice of her husband - - Nylepha is loved by her people. Assignment 1. In two sentences one for each, summarise what nylepha would give to the man she loves. 2. In four sentesces one for each, summarise the attribute of Curtis that endeared him to Nylepha. Week 4 ( Continuous writing) Unit topic; Essay writing Lesson topic; Argumentative Essay (to prove a point) An argumentative essay is an essay in which the writer tries to persuade and convince the reader to accept and agree with his point of view. Topic in this form of essay demands that the writer should prove a point ,epress an opinion and support or oppose a given idea Example 1. Child training is the sole responsibility of a mother

2. Covid – 19 is a blessing in disguise 3. Modern technology has done harm than good 4. Female should be given leadership position in the society Guidelines for an argumentative essay 1. State the topic. 2. State your vocatives; This is the greeting to acknowledge the presence of the panel and the audience. e.g The moderator/ chairman, panel of judges, accurate time keeper, co – debaters, fellow student/audience, 3. Introduction; Define a content and take a stand 4. Body; make sure you are convinced about the side you are opposing or supporting. If you support the side you do not belief in, you will run out of points and ideas. 5. Conclusion; do not draw a general conclusion from one example or a few points you need a number of points to reach a convincing conclusion. 6. Do not be illogical in your argument. 7. be sure that your points can support the conclusion you want to reach. Example; Female leaders perform better in authority than their male counter parts; Points to support 1. Her role in the home as a home maker, manager of works, husband and kids will be extended to leadership. 2. More compassionate and firm as a result of the bond created during pregnancy, thus no woman leader will see the multitude of unemployed youths roaming the street without creating jobs. 3. Woman value more the sancity of human lives and thus, would have fued of farmers and cattle rearer before it generates to killings 4. Women leaers are more collaborative and trusted. Points use to oppose 1. Pregnancy and metanity leaves take women away from their role of leaders. 2. Expert advice husbands ( good or bad) may be extended to leadership position. 3. For surprise,disbelief,doubt e.g i. (Ada is a witch) Really? ii. ( Musa is a millionaire) You must be joking 3. The rise and fall tone; This tone is an enumerating items, Here, the pitch begins to rise on each of the items listed while the last item receive the falling tone, e.g one, two three and five. Week 9 Topic: Tenses Sequence of Tenses Tenses is any form of a verb used to show time of action or state expressed by a verb present, past or feature. They are four (4) tenses each in a present past and future respectively. Simple past Present Continuous Present perfect Present perfect continuous etc.

Sequence of tense is the agreement between the tenses of a verb in a sentence.It is the use of verb in expression and the harmony that exist between the verb used.It should be noted that the tense in the subordinated clause always follow the tense in the main clause though there are exception to this rule Rules guiding the sequence of tense 1. When the verb in the main clause is in the present tense,the verb in the subordinated clause will also be in the present tense. E.g He sees that he has made a mistake. The miner works so hard that he is tired. The old woman says that she is going to wash the dishes. Exception; A present tense in the main clause may be followed by any tense in the subordinate depending on the context or meaning conveyed. E.g I know that my father was annoyed. (present-past) You will soon receive the letter that I sent you. (future-past) He will live in the house that he will build. (future-future) 2. A past tense in the main clause is followed by a past tense in the subordinate. E.g The miner worked so hard that he was tired. I found out that she was out of town. John succeded because he (had) worked hard. Exception; A past tense in the main clause can be followed by a present tense in the subordinate clause if it is using a universal truth. E.gThe children were thought that Honesty is the best policy.

3. A future tense in the main clause is not followed by a future tense in the subordinate clause if there are conjunctions like ; When, until, before, after. E.g I will call you when dinner is ready. I will call you when dinner will be ready (incorrect) I shall wait until you return I shall wait until you will return (incorrect) 4. When a subordinate clause is introduced by ;then, or that; the verb in the main clause may be any tense to suit the context. E.g we eat that we may live. Joy liked literature more than she likes history. I know that my dad was annoyed. She is she is saying that she is right. 5. When phrases like ;if only, wish that, what if, it is time, it is high time; are used, a past tense in the main clause follows. E.g I wish I could eat another ice cream. it is high time you studied your books. if only I had I had enough money, I would have bought more food. 6. In direct speech, the verb in the present tense changes to past and past to past perfect tense E.g a. Dir;The train will be late. Ind; He said that the train will be late. b. Dir;I wish I know where it is said Tony Ind;Tony said he wish that he had know where it was. c. Dir;He said, ; I will be using my new car next week. Ind; He said that he will be using his car the following week. A. Tense in the present

i. Present; This is used to show present action.E.g He works ii. Present continuous;To show continuous action or an event in progress. E.g he is working iii. Present perfect; to show complete action at present E.g He has worked iv. Present perfect continuous; To show an event in the progress that begin in the past and still in progress in the present. However, some phrasal verbs are inseparable i.e the verb and the article can never be separated. Inseparable verbs are marked with an asterisk. Example; *. Rotten fish gives off a bad smell. A prefix is a group of letters added to a root word to form new words and new meaning or an affix attached to the beginning of a word, base ,or phrase and serving to produce a derivative word or an inflectional from. Example:- un, mis, il, in, im, dis, etc. A prefix added to a word usually does not change the word class (Part of Speech) of the word e.g material-immaterial(adjective) Behave-misbehave(verb) Personal-impersonal(adjective). Types of Prefix A Prefixes showing negation Dis Away, A part Disappear, disagree and disown Ill Not Illogical, illegal, illiterate Im Not Immodest, impossible, imperfect, immobile Un Not Unhappy, uncertainly, unfair

Anti Against Antisocial, antibiotics Mai Badly Malnourish, maltreat B prefix that show number Uni One Unilateral, unison Mono One Monopoly, monologue Bi Tow Bilateral, binomial Di Two Diphthong, dissect Tri Three Tricycle, tipped Penta Five Pentagon, pentagram, pentameter Poly Many Polysyllable, polygamy, polytechnique Homo Same Homophone, homogeneous Hetero Different Heterosexual, heterogeneous C. Prefixes showing attitude Pro For, infavour, support Pro-democrat, pro-militant, pro-war, pro-government Anti Against, opposed to Anti-social, anti-corruption, anti-clerical Co Together with Co-operate, co-worker, co-tenant, co- channel, co-editor, co-exist D. prefixes that are used to generate antonyms Un Unhealthy, untainted, unserious, unaided, uninformed, unfair, untie Mis Mislead, misquote, misspell, misunderstand Ill Illegal, illogical, illegitimate, illiterate In Indecision, inaudible, inaccessible, Im Improper, impossible, monorail, impolite, immature, immodest

Week ( structure) Unit Topic:- Figurative expression lesson topic figure of speech Figures of speech are special expression used to covey clear and brief impression than when expressed in ordinary works colourful, forceful, powerful and impressive. 1. SIMILE: It compares one thing with another using the words like or ‘as’ the two things in comparison are not similar but have similarity in the area being compared example : i. he is as dirty as a pig ii. she talks like a parrot 2. METAPHOR: a metaphor is a figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that is not literally true but helps to explain an idea or idea or make comparison . Example: i. Emeka is a tiger ii. She has a hear of stone 3. HYPERBOLE: it is an exasperation of fact for the sake of emphasis or to lighten effect. Example i. All the water in the ocean cannot wash the dert in his clothes. ii. I ate a mountain of food 4. PERSONIFICATION: It is giving of life and human attributes to inanimate objects or abstract things e.g i. The leaves are dancing to the tune of the wind ii. Evil walk in the shadow of night 5. OXYMORON: This is placing side by side two words that are contradict each other i. Etuk is a holy sinner

ii. It is an open secret that Odo is an armed robber iii. Ada is an honest liar 6. ANTITHESIS: It is pairing of two opposite ideas in a sentence in order to heighten a sharp contract between the ideas example: i. Man proposes, God disposes ii. United we stand, divided we fall iii. To err is human, to forgive is divine 7. SYNECDOCHE: This is when a part used to represent a whole things or a hole car be used to represent a part . Example: i. All fingers are not equal ii. The st best brains are in my class iii. Two heads are better than one 8. METONYMY: It is the act of referring to something by the name of something else that is closely connected or associated with it example: i. The crown has summon elders for a meeting ii. All the speakers must get the chair iii. Judgments will start from the pulpit 9. EVPHENISM: It talks of harsh and unpleasant things in a mild or pleasant way. Eg i. Mr. Sunday kicked the bucket last night ii. The man of the underworld sent him to the world beyond iii. He fought with his better half 10. ONOMATOPOEA: It is the ability of words to echo their meaning e.g (i) The bell of the chock jingles (ii) The student hissed 11. Rhetorical question:- It is when a question that does not need an answer is asked just for the purpose of persuading and appealing to the mind of the audience (i) E.g My people, will I like myself for you (ii) Can a kettle call a pot black? (iii) Who will say that his mother soup is bitter. 12. APOSTROPHE:- this is addressing an about person (abstract now) as if it were present, heving life and listening to the speaker. Example:- a. Oh! Death where is thy sting? b. O! WAEC, why are you treating me badly. c. Hear me, O earth, hear me, O hills 13. PARADOX:- it is a self contrary statement which seems to appear meaningless and unreasonable in the first thought but if closely examined, it contains an element of truth e.g i. The best way to learn a subjects is to teach it.

ii. Cowards dies many times before their death iii. For whosever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel shall save it. Grammatical Function; This is used to differentiate between specific type, declarative, interrogative, polar questions e.t.c e.g When a speaker wants to give information, a falling tune is used. 2. WH-questions e.g when are you coming? ii. Why are you late to school?

iii. Where does he lives? 2. The Rising tone; This is used to indicate a rise in the pitch of a speaker voice begins from the first stressed syllable until it reaches the highest peak. If there are unstressed syllable at the end of the sentences, the syllables are said with the rising tone to maintain the rise in pitch. Uses of the rising tone 1.Questions requiring Yes or No answer e.g i. Did she pass ii. Are you coming iii. Will you go to lagos? 2. Questions that shows warm personal interest e.g i. For greetings e.g i.Good morning sir ii. Complement of the season 5. To indicate uncertainty e.g

i. Will John come to school tomorrow? I think so ii. They may call of strike tomorrow 6. For incomplete statement; e.g i. While they were playing ( Dayo was reading) 7. For surprise,disbelief,doubt e.g i. (Ada is a witch) Really? ii. ( Musa is a millionaire) You must be joking 3. The rise and fall tone; This tone is an enumerating items, Here, the pitch begins to rise on each of the items listed while the last item receive the falling tone, e.g one, two three and five. Week 9 Topic: Tenses Sequence of Tenses Tenses is any form of a verb used to show time of action or state expressed by a verb present, past or feature. They are four (4) tenses each in a present past and future respectively. Simple past Present Continuous Present perfect Present perfect continuous etc.

Sequence of tense is the agreement between the tenses of a verb in a sentence.It is the use of verb in expression and the harmony that exist between the verb used.It should be noted that the tense in the subordinated clause always follow the tense in the main clause though there are exception to this rule Rules guiding the sequence of tense 1. When the verb in the main clause is in the present tense,the verb in the subordinated clause will also be in the present tense. E.g He sees that he has made a mistake. The miner works so hard that he is tired. The old woman says that she is going to wash the dishes. Exception; A present tense in the main clause may be followed by any tense in the subordinate depending on the context or meaning conveyed. E.g I know that my father was annoyed. (present-past) You will soon receive the letter that I sent you. (future-past) He will live in the house that he will build. (future-future) 2. A past tense in the main clause is followed by a past tense in the subordinate. E.g The miner worked so hard that he was tired. I found out that she was out of town. John succeded because he (had) worked hard. Exception; A past tense in the main clause can be followed by a present tense in the subordinate clause if it is using a universal truth. E.gThe children were thought that Honesty is the best policy.

3. A future tense in the main clause is not followed by a future tense in the subordinate clause if there are conjunctions like ; When, until, before, after. E.g I will call you when dinner is ready. I will call you when dinner will be ready (incorrect) I shall wait until you return I shall wait until you will return (incorrect) 4. When a subordinate clause is introduced by ;then, or that; the verb in the main clause may be any tense to suit the context. E.g we eat that we may live. Joy liked literature more than she likes history. I know that my dad was annoyed. She is she is saying that she is right. 5. When phrases like ;if only, wish that, what if, it is time, it is high time; are used, a past tense in the main clause follows. E.g I wish I could eat another ice cream. it is high time you studied your books. if only I had I had enough money, I would have bought more food. 6. In direct speech, the verb in the present tense changes to past and past to past perfect tense E.g a. Dir;The train will be late. Ind; He said that the train will be late. b. Dir;I wish I know where it is said Tony Ind;Tony said he wish that he had know where it was. c. Dir;He said, ; I will be using my new car next week. Ind; He said that he will be using his car the following week. A. Tense in the present

i. Present; This is used to show present action.E.g He works ii. Present continuous;To show continuous action or an event in progress. E.g he is working iii. Present perfect; to show complete action at present E.g He has worked iv. Present perfect continuous; To show an event in the progress that begin in the past and still in progress in the present. A prefix is a group of letters added to a root word to form new words and new meaning or an affix attached to the beginning of a word, base ,or phrase and serving to produce a derivative word or an inflectional from. Example:- un, mis, il, in, im, dis, etc. A prefix added to a word usually does not change the word class (Part of Speech) of the word e.g material-immaterial(adjective) Behave-misbehave(verb) Personal-impersonal(adjective). Week ( structure) Unit Topic:- Figurative expression lesson topic figure of speech Figures of speech are special expression used to covey clear and brief impression than when expressed in ordinary works colourful, forceful, powerful and impressive. 1. SIMILE: It compares one thing with another using the words like or ‘as’ the two things in comparison are not similar but have similarity in the area being compared example : i. he is as dirty as a pig ii. she talks like a parrot 2. METAPHOR: a metaphor is a figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that is not literally true but helps to explain an idea or idea or make comparison . Example: i. Emeka is a tiger ii. She has a hear of stone 3. HYPERBOLE: it is an exasperation of fact for the sake of emphasis or to lighten effect. Example i. All the water in the ocean cannot wash the dert in his clothes. ii. I ate a mountain of food 4. PERSONIFICATION: It is giving of life and human attributes to inanimate objects or abstract things e.g i. The leaves are dancing to the tune of the wind ii. Evil walk in the shadow of night 5. OXYMORON: This is placing side by side two words that are contradict each other i. Etuk is a holy sinner

ii. It is an open secret that Odo is an armed robber iii. Ada is an honest liar 6. ANTITHESIS: It is pairing of two opposite ideas in a sentence in order to heighten a sharp contract between the ideas example: i. Man proposes, God disposes ii. United we stand, divided we fall iii. To err is human, to forgive is divine 7. SYNECDOCHE: This is when a part used to represent a whole things or a hole car be used to represent a part . Example: i. All fingers are not equal ii. The st best brains are in my class iii. Two heads are better than one 8. METONYMY: It is the act of referring to something by the name of something else that is closely connected or associated with it example: i. The crown has summon elders for a meeting ii. All the speakers must get the chair iii. Judgments will start from the pulpit 9. EVPHENISM: It talks of harsh and unpleasant things in a mild or pleasant way. Eg i. Mr. Sunday kicked the bucket last night ii. The man of the underworld sent him to the world beyond iii. He fought with his better half 10. ONOMATOPOEA: It is the ability of words to echo their meaning e.g (i) The bell of the chock jingles (ii) The student hissed 11. Rhetorical question:- It is when a question that does not need an answer is asked just for the purpose of persuading and appealing to the mind of the audience (i) E.g My people, will I like myself for you (ii) Can a kettle call a pot black? (iii) Who will say that his mother soup is bitter. 12. APOSTROPHE:- this is addressing an about person (abstract now) as if it were present, heving life and listening to the speaker. Example:- a. Oh! Death where is thy sting? b. O! WAEC, why are you treating me badly. c. Hear me, O earth, hear me, O hills 13. PARADOX:- it is a self contrary statement which seems to appear meaningless and unreasonable in the first thought but if closely examined, it contains an element of truth e.g i. The best way to learn a subjects is to teach it.

ii. Cowards dies many times before their death iii. For whosever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel shall save it. Intonation is the variation of pitch of voice used in making Intelligible communication. It gives special meaning and utterances. Functions; Intonation is used in two major ways;

1. Grammatical Function; This is used to differentiate between specific type, declarative, interrogative, polar questions e.t.c e.g When a speaker wants to give information, a falling tune is used. 2. Attitudinal Function; This attitude can be that of surprise, doubt, sarcasm, warm interest, indifference, disbelief, uncertainty e.t.c. Types of intonation i. Falling tone (ii) Rising tone (iii) Fall-Rise tone. 1. The falling tone; This is used to indicate the fall in pitch of a speaker voice, in writing, we use the downward arrow to show a sentence uttered with the falling tone Uses of the falling tone i. The falling tone is use to make statement e.g We shall all pass English ii. The teacher is coming iii. Abuja is the capital of Nigeria 2. The falling tone is use to command e.g i. Shut the door ii. Keep the book on my table iii.Dont disobey your parents 3. The falling tone is used to make exclamation e.g i. What a pleasant surprise ii. How lovely she works iii. Wow, that’s great indeed 4. WH-questions e.g when are you coming? ii. Why are you late to school?

iii. Where does he lives? 2. The Rising tone; This is used to indicate a rise in the pitch of a speaker voice begins from the first stressed syllable until it reaches the highest peak. If there are unstressed syllable at the end of the sentences, the syllables are said with the rising tone to maintain the rise in pitch. Uses of the rising tone 1.Questions requiring Yes or No answer e.g i. Did she pass ii. Are you coming iii. Will you go to lagos? 2. Questions that shows warm personal interest e.g i. Have you taken anything since you came? ii. Will you still leave today? 3.For simple polite request; e.g i. Please come in (warm reception) ii. May I borrow your book please 4. For greetings e.g i.Good morning sir ii. Complement of the season 5. To indicate uncertainty e.g

i. Will John come to school tomorrow? I think so ii. They may call of strike tomorrow 6. For incomplete statement; e.g i. While they were playing ( Dayo was reading) 7. For surprise,disbelief,doubt e.g i. (Ada is a witch) Really? ii. ( Musa is a millionaire) You must be joking 3. The rise and fall tone; This tone is an enumerating items, Here, the pitch begins to rise on each of the items listed while the last item receive the falling tone, e.g one, two three and five. Week 9 Topic: Tenses Sequence of Tenses Tenses is any form of a verb used to show time of action or state expressed by a verb present, past or feature. They are four (4) tenses each in a present past and future respectively. Simple past Present Continuous Present perfect Present perfect continuous etc.

Sequence of tense is the agreement between the tenses of a verb in a sentence.It is the use of verb in expression and the harmony that exist between the verb used.It should be noted that the tense in the subordinated clause always follow the tense in the main clause though there are exception to this rule Rules guiding the sequence of tense 1. When the verb in the main clause is in the present tense,the verb in the subordinated clause will also be in the present tense. E.g He sees that he has made a mistake. The miner works so hard that he is tired. The old woman says that she is going to wash the dishes. Exception; A present tense in the main clause may be followed by any tense in the subordinate depending on the context or meaning conveyed. E.g I know that my father was annoyed. (present-past) You will soon receive the letter that I sent you. (future-past) He will live in the house that he will build. (future-future) 2. A past tense in the main clause is followed by a past tense in the subordinate. E.g The miner worked so hard that he was tired. I found out that she was out of town. John succeded because he (had) worked hard. Exception; A past tense in the main clause can be followed by a present tense in the subordinate clause if it is using a universal truth. E.gThe children were thought that Honesty is the best policy.

3. A future tense in the main clause is not followed by a future tense in the subordinate clause if there are conjunctions like ; When, until, before, after. E.g I will call you when dinner is ready. I will call you when dinner will be ready (incorrect) I shall wait until you return I shall wait until you will return (incorrect) 4. When a subordinate clause is introduced by ;then, or that; the verb in the main clause may be any tense to suit the context. E.g we eat that we may live. Joy liked literature more than she likes history. I know that my dad was annoyed. She is she is saying that she is right. 5. When phrases like ;if only, wish that, what if, it is time, it is high time; are used, a past tense in the main clause follows. E.g I wish I could eat another ice cream. it is high time you studied your books. if only I had I had enough money, I would have bought more food. 6. In direct speech, the verb in the present tense changes to past and past to past perfect tense E.g a. Dir;The train will be late. Ind; He said that the train will be late. b. Dir;I wish I know where it is said Tony Ind;Tony said he wish that he had know where it was. c. Dir;He said, ; I will be using my new car next week. Ind; He said that he will be using his car the following week. A. Tense in the present

i. Present; This is used to show present action.E.g He works ii. Present continuous;To show continuous action or an event in progress. E.g he is working iii. Present perfect; to show complete action at present E.g He has worked iv. Present perfect continuous; To show an event in the progress that begin in the past and still in progress in the present. E.g He has been working B . Tense in the past i. Past; To report a past event. It is commonly used in narration E.g He worked ii. Past continuous; To show a past event in progress E.g He was working (when I entered the room) iv. Past perfect continuous; show an event in progress before a past event. E.g He had been working (since morning) c. Tense in the future i. Future tense; To refer to events and circumstances in the future. E.g He shall work. ii. Future continuous; To refer to action that is on going or continuous. E.gHe shall be working. A prefix is a group of letters added to a root word to form new words and new meaning or an affix attached to the beginning of a word, base ,or phrase and serving to produce a derivative word or an inflectional from. Example:- un, mis, il, in, im, dis, etc. A prefix added to a word usually does not change the word class (Part of Speech) of the word e.g material-immaterial(adjective) Behave-misbehave(verb) Personal-impersonal(adjective). Week ( structure) Unit Topic:- Figurative expression lesson topic figure of speech Figures of speech are special expression used to covey clear and brief impression than when expressed in ordinary works colourful, forceful, powerful and impressive. 1. SIMILE: It compares one thing with another using the words like or ‘as’ the two things in comparison are not similar but have similarity in the area being compared example : i. he is as dirty as a pig ii. she talks like a parrot 2. METAPHOR: a metaphor is a figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that is not literally true but helps to explain an idea or idea or make comparison . Example: i. Emeka is a tiger ii. She has a hear of stone 3. HYPERBOLE: it is an exasperation of fact for the sake of emphasis or to lighten effect. Example i. All the water in the ocean cannot wash the dert in his clothes. ii. I ate a mountain of food 4. PERSONIFICATION: It is giving of life and human attributes to inanimate objects or abstract things e.g i. The leaves are dancing to the tune of the wind ii. Evil walk in the shadow of night 5. OXYMORON: This is placing side by side two words that are contradict each other i. Etuk is a holy sinner

ii. It is an open secret that Odo is an armed robber iii. Ada is an honest liar 6. ANTITHESIS: It is pairing of two opposite ideas in a sentence in order to heighten a sharp contract between the ideas example: i. Man proposes, God disposes ii. United we stand, divided we fall iii. To err is human, to forgive is divine 7. SYNECDOCHE: This is when a part used to represent a whole things or a hole car be used to represent a part . Example: i. All fingers are not equal ii. The st best brains are in my class iii. Two heads are better than one 8. METONYMY: It is the act of referring to something by the name of something else that is closely connected or associated with it example: i. The crown has summon elders for a meeting ii. All the speakers must get the chair iii. Judgments will start from the pulpit 9. EVPHENISM: It talks of harsh and unpleasant things in a mild or pleasant way. Eg i. Mr. Sunday kicked the bucket last night ii. The man of the underworld sent him to the world beyond iii. He fought with his better half 10. ONOMATOPOEA: It is the ability of words to echo their meaning e.g (i) The bell of the chock jingles (ii) The student hissed 11. Rhetorical question:- It is when a question that does not need an answer is asked just for the purpose of persuading and appealing to the mind of the audience (i) E.g My people, will I like myself for you (ii) Can a kettle call a pot black? (iii) Who will say that his mother soup is bitter. 12. APOSTROPHE:- this is addressing an about person (abstract now) as if it were present, heving life and listening to the speaker. Example:- a. Oh! Death where is thy sting? b. O! WAEC, why are you treating me badly. c. Hear me, O earth, hear me, O hills 13. PARADOX:- it is a self contrary statement which seems to appear meaningless and unreasonable in the first thought but if closely examined, it contains an element of truth e.g i. The best way to learn a subjects is to teach it.

ii. Cowards dies many times before their death iii. For whosever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel shall save it. An adverb is a word that modifies or qualifies an adjectives, verb or other adverb, Or a group of words expressing a relationship of place, time, circumstances, manner, causes degree e.t.c. E.g quickly, beautiful, foolishly, wisely, well, enough, much, soon, quiet. e.t.c. Adverb have three degrees of comparism which are the positive, comparative and suparative. Adverb which ends in ;ly, have their comparative and suparative formed by adding more and most. Example; (A) POSITIVE COMPARATIVE SUPARATIVE Quickly More quickly Most quickluy

Dangerously More dangerously Most dangerously Slowly More slowly Most slowly Fortunately More fortunately Most fortunately Carefully More carefully Most carefully Excitedly More excitedly Most excitedly Foolishly More foolishly Most foolishly Rampanthy More rampanthy Most rampanthy Beautifully More beautifully Most beautifully Sensibly More sensibly Most sensibly Rashly More rashly Most rashly B. Week 7 ( Continuous writing) Unit topic; Letter writing Lesson topic; Semi-formal letters Semi-formal letters are letters we write to people who are not total strangers to us but are not close enough to deserve a personal letter, the people may be older or younger than we are. The are people like our teachers, parents, friends, distant uncles and aunts, elderly

Features of semi-formal letters 1. Signature is not necessary, but if you wish to, you can sign. Example; Yours sincerely James Okeke Week 8 ( Speech) Unit Topic; Intonation Pattern. Lesson Topic; Rising and Falling tunes. Intonation is the variation of pitch of voice used in making Intelligible communication. It gives special meaning and utterances. Functions; Intonation is used in two major ways;

1. Grammatical Function; This is used to differentiate between specific type, declarative, interrogative, polar questions e.t.c e.g When a speaker wants to give information, a falling tune is used. 2. Attitudinal Function; This attitude can be that of surprise, doubt, sarcasm, warm interest, indifference, disbelief, uncertainty e.t.c. Types of intonation i. Falling tone (ii) Rising tone (iii) Fall-Rise tone. 1. The falling tone; This is used to indicate the fall in pitch of a speaker voice, in writing, we use the downward arrow to show a sentence uttered with the falling tone Uses of the falling tone i. The falling tone is use to make statement e.g We shall all pass English ii. The teacher is coming iii. Abuja is the capital of Nigeria 2. The falling tone is use to command e.g i. Shut the door ii. Keep the book on my table iii.Dont disobey your parents 3. The falling tone is used to make exclamation e.g i. What a pleasant surprise ii. How lovely she works iii. Wow, that’s great indeed 4. WH-questions e.g when are you coming? ii. Why are you late to school?

iii. Where does he lives? 2. The Rising tone; This is used to indicate a rise in the pitch of a speaker voice begins from the first stressed syllable until it reaches the highest peak. If there are unstressed syllable at the end of the sentences, the syllables are said with the rising tone to maintain the rise in pitch. Uses of the rising tone 1.Questions requiring Yes or No answer e.g i. Did she pass ii. Are you coming iii. Will you go to lagos? 2. Questions that shows warm personal interest e.g i. Have you taken anything since you came? ii. Will you still leave today? 3.For simple polite request; e.g i. Please come in (warm reception) ii. May I borrow your book please 4. For greetings e.g i.Good morning sir ii. Complement of the season 5. To indicate uncertainty e.g

i. Will John come to school tomorrow? I think so ii. They may call of strike tomorrow 6. For incomplete statement; e.g i. While they were playing ( Dayo was reading) 7. For surprise,disbelief,doubt e.g i. (Ada is a witch) Really? ii. ( Musa is a millionaire) You must be joking 3. The rise and fall tone; This tone is an enumerating items, Here, the pitch begins to rise on each of the items listed while the last item receive the falling tone, e.g one, two three and five. Go to the hall with a pen, a pencil, a ruler, and eraser. Week 9 Topic: Tenses Sequence of Tenses Tenses is any form of a verb used to show time of action or state expressed by a verb present, past or feature. They are four (4) tenses each in a present past and future respectively. Simple past Present Continuous Present perfect Present perfect continuous etc.

Sequence of tense is the agreement between the tenses of a verb in a sentence.It is the use of verb in expression and the harmony that exist between the verb used.It should be noted that the tense in the subordinated clause always follow the tense in the main clause though there are exception to this rule Rules guiding the sequence of tense 1. When the verb in the main clause is in the present tense,the verb in the subordinated clause will also be in the present tense. E.g He sees that he has made a mistake. The miner works so hard that he is tired. The old woman says that she is going to wash the dishes. Exception; A present tense in the main clause may be followed by any tense in the subordinate depending on the context or meaning conveyed. E.g I know that my father was annoyed. (present-past) You will soon receive the letter that I sent you. (future-past) He will live in the house that he will build. (future-future) 2. A past tense in the main clause is followed by a past tense in the subordinate. E.g The miner worked so hard that he was tired. I found out that she was out of town. John succeded because he (had) worked hard. Exception; A past tense in the main clause can be followed by a present tense in the subordinate clause if it is using a universal truth. E.gThe children were thought that Honesty is the best policy.

3. A future tense in the main clause is not followed by a future tense in the subordinate clause if there are conjunctions like ; When, until, before, after. E.g I will call you when dinner is ready. I will call you when dinner will be ready (incorrect) I shall wait until you return I shall wait until you will return (incorrect) 4. When a subordinate clause is introduced by ;then, or that; the verb in the main clause may be any tense to suit the context. E.g we eat that we may live. Joy liked literature more than she likes history. I know that my dad was annoyed. She is she is saying that she is right. 5. When phrases like ;if only, wish that, what if, it is time, it is high time; are used, a past tense in the main clause follows. E.g I wish I could eat another ice cream. it is high time you studied your books. if only I had I had enough money, I would have bought more food. 6. In direct speech, the verb in the present tense changes to past and past to past perfect tense E.g a. Dir;The train will be late. Ind; He said that the train will be late. b. Dir;I wish I know where it is said Tony Ind;Tony said he wish that he had know where it was. c. Dir;He said, ; I will be using my new car next week. Ind; He said that he will be using his car the following week. A. Tense in the present

i. Present; This is used to show present action.E.g He works ii. Present continuous;To show continuous action or an event in progress. E.g he is working iii. Present perfect; to show complete action at present E.g He has worked iv. Present perfect continuous; To show an event in the progress that begin in the past and still in progress in the present. E.g He has been working B . Tense in the past i. Past; To report a past event. It is commonly used in narration E.g He worked ii. Past continuous; To show a past event in progress E.g He was working (when I entered the room) iv. Past perfect continuous; show an event in progress before a past event. E.g He had been working (since morning) c. Tense in the future i. Future tense; To refer to events and circumstances in the future. E.g He shall work. ii. Future continuous; To refer to action that is on going or continuous. E.gHe shall be working. Week 9 (continuous writing) Unit Topic Letter Lesson Topic Formal Letter A formal letter is a letter written to someone or a group of people in official position . it is also called an official letter . it includes letters to the press news paper or magazine, companies, offices, schools letter, realest for casual leave by staff in offices, an application for a job e.t.c. Types of formal letter 1. Letter of enquiry 2. Order letter 3. Letter of complaint 4. Promotion letter 5. Sales letters 6. Recovery letter Features of a formal letter 1. Writer’s address idate: This should be written at the top of a letter on the right hand corner. This includes the name of your school post office, Number, state, date e.t.c write the date in full and put a dot after each abbreviation Government Secondary School, P.M.B. 227 Kubwa, Abuja. 28 th October,2024. 2. The recipient’s address. This is written at the left hand side below the writer’s address . Example The commissioner of education, Abia State. e.g The Registrar,

University of Abuja, Abuja. 3. Salutation :- This is followed by a comma e.g Dear Sir, 4. Title:- a formal letter should have a title underlined if written in small letter or with initial of each headword in capital letter) But not underlined if written in capital letters e.g APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF A SECRETARY 5. Introduction:- This gives a brief account of what the letter talks about 6. The body of the letter:- write clear and simple English. Mind your tenses pay attention to spellings and punctuation 7. Conclusion:- This draws together the ideas and its relationship with the major points. 8. Subscription :- This comes at the end of the letter followed by a comma. Only the letter (in yours) is written in capital letter. eg Yours Faithfully 9. Signature and name :- name should be written below the signature Sign Ayo Obi Musa Assignment Write a letter to the director of the environmental protection Agency in your country commplaning about environmental pollution of your area, requestiong that urgent action be taken to improve the situation WAEC 2002 Week 10 (Structure) Unit topic; Phrasal verb Lesson topic; Phrasal verbs with more than one particles. A phrasal verb is a group of two or three words that begins a verb and is followed by a particle. The particle can be an adverb or preposition. example; Grew up, turn out

Work after, apply for ran in to, think about. Phrasal verb can be in the following format 1. Verbs + Adverb e.g put heavily walk quietly speak kindly 2. Verbs + Preposition e.g look on come across go over put up come round come off come after see to 3. Three words phrasal verb e.g look forward to come back to come away with catch up with stick out to tune in to look down on give in to

put up with go in for Features of phrasal verbs 1. It consist of two or three words 2. The first word is a verb 3. The second word is either an adverb or preposition. Phrasal verbs can have both literal/denotative and idiomatic/connotative meaning Phrasal verbs Literal meaning Idiomatic meaning Sentence Break down To stop functioning To start crying She break down when she see her score in mathematics Speak out Talk audibly To stop complaint The staff decided to speak against suspension of their president Take off To remove To go in to the air The plain did not take off until midnight Turn down To reduce volume To reject His offer was turned down Call out Mention To announce The teacher call out their names Look up To look towards the sky/ceiling To check information We need to look up for the meaning of the words in dictionary Put away To remove from sight To jail or put something in an enclosure The animal was finally put away Separable phrasal verbs Some phrasal verbs are separable by inserting an object in between them e.g 1. The widow brought up her son well The widow brought her son up well. 2. He picked up the baby He picked the baby up

However, some phrasal verbs are inseparable i.e the verb and the article can never be separated. Inseparable verbs are marked with an asterisk. Example; *. Rotten fish gives off a bad smell. Rotten fish gives a bad smell off. Some phrasal verb and their meaning 1. Come about – happened call at – to visit 2. Come across – find call for – to require 3. Come by – obtain call off – to cancel 4. Come in – to be received call out – to announce 5. Come forward – to be identify 6. Come around – regain consciousness 7. Come through – to survive 8. Come to – to add up 9. Check out – leave 10. Check in – arrive 11. Hear out – listen to the end 12. Long for – to desire something clearly 13. Get over – recover from a shock or surprise Give away – to reveal a secret Give in – surrender Give up – to stop Cut off – disconnect Cut up – slice Come up-with – to reveal or disclose

Dress down – to scold severely Set in – to commence. Assignment Exercise 2 pg 169 of of their text book, new concept English. 1. Speech Oral Argument / Debate An oral argument or debate is a formal discussion where speakers present opposing views on a topic. Features of a Debate  Two sides: For (Proposition) and Against (Opposition)  Each side presents arguments to support their view  Speakers take turns to speak  There may be a moderator or chairperson Skills Needed for Oral Argument  Clear and confident speech  Logical reasoning  Use of facts and examples  Good listening skills  Respect for opposing views Structure of an Oral Argument 1. Introduction – greet audience and state your position 2. Body – present strong points with examples 3. Rebuttal – respond to opposing arguments 4. Conclusion – restate position clearly Importance of Debate  Improves speaking skills  Develops critical thinking  Builds confidence 2. Structure Suffixes A suffix is a group of letters added to the end of a word to change its meaning or form. Common Suffixes and Their Functions

 -er / -or – a person who does something teacher, actor  -ness – forms nouns showing a state or quality kindness, darkness  -ment – forms nouns from verbs development, punishment  -tion / -sion – forms nouns education, decision  -ful – full of careful, helpful  -less – without fearless, careless  -ly – forms adverbs quickly, slowly Examples in Sentences  The judgement was fair.  Honesty leads to success . 3. Vocabulary Development Words Associated with Law and Order Law and order refers to rules that govern society and the system that enforces them. Conflict resolution The students listen as the teacher reads, the listen in comprehension Appendix 3 page 259 on the Adventures of Solomon Assignment Provide the answers to the text on page 228. Week ( structure) Unit Topic:- Figurative expression lesson topic figure of speech Figures of speech are special expression used to covey clear and brief impression than when expressed in ordinary works colourful, forceful, powerful and impressive. 1. SIMILE: It compares one thing with another using the words like or ‘as’ the two things in comparison are not similar but have similarity in the area being compared example : i. he is as dirty as a pig ii. she talks like a parrot 2. METAPHOR: a metaphor is a figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that is not literally true but helps to explain an idea or idea or make comparison . Example: i. Emeka is a tiger ii. She has a hear of stone 3. HYPERBOLE: it is an exasperation of fact for the sake of emphasis or to lighten effect. Example i. All the water in the ocean cannot wash the dert in his clothes. ii. I ate a mountain of food

4. PERSONIFICATION: It is giving of life and human attributes to inanimate objects or abstract things e.g i. The leaves are dancing to the tune of the wind ii. Evil walk in the shadow of night 5. OXYMORON: This is placing side by side two words that are contradict each other i. Etuk is a holy sinner ii. It is an open secret that Odo is an armed robber iii. Ada is an honest liar 6. ANTITHESIS: It is pairing of two opposite ideas in a sentence in order to heighten a sharp contract between the ideas example: i. Man proposes, God disposes ii. United we stand, divided we fall iii. To err is human, to forgive is divine 7. SYNECDOCHE: This is when a part used to represent a whole things or a hole car be used to represent a part . Example: i. All fingers are not equal ii. The st best brains are in my class iii. Two heads are better than one 8. METONYMY: It is the act of referring to something by the name of something else that is closely connected or associated with it example: i. The crown has summon elders for a meeting ii. All the speakers must get the chair iii. Judgments will start from the pulpit 9. EVPHENISM: It talks of harsh and unpleasant things in a mild or pleasant way. Eg i. Mr. Sunday kicked the bucket last night ii. The man of the underworld sent him to the world beyond iii. He fought with his better half 10. ONOMATOPOEA: It is the ability of words to echo their meaning e.g (i) The bell of the chock jingles (ii) The student hissed 11. Rhetorical question:- It is when a question that does not need an answer is asked just for the purpose of persuading and appealing to the mind of the audience (i) E.g My people, will I like myself for you (ii) Can a kettle call a pot black? (iii) Who will say that his mother soup is bitter. 12. APOSTROPHE:- this is addressing an about person (abstract now) as if it were present, heving life and listening to the speaker. Example:-

a. Oh! Death where is thy sting? b. O! WAEC, why are you treating me badly. c. Hear me, O earth, hear me, O hills 13. PARADOX:- it is a self contrary statement which seems to appear meaningless and unreasonable in the first thought but if closely examined, it contains an element of truth e.g i. The best way to learn a subjects is to teach it. ii. Cowards dies many times before their death iii. For whosever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel shall save it. Chimere travelled to umueze in search of root I father 2. She has not being to Umueze before 3. She did not know the Umueze that she was going to 4. The driver tried to help her by stopping her at a convenient place 5. Chemere stopped at church in order to bring her quest Assignment Provide the answers to all the comprehension questions (a – g) Week 3 (continuous writing) Unit Topic :-Speeches Unit Title:- writing speeches (An address given on a prize given day) A speech is a written material meant to be read to a group of listeners. Speeches are meavit to entain, educate and inform people

Features of a speech It is also meant to motivate people to action 1. The title there should be a title for the speech you are to deliver. The title should indicate the mark of identification such as the - The purpose - Name and the title of speaker - Occasion - Place - Date and time An Address give on a prize giving day, by Joy Okoli the Head girl of government secondary school, Kubwa, the school Assembly Hall this day with September, 2017. 2. The introduction: this must be interesting and captivating so as to elicit the interest of the listeners. It must start within salutation e.g Good morning the chairman, the principal, the school management, the P.T.A, ladies and gentlemen . I feel highly honoured to stand here today to deliver my speech on ............... 3. The body:- this is the stage that contains the actual message. Start by giving. Your main points and then support each point with relevant details, comparisons and contrasts e.t.c explain who, where, why, how. The ideas must be stated in good clear sentences 4. The conclusion:- here you summarize your main points . it is important to end in a memorable way by: - Making a forceful and shocking statement - urging your audience to follow a certain line of action or thought e.t.c - Ending in an interesting and captivating manner. Guidelines Required for speech written 1. A speech is meant to be delivered to an audience. Hence the use of present tense is require 2. A speech should be in four sentence viz, heading introduction, body and conclusion 3. Slangs and humour should be avoided since the speech is meant to be delivered to an audience superior to the writer. The use of humour is appropriate only in an informal situation like party. 4. No use of name (s) at the end of the speech since it would have been introduction at the heading. Assignment

Prepare a speech to be delivered on the prize and award giving day of the final year students of the school.

Week 3 (Speech) Unit Topic-;Listening Comprehension (oral) Lesson Topic-; Listening to summarize speeches. Listening is the ability to pay attention to and effectively interpret what other people are saying. While A speech is written material meant to be read to a group of listeners importance of developing listening skill 1. Listening encourage empathy 2. Reduces misunderstanding 3. Builds relationship 4. Improves thought process 5. Conflict resolution The students listen as the teacher reads, the listen in comprehension Appendix 3 page 259 on the Adventures of Solomon Assignment Provide the answers to the text on page 228. Week ( structure) Unit Topic:- Figurative expression lesson topic figure of speech Figures of speech are special expression used to covey clear and brief impression than when expressed in ordinary works colourful, forceful, powerful and impressive. 1. SIMILE: It compares one thing with another using the words like or ‘as’ the two things in comparison are not similar but have similarity in the area being compared example : i. he is as dirty as a pig ii. she talks like a parrot 2. METAPHOR: a metaphor is a figure of speech that describes an object or action in a way that is not literally true but helps to explain an idea or idea or make comparison . Example: i. Emeka is a tiger ii. She has a hear of stone 3. HYPERBOLE: it is an exasperation of fact for the sake of emphasis or to lighten effect. Example i. All the water in the ocean cannot wash the dert in his clothes. ii. I ate a mountain of food

4. PERSONIFICATION: It is giving of life and human attributes to inanimate objects or abstract things e.g i. The leaves are dancing to the tune of the wind ii. Evil walk in the shadow of night 5. OXYMORON: This is placing side by side two words that are contradict each other i. Etuk is a holy sinner ii. It is an open secret that Odo is an armed robber iii. Ada is an honest liar 6. ANTITHESIS: It is pairing of two opposite ideas in a sentence in order to heighten a sharp contract between the ideas example: i. Man proposes, God disposes ii. United we stand, divided we fall iii. To err is human, to forgive is divine 7. SYNECDOCHE: This is when a part used to represent a whole things or a hole car be used to represent a part . Example: i. All fingers are not equal ii. The st best brains are in my class iii. Two heads are better than one 8. METONYMY: It is the act of referring to something by the name of something else that is closely connected or associated with it example: i. The crown has summon elders for a meeting ii. All the speakers must get the chair iii. Judgments will start from the pulpit 9. EVPHENISM: It talks of harsh and unpleasant things in a mild or pleasant way. Eg i. Mr. Sunday kicked the bucket last night ii. The man of the underworld sent him to the world beyond iii. He fought with his better half 10. ONOMATOPOEA: It is the ability of words to echo their meaning e.g (i) The bell of the chock jingles (ii) The student hissed 11. Rhetorical question:- It is when a question that does not need an answer is asked just for the purpose of persuading and appealing to the mind of the audience (i) E.g My people, will I like myself for you (ii) Can a kettle call a pot black? (iii) Who will say that his mother soup is bitter. 12. APOSTROPHE:- this is addressing an about person (abstract now) as if it were present, heving life and listening to the speaker. Example:-

a. Oh! Death where is thy sting? b. O! WAEC, why are you treating me badly. c. Hear me, O earth, hear me, O hills 13. PARADOX:- it is a self contrary statement which seems to appear meaningless and unreasonable in the first thought but if closely examined, it contains an element of truth e.g i. The best way to learn a subjects is to teach it. ii. Cowards dies many times before their death iii. For whosever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel shall save it. Assignment Make sentence to show the following figure of speech (2 sentence for each) (1) (i) Simile (ii) metaphor (iii) personification (iv) hyperbole (v) Oxymoron Week 3 ( Comprehension) Unit Topic :- Reading for structural pattern Lesion Topic:- “Chimere in search of her roofs” Page 205 – 206 unit 17 Structural pattern is the overall form organization of sentences something in this case we look at the structure of sentence in a passage and identify those that are simple sentences or compound sentences e.t.c e.g the first sentence in the 1 st paragraph is a complex sentence because it as two subordinate clause and one simple sentence Second sentence is a compound sentence, the 3 rd is a complex sentence e.t.c The main points include 1. Chimere travelled to umueze in search of root I father 2. She has not being to Umueze before 3. She did not know the Umueze that she was going to 4. The driver tried to help her by stopping her at a convenient place 5. Chemere stopped at church in order to bring her quest Assignment Provide the answers to all the comprehension questions (a – g) Week 3 (continuous writing) Unit Topic :-Speeches Unit Title:- writing speeches (An address given on a prize given day) A speech is a written material meant to be read to a group of listeners. Speeches are meavit to entain, educate and inform people

Features of a speech It is also meant to motivate people to action 1. The title there should be a title for the speech you are to deliver. The title should indicate the mark of identification such as the - The purpose - Name and the title of speaker - Occasion - Place - Date and time An Address give on a prize giving day, by Joy Okoli the Head girl of government secondary school, Kubwa, the school Assembly Hall this day with September, 2017. 2. The introduction: this must be interesting and captivating so as to elicit the interest of the listeners. It must start within salutation e.g Good morning the chairman, the principal, the school management, the P.T.A, ladies and gentlemen . I feel highly honoured to stand here today to deliver my speech on ............... 3. The body:- this is the stage that contains the actual message. Start by giving. Your main points and then support each point with relevant details, comparisons and contrasts e.t.c explain who, where, why, how. The ideas must be stated in good clear sentences 4. The conclusion:- here you summarize your main points . it is important to end in a memorable way by: - Making a forceful and shocking statement - urging your audience to follow a certain line of action or thought e.t.c - Ending in an interesting and captivating manner. Guidelines Required for speech written 1. A speech is meant to be delivered to an audience. Hence the use of present tense is require 2. A speech should be in four sentence viz, heading introduction, body and conclusion 3. Slangs and humour should be avoided since the speech is meant to be delivered to an audience superior to the writer. The use of humour is appropriate only in an informal situation like party. 4. No use of name (s) at the end of the speech since it would have been introduction at the heading. Assignment

Prepare a speech to be delivered on the prize and award giving day of the final year students of the school.

rawText:
Week 2 (speech) Speech:- Unit Topic :- Poetry Lesson Topic:- listening to poetry for comprehension pleasure Poetry is the sum total of the use of certain devices in writing such as rhyme, rhythm, figures of speech, stanza, the poet’s feeling and attitude to the subject matter poetry is an imaginative and emotional writing to stimulate thought to be enjoyed . Types of poetry 1. Narrative poem:- poem that tell a story 2. Lyrics Poem:- Poem that is musical 3. Dramatic Poem:- Poem involving characters that interest in verse form 4. Sonnet:- A 14 – line poem, we have two types of sonnet. a. Retrachan Italian sonnet divided into octave and sestet with rhyming schema of abba, abba, ade, ade b. Shakes pearan sonnet with has 3 set of four lines followed by a couplet. 5. Pastoral poem:- Poem on a country side or rural life 6. Dirge, poem for the dead 7. Epigram:- Poem about the deeds of great people 8. Ode:- Poem that addresses a person or thing others include limerick, Elegy, epigram, Ballad e.t.c Features of poetry 1. A poem in nerse form or stanza 2. A poem uses rhyme or rhythm 3. A poem makes use of figures of speech like smile, metaphor, alitrtstion, repetition, onomatopoeia e.t.c to create imagery which appeal to the senses 4. The language of poetry is usually concise when compared to a short story or drama To read the poem on page 217 of the English text titled “On the grasshopper and cricket by John Keats. To analyze the poem To analyze the poem The poem is about nature and the beauty of simple and natural things of life, it mainly talks about two insects the grasshopper and the cricket According to

the poet, the earth can never be dead or silent because nature keeps it alive. The natural things objects used in the setting include insect, birds, sun, trees and weed. The poem is a petracham sonnet, the rhyming scheme used is abba abba ede ede. Assignment 1. write a short poem of your own 2. Differentiate between patriarchal and Shakespeare sonnet. 3. provide answers to the poem read in the class. Week 2 ( vocabulary development) Unit topic; Words associated with building Lesson topic; Types of building, building materials and workers. A. A building is a structure such as house, church or factory that has a roof and wall, the building have types and some are constructed for different purpose e.g for resident, hotel, church, hospital, factory, office, e.t.c. These are also different materials for building and workers. B. Types of building; bungalow, cottage, mansion, one storey building, high rise building, block of flats, dethatched or semi detected building place sky scrappers e.t.c. C. Workers; bricklayer, mason, plumber, carpenter, architect, engineer, painter, welder, contractor, labourers, electrician, surveyor e.t.c. D. building materials; nails, bricks, wood, bamboo, paint, block, concrete, sand, cement, tiles, marble, stones, planks, rod, zinc, saw, hammer, e.t.c. E. Part of the house; bedroom, kitchen, doors, window, roof, sitting room, dining room, toilet, bathroom, lobby, varanda, garage, basement e.t.c. F. Plans; survey, building plan, 1. foundation 2. cistern, 3. certificate of occupancy G. Other words; involve in building site, approval paper, certificate of occupancy e.t.c.

1. Airways : a space between roof insulation and roof boards for movement of ar. 2. Asphalt:- This is used n building for the water proof covering of roofs, flours, and other exterior parts 3. Conduit:- A ppe used n electrical work n which wire is installed 4. The margin of a roof projecting over the wall 5. Foundation:- The supporting proton of any structure below the frst floor 6. Partition:- a wall that subdivides spaces within any story f a building 7. Rafter :_ structure designed t support the roof 8. Veneer:- than sheets f wood made by rotary cutting or slicing a log. Tragedy; A drama full of suspense and frightful scene and in which the protagonist in constant danger. it ends on a sorrowful note e.g; Othello; by shake spear. 2. Tragedy-comedy; a drama piece in which the protagonist is faced with over bearing challenges and confrontation from his or her rivals. the suffering of protagonist provokes the sympathy of the reader. Opera:- A drama work in which all the actions are accompanied by music 7. Passion Play:- A Christian play in which the trail, Crucifixion death and resurrection of Jesus Christ is enacted 8. Masque or mask:- A drama in which poetry, music, dance, song, lavish costumes and costly stage, effects are used in an indoor performance.

Tragic Hero:- A character who rises to a noble height by his/ her extraordinary trait but is ruined by an inherent human flow 3. Protagonist:- The main character who under takes a lot of risk and face a lot of antagonism in other fight for survival and to ensure that the truth and other legitimate course is ensured and presented in a literal work 4. Antagonist:- A charater who is a close rival of the protagonist. Features of drama 1. Acts:- A major section of the action in a play which may contain one or two scenes.
