LESSON NOTE Date: 26/10/23 Class: SS 2 Time: 08:40 – 9:20 Duration: 40minutes Subject: English language Topic: Modifier Instructional Resources: Lists of modifier adjectives on a cardboard paper Objectives: 1. 2. 3. 4. At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to: Explain a modifier. Identify and give examples of modifier words. State various and suitable use of modifiers in sentences. Mention some modifiers adjectives and adverbs. STEP 1: Identification of prior idea. MODE: The entire class STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher asks the students to explain a modifier.

TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher explains that a modifier is a group of words that modifies another word. You can also say that a modifier is a word or group of words that describes a noun phrase or restricts its meaning in some way or it is a word or phrase added to give a clearer picture of the latter. That is, it say, it add meaning to a word. They describes words like adjectives and adverbs. Some examples of the adverbs it describes are: swiftly, awful, lovely etc. it involves the use of sensuous adjectival words associated with (a) Colours e.g. reddish, greenish, brownish, whitish, etc. (b) Smell e.g. sharp, pungent, unsavory, odorous, fowl, bitter, sweet, sour, acid, acidic etc. STEP 2: Exploration MODE: The entire class STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher asks the students to mention and give examples of modifier words. TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher tells the students that modifier words include adjectives and adverbs. It also deal with adverbials associated with:

a. b. c. d. (a) movement (b) manner (c) rate of occurrence (d) to describe accurately different aspects of things. Examples of movement are: rapidly, swiftly, speedily, sluggishly, majestically, awkwardly, gingerly, cautiously, stealthily as in walking, briskly, hurriedly, gently etc. Examples of manner like rashly, brusquely, carelessly, haphazardly, manner of speaking like roughly, politely, rudely, softly, tenderly etc. Rate of occurrence examples: frequently, permanently, annually, hourly, perennially, temporarily, occasionally, monthly, weekly, daily etc. To describe accurately different aspect of things modifiers e.g., describing a look in a person’s eye one can say that the eyes were glistening with tears, sparked with joy, glowing with enthusiasm, flashed sudden anger or glittered with envy/cruelty or gleamed with desire, twinkled with secret merriment and shone with happiness. The modifiers we used will help to enhance the meaning of words.

STEP 3: Discussion MODE: The entire class STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher asks the students to state the various and suitable use of modifiers. TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher guides the students to state that adjectives and adverbs will make your descriptive and narrative essay more interesting to read, below are some lists of modifiers: a. Colour – blue, bright, green, off-brown, shocking pink, deep crimson, royal blue, lemon green, pinkish etc. b. Smell – sharp, unsavouring, acidic, lovely, sweet, fowl, odorous, stinking, putrid, pungent etc. c. Taste – appetizing, bitter, delicious, awful, foul, refreshing, sugary, sweet, savoury etc. d. Sight – slender, amorphous, ugly, colossal, elegant, scruffy, plain, trime etc. e. Touch – feathery, wooly, tepid, hot, thorny, bickly, ice-cold, slippery etc. Modifier adverbs: a. Movement - sluggishly, jerkily, rapidly, awkwardly, gingerly, cautiously. b. Frequency – occasionally, permanently, lately, intermittently, bi-monthly, bi-weekly, etc.

c. Manner of doing things, brazenly, brusquely, fiercely, nonchalantly, crueltly, lovingly, thoughtlessly, carelessly etc. STEP 4: Application MODE The entire class STUDENT’S ACTIVITIES: The teacher asks the students to state the uses of modifiers in sentences. TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher guides the students to identify modifiers by comparing the sentences below: - Without modifier With modifier 1. The hunter entered The hunter entered the The forest forbidden virgin forest 2. He showed her love He showed her true love 3. There was applause There was a deafening for the musician applause for the supper star pop musician 4. She served us She served us rotten chicken putrid frozen chicken 5. She served soup She served us stone- which I did touch cold soup which I did not touch etc you can see that the use of modifier have greatly enrich the sentences on the right hand side. They have assisted to present better pictures of the nouns and verbs they describe. The above

sentences appear to our senses of sight, feelings, hearing, taste and touch respectively. Look at these sentences again Without modifier With modifier a. He surrendered his He reluctantly keys. surrendered his keys. b. He completed his He completed his assignment and assignment haphazardly submitted and submitted c. He pays us a visit He regularly pays us a visit. We can see that the last three above clearly tell us how actions were performed. The first five are adjectival modifier while the last three are adverbial modifiers. Adjectival modifier describes nouns while adverbial modifier modifies verbs. STEP 5 The teacher asks these questions: 1. Explain what a modifier mean. 2. Mention two modifier words with their examples 3. Identify two adjectival modifiers and two of the adverbial modifiers.

4. What are the uses of modifiers in a sentence? ASSIGNMENT: Make sentences with the following words. Savoury, flighty, acrid, tepid. REFERENCE BOOKS: 1. English Grammar for Senior Secondary School Book 2.

Week 4 (Speech) Lesson Topic; Health Education and health inspectors are more beneficial than doctors. Points to Oppose - Application of knowledge of first aid before going to the hospital - Preventive health care i.e preventive measures or steps to put in place to avoid sickness and diseases. - Nutrition education; these are the things to avoid or consume. - Skills and knowledge to form life long habbit. Assignment Write your speech for or against the motion Debate is an argumentative discussion in which the speaker tries to persuades and convince the listeners to accept and agree with his points o view. Features 1. The topic 2.The nocatives 3. The introduction 4. The body 5. The conclusion Points to consider (proposing) Health education is the understanding of how to maintain personal health. -Health education helps an individual to be more proactive in health The steps points to oppose application of knowledge of first aid before going to the hospital. The necessary things to avoid or consume. - First Aid: Application of knowledge of first aid before gong to hospital - Preventive health care: i.e preventive measures or steps to put in place to avoid sickeness and deases. - Nutrition education: those are the things to avoid to consumer - Skills and knowledge to form long life habits: sklls and knowledge to from life long habits. Opposing; A doctor is a person who is qualified to treat people who are sick.

- Doctors saves lives - They are equipped with relevant knowledge and skills - Doctors knows different equipment that will help detect medical problems. - Doctors provide adequate treatment for everybody. Assignment Write your speech for against the motion Week 4 (Structure) Unit topic; Suffixes Lesson Topic; Suffixes ( able, age, action, en e.t.c.) Suffixes are added at the end of a word to form another word, In actual fact, many of the words, either prefixes or suffixes, If you are able to add a suffix to a word, it becomes easier to identify the word classes ( parts of speech). Nouns, adjectives, adverb are easily identifiable in words bearing suffixes. Example; Able; Laugh – laughable Wash – washable Loud – loudable Age Bond – bondage Waste – wastage Drain – drainage Mile – miieage Dose – dosage Ant Assist – assistant Serve – servant Depend – dependant Aspire – aspirant

En Loose – loosen Dead – deaden Tight – tighten Quick – quicken Full Month – monthful Sorrow – sorrowful care – careful Hope – hopeful Week 4 ( vocabulary development) Unit topic; Words associated with law and order Lesson topic; order in the court, legal action e.t.c. law is the whole system of rules that people in a particular country or area must obey. Order means a situation in which rules are obeyed and authority are respected,The dictionary interpretes the law of the nation which must be obeyed to maintain order in that nation. Words associated with law and order. 1.Accuse; To say that somebody has done wrong 2. Aquit; To give a legal decision 3. Adjournment; To postpone proceeding in a law court. 4. Adjudicate; To give official judgement or decision upon somebody ( usually lawyer) 5. Advocate; A lawyer who speaks in favour of somebody in the court of law 6. Appeal; Taking the decision of a lower court to higher court. 7. Bail; To secure the release of somebody accused to higher court 8. Client; A person who gets help or advice from a lawyer. 9. Contempt of court; Breach or act of disloyalty or disrespect to a court. 10. Councel; Advice, (also a lawyer). 11. Court; A person who commit crime. 12. Damage; Money paid by person or company for cousing injury to another. 13. Defendant; A person against who a legal action is brought. 14. Equity; fairness, right, judgement 15. Legal action

Assignment 1. List atleast ten words associated with law and order. 2. Use those words in sentence. Week 4 (Summary) Unit topic; Reading to pick out topic sentence. Lesson topic; Summary passage – The unafraid lover unit 15 chapter 176. Summary is a brief form of writing a long passage, after removing irrelevant information from the main points using ones own words Useful tips in writing good summary i. Briefy (ii). Relevance (iii). Clarity (iv). Identify the topic sentence (v). Originality (vi). Write answers in complete sentence Topic sentence is a sentence that epresses the main idea of the paragraph in which it occurs.A topic sentence reveals the writer direction and tell the reader where the writers thoughts are leading to. Facts about un afraid lover - Nylepha is ready to leave the throne for the sake of the man she loves - People are usually jealous of the love that is unafraid. - Nylepha convinced her people about the choice of her husband - - Nylepha is loved by her people. Assignment 1. In two sentences one for each, summarise what nylepha would give to the man she loves. 2. In four sentesces one for each, summarise the attribute of Curtis that endeared him to Nylepha. Week 4 ( Continuous writing) Unit topic; Essay writing Lesson topic; Argumentative Essay (to prove a point)

An argumentative essay is an essay in which the writer tries to persuade and convince the reader to accept and agree with his point of view. Topic in this form of essay demands that the writer should prove a point ,epress an opinion and support or oppose a given idea Example 1. Child training is the sole responsibility of a mother 2. Covid – 19 is a blessing in disguise 3. Modern technology has done harm than good 4. Female should be given leadership position in the society Guidelines for an argumentative essay 1. State the topic. 2. State your vocatives; This is the greeting to acknowledge the presence of the panel and the audience. e.g The moderator/ chairman, panel of judges, accurate time keeper, co – debaters, fellow student/audience, 3. Introduction; Define a content and take a stand 4. Body; make sure you are convinced about the side you are opposing or supporting. If you support the side you do not belief in, you will run out of points and ideas. 5. Conclusion; do not draw a general conclusion from one example or a few points you need a number of points to reach a convincing conclusion. 6. Do not be illogical in your argument. 7. be sure that your points can support the conclusion you want to reach. Example; Female leaders perform better in authority than their male counter parts; Points to support 1. Her role in the home as a home maker, manager of works, husband and kids will be extended to leadership. 2. More compassionate and firm as a result of the bond created during pregnancy, thus no woman leader will see the multitude of unemployed youths roaming the street without creating jobs. 3. Woman value more the sancity of human lives and thus, would have fued of farmers and cattle rearer before it generates to killings 4. Women leaers are more collaborative and trusted.

Points use to oppose 1. Pregnancy and metanity leaves take women away from their role of leaders. 2. Expert advice husbands ( good or bad) may be extended to leadership position. 3. Family responsibility. Assignment 1. In not less than 400 words, write either for or against the topic treated in class ; Female.

Week 5 ( Communication) /Kamjuinikeisn/ Unit topic; Word stress Lesson topic; monosyllabic and polysyllabic words. A. Stress is the exertion of breath effort (force) on some sound during production. all the sound do not have equal force in production because some are said with greater force and are said louder while others are not . therefore those sound produced with greater force and energy is the stressed sound. We have primary and secondary stress , shoe, erase, people, draw, above e.t.c.The student pronounce the words above B. Syllable is the breaking down of words nto sectons that contan the smallest vowel sound, or word that an be produced at one heart beat e.g the word “Monday” contains two syllables Monday 1. Types of syllable monosyllabic words such words are usually stressed when pronounce in isolation. Example are; Go, do, gain, come, jump e.t.c load, ask, more, live, such. C. Bisyllabc:- these are words that contain two syllables. When there is more than syllable in a word, one syllable will be pronounced louder than the other sounds e.g /law/yer. More examples of Bisyllabic are : Eng/lish, fa/ther, E/ffort e.t.c. C. Polysyllabic words are words with three or more syllables and they have their own stress. Pattern Example; (a) Words with three syllables are; (i). advantage – ad – vantage (ii). expertise – ex – per – tise (iii). disagree dis – a –gree (iv). understand – un – der – stand (v). character – cha – racter Words with four syllables (i). Confidential – Con – fi – den – tial (ii)communicate – com – mu – ni –cate (ii). imposible – im – po – si – ble (iv). political – po – li – ti – cal words with five syllables (i). possibility – po – ssi – bi – li – ty

(ii). modification – mo – di – fi – ca – tion (iii). dramatization – dra – ma – ti – za – tion Words with six syllables i. Personification – per – so – ni – fi – ca – tion ii. ceremoniously – ce – re – mo- nio – us – ly iii. misrepresentation – mis – re – pre – sen – ta – tion iv. simultaneously – si – mul – ta – neo – us – ly Assignment indicate the stress syllable in each of the following words by representing it with capital letters 1. solution 2. important 3. import 4. fortunate 5. bachelor. subject: English Language
rawText:
Week 9 Topic: Tenses Sequence of Tenses Tenses is any form of a verb used to show time of action or state expressed by a verb present, past or feature. They are four (4) tenses each in a present past and future respectively. Simple past Present Continuous Present perfect Present perfect continuous etc. Sequence of tense is the agreement between the tenses of a verb in a sentence.It is the use of verb in expression and the harmony that exist between the verb used.It should be noted that the tense in the subordinated clause always follow the tense in the main clause though there are exception to this rule Rules guiding the sequence of tense 1. When the verb in the main clause is in the present tense,the verb in the subordinated clause will also be in the present tense. E.g He sees that he has made a mistake. The miner works so hard that he is tired. The old woman says that she is going to wash the dishes. Exception; A present tense in the main clause may be followed by any tense in the subordinate depending on the context or meaning conveyed. E.g I know that my father was annoyed. (present-past) You will soon receive the letter that I sent you. (future-past)

He will live in the house that he will build. (future-future) 2. A past tense in the main clause is followed by a past tense in the subordinate. E.g The miner worked so hard that he was tired. I found out that she was out of town. John succeded because he (had) worked hard. Exception; A past tense in the main clause can be followed by a present tense in the subordinate clause if it is using a universal truth. E.gThe children were thought that Honesty is the best policy. 3. A future tense in the main clause is not followed by a future tense in the subordinate clause if there are conjunctions like ; When, until, before, after. E.g I will call you when dinner is ready. I will call you when dinner will be ready (incorrect) I shall wait until you return I shall wait until you will return (incorrect) 4. When a subordinate clause is introduced by ;then, or that; the verb in the main clause may be any tense to suit the context. E.g we eat that we may live. Joy liked literature more than she likes history. I know that my dad was annoyed. She is she is saying that she is right. 5. When phrases like ;if only, wish that, what if, it is time, it is high time; are used, a past tense in the main clause follows. E.g I wish I could eat another ice cream. it is high time you studied your books.

if only I had I had enough money, I would have bought more food. 6. In direct speech, the verb in the present tense changes to past and past to past perfect tense E.g a. Dir;The train will be late. Ind; He said that the train will be late. b. Dir;I wish I know where it is said Tony Ind;Tony said he wish that he had know where it was. c. Dir;He said, ; I will be using my new car next week. Ind; He said that he will be using his car the following week. A. Tense in the present i. Present; This is used to show present action.E.g He works ii. Present continuous;To show continuous action or an event in progress. E.g he is working iii. Present perfect; to show complete action at present E.g He has worked iv. Present perfect continuous; To show an event in the progress that begin in the past and still in progress in the present. E.g He has been working B . Tense in the past i. Past; To report a past event. It is commonly used in narration E.g He worked ii. Past continuous; To show a past event in progress E.g He was working (when I entered the room) iv. Past perfect continuous; show an event in progress before a past event. E.g He had been working (since morning)

c. Tense in the future i. Future tense; To refer to events and circumstances in the future. E.g He shall work. ii. Future continuous; To refer to action that is on going or continuous. E.gHe shall be working. Types of formal letter 1. Letter of enquiry 2. Order letter 3. Letter of complaint 4. Promotion letter 5. Sales letters 6. Recovery letter Features of a formal letter 1. Writer’s address idate: This should be written at the top of a letter on the right hand corner. This includes the name of your school post office, Number, state, date e.t.c write the date in full and put a dot after each abbreviation

Government Secondary School, P.M.B. 227 Kubwa, Abuja. 28 th October,2024. 2. The recipient’s address. This is written at the left hand side below the writer’s address . Example The commissioner of education, Abia State. e.g The Registrar, University of Abuja, Abuja. 3. Salutation :- This is followed by a comma e.g Dear Sir, 4. Title:- a formal letter should have a title underlined if written in small letter or with initial of each headword in capital letter) But not underlined if written in capital letters e.g APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF A SECRETARY 5. Introduction:- This gives a brief account of what the letter talks about 6. The body of the letter:- write clear and simple English. Mind your tenses pay attention to spellings and punctuation 7. Conclusion:- This draws together the ideas and its relationship with the major points. 8. Subscription :- This comes at the end of the letter followed by a comma. Only the letter (in yours) is written in capital letter. eg Yours Faithfully 9. Signature and name :- name should be written below the signature Sign Ayo Obi Musa Assignment

Syllable can be define as part of a word that can be produce at one heart-beat, In every syllable, there must be a vowel sound. Five syllable words with stress on the first syllable 1.CAPitalism 2. Regionalism 3. Radicalism 4.FAvouritism 5.FUNCtionalism Five- syllable words with stress on the second syllable 1.MaNIpulator (2) industrialist (3) adMInistrature (4) maNIpulative (5) obSTUCtionaism (6) particularly. Five syllable words with stress on the third syllable 1. incapacitate (2) conversational (3) intrenNAtional (4) opeRAtional (5) agriCULtural (6) inciDENtally Five syllable words with stress on the fourth syllable. 1. dramatiSAtion 2. organiSAtion 3. examiNAtion 4.glorifiCAtion 5. consideRAtion 6. investiGAtion

Assignment Write 10 words of five syllables stressed in the first and second syllables. Week 6 (Structure) Unit Topic; Adjectives Lesson Topic; Types and order of adjectives. Adjectives are words which gives more information about nouns. Adjectives precede nouns which they qualify. Adjectives qualify or modify nouns or pronouns. There are types of adjectives which include; 1. Adjectives of quality-what sort, big, black sweet. 2. Adjectives of quantity- How many? 3. Demostrative adjectives- Pointing out. 4. Intrerrogative adjectives- Asking questions. 5. Possessive adjectives- showing ownership. Examples; 1. Adjectives of quality; A tough meal, strong wood, hard surface, soft leather, sour orange e.t.c. 2 .Adjectives of quantity; Five plates, little oil. 3. Demostrative adjectives; Those houses. 4. Interrogative adjectives; what book are you reading? e. Possessive adjectives; My car, your house Ordering of adjectives 1. Quality (2). Size (3). Shape (4). Colour (5). Noun. A longer type of adjectives would look like this; a. Opinion – Clean, good, beautiful, ugly e.t.c.

b. Size – Small, little, short, oversize e. t.c c. Age – New, 25 years old, teenage old e.t.c. d. Shape – Triangular, flat, circular e.t.c.ss e. Colour – Pink, dark, grey, blue e.t.c f. Material – Wooden, plastic, paper, cotton e.t.c. g. Purpose – purpose adjectives describe what something is used for. This adjectives often ends with ing, e.g Sleeping bed, dressing table, cooking pot e.t.c. Note; When two colours are involved, you join them by “and” Example; (a). Many news papers are black and white. (b). She was wearing a long blue and yellow dress Assignment Arrange this in correct order of adjectives 1. A new steel carving knife 2. A plastic big red cup 3. A sealing beautiful blue boat 4. A canadian small thin lady Week 6 (Comprehension) Unit topic; Reading to paraphrase poems and dramatic words. Lesson Unit; A poem “Africa”. By R.E.G Armattoe pg 77 new concept English. A. A paraphrase expects the general ideas contained in the poem. In actual fact, It is a test of your skill at writing a good composition. In this, you are able to exhibit your know ledge in recognizing the points arranging these ideas, using your own English expressions and vocabulary B. Poetry is a sum total of the use of devices in writing such as; rhyme, rythm, meter figures, of speech, stanza, subject material, The poet feelings and attitude to the

subject matter, It is also piece of creative writing in verse especially one experiencing deep feelings . Poetic devices 1. verse – Poetry is written in verses or stanzas. A stanza may be made up of 4 line or more 2. imagery:- An imagery is a mind picture . it is a collection of mages or a mental picture called to mind by the use of concrete expression to appeal to the readwe’s sense of imagination 3. language:- the language is writer;s choice of words . it is also called “Diction” The writer may choose to make his language simple and sometimes difficult poetry makes use of rhyme unlike prose. (Africa” pg77) The poem is an ellgy I a poem that expresses sadness) it takes a pretty lady with a warm heart who later be comes sad because of the circumstances that surrounded her 1. The mood of the malden id sadness. Line 8 show the evidence “makes my warm heart grow very cold and number 2. The malden felt that way because she is living amoung people that have no feeling line 6 3. The lady referred to her as a pretty maiden 4. She is from Africa- people from the dark origin 5. Personification 6. it is a metaphor 7. Sad, dark, lovely/ deaf dumb, cols /numb Devices used in the poem 1. Setting; by the road side, along the road. 2. Rhyming; Scheme AB AB CD CD. 3. Imagery; Pretty maiden, wayside, deaf and dumb, shameless, dead heart. 4. Language; Rich and simple to an average reader. 5. Figures of speech; Metaphor. Assignment

Read the poem again and paraphrase it in just a paragraph. Make sure that the feeling embedded in the poem reflects fully in your para-phrase. Week 7 (Speech) Unit Topic; Stress on poly syllabic words Lesson Topic; Words with six syllable stressed on the fifth syllables. There are words with six syllables ending in –ion,ity,ism, al, ly, The rules that apply to the stress of words of three to five syllables, also apply to words with six syllables> Example; 1. Electrification-electrification 2. Industrialization-industrialiZAtion 3. Experimentation-experimenTAtion 4. Syllabification-syllabifiCAtion 5. Industrialisation-industrialiSAtion 6. generalization-generaliSAtion 7. electrification-electrifiCAtion 8. personification-personifiCAtion Assignment With the aid of your dictionary ,identify the word with six syllables and put stress correctly on them.

A prefix is a group of letters added to a root word to form new words and new meaning or an affix attached to the beginning of a word, base ,or phrase and serving to produce a derivative word or an inflectional from. Example:- un, mis, il, in, im, dis, etc. A prefix added to a word usually does not change the word class (Part of Speech) of the word e.g material-immaterial(adjective) Behave-misbehave(verb) Personal-impersonal(adjective). Types of Prefix A Prefixes showing negation Dis Away, A part Disappear, disagree and disown Ill Not Illogical, illegal, illiterate Im Not Immodest, impossible, imperfect, immobile

Un Not Unhappy, uncertainly, unfair Anti Against Antisocial, antibiotics Mai Badly Malnourish, maltreat B prefix that show number Uni One Unilateral, unison Mono One Monopoly, monologue Bi Tow Bilateral, binomial Di Two Diphthong, dissect Tri Three Tricycle, tipped Penta Five Pentagon, pentagram, pentameter Poly Many Polysyllable, polygamy, polytechnique Homo Same Homophone, homogeneous Hetero Different Heterosexual, heterogeneous C. Environment refers to our immediate surroundings in which all living and non- living component co-exist. Environment is made of the air, water and land on earth, which can be harmed by man’s activities, the people and things around you in your life. Example, the building you use, people you live or work with and the general situation you are in. Also, Environment is a natural features of a place e.g whether, the type of land it has and the type of plants tt grow on it. Environmental Problems Pollution, Bush Burning, Disposal of refuse, Pest control, Sewage System, Smoking, Drainage. Soil excavation, Environmental degradation e.t.c. All these problems are caused by man

that inhabit it which in effect directly or in directly affects the life of man or animals health wise. Solutions to some Environmental problems are; 1) Sustainable Building 2) Recycle properly 3) Renewable energy 4) Conserve water and electricity 5) Replace disposable items with reusable. Words associated with natural environment. 1. Atmosphere (ii) earth (iii) gasses (iv) carbon dioxide v) sewage (vi) rain (vii) disposal (viii) climate (ix) hurricanes (x) pollution. Assignment:- Check the environment Where you live and write down at least five environmental problems you notice, prefer solutions

title: NOUN PHRASES
subject: English Language
rawText:
1 LESSON NOTE Date: 13/10/2025 Class: SS 2 Time: 08:00 -08:30 Duration: 30munites Subject: English language Topic: Noun Phrases Objectives: 1. 2. 3. At the end of the lesson, the students should be able to: Explain a phrase and a noun phrase Identify the functions of noun phrases Identify and use noun phrases in sentences Instructional Resources: Features of noun phrases on a cardboard paper STEP 1: Identification of prior idea MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher introduces the lesson by saying that phrases are group of words which when put together have some meaning but not a complete meaning e.g. (a) Surrounded by tall trees (b) Waiting for a friend. (c) Without a word. From the few examples cited you can see that none of these phrases made a complete sense. STUDENT’S ACTIVITY: The teacher asks the students to explain a noun phrase.

STEP 2: Exploration MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: The teacher gives the students to explain a noun phrase as a phrase in which the main word or word head is a noun or pronoun. It always answer the question what? Or whom e.g. my bag, their land, easy job. When a noun phrases occurs in a group of other words, without a finite verb, it becomes a noun phrase. Most times, nouns do not occur alone. There are qualified by other words. When this happens, the noun becomes a noun phrase. STUDENT’S ACTIVITY: i. ii. iii. The teacher asks the students to mention the functions of a noun phrases. Noun phrase performs any of the functions of a noun: It can function as subject of a verb e.g. (a) Thegirl came here (b) Theclass is noisy (c) Myfriend bought it. It can function as object of a verb e.g. (a) I bought myfriend (b) we honouredallof them (c) I shall send the letter. It can function as compliment of subject (a) He is thechairman e.g. (a) His wife is anurse (b) she may be ateacher.

iv. v. It can function as compliment of object e.g. we call her The lilly of the valley (b) They made him the guest speaker (c) I appointed him my advocate. It can function as opposition to a noun e.g. Grave, a centre of reality, is a place to be for the saints. (b) my dear, our new leader is very friendly (c) Nigeria, the giant of Africa is winning again. STEP 3: Discussion MODE: The entire class TEACHER’S ACTIVITY: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. The teacher gives more examples of noun phrases. The abandoned building have been demolished by government (subject of the verb). The down looks very annoying (subject of the verb) look. Fatima has a kind heart (subject of a verb has). Musa was elected the captain of the team (subject compliment to Musa). Our school team won the match (subject of the verb won). STUDENT’S ACTIVITY: The teacher asks the students to give more examples.

STEP 4: Application MODE: The entire class STUDENT’S ACTIVITY: 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. The teacher asks the students to identify the functions of noun phrase in the following sentences below: - My mother calls me sweetheart We all bought our favourite novel The noise maker was a nuisance The high chief was invited to the ceremony My friend’s parents named their new baby the Lilly The house needs some repairs STEP 5: 1. 2. 3. a. b. c. d. title: NOMINALIZATION
subject: English Language
rawText: Nominalization Most of the time, nouns are created from other parts of speech through the use of suffixes. In other cases, the word remains the same but is simply used in a different way; this is known as conversion or zero derivation. Nominalization is the process of changing a word from another part of speech to a noun. This can be done by adding suffixes to adjectives or verbs, or by using a prepositional phrase with the word "of". For example, the adjective "happy" can be nominalized by adding the suffix "ness" to form the noun "happiness". The verb "to run" can be nominalized by adding the suffix "ing" to form the noun "running". And the prepositional phrase "of happiness" can be nominalized by using the word "happiness" as the head of the noun phrase. Nominalization is the process of turning a word from another grammatical class into a noun. This usually happens by means of adding a suffix. Suffixes are certain groupings of letters that can be attached to the end of words to change their meaning. Most verbs and adjectives that become nouns are changed using suffixes. Adjective Verb Able-Enable Abundant-Abound Wide- Widen Specific- Specify Rich- Enrich Popular- Popularize Just- Justify Flat -Flatten Pure-Purify Different- Differentiate

title: ADJECTIVAL CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Adjectival Clauses Adjectival clauses are dependent clauses that describe or modify a noun or pronoun, just like a single adjective would. They usually start with a relative pronoun: _who, whom, whose, which, that_, or a relative adverb: _where, when, why_. They usually start with a relative pronoun: _who, whom, whose, which, that_, or a relative adverb: _where, when, why_. 1. Basic structure Noun/Pronoun + Relative word + Clause > The book that you recommended was great. > “that you recommended” describes _book_ 2. Grammatical functions Adjectival clauses always function as adjectives, but they can do this in 3 ways: a. Attributive / Modifying a noun directly The clause sits right next to the noun it modifies. > The student who won the prize is my friend. > Function: modifies _student_ b. Restrictive vs. Non-restrictive* - Restrictive/Defining: Limits which noun you mean. No commas. > Cars that run on electricity are expensive. > Only electric cars, not all cars. - Non-restrictive/Non-defining: Adds extra info. Uses commas. > My car, which is 10 years old, still runs well. > You already know which car I mean. c. Postmodifier in a noun phrase They expand the noun phrase to give more detail, answering _which one? what kind?_

> The house where I grew up was sold last year. > Function: modifies _house_, tells you which house

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH Topic: Consonant Clusters (Three Consonants in Initial Position) Meaning A consonant cluster is a group of two or more consonant sounds pronounced together in a word without any vowel sound between them. When three consonants occur at the beginning of a word , it is called a three-consonant cluster . These clusters can be difficult to pronounce, especially for beginners, because all the sounds must be pronounced quickly and smoothly. Common Patterns of Three-Consonant Clusters Cluster Example Words Pronunciation /spr/ spring, spray, spread, sprain, sprite /sprɪŋ/, /spreɪ/, /sprɛd/ /spl/ splash, splendid, split, splay /splæʃ/, /splɪt/ /str/ strong, street, strike, strap, stream /strɒŋ/, /striːt/, /straɪk/ /skr/ scream, scrape, scroll, scratch /skriːm/, /skræʧ/ /shr/ shriek, shrink, shrub, shred /ʃriːk/, /ʃrʌb/ /skw/ square, squeeze, squirm, squad /skweə/, /skwiːz/ /skr/ screw, scrape, scroll /skruː/, /skrəʊl/ Pronunciation Tips 1. Do not insert vowels between consonants. su-pring → spring 2. Pronounce the sounds smoothly and continuously. 3. Practice slowly, then increase your speed. Class Activity Pronounce the following words correctly: spring, splash, street, scream, shrink, square. Then write two new words for each cluster. READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Reading for the Main Gist in a Prose Passage Meaning Reading for the main gist means finding the central idea or main message in a passage, especially in prose (story form). It is about understanding what the passage is mainly about rather than every single detail.

Skills Needed 1. Skimming: Read quickly to get a general idea. 2. Identifying key sentences: Focus on topic sentences and concluding sentences. 3. Recognizing main ideas: What is the passage mainly discussing? 4. Ignoring minor details: Avoid unnecessary examples or descriptions. 5. Understanding tone and purpose: Is the writer informing, entertaining, or describing? Steps to Find the Main Gist 1. Read the passage once to understand the story or discussion. 2. Ask yourself: “What is the writer really talking about?” 3. Identify the main idea in each paragraph. 4. Combine these ideas into one or two sentences. Example Passage: John woke up late and missed his school bus. He decided to walk to school but got caught in the rain. When he finally arrived, the gate was closed. It was the worst morning of his life. Main Gist: John had a bad morning because he was late to school and faced several problems. Tips for Reading for Gist • Read quickly and do not focus on every word. • Look for repeated ideas or important events. • Write the gist in your own words. STRUCTURE Topic: Adjectival Phrases and Their Grammatical Functions in a Sentence Meaning An adjectival phrase is a group of words that functions as an adjective in a sentence. It describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun . Examples of Adjectival Phrases Adjectival Phrase Noun Described Example Sentence full of sugar tea I drank a cup full of sugar . made of wood table The table made of wood is strong. very beautiful girl The very beautiful girl won the prize. with long hair woman The woman with long hair is my sister.

Adjectival Phrase Noun Described Example Sentence in the blue shirt boy The boy in the blue shirt is my friend. Functions of Adjectival Phrases in a Sentence 1. To describe nouns or pronouns The man with the red cap is my uncle. 2. To qualify or modify subjects or objects I saw a car covered with dust. 3. To make sentences more detailed and interesting The teacher known for her kindness helped the students. How to Identify Adjectival Phrases • They usually come after the noun they describe. • They often begin with prepositions (in, with, made of, full of, etc.) or intensifiers (very, quite, too). • They answer the question “what kind of?” Exercise Underline the adjectival phrases in the following sentences: 1. The girl with the red ribbon is my cousin. 2. We bought fruits full of juice. 3. The man in the black coat left early. 4. The car parked beside the gate is new. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Creative Writing Meaning Creative writing is writing that shows imagination and creativity , usually to entertain, describe, or express emotions. It includes stories, poems, plays, and personal experiences. (1) Features of a Short Story A short story is a brief work of fiction that can be read in one sitting. Feature Explanation Plot The sequence of events or actions in the story. Characters The people or animals that take part in the story. Setting The time and place where the story happens. Theme The main idea or message of the story (e.g., honesty, love, betrayal).

Feature Explanation Conflict The problem or struggle between characters or forces. Action The movement of events that make the story interesting. Style The writer’s way of expressing ideas (simple, clear, or descriptive). Example (Short Story Opening): It was raining heavily when Musa left the house. He had forgotten his umbrella, but he was determined to reach school on time. Little did he know that the rain would lead him to an unexpected discovery. (2) Features of a Person (Descriptive Writing) When describing a person in creative writing, focus on appearance, character, and behavior . Feature Example Height/Size tall, short, slim, fat, broad-shouldered Complexion fair, dark, light-skinned Hair long, curly, straight, grey Face/Eyes round face, blue eyes, kind eyes Clothing neat, shabby, fashionable Character Traits honest, hardworking, kind, proud, gentle Language clear, concise, and descriptive Example Description: Aisha is a tall, graceful girl with long black hair and bright eyes. She speaks gently and always smiles at everyone. Her kindness makes her loved by all her classmates. Tips for Good Creative Writing 1. Plan your story before writing. 2. Use interesting and descriptive language. 3. Keep the story short and focused. 4. Develop your characters and setting. 5. End the story with a clear or surprising conclusion.

READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Reading for the Main Gist in a Prose Passage Meaning Reading for the main gist means finding the central idea or main message in a passage, especially in prose (story form). It is about understanding what the passage is mainly about rather than every single detail.

Skills Needed 1. Skimming: Read quickly to get a general idea. 2. Identifying key sentences: Focus on topic sentences and concluding sentences. 3. Recognizing main ideas: What is the passage mainly discussing? 4. Ignoring minor details: Avoid unnecessary examples or descriptions. 5. Understanding tone and purpose: Is the writer informing, entertaining, or describing? Steps to Find the Main Gist 1. Read the passage once to understand the story or discussion. 2. Ask yourself: “What is the writer really talking about?” 3. Identify the main idea in each paragraph. 4. Combine these ideas into one or two sentences. Example Passage: John woke up late and missed his school bus. He decided to walk to school but got caught in the rain. When he finally arrived, the gate was closed. It was the worst morning of his life. Main Gist: John had a bad morning because he was late to school and faced several problems. Tips for Reading for Gist • Read quickly and do not focus on every word. • Look for repeated ideas or important events. • Write the gist in your own words. STRUCTURE Topic: Adjectival Phrases and Their Grammatical Functions in a Sentence Meaning An adjectival phrase is a group of words that functions as an adjective in a sentence. It describes or gives more information about a noun or pronoun . Examples of Adjectival Phrases Adjectival Phrase Noun Described Example Sentence full of sugar tea I drank a cup full of sugar . made of wood table The table made of wood is strong. very beautiful girl The very beautiful girl won the prize. with long hair woman The woman with long hair is my sister.

Adjectival Phrase Noun Described Example Sentence in the blue shirt boy The boy in the blue shirt is my friend. Functions of Adjectival Phrases in a Sentence 1. To describe nouns or pronouns The man with the red cap is my uncle. 2. To qualify or modify subjects or objects I saw a car covered with dust. 3. To make sentences more detailed and interesting The teacher known for her kindness helped the students. How to Identify Adjectival Phrases • They usually come after the noun they describe. • They often begin with prepositions (in, with, made of, full of, etc.) or intensifiers (very, quite, too). • They answer the question “what kind of?” Exercise Underline the adjectival phrases in the following sentences: 1. The girl with the red ribbon is my cousin. 2. We bought fruits full of juice. 3. The man in the black coat left early. 4. The car parked beside the gate is new. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Creative Writing Meaning Creative writing is writing that shows imagination and creativity , usually to entertain, describe, or express emotions. It includes stories, poems, plays, and personal experiences. (1) Features of a Short Story A short story is a brief work of fiction that can be read in one sitting. Feature Explanation Plot The sequence of events or actions in the story. Characters The people or animals that take part in the story. Setting The time and place where the story happens. Theme The main idea or message of the story (e.g., honesty, love, betrayal).

Feature Explanation Conflict The problem or struggle between characters or forces. Action The movement of events that make the story interesting. Style The writer’s way of expressing ideas (simple, clear, or descriptive). Example (Short Story Opening): It was raining heavily when Musa left the house. He had forgotten his umbrella, but he was determined to reach school on time. Little did he know that the rain would lead him to an unexpected discovery. (2) Features of a Person (Descriptive Writing) When describing a person in creative writing, focus on appearance, character, and behavior . Feature Example Height/Size tall, short, slim, fat, broad-shouldered Complexion fair, dark, light-skinned Hair long, curly, straight, grey Face/Eyes round face, blue eyes, kind eyes Clothing neat, shabby, fashionable Character Traits honest, hardworking, kind, proud, gentle Language clear, concise, and descriptive Example Description: Aisha is a tall, graceful girl with long black hair and bright eyes. She speaks gently and always smiles at everyone. Her kindness makes her loved by all her classmates. Tips for Good Creative Writing 1. Plan your story before writing. 2. Use interesting and descriptive language. 3. Keep the story short and focused. 4. Develop your characters and setting. 5. End the story with a clear or surprising conclusion.

title: GRAMMAR
subject: English Language
rawText:
PRONOUNS: RELATIVE AND DEMONSTRATIVE (FUNCTIONS AND POSITION) Pronouns are words used instead of nouns. Without pronouns, we would constantly have to repeat nouns, and that would make our speech very repetitive. Using pronouns help the flow of sentences and makes them more interesting. In nearly all cases, a pronoun must follow an expression called an antecedent. The following are some types of pronouns:  Indefinite pronouns: pronouns referring to one or more unspecified noun; anyone, somebody, whichever, whoever, other, something, nobody, this, all, such.  Personal pronouns: pronouns used to replace proper nouns; I, you, we, he/she, him/her, it, e.t.c.  Reflexive pronouns: pronouns used to refer back to the subject; myself, themselves, himself/herself, ourselves, e.t.c.  Possessive pronouns: pronouns showing possession; mine, its, hers, yours, ours, theirs, e.t.c.  Interrogative pronouns: pronouns which introduce a question; who, whose, whom, what, and which.  Reciprocal pronouns: pronouns that show mutual actions or relationship; one another and each other .  Relative Pronouns : these are pronouns that are used to refer to nouns mentioned previously, whether they are people, places, things, animals or ideas. Relative pronouns can be used to join two sentences. The most common relative pronouns are: which, that, whose, who and whom . They are used to introduce relative clauses. Examples: 1. The cyclists who won the race trained hard. 2. The pants that I bought yesterday are already dirty. 3. Indomie, which we eat once a week, is the kids’ favourite. 4. This is the girl, whose key you found. 5. He’s a person whom I spoke about.  Demonstrative Pronouns: A demonstrative pronoun is a pronoun that is used to point something specific within a sentence. These pronouns can indicate items in space or time, and they can either be singular or plural. They are: this, these, that and those. Others are none, such, neither, either. Examples: 1. This was my mother’s ring. 2. That looks like my car. 3. These are nice shoes but uncomfortable. 4. Those look riper than the oranges on my trees. Class-work/Assignment

1. ___________ was such an interesting experience. A) that b) these c) those d) such. 2. I am looking for someone ____ can watch my dog. A) which b) who c) whom d) whoever 3. __________ of them had seen it before. A) those b) neither c) such d) this 4. The festival, _________ lasted all day, ended with a banquet. A) that b) who c) which d) what 5. Is _______ yours? A) this b) those c) these c) such

Words commonly Misspelt Spelling is the formation of words correctly from individual letters when put together in a particular order. It is the act of forming words correctly from other letters. Guidelines to a good spelling 1. Read extensively and intensively. One learns to spell more words through reading. 2. As you read, learn spellings of the words. 3. Do not guess at any spelling but look it up in the dictionary if you are in doubt. 4. Learn to pronounce words correctly from others and from the dictionary. Spelling problems emanate from incorrect pronunciations. 5. Always concentrate on the words that are likely to give you trouble all the time. 6. Correct every spelling error that is brought to your attention. 7. Have a study group where you can test your ability, through spelling and dictation. A dictionary is a book that gives the list of words of a language in alphabetical order and explain their meaning in the same language. Uses of the dictionary/E.g. inspection 1. The word list shows spelling and number of syllables. 2. Transcribes word /inspekʃn/ 3. Shows the stressed syllable and pronunciation -/in’spekʃn/ - 2 nd syllable. 4. Shows the part of speech (noun) 5. (C, U) shows whether it is countable or uncountable noun. 6. (I, Z): number shows different meaning. 7. Usage: shows the usage in a sentence. 8. title: FIGURES OF SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText: FIGURES OF SPEECH - Figures of speech are words flowers that adorned or embellished the bony structure of communication. Different types of figures of speech 1. Simile: is the comparison of two different things which have the same qualities with the use of As and Like E .g i. she is like a flower ii. Your love is as sweet as honey iii. He fought as brave as a lion 2. Metaphor: Is s a direct comparison of two different things that share the same qualities without the use of as and like E .g i.Chika is an angel ii. Gbenga is a lion on the field 3. Personification: Is an inanimate object (non living) is giving an address as human attribute or qualities. E .g i. The earth is smiling ii. The river Niger is clapping iii. Today’s weather is sad. 4. Irony: Is expresses an opposite of what a speaker actually means. E .g i. James is the tallest boy in the class whereas he is the shortest ii. King Audu is a generous man, he can even take from a street beggar 5. Hyperbole: Is an exaggeration of facts or an event to show how serious it is, sometimes to make fun of some things E .g i. The man is taller than the cocoa house in Ibadan. ii. The whole world stood still to welcome the president.

rawText: Vocabulary of Health 1. Out – patient: a person who visits a hospital for treatment and return to his house. 2. In – patient: a person admitted in a hospital ward. 3. Dislocation: shifting of the bone from its normal position. 4. Fracture: broken bones 5. Amputation: cutting off a part of the body. 6. Paralysis: inability to move the body or part of the body 7. Consultant: a person who gives expert advice on medicine and surgery. 8. Bandage: strip of material for binding round a wound. 9. Blood donor: a person who gives blood for blood transfusion. 10. Bone-setter: a person who sets broken bones. 11. Clinic: hospital or institution where medical advice and treatment are given. 12. Dentist: a person whose work is filling, cleaning and taking out teeth and fitting artificial teeth. 13. Dermatology: medical study of the skin and skin disease. 14. Dispenser: a person who dispenses medicine. 15. Doctor: a person who has been trained in medical science. 16. Matron: a woman who manages the domestic affairs and nursing staff of a hospital. 17. Medicine: the act and science of preventing disease. 18. Nurse: a person trained to take care of people who are ill or injured. 19. Surgeon: a doctor who performs operations. 20. Theatre: a room in a hospital where surgical operations are performed.

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Pronouns Relative and Demostrative A relative pronoun does the work of a pronoun and a conjunction in a sentence. It stands alone instead of a noun and also joins an adjective clause in a complex sentence. The relative pronoun are who, who, that, which, and whose. Examples: i. The man who came here yesterday is my friend ii. I read the book that was given to me iii. He saw the man whose house was burnt. Note that the relative pronoun is close to the noun it is describing. The relative pronouns can be subdivided into two. a. Those that are used when we want to refer to inanimate objects or ideas such as which, that. b. Those that are used when we want to refer to human beings such as who, whom, and whose. Examples: i. Who’s is used for people in the subject position e.g is that the girl who sang the song? ii. Which refers to inanimate objects or ideas e.g the shoe which you bought is too small. Which is also used when the information is not critical and we need a comma E.g Bukola sent away the dog which she bought last month iii. Whom is used for people but it is used when the person or people we are referring to are the objects. Example: the girl whom you saw has come back iv. That is used for both human beings and things. It is mostly used when the information in the subordinate clause is essential to the meaning of the main clause. E.g she has gone to place that is dangerous. v. Whose shows possession. Example: the man whose pen you took is upset. Demonstrative pronouns point to items being referred to and they are four (4) pronouns whose work is to point out things. They are This, That, These, Those. They are subdivided into:

a. Singular pronouns This (Near) That (far) b. Plural pronouns These Those This and These refers to items that are close to the speaker, however, while this is used for a single item, these refers to more than one item. Examples. i. I want these cups ii. This is the book iii. That is my pen iv. Those oranges are spoilt. Demonstrative pronouns can occupy the following positions in the sentences. a. title: NOUN PHRASE
subject: English Language
rawText:
NOUN PHRASE This is a phrase headed by a noun pronoun or determiners A noun phrase answer the question “what” or who” this mean that once a given expression , which is a phrase is the answer to a question formed with the interrogative words . Function of noun phrase Subject of a verb : A Noun phrase is the subject of a verb if it followed the verb in a sentence E.g The intelligent children were given an award. The lady has woken up. object of a verb: A noun phrase is the object of or verb if it comes after the verb in a sentence e.g i. He tore the man’s birth certificate. ii. She bought a mango. complement of an object: when a noun phrase is placed immediately after an object in a sentence. e.g i. The teacher appointed the boy the captain of the class. ii. I enjoy the book Chike and River. Complement of a preposition: where a noun phrase is the complement of a preposition in a sentence, it directly succeed placed after the preposition e.g i. she gave the letter to the teacher. ii. The drug is for victims of HIV/AIDs, Complement of a subject: wherever a noun phrase describes the subject of a sentence E.g i. Mr Ojo is the younger brother of the president.

ii. Joy and Rita are birds of a feather. In apposition of a noun: a noun phrase is in apposition to a noun if it is the same thing or person as the noun in a sentence E.g i. Honesty, the best policy in life, is better than riches. ii. We saw Muhammad Buhari, the president of Nigeria at the occasion.

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT
subject: English Language
rawText: Internal Human Organ The human body is made up of many organs both internal and external and each has a unique function it performs in the body. The students are instructed to write down the internal body organ they know and the work they do in human body. They should keep it until discussion time. The human internal body system which are the internal organs of the body. As she mention each, the student checks what they have written whether it contains such. Students try to explain their function. The functions of the various internal organs. 1. Heart: it is an organ which pumps blood through the body. 2. Brain: it is the organ inside the head which controls our thinking, feeling and movement. 3. Kidney: this separates waste products from the blood and makes urine. 4. Liver: it produces bile and cleans the blood. 5. Intestine: it is the long tube like organ in the body through which food passes after it leaves the stomach. It is of two types – the large intestine and the small intestine. 6. Muscles: pieces of flesh inside the body that is used in order to move and that connects the bones together. 7. Bladder: This holds urine until it is passed out of the body. 8. Veins: the tubes which carry blood to the heart from other parts of the body. 9. Nerves: they are tiny veins like threads which carry messages between the brain and other parts of the body. Lungs: these are the two organs in the body that we breathe with.

title: CONTINUOUS WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Descriptive Essay A descriptive essay is an essay that required one to describe something- a person, place, object or an event as clearly as possible so that the reader can have a vivid mental picture of what the thing being described looks like. E.g. My best friend Questions to serve as a good guide. Key words used. 1. Who is your friend? (provide name etc.) 2. Where does he come from? 3. What are his qualities – good or bad 4. What is his facial expression –ugly / handsome 5. Is he in the same school with you? 6. Is he in the same class with you? 7. What are his hobbies? Why do you like your best friend?

subject: English Language
rawText: NOMINALISATION Nominalisation is when we take verbs or adjectives and turn them into nouns. In other words, we are transforming actions or events (verbs) or descriptions of nouns and pronouns (adjectives) into things, concepts or people (nouns). This can be done by adding suffixes to adjectives or verbs. Examples of Nominalised Verbs VERB NOUN 1. Develop development 2. Confuse confusion 3. Adapt adaptation 4. Perform performance 5. Diagnose diagnosis Class-work/Assignment 6. Reproduce reproduction 7. Achieve achievement 8. Civilise civilization 9. Discover discovery 10. subject: English Language
rawText:
PRONOUNS: RELATIVE AND DEMONSTRATIVE (FUNCTIONS AND POSITION) Pronouns are words used instead of nouns. Without pronouns, we would constantly have to repeat nouns, and that would make our speech very repetitive. Using pronouns help the flow of sentences and makes them more interesting. In nearly all cases, a pronoun must follow an expression called an antecedent. The following are some types of pronouns:  Indefinite pronouns: pronouns referring to one or more unspecified noun; anyone, somebody, whichever, whoever, other, something, nobody, this, all, such.  Personal pronouns: pronouns used to replace proper nouns; I, you, we, he/she, him/her, it, e.t.c.  Reflexive pronouns: pronouns used to refer back to the subject; myself, themselves, himself/herself, ourselves, e.t.c.  Possessive pronouns: pronouns showing possession; mine, its, hers, yours, ours, theirs, e.t.c.  Interrogative pronouns: pronouns which introduce a question; who, whose, whom, what, and which.  Reciprocal pronouns: pronouns that show mutual actions or relationship; one another and each other .  Relative Pronouns : these are pronouns that are used to refer to nouns mentioned previously, whether they are people, places, things, animals or ideas. Relative pronouns can be used to join two sentences. The most common relative pronouns are: which, that, whose, who and whom . They are used to introduce relative clauses. Examples: 1. The cyclists who won the race trained hard. 2. The pants that I bought yesterday are already dirty. 3. Indomie, which we eat once a week, is the kids’ favourite. 4. This is the girl, whose key you found. 5. He’s a person whom I spoke about.  Demonstrative Pronouns: A demonstrative pronoun is a pronoun that is used to point something specific within a sentence. These pronouns can indicate items in space or time, and they can either be singular or plural. They are: this, these, that and those. Others are none, such, neither, either. Examples: 1. This was my mother’s ring. 2. That looks like my car. 3. These are nice shoes but uncomfortable. 4. Those look riper than the oranges on my trees. Class-work/Assignment

1. ___________ was such an interesting experience. A) that b) these c) those d) such. 2. I am looking for someone ____ can watch my dog. A) which b) who c) whom d) whoever 3. __________ of them had seen it before. A) those b) neither c) such d) this 4. The festival, _________ lasted all day, ended with a banquet. A) that b) who c) which d) what 5. Is _______ yours? A) this b) those c) these c) such

SPEECH Topic: Unstressed Vowel Sounds (e.g. /ə/ – the Schwa Sound) Meaning In English, not all syllables in words are pronounced with the same force. An unstressed vowel sound is a weak sound in a word — it is not emphasized when spoken. The most common unstressed vowel sound in English is /ə/, called the schwa sound. It is the weakest and most common vowel sound in English speech. Examples of Words with the Unstressed Vowel /ə/ Word Phonetic Form Unstressed Vowel about /əˈbaʊt/ a = /ə/ teacher /ˈtiːtʃə/ er = /ə/ doctor /ˈdɒktə/ or = /ə/ banana /bəˈnɑːnə/ 1st and last ‘a’ = /ə/ mother /ˈmʌðə/ er = /ə/ support /səˈpɔːt/ su = /sə/ problem /ˈprɒbləm/ em = /əm/ How to Identify Unstressed Vowel Sounds 1. They occur in weak syllables. 2. They are short and soft when spoken. 3. They are usually written with vowels like a, e, i, o, u but pronounced as /ə/. 4. They are common in function words (articles, prepositions, pronouns, etc.). Examples: • a boy → /ə bɔɪ/ • an apple → /ən ˈæpəl/ • to go → /tə gəʊ/ Importance of Learning Unstressed Vowels 1. It improves pronunciation.

2. It helps in correct word stress and rhythm. 3. It makes speech sound more natural and fluent. STRUCTURE Topic: Pronouns – Other Types of Pronouns Meaning of Pronouns A pronoun is a word used in place of a noun to avoid repetition. Types of Pronouns (Other than Personal Pronouns) 1. Reflexive Pronouns Used when the subject and the object of a sentence are the same person. Examples: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. He hurt himself while running. 2. Relative Pronouns Used to introduce a clause and relate it to a noun mentioned earlier. Examples: who, whom, whose, which, that. The boy who won the prize is my friend. 3. Demonstrative Pronouns Used to point out specific persons or things. Examples: this, that, these, those. This is my pen; those are yours. 4. Interrogative Pronouns Used to ask questions. Examples: who, whom, whose, which, what. Who is at the door? 5. Indefinite Pronouns Refer to people or things in a general way. Examples: someone, everyone, anyone, nobody, something, each, few, all, many. Everybody likes music.

6. Reciprocal Pronouns Used to show a mutual relationship or action. Examples: each other, one another. The two friends helped each other. 7. Possessive Pronouns Show ownership or possession. Examples: mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs. That book is mine. Exercise: Choose the correct pronoun to complete each sentence: 1. The man ___ helped you is my uncle. 2. The boys fought among ___ . 3. Is this book ___ ? 4. ___ of the answers is correct. (Answers: who, themselves, yours, none) READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Reading for Critical Evaluation Meaning Reading for critical evaluation means analyzing and judging what you read to decide whether it is true, logical, or biased. It goes beyond understanding — it tests your reasoning and judgment. Skills Needed 1. Identify the writer’s purpose – Why was the passage written? 2. Check for facts and opinions – Distinguish between what is true and what is believed. 3. Detect bias or prejudice – Is the writer fair or one-sided? 4. Examine evidence – Are claims supported with proof? 5. Evaluate arguments – Are they logical and convincing?

6. Form your own opinion – Agree or disagree based on reasoning. Example: Sentence: “Private schools are better than public schools because all their students pass exams.” Critical Evaluation: • The statement is an opinion, not a fact. • It is biased because not all private schools perform better. • A critical reader will look for evidence or statistics before agreeing. Purpose of Critical Reading 1. To develop independent thinking. 2. To help identify truth from falsehood. 3. To improve judgment and reasoning skills. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Argumentative Essay Meaning An argumentative essay is a piece of writing where the writer gives reasons for or against a particular topic to convince the reader. It is based on logic, facts, and reasoning, not just opinions. Features of an Argumentative Essay 1. Introduction: o State the topic clearly. o Indicate the side you are supporting (for or against). 2. Body: o Present your arguments point by point. o Support each point with facts, examples, and evidence. o Present opposing views and refute them logically. 3. Conclusion:

o Summarize your main points. o Restate your position clearly and strongly. 4. Language Features: o Use logical connectives (therefore, however, because, in conclusion). o Use persuasive language (clearly, obviously, it is evident that…). o Maintain formal tone and third-person voice. Example of Argumentative Essay Introduction Topic: Should Students Use Mobile Phones in School? Mobile phones have become very common among students today. While some people believe that they are useful for learning and communication, others think they distract students from their studies. This essay will argue that students should not be allowed to use mobile phones in school because they cause distraction and encourage laziness. Common Features to Remember • Logical organization • Balanced discussion • Clear position (for or against) • Evidence-based arguments • Persuasive tone

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH Topic: Diphthongs – /eɪ/, /aɪ/, /ɔɪ/, /aʊ/, /əʊ/, /ɪə/, /eə/, /ʊə/ Meaning of Diphthongs A diphthong is a gliding vowel sound made by combining two vowel sounds in one syllable. When pronouncing a diphthong, the tongue glides from one vowel position to another smoothly. Example: “boy” – /ɔɪ/, “time” – /aɪ/ List and Examples of Diphthongs Symbol Example Words Description /eɪ/ day, name, rain, play Glides from /e/ to /ɪ/ /aɪ/ time, fine, high, write Glides from /a/ to /ɪ/ /ɔɪ/ boy, toy, boil, noise Glides from /ɔ/ to /ɪ/ /aʊ/ now, cow, loud, house Glides from /a/ to /ʊ/ /əʊ/ go, show, no, road Glides from /ə/ to /ʊ/ /ɪə/ here, near, ear, fear Glides from /ɪ/ to /ə/ /eə/ hair, chair, fair, air Glides from /e/ to /ə/ /ʊə/ pure, sure, tour, cure Glides from /ʊ/ to /ə/ Practice Activity 1. Pronounce the following words and identify the diphthongs: o play, fire, boil, loud, go, near, fair, pure 2. Use each in a short sentence. READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Word Substitution in Passages – Connotation and Denotation Meaning of Word Substitution Word substitution means replacing a group of words with a single word or finding a word that best fits a given meaning in a passage. It helps improve vocabulary and reading comprehension. Denotation • Denotation is the dictionary meaning of a word — its literal or exact meaning. • Example: o Snake → a long, legless reptile. Connotation • Connotation is the emotional or suggested meaning of a word — what it implies or feels like. • Example: o Snake → may suggest danger, evil, or betrayal. Examples of Denotation and Connotation

Word Denotation (Literal Meaning) Connotation (Suggested Meaning) Home A place where one lives Comfort, love, safety Youthful Young, energetic Immature, inexperienced Cheap Low in price Poor quality Slim Thin Attractive Stubborn Not easily persuaded Determined or rude (depends on tone) Activity Read a short passage and identify: 1. Words that carry positive connotation. 2. Words that carry negative connotation. 3. Replace a phrase like “a person who studies the stars” with “astronomer” (word substitution). Examples of Word Substitution Phrase Single Word A person who teaches Teacher A person who studies the stars Astronomer A place where books are kept Library A person who writes poems Poet The killing of oneself Suicide The study of plants Botany SUMMARY WRITING Topic: Reading to Summarize in a Specific Number of Sentences Meaning Summary writing means expressing the main ideas of a passage in fewer words without changing the meaning. It requires reading comprehension and the ability to identify key points. Steps in Summary Writing 1. Read the passage carefully. 2. Identify the main ideas or topic sentences. 3. Underline key points and important facts. 4. Ignore examples, repetitions, or illustrations. 5. Write your summary in your own words. 6. Keep to the required number of sentences. Qualities of a Good Summary 1. Short and precise. 2. Written in your own words. 3. Includes only main ideas.

4. Maintains the writer’s original meaning. 5. Flows logically and clearly. Example Passage: Water is important for life. People use it for drinking, washing, cooking, and farming. Without water, living things cannot survive. Summary (in two sentences): Water is essential for all living things. It is used for drinking, cooking, and farming. Practice Task Read a passage of about 150 words and summarize it in five sentences. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Formal Letter – Letter of Request Meaning A letter of request is a formal letter written to ask for permission, assistance, or support from a person in authority — such as a principal, manager, or government officer. (a) Features of a Formal Letter Feature Explanation Writer’s Address Top right-hand corner (e.g. 12, Garki Road, Abuja). Date Below the address. Receiver’s Address Below on the left-hand side. Salutation Dear Sir/Madam, Heading/Subject Written in capital letters (e.g. REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE WITH SCHOOL PROJECT ). Introduction State who you are and your purpose for writing. Body Give full details of your request clearly and politely. Conclusion Express gratitude and expectation for a positive response. Closing Yours faithfully, Signature and Name (Signed) Musa Ibrahim (b) Language of a Formal Letter • Polite and respectful tone. • Clear and simple sentences. • No slang or contractions (e.g. use I am instead of I’m ). • Use formal words such as request , kindly , appreciate , assistance , consideration . • Maintain correct punctuation and spelling. Example: Letter of Request

12, Garki Road, Abuja. 2nd November, 2025. The Principal, Government Secondary School, Garki, Abuja. Dear Sir, REQUEST FOR PERMISSION TO USE THE SCHOOL HALL FOR DEBATE PRACTICE I am the president of the school debate club. On behalf of the members, I am writing to request permission to use the school hall every Wednesday between 3:00 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. for our debate practice. This request will enable us to prepare adequately for the forthcoming inter-school debate competition. We promise to handle the hall and its equipment with care. We shall be grateful if this request is granted. Thank you for your kind consideration. Yours faithfully, (Signed) Musa Ibrahim (President, Debate Club) Tips for Writing a Good Letter of Request 1. Be clear about what you are asking for. 2. Use formal, polite language. 3. Give reasons for your request. 4. Express gratitude at the end.

pages.text: SPEECH Topic: Diphthongs – /eɪ/, /aɪ/, /ɔɪ/, /aʊ/, /əʊ/, /ɪə/, /eə/, /ʊə/ Meaning of Diphthongs A diphthong is a gliding vowel sound made by combining two vowel sounds in one syllable. When pronouncing a diphthong, the tongue glides from one vowel position to another smoothly. Example: “boy” – /ɔɪ/, “time” – /aɪ/ List and Examples of Diphthongs Symbol Example Words Description /eɪ/ day, name, rain, play Glides from /e/ to /ɪ/ /aɪ/ time, fine, high, write Glides from /a/ to /ɪ/ /ɔɪ/ boy, toy, boil, noise Glides from /ɔ/ to /ɪ/ /aʊ/ now, cow, loud, house Glides from /a/ to /ʊ/ /əʊ/ go, show, no, road Glides from /ə/ to /ʊ/ /ɪə/ here, near, ear, fear Glides from /ɪ/ to /ə/ /eə/ hair, chair, fair, air Glides from /e/ to /ə/ /ʊə/ pure, sure, tour, cure Glides from /ʊ/ to /ə/ Practice Activity 1. Pronounce the following words and identify the diphthongs: o play, fire, boil, loud, go, near, fair, pure 2. Use each in a short sentence. READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Word Substitution in Passages – Connotation and Denotation Meaning of Word Substitution Word substitution means replacing a group of words with a single word or finding a word that best fits a given meaning in a passage. It helps improve vocabulary and reading comprehension. Denotation • Denotation is the dictionary meaning of a word — its literal or exact meaning. • Example: o Snake → a long, legless reptile. Connotation • Connotation is the emotional or suggested meaning of a word — what it implies or feels like. • Example: o Snake → may suggest danger, evil, or betrayal. Examples of Denotation and Connotation

Word Denotation (Literal Meaning) Connotation (Suggested Meaning) Home A place where one lives Comfort, love, safety Youthful Young, energetic Immature, inexperienced Cheap Low in price Poor quality Slim Thin Attractive Stubborn Not easily persuaded Determined or rude (depends on tone) Activity Read a short passage and identify: 1. Words that carry positive connotation. 2. Words that carry negative connotation. 3. Replace a phrase like “a person who studies the stars” with “astronomer” (word substitution). Examples of Word Substitution Phrase Single Word A person who teaches Teacher A person who studies the stars Astronomer A place where books are kept Library A person who writes poems Poet The killing of oneself Suicide The study of plants Botany SUMMARY WRITING Topic: Reading to Summarize in a Specific Number of Sentences Meaning Summary writing means expressing the main ideas of a passage in fewer words without changing the meaning. It requires reading comprehension and the ability to identify key points. Steps in Summary Writing 1. Read the passage carefully. 2. Identify the main ideas or topic sentences. 3. Underline key points and important facts. 4. Ignore examples, repetitions, or illustrations. 5. Write your summary in your own words. 6. Keep to the required number of sentences. Qualities of a Good Summary 1. Short and precise. 2. Written in your own words. 3. Includes only main ideas.

4. Maintains the writer’s original meaning. 5. Flows logically and clearly. Example Passage: Water is important for life. People use it for drinking, washing, cooking, and farming. Without water, living things cannot survive. Summary (in two sentences): Water is essential for all living things. It is used for drinking, cooking, and farming. Practice Task Read a passage of about 150 words and summarize it in five sentences. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Formal Letter – Letter of Request Meaning A letter of request is a formal letter written to ask for permission, assistance, or support from a person in authority — such as a principal, manager, or government officer. (a) Features of a Formal Letter Feature Explanation Writer’s Address Top right-hand corner (e.g. 12, Garki Road, Abuja). Date Below the address. Receiver’s Address Below on the left-hand side. Salutation Dear Sir/Madam, Heading/Subject Written in capital letters (e.g. REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE WITH SCHOOL PROJECT ). Introduction State who you are and your purpose for writing. Body Give full details of your request clearly and politely. Conclusion Express gratitude and expectation for a positive response. Closing Yours faithfully, Signature and Name (Signed) Musa Ibrahim (b) Language of a Formal Letter • Polite and respectful tone. • Clear and simple sentences. • No slang or contractions (e.g. use I am instead of I’m ). • Use formal words such as request , kindly , appreciate , assistance , consideration . • Maintain correct punctuation and spelling. Example: Letter of Request

12, Garki Road, Abuja. 2nd November, 2025. The Principal, Government Secondary School, Garki, Abuja. Dear Sir, REQUEST FOR PERMISSION TO USE THE SCHOOL HALL FOR DEBATE PRACTICE I am the president of the school debate club. On behalf of the members, I am writing to request permission to use the school hall every Wednesday between 3:00 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. for our debate practice. This request will enable us to prepare adequately for the forthcoming inter-school debate competition. We promise to handle the hall and its equipment with care. We shall be grateful if this request is granted. Thank you for your kind consideration. Yours faithfully, (Signed) Musa Ibrahim (President, Debate Club) Tips for Writing a Good Letter of Request 1. Be clear about what you are asking for. 2. Use formal, polite language. 3. Give reasons for your request. 4. Express gratitude at the end.
