subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH Topic: Vowels – /e/ and /ɜ:/ Meaning of Vowels Vowels are speech sounds produced without any obstruction of the air flow in the mouth. They are very important because every English word must contain a vowel sound. Short Vowel /e/ • The /e/ sound is a short vowel. • It is produced with the tongue in the middle front of the mouth. • The lips are slightly spread. Examples of /e/ Word Phonetic Form set /set/ bed /bed/ pen /pen/ men /men/ bread /bred/ send /send/ friend /frend/ letter /ˈletə/ Tip: /e/ is a short, light sound — do not say “ay” or “ee.” Long Vowel /ɜ:/ • The /ɜ:/ sound is a long vowel. • It is made with the tongue in the centre of the mouth. • The lips are slightly rounded. • It is usually spelt with “ir,” “ur,” “ear,” or “or.” Examples of /ɜ:/ Word Phonetic Form first /fɜ:st/ girl /gɜ:l/ learn /lɜ:n/ bird /bɜ:d/ nurse /nɜ:s/ early /ˈɜ:li/ world /wɜ:ld/ church /tʃɜ:tʃ/ Tip: The /ɜ:/ sound is long and steady—stretch it slightly.

Practice 1. Read and pronounce: o set – shirt, pen – burn, bed – bird, men – learn 2. Note the difference between short /e/ and long /ɜ:/ sounds. STRUCTURE Topic: Adverbial Phrases and Their Grammatical Functions Meaning An adverbial phrase is a group of words that acts as an adverb in a sentence. It tells how, when, where, or why an action happens. Examples of Adverbial Phrases Function Example Phrase Example Sentence Manner (how) in a hurry He left in a hurry. with great care She handled the baby with great care. Time (when) in the morning They go jogging in the morning. after the meeting We will discuss it after the meeting. Place (where) at the market Mother is at the market. on the table The book is on the table. Reason (why) because of the rain The match was postponed because of the rain. Frequency (how often) once in a week I visit her once in a week. Grammatical Functions of Adverbial Phrases 1. Modify verbs – tell how or when an action takes place. He spoke in a low voice. 2. Modify adjectives – describe the extent of a quality. The girl is very beautiful. 3. Modify other adverbs – show degree or manner. She danced too quickly for a beginner. 4. Provide additional information about actions or events. Exercise Underline the adverbial phrases in the sentences below: 1. The teacher arrived in the afternoon. 2. The children played with excitement. 3. My father works at night. 4. The man spoke in anger. 5. We met after the show. READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Reading Chapters of Books and Making Notes

Meaning This involves reading longer passages or chapters of books to understand and extract key ideas. After reading, you write notes or summaries in your own words to remember the main points. Purpose of Reading and Note-Making 1. To understand the main ideas in a chapter. 2. To remember important facts and details. 3. To prepare for examinations or discussions. 4. To make revision easier. 5. To improve your writing and comprehension skills. Steps for Effective Note-Making 1. Read the chapter carefully and identify key points. 2. Underline or highlight important ideas. 3. Write short notes using your own words. 4. Use headings and subheadings to organize ideas. 5. Avoid copying long sentences directly. 6. Review your notes to ensure they are clear. Example Topic: The Water Cycle Notes: • Water from rivers, lakes, and oceans evaporates. • Vapour forms clouds in the sky. • Clouds cool and produce rain. • Rain returns water to the earth. Always keep your notes neat, short, and easy to understand. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Formal Letter – Letter of Complaint Meaning A formal letter is a letter written to a person in authority or an official body, using formal language and structure. A letter of complaint is written to express dissatisfaction or report a problem. Features of a Formal Letter Feature Example/Explanation Writer’s Address Top right-hand corner (e.g. 10, Okoro Street, Enugu). Date Written below the address (e.g. 2nd November, 2025). Receiver’s Address Below on the left-hand side. Salutation Dear Sir/Madam, Heading/Subject In capital letters, e.g. COMPLAINT ABOUT BAD ROADS IN OUR AREA

Feature Example/Explanation Introduction State who you are and the reason for writing. Body Describe the problem clearly and politely. Give facts, dates, and examples. Conclusion State what you want the receiver to do (e.g. repair, investigate, refund). Closing Yours faithfully, Signature and Name (Signed) Aisha Bello Example: Letter of Complaint 10, Unity Road, Kaduna. 2nd November, 2025. The Manager, NEPA Office, Kaduna. Dear Sir, COMPLAINT ABOUT IRREGULAR ELECTRICITY SUPPLY I am writing to complain about the irregular supply of electricity in our area. For the past three months, we have experienced constant power failure, which has affected our businesses and daily activities. Many electrical appliances have been damaged as a result of sudden power surges. We have reported this issue several times, but no action has been taken. I, therefore, appeal to your office to look into this matter urgently and ensure that regular power supply is restored to our area. Thank you for your prompt attention. Yours faithfully, (Signed) Aisha Bello Tips for Writing a Good Letter of Complaint 1. Be polite but firm. 2. State the problem clearly. 3. Give facts and examples. 4. Suggest a solution if possible. 5. Keep the letter short and formal.

title: REGISTER OF TRAVELLING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Week 8 ( Speech) Unit Topic; Intonation Pattern. Lesson Topic; Rising and Falling tunes. Intonation is the variation of pitch of voice used in making Intelligible communication. It gives special meaning and utterances. Functions; Intonation is used in two major ways; 1. Grammatical Function; This is used to differentiate between specific type, declarative, interrogative, polar questions e.t.c e.g When a speaker wants to give information, a falling tune is used. 2. Attitudinal Function; This attitude can be that of surprise, doubt, sarcasm, warm interest, indifference, disbelief, uncertainty e.t.c. Types of intonation i. Falling tone (ii) Rising tone (iii) Fall-Rise tone. 1. The falling tone; This is used to indicate the fall in pitch of a speaker voice, in writing, we use the downward arrow to show a sentence uttered with the falling tone Uses of the falling tone i. The falling tone is use to make statement e.g We shall all pass English ii. The teacher is coming iii. Abuja is the capital of Nigeria 2. The falling tone is use to command e.g i. Shut the door ii. Keep the book on my table iii.Dont disobey your parents 3. The falling tone is used to make exclamation e.g

i. What a pleasant surprise ii. How lovely she works iii. Wow, that’s great indeed 4. WH-questions e.g when are you coming? ii. Why are you late to school? iii. Where does he lives? 2. The Rising tone; This is used to indicate a rise in the pitch of a speaker voice begins from the first stressed syllable until it reaches the highest peak. If there are unstressed syllable at the end of the sentences, the syllables are said with the rising tone to maintain the rise in pitch. Uses of the rising tone 1.Questions requiring Yes or No answer e.g i. Did she pass ii. Are you coming iii. Will you go to lagos? 2. Questions that shows warm personal interest e.g i. Have you taken anything since you came? ii. Will you still leave today? 3.For simple polite request; e.g i. Please come in (warm reception)

ii. May I borrow your book please 4. For greetings e.g i.Good morning sir ii. Complement of the season 5. To indicate uncertainty e.g i. Will John come to school tomorrow? I think so ii. They may call of strike tomorrow 6. For incomplete statement; e.g i. While they were playing ( Dayo was reading) 7. For surprise,disbelief,doubt e.g i. (Ada is a witch) Really? ii. ( Musa is a millionaire) You must be joking 3. The rise and fall tone; This tone is an enumerating items, Here, the pitch begins to rise on each of the items listed while the last item receive the falling tone, e.g one, two three and five. Go to the hall with a pen, a pencil, a ruler, and eraser. Assignment Look at the following sentences, indicate ones that should have falling tone with the downward arrow and rising tone with upward arrow. 1. There was inferior in London last week 2. Our school is the best in Nigeria 3. Are you sure of what you are saying

4. There are a lot of books in the study 5. Do you think he can dance 6. I am glad you are here 7. Too many cooks spoil the both 8. Get out of my sight 9. That all we have for today 10. Have a pleasant weekend. Week 8 (Vocabulary development) Unit topic; Vocabulary development Lesson Topic; Words associated with travelling Travelling is the act of embarking on a journey, leaving a place to another far place by road, rail, sea, or air. The person (s) has his baggage or luggage, briefcase, bag, boxes e.t.c. in which he parked his personal belongings or the trip. Words associated with travelling (1). Motor park garage; A Place where vehicles are parked and passengers board available vehicle for travelling (2). Passengers; These are people travelling or making journey. (3). Transport fare; This is the money paid by travelers to owner of the vehicle (4). Luggage; A personal belonging of a passenger. (5). Licensed driver; A person who has a licsense to drive a vehicle after being tested (6). High way; Express main road (7). Particulars; Vehicles and driving document (8). Radiator; A device for cooling and circulating water especially in a car

(9). Vulcanizer; Equipment used for the vulcanization of rubber/tyre (10). Road worthy; When a vehicle is in a good worthy (11). Mileage.; The number of miles traveled by a vehicle on a certain volume of fuel (12). Petrol station; A place where vehicles are fueled. (13). Trunk road; An important main road used by long distance traffic as well as heavy lorries. Types and parts of vehicles A. Types of vehicles; cars, bicycle, lorry, bus, trailer, pick-up, vans, motor cicle, saloon, station wagon, sport car, jeep, mini bus, van e.t.c. B. Part of motor vehicle; Wind screen, bonnet, trunk engine, bumpers, headlight, steering, wheel, speedometer, horn, brake. e.t.c. C. The road; high way, ring road, T-junction, Y-junction, cross road, roundabout, gutter, traffic, culvert, bend, bridge, sharp bend. e.t.c. Assignment 1. Answer any question on lexis and structure as relate to travelling contained in the WAEC past questions and answers 2. Use the following words in sentence; high way, flat tyre, wiper, roundabout, traffic, road accident Week 8 (Comprehension) Unit topic; Comprehension Unit lesson; Reading to paraphrase a poem. Stanly meets mutesa by Darid Rubadri pg 140 unit 12 Week 8 (Summary) Unit topic; Reading to summarize an argumentative passage Lesson topic; Teachers are more important than Doctors a sample debate in pg 35

The argumentative summarization require you to summarize the argument FOR or AGAINST what is discussed in the passage. In this case, you only have to shortened the points which writer makes in the writer makes in the passage A Teacher is an expert who is capable of imparting knowledge, that will help learners to build, identify, and to aquire skills that will be used to face the challenge in life. A Doctor is a health professional who practices medicine, which is concerned in promoting, maintaining or restoring health through Points to support -Teachers impart knowledge to all leaners of different field -Teachers guide and encourage students -Teachers prepare students for the future Points to oppose. -Doctors saves lives -Doctors control the epidemics e.g covid 19, cholera e.t.c. -Doctors care for patients including teachers Assignment In four sentences,summarise the role of a teacher in our society.

rawText:
Week 10 (Structure) Unit topic; Phrasal verb Lesson topic; Phrasal verbs with more than one particles. A phrasal verb is a group of two or three words that begins a verb and is followed by a particle. The particle can be an adverb or preposition. example; Grew up, turn out Work after, apply for ran in to, think about. Phrasal verb can be in the following format 1. Verbs + Adverb e.g put heavily walk quietly speak kindly 2. Verbs + Preposition e.g look on come across go over put up come round come off come after see to 3. Three words phrasal verb e.g look forward to come back to

come away with catch up with stick out to tune in to look down on give in to put up with go in for Features of phrasal verbs 1. It consist of two or three words 2. The first word is a verb 3. The second word is either an adverb or preposition. Phrasal verbs can have both literal/denotative and idiomatic/connotative meaning Phrasal verbs Literal meaning Idiomatic meaning Sentence Break down To stop functioning To start crying She break down when she see her score in mathematics Speak out Talk audibly To stop complaint The staff decided to speak against suspension of their president Take off To remove To go in to the air The plain did not take off until midnight Turn down To reduce volume To reject His offer was turned down

Call out Mention To announce The teacher call out their names Look up To look towards the sky/ceiling To check information We need to look up for the meaning of the words in dictionary Put away To remove from sight To jail or put something in an enclosure The animal was finally put away Separable phrasal verbs Some phrasal verbs are separable by inserting an object in between them e.g 1. The widow brought up her son well The widow brought her son up well. 2. He picked up the baby He picked the baby up However, some phrasal verbs are inseparable i.e the verb and the article can never be separated. Inseparable verbs are marked with an asterisk. Example; *. Rotten fish gives off a bad smell. Rotten fish gives a bad smell off. Some phrasal verb and their meaning 1. Come about – happened call at – to visit 2. Come across – find call for – to require 3. Come by – obtain call off – to cancel 4. Come in – to be received call out – to announce 5. Come forward – to be identify 6. Come around – regain consciousness

7. Come through – to survive 8. Come to – to add up 9. Check out – leave 10. Check in – arrive 11. Hear out – listen to the end 12. Long for – to desire something clearly 13. Get over – recover from a shock or surprise Give away – to reveal a secret Give in – surrender Give up – to stop Cut off – disconnect Cut up – slice Come up-with – to reveal or disclose Dress down – to scold severely Set in – to commence. Assignment Exercise 2 pg 169 of of their text book, new concept English. title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH Topic: Listening Comprehension – Listening for Details/Examples Meaning Listening comprehension is the ability to understand and interpret spoken information. When you listen for details , you focus on specific facts, names, dates, numbers, or examples mentioned in a passage or recording. Skills Needed 1. Concentration: Pay full attention while listening. 2. Note-taking: Write down key points and examples. 3. Memory: Recall details such as figures, names, or reasons. 4. Understanding relationships: Note how ideas are connected. How to Listen for Details 1. Listen carefully to the introduction —it often gives the topic. 2. Identify the main points and examples that support them. 3. Write short notes while listening. 4. Focus on who, what, when, where, how, and why . 5. Check your answers after the second reading (if allowed). Example Passage Summary: The teacher explained that HIV/AIDS can be prevented by abstinence, faithfulness, and use of clean needles . She added that drug abuse destroys health and future dreams. Sample Questions: 1. Mention two ways of preventing HIV/AIDS. 2. What did the teacher say about drug abuse? Answers: 1. Abstinence and use of clean needles. 2. It destroys health and future dreams. Tips • Don’t try to write every word. • Listen for examples and illustrations . • Review your notes before answering. VOCABULARY Topic: Spelling of Words 1. Treatment of Commonly Misspelt Words Common spelling errors come from wrong pronunciation or confusion of similar-sounding words. Below are some examples and corrections: Wrong Spelling Correct Spelling Meaning beleive believe to have faith recieve receive to get something

Wrong Spelling Correct Spelling Meaning seperate separate to divide occassion occasion event accomodate accommodate to provide lodging definately definitely without doubt enviroment environment surroundings goverment government ruling authority adress address location or speech occured occurred happened Tips for Correct Spelling 1. Sound out the word slowly. 2. Break it into syllables (e.g. ac-com-mo-date). 3. Use mnemonics (e.g. “I before E except after C” → believe, receive). 4. Practise writing difficult words repeatedly. 5. Read widely —seeing words often helps you remember correct spellings. 2. Dictation Exercise and Correction In a dictation test: • Listen carefully to each sentence. • Write what you hear. • Afterward, check for spelling and punctuation errors. • Correct mistakes neatly and learn the correct forms. 3. Use of Dictionary A dictionary is a book (or digital tool) that lists words alphabetically and gives their meanings, spellings, pronunciations, and usage . Functions of a Dictionary 1. Helps to check correct spelling of words. 2. Gives meanings and examples of use . 3. Shows word class (noun, verb, adjective, etc.). 4. Gives pronunciation using phonetic symbols. 5. Shows plural and past forms of words. Example: Word: accommodate • Part of speech: verb • Meaning: to provide a place to stay or to adjust. • Example: The hotel can accommodate fifty guests. Dictionary Skills • Arrange words alphabetically (A–Z). • Use guide words at the top of dictionary pages. • Study the phonetic symbols to improve pronunciation.

SUMMARY WRITING Topic: Reading to Summarize Longer Selections into a Specific Number of Sentences Meaning Summary writing means presenting the main ideas of a passage in short and clear sentences . When asked to summarize into a specific number of sentences , you must keep to that number exactly. Steps for Writing a Good Summary 1. Read the passage carefully to understand the main idea. 2. Identify key points and ignore unnecessary details or examples. 3. Paraphrase —write in your own words. 4. Combine related ideas into one sentence if possible. 5. Count your sentences to match the required number. 6. Write in continuous prose (no bullet points). Example Passage Summary Instruction: Summarize this passage in three sentences. Passage: Regular exercise keeps the body strong and healthy. It helps the heart and muscles work well. Exercise also prevents diseases and improves sleep. Summary (Three Sentences): Regular exercise makes the body fit and strong. It improves the heart and muscles. It also helps prevent diseases and aids good sleep. Tips • Use simple, short sentences. • Avoid personal opinions. • Do not repeat words or phrases from the passage. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Narrative Essay Meaning A narrative essay tells a story or event , real or imagined, in a clear and orderly way. It aims to entertain, inform, or teach a lesson . Features of a Narrative Essay Feature Explanation Title Should relate to the story (e.g., The Day I Will Never Forget ). Introduction Introduce the setting, main characters, and situation. Body (Events) Tell the events in logical order (beginning → middle → end). Climax The most exciting or emotional part of the story. Conclusion How the story ends or the lesson learned.

Feature Explanation Language Use past tense, connectives (then, later, suddenly), and descriptive words. Example Opening: It was a bright Monday morning when I left home for school. I had no idea that the day would change my life forever. Tips for Writing a Good Narrative Essay 1. Use past tense verbs. 2. Make your story realistic and interesting . 3. Arrange events in chronological order . 4. Include dialogue to make it lively. 5. End with a lesson or reflection . Example Topics 1. The Day I Will Never Forget 2. How I Saved a Friend 3. My First Day in Boarding School 4. An Unexpected Visitor

Week 7 (structure) Unit Topic; Adverbs Lesson Topic; Comparism and functisons of Adverbs. An adverb is a word that modifies or qualifies an adjectives, verb or other adverb, Or a group of words expressing a relationship of place, time, circumstances, manner, causes degree e.t.c. E.g quickly, beautiful, foolishly, wisely, well, enough, much, soon, quiet. e.t.c. Adverb have three degrees of comparism which are the positive, comparative and suparative. Adverb which ends in ;ly, have their comparative and suparative formed by adding more and most. Example; (A) POSITIVE COMPARATIVE SUPARATIVE Quickly More quickly Most quickluy Dangerously More dangerously Most dangerously Slowly More slowly Most slowly Fortunately More fortunately Most fortunately Carefully More carefully Most carefully Excitedly More excitedly Most excitedly Foolishly More foolishly Most foolishly Rampanthy More rampanthy Most rampanthy Beautifully More beautifully Most beautifully Sensibly More sensibly Most sensibly Rashly More rashly Most rashly

B. Regular adverbs Fake ier; and est in forming their comparative and suparative. e.g Early earlier earliest Soon Sooner Soonest HarD HARDER HARDEST FAST FASTER FASTEST FAR FATHER/FURTER FATHEST/FURTHEST C. IRREGULAR ADVERB TAKE THE SAME FORM OF COMPARISM AS ADJECTIVES EXAMPLES; MUCH MORE MOST LITTLE LESS LEAST WELL BETTER BEST BADLY WORSE WORST Functions of adverbs. (1). As modifiers of adjectives (a). Joy is far more beautiful than her sister Ada (The adverbial phrase ;far more; modifies adjectives beautiful) (b). This is good enough (enough modifies the adjective good (c). The girl is too fat for her age (Too modifies the adjective fat) (2). As modifiers of order adverbs. (a). The train was extremely fast (extremely modifies the adverb fast) (b)The girl danced very well at the party (very modifies the adverbs ;well;) (c). Amina cook really well, ( really modifies the adverb well)

(3). As modifiers of preposition phrase (a). We are quite on time for the party, (quite modifies on time). (b).The driver stopped right in the middle of the road, (right modifies the prepositional phrase in the middle of the road) (c). Peter was left behind in the race,(behind modifies in the race). (4). As modifiers of noun phrases. (a). He told such a funny story that everyone laughed (such modifies a funny story) (b). It was rather a sorry sight ( rather modifies a sorry sight) (c). The meeting yesterday was a big success ( Yesterday modifies the meeting) 5. Adverb modifies verb ASSIGNMENT USE THE FOLLOWING ADVERBS IN SENTENCE. (1). FOOLISHLY (2). FORTUNATELY (3). SOON (4) TOO (5) EARLIER (6) MOST SENSIBLY (7) ENOUGH (8) QUIET (9) EXTREMELY (10) RATHER. Week 7 (Summary) Unit Topic; Summary Writing Lesson Topic; Reading To Summarize A Given Passage; The Wealthy Man; Pg 40-41 (Unit 4) Summary Simply Means Writing A Long Prose In Such A Way That The Important Points In The Original Passage Will Still Be Retained In Your Own Much Short Form.

Point About The Passage -The Passage Talks About The Experience Of A Traveller. -In The Passage The Attribute Of Human Being Are Given To Animals. -The Traveller Who Is Also The Narrator Has A Gift Ready For A Host (Ess) -The Host Are Indians and Americans. Assignment In four sentence, one for each summarize the experience that surprise the narrator. Week 7 ( Continuous writing) Unit topic; Letter writing Lesson topic; Semi-formal letters Semi-formal letters are letters we write to people who are not total strangers to us but are not close enough to deserve a personal letter, the people may be older or younger than we are. The are people like our teachers, parents, friends, distant uncles and aunts, elderly neighbours, house masters, e.t.c. We can also write such letters to people we admire, such as foot ball stars, filmstars, famous singers. Semi formal lettrs are closer to informal letters. Features of semi-formal letters 1. Writer address-; Semi –formal letters only require the writers address and date, It does not require receivers address or any heading e.g Government secondary school, Kubwa, Abuja. 26 Febuary,2018 2. Salutation; The greeting is usually ; Dear; name of the person you are writing to. Example; Dear Mr Bode, Dear uncle Smart, Dear Miss Eze, Dear Dr Akpan e.t.c.

3. Body of the letter; This depends on the topic or what the question demands You must discuss it fully to get a good letter, your paragraphs and sentences must be well linked 4.Complemntary close; Use Yours sincerely only and write your two names fully. Signature is not necessary, but if you wish to, you can sign. Example; Yours sincerely James Okeke

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH Topic: Vowel Sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ (e.g. full and fool , would and coup ) Meaning Vowels are sounds made when air passes freely through the mouth without any obstruction. The vowel sounds /ʊ/ and /uː/ are both back vowels, but they differ in length and tongue position. Short Vowel /ʊ/ • It is a short and lax vowel sound. • The tongue is raised near the back of the mouth. • The lips are rounded but not tightly. • It occurs in words like book, good, full, put, would. Examples: Word Phonetic Meaning full /fʊl/ not empty pull /pʊl/ drag towards you could /kʊd/ past of can look /lʊk/ to see put /pʊt/ to place something Long Vowel /uː/ • It is a long and tense vowel sound. • The tongue is slightly higher and the lips are strongly rounded. • It occurs in words like food, fool, school, mood, coup. Examples: Word Phonetic Meaning fool /fuːl/ a silly person food /fuːd/ what we eat school /skuːl/ a place of learning true /truː/ correct or real coup /kuː/ sudden takeover of government Minimal Pairs (/ʊ/ vs /uː/) /ʊ/ /uː/ full fool pull pool could cooled look Luke cook cool Note: The /uː/ sound is longer and more rounded than /ʊ/.

Practice Exercise Pronounce these words in pairs: full–fool, could–cooled, pull–pool, look–Luke. Listen carefully to the length of the vowel sound. READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Word Substitution in Passages Meaning Word substitution means using one word to replace a group of words or a phrase that has the same meaning. It helps to make writing shorter, clearer, and more interesting. It also improves vocabulary and reading comprehension. Examples of Common Word Substitutions Phrase One Word A place where books are kept Library A person who studies plants Botanist A person who studies animals Zoologist A place where sick people are treated Hospital A person who writes poems Poet A person who steals Thief The killing of oneself Suicide The killing of a king Regicide A place where money is kept Bank A person who flies an aircraft Pilot One who sells medicines Pharmacist A person who makes clothes Tailor A person who writes novels Novelist Tips for Understanding Word Substitution in Passages 1. Read the sentence or passage carefully. 2. Find the meaning or description of the word. 3. Replace the phrase with the most suitable single word. 4. Ensure the word fits grammatically and logically. Example Exercise Passage: A person who treats our teeth visited our school last week to teach us oral hygiene. Answer: A dentist visited our school last week to teach us oral hygiene.

Practice Activity Replace the underlined parts with one word: 1. A person who repairs cars is a _______. 2. A person who acts in a film is an _______. 3. A person who cuts hair is a _______. 4. A person who leads prayers in a mosque is an _______. 5. A person who treats sick animals is a _______. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Revision — Formal Letters (Types: Letter of Complaint, Request, Application, and Apology) Meaning A formal letter is an official letter written to a person in authority, such as a principal, manager, or government official. It follows a standard format and uses formal language. Features of a Formal Letter Feature Description Writer’s Address Top right-hand corner Date Below the address Receiver’s Address Below on the left Salutation “Dear Sir” or “Dear Madam” Heading/Subject Written in capital letters Introduction State who you are and purpose of writing Body Give details clearly and politely Conclusion Express appreciation or expectation Closing “Yours faithfully,” followed by your name and signature Letter of Complaint Purpose: To express dissatisfaction about something (e.g., poor service, damaged goods). Example Heading: COMPLAINT ABOUT SPOILT PRODUCTS SUPPLIED TO OUR SCHOOL CANTEEN Key Expressions: • I wish to bring to your attention... • I am dissatisfied with... • I hope this issue will be resolved promptly. Letter of Request Purpose: To ask for permission, help, or information. Example Heading: REQUEST FOR USE OF SCHOOL HALL FOR DEBATE PRACTICE

Key Expressions: • I am writing to request... • Kindly grant us permission to... • I shall be grateful if this request is approved. Letter of Application Purpose: To apply for a job, admission, or scholarship. Example Heading: APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF SCHOOL LIBRARIAN Key Expressions: • I wish to apply for the position... • I possess the required qualifications... • I look forward to your favourable consideration. Letter of Apology Purpose: To express regret for a mistake or offence. Example Heading: LETTER OF APOLOGY FOR ABSENCE FROM SCHOOL Key Expressions: • I sincerely apologize for... • It was not my intention to... • I assure you it will not happen again. Language Features of Formal Letters • Use polite and respectful tone. • Avoid slang or contractions (use I am not I’m ). • Use clear and simple sentences. • Be concise and factual. Sample: Letter of Apology 10, Independence Road, Kaduna. 2nd November, 2025. The Principal, Government Secondary School, Kaduna. Dear Sir, LETTER OF APOLOGY FOR MISSING SCHOOL ASSEMBLY I sincerely apologize for not attending the school assembly on Monday, 27th October 2025. I had a sudden stomach pain and could not leave home early enough. It was not intentional, and I assure you that I will always attend future assemblies on time. I am very sorry for any inconvenience caused. Thank you for your understanding. Yours faithfully, (Signed) Ibrahim Musa

Classwork / Practice 1. Write a formal letter complaining about the delay in delivery of textbooks your school ordered. 2. Write a letter of application for the post of library assistant in your school. 3. Write a letter of apology to your class teacher for not submitting your homework on time.

title: ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY DEFINITION Argumentative writing is a type of essay in which the writer attempts to make the reader or audience accept his views as a valid option. It can also be defined as a type of writing that involves expression of one’s independent views or opinion on a topic that has been opened to a debate. NATURE OF AN ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY SIDES TO EVERY ARGUMENT There are two sides to every argument. 1. The Proposition which is the side to argue in favour or support of a given topic. 2. The Opposition which is the side to present opinion against the topic. FEATURES OF AN ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY. A) It requires no topic. The motion moved represents the topic and the speaker’s interest.(speak for or against). B) INTRODUCTION For instance, in a school setting, one can have the following introduction : The Principal, Vice Principal, members of Staff, invited guests, panel of Judges, accurate time keeper, co debaters and fellow students. I am here to speak against the motion which states that…………. C) Body of the Essay. This is a focus to back up points for your motion. E.g. provision of infrastructural facilities, To debate a point. To defend an idea, policy or proposal. To defend an accused in a court of law. To convince your parents or others to do certain things

promotion of games, etc. in short, you must support or oppose with valid reasons and figures if need be.  The use of apt words i.e relevant registers or vocabularies and phrases as the case may be is very important. Whichever stand you intend to take, the use ofpersuation is very important.  There must be clarity of argument.  There must be logical presentation of ideas or points. That is, the essay must be well organized to attract valuable marks from the examiner. D) Conclusion: In concluding this type of essay, reference must be made to your listeners while giving a summary of all your points. A typical conclusion may end like this: The Principal, Vice Principal, Panel of Judges, Ladies and Gentlemen and my Listeners, I hope you will all agree with my logical presentation of views that …………….. MORE TECHNIQUES  Audience inclusion  Alliteration  Acknowledging the opposing view….. then showing that it is wrong’  Use powerful language to really get your point across.  Use a variety of sentence types and lengths.

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText:
SPEECH Topic: Vowel Sounds /ɪ/ and /iː/ (e.g. bit and beat , bid and bead ) Meaning Vowel sounds are speech sounds produced without any obstruction of air from the mouth. In English, there is a short vowel /ɪ/ and a long vowel /iː/. The length of the sound (short or long) changes the meaning of words. 1. The Short Vowel /ɪ/ • It is a short sound. • The tongue is slightly raised, and the lips are spread a little. • Common in words spelled with “i” or “y”. Examples: Word Phonetic Meaning bit /bɪt/ small piece sit /sɪt/ to be seated ship /ʃɪp/ vessel on water live /lɪv/ to exist pick /pɪk/ choose or select 2. The Long Vowel /iː/ • It is a long sound. • The tongue is higher and more forward. • The lips are spread wider. Examples: Word Phonetic Meaning beat /biːt/ strike repeatedly seat /siːt/ chair or place to sit sheep /ʃiːp/ animal that gives wool

Word Phonetic Meaning leave /liːv/ go away peek /piːk/ look quickly 3. Minimal Pairs These are pairs of words that differ in only one sound (here, /ɪ/ and /iː/). /ɪ/ /iː/ bit beat sit seat live leave lick leak fill feel ship sheep Practice: Pronounce both words in each pair carefully. Notice how the long sound /iː/ is held longer than /ɪ/. STRUCTURE Topic: Determiners (e.g. few, many, some, a little, etc.) Meaning A determiner is a word that comes before a noun to show quantity, possession, or definiteness. It helps specify which, how many, or whose noun we are talking about. Types and Examples of Determiners Type Examples Usage Quantifiers some, many, few, a little, much, several Show quantity or amount Articles a, an, the Indicate definiteness Demonstratives this, that, these, those Point out nouns Possessives my, your, his, her, our, their Show ownership

Type Examples Usage Numbers one, two, first, second Indicate number or order Examples in Sentences 1. Some students are absent today. 2. There are many books on the shelf. 3. She has a little sugar left. 4. Few people attended the meeting. 5. This house is very old. 6. My father bought a new car. A few Some (positive idea) A few students passed the exam. Little Almost none (negative idea) There is little water in the bucket. A little Some (positive idea) There is a little water left. READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Reading for Critical Evaluation Meaning Reading for critical evaluation means analyzing and judging what you read to decide if it is true, fair, logical, and useful. It is reading beyond the surface, to assess the writer’s ideas, arguments, and opinions. Skills Required 1. Identify facts and opinions – Know what can be proven and what is just a belief. 2. Examine arguments – Check if the points are logical and supported by evidence. 3. Detect bias – Identify if the writer is being unfair or one-sided.

4. Check tone – Determine if the language is emotional, persuasive, or neutral. 5. Evaluate conclusions – See if they are based on facts or assumptions. Example Passage: “Television damages children’s learning because they spend all their time watching cartoons.” Critical Evaluation: • Is it true that all children spend all their time on TV? (Generalization) • Are there studies or facts to support the claim? (Evidence) • What is the writer’s tone — angry, persuasive, or neutral? A good reader questions and evaluates before agreeing or disagreeing. Practice: Read an article and answer: 1. What is the writer’s main argument? 2. What facts or evidence are used? 3. Do you agree with the writer? Why or why not? CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Formal Letter (Other Types) Examples: Application, Apology, Order, etc. 1. Features of a Formal Letter 1. Writer’s Address – Top right-hand corner. 2. Date – Below the address. 3. Receiver’s Address – Left-hand side. 4. Salutation – “Dear Sir/Madam.” 5. Heading/Subject – States the purpose of the letter. 6. Introduction – State who you are and why you’re writing. 7. Body – Give full details clearly and politely. 8. Conclusion – End with appreciation or expectation.

9. Closing – “Yours faithfully,” followed by signature and name. 2. Types and Examples (a) Application Letter Purpose: To apply for a job, scholarship, or position. Language: Formal, polite, persuasive. Example Heading: APPLICATION FOR THE POST OF SCHOOL LIBRARIAN Sample Sentence: “I wish to apply for the position of School Librarian as advertised in the Daily Times of 20th October, 2025.” (b) Letter of Apology Purpose: To express regret for a mistake or wrongdoing. Language: Polite, sincere, and respectful. Example Heading: LETTER OF APOLOGY FOR MISSING SCHOOL EXAM Sample Sentence: “I sincerely apologize for my inability to attend the examination due to ill health.” (c) Letter of Order Purpose: To request goods or services from a company. Language: Formal, clear, specific. Example Heading: ORDER FOR STATIONERY MATERIALS Sample Sentence: “We wish to order the following items: 10 reams of A4 paper, 5 boxes of pens, and 3 office staplers.” 3. Language Features of Formal Letters • No contractions (write I am not I’m ). • Polite and respectful tone. • Simple and clear sentences. • Use formal vocabulary (e.g., “Kindly,” “Request,” “Assistance,” “Consideration”).

Dear Sir, APPLICATION FOR THE POSITION OF SALES ATTENDANT I wish to apply for the position of Sales Attendant in your supermarket as advertised in the Daily Trust newspaper of October 25, 2025. I am a graduate of Government Secondary School, Kano, and I possess good communication skills and experience in customer service. I am hardworking, honest, and ready to learn. I would be grateful if my application is given favourable consideration. Thank you for your time and kind attention. Yours faithfully, (Signed) Amina Yusuf

SPEECH Topic: Consonant Clusters (Two Consonants in Initial Position) Meaning A consonant cluster is a group of two or more consonants that appear together without a vowel sound between them. When the cluster occurs at the beginning of a word, it is called an initial consonant cluster. Examples of Two-Consonant Clusters in Initial Position Cluster Example Words Pronunciation /sl/ slice, slow, slip, sleep /slaɪs/, /sləʊ/, /slɪp/, /sliːp/ /tr/ tree, train, truck, tribe /triː/, /treɪn/, /trʌk/, /traɪb/ /sk/ sky, skip, scalp, skate /skaɪ/, /skɪp/, /skælp/, /skeɪt/ /kl/ cloud, clean, class, clock /klaʊd/, /kliːn/, /klɑːs/, /klɒk/ /kr/ crush, cry, cross, cream /krʌʃ/, /kraɪ/, /krɒs/, /kriːm/ /bl/ blue, blow, block, blame /bluː/, /bləʊ/, /blɒk/, /bleɪm/ /pl/ play, please, plane, plum /pleɪ/, /pliːz/, /pleɪn/, /plʌm/ /gr/ green, grow, grass, group /griːn/, /grəʊ/, /grɑːs/, /gruːp/ Pronunciation Tips 1. Do not add a vowel sound between the two consonants. “suh-lice” → “slice” 2. Say both consonant sounds clearly but quickly. 3. Practice slowly at first, then increase speed for fluency. Class Activity Pronounce and write 5 words each with the following clusters: /sl/, /tr/, /kl/, /pl/, /gr/ VOCABULARY Topic: Modifiers (Word Modifiers)

Meaning A modifier is a word or group of words that describe or add meaning to another word in a sentence. Modifiers tell how, when, where, what kind, or to what extent something happens. The two main types of word modifiers are: 1. Adjectives – modify nouns or pronouns. 2. Adverbs – modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs. 1. Adjectives (Modifiers of Nouns) Adjectives describe the quality, colour, size, shape, or quantity of nouns. (a) Adjectives of Colour • red dress • blue sky • green leaf • black shoes • white house (b) Adjectives of Size or Smallness • small boy • tiny insect • little baby • short rope • narrow road 2. Adverbs (Modifiers of Verbs, Adjectives, or Adverbs) (a) Adverbs of Manner (how an action is done) Examples: slowly, quickly, neatly, carefully, loudly, silently She spoke softly. He ran quickly to school. (b) Adverbs of Frequency or Rate of Occurrence (how often) Examples: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never They always pray before eating. I sometimes go to the market.

(c) Adverbs of Degree (to what extent) Examples: very, too, quite, almost, extremely, rather The soup is too hot. She is very intelligent. Summary Table Type Function Examples Adjective of Colour Describes colour red, blue, white Adjective of Size Describes smallness/size little, tiny, small Adverb of Manner Describes how an action is done carefully, quickly Adverb of Frequency Describes how often always, rarely Adverb of Degree Describes extent very, too, quite SUMMARY WRITING Topic: Reading to Summarize Longer Sentences into a Specified Number of Sentences Meaning Summary writing is the process of shortening a passage by expressing only the main ideas in fewer sentences and in your own words. It involves reading, understanding, and rewriting long or detailed sentences in a brief and clear form. Steps in Summary Writing 1. Read the passage carefully. 2. Understand the main ideas in each sentence. 3. Ignore examples, illustrations, and repetitions. 4. Combine related ideas where necessary. 5. Rewrite in your own words using simple language. 6. Follow the number of sentences required in the question. Example

Original Sentence (long): The teacher who taught us last term was very strict, but he helped us to pass our examination because he always gave us difficult exercises. Summary (shorter sentence): The strict teacher helped us to pass our examination. Tips for Good Summary Writing • Use simple and short sentences. • Avoid examples and quotations. • Do not copy long phrases directly. • Stick to the number of sentences asked for. • Keep your summary brief and accurate. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Argumentative Essay Meaning An argumentative essay is a type of essay in which the writer gives reasons for or against a topic, using facts, logic, and examples to persuade the reader. Features of an Argumentative Essay 1. Introduction – state the topic and your stand (for or against). 2. Body Paragraphs – present arguments (each paragraph for one point). 3. Opposing View – mention and refute the other side’s argument. 4. Conclusion – restate your position firmly. 5. Language – formal, logical, and persuasive. a) Topic: Should Female Circumcision Be Abolished? Introduction: Female circumcision, also known as female genital mutilation (FGM), is an ancient practice in some communities. While some people see it as a cultural tradition, others believe it is harmful and should be stopped. This essay argues that female circumcision should be abolished because it is dangerous and violates human rights.

Main Points (For Abolition): 1. It causes severe pain and health complications. 2. It can lead to infections, bleeding, and even death. 3. It denies women their right to bodily integrity. 4. It has no medical or religious benefit. Conclusion: Female circumcision should be completely abolished because it endangers the lives and dignity of women. b) Topic: Military Rule Is Better Than Civilian Rule Introduction: Government can be led either by the military or by civilians. Some people believe that military rule is better because it brings discipline and order, while others prefer civilian rule for its democracy and freedom. This essay argues that civilian rule is better than military rule. Main Points (Against Military Rule): 1. Military rule denies citizens their rights and freedom. 2. Soldiers often rule by force and fear. 3. There is no accountability or free election under military regimes. 4. Civilian rule promotes democracy and development. Conclusion: Although military governments may appear strong, civilian rule is better because it respects the people’s rights and encourages progress. Useful Expressions in Argumentative Essays • Firstly / Secondly / Finally • On the other hand • In conclusion • It is clear that... • I strongly believe that...

title: PREFIX
subject: English Language
rawText: English Language Class: VEI2/ SS2 Topic: Prefixes Prefix is a letter or letters added to the start of words to change their meaning - Examples: un-, re-, pre-, dis-, co-, ante etc Common Prefixes & Meanings 1. un-: not (e.g., unhappy = not happy) 2. re-: again (e.g., rewrite = write again) 3. pre-: before (e.g., prepaid = paid before) 4. dis-: not/opposite (e.g., dislike = not like) 5. co-: together (e.g., cooperate = work together) How do Prefixes Work? -They change word meanings: happy → unhappy (opposite) -They add to root words: appear → disappear (different meaning) Examples - un- + known = unknown (not known) - re- + play = replay (play again) - dis- + agree = disagree (not agree) Why Prefixes Matter - Improve vocabulary 🠀 - Help understand unfamiliar words 🔍 - Boost reading and writing skills 📚 Assignment 1. Add prefixes: _____happy, _____do, _____view 2. Use in sentences: unwell, prepaid, cooperate

rawText:
English Language VTC 2 Topic: Unstressed Vowel Sounds Definition: Unstressed vowel sounds refer to vowel sounds that are pronounced with less emphasis or stress in a word or sentence. Examples 1. Schwa Sound (/ə/): a neutral, relaxed vowel sound often found in unstressed syllables (e.g., "about," "sofa"). 2. Reduced Vowels: vowels that are pronounced with less clarity or duration in unstressed syllables (e.g., "banana" /bəˈnɑːnə/). Importance 1. Pronunciation: Understanding unstressed vowel sounds is essential for accurate pronunciation. 2. Intonation: Recognizing unstressed vowel sounds helps with intonation and stress patterns in speech. More Words with the Schwa Sound (/ə/) Examples 1. About /əˈbaʊt/ 2. Sofa /ˈsoʊfə/ 3. Banana /bəˈnɑːnə/ 4. Cousin /ˈkʌzən/ 5. Pencil /ˈpɛnsəl/ 6. Lesson /ˈlɛsən/ 7. Doctor /ˈdɒktər/ 8. Computer /kəmˈpjuːtər/ 9. Around /əˈraʊnd/ 10. Support /səˈpɔːrt/

Tips 1. Listen Carefully: Pay attention to the schwa sound in words. 2. Practice Pronunciation: Practice pronouncing words with the schwa sound. 3. Record Yourself: Record yourself speaking and listen for the schwa sound. By practicing words with the schwa sound, you can improve your pronunciation and fluency in English.

title: GRAMMAR
subject: English Language
rawText:
Subject-Verb Concord You already know what ‘subject’ and ‘ verb ‘ are in a sentence. ‘Subject’ is a noun or pronoun that tells us what the sentence talks about and ‘verb’ represents the action in the sentence. Then what is ‘subject verb concord/agreement’? It means that the subject and verb in a sentence should agree or match, otherwise the sentence will not sound right. Let’s understand the basic rules of subject-verb agreement . Rules 1. The verb and subject must agree in number (singular or plural) : This means that if the subject is singular, the verb should be singular and if the subject is plural, the verb should also be plural. Examples: a. He plays football . (SINGULAR) b. They play football. (PLURAL) 2. The number of the subject (singular or plural) will not change due to words/phrases in between the subject and the verb. Examples: a. One of the glasses is empty. (Here, since the subject is ‘one’, the verb should be ‘is’). b. The bouquet of red roses smells so sweet. (Here, since ‘bouquet’ is the subject and not ‘roses’, the verb should be ‘smells’ and not ‘smell’) 3. Subjects that are joined b y ‘and’ in a sentence , use a plural verb. Subjects that are joined by ‘either/or’, neither/nor’ use a singular verb. Examples: a. Radha and Meera are coming home. b. Neither Akshay nor Rohit is coming home. c. My dad or my mom is arriving today. 4. The verb in a sentence containing ‘or’, ‘either/or’, ‘neither/nor’ agrees with the noun or pronoun closest to it.

a. Neither the shoes nor the bag matches the dress. (Here, ‘bag’ is closest to the verb, hence ‘matches’) b. Neither the bag nor the shoes match the dress. (Here, ‘shoes’ is closest to the verb, hence ‘match’) 5. When the subject is followed by words such as ‘as well as’, ‘along with’, ‘besides’, ‘not’ etc. ignore them and use a singular verb if the subject is singular. a. Matt, as well as his dog, is expected shortly. b. Pratik, along with his brother, is going to school . 6. In sentences that begin with ‘here’, ‘there’, the true subject usually follows the verb. a. Here are the chocolates . b. There is a big puddle on the road. 7. In sentences that include sums of money, periods of time or distances etc. (as a unit), use singular verbs. a. 500 rupees is a high price to pay. b. 62 years is the minimum age of retirement. c. 10 kilometers is too far to walk. 8. In the case of words such as ‘a lot of’, all’, ‘some’ etc. in a sentence, pay attention to the noun after ‘of’. If the noun after ‘of’ is singular then use a singular verb, if plural, use a plural verb. a. All of the cake is gone. b. All of the cakes are gone. c. A lot of the cake is gone. d. A lot of the cakes are gone. e. Some of the cake is gone. f. Some of the cakes are gone. 9. In the case of collective nouns such as ‘group, ‘population’, ‘family’, in a sentence, the verb can be singular or plural depending on their use in the sentence. a. Most of my family is here OR are here. b. Half of the population was against the bill OR were against the bill. 10. Nouns such as ‘mathematics’, ‘civics’, ‘news’ etc. while plural in form, are singular in meaning and use singular verbs. a. Mathematics is very difficult for some people. b. The news is very saddening. 11. In sentences that express a wish, request or contrary to fact, the word ‘were’ is used instead of ‘was. a. I wish my sister were here. b. Aditya requested that she raise her glass.

Solved Examples for You on Subject Verb Concord Question: Choose the correct subject verb combinations in the sentences below. a. The lady in the car (look/looks) like your mother . b. Most of the milk (is/are) gone. c. One of the flowers (has/have) wilted. d. Either Ram or Shyam (is/are) coming today. e. Here (is/are) the newspaper . f. The group of dancers (is/are) here. g. Civics (is/are) my favo rite subject. Solution: a. The lady in the car looks like your mother. b. Most of the milk is gone. c. One of the flowers has wilted. d. Either Ram or Shyam is coming today. e. Here is the newspaper. f. The group of dancers is OR are here. g. Civics is my favorite subject.

title: READING AND MAKING NOTES
subject: English Language
rawText:
Subject: English Language Class: VEI2 /SS2 Topic: Reading and Making Notes Note-making is the process of reviewing, connecting, and recording key ideas from a text, lecture, or discussion. It's an active learning technique that helps individuals engage with information, retain knowledge, and recall important details. Key Features of Effective Note-making: 1. Concise: Focus on main ideas, omit unnecessary details 2. Organized: Use headings, subheadings, bullet points, and numbering 3. Clear: Use simple language, avoid jargon 4. Selective: Identify key points, prioritize important information 5. Visual: Incorporate diagrams, charts, and mind maps 6. Reviewable: Regularly review and revise notes 7. Personalized: Tailor notes to individual learning style 8. Accurate: Ensure notes accurately represent original content Benefits: - Enhances understanding and retention - Supports learning and revision - Develops critical thinking and analysis Importance of Reading: - Improves knowledge and understanding - Enhances critical thinking and analysis - Develops vocabulary and communication skills Effective Reading Strategies: 1. Preview: Skim headings, subheadings, and summaries 2. Question: Identify purpose and main ideas 3. Read: Focus on key points and supporting details 4. Recall: Summarize main ideas 5. Review: Reinforce understanding

Purpose: Condenses information, aids retention Methods: 1. Outline method (headings, subheadings, points) 2. Mind mapping (visual representation) 3. Cornell notes (key points, summaries) Tips for Effective Note-making: - Identify main ideas and key points - Use headings, subheadings, and bullet points - Keep notes concise and organized - Review and revise notes regularly Benefits of Note-making: - Improves understanding and retention - Enhances recall and revision - Supports exam preparation

title: PHRASES
subject: English Language
rawText:
The teacher begins the discussion by defining phrase to the students as a group of words that does not make a complete sentence. It forms part of a sentence, for example; The following group of words are phrases- The man, is my uncle, in the room, who sleeps. *The man who sleeps in the room is my uncle* The example of phrases given above don’t have complete meanings not until they are put together to form a logical sentence. A phrase in another dimension is a small group of words that adds meaning to a sentence. A phrase is not a sentence because it is not a complete idea with a subject, verb and predicate. TYPES OF PHRASES 1)NOUN PHRASE:- Is a phrase that made up of a noun or pronoun (as the head word). A noun phrase can be pre- modified by article, possessive or demonstrative pronouns and adjectives. A noun phrase can also be post – modified by adjectives and prepositional phrases or clauses. In a noun phrase, the headword must be a noun or a pronoun. Examples: a) The man and a boy ate an orange b) That boy and my brother are friends c) The faithful man is highly respect (the use article and adjective as pre- modifiers. d) The girl in the garden is my sister (prepositional phrase as post- modifier) e) I saw the village headmaster 2)ADJECTIVAL PHRASE:- Performs the grammatical function of qualifying the noun that precedes it in a sentence. E.g - The man standing at the gate is my father. It qualifies the man noun -The student to be suspended has stopped coming to school. It qualifies the noun student. Similarly, an adverb could be joined to an adjective to form an adjective phrase. e.g fairly used - fairly used(adjectival phrase) | | Adv Adj Wonderfully used - wonderfully used

3)ADVERBIAL PHRASE:- An adverbial phrase modifies the verb in the sentence. It indicates time, place, manner, frequency, degree, result of action, condition, purpose, reason, for an action etc. examples a) I put the food on the table (where) modified the verb put. b) The students come to school twice a week (frequency) modified the verb come c) He studies hard in order to pass (purpose) modifies the verb studies. 4) PREPOSITIONAL PHRASE:- Is a phrase that begins with a preposition followed by a noun phrase. The following expressions are therefore prepositional phrase: In the class, on the table, behind the class, through the door, to their friend, for a purpose etc. Prepositional phrases function as adverbial phrase and also as adjectival phrase. When prepositional phrase modify verb, they are called adverbial phrases. They are treated as adjectival phrases when they qualify nouns or pronouns. Examples: a) The shop near the school is my mother’s……near the school is an adjectival phrase which qualifies the noun ‘shop’. b) We saw the boy across the road……. across the road is an adverbial phrase of place which modifies the verb ‘saw’ in the main clause.

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText: Nasal C onsonants /m, n, ŋ / A nasal consonant is a consonant whose production involves a lowered velum and a closure in the oral cavity, so that air flows out through the nose. Examples of nasal consonants are [m], [n], and [ŋ] (as in think and sing). /m/ - This sound has the following spelling forms; ‘m’: man, mark, human, meet, mood, mile, meat, some, b o mb, women, mad, made, mammal, committee, common, calm, game, bloom, groom, mouth, smile, family, harm, palm, name, come, dumb, farm etc . /n/ This sound has the following spelling forms ; neat, fan, man, gun, fun, hand, kind, pen, pain, hunt, sun, son, need, gain, ten, near, needle, can, earn, tin, nose, note, run, benefit, turn. ‘ gn ’ - gnash, feign, resign, sign, malign, assign, etc ‘ kn ’ - knight, knowle dge, knife, knead, knit, kneel, knee, knock, knot etc ‘ n ’ is silent that is, not pronounced if it occurs after ‘m’ at the end of the word such as damn, autumn, hymn, solemn, condemn, /ŋ/ is a voiced velar nasal produced with the back of the tongue formi ng a closure with the velum and the air stream passing through the nose. The most common spelling forms or letters for /ŋ/ are: ‘ ng ’ - as in sing, hang, bang, gang, ring, sting, wing, wrong, strong, king, fang, young, pangs, long, bring, etc ‘ n ’ - as in ba ngle, dangle, finger, jungle, hungry, mingle, etc (when ’n’ occurs before ‘g’ in a word that is more than one syllable, it is realized as /ŋ/ while the ‘g’ is /g/ to give two sound /ng/) ‘ nk ’ - as in blink, bank, pranks, think, sink, stink wink, tank, jinks, frank, drink, wrinkle, ankle, zink, etc Exercise From the words lettered A to D, choose the word that has the same consonant sounds as the one represented by the letters underlined. 1. Hang A. hinge B. tinge C. song D. balm 2. Dangle A. Stink B. Barn C. Turn D. Wiggle

title: PRONOUN
subject: English Language
rawText: Pronouns- Pronouns are words which are used to replace nouns in a sentence. They are mostly used in order to avoid unnecessary repetition of nouns in a sentence. Both nouns and pronouns are used interchangeably in a sentence, therefore they both perform the same function. Examples are: he, they, we etc. TYPES OF PRONOUNS Personal pronouns: Examples I, we, they , us etc. Possessive pronouns: yours, his, hers, theirs, its, yours etc. Demonstrative pronouns: this that these those. Interrogative pronouns: who which, whom, whose, etc. Reflexive pronouns: myself, themselves, yourselves/yourself, ourselves, oneself etc. Reciprocal pronouns: each other and one another. Relative pronoun: which, whom, whose, who, that etc. Indefinite pronouns: someone, somebody, anything, anyone, everything, everyone, nobody, nothing etc.

WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH HEALTH Health means the general condition of body and mind. Illnesses and diseases affect the body, causing unhealthiness. Some diseases/illnesses: malaria, fever, flu, catarrh, migraines, cancer, HIV/AIDS, hepatitis, e.t.c Some actions: diagnose, check-up, test, prescribe, treat, inject, admit, discharge, e.t.c. Some places: office, waiting hall/room, theatre, laboratory, ward, e.t.c Some people: doctors, nurses, lab technicians, cleaners, e.t.c. title: PHRASE
subject: English Language
rawText: Noun Phrases and Their Functions Definition: A noun phrase is a phrase that consists of a noun or pronoun and any accompanying modifiers, determiners, or complements. Functions of Noun Phrases 1. Subject: A noun phrase can function as the subject of a sentence, performing the action described by the verb. 2. Object: A noun phrase can function as the object of a verb or preposition, receiving the action described by the verb. 3. Complement: A noun phrase can function as a complement, providing more information about the subject or object. 4. Modifier: A noun phrase can function as a modifier, providing more information about another noun or pronoun. Types of Noun Phrases 1. Simple Noun Phrase: Consists of a single noun or pronoun e.g., "the book". 2. Complex Noun Phrase: Consists of a noun or pronoun with one or more modifiers e.g., "the big red car’. 3. Compound Noun Phrase: Consists of two or more nouns or pronouns joined by a conjunction e.g., "John and Mary". Examples 1. "The students are studying for their exams." (Subject) 2. "She ate a sandwich for lunch." (Object) 3. "He is a brilliant scientist." (Complement) 4. "The city of Paris is famous for its art." (Modifier) Importance of Noun Phrases 1. Clarity: Noun phrases help to clarify the meaning of a sentence. 2. Specificity: Noun phrases provide specific details about the nouns or pronouns they modify. 3. Effective Communication: Understanding noun phrases is essential for effective communication in writing and speaking.

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT
subject: English Language
rawText: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH AGRICULTURE Agriculture is the science or practice of farming, including cultivation of the soil for the growing of crops and the rearing of animals to provide food, wool, and other products. 1. Crop farming- it is the production of crops on a large scale 2. Livestock- it is the domestication of animals for cultivation 3. Horticulture- it is the art or science of cultivating gardens; gardening Some terms and their meanings Bush fallowing : is a system of farming whereby the farmer cultivates one piece of land for some years and later leave it for some years with the aim of restoring the fertility of the soil naturally. During this fallow period, the farmer cultivates another piece of land . Irrigation : the process of applying water to the crop artificially to fulfil their water requirements Subsistence: the practice of growing crops and raising livestock sufficient only for one’s own use without any surplus for trade. The opposite is mechanized farming. Other terms include : crop rotation, rearing, planting, harvesting, pruning, , mechanized, large scale, fertilization, cultivating, digging, clearing, farming, ploughing, organic farming, crop yield, agrarian, root, stem, shoot, e. t.c Tools Tractor, bulldozer, cutlass, hoe, sickle, pen, trough, hand gloves, cage, tiller Plants, Animals and Flowers Maize, cattle, grains, seedlings, tubers, seeds, Places: Garden, vase, pot, green house, farm, farmland, land, bush, barn, silo, People involved: farmer, herdsmen, cattle-rearer, horticulturist, nomad, agronomist

It is articulated when the back of the tongue makes Contact with the velum. The Contac results in a total obstruction of the flow of air. The air pressure which

builds up is suddenly released with an explosive Sound. There glottis is open so that the vocal cords do not vibrate. The adverbial clauses are classified according to the meaning they Convey in sentence They answers questions like when, where, how why, etc. The functions of adverbial clause is to modifies verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs in a sentence Types and functions of adverbial clause 1. Adverbial clause of time: This expresses the time of the action-contained in the main clause .It answers the question when, and is often Introduced by while, since, after, when, as, before, untill during etc.

Examples. a. It was raining when I woke up . when I woke up modifies the verb "raining" in the main Clause b. I will not go away until he comes back until he comes back modifies the verb "go away". 2. Adverbial clause of place: This shows the place where the action occurs. It answers the question where and is often introduced by where, whenever anywhere, everywhere, etc Examples a. my father left the money where it could be seen Where it could be seen modifies the verb "left". b. He eats anywhere he sees food. (anywhere he Sees food) modifies the verb "left" 3. Adverbial clause of manner: An adverbial Clause of manner is used to express the way. in which the action in the mam clause is carried out. It answers the question "how" and is often Introduced by as, as if, as though, etc. Eg a. she sang as if she was a solost. as if she was a soloist modifies the verb "sang". b. He parades himself as though he is the president of the whole world. as though he is the president of the whole world modifies the verb "Parades 4. Adverbial clause of reason. An adverbial clause of reason explains the cause of the action in the mam clause. It is an expression for justification for something that has happened. It answer the question why and it is introduced by because, since for, as, seeing that etc. Eg: a. The teacher punished the student because he Came late to class. because he came Lode to School modifies the verb "punished" b. . We left Since he was not ready to Increase our Salary.Since he was not ready to Increase our Salary modifies the verb "Left"! 5. Adverbial Clause of result: An adverbial clause of result mentions the Consequence the action in the main clause. It is Introduced by that, So that, Such that Example a. she sang in a manner that made every body to admire her.. that made everybody to admire her, modifies to verb sang! Her. b. It rained heavily such that vehicles stopped moving .Such that vehicles stopped moving modifier the aduerb "heavily. 6. Aduerbial clause of purpose: An adverbial clause purpose expresses the aim of the action in the many Clause: It answers the question for what purpose? and is usually Introduced by So that, in order that In case, should, etc. Examples.

a. He prays so that God will hear him... So that God will hear him modifies the verb 'prays in the main clause. b. Truth is necessary so that people will have Confidence In you. so that people will have confidence in you modifies the verb is in the main clause. 7. Adverbial clause of degree. An adverbial clause of degree expresses the weight (gravity or level) of the action in the main clause. It is introduce by then, as... as. Examples a. He is more dangerous than you think... than you think modifies the verb is' in the main clause. b. He works longer than his boss permits. than his boss permits modifier the verb "Works in the main clause. 8 Adverbial clause of Condition: An adverbial Clause of Condition states the situation (Condition) under which the action in the mains clause will take place. It is introduced by the conditional words if, unless, except, provided, until, once. Examples. a. I will not let you go unless you bless me. Unless you bless me modifies the verb "will not let go in the main clause. b. If you do not marry me, I will die. If you do not marry me modifies the verb "will die in the main clause. Features of informal letter A. Writers Address with date. It requires only the address of the writer. B Salutation: The correct way of greeting is Dear first name as in Dear Peter, Dear brother John, Dear mother, Dear Brother. C. Introduction: The writer may wish to start with acknowledging the receipt of the letter written to you by the person. D. Body of the letter: This is where you try to according to what the question demands. you must make at least three good points but you can give more points if you know the question for well. The Length has to be between two and a half or three pages. E. Subscription: Informal letter close with Yours Sincerely,

Adverbial clause of time: This expresses the time of the action-contained in the main clause .It answers the question when, and is often Introduced by while, since, after, when, as, before, untill during etc.

It answer the question why and it is introduced by because, since for, as, seeing that etc. Eg: a. The teacher punished the student because he Came late to class. because he came Lode to School modifies the verb "punished" b. . We left Since he was not ready to Increase our Salary.Since he was not ready to Increase our Salary modifies the verb "Left"! 5. It is Introduced by that, So that, Such that Example a. she sang in a manner that made every body to admire her.. that made everybody to admire her, modifies to verb sang! Her. b. It rained heavily such that vehicles stopped moving .Such that vehicles stopped moving modifier the aduerb "heavily. 6. Aduerbial clause of purpose: An adverbial clause purpose expresses the aim of the action in the many Clause: It answers the question for what purpose? and is usually Introduced by So that, in order that In case, should, etc. Examples.

Truth is necessary so that people will have Confidence In you. so that people will have confidence in you modifies the verb is in the main clause. 7. Adverbial clause of degree. An adverbial clause of degree expresses the weight (gravity or level) of the action in the main clause. It is introduce by then, as... as. Examples a. He is more dangerous than you think... than you think modifies the verb is' in the main clause. b. He works longer than his boss permits. than his boss permits modifier the verb "Works in the main clause. 8 Adverbial clause of Condition: An adverbial Clause of Condition states the situation (Condition) under which the action in the mains clause will take place. A. p as in pin, peace, play form, trap, leap, plum, paralyze, cup, Stamp. pp" as in slippers, applause, stopped, copper, apple, trapped ph as in shepherd. /P/ is silent that is not pronounced in words like Psalm, psychology, Corps, Coup, cupboard etc. If is pronounced as /f/ in "ph" spellings such as Phase, Pharmacy, Physics nephew etc B. /b/ is a voiced bilabial plosive which articulated when the Lips are brought together; obstruct the air which is released with an explosive Sound. The vocal Cords vibrate during the Production. The Spelling symbols include: "b" as in ball, bonus, boast, job, mobile, numbers, back, table "bb" as in rubber, rubbed, bubble, ribbon, mobbed, sobbing Minimal pairs for /p/ and /b/ . Initial /b/. /P/. last /b/. /p/ Bad. Pad. mob mop Bark. Park. tab. tap Bet. Pet. cab. Cap bush. Push. robe. rope bay. pay. rib. rip blot. plot. brow. prow brim. Prim. bride. Pride /k/and/g/ are the two velar plosives m English Language. For the production of these Sounds, there is a total obstruction in the flow of the air which is released in an explosive manner Also, the back of the tongue is raised and therefore forms a Closure the velum (place of articulation) during their production. /k/ is a voiceless velar plosive. It is articulated when the back of the tongue makes Contact with the velum. The Contac results in a total obstruction of the flow of air. The air pressure which

builds up is suddenly released with an explosive Sound. There glottis is open so that the vocal cords do not vibrate. The spelling Symbol includes: K as in King, bank "C" as in Coat, cat "CC" as in account, accord CH an in Chemistry, mechanic CK as in quick, mock /g/ is a voiced velar plosive. The manner of articulation is similar to that of/k/ except that the vocal Cords vibrate. The Spelling Symbol includes: g' as in give, goat, go, gold, guide. - gg" as in Struggle, beggers Juggling, stagger. "gh" as in ghost, ghastly, dinghy "x" as in exact examination, exempt mimmal pairs for/k/ and /g/ /k/. /g/. /k/. /g/ Crow. grow. Krdu. grdu Coat. goat. kdrl. garl Cap gap. Keep. grep Card. guard. Kard. ga:d class. glass. Klais. glais Cane. gave keiv. geiv leak. league. li:k. li:g /t/ and /d/ ane alveolar stop consonant. Their manner of articulation and place of articulation are the same. The only difference. is that /f/ is fortis, le, Strong and Voiceless Stop Consonant, /d/ is lenis, le weak and Voiced Stop Consonant. Code. kaud. krud hurt. heard. h3it. h3id Theme: Structure Unit Topic: clause Lesson topic: Adverbial clause and function An adverbial clause is the clause that performs the work of an adverb in a sentence. The adverbial clauses are classified according to the meaning they Convey in sentence They answers questions like when, where, how why, etc. The functions of adverbial clause is to modifies verbs, adjectives, and other adverbs in a sentence Types and functions of adverbial clause 1. Adverbial clause of time: This expresses the time of the action-contained in the main clause .It answers the question when, and is often Introduced by while, since, after, when, as, before, untill during etc.

Examples. a. It was raining when I woke up . when I woke up modifies the verb "raining" in the main Clause b. I will not go away until he comes back until he comes back modifies the verb "go away". 2. Adverbial clause of place: This shows the place where the action occurs. It answers the question where and is often introduced by where, whenever anywhere, everywhere, etc Examples a. my father left the money where it could be seen Where it could be seen modifies the verb "left". b. He eats anywhere he sees food. (anywhere he Sees food) modifies the verb "left" 3. Adverbial clause of manner: An adverbial Clause of manner is used to express the way. in which the action in the mam clause is carried out. It answers the question "how" and is often Introduced by as, as if, as though, etc. Eg a. she sang as if she was a solost. as if she was a soloist modifies the verb "sang". b. He parades himself as though he is the president of the whole world. as though he is the president of the whole world modifies the verb "Parades 4. Adverbial clause of reason. An adverbial clause of reason explains the cause of the action in the mam clause. It is an expression for justification for something that has happened. It answer the question why and it is introduced by because, since for, as, seeing that etc. Eg: a. The teacher punished the student because he Came late to class. because he came Lode to School modifies the verb "punished" b. . We left Since he was not ready to Increase our Salary.Since he was not ready to Increase our Salary modifies the verb "Left"! 5. Adverbial Clause of result: An adverbial clause of result mentions the Consequence the action in the main clause. It is Introduced by that, So that, Such that Example a. she sang in a manner that made every body to admire her.. that made everybody to admire her, modifies to verb sang! Her. b. It rained heavily such that vehicles stopped moving .Such that vehicles stopped moving modifier the aduerb "heavily. 6. Aduerbial clause of purpose: An adverbial clause purpose expresses the aim of the action in the many Clause: It answers the question for what purpose? and is usually Introduced by So that, in order that In case, should, etc. Examples.

a. He prays so that God will hear him... So that God will hear him modifies the verb 'prays in the main clause. b. Truth is necessary so that people will have Confidence In you. so that people will have confidence in you modifies the verb is in the main clause. 7. Adverbial clause of degree. An adverbial clause of degree expresses the weight (gravity or level) of the action in the main clause. It is introduce by then, as... as. Examples a. He is more dangerous than you think... than you think modifies the verb is' in the main clause. b. He works longer than his boss permits. than his boss permits modifier the verb "Works in the main clause. 8 Adverbial clause of Condition: An adverbial Clause of Condition states the situation (Condition) under which the action in the mains clause will take place. It is introduced by the conditional words if, unless, except, provided, until, once. Examples. a. I will not let you go unless you bless me. Unless you bless me modifies the verb "will not let go in the main clause. b. If you do not marry me, I will die. If you do not marry me modifies the verb "will die in the main clause. T heme : Comprehension Unit Topic: Reading Comprehension Lesson Topic: Reading for meaning in context Reading for meaning in context means to provide the word meaning used in the passage according to the context and not dictionary meaning: Sometimes in comprehension passage we come across difficult words whose meaning we do not know. However, the context in which these words are used may serve as a clue the environment in which a word occurs is usually essential for decoding the meaning of the word. From the passage titled "the joy of victory" on Unit 10 the students will find alternative words to substitute the key words to fit perfectly into the passage the alternative must be in the same tense and word class as the key words given in the passage Theme : Continuous writing.

Unit Topic : better writing Lesson topic: Informal letter features and Language Informal letters are private or personal Letters. They are letters written to people who are very familiar to us such as our parent’s relatives, friends, classmate, brothers and sisters, husband and wives and other people with whom we have close relationship. Features of informal letter A. Writers Address with date. It requires only the address of the writer. It could be written in two main ways, either in the block form or slanting or Indented form Examples i. Block form Government Secondary School PMB 227, Kubwa, Abuja. 30th March, 2024. ii. Slanting form Govemmeat Secondary school PMB 227. Kubwa, Abuja 30th march, 2024. B Salutation: The correct way of greeting is Dear first name as in Dear Peter, Dear brother John, Dear mother, Dear Brother. C. Introduction: The writer may wish to start with acknowledging the receipt of the letter written to you by the person. You may also start by asking after the person's health, Job, Family etc. do not begin your letter with religions or tribal sentiments or to conclude with such Words as, greetings in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, or any other religious form... D. Body of the letter: This is where you try to according to what the question demands. you must make at least three good points but you can give more points if you know the question for well. The Length has to be between two and a half or three pages. E. Subscription: Informal letter close with Yours Sincerely,

James, Then your first name no signature needed. Assignment. A friend of yours wants to study in your school and has written to you for information and advice writes a reply to him telling him all that he needs to know about the school. WASSCE 2016.

title: COMPREHENSION: READING FOR MAIN GIST
subject: English Language
rawText:
2nd Term Lesson Note For SS2 9/01/2026 READING FOR MAIN GIST Meaning of Main Gist The main gist is the central or most important idea in a passage. It tells what the whole passage is about in a few words or one sentence. How to Identify the Main Gist To find the main gist of a passage, do the following: Read the title carefully. Read the first paragraph and the last paragraph. Look for repeated words or ideas. Ignore minor details and examples. Ask yourself: What is the writer mainly talking about? Main Gist and Supporting Details The main gist is the central idea of the passage. Supporting details are facts, examples, or explanations that help to explain the main gist. Example: Passage talks about the causes of air pollution. Main gist: Causes of air pollution. Supporting details: Smoke from vehicles, factory waste, burning of refuse. Importance of Reading for Main Gist Reading for main gist helps students to: * Understand passages quickly *Answer comprehension questions correctly

*Summarize passages easily *Improve reading and examination skills
