Theme : speech Unit topic: Consonant sounds. Lesson Topic: Nasal sounds/n//m/and/g/ Nasal sounds are consonants which are produced when the soft oft palate is lowered to close the oral cavity so that air-Steam passes through the nasal cavity (The nose) The nasal are /n//m//sand /g/ and they are all voiced /m/ is a voiced bilabial nasal which is produced when upper and lower lips come together, you breathe out through the nose and add some voice to the breaths Stream. The spelling Symbol includes. m as in man, meat march, move, mat Mas. mm as in Commit, summon recommend. mb as in tomb bomb, Comb, Thumb. mn as in damn, column, Solemn . /n/ is a voiced alveolar nasal sound and for the production to it, the tip of the tongue forms a closure with the alveolar ridge, allowing the air stream pass through the nasal Cavity (the nose). The vocal Cords Vibrate during the articulation of /n/ which makes if a voiced Sound. The spelling symbols for the /n/ sound are. 'n' as in-nail, neat, never, noon, Snake. Nn as in funny, annoy, dinner kn as in know, knot, knit, knife "gn" as in gnat, gnaw, gnarle, gnash. Dz/ is a voiced velar nasal produced with the basis of the tongue forming a closure with the Velum and the air stream passing through the nasal cavity (noise). There is a vibration at the vocal Cords during the Production of/dz/ The /dz/ Sound does not occur at the beginning of a word. The spelling Symbol Includes:" /ng/ as in bring, anger, tongue, wing, sing, ring, king, Spring, morning. When 'n' occurs before 'g' in a word that is more than one syllable, it is pronounced as/g/while the g' is pronounced as /g/ to give the two Sounds /dg/. Eg: bangle, angle dangle, finger, hungry, Jungle ete... Note that not all 'ng' letter become /g/in word like fringe, Stingy, revenge, do not have the /g/ sound because the sound realized there is /n/

Theme: Structure Unit Topics: Concord Lesson topic : Concord-agreement between subject and verb Concord means agreement between the subject and the verb m any sentence both im number and person. A sentence will always be wrong if the subject and verb do not agree. Concord has rules guiding it which must be known For Correct sentence Constructions. 1. When the subject is Singular It takes a Singular verb and when the subject is plural, if takes a plural verb. Examples. a. The Lecturer comes to class every Tuesday!! b. she has a very good hand writing. c. Some students want to pass without reading. d. They come here every day. Note that when the pronoun I is used it uses a plural verb "have" even though it is a singular person. Example. a. I have some work to do. b. I have finished cooking the food. 2. When two or more subjects are connected by 'and' a plural verb is used Example. a. John and Adamu play football every day. b. The Woman and her twins were honored. If the subjects are connected by each' or 'every, a singular verb is required. Examples. a. Each boy and girl is to bring a hoe. b. Every man and woman has a role to play in fighting corruptions. If two singular subjects Connected by "and" refer to the same personal, a Singular verb is used. Example. a. My Sister and friend is very good to me. b. He is your husband and mentor.

3. When two or more singular subjects are joined by neither now, either or not only-but, take a Singular verb. Eg. a. Neither the man nor his wife qualifies for the award. b. Either the principal or the vice gives out the certificates. C. Not only the robbers but the policeman was responsible for the theft. Note that if one of the subjects is Singular and the other is plural the rule of proximity (nearness) is applied. This means that the Last subject that followed by the verb determines the form the verb would be. Example. a. Neither the man or his children were honored. 4. when two subjects and connected by as well as Including, along with, In addition to a Singular verb is used Eg. a. The principal together with his teachers encourage Students to study hard. b. mathematics as well as English Language is Compulsory. C. the man along with his wife is here. 5 when two singular subjects Connected by and are regarded as the same entity, They take a singular verb. Example: a. Bread and butter is delicious. b. Rice and beans is my favorite dish. 6. when Indefinite pronouns like nobody, Someone, Somebody, no one, none, everybody, are subjecte in the sentence, they take singular verb Eg a. Nobody cares about the orphan. b. Every body does as he likes C. None of you Sweeps on Mondays d Somebody suspects you. Also, the indefinite pronoun such as all which is in the plural form take singular verbs in some cases. Example. a. All is well b. All has not finished Theme: Summary writing

Your language must be formal and straight to the point. Slangs must not be used and do not ask about This jobs family or heath no matter how close you are with the chairman.. 6. The vocal Cords Vibrate during the articulation of /n/ which makes if a voiced Sound. The spelling symbols for the /n/ sound are. 'n' as in-nail, neat, never, noon, Snake. Nn as in funny, annoy, dinner kn as in know, knot, knit, knife "gn" as in gnat, gnaw, gnarle, gnash. Dz/ is a voiced velar nasal produced with the basis of the tongue forming a closure with the Velum and the air stream passing through the nasal cavity (noise). There is a vibration at the vocal Cords during the Production of/dz/ The /dz/ Sound does not occur at the beginning of a word. The spelling Symbol Includes:" /ng/ as in bring, anger, tongue, wing, sing, ring, king, Spring, morning. When 'n' occurs before 'g' in a word that is more than one syllable, it is pronounced as/g/while the g' is pronounced as /g/ to give the two Sounds /dg/. Eg: bangle, angle dangle, finger, hungry, Jungle ete... Note that not all 'ng' letter become /g/in word like fringe, Stingy, revenge, do not have the /g/ sound because the sound realized there is /n/

Theme: Structure Unit Topics: Concord Lesson topic : Concord-agreement between subject and verb Concord means agreement between the subject and the verb m any sentence both im number and person. A sentence will always be wrong if the subject and verb do not agree. Concord has rules guiding it which must be known For Correct sentence Constructions. 1. When the subject is Singular It takes a Singular verb and when the subject is plural, if takes a plural verb. Examples. a. The Lecturer comes to class every Tuesday!! b. she has a very good hand writing. c. Some students want to pass without reading. d. They come here every day. Note that when the pronoun I is used it uses a plural verb "have" even though it is a singular person. Example. a. I have some work to do. b. I have finished cooking the food. 2. When two or more subjects are connected by 'and' a plural verb is used Example. a. John and Adamu play football every day. b. The Woman and her twins were honored. If the subjects are connected by each' or 'every, a singular verb is required. Examples. a. Each boy and girl is to bring a hoe. b. Every man and woman has a role to play in fighting corruptions. If two singular subjects Connected by "and" refer to the same personal, a Singular verb is used. Example. a. My Sister and friend is very good to me. b. He is your husband and mentor.

3. When two or more singular subjects are joined by neither now, either or not only-but, take a Singular verb. Eg. a. Neither the man nor his wife qualifies for the award. b. Either the principal or the vice gives out the certificates. C. Not only the robbers but the policeman was responsible for the theft. Note that if one of the subjects is Singular and the other is plural the rule of proximity (nearness) is applied. This means that the Last subject that followed by the verb determines the form the verb would be. Example. a. Neither the man or his children were honored. 4. when two subjects and connected by as well as Including, along with, In addition to a Singular verb is used Eg. a. The principal together with his teachers encourage Students to study hard. b. mathematics as well as English Language is Compulsory. C. the man along with his wife is here. 5 when two singular subjects Connected by and are regarded as the same entity, They take a singular verb. Example: a. Bread and butter is delicious. b. Rice and beans is my favorite dish. 6. when Indefinite pronouns like nobody, Someone, Somebody, no one, none, everybody, are subjecte in the sentence, they take singular verb Eg a. Nobody cares about the orphan. b. Every body does as he likes C. None of you Sweeps on Mondays d Somebody suspects you. Also, the indefinite pronoun such as all which is in the plural form take singular verbs in some cases. Example. a. All is well b. All has not finished Theme: Summary writing

SPEECH Topic: Making a Toast a. Meaning of a Toast A toast is a short speech made in honor of a person, group, or event, usually during a social gathering. It is often followed by raising a glass and taking a drink to express goodwill or celebration. In other words, a toast is a brief, meaningful speech that shows appreciation, congratulations, or best wishes to someone or something being celebrated. b. Occasions for a Toast A toast can be made on several special occasions such as: 1. Weddings – to celebrate the bride and groom. 2. Birthdays – to honor the celebrant. 3. Graduations – to congratulate the graduates. 4. Retirement ceremonies – to appreciate someone’s service. 5. Award ceremonies – to celebrate achievement. 6. Farewell parties – to wish someone success in their new journey. 7. Anniversaries – to celebrate years of marriage, business, or friendship. Features of a Good Toast 1. It is short and clear. 2. It includes words of praise or congratulations. 3. It expresses good wishes for the future. 4. It ends with an invitation to raise glasses. 5. The tone is positive, cheerful, and respectful. Example of a Toast: “Ladies and gentlemen, please join me in celebrating our dear friend, Mr. James, who has dedicated 30 years of service to this company. His hard work and honesty have inspired us all. We wish him a joyful retirement filled with peace and happiness. Let’s raise our glasses to Mr. James! ” READING COMPREHENSION Topic: Reading for Implied Meaning Meaning Reading for implied meaning means understanding what the writer suggests or hints at but does not say directly. It involves reading between the lines to find the hidden or deeper message. Skills Needed 1. Identify tone and attitude of the writer. 2. Recognize emotions expressed indirectly. 3. Understand cause and effect relationships. 4. Use context clues to guess hidden ideas. 5. Differentiate between literal and figurative meaning. Example: Sentence: “John looked at his empty wallet and sighed.”

• Literal meaning: John’s wallet has no money. • Implied meaning: John is worried or sad because he is broke. STRUCTURE Topic: Nominalization Meaning Nominalization is the process of changing verbs, adjectives, or clauses into nouns. It is often used in formal writing to make sentences more academic or impersonal. Examples: Verb / Adjective Noun (Nominalized form) Decide Decision Approve Approval Educate Education Strong Strength Happy Happiness Fail Failure Grow Growth Examples in Sentences: 1. Verb: The teacher explained the lesson clearly. → Nominalized: The teacher’s explanation was clear. 2. Adjective: He was strong. → Nominalized: His strength impressed everyone. 3. Verb: They decided to leave early. → Nominalized: Their decision to leave early was wise. Uses of Nominalization 1. To make writing formal. 2. To summarize ideas. 3. To avoid repetition. 4. To express ideas in a compact way. CONTINUOUS WRITING Topic: Writing Speeches for Specific Purposes Meaning of a Speech A speech is a formal talk or address given to an audience to inform, persuade, or entertain them. Purposes of a Speech 1. To inform – give information about a topic. 2. To persuade – convince the audience to accept an idea or take action. 3. To entertain – amuse or inspire the audience. 4. To motivate – encourage people to act positively. 5. To appreciate – show gratitude or honor to someone. Features of a Good Speech

1. Clear Introduction – Greet the audience and state your purpose. 2. Body – Present main points in a logical order. 3. Conclusion – Summarize and end with a strong message. 4. Tone and Language – Formal, respectful, and suitable for the audience. 5. Organization – Ideas arranged in paragraphs. 6. Audience Awareness – Use appropriate words for listeners. 7. Sign-off – End politely (e.g., “Thank you for listening.”) Structure of a Speech 1. Opening greeting: “Good morning, ladies and gentlemen,” or “Mr. Chairman, invited guests, fellow students…” 2. Introduction: State who you are and why you are speaking. e.g., “I am here to speak on the topic ‘The Dangers of Drug Abuse.’ ” 3. Body: o Discuss your points clearly and in order. o Support each point with examples or facts. 4. Conclusion: o Summarize your points. o End with a call to action or appreciation. e.g., “Let us all work together to stop drug abuse in our society. Thank you.” Example of a Speech (for Specific Purpose) Topic: Speech on the Importance of Education Good morning, teachers and fellow students. I am here to speak on the importance of education. Education is the key to success. It helps us develop our talents and prepares us for the future. Without education, a nation cannot grow. Every child should go to school and work hard to achieve their goals. Let us value education and encourage others to learn. Thank you for listening.

subject: English Language
rawText: DETERMINERS AND QUANTIFIERS Determiners modify nouns by setting a limitation over the nouns to indicate how specific or general they are. A determiner usually begins at the beginning of a noun phrase and works as an adjective to modify the nouns. However, determiners are not necessary for every noun phrase. Determiners include: a. The definite article: the  Give me the book I read to you yesterday. (specific book)  I want the pencil you borrowed yesterday b. The indefinite articles a, an  Give me a book from the shelf (A general/random book from a specific shelf)  I want an apple. c. The possessives: my, your, his, her, our, their, its, whose  My car is parked outside (Specific car)  His house is near the bridge. d. The demonstratives: this, that, these, those  This is my book.  That house belongs to me.  Those ducks are beautiful e. Interrogatives: which, what  Which car do you want to buy?  What product do you use? Quantifiers are also determiners, which modify a noun to indicate its quantity. The quantifiers are: any, all, many, much, most, some, a few, a lot of, a little, a large amount of, none, and the cardinal numbers [one, two, three, four], e.t.c Examples:  I have some money but not a lot of it.  Many people were hurt in that calamity. Note : there are some rules for using determiners and quantifiers. Some of them can be used only with countable nouns and some of them with uncountable nouns, while others can be used with either of them.

OTHER PRONOUNS Pronouns can be classified into different types based on their functions. Given below are the remaining types of pronouns. Go through the examples carefully to have a clear understanding of each type of pronoun and its function.  Possessive Pronouns are pronouns that are used to show possession. Some examples of possessive pronouns are mine, yours, his, hers, theirs and its.  Reflexive Pronouns are pronouns that are used to refer back to the subject in the sentence. Some examples of reflexive pronouns are myself, yourself, herself, himself, oneself, itself, ourselves, themselves and yourselves.  Interrogative Pronouns are pronouns that are used to ask questions. Some examples of interrogative pronouns are who, what, when, why and where.  Indefinite Pronouns are pronouns that do not refer to any particular person, place or thing. Some examples of indefinite pronouns are someone, somebody, somewhere, something, anyone, anybody, anywhere, anything, no one, nobody, nowhere, everyone, everybody, everywhere, everything, each, none, few, and many.  Reciprocal Pronouns are pronouns that are used to express a mutual relationship. Some examples of reciprocal pronouns are each other and one another. U se suitable pronouns to substitute the underlined nouns in the following sentences: 1. Josh and Derrick visited Disneyland last month. 2. Sarah did not come home last evening. 3. My mo m could not find her cupboard keys. 4. Yesterday was my parents’ wedding anniversary. 5. The cat drank all the milk that was left in the kitchen. 6. Sheela and Teena found it hard to move the sofa set across the hall as the sofa set was too heavy for Sheela and Teena to carry. 7. Divya is Danny’s sister. 8. That silver Brezza belongs to Emmanuel and Usha . 9. My pet dog just lay on the floor the whole day. 10. rawText: PREFIXES (AS WORD EXTENSION) Prefix /pri:fiks/ Prefixes are letters that are added to the beginning of a root word to make a new word with a different meaning. E.g: build – re build Prefixes are used mainly to shorten phrases into a single word. They also have meanings and the meanings remain the same no matter the base words they are fixed to. E.g: re- means ‘to do again’ So, rebuild, rewrite, mean doing the actions again. We can use prefixes to create antonyms, e.g: possible – im possible SOME COMMON PREFIXES Prefix Meaning Examples Anti- Against/opposed to Anti-war, anti-government, anti- Christ Auto- self Autobiography, automobile De- Reverse or change De-classify, decontaminate, demotivate Dis- Reverse or remove Disagree, displeasure, disqualify Down- Reduce or lower Downgrade, downhearted Extra- beyond Extraordinary, extraterrestrial Hyper- extreme hyperactive Il-, im-, in-, ir- not Illegal, impossible, insecure, irregular Inter- between Inter-house, interactive, international Mid- middle Midday, midnight, mid-January Mis- Incorrectly, badly Misaligned, mislead, misspelt Non- not Non-payment, non-alcoholic, non- auto, non-cancerous Post- after Post-colonialism, post-election Pre- before Prehistoric, prefix, pre-war Pro- In favour of Pro-communist, proactive, pro- democracy Re- again Reconsider, redo, rewrite Sub- Under, below Submarine, submerge, sub-Saharan Tele- At a distance Television, telepathic Ultra- Extremely Ultra-compact, ultrasound Un- Remove, reverse, not Undo, unpack, unhappy Under- Less than, beneath Undercook, underestimate Up- Make or move higher Upgrade, uphill

Cultist engage in nefarious activities like armed robbery, prostitution etc. to meet up with their extravagant lifestyle. Theme: Grammar Unit Topic: Verb Le sson Topic: Auxiliary verb. An auxiliary verb is a verb used with the Lexical main verb to show tense etc and to form questions and negatives. Auxiliary verbs are classified into two types a. primary Auxiliary - be, do, have b. Modal Auxiliary - may, shall, can. Primary Auxiliary verbs are not used exclusively as auxiliary.They have four main functions. 1. They function as main verb eg

we were here They have some grapes Ngozi did her job well. 2. Used to form tense of the verb. Eg: They had gone home He was Coming home when I see him. 3. Used to form passive transformations in English Language eg He was given another chance by the principal 4. As auxiliary eg. They were playing I have brought a new dress I did enjoy the food. Do: This uses" Do, did and does" in question. Where you have no other auxiliary and where the main verb is not in the same form as be eg. a. what do you know about them? b Do they go there always? c. a. with the irregular verbs, have chosen, have eaten. b. with the regular verb.: have talked, has eaten. c. He has to work hard in English I have eaten. I would have given you the money if I was around Theme: Vocabulary Development Unit Topic: Register of plumbing Lesson Topic: Words associated with plumbing. Plumbing is the work of fitting and repairing water pipes, baths, toilets, sinks etc. in a building- plumbing is the system fixing Pipes and other fittings such that water will be supplied to a building. Plumber is a Person whose job is to fit and repair things such as water pipes, toilet, bathroom fittings etc Words associated with plumbing 1. Pipes: These are tubes through which liquid flow eg a water pipe, waste Pipes. 2. Connect: it is to join pipe of the various parts of a building to connect water tap and to join waste Pipes from toilets and bathrooms to the main soak away 3. Plumb line: a Pipe of string with a small heavy object tied to one end used for measuring the depth of water or for Checking whether something such as wall is built exactly upright or straight. 4. Sink a Large open Container that you ful with water and use for washing dishes in the Kitchen or for washing yourself. 5. Tap; It is a piece of equipment for Controlling the flow of water from a pipe or Container 6. Shower It is a piece of equipment that you stand under to wash your whole body

7. Water heater: an instrument used in heating water usually hung on the top side Corner of the bathroom. 8. Bath tub: It is a long Large Container that you fill with water and sit or lie in to wash yourself 9 Soak away: A Large deep pit dug on the ground where all the wastes from toilets and bathroom flow into. 10. Sewage: The mixture of waste from the human body and used water that is carried away from houses by pipe under the ground. 11. Toilet Seat: a closet where one sits to pass out feaces or urine. 12. Wash hand basin - A breakable basin fixed to a wall with a tap for hand washing. 13. Flush handle: A small iron handle use to flush toilet.

An auxiliary verb is a verb used with the Lexical main verb to show tense etc and to form questions and negatives. Auxiliary verbs are classified into two types a. primary Auxiliary - be, do, have b. Modal Auxiliary - may, shall, can. Primary Auxiliary verbs are not used exclusively as auxiliary.They have four main functions. 1. They function as main verb eg

Used to form passive transformations in English Language eg He was given another chance by the principal 4. As auxiliary eg. They were playing I have brought a new dress I did enjoy the food. title: CONTINUOUS WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: SPEECH WRITING Speech writing is a formal writing that a person delivers to an audience, which requires the ability to speak and write. Format of a good speech writing a. Write the title of the speech b. Greet the audience present starting from the most important c. Express delight of opportunity given to you to deliver the speech d. Bring in some humour, rhetorical questions, proverbs, quotation, local idioms/slangs etc e. Present both sides of an issue depending on the purpose of the speech f. Sum up and give your final opinion on the issue g. Thank the audience for listening patiently h. Append your full name and designation Features comprise of language and tone to used in speech writing a. Speech is supposed to be given to a live audience. Conversational English is needed, use short forms of words such as I’m, you’re, and they’re b. Use short simple words and sentences for clarity. c. Use local slangs if the speech is for local audience. d. Use suitable writing expression embedded in proverbs, questions and idioms etc. e. Use personal pronouns such as I, we, us, our, they etc. Major Features of a Speech (a). It must contain a heading or the type- a speech could be a welcome address, a farewell speech, or an appreciation etc. you should state what your speech is all about in a topic sentence. E.g. A Farewell address presented to Mr. Smart, the head of Visual Arts Department of Government Secondary School, Gwarinpa. Abuja. (b). Identification Data – This includes the name of the presenter, the official position, event, venue, date and time of the speech. E.g. …….. by Miss Zana Ayum, the senior prefect of the school, during the teacher’s send forth party at the school Hall on July 24 th , 2016 (c). Salutation – The Principal, Vice Principal, precious teacher Mrs. Ugah, respected members of staff and my fellow students (d). Body – This constitutes the speech itself which must be written in paragraphs observing all the rules in essay writing (e) Signature / Full name/ Designation – Here, the speechwriter should put down his/her signature, full name and official position if available. If the writer is writing on behalf of the other students, he/she must indicate it. Kinds of Speeches (a). Informative – when you deliver an informative speech, your intent is to enlighten your audience to increase understanding and creating awareness (b). Persuasive – your intent is to persuade your audience to agree with your point of view, to change attitudes or beliefs to bring about a specific desired action (c). Entertaining speech – Here, your intent is to entertain, inspire, or humour your audience In all of the above, here are minor difference in style, language, presentation, and address. Assignment Read up the written speech sample and try modelling it.

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Adjectives (Types and Order) Adjectives are words that describe nouns. She explains that adjectives work with nouns all the time. Eg. Short, long, beautiful, young, dark big, new etc. Types of Adjectives 1. Adjectives of quality. Eg. Good, delicious, terrible, evil, bad 2. Adjectives of quantity : ten, fifteen, many, more, second 3. Adjectives of colour : Blue, Greenish, Pinkish, Purple 4. Adjectives of size and shape : tall, round, fat, small 5. Adjectives of origin : Nigerian, Metallic, wooden Order of Adjectives It is possible to modify a particular noun with more than one adjective but that there is an order in which this could be done. ( NOSASCOM ) NUMBER- few, many, one OPINION-delicious, horrid, lovely SIZE-large, small, tiny AGE- young, old, new SHAPE- rectangular, circular, round COLOUR- red, green, white, yellow, blue ORIGIN- American, Chinese, French, British MATERIAL- leather, ceramic, plastic, steel, copper PURPOSE- gardening, shopping, riding Adjectives are never plural, therefore, when the adjective contains a number and noun, the noun associated with the number is singular. Eg A. This is a three year old car – Correct B. This is a three years old car – Incorrect If you want to buy a car and you are asked what kind of car you want, you may say: I want to buy a blue car

I want to buy a new car I wait to buy a European car I want to buy a beautiful car With the help of order of adjectives, the above sentences could be written as one sentence Eg. I want to buy a beautiful, new, blue, European car. Comparing Adjectives (Degrees of Comparison) Adjectives can be recognized by some suffixes such as –ous, -ful, -less, -ish, -able, -ic etc. she goes on to discuss the comparative and superlative forms of adjectives. Eg. Positive : This is simple adjectives for example: tall, fat, short, long Comparative : This is used to compare two things. It can be formed by adding ‘er’ or ‘more’ to an adjective. Eg. Bigger, more beautiful. Superlative : This compares more than two things. This is formed by adding ‘est’ or ‘most’. E.g. Bigger, most beautiful. Positive Comparative Superlative Easy Easier Easiest Happy Happier Happiest Intelligent More Intelligent Most intelligent Difficult More difficult Most difficult Careless More careless Most Careless Responsible less responsible least responsible Other Adjectives with Different Comparative and Superlative Positive Comparative Superlative Good Better Best Bad worse worst Ill worse worst Little less least Many more most Far Farther Farthest

title: WORD STRESS
subject: English Language
rawText: MONOSYLLABIC AND POLYSYLLABIC WORDS Stress is the degree of force placed on a word or part of a word in speech. While a syllable is the smallest meaningful unit of a word. A word may have one or more syllables and it is part of these syllables that the stress is placed on, that is why it is important to learn about syllables. Monosyllables are words with just one syllable while polysyllables are words with more than two syllables. For example Monosyllabic words are : man, girl, beg, pen, pot, bin, law, set, bat, pat, leg, pan, pen, peth, tap, lip Polysyllabic words are: transplant, table, export, pacify, paragraph, education, demo crate, mathematics, international, possibility, innocent, chalkboard. RULES 1. Monosyllabic words are usually stress in isolation when pronounced eg. AGE, BEAST, CLASS etc 2. In word of two syllables, prefixes and suffixes are not stressed. Eg. re’PORT, un’DO, BEAST’ly 3. When a word is used as a noun, the first syllable is stressed but the same word is used as a verb, the second syllable will attract stress. Eg. Noun VERB CONvict conVICT REcord reCORD INcrease inCREASE EScort esCORT SUBject subJECT 4. Words ending in –ion, -ic, -cal, -ial, -ian, are stressed on the second syllable from the end of the word. Eg. dis CU ssion, o CCA sion, draMAtic,testimonial, civilian. 5. Words that end in -ate, -cal-, -ty, and –al are stressed on the third syllable from the end eg. co MMU nicate, DE dicate, eco NO mical, hu MI lity, educational 6. Words ending in –ism are stressed on the first syllable eg. FUNC tionalism, So cialism 7. Words ending in –ish are stressed on the syllable before the –ish. Eg. mal NOUR ished, FLOU rish 8. Words ending in –fy are stressed on the third to the last syllable eg. CLA rify, dis QUA lity, DIG nity, in TEN sify Class-Work B reak the words below into syllables and place stress on the appropriate syllable. WEB master, SEC ondary, De licate, FOR tunate, PRE sently, QUAN tity, CHA racter, Ba chelor , SYM plify, SYL lable, DIS cussion, o CCA sion, pro JEC tion, dra MA tic, exami NA tion, ci VI lian, superin TEN dent, agri CUL tural, funda MEN tally etc. Assignment Using the above rules guiding stress, place appropriate stress on the following words. - table, flourish, communicate, favouritism, television

title: SPEECH WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Speech Writing A speech is a talk or spoken address or a written version of it given by a speaker. A formal address or discourse delivered to an audience by a speaker. Speeches are meant to entertain, educate and inform. They are also written to motivate people to action. Examples: presidential speech, the principal’s speech, welcome speech, farewell speech or addresses. Speech writing is the art of writing a speech for public presentation. Speech Writing is an art of conveying a message to your audience. Either through oral communication or through other means, such as PowerPoint slides. Speech writing has the same function as normal writing. The reasons for writing are to inform, to explain or to persuade. In a speech, typically the main purpose is to persuade the listener/reader to take up and support your views. What can differentiate a speech from a normal essay is that your audience can be from all sorts of backgrounds There are certain things you need to keep in mind when writing a speech. They are: - the ability of the audience to understand you, who your audience is, time limits, and being able to get your point across the first time through. Parts of a speech The Heading The Salutation Introduction to the body of the essay. The Body of the speech. The Heading: This should be written clearly indicating the following: Type of speech Name of speaker Title of speaker Occasion Place Date and time. Example of the Heading: A farewell address given by Dr. Umar, the Vice Principal Academics, Girls College Karu on the

send off party of Mr Janda, the Principal of the College at the Assembly hall on the 21st of May, 2020 at 10am. Salutation: The names of people to be recognized are written out in the order of their status or importance. Use the appropriate greeting for the audience. Example : Good Afternoon, Mr Chairman, His Excellency the Governor of Kogi State, special Guest of Honour, Honourable Commissioners, Your Royal Highness, The principal, Staff and Students, Ladies and Gentlemen. NOTE: the first letter of each key word in the salutation is written in capital letters Introduction to the body of the speech. This must be interesting and captivating so as to elicit the interest of the listeners. Start by indicating your gratitude for being given the opportunity to deliver the speech, or you indicate your great pleasure in making the speech. Next, you state the topic of the speech. Example: It gives me great pleasure…… I feel honored ……. I feel privileged to have been requested to give this speech. I have come here to deliver a farewell address in honour of our retired principal, Mr Janda.. The Body of the Speech Paragraphs should be logically presented and only a point should be discussed in each paragraph. Formal expressions and vocabulary should be used. The speech should be written with the first person pronoun ‘I’. End your speech by thanking your listeners.

pages.text: MONOSYLLABIC AND POLYSYLLABIC WORDS Stress is the degree of force placed on a word or part of a word in speech. While a syllable is the smallest meaningful unit of a word. A word may have one or more syllables and it is part of these syllables that the stress is placed on, that is why it is important to learn about syllables. Monosyllables are words with just one syllable while polysyllables are words with more than two syllables. For example Monosyllabic words are : man, girl, beg, pen, pot, bin, law, set, bat, pat, leg, pan, pen, peth, tap, lip Polysyllabic words are: transplant, table, export, pacify, paragraph, education, demo crate, mathematics, international, possibility, innocent, chalkboard. RULES 1. Monosyllabic words are usually stress in isolation when pronounced eg. AGE, BEAST, CLASS etc 2. In word of two syllables, prefixes and suffixes are not stressed. Eg. re’PORT, un’DO, BEAST’ly 3. When a word is used as a noun, the first syllable is stressed but the same word is used as a verb, the second syllable will attract stress. Eg. title: ADVERBIAL PHRASES AND THEIR GRAMMATICAL FUNCTIONS
subject: English Language
rawText: Adverbial Phrases and Their Grammatical Functions An adverbial phrase is a phrase that functions as an adverb, modifying a verb, adjective, or another adverb. It provides more information about the manner, time, place, frequency, or degree of an action or state. Sentences 1. "She sings with great enthusiasm." (Adverbial phrase "with great enthusiasm" modifies the verb "sings") 2. "He drives very carefully." (Adverbial phrase "very carefully" modifies the verb "drives") 3. "They arrived at the station." (Adverbial phrase "at the station" modifies the verb "arrived") Types of adverbial phrases: 1. Manner adverbials: Describe how something is done (e.g., "She sings *with passion*"). 2. Time adverbials: Indicate when something happens (e.g., "We'll meet *at 5 o'clock*"). 3. Place adverbials: Indicate where something happens (e.g., "They live *in the city*"). 4. Frequency adverbials: Indicate how often something happens (e.g., "We exercise *every day"). 5. Degree adverbials: Indicate the extent or degree of an action or state (e.g., "He's *extremely intelligent").

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: ADVERBIAL PHRASE A group of words that describe when, where, how, or why something happens. An adverbial phrase is a group of words which act together like an adverb to add further detail (to modify) to a verb, adjective, or other adverbs in a sentence. They can be made up of prepositions, nouns, gerunds, and more. Its purpose is to add detail and description to sentences. Types of adverbial phrases are that of time, place, manner and reason. Examples 1. Adverbial Phrase of Manner : An adverbial phrase of manner states how something is done. a. I will sit in silence . b. She sleeps like a baby. 2. Adverbial Phrase of Place : An adverbial phrase of place states where something happens. a. The cat hid under the bed . b. He went to the market and he couldn’t get anywhere to park . c. The man was stabbed in the back . 3. Adverbial Phrase of Time : An adverbial phrase of time states when something happens or how often. a. We will leave tomorrow . b. I’ll come in 10 minutes . c. He visits my house everyday . 4. Adverbial Phrase of Reason : An adverbial phrase of reason states why something happened. a. I went to the store to buy milk . b. To move the snake away , I guided it to creep on a long stick. ACTIVITY 1. He spoke to the class in a polite tone. 2. We are opening a new branch very soon. 3. He joined boxing classes to learn self-defense. 4. We will meet in the park.

Theme: Structure. Unit Topic : Tags questions. Lesson Topic: formation of tag questions. Question tags are short responses at the end of sentences in Speech. Question tag are not used for asking questions but for The confirmation of what the speaker already knows. There are Six (6) ways of forming Tag question 1. Positive statement + nagatine tag: positive response. When you require a yes answer, use a positive statement and a negative tag. Examples: a. I can do it , Can't I? b. We are right, aren't we? c. she is going, Isn't she? 2. Negative Statement attract positive tags. a. He is not here, is he? b. No you are not hungry, are you? 3. The finite auxiliary or helping verbs are usually repeated in the tag. Examples a. He is eating the food, isn't he? b. we shall not die, shall we? c. They can do it, can't they? 4. the mam or lexical verbs uses do, does or did in the tag. Examples a. you don't care about her, do you? b. I didn't do that, did I? c. The girl cried bitterly, didn't she? 5 The subject in the tag question is a pronoun Example. a. musa didn't do that, did he? b. mary called you yesterday. didn't she? c. The sun is bright, isn't it?

6. The choice and tense of the auxiliary ( operator) are determined by the verb phrase in the main clause of statement. Examples a. David Jumps over the fence, doesn't he? (Present) b. David jumped over the fence, didn't he? (past) Special forms. I am your friend, aren't I? The above form is only possible when the statement is positive, the fag remains am I?.. eg a. I am not your friend, am I? Note, using need, let us rather, used to, example. a. We need to know, don't we? b. We need to ask him first, needn't we? c. You had rather say, wouldn't you? d. He used to lie, didn’t he?. Theme: summary Writing. Unit topic: How to write summary answer. Lesson Topic: Using simple sentences in Summary writing Lesson according the summary page titled "war on honest man" unit 11 Theme: Continuous writing Unit Topic Essay writing Lesson Topic: Argumentative Essay-features An argumentative essay is like a debate in which the writer is expected to argue logically in support or against a given topic. It aims of convincing the audience or the reader to share the

view point of the writer. It could be written or delivered orally as a debate. In a debate, a format is followed, while in ordinary argumentative essay the vocatives may not be necessary. In argumentative essay, the writer raises Points both "for" and against' and balance. While in debate, the writer takes a stand. Features / Format of Argumentative essay 1. The Topic: State the topic on the question. 2. The vocatives: This is the greeting to acknowledge the presence of members of the panel and the audience. Example: The chairman or the moderator, panel of Judges Accurate Time keeper, Co-debaters, Ladies and Gentlemen. 3. The introduction: In the Introductory Paragraph, the writer is expected to introduce him/herself and take a stand while stating the topic example." My name is.......a student of...... I am here to propose the motion which says that.......if there are certain key words in the topic, they have to be defined or explained quoting from a reliable source. 4. The body: The writer must state or give at least three strong points in favour of his/her stand to convince the Judges and the audience and win them to his/her side Also, good paragraphing is very Important and one points should be explained in paragraph. It is equally good for the writer to raise one or two points expected from the opponent and Counter them with good points 5. The Conclusion: the concluding paragraph requires the writer to reaffirm his position earlier taken. Example?" I once agam state without fear of Contradiction that................ Thanks for Listening. Assignment . You are the mam speaker in a debate on the topic: children of literate rate parents parents perform better in school than those of illiterate Parents . Write your argument for or against the motion.

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH ENVIRONMENT
subject: English Language
rawText:
Words Associated with Environment The environment refers to everything around us, both living and non-living things. It includes land, water, air, plants, animals, and human activities. Common Words Associated with the Environment 1. Pollution Pollution is the contamination of air, water, or land by harmful substances. 2. Deforestation Deforestation is the cutting down of trees without replacing them. 3. Climate Climate is the average weather condition of a place over a long period of time. 4. Erosion Erosion is the wearing away of soil by water, wind, or human activities. 5. Flooding Flooding occurs when water covers land that is normally dry. 6. Conservation Conservation is the protection and careful use of natural resources. 7. Recycling Recycling is the process of reusing waste materials to make new products. 8. Waste Disposal Waste disposal is the proper management and removal of waste materials. 9. Ecosystem An ecosystem is a community of living organisms interacting with their environment. 10. Greenhouse Effect The greenhouse effect is the warming of the earth caused by gases trapping heat in the atmosphere. Importance of Environmental Words

Learning words associated with the environment helps students to: Understand passages on environmental issues Communicate clearly about environmental problems Improve vocabulary and comprehension skills Answer examination questions correctly

title: ADJECTIVAL PHRASES AND THEIR GRAMMATICAL FUNCTIONS
subject: English Language
rawText: Adjectival Phrases and Their Grammatical Functions An adjectival phrase is a phrase that functions as an adjective, modifying a noun or pronoun. It typically consists of an adjective headword, often accompanied by modifiers or complements. Sentences 1. "The big red car drove down the street." (Adjectival phrase "big red" modifies the noun "car") 2. "The very tired student fell asleep." (Adjectival phrase "very tired" modifies the noun "student") 3. "The difficult-to-solve problem stumped everyone." (Adjectival phrase "difficult-to-solve" modifies the noun "problem") Grammatical functions: 1. Modifying a noun: Adjectival phrases typically modify nouns or pronouns, providing more information about their qualities, properties, or characteristics. 2. Describing or qualifying: Adjectival phrases describe or qualify the noun or pronoun they modify, helping to identify, distinguish, or specify it. 3. Providing additional information: Adjectival phrases can provide additional information about the noun or pronoun, such as its size, shape, color, origin, or other attributes.

Theme: Speech Unit topic: Stress in sentences Lesson Topic: sentential/Emphatic stress. Emphatic stress is also known as sentential stress or contrastive stress. It is the act of stressing a particular word more than other words in a sentence such a stress is important in conveying the appropriate meaning or information. Emphatic stress is different from primary Stress because while a whole word is stressed in a sentence to indicate emphatic Stress, just a syllable is stressed on a word to Indicate primary stress. Note that a Lexical item such as noun, verb, adjective, or adverb is usually stressed in sentences. Grammatical such as Pronouns, determiners, auxiliary verbs, Conjunctions, etc are not usually stressed that notwithstanding, any class of word can be stressed in a sentence if any important or special emphasis or message is intended. Examples 1. The child broke the MIRROR (not the plate) 2 James BORROWED my shirt ( he did not steal nor buy it) 3. I placed the cup on the table (not under) 4. We cooked the food (not any other person) 5. John bought NEW bicycle (not an old one) To indicate emphatic stress, a sentence is given and a word is written in capital Letter (indicating stress). Some questions an asked from which an appropriate option is selected as the best question meant for the Statement given. Examples: 1. Students must study HARD to pass their exams. a. Why must study hard to pass their exams? b. Why must students study hand? c. How must students study to pass their exams d. when must students study to pass their exams 2. Honesty is Always the best policy. a. Is honesty always the best policy? b. Is honesty always the worst policy? C.is dishonesty always the best policy?

d. Is honesty seldom the best policy? The tips needed while reading for Implied meaning Include: 1. Keep asking question as you reads; question such as where, when? why?, How ?, will shed more light to the content of the passage. 2. You will note that subtle expressions αre laden with deeper meaning. keep linking ideas as you read on to understand the writer's line of development. This will enable you know when a gap is created 3. Your background knowledge of a topic or your past experience may assist you to decipher a hidden or implied meaning in the Passage 4. If something is amiss you assume what has happened. This assumption will help you draw Conclusions and subsequently help you locate the implied meaning. This means that It qualifies or tells us more about a noun or pronoun in the sentence. Therefore, any clause which l gives more information about a noun or pronoun is an adjectival clause. It can also be called a relative clause. It is introduced by the following (wh) words. who, whom, which, whose, where, when thats etc. Eg 1. Adamu followed the road which was very rough function of qualifies the noun "road" 2. Okoye met the girl who insulted his father

It qualifies the noun girl" 3. He showed me the place where his friend kept the bag: function It qualities the noun places. 4. These are the books which I bought last week . It qualifies the noun books". Theme: Continuous Writing. Unit topic : article writing Lesson Topic: Article witting (introduction, illustration and practice). An article is a piece of writing on national or regional issues of public Interest, usually meant for publication in of magazine of a newspaper. Note that in writing an article, the writer expresses his /her views or opinion on a given topic with good and logical points or facts. Features/format of an Article A. The title: It should be clearly written. Eg: The falling standard of Edicatan in Nigeria B. Introduction: This paragraph should introduce your topic or review whether people had written previously on the topic C. Body: This should contain relevant points discussed extensively and logically to give a clear understanding of the topic in question points raised should be discussed and arrange Paragraphs D. Conclusion: This is where the writer makes suggestions for solutions. E. Closure: It requires only the name of the writer and location where he/she is writing from Furthermore, your location should be your class in the school if the article is meant for a school publication. On the other hand d, your location should be the state from which you write if the article is meant for a national publication, Note that Signature is not needed! NOTE, the language of an article is formal and straight forward. Slangs are not required. Some article topics for publication include: 1. Insecurity in Nigeria. 2. Unemployment problem in the country. 3. High rate of kidnapping / human trafficking in Nigeria. 4. the falling standard of education in Nigeria. 5 Drug abuse among Nigeria youths. Assignment

write an article suitable for publication in a national newspaper on the growing Incidence of drug abuse among the youth, Stating the causes and Suggesting the way It can be curbed. Question and Answer WASSCE 2019.

rawText: UNSTRESED VOWEL SOUND /Ə/ SCHWA Unstressed vowels are sounds that are not pronounced with as much emphasis as stressed vowels. They are often found in unstressed syllables, which are not as important as stressed syllables. In English, unstressed vowels are often pronounced as a schwa sound, which is short, neutral sound. The schwa sound is represented the symbol /Ə/. It is pronounced like ‘uh’. Examples: ‘a’: alone, agree, announce, attend, agenda, allow, about, again, away ‘er’: teacher, sister, mother, father, brother ‘ re’ : nature, metre, centre ‘or’: pastor, tutor, tailor, creator, author, doctor ‘our’: colour, labour, honour EXERCISE 1. A book with words in A to Z order (10 letters, begins with d) Answer: dictionary 2. Rings, necklaces, bracelets and brooches. (9 letters, begins with j) Answer: jewellery 3. It means deadly or venomous, in the way some snakes are. (9 letters, begins with p) Answer: poisonous 4. How hot or cold something is. (11 letters, begins with t) Answer: temperature 5. Not the same as something else. (9 letters, begins with d) Answer: different 6. Wonderful, tremendous and absolutely amazing. (10 letters, begins with m) Answer: marvelous Assignment Search for more words in your dictionary that contain the weak sound and write down as many as you can get.

Adverbs (Types and Functions) Adverbs are modifiers (words or phrases added to another words to give a clearer picture). It could also be defined as member of a class of words that functions as modifiers of verbs or clauses Types of Adverbs 1. Adverb of Time – This shows when an action is done or happened. It answers the question ‘when’. It is placed at the beginning or at the end of a sentence. When they are at the beginning, they are often emphasized e.g (a). I phone you yesterday (b). I saw her a few month ago (c). Last week, I saw them walking together 2 . Adverb of Place – This shows where an action is done or performed. It answers the question ‘where’. Such adverb are placed after verb e.g (a). I live here (b). They are talking outside (c). We met her in the zoo (d). They walked along the river 3 . Adverb of Manner – This shows how an action or something is done. It answers the question ‘how’. The adverb is a place just after the verb when it is used in a sentence (a). She cried loudly (b). He drives speedily 4 . Adverb of Degree or Quantity – This answer the question ‘ to what degree’ , how much. It is usually placed before the adjectives and the adverb. (a) it is too dark for us to see anything (b). last night, it rained very heavily.

5 . Adverb of Frequency – This answer the question ‘ how often’ . Adverb of frequency are very important because we often use them. Examples include: never, seldomly, occasionally, sometimes, generally, usually, quick, always, already, nearly, almost, hardly etc. (a). Jane rarely late for work (b). We only write to each other occasionally 6 . Affirmative Adverb (Yes) and Adverb of Negation (No). Examples include Yes, Surely, certainly, indeed, by any means, not at all. (a). I hope my parents just for once will say yes to my latest idea (b). It would indeed help, if I had a body guard 7 . Interrogative Adverb – it answer question when, where, how, why, how much, often etc (a). When was the last time you saw her? (b). How could you have overlooked all these mistakes Functions of Adverbs 1. Adverbs modifies verb e.g She walks slowly 2. Adverbs modifies adjectives e.g The boldly written word 3. Adverbs modifies other adverbs e.g The thief acts really stupidly

subject: English Language
rawText: SEQUENCE OF TENSES Sequence of tenses is the order in which tenses appear in a sentence. It is a set of rules that determine how the tense of a subordinate clause depends on the tense of the main clause. Rules There are two major rules: 1. When an independent clause is in the past tense, any dependent clauses must also be in the past: Past follows past. E.G. a) The cat was bathing /because his feet were dirty. b) I knew /that he wanted to say something. c) I would do this/ if I were permitted. d) The patient had escaped / before the doctor came . 2. A present or future tense in the main clause might be followed by any tense required by the sense to convey in the subordinate clause. E. G a) I think / that the food is good. b) You know / that she sings like a nightingale. c) He will know/ that she is beautiful. d) He will think/that we did not invite him. 3. (Exception to Rule 1): A past tense in the principal clause might be followed by a present tense in the subordinate clause when the subordinate clause expresses some daily habit of a universal fact in a sentence. E. G. a) The teacher taught us /that the sun rises from the East. b) The king said /that all humans are mortal. 4. If the verb in the main clause is used with the past tense, the verb in the subordinate clause must be expressed by ‘might’ (past tense). E. G. a) He worked hard that he might win the tournament. b) He had been working hard that he might win the tournament. Class work a) No one could understand how the prisoner ----------from the prison. (escape) b) Italy declared war that she ----------------her empire. (extend) c) His health ------------ since he left the city. (improve)

rawText:
Theme: Speech Unit Topic Rhymes. Lesson Topic: Rhyming words. Rhyme occurs when two or more words end on the same Vowel Sound, the same Vowel plus Consonant sequence sound or in the same sequence of Consonant cluster. Rhyme does not occur when two word end in the same single final Consonant eg wood and did. This shows that sound determines rhyme, not spelling. This is because two word must have the same sound in the last syllable before they can be said to rhyme. The harmonization of sound rhymes Can either be in part of the words Involved or in the whole words. There are two types of rhyme. a. Total rhyme b. partial rhyme. a. In total thyme the similarity of the Sound of the words occur at both the Inital and final Positions.Eg- Sweet - Suite waist - waste hot - hut Root-route knot- nut Meat - meet born - burn Wood - Would b. In partial rhyme, the thyme is at the end of the word. Eg: rice - dice while-smile Purse- curse. keep-heap part - heart. fond - pond pure. - sure. some - come comb - tomb. Fright - tight

Theme: Structure Unit Topic: Adjuncts. Lesson Topre: Types of adjuncts Adjuncts are forms of adverbs which answer the questions how, where when, wing under what Condition, to what degree, how often, for how long.. etc. Adjunct is a word or group of words added to a sentence to modify the meaning of the verb, adjective other adverbs and Sometimes modify a whole sentence. Adjuncts in order words are adverbs of time, place, direction reason/cause, result, purpose, duration, frequency comparison, Condition and Concession. Some adjuncts appear as single words while other paper as adverbial phrases and clauses. Types of Adjuncts 1. Adjunct of time: It tells us when an action took place and it answer the question when? a. He was admitted into the college Last year. 2 Adjunct place; It tells us where an action took place. It answer the question where? a. the food is on the table b. I was in the office when my wife return. 3. Adjunct of degree /manner: It show how an action is done. Example. quickly, bravely, happily, hand, fast, well etc. a. He came back home as quickly as possible. b. He caught the Boll as if he were a good keeper. 4. Adjunct of Reason/ Purpose: It shows why an action is taking place. Examples. Since, because,hence etc. 1. the woman went to church since it was agree on 2. The minister was Sacked because of bribery. 5. Adjunct of frequency: describes how often an action happens. Example always, usually, normally, often Sometimes, rarely and never. a. I have never insulted him. b. she comes here often 6. Adjunct of Condition: establish the condition in which an action occars or state holds. a. I would go to lagos, If I had the money.

b. you will be jailed unless the president says otherwise. 7. Adjuncts of concession (in spite of) It offers a statement which Contrasts with the mam Idea. it offen starts with one of the following Subordinating Conjunctions: "though, although, even though, while, whereas or even if a. A Loud voice cannot compete with a clear vorce, even if it's a whisper b. She Laughed where as I told him not to. title: FALLING TONE
subject: English Language
rawText:
FALLING TONE A falling tone, also known as a dropping tone, is a type of intonation pattern in speech where the pitch of the voice falls or drops at the end of a sentence or phrase. It's like your voice is going down a slide. Falling tones often: 1. Indicate a statement or declaration 2. Show finality or completion 3. Can sound assertive or definitive Example: "I'm going home." (voice falls on "home") Want more examples or need help with anything else? 😊 1. Statements: - "I'm going to the store." - "She's eating breakfast." - "The meeting is at 3 PM." 2. Declarative sentences: - "I love reading books." - "He's a great teacher." - "The weather is nice today." 3. Commands: - "Close the door." - "Stop talking." - "Eat your dinner." 4. Exclamations: - "What a beautiful day!" - "I'm so excited!" - "That's amazing!"

In these examples, the voice tends to fall at the end, indicating finality or assertiveness.

title: LITIRESO
subject: English Language
rawText:
EKA ISE: LITIRESO AKOLE ISE: LITIRESO ALOHUN TO JE MO AYEYE. Litireso je ona ti Yoruba n gba lati fi ero inu won han lori ohun ti a je koko tabi iriri aye won. ISORI LITIRESO Litireso alohun Litireso apileko Litireso alohun ni litiresso ti a fi ohun enu gbe jade ti a jogun lati odo awon babanla wa. Litireso apileko ni litireso ti a se akosile re nigba ti imo moo ko – moo ka de si ile wa. Litireso alohun ajemayeye Eyi ni awon litireso ti a n lo lati gbe asa laruge nibi ayeye gbogbo. Awon ewi alohun ajemayeye niwonyi, Ekun iyawo Dadakuada Bolojo Etiyeri Rara

Alamo Oku pipe Efe abbl EKUN IYAWO Eyi ni ewi ti a maa n lo ni ibi ayeye ti omobinrin ti n lo si ile oko. O je ewi ti omobinrin ti o n lo si ile oko maan sin lojo igbeyawo lati je ki a mo pe oun mo riri, itoju ti awon obi se nigba ti oun wa ni ewe. Ewi yii wopo laarin agbegbe bi, iseyin ikirun, Ede, Osogbo, oyo, ogbomoso. Ekun iyawo je ewi ti o nko wondia leko lati pa ara re mo titi di ojo igbeyawo. Apeere ekun iyawo sisun Iya mo n lo Mo wa gbare temi n to maa lo E ba sure ki n lowo lowo E ba sure ki n sowo, n jere E ba sure ki n bimo lemo E ba sure ki n ma kelenini loode oko

Ire loni, ori mi a fi re Hi hi hihin (ekun) ETIYERI Etiyeri je ere awon odo okunrin ni gbegbe oyo. Awon ohun elo orin etiyeri ni, Agogo, ilu sakara, sekere. Etiyeri maa n gbe ago/eku bori bi egungun sugbon kii bo gbogbo ara re tan. olori ti o gbe ago wo ni yoo maa le orin ti awon yooku yoo si maa gbe. Oro awada, eebu, yeye, apara, po ninu orin etiyeri bee ni oro bi epe bi epe ni won fi n se ihure won Apeere Lile: Mo setan Eyin menugun Mo setan ti n o rode Kikona ko ma ko mi lona o Egbe: Ha ha ha, mo se tan

Eyin menugun Mo setan ti n o rode Kikona ko ma ko mi lona o Lile: mo setan Eyin menugun Mo setan ti n o korin Ko gbigba ko ma gba mi lohun o Egbe: Mo se tan Eyi menugun Mo setan ti n o korin Kogbigba ko ma gba mi lohun o…… DADAKUADA

Ewi yii je adapo ilu ati orin. Iwulo orin dadakuada Won fi n ki eniyan Won fi n panilerin Won fi n bu eniyan Won fi n kilo iwa Won fi n toka aleebu awujo Orin Dadakuada wopo ni agbegbe Ilorin, awon okunrin ni o saaba maa n se ere yi. Olori yoo ma le orin, enikan yoo si maa soro lori orin naa ki awon elegbe to gbe e. Apeere: “Ko sohun t’olorun o lee se Amo ohun t’olorun le se ti o ni Se lopo Keeyan o geri maagoro ko ka Ibepe ni be Oloun le se e o Amo bo ba se e, iru wa o tu bu

Emi mo pe n o lee j’Alaafin oyo Laelae Iwo naa o si lee joba ilu Ilorin wa Afonja enu dun juyo waa te Yan – an – yan”.

title: CONTINUOUS WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: CREATIVE WRITING Creative writing is literary work produced by students themselves. It can be a short story, a drama piece or poem. Features of a Good Story (a). Theme – A short story must have a central point from which a story is developed. E.g. i. crimes never goes unpunished. ii. One good turn deserves another. (b). Plot – It must have a story line. This is simply the order the story follows to develop the theme including the result confirming the theme e.g. The plot of ‘crime’ never goes unpunished must feature a bad character or a villain who committed a crime on several occasion and got away with that initially but eventually one caught and brought book. (c). Characters – The story must show who and who took part in the action/events of the story for it to be real or unreal. These characters must have names and interact among themselves through the use of dialogue (d). Setting – The story must tell its readers where interaction and when the events/action took place (e). It must have a beginning, a climax, an anti-climax and a conclusion. Three models (1). From the beginning On the 16 th April 2009, I set out with my Sister Obiageli for our Grandma’s at Bodija in Ibadan about five kilometers away from our house in the University of Ibadan. (2). From the Climax Watch Out! I shouted. The driver swerved but it was too late. A trailer overtaking at top speed had brushed the bus conveying us to Grandma’s house. The rest story was sad to tell. I lay on my pool of blood. I managed a fainted cry…………. (3). From the conclusion Can I ever walk again? In my dream of entering a University, this session is over? Would I had listened to the voice of wisdom. These were my words a regret as I remember the 16 th April, 2011 when I set out with my Sister Obiageli for………….. ASSIGNMENT: Write a short story about your family background

rawText: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH COMMERCE Commerce is business of buying and selling of commodities; especially the exchange of merchandise on a large scale, between different places or communities. Some Words Associated with Commerce Share, Stock, Shareholder, Stock broker, Invest, Account, Advance, Agreement, Allotment, Annuity, Assessment, Asset, Tariff, Lease, Liabilities, Profit, Profit and Loss Account, Profit gained, Dividend, Bank, Bargain, Bill, Cash, Credit, Contract, Income, Investment. Meaning of Some Words 1. Share : This is one of the equal parts into which the ownership or the capital of a company is divided. A person can buy or sell shares. 2. Shareholder : Someone who owns shares in a company or business. 3. Invest : This is the act of buying shares with the hope that the value will increase with time and the investor can make profit. This investment gives you the right of ownership. 4. Profit : This is the money that someone or company gains by selling things or doing business after the costs have been paid. 5. Dividend : It is the profit of a company or firm distributed among stock holders according to the amount invested. The individual portions of the profits are called dividends. title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: VERB FORMS : ACTIVE AND PASSIVE VERBS T o discuss the active and pa ssive voice in English Language , students need a knowledge of the function of a verb as either ‘subject’ or ‘object’ . ‘ Voice’ denotes the relationship between the verb and the subject or object in a sentence. A verb is said to be in active voice when it tells us what a person or thing does. E.g. The teacher picked up the marker. And a verb is said to be in passive voice when it tells us what is done to someone or something. E.g. The marker was picked up by the teacher. PURPOSES OF PASSIVE VERBS IN ENGLISH LANGUAGE 1. When the speaker wants to focus on the action E.g. The kettle was stolen. What is the important to the speaker is the fact that the kettle has been stolen. 2. If the speaker does not know the doer of the action e.g. A. This letter was tampered with B. My car window was broken 3. Sometimes, the writer may want to shield the identity of the doer. This is commonly used by reporters or pressmen. Eg. A. I was told that you took the pen B. The manager was directed to write the letter discussing the man. 4. If the listeners or the audience already know the doer A. John was arrested yesterday B. The children are well trained Passive expressions are mostly used in academic writing, in official letter and by journalists because of the above listed reasons Class-Work Change the following active sentences to passive sentences. 1. Someone took it from the window 2. They sent us out of the class 3. They nominated twenty prefects 4. My uncle bought a book 5. My sister gave me a bowl of custard

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: Adverbial Clauses Adverb is a word or a group of words that modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs in a sentence. Adverbial clause just like adverb tells how, when, where, why, to what extent or under what condition, the action of the main verb is performed. Adverbial clauses modify the verbs, adjectives and another adverb in a given sentence. They are often introduced in sentences by words such as: (subordinating conjunctions) After, because, until, although, even though, when, as long as, except, while as If, if, where, as soon as, in order that, whenever, provided that, for, since etc. 1. Adverbial clause of time : tells us when the action of the main verb took place (a) I was eating when the man arrived (modifies the verb “was eating”) (b) As soon as he came in, the work started (modifies the verb, “started”) 2. Adverbial clause of place : tells where the action of the verb took place. (a) Children can play wherever they like (modifies the verb, “can play”) (b) She left the bag where it could be found (modifies the verb, “left”) 3. Adverbial clause of manner : shows how the action of the main verb is performed. title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH AGRICULTURE AND HORTICULTURE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Words Associated with Agriculture and horticulture Agriculture Definition: Agriculture is the art and science of cultivating crops and rearing animals for food, clothing, shelter, medicine, and other useful products for humans. Horticulture Definition: Horticulture is a *branch of agriculture* that deals with the *intensive cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants* usually in gardens, orchards, or greenhouses. Words & Meanings 1. Agronomy Meaning: The science of soil management and crop production for field crops like maize, rice, millet. It’s a branch of agriculture focused on staple foods. 2. Irrigation Meaning: Artificial supply of water to farmland or gardens through canals, sprinklers, or drip systems to support crop growth during dry seasons. 3. Compost Meaning: Decayed organic matter like plant waste, food scraps, and animal dung used as natural fertilizer to improve soil fertility in farms and gardens. 4. Pruning Meaning: Cutting off dead, diseased, or unwanted branches of plants to improve shape, growth, and fruit production. Very common in horticulture for fruit trees and ornamentals. 5. Mulching Meaning: Covering the soil surface with materials like dry grass, leaves, or plastic to conserve moisture, control weeds, and regulate soil temperature. 6. Hybrid Meaning: A crop variety produced by crossing two different parent plants to get better yield, disease resistance, or quality. E.g. hybrid maize, hybrid tomatoes. 7. Nursery Meaning: A place where young seedlings are raised under special care before transplanting to the main farm or garden. Common in horticulture and forestry.

8. Pesticide Meaning: Chemicals used to kill or control pests like insects, fungi, and weeds that attack crops. Examples: insecticides, fungicides, herbicides. 9. Harvesting Meaning: The process of gathering mature crops from the field or garden when they are ripe. Done manually or with machines like combine harvesters. 10. Grafting Meaning: A horticultural technique where the stem of one plant (scion) is joined to the root/stem of another (rootstock) so they grow as one. Used to combine good fruit quality with strong roots. Common in mango, citrus.

subject: English Language
rawText:
26th April,2024. CONCORD Concord is the grammatical agreement between the different parts of speech in a sentence. It is also when a subject of a sentence and the verb of a sentence agree. RULES OF CONCORD The rules says that the verb must agree with the subject in terms of numbers. Concord has many rules, some of them are as follows: Rule 1. Singular subject takes singular verb. Examples: - He runs -She is a lovely person. Rule 2. A plural subject take a plural verb. Examples -The men are playing. -we study hard Rule 3. When a sentence has two or more singular subjects joined by 'and' the verb should be plural. Examples: -The book,pen, and the pencil are on the table -The boy and the girl are related. Rule 4. Singular subject that is followed by a phrase or clause takes singular verb. Examples - The boy who has the cars is here. -Jane, like John is smart. Rule 5. Two singular subject joined by neither...nor, either...or is followed by a singular verb. Examples: -Neither June nor James knows the answer. -either Mary or Aisha forget the key. When the other subject is plural. Examples: - Neither Ade nor the students are at the occasion. The verb agree with the subject closes to it.

Rule 6.Compound sentence connected with and takes singular verb. Examples: - Butter and bread is sweet. -Rice and beans is my favorite meal. Rule 7. Plural subject that called for singular verb are: - Ninety five cents is my money. -Twenty minutes is all I have to prepare for the exam. Rule 8.Subject that are collective noun takes singular verb. Examples: -The staff is in a meeting. -The team is due to fly out Note: The following words all take singular verb: Each, everyone, everybody, anybody, anyone, someone, somebody Nobody, none,no one, each other, one another etc takes singular verb. Examples: -Each candle is burning. -Nobody is going out. - None of us is to blame. ASSIGNMENT Fill in the blanks space in the following sentences: 1. The window_____ open. 2.The pages _____ held together by staple. 3.The creator and giver of life ______God. 4. Elisha and Ruth ____ New project manager. 5. Neither the man nor the women ____ at the room.

title: EXPOSITORY ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
EXPOSITORY ESSAY An expository essay is a type of writing that explains, informs, or describes a topic in a clear, factual, and logical way. Simple definition: It’s writing that answers “What is it?” or “How does it work?” or “Why does it happen?” without trying to persuade you. Examples of expository topics: - How photosynthesis works - The causes of flooding in urban areas - The importance of reading An expository essay has 3 parts. 1. Introduction Get the reader’s attention and tell them what you’ll explain. 2. Body Explain the topic using facts, examples, and logic. - Usually 2-3 paragraphs. Each paragraph explains ONE main idea from your thesis. - Structure of each body paragraph: 1. Topic sentence: States the main idea of that paragraph. 2. Supporting details*: Facts, examples, statistics, steps. 3. Explanation: Show how the details prove your point. - Linking words keep it smooth: _first, next, however, for example, therefore_. _Example body paragraph for the phone topic:_ “First, mobile phones use signal transmission to connect calls. When you dial a number, your phone converts your voice into radio waves and sends them to the nearest cell tower. Without this process, communication would not be possible.” 3. Conclusion

Wrap up and leave the reader with a clear understanding. What it contains: - Restated thesis: Say your main idea again, but use different words. - Summary: Briefly remind the reader of the 2-3 main points from the body. - Closing thought: End with why it matters or a final clear statement. No new information. _Example_: “In conclusion, mobile phones function through signal transmission, data processing, and power management. Understanding these processes helps users appreciate the technology they use daily.” Quick way to remember: Intro= What I’ll explain Body = Here’s the explanation Conclusion = That’s what I explained

Agriculture Agriculture & Horticulture: Key Words & Meanings Agriculture large-scale farming of crops and livestock for food, fiber, and fuel Horticulture* = specialized branch focused on growing fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants, usually in gardens or controlled spaces. Common words associated with both: 1. Cultivation Preparing soil and growing plants. 2. Crop: Plant grown and harvested for use, e.g., maize, wheat. 3. SoiGrowing medium. Pest: Insects or animals that damage plants. 7. Pesticide/Herbicide: Chemicals to control pests and weeds. 8. Harvest Gathering mature crops. 9. Yield Amount of crop produced per area. 10. Propagation Creating new plants. In horticulture: cuttings, grafting, budding. Horticulture-specific words: - Orchard Land planted with fruit trees. - Nursery Place where young plants are raised. - Greenhouse: Controlled structure for plant growth. - FloricultureGrowing ornamental flowers. - OlericulturGrowing vegetables. - Pomology Study of fruit cultivation. Agriculture-specific words: - Agronomy Science of soil and crop management. - Livestock Farm animals like cattle, goats, poultry.

- Pasture:ll Land covered with grass for grazing. - Tillage Preparing land by plowing.

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText: POETRY Poetry is a genre or type of literature that uses language in a rhythmic and expressive way to evoke meaning. William Wordsworth famously writes: ‘poetry is the spontaneous overflow of powerful feelings: it takes its origin from emotion recollected in tranquility’. Types of Poetry Poems are categorised based on their meanings and structures. Some types of poetry are: 1. Elegy: a poem that reflects on death and loss, and often includes a theme of mourning. 2. Sonnet: a poem of 14 lines and usually about the topic of love with rhyme scheme 3. Ode: a poem that serves as a tribute/praise to a subject which can be a person or inanimate object 4. Free verse: this is a poem that does not follow any structure, it allows freedom in writing. 5. Lyrical: short and expressive poems that centre on feelings rather than story. title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: INTRODUCTION TO CLAUSES The teacher defines clause as a group of words that usually contain a subject and a verb (predicate). A clause has a finite verb. A Finite verb is finite when it is complete and a verb is complete when it has a subject and / or indicate number or tense. E.g. i. He comes here always. ii. The boys are irresponsible. iii. John eats too much. There are two types of clauses; i. Main or Independent Clause ii. Subordinate or Dependent Clause Main/Independent Clause – This is also known as independent clause. Main Clause is usually a simple sentence made up of a subject and a predicate that can stand-alone; thus, conveys full meaning. E.g. i. John ate. ii. Yemi came / she came yesterday. iii. The dog ate the raw meat. Subordinate Clause – This is also known as helping or dependent clause because it depends on the main clause for its full meaning. The subordinate or helping clause cannot stand-alone or convey full meaning E.g. i. When the children were sleeping, the dog came in and ate the raw meat. ii. As it continued to rain and there was no shelter in sight, we had to walk to the next village in the rain. Class-Work/Home-Work Identify the following clauses: i. I like bananas and I like grapes. ii. After she picks me up, Mum is taking me to buy shoes. iii. I first met her in Paris where I lived as a small child.

title: WORD ASSOCIATED WITH HEALTH
subject: English Language
rawText:
Words associated with Health. Health is the state of being free from illness or injury. Health is the freedom from disease or well - being (physical or mental). OR wholeness, a state of being whole, sound or well. The major classification can be; physical, emotional, social, spiritual, environmental and vocational. Words associated with Health are symptom, diagnosis, operation, cure, prescribe, hospital, clinic, maternity, wound, sickly, maternity, bruise, pain, patient, emergency, casualty, medicine, drug, abnormal, abstinence, ache, activity, addictive, aerobics, aids, allergy, anemia, anorexia, antidote, vitality, wellness, illness, disease, malnutrition, diagnose, vaccine, nutrition, hygiene, injection, contagious, chronic, dislocation, paralysis. 1. Infection: The act or process of causing or getting a disease. 2. Symptoms : A change in your body or mind that shows that you are not healthy. 3. Diagnose: To say exactly what an illness or the cause of a problem.

4. Chronic : Long lasting disease e.g pneumonia, tuberculosis 5. Convalescence: A Resting period of a sick person after recovery from an illness. 6. Sprain: Injury to a ligament /tendon Examples 1. An illness is diagnosed by a doctor 2. Disease can be infectious, contagious and fatal 3. An out patient receives treatment for his illness and goes home.

title: SUMMARY WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Summary Writing Summary is the shortening of a passage or text to its main points, using your own words. Guidelines to Follow 1. A summary forces you to understand the line of thought of a passage (argument) precisely 2. It helps you to identify the key facts in the passage 3. The examples and illustrations that help to give details about a point are usually not considered for summary passage 4. Be precise, be concise, be exact and direct to the point. title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: SENTENCE TYPES A sentence is a statement, a question or an order which usually contains a subject and a verb. Types of Sentences i. Simple sentence ii. Compound sentence iii. Complex sentence iv. Compound-Complex sentence Simple Sentence – This contains one idea or subject and a finite verb e.g. i. John ate ii. Yemi Came / she came yesterday iii. The dog ate the raw meat Compound Sentence – A compound sentence consists of at least two independent clauses with the use of ‘and’ E.g. i. Ada came and saw the food on the table. ii. Blessing clapped and danced in the church yesterday. Complex Sentence – This has one independent clause and two or more dependent clauses. i. When the children were sleeping, the dog came in and ate the raw meat. ii. As it continued to rain and there was no shelter in sight, we had to walk to the next village in the rain. Compound-Complex Sentence – This has two independent clauses and one or more dependent clauses e.g. i. I know that you always wanted to become a writer, but I always wanted to become a doctor.
