title: VOWEL /E/ AND /3:/
subject: English Language
rawText: VOWEL /e/ AND /3:/ Vowel sounds are sounds produced by the flow of air through the mouth without any obstruction, creating different sounds based on the shape of the lips, tongue, and vocal cords. Let's contrast the vowel sounds /e/ and /3ː/ (also represented as /ɜː/ in some transcriptions): 1. */e/* (as in "pet" or "bet"): This is a mid-front vowel sound, pronounced with the tongue positioned mid-way in the mouth and the lips unrounded. The sound is relatively short and sharp. 2. */3ː/* (as in "bird" or "nurse"): This is a central vowel sound, often referred to as the "schwa" sound when unstressed, but when stressed and long (as /3ː/), it's pronounced with the tongue positioned more centrally in the mouth. The lips are relaxed, and the sound is longer and more neutral. Key differences: - *Tongue position*: For /e/, the tongue is positioned more towards the front of the mouth, while for /3ː/, it's more central. - *Lip shape*: The lips are unrounded for both sounds, but the overall mouth shape is more open for /3ː/. - *Length*: /3ː/ is typically longer than /e/. - *Sound quality*: /e/ has a more distinct, sharp quality, while /3ː/ has a more neutral, relaxed quality. Examples: - /e/ : pet, bet, met - /3ː/ : bird, nurse, girl These sounds can be challenging for non-native speakers to distinguish, especially in certain accents.

title: EXPOSITORY ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText:
Expository Essay Expository Essay us an essay in which the writer is expected to expose or explain a given topic or object. The writer is expected to explain in full or details the object in question for a better understanding by the reader. Features of an Essay 1. The title/topic 2. Introduction 3. Body of the Essay in paragraphs 4. Conclusion 5. Name of the writer. Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome in Nigeria : causes, effects and solutions. The Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome otherwise called AIDS is undoubtedly a threatening disease in Nigeria inspite of the fact that some people still believe it is a myth meant to scare

people from enjoying themselves. However medical practitioners have confirmed that AIDS is actually present in Nigeria. There are still controversies about how AIDS developed and where it developed from. For some racial reasons, the whites have claimed that AIDS developed in African through a sexual union between man and some other animals, Africans have denied this and strongly maintained that AIDS did not and in fact could not have developed in African. Their Argument is based on the fact that the first incident of AIDS was recorded in the western world.

title: CONTINUOUS WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY An argumentative essay is a type of essay that takes a stance on an issue and argues for that stance. It is a formal piece of writing that requires you to research the issue, gather evidence, and present your argument in a clear and logical way. An argumentative essay is defined as a piece of writing that illustrates the writer’s part on a controversial issue and supports that position with evidence. FEATURES OF ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY The features of an argumentative essay include: 1. A clear thesis statement that states the writer’s position on the issue. 2. Evidence to support the thesis statement, such as facts, statistics, expert opinions and examples. 3. A logical argument that presents the evidence in a clear and orderly way. 4. A conclusion that summarises and restates the thesis statement. Note: not all argumentative essays are debate, but all debates are argumentative essays. In a debate, the writer knows the audience and setting. In a debate, the vocative is compulsory, that is, the writer should recognize the presence of the members of the audience. E.g The Chairman, panel of Judges, Co-debators, Ladies and Gentlemen, e.t.c. In an ordinary argumentative essay (not a debate), no audience is indicated and no vocative is necessary. Assignment You have been invited to participate in an inter-school debate competition to speak for or against the topic: ‘Corruption is worse than Armed Robbery’. Write out your contribution.

title: SPEECH COMPREHENSION VOCAB DEV:
subject: English Language
rawText:
LESSON NOTE: SPEECH COMPREHENSION 1. Meaning of Speech Comprehension Speech comprehension is the ability to listen to spoken language and understand the message being communicated. 2. Skills Required for Speech Comprehension • Active listening – paying full attention • Concentration – avoiding distractions • Note-taking – writing key points • Understanding tone and purpose • Identifying main ideas and supporting details LISTENING COMPREHENSION 1. Listening to Debate for Main Points A debate is a formal discussion where opposing sides present arguments. How to Identify Main Points in a Debate • Listen for key arguments from each speaker • Identify supporting facts and examples • Note repeated ideas (these are often important) • Distinguish between facts and opinions 2. Passing Judgment in a Debate To evaluate (judge) a debate, consider: • Clarity of arguments • Use of evidence and examples • Logical reasoning

• Confidence and delivery • Ability to convince the audience The winner is usually the speaker with the strongest, clearest, and most convincing argument. READING COMPREHENSION 1. Reading to Answer Questions on a Passage Reading comprehension involves carefully reading a passage and answering questions based on it. 2. Steps to Answer Questions Effectively 1. Read the passage carefully 2. Identify the main idea 3. Look for key details 4. Understand the meaning of difficult words from context 5. Answer questions clearly and correctly 3. Types of Questions • Literal questions – answers directly from the passage • Inferential questions – require thinking beyond the text • Vocabulary questions – meaning of words in context VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT (VOCAB DEV) 1. Meaning Vocabulary development is the process of improving one’s knowledge and use of words.

2. Methods of Vocabulary Development • Reading widely • Using a dictionary • Learning synonyms and antonyms • Practicing new words in sentences • Listening to speeches and debates WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH COMMERCE 1. Meaning of Commerce Commerce refers to the buying and selling of goods and services, especially on a large scale. 2. Common Commerce Vocabulary • Trade – buying and selling of goods • Market – place where goods are bought and sold • Profit – financial gain • Loss – financial setback • Capital – money used to start a business • Goods – items for sale • Services – activities offered for payment • Consumer – person who buys goods/services • Producer – person who makes goods • Supply – amount of goods available • Demand – desire for goods/services • Retail – selling in small quantities • Wholesale – selling in large quantities

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT
subject: English Language
rawText:
Words Associated with Agriculture and horticulture Agriculture Definition: Agriculture is the art and science of cultivating crops and rearing animals for food, clothing, shelter, medicine, and other useful products for humans. Horticulture Definition: Horticulture is a *branch of agriculture* that deals with the *intensive cultivation of fruits, vegetables, flowers, and ornamental plants* usually in gardens, orchards, or greenhouses. Words & Meanings 1. Agronomy Meaning: The science of soil management and crop production for field crops like maize, rice, millet. It’s a branch of agriculture focused on staple foods. 2. Irrigation Meaning: Artificial supply of water to farmland or gardens through canals, sprinklers, or drip systems to support crop growth during dry seasons. 3. Compost Meaning: Decayed organic matter like plant waste, food scraps, and animal dung used as natural fertilizer to improve soil fertility in farms and gardens. 4. Pruning Meaning: Cutting off dead, diseased, or unwanted branches of plants to improve shape, growth, and fruit production. Very common in horticulture for fruit trees and ornamentals. 5. Mulching Meaning: Covering the soil surface with materials like dry grass, leaves, or plastic to conserve moisture, control weeds, and regulate soil temperature. 6. Hybrid Meaning: A crop variety produced by crossing two different parent plants to get better yield, disease resistance, or quality. E.g. hybrid maize, hybrid tomatoes. 7. Nursery Meaning: A place where young seedlings are raised under special care before transplanting to the main farm or garden. Common in horticulture and forestry.

8. Pesticide Meaning: Chemicals used to kill or control pests like insects, fungi, and weeds that attack crops. Examples: insecticides, fungicides, herbicides. 9. Harvesting Meaning: The process of gathering mature crops from the field or garden when they are ripe. Done manually or with machines like combine harvesters. 10. Grafting Meaning: A horticultural technique where the stem of one plant (scion) is joined to the root/stem of another (rootstock) so they grow as one. Used to combine good fruit quality with strong roots. Common in mango, citrus.

Supply - The amount of a product or service available for sale at a given time. 2. Demand - The desire and ability of buyers to purchase a product or service. 3. title: PREFIXES AS WORD EXTENSION
subject: English Language
rawText: A prefix is a letter or group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning or create a new word. Prefixes can modify or extend the original word's meaning, often indicating things like location, time, direction, or intensity. For example: - un- (not) + happy = unhappy - re- (again) + cycle = recycle - eco- (environment) + friendly = eco-friendly - Bio- (life): biology, biodegradable, biosphere - Eco- (environment): ecology, ecosystem, eco-friendly - Geo- (earth): geology, geosphere, geothermal - Hydro- (water): hydrology, hydroelectric, hydrate - Re- (again): recycle, reuse, renew Some prefixes that can be used with environmental words: - Un- (not): unpolluted, unsustainable, unrecyclable - Non- (not): non-renewable, non-biodegradable, non-toxic - Multi- (many): multi-purpose, multi-layered, multi-functional - Co- (together): co-exist, co-friendly, co-preservation

rawText: COMMONLY MISSPELT WORDS Spelling refers to the correct arrangement of letters to form words in a language. In other words, spelling is about writing words correctly, using the right letters in the right order, so that others can understand and read what you've written. title: GRAMMAR
subject: English Language
rawText: TAG QUESTIONS A tag question is a statement followed by a mini question. We use it to ask for confirmation. Aspects of Tag Questions 1. The statement 2. Tag Aspect 3. Short answer aspect Tag Question Principle 1 . When a positive statement is made, it is normally followed by a negative tag question, then both will produce a short positive response 2. When the statement made as negative, a positive tag, is expected to follow then the two of them will result in a short negative response. Positive statement + Negative tag = positive response Negative statement + Positive tag = Negative response Note – in question tag, almost all auxiliary verbs are to be repeated in both the tag and the response. E. g. The weather is bright today, Isn’t it? Response – yes, it is. More examples 1. She will come for the meeting, Won’t she? Yes, she would. 2. She has gone home, hasn’t she? Yes, she has. 3. I didn’t do the job, did I? Yes, I did. EXERCISE From English past questions

title: CREATIVE WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: Creative writing is the art of writing in a way that expresses thoughts, feelings, and ideas in an imaginative and unique way. It's a form of self-expression that can take many forms, including: 1. Poetry 2. Short stories 3. Novels 4. Flash fiction 5. Scripts Creative writing often involves: 1. Using descriptive language to paint vivid pictures 2. Developing characters and plotlines 3. Exploring themes and emotions 4. Experimenting with style and structure The goal is to engage, inspire, or provoke the reader. It's a way to tell stories, share perspectives, and connect with others.

rawText: RHYMES Rhyme or rhyming is a systematic repetition of similar sounds especially in poetry. The harmonization of sound rhymes can either be in part of the words concerned or in the whole words (homophones). Two words rhyme with each other when they end with the same vowel or have the same vowel and consonant sequence and therefore pronounced exactly in the same way. title: CONTINUOUS WRITING
subject: English Language
rawText: NARRATIVE ESSAY A narrative essay is a story or account that is narrated verbally or in writing: therefore, a narrative essay is an essay that tells a story about a personal experience and is narrated by the author. It is a prose-written story that uses the 1 st person point of view and written in the past tense. Building a Good Narrative. 1. The story is typically told in chronological order. 2. The essay is clearly organized to allow the reader to follow the story line. 3. The story will have a point, often expressed as a lesson or theme. 4. The story includes sensory details. Assignment Write a good narrative story on what happened on your way to school today.

• Main points are presented • Ideas are explained clearly • Examples and facts are used 3. SS 2 ENGLISH LANGUAGE NOTE Topic: Speech – Words with Six Syllables Stressed on the Fifth Syllable 1. Meaning of Syllable A syllable is a unit of pronunciation that contains one vowel sound. Example: • education → ed-u-ca-tion (4 syllables) 2. Meaning of Stress Stress is the force or emphasis placed on a particular syllable in a word. In English, some syllables are pronounced louder and stronger than others. 3. Words with Six Syllables A six-syllable word has six beats when pronounced. Example of counting syllables: in-ter-na-tion-al-ly (6 syllables) 4. Stress on the Fifth Syllable When we say a word is stressed on the fifth syllable , it means the fifth syllable is pronounced louder and stronger than the others. Structure: 1 – 2 – 3 – 4 – 5 – 6 (Weak – weak – weak – weak – STRONG – weak) 5. Examples of Six-Syllable Words Stressed on the Fifth Syllable 1. in-ter-na-tion- AL -ly 2. in-di-vi-du- AL -ly 3. un-in-ten-tion- AL -ly 4. ir-re-spon-si- BIL -i-ty 5. dis-a-bil- I -ty 6. op-por-tu- NI -ty 7. re-a-bil-i- TA -tion

8. a-vail-a- BIL -i-ty 9. sen-si-bil- I -ty 10. pos-si- BIL -i-ty (Note: The capital letters show the stressed syllable.) 6. How to Identify the Fifth Syllable Step 1: Divide the word into syllables. Step 2: Count them carefully. Step 3: Identify the fifth syllable. Step 4: Pronounce it louder and stronger. 7. Importance of Correct Word Stress • Helps in clear communication • Prevents misunderstanding • Improves spoken English • Important for WAEC, NECO and oral English exams 8. Class Activity Divide the following words into syllables and identify the stressed syllable: 1. impossibility 2. productivity 3. accountability 4. adaptability 5. reliability

title: PREFIX AS WORDS EXTENSION
subject: English Language
rawText:
PREFIX AS WORD EXTENSION 1. Introduction A prefix is a word element (morpheme) added to the beginning of a root word or base word to change its meaning. Prefixes are called word extensions because they extend or modify the meaning of the original word without changing its grammatical class in most cases. Example:  happy → un + happy = unhappy  write → re + write = rewrite 2. Meaning of Prefix The word prefix comes from two Latin words:  pre = before  fix = attach Therefore, a prefix is attached before a word to form a new word. 3. Functions of Prefixes Prefixes perform the following functions: 1. They change the meaning of a word. 2. They express negation or opposition . 3. They show degree or size . 4. They indicate time or order . 5. They show number or quantity . 6. They show direction or position .

4. Common Prefixes and Their Meanings A. Prefixes of Negation These prefixes show not or opposite of . Prefi x Meanin g Example un- not unhappy in- not incorrect im- not impossibl e il- not illegal ir- not irregular non- not nonsense dis- opposit e disagree B. Prefixes of Degree or Size Prefix Meanin g Example over- too much overheat under - too little underestimat e super- above supernatural mini- small minibus maxi- large maximum

Prefix Meanin g Example C. Prefixes of Time and Order Prefi x Meanin g Example pre- before preview post- after postnata l re- again rewrite fore- before foretell D. Prefixes of Number or Quantity Prefix Meanin g Example bi- two bicycle tri- three triangle mono - one monologue multi- many multination al poly- many polygon

E. Prefixes of Direction or Position Prefi x Meanin g Example sub- under submarine inter- betwee n international trans- across transport extra- outside extracurricula r intra- within intramural 5. Spelling Rules of Prefixes 1. No change in spelling when prefix is added: o unhappy, rewrite, preview 2. Double consonants are not usually added: o misspell (not mispell) 3. Prefixes ending with vowels usually combine smoothly: o cooperate, reappear 4. Some prefixes change form to match the root word: o in- im- (impossible) → o in- il- (illegal) → o in- ir- (irregular) → 6. Importance of Prefixes in English Language 1. They help students understand word meanings . 2. They improve vocabulary development . 3. They help in correct spelling and pronunciation .

4. They aid comprehension in reading and writing . 7. Examples in Sentences 1. The teacher rechecked the examination scripts. 2. It is illegal to cheat during exams. 3. The boy was unhappy about the result. 4. Nigeria is a multicultural country. 8. Summary A prefix is a word extension added to the beginning of a base word to change its meaning. Prefixes play an important role in vocabulary building and effective communication in English. 9. Evaluation Questions 1. Define a prefix. 2. List five prefixes of negation with examples. 3. Use the prefixes re- , un- , and pre- in sentences. 4. Identify the prefix in the word international . 10. Assignment Form ten words using prefixes and use five of them in sentences.

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText: EMPHATIC STRESS Emphatic stress is the same as sentence stress and as such, different from the stress learnt the previous term, which is syllable stress. Emphatic stress is the placing of emphasis on a particular word in a sentence. Exam questions on Emphatic stress are often written as statements with the emphasized word CAPITALIZED, while the options are in form of questions. E.G The teacher adds that the golden rule for correctly answering questions on emphatic stress in English states that the correct answer is ALWAYS the option that does NOT have the capitalized word . Examples: (I). The manager travelled LAST year. (a). Did the Manager travel last month? (b). Did the Chairman travel last year? (c). Did the Manager travel this year? (d). Did the President come home last year? The correct answer is C (2). Aminu came home in AUGUST. (a). Who came home in August? (b). When did Aminu come home? (c). Did Aminu come to Maiduguri in August? title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: PRESERVATIVE PREFIXES These are prefixes that keep the original or root word and still preserves the meaning. It keeps the present quality or condition of a word from changing. The prefix “RE” is usually used. It often means to do something again. Examples: Rework Reassure Recast Reallocate Reapply Rebrand Reconsider Re-examine Reform Readmit Rearrange Reawaken Rebound Reclaim Reconstruct Reaffirm recount Re-elect Realign Reappear Reassemble Recapture Recharge Redesign There are many of such words. However, you must be careful as not every word with‘re’ belongs to this group. Examples: repeat, revise, reception, recess, remember, reveal, reasonable, receive, reconcile, recite, e.t.c.

Doctors: A trained personnel who has been given license to practice medicine. 2. Surgeon: A doctor who performs operation. 3. Nurse: A trained personnel who takes care of people who are ill or injured. 4. Pediatrician: A trained personnel who specializes in the treatment of babies. 5. Obstetrician: Doctors who specializes in the delivery of children. 6. Gynecologist: Trained personnel who specializes in the treatment of pregnant women and women generally. 7. Dermatologist: those who specializes in skin disease. 8. Radiotherapist: one trained to take x-rays or other forms of radiation the treatment of diseases. 9. Optician: A doctor who examines people’s eye and recommends glasses. 10. Dentist: A doctor in charge of tooth treatment. B. Verbs used in medical lines • Operate • Care • Cure • Injure • Heal • Prescribe • Treat • Hurt • Diagnose

• Admitted • Discharged • Referred. C. Departments in the hospital. • OPD – (out-patient department): for patients who are not admitted in the hospital. • IPD-(in-patient department): for admitted patients. • Pharmacy department • ICU: intensive care unit. • Radiology department • Records • Emergency unit • Prenatal ward • Postnatal ward. D. Words Pertaining to Death. • Pathology: A doctor who examines dead bodies to find out the cause of death. • Corpse: The dead body of humans. • Carcass: The dead body of animals. • Cremation: Disposal of corpse through burning. • Embalm: Preservation of corpse from decaying. • Hearse /(h з : з ): Vehicles for carrying corpse. • Ambulance: Vehicle with special gadgets for taking sick or injured people to the hospital. e. Other words • Anemia: lack of blood in the body. • Narcotic: Drugs that make one to relax and sleep. • Antiseptic: drugs that weakens or kills germ. • Dispenser: A person who dispenses drugs. iii) GRAMMAR- Pronouns: types, functions and position A pronoun is a word that is used instead of a noun in a sentences to avoid repetition. Types of pronoun • Personal pronoun • Indefinite pronoun

• Possessive pronoun • Interrogative pronoun • Relative pronoun • Reflective pronoun • Reciprocal pronoun • Emphatic pronoun. 1. Personal pronoun : they are called personal pronouns because they stand for three persons namely; a) The person speaking (The first person) b) The person spoken to or addressed (The second person) c) The person spoken about or being discussed (The third person). Examples: I, we, me, our, us (first person pronoun). You, Yours (second person pronoun). She, Her, He, It, him, They, Their (their person pronoun). I go to church every Sunday. You saw her in the market. 2. Possessive pronoun: They show possession or ownership. It includes mines, yours, her, his, ours and theirs. Examples: That book is mine. The school across the road is theirs. The food is yours. The difference between possessive pronouns and possessive adjective. I) possessive pronouns are pronouns indicating ownership but do not precede or come before a Noun or in a Noun phrase. For example, Mine, yours, hers, theirs, ours, it's. II) possessive adjective: it comes before a Noun or pronoun to show who and what owns it. It shows who or what something is to or is. It is an adjective that is used to show ownership. It comes before a Noun in the sentence and let use to know to whom, including my, your, his, her, it's, our, their. Each one corresponds to a subject pronoun. They are used alone. 3) Demonstrative pronoun: These are used to point out specific things, persons or places referred to. They include: this, that, those, these .

Examples: This biro is mine, that is yours These are my students, those are yours. These are my friends. 4) Relative pronoun: This relates to other nouns or pronouns and it also function as a conjunction. It introduces a clause. It includes: who, whom, that, which, whose. Examples: The man who came here last week is my friend. The students who were publicly flogged have been expelled. I read the book that was given to me. Relative pronouns are pronouns that connect a descriptive expression (adjectival or relative clause) to the noun that is being described by the expression. They are always close to the nouns or pronouns they are describing. Relative pronoun is sub-divided into two: a) Those that are used to refer to human beings – who, whom, whose,that, whomever. They are the relative pronouns for people b) Those that are used to refer to animals/ inanimate objects or ideas – that, which. Other division of relative pronouns are I) ownership - whose. It indicates possession, the owner of something. II) places - where. POSITION OF RELATIVE PRONOUNS Relative pronouns can appear at the initial, medial. Penultimate and final positions of a sentence. FUNCTIONS OF A RELATIVE PRONOUNS Relative pronouns perform the following functions in a sentence; 1. It shows possession or ownership e.g The man whose car was stolen is here 2. It indicates the location being referred to, e.g

Where I saw her. 3. Relative pronouns is used for specifications. It singles out an item from the rest, e.g That book( not others but that particular one is indicated). 4. Relative pronouns differentiate between animate objects and inanimate objects in a sentence. 5) Indefinite pronoun: this is not definite or specific but stands generally for a noun. It includes anyone, anybody, anything, everyone, somebody, someone, none, some, etc. It can also be referred to objects or people that are not specified they include all, any, some. Examples: Nobody wants him back as teacher. Each candidate has Master’s Degree. Many want to eat her food . 6) Reciprocal pronoun: This represents persons or things as being interactive. It is used when the action expressed by the verb is shared by those concerned. It includes: each other and one another. Examples: The students taught one another in the examination. John and Esther like each other. IV) Continuous Writing: Expository Essay: An expository essay is an explanatory essay where the writing aims to inform, instruct, explain, criticize, or analyze some concepts or situation to the reader. It allows the writer to how his capability for logical thoughts and reasoning. It is a factual essay and most times, makes judgment. Topics Related to Expository Essay 1. How my favorite food is prepared. 2. Dangers of drug abuse. 3. The dangers of premarital sex. 4. The future of Nigerian Youth. 5. Causes of indiscipline in Nigeria Secondary Schools. 6. The consequences of indecent dressing 7. Why prostitution is a crime

8. Managing population explosion in Nigeria 9. My English teacher: How I saw him/her 10. Controlling HIV/AIDS in Nigeria . Guidelines for writing an expository essay: 1. Think of the most logical way of presenting in order to avoid missing links that could hinder full understanding. 2. Follow a sequential order: organize your thoughts carefully 3. Concentrate on one main point at a time 4. Mention the particular moments when thing should be done 5. Develop your paragraphs. Example - Topic for class discussion: “Dangers of Premarital Sex” a. Introduction: Definition of Premarital Sex : Who should engage in sex b. Body: Dangers: i. Why youths should avoid sex. ii. Unwanted pregnancy. iii. Sexually transmitted diseases. iv. School dropout. v. Stigmatization. vi. VVF – Vesico-vaginal fistula. c. Conclusion: Your advice to the youths. Sanctions to Youths who engage in premarital sex.

title: RISING TUNE
subject: English Language
rawText:
SS 2 ENGLISH LANGUAGE NOTE Topic: Speech – Intonation Pattern (Expressing Surprise / Disbelief – Exclamation) 1. Meaning of Intonation Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice when speaking. It shows the speaker’s feelings or attitude. There are three main types of intonation: 1. Falling intonation (↘) 2. Rising intonation (↗) 3. Fall–rise intonation 2. Intonation for Surprise or Disbelief When expressing surprise or disbelief, we usually use: • A rising intonation (↗) • Sometimes a sharp fall–rise tone • Strong emphasis (stress) on important words This makes the statement sound emotional or shocked. 3. Examples 1. Ade is a witch? ↗ 2. Really?! ↗ 3. Musa is a millionaire?! ↗ 4. You must be joking! ↗ 5. Richard is a spy?! ↗ 6. I don’t believe it! ↗ 7. Ibrahim is dead?! ↗ 8. Is he?! ↗ In these examples, the voice rises sharply to show shock, doubt, or disbelief.

4. Explanation of the Examples • “Ade is a witch?!” – The speaker is shocked and does not believe it. • “Musa is a millionaire?!” – The speaker finds it hard to believe. • “You must be joking!” – The speaker thinks it is a joke. • “I don’t believe it!” – Direct expression of disbelief. • “Is he?!” – Rising tone shows doubt and surprise. 5. Features of Intonation for Surprise • Voice rises sharply at the end. • Important words are stressed. • Facial expression usually shows shock (wide eyes, raised eyebrows). • Sometimes repeated words (Really?! What?!). 6. Dialogue (Acting Practice) Dialogue 1 Bola: Have you heard the news? Tunde: What news? Bola: Musa is a millionaire. Tunde: Musa is a millionaire?! ↗ Bola: Yes, he won a business award. Tunde: Really?! I can’t believe it! Dialogue 2 Aisha: Ibrahim is dead. Fatima: Ibrahim is dead?! ↗ Aisha: Yes, it happened yesterday. Fatima: Oh no! Is he?! That’s shocking! Dialogue 3 John: Richard is a spy. Mary: You must be joking! ↗ John: I’m serious. Mary: Richard? A spy?! I don’t believe it!

7. Class Activity Students should: 1. Form pairs. 2. Create a short dialogue expressing surprise. 3. Use rising intonation correctly. 4. Act it out in front of the class. Conclusion Intonation helps us express emotions clearly. When showing surprise or disbelief, we use a rising tone and strong stress on important words. Correct intonation makes spoken English more natural and meaningful. Make ss 2 note on the following topics: Speech Rising tune. E.g. 1. Will you come home tonight? 2. Can David do this, for me 3. Help me with this, please 4. Do this for me, will you? SS 2 ENGLISH LANGUAGE NOTE Topic: Speech – Rising Tune (Rising Intonation) 1. Meaning of Rising Tune A rising tune (or rising intonation) is when the voice goes up at the end of a sentence. It is usually marked with an arrow (↗). Example: Are you coming? ↗ The voice rises at the end to show a question, request, or uncertainty. 2. Situations Where Rising Tune Is Used Rising tune is commonly used in: 1. Yes/No questions 2. Polite requests 3. Question tags (when seeking confirmation) 4. Incomplete statements 5. Expressions of doubt or uncertainty

3. Examples and Explanation 1. Will you come home tonight? ↗ This is a Yes/No question, so the voice rises at the end. 2. Can David do this for me? ↗ Also a Yes/No question. The voice rises on me . 3. Help me with this, please? ↗ This is a polite request. The rising tone makes it sound gentle and respectful. 4. Do this for me, will you? ↗ This is a question tag. The voice rises on you because the speaker wants confirmation. 4. Features of Rising Tune • The voice moves upward at the end of the sentence. • It is common in Yes/No questions. • It shows politeness in requests. • It indicates that the speaker expects a response. 5. More Examples 1. Are you ready? ↗ 2. Can I borrow your pen? ↗ 3. She is coming, isn’t she? ↗ 4. You understand, don’t you? ↗ 6. Contrast with Falling Tune • Rising tune (↗) – used for Yes/No questions and requests. • Falling tune (↘) – used for statements and WH-questions. Example: Where are you going? ↘ (falling tone)

7. Class Activity Students should: 1. Read the given sentences aloud. 2. Raise their voice at the end of each sentence. 3. Create five Yes/No questions using rising tune. 4. Practice in pairs.

7. Class Activity Students should: 1. Read the given sentences aloud. 2. Raise their voice at the end of each sentence. 3. Create five Yes/No questions using rising tune. 4. Practice in pairs.

title: STRUCTURE
subject: English Language
rawText: ADJECTIVAL CLAUSE Adjectival clause is a dependent clause that contains a relative pronoun. It should also be noted that there must be a noun placed in position before the relative pronoun. This noun or pronoun is called the antecedent to the relative pronoun. The relative pronouns are fixed in number, they include who, whom, whose, which, where, when, why and that. Adjectival clause functions the same as the grammatical function of an adjective in a sentence. It describes, qualifies or gives more information about the subject (doer of an action) in a sentence which could be a noun or pronoun. Class-work (a). She took out the box which lay in the drawer. (b). The trader who sold this wristwatch came from Ghana. (c). I have a friend whose father is a millionaire. Home-work (d). Mallam Zubairu whom we all like so much is leaving the school. (e). The girl that owns the supermarket is my close friend.

title: SPEECH
subject: English Language
rawText:
SS1 lesson note on the listed topics: LESSON NOTE: SPEECH 1. Meaning of Speech Speech is the expression of ideas, thoughts, and feelings through spoken words. 2. Structure of a Speech A good speech has three main parts: a. Introduction • Greets the audience • Introduces the topic • Captures attention b. Body • Presents main ideas • Explains points clearly • Provides examples and facts c. Conclusion • Summarizes key ideas • Emphasizes the main message • Ends with a strong closing SUMMARY WRITING 1. Meaning of Summary A summary is a shortened version of a passage that contains only the main points. 2. Features of a Good Summary • Brief and concise • Contains only main ideas • Written in your own words • Clear and well-organized 3. Steps in Writing a Summary 1. Read the passage carefully 2. Identify the main points 3. Remove unnecessary details 4. Write in your own words

5. Ensure clarity and correctness CONTINUOUS WRITING 1. Meaning Continuous writing is the process of writing complete sentences and paragraphs on a given topic. 2. Types of Continuous Writing • Narrative writing • Descriptive writing • Expository writing • Argumentative writing ORAL COMMUNICATION: GIVING DIRECTIONS 1. Meaning Giving directions is the act of guiding someone on how to reach a place or do something. 2. Features of Good Directions • Clear and simple language • Concise (brief) explanation • Correct sequence of steps • Use of landmarks • Polite expressions 3. Example “Go straight, turn left at the junction, then walk past the school. The house is on your right.” NOUN CLAUSES 1. Meaning of a Noun Clause A noun clause is a group of words with a subject and verb that functions as a noun in a sentence. 2. Types of Noun Clauses a. Subject Noun Clause Acts as the subject of a sentence. Example: What she said is true. b. Object Noun Clause

Acts as the object of a verb. Example: I believe that he is honest. c. Complement Noun Clause Completes the meaning of the sentence. Example: The truth is that he lied. 3. Functions of Noun Clauses • As subject • As object • As complement READING TO SUMMARIZE IN A SPECIFIC NUMBER OF SENTENCES 1. Guidelines • Read the passage carefully • Pick only key points • Combine ideas where possible • Avoid repetition • Stick strictly to the required number of sentences 2. Example If asked to summarize in 3 sentences, ensure: • Each sentence contains a main idea • No extra or irrelevant information EXPOSITORY ESSAY 1. Meaning An expository essay is a type of writing that explains, informs, or describes a topic clearly and logically. 2. Features of an Expository Essay • Clear introduction • Well-organized body paragraphs • Logical explanation of ideas • Use of facts and examples • Formal language 3. Structure

a. Introduction • Introduces the topic • States the purpose b. Body • Explains ideas in paragraphs • Each paragraph focuses on one point c. Conclusion • Summarizes the discussion • Restates the main idea 4. Example Topics • Importance of education • Effects of pollution • Benefits of good hygiene

title: VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT
subject: English Language
rawText: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH HUMAN INTERNAL BODY SYSTEM AND THEIR FUNCTIONS The body includes nine major organ systems, each composed of various organs and tissues that work together as a functional unit. The chief constituents and prime functions of each system are: 1. The integumentary system , composed of the skin and associated structures, protects the body from invasion by harmful microorganisms and chemicals; it also prevents water loss from the body. 2. The musculoskeletal system (also referred to separately as the muscle system and the skeletal system ), composed of the skeletal muscles and bones (with about 206 of the latter in adults), moves the body and protectively houses its internal organs. 3. The respiratory system , composed of the breathing passages, lungs, and muscles of respiration , obtains from the air the oxygen necessary for cellular metabolism; it also returns to the air the carbon dioxide that forms as a waste product of such metabolism. 4. The circulatory system , composed of the heart, blood, and blood vessels, circulates a transport fluid throughout the body, providing the cells with a steady supply of oxygen and nutrients and carrying away waste products such as carbon dioxide and toxic nitrogen compounds. 5. The digestive system , composed of the mouth, esophagus , stomach, and intestines, breaks down food into usable substances (nutrients), which are then absorbed from the blood or lymph; this system also eliminates the unusable or excess portion of the food as fecal matter. 6. The excretory system , composed of the kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder , and urethra , removes toxic nitrogen compounds and other wastes from the blood. 7. The nervous system , composed of the sensory organs, brain, spinal cord, and nerves, transmits, integrates , and analyzes sensory information and carries impulses to effect the appropriate muscular or glandular responses. 8. The endocrine system , composed of the hormone -secreting glands and tissues, provides a chemical communications network for coordinating various body processes. 9. The reproductive system , composed of the male or female sex organs, enables reproduction and thereby ensures the continuation of the species. Class - work List two female and two male reproductive organs. Assignment List ten organs associated with the human body system. D raw the human heart

rawText:
WEEK 4 1. SPEECH : Unstressed vowel sounds / ə /. Schwa sound / ə / vowel / Ձ /. Vowel sounds are sounds that are produced without any frication or obstruction in the flow of air in the vocal cord. / ə / the central character is an upside-down and backward lower- case “e”= /ə in English the vowel no 2/ Ձ / is used to represent the weak form of vowel in an unstressed (unaccepted) syllable of a given word, it is not stressed in any word. It is referred to as schwa sound. Schwa is a short vowel produced with the lips in neutral position, it is the mid central vowel or neutral vowel sound typically occurring in unstressed syllables in English. In articulation the sound, the tongue is in a central position and the lip in a neutral position. Note: the schwa sound / ə/ is represented by the letters “ a, ar,e, er, eo/ei, I, iou, o, or, oar, ou/our, ough, oir, re,u, ure, in some words. This means that the underline letters in the word below are pronounced as the schwa sound In English. Spelling symbols for / ə / 1. letter “ɋ” as in ə go, chin ə ,m ə chete, orph ə n, move ə ble, vill ə , wom ə n, mir ə cle, m ə d ə m ete 2. letter “ɋr” as in collar, pə rticular, mon ə rchy, gr ə mm ə r, mot ə r, forw ə rd, sug ə r, stew ə rd etc. 3. letter “e” as in open, sharpen, deepen, ripen, cemetery, etc. 4. letter “er” as in starter, wonder, founder, perhaps, superman, latter, weather, etc. 5. letters “eou” as in righteous. 6. letters “eo/ei” as in luncheon, foreigner, surgeon, pigeon etc. 7. letter “I” as in possible, terrible, accessible, invisible, divisible, permissible etc. 8. letter “o” as in collate, photography, tomorrow, obey, polite, second, pilot, wisdom, etc 9. letters “oar” as in cupboard. 10.. letters “or” as in doctor, rector, supervisor, governor, minor, calculator, forget, etc. 11. letters “ou/our” as in famous, generous, glamour, colour, favour, rumour etc. 12. letters “ough” as in thorough

13. letters “oir” as in junior, senior etc. 14.letter “re” as in acre, metre, caliber, goiter, theatre, centra, meager, manouvre etc. 15. letter “u” as in litmus, suspect, minus, autumn, support, column, sustain, campus, etc 16. letter “ur“ as in augur, survive, surprise, surround, survey, surmount. Etc. 17. letters “ure” as in figure, furniture, injure, nature, culture, seizure, structure, etc The sound understudy can occur at the initial, medical and final position of a word thus: Initial position medical position final position 1. Again / ə gen/ Commit /k ə mit / Teacher /ti:t ꭍə / 2. Above / ə bnv/ Success /s ə kses/ Mother /m Λðə / 3. Offend / ə fend/ Cupboard /k Λ b ə / Plumber /pl Λ m ə / 4. Among / ə m Λ g/ Vegetable /ve ʤ t ə bl/ Actor/ ӕ kt ə / 5. Attack / ə t ӕ k/ Method /me ѳə d/ Sister/sist ə / ii. STRUCTURE: Pronoun – Types of pronoun. Pronouns are words that are used to replace nouns in expressions, they are words that are used instead of a noun or in replacement of a noun to avoid the repetition of such nouns. The noun being replaced is referred to as the antecedent. E.g Ngozi and John are here. They are here. Pronouns unlike nouns, cannot be preceded by modifiers and they are not accompanied by the apostrophe like nouns. We cannot have your’s or their’s but we can have Tom’s as in Tom’s house. E.G Pronouns are used in sentences according to the number, gender, and case of the replaced noun or the function it performs. Consistency is required in the use of pronouns in sequence. She/he, it, mine, your, this, that, are quintessential examples of some pronouns. Types of pronoun The nine (9) types of pronouns in English includes personal, possessive, demonstrative, emphatic or intensive, interrogative, indefinite, relative, reciprocal and reflective or reflexive as earlier discussed in week one(1) or two (2), have more explanations of each below

1. personal pronouns: these refer to specific people or things, for example: I, me , you, she, he, they, us, it. They are used according to the number (singular or plural) of people or things. They also reflect gender and case thus: A.- number (singular and plural ) PERSON SINGULAR PLURAL First person i. me we, us Second person you you Third person he, she, it, her, him. They, them. B. Gender differentiates between male and female. Gender pronouns Masculine (male) he, him. Feminine (female) she, her Neuter (neutral) it, they, them. C. case Case indicates the role a pronoun is playing in an expression, whether subjective or objective. i. – subject pronoun performs the action of the verb or plays the role of the subject in a sentence. E. g He went home Subject He can be replaced with other subject pronouns; I, you, she, they. ii. Objective pronouns: these pronouns act as the receiver of the action of the verb thus; they occupy the object position in a sentence. Example mum gave me a pair of shoes subject object. 2. EMPHATIC OR INTENSIVE PRONOUN:

Emphatic or intensive pronouns have the suffixes – self or selves like the reflective pronouns but they emphasize the noun (or pronoun) that precedes them. Example i. Ann herself went there . noun antecedent. Pronoun emphasizing Ann. The following expressions are wrong; himself, sheself, theirselves, themselves, weselves, ourself. 3. INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS: Interrogative pronouns are used to ask questions. We have who, whom, which, whose and what. Each of these examples can be formed with the suffix – ever to get whoever, whenever, whichever. Note that we use which to ask about a noun that is not a human being, it could be an animal or an object. Who are used for people and whom asks questions about the object (receiver) of the action. Whose expresses ownership E.g whose books are these? 4 .REFLECTIVE OR REFLEXIVE PRONOUNS : These pronouns refer back to the subject. The singular forms are myself, yourself, himself, herself, and their plural forms are ourselves, yourselves and themselves. E.G I took care of myself during the holiday. (“I” = subject and pronoun, “myself refer to it) 5 . RECIPROCAL PRONOUNS: These are pronouns used to join two or more subject. They are used to indicate a two-way relationship between two or more people. They are only two reciprocal pronoun in English language Viz , each other and one another. a. – each other: this is used to join two subjects, when talking about two people. E.g Tunde and Musa greeted each other. b. – one another: this is used to join three or more subjects when talking about an action involving more than two people. E.g At the re-union, the old friends hugged one another. 6. DEMONSTRATIVE PRONOUNS:

Demonstrative involves a supplementary gesture. (demonstration) is a special setting in order to determine reference. They point to specific items being referred to within a sentence. Basically, there are four demonstrative pronoun in English; this, these, that, those. I. This, these. - This (pronounced with /s/) is used for a singular item. While these(pronounced with/z/) refers to more than one item, it indicates plurality. This/these † noun are used to refer to things near to use (they refer to items that are not close to the speaker) or to things that we are mentioning now. ii. That, those That and those † noun are used to refer to things that are not so near (they refer to singular and plural but distance objects accordingly) or to things we mentioned before or to things that we are going to mention later. POSITION OF DEMONSTRATIVEPRONOUN Demonstrative pronouns can appear at the initial, medial, penultimate and final positions of a sentence. FUNCTIONS OF DEMONSTRACTIVE PRONOUNS Demonstrative pronoun perform the following functions in a sentences. 1. They point to specific items bring referred to within a sentences. 2.They indicate items that are nearby or far away in space/place or time. iii COMPREHENSION: Reading for critical evaluation. Reading for critical evaluation is the ability to make careful Judgements about how good or bad a text, a person, a situation, a law etc is, it is about readers ability to detect facts, opinions, logicality/ consistency, illogicality/ inconsistency in a written comprehension passage, it is the ability to access the argument or proposition and to be able to determine its appropriateness and writes it on the board as the topic to be taught. One of the skills that are tested In comprehension questions is your ability to read the passage for critical evaluation. For example, as you read, you need to examine the three factors that are involved in a reading exercise the writer, the writing and reader.

The writing is the topic, the subject matter, this will be judged on its own merits as the reader takes a look at the content, and context. Consider this short text for example: “in1984 when Nigeria had her independence, the Americans did not know that Nigeria would be a fertile nation economically. Otherwise, they would have delayed the independence in order to exploit and plunder our resources more”. The question is: did Nigeria gain independence in 1984? Or you ask what was America’s connection with Nigeria independence? Now, ponder more on the writers content and context. Thus, is the author able to convey the intended message in the text above? This is reading for critical evaluation. As the reader, you need to understand the purpose for which you are reading. What are your expectations in this writing? Can you find them? Are the facts or points satisfactory? You need to look closely at the writing to get what you want. The essence of reading for critical evaluation is to have questions in mind to probe the writer, the writing and yourself and to try to provide answers to all the questions asked below: i. are there understatements or exaggeration? ii. are the facts correct? iii. does the writers mix facts with opinions? Iv .are there illogicalities or inconsistencies? v. is any information left out? vi. are you able to grasp connections, transitions or implied meaning? vii. what are the purpose of the writer? What is he/she driving at or what does she / he want me to know? What message is she/ he passing across? viii. is the writer appealing, arguing, giving facts, expressing opinion, supporting a view, explaining a process, etc. ix. is the writer capable of treating the subject matter? Has he/she the knowledge or the facts?. x. is the writer biased? Does he/she tilt towards a particular view or factor? The questions are good preparation for reading for critical evaluation. Your assessment, your analysis and your comprehension will improve if you have a questioning mind as you read. Referred to “uduefe the rubber thief” on page 103 -104 and answer question number 1-3

Iv. CONTINUOUS WRITING- ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY Argumentative essay I a form of persuasive writing which is any written work that tries to convince or influence the reader of the writers opinion. Argumentative essay as the type of essay whose business is to argue. The writer makes attempt to prove with sound reasons, the validity of his/her point of view put differently, argumentative essay is a piece of writing that takes a stance on an issue. A writer attempts to persuade readers to understand and support their point of view about a disputable topic by stating their reason/s and providing evidence to break it up. In argumentative essay, the writer presents two sides of an issue. He makes known his own stand with convincing reasons and facts. Consider this argumentative essay topic “Democracy is better than military rule”. One can either support or oppose the topic. In supporting or opposing the topic, one must first reflect on the two sides, then take a definite position with good reasons that can convince ones readers. Features of argumentative essay Below are the salient features (format or style) of an argumentative essay. 1. TITLE/TOPIC/HEADING : controversial title(or disputable topic or polar position) from which you take a stance is presented. The topic for debate is known as Motion while in argumentative essay writing, it is known as topic or title. Examples of argumentative essay topics a- Teachers are more important than doctors. b- English is more beneficial to students than mathematics. c- Mathematics is an easy subject. d- Military rule is better than civil rule e- Child labour should be a punishable offence. f- corporal punishment should not be a disciplinary measure. g- female circumcision should be abolished. h- boarding school is better than day school.

2. VOCATIVE : Salutation or greeting. Greet the audience, starting from the highest in rank of the dignitaries to the least personality present. Below are the formats of vocative in this essay type. Examples- Mr chairman (or the moderator), the organizers, panel of judges, accurate time keeper, my co-debators, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, good morning. 3. INTRODUCTION: The introduction should be interesting, captivating and stimulating, sustain the readers interest to want to read on. State the purpose and indicate the thesis(goal) of the essay then take a stance. Tell the audience what the motion is (all about), explain the polar position, the two faces or how side of a coin and indicate the side on which you stand. State what is boarding school, what is day school; add the background knowledge at this stage, if you are proposing the motion. Example: I am writing to oppose the motion which says that/ states, “Boarding school is better than day school” first of all, we all know that “Boarding school” is an educational institution where students live within premises while being given formal instructions during the school terms. Conversely, “day school” is an educational institution where students attend classes are given instruction during the day but return home in the evening on a daily basis. 4. BODY : at this stage, present some sound, solid and valid reasons to prove your claim with convincing points; why you believe a day school is better than boarding school as you have chosen. You should have at least, three to four good reasons to give in the body of the essay. If you are proposing the motion, the claims or arguments are presented at this level. Three to four valid ideas, reasons, evidences and facts could be presented in logical sequence or chronological order within paragraphs. Conversely, if you are opposing the motion, you could counter claim or counter the points raised by the opponent first then explain the motion an give or state at least three to four valid for opposing the motion. Pick on a point you think your opponent must have in support of the motive, e.g Boarding school……and try to counter it, by so doing, you are refuting earlier argument before presenting your points or lines of arguments in order to give weight to the actual position you are taking. Example The “chief proposer” has told you that students in boarding schools are more morally upright as teachers live with them in the compound to monitor their behavior. Do we not know that

cultism, homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. A day school goes home to his/her parents and siblings where all eyes are closely on him/her, he feels happy and none of these evil practices crosses his/her mind. A teacher does not give that close attention to boarders. The body of argumentative essay should be persuasive and devoid of waffing (avoid going off track/topic/theme or context), mal-propism, slang expression, contraction, dirty and abusive language. Employ the use of forceful and aggressive tone with rhetorical questions. Use moderate repetition and rhythmical pattern to spice up your writing, follow the rules of writing in English and properly apply the right punctuation marks, content, organization, expression and mechanical accuracy (C.O.E.M.A) should be apt in each content. 5. CONCLUSION : Have an effective and appealing conclusion. Summarize your ideas effectively and reaffirm your claim/s. sum up your points to remind your readers of the points you have raised. Use strong appealing words to make the readers (or listeners/hearers/audience) see your points of view and agree with you. Your ability to conclude your writing well will undoubtly win the audience to your side. Examples - with the points I have raised above or before you, I am left in no doubt that you will agree with me that day school is better than boarding school. 6 . CLOSURE : thank you

pages.text: WEEK 4 1. SPEECH : Unstressed vowel sounds / ə /. Schwa sound / ə / vowel / Ձ /. Vowel sounds are sounds that are produced without any frication or obstruction in the flow of air in the vocal cord. / ə / the central character is an upside-down and backward lower- case “e”= /ə in English the vowel no 2/ Ձ / is used to represent the weak form of vowel in an unstressed (unaccepted) syllable of a given word, it is not stressed in any word. It is referred to as schwa sound. Schwa is a short vowel produced with the lips in neutral position, it is the mid central vowel or neutral vowel sound typically occurring in unstressed syllables in English. In articulation the sound, the tongue is in a central position and the lip in a neutral position. Note: the schwa sound / ə/ is represented by the letters “ a, ar,e, er, eo/ei, I, iou, o, or, oar, ou/our, ough, oir, re,u, ure, in some words. This means that the underline letters in the word below are pronounced as the schwa sound In English. Spelling symbols for / ə / 1. letter “ɋ” as in ə go, chin ə ,m ə chete, orph ə n, move ə ble, vill ə , wom ə n, mir ə cle, m ə d ə m ete 2. letter “ɋr” as in collar, pə rticular, mon ə rchy, gr ə mm ə r, mot ə r, forw ə rd, sug ə r, stew ə rd etc. 3. letter “e” as in open, sharpen, deepen, ripen, cemetery, etc. 4. letter “er” as in starter, wonder, founder, perhaps, superman, latter, weather, etc. 5. letters “eou” as in righteous. 6. letters “eo/ei” as in luncheon, foreigner, surgeon, pigeon etc. 7. letter “I” as in possible, terrible, accessible, invisible, divisible, permissible etc. 8. letter “o” as in collate, photography, tomorrow, obey, polite, second, pilot, wisdom, etc 9. letters “oar” as in cupboard. 10.. letters “or” as in doctor, rector, supervisor, governor, minor, calculator, forget, etc. 11. letters “ou/our” as in famous, generous, glamour, colour, favour, rumour etc. 12. letters “ough” as in thorough

Etc. 17. letters “ure” as in figure, furniture, injure, nature, culture, seizure, structure, etc The sound understudy can occur at the initial, medical and final position of a word thus: Initial position medical position final position 1. Again / ə gen/ Commit /k ə mit / Teacher /ti:t ꭍə / 2. Above / ə bnv/ Success /s ə kses/ Mother /m Λðə / 3. Offend / ə fend/ Cupboard /k Λ b ə / Plumber /pl Λ m ə / 4. Among / ə m Λ g/ Vegetable /ve ʤ t ə bl/ Actor/ ӕ kt ə / 5. Attack / ə t ӕ k/ Method /me ѳə d/ Sister/sist ə / ii. STRUCTURE: Pronoun – Types of pronoun. Pronouns are words that are used to replace nouns in expressions, they are words that are used instead of a noun or in replacement of a noun to avoid the repetition of such nouns. The noun being replaced is referred to as the antecedent. E.g Ngozi and John are here. They are here. Pronouns unlike nouns, cannot be preceded by modifiers and they are not accompanied by the apostrophe like nouns. We cannot have your’s or their’s but we can have Tom’s as in Tom’s house. E.G Pronouns are used in sentences according to the number, gender, and case of the replaced noun or the function it performs. Consistency is required in the use of pronouns in sequence. She/he, it, mine, your, this, that, are quintessential examples of some pronouns. Types of pronoun The nine (9) types of pronouns in English includes personal, possessive, demonstrative, emphatic or intensive, interrogative, indefinite, relative, reciprocal and reflective or reflexive as earlier discussed in week one(1) or two (2), have more explanations of each below

1. personal pronouns: these refer to specific people or things, for example: I, me , you, she, he, they, us, it. They are used according to the number (singular or plural) of people or things. They also reflect gender and case thus: A.- number (singular and plural ) PERSON SINGULAR PLURAL First person i. me we, us Second person you you Third person he, she, it, her, him. They, them. B. Gender differentiates between male and female. Gender pronouns Masculine (male) he, him. Feminine (female) she, her Neuter (neutral) it, they, them. C. case Case indicates the role a pronoun is playing in an expression, whether subjective or objective. i. – subject pronoun performs the action of the verb or plays the role of the subject in a sentence. E. g He went home Subject He can be replaced with other subject pronouns; I, you, she, they. ii. Objective pronouns: these pronouns act as the receiver of the action of the verb thus; they occupy the object position in a sentence. Example mum gave me a pair of shoes subject object. 2. EMPHATIC OR INTENSIVE PRONOUN:

Emphatic or intensive pronouns have the suffixes – self or selves like the reflective pronouns but they emphasize the noun (or pronoun) that precedes them. Example i. Ann herself went there . noun antecedent. Pronoun emphasizing Ann. The following expressions are wrong; himself, sheself, theirselves, themselves, weselves, ourself. 3. INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS: Interrogative pronouns are used to ask questions. We have who, whom, which, whose and what. Each of these examples can be formed with the suffix – ever to get whoever, whenever, whichever. Note that we use which to ask about a noun that is not a human being, it could be an animal or an object. Who are used for people and whom asks questions about the object (receiver) of the action. Whose expresses ownership E.g whose books are these? 4 .REFLECTIVE OR REFLEXIVE PRONOUNS : These pronouns refer back to the subject. The singular forms are myself, yourself, himself, herself, and their plural forms are ourselves, yourselves and themselves. E.G I took care of myself during the holiday. (“I” = subject and pronoun, “myself refer to it) 5 . RECIPROCAL PRONOUNS: These are pronouns used to join two or more subject. They are used to indicate a two-way relationship between two or more people. They are only two reciprocal pronoun in English language Viz , each other and one another. a. – each other: this is used to join two subjects, when talking about two people. E.g Tunde and Musa greeted each other. b. – one another: this is used to join three or more subjects when talking about an action involving more than two people. E.g At the re-union, the old friends hugged one another. 6. DEMONSTRATIVE PRONOUNS:

Demonstrative involves a supplementary gesture. (demonstration) is a special setting in order to determine reference. They point to specific items being referred to within a sentence. Basically, there are four demonstrative pronoun in English; this, these, that, those. I. This, these. - This (pronounced with /s/) is used for a singular item. While these(pronounced with/z/) refers to more than one item, it indicates plurality. This/these † noun are used to refer to things near to use (they refer to items that are not close to the speaker) or to things that we are mentioning now. ii. That, those That and those † noun are used to refer to things that are not so near (they refer to singular and plural but distance objects accordingly) or to things we mentioned before or to things that we are going to mention later. POSITION OF DEMONSTRATIVEPRONOUN Demonstrative pronouns can appear at the initial, medial, penultimate and final positions of a sentence. FUNCTIONS OF DEMONSTRACTIVE PRONOUNS Demonstrative pronoun perform the following functions in a sentences. 1. They point to specific items bring referred to within a sentences. 2.They indicate items that are nearby or far away in space/place or time. iii COMPREHENSION: Reading for critical evaluation. Reading for critical evaluation is the ability to make careful Judgements about how good or bad a text, a person, a situation, a law etc is, it is about readers ability to detect facts, opinions, logicality/ consistency, illogicality/ inconsistency in a written comprehension passage, it is the ability to access the argument or proposition and to be able to determine its appropriateness and writes it on the board as the topic to be taught. One of the skills that are tested In comprehension questions is your ability to read the passage for critical evaluation. For example, as you read, you need to examine the three factors that are involved in a reading exercise the writer, the writing and reader.

The writing is the topic, the subject matter, this will be judged on its own merits as the reader takes a look at the content, and context. Consider this short text for example: “in1984 when Nigeria had her independence, the Americans did not know that Nigeria would be a fertile nation economically. Otherwise, they would have delayed the independence in order to exploit and plunder our resources more”. The question is: did Nigeria gain independence in 1984? Or you ask what was America’s connection with Nigeria independence? Now, ponder more on the writers content and context. Thus, is the author able to convey the intended message in the text above? This is reading for critical evaluation. As the reader, you need to understand the purpose for which you are reading. What are your expectations in this writing? Can you find them? Are the facts or points satisfactory? You need to look closely at the writing to get what you want. The essence of reading for critical evaluation is to have questions in mind to probe the writer, the writing and yourself and to try to provide answers to all the questions asked below: i. are there understatements or exaggeration? ii. are the facts correct? iii. does the writers mix facts with opinions? Iv .are there illogicalities or inconsistencies? v. is any information left out? vi. are you able to grasp connections, transitions or implied meaning? vii. what are the purpose of the writer? What is he/she driving at or what does she / he want me to know? What message is she/ he passing across? viii. is the writer appealing, arguing, giving facts, expressing opinion, supporting a view, explaining a process, etc. ix. is the writer capable of treating the subject matter? Has he/she the knowledge or the facts?. x. is the writer biased? Does he/she tilt towards a particular view or factor? The questions are good preparation for reading for critical evaluation. Your assessment, your analysis and your comprehension will improve if you have a questioning mind as you read. Referred to “uduefe the rubber thief” on page 103 -104 and answer question number 1-3

Iv. CONTINUOUS WRITING- ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY Argumentative essay I a form of persuasive writing which is any written work that tries to convince or influence the reader of the writers opinion. Argumentative essay as the type of essay whose business is to argue. The writer makes attempt to prove with sound reasons, the validity of his/her point of view put differently, argumentative essay is a piece of writing that takes a stance on an issue. A writer attempts to persuade readers to understand and support their point of view about a disputable topic by stating their reason/s and providing evidence to break it up. In argumentative essay, the writer presents two sides of an issue. He makes known his own stand with convincing reasons and facts. Consider this argumentative essay topic “Democracy is better than military rule”. One can either support or oppose the topic. In supporting or opposing the topic, one must first reflect on the two sides, then take a definite position with good reasons that can convince ones readers. Features of argumentative essay Below are the salient features (format or style) of an argumentative essay. 1. TITLE/TOPIC/HEADING : controversial title(or disputable topic or polar position) from which you take a stance is presented. The topic for debate is known as Motion while in argumentative essay writing, it is known as topic or title. Examples of argumentative essay topics a- Teachers are more important than doctors. b- English is more beneficial to students than mathematics. c- Mathematics is an easy subject. d- Military rule is better than civil rule e- Child labour should be a punishable offence. f- corporal punishment should not be a disciplinary measure. g- female circumcision should be abolished. h- boarding school is better than day school.

2. VOCATIVE : Salutation or greeting. Greet the audience, starting from the highest in rank of the dignitaries to the least personality present. Below are the formats of vocative in this essay type. Examples- Mr chairman (or the moderator), the organizers, panel of judges, accurate time keeper, my co-debators, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, good morning. 3. INTRODUCTION: The introduction should be interesting, captivating and stimulating, sustain the readers interest to want to read on. State the purpose and indicate the thesis(goal) of the essay then take a stance. Tell the audience what the motion is (all about), explain the polar position, the two faces or how side of a coin and indicate the side on which you stand. State what is boarding school, what is day school; add the background knowledge at this stage, if you are proposing the motion. Example: I am writing to oppose the motion which says that/ states, “Boarding school is better than day school” first of all, we all know that “Boarding school” is an educational institution where students live within premises while being given formal instructions during the school terms. Conversely, “day school” is an educational institution where students attend classes are given instruction during the day but return home in the evening on a daily basis. 4. BODY : at this stage, present some sound, solid and valid reasons to prove your claim with convincing points; why you believe a day school is better than boarding school as you have chosen. You should have at least, three to four good reasons to give in the body of the essay. If you are proposing the motion, the claims or arguments are presented at this level. Three to four valid ideas, reasons, evidences and facts could be presented in logical sequence or chronological order within paragraphs. Conversely, if you are opposing the motion, you could counter claim or counter the points raised by the opponent first then explain the motion an give or state at least three to four valid for opposing the motion. Pick on a point you think your opponent must have in support of the motive, e.g Boarding school……and try to counter it, by so doing, you are refuting earlier argument before presenting your points or lines of arguments in order to give weight to the actual position you are taking. Example The “chief proposer” has told you that students in boarding schools are more morally upright as teachers live with them in the compound to monitor their behavior. Do we not know that

cultism, homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. A day school goes home to his/her parents and siblings where all eyes are closely on him/her, he feels happy and none of these evil practices crosses his/her mind. A teacher does not give that close attention to boarders. The body of argumentative essay should be persuasive and devoid of waffing (avoid going off track/topic/theme or context), mal-propism, slang expression, contraction, dirty and abusive language. Employ the use of forceful and aggressive tone with rhetorical questions. Use moderate repetition and rhythmical pattern to spice up your writing, follow the rules of writing in English and properly apply the right punctuation marks, content, organization, expression and mechanical accuracy (C.O.E.M.A) should be apt in each content. 5. CONCLUSION : Have an effective and appealing conclusion. Summarize your ideas effectively and reaffirm your claim/s. sum up your points to remind your readers of the points you have raised. Use strong appealing words to make the readers (or listeners/hearers/audience) see your points of view and agree with you. Your ability to conclude your writing well will undoubtly win the audience to your side. Examples - with the points I have raised above or before you, I am left in no doubt that you will agree with me that day school is better than boarding school. 6 . CLOSURE : thank you

title: READING COMPREHENSION – READING FOR MAIN GIST
subject: English Language
rawText:
1. Reading Comprehension – Reading for Main Gist Meaning of Main Gist The main gist is the central idea or general meaning of a passage. It tells what the passage is mostly about, not the small details. How to Find the Main Gist • Read the title of the passage • Read the first and last sentences carefully • Look for repeated ideas or words • Ask: “What is the writer mainly talking about?” Example Passage: Environmental pollution is a major problem in many cities. Smoke from cars, factories, and burning refuse makes the air dirty. This affects human health and the environment. Main Gist: Environmental pollution and its effects. 2. Structure – Prefixes (Word Extension) Meaning of Prefix A prefix is a group of letters added to the beginning of a word to change its meaning. Common Prefixes and Their Meanings Prefix Meaning Example New Meaning un- not healthy → unhealthy not healthy in- not correct → incorrect not correct im- not possible → impossible not possible il- not legal → illegal not legal mis- wrong spell → misspell spell wrongly dis- opposite of agree → disagree not agree More Examples

• belief → unbelief • understand → misunderstand • responsible → irresponsible • appear → disappear 3. Vocabulary Development – Environmental Words Environment The environment is everything around us, including land, water, air, plants, animals, and human activities. Environmental Problems and Meanings • Environmental pollution: Making the environment dirty or unsafe • Bush burning: Setting fire to bushes and grass • Pest control: Methods used to kill or reduce harmful insects or animals • Disposal of refuse: Proper throwing away of waste materials • Sewage system: A system for carrying waste water away from homes • Smoking: Inhaling tobacco smoke, which pollutes the air and harms health • Drainages: Channels for carrying dirty water away • Environmental degradation: Damage to the environment due to human activities Sentence Examples • Bush burning causes environmental degradation. • Poor sewage systems lead to pollution. • Proper disposal of refuse keeps the environment clean.
