Such relationships exist between Singular and plural forms of regular nouns. pluraity is therefore Indicated with the suffix or Inflectional marker, ' s' or es which is also known as pulural markers. This letter’s’ has three forms of pronunciation which is realized as/s/, /z/ and /iz/. This however, depends on the sound that ends the Word (root word) before the plural’s’ is added. Sibilant is an’s’ sound or letter at the end of a word. It can be a letter or a group of letters added to the end of a Lexica / l root word to form plural or to change It into a new grammatical meaning. Types 1. 's suffix 2. es' suffix 3 ies' suffix 4. ves' suffix 1. Formation of plural using the’s’ suffice Examples: boy-boys day-day donkey-donkeys roof - roofs Key - keys Toy-toys. 2. Formation of plurals using the 'es' suffix Eg. Tomato- tomatoes class - classes

bush - bushes axis - axes basis - bases box- boxes fish- fishes match- matches Criss - Crises hypothesis - hypotheses- 3. Formation of plurals using the 'ies' suffix eg: Cuty - Cities Country - Countries. assembly - assemblies daily - dailies dairy dairies diary diaries 4 Formation of plurals using the 'ves' suffix Eg: thief -thieves. life - Lives self - selves Knife - Knives wife - wives Leaf - Leaves. 5. pluralization by either 's' suffix or res Suffix: scarf - scarfs/scarves

hoot-hoofs/hoves wharf - wharfs/ wharves. Plural marker's- S Z iz Ways of forming plural maker. A. pronounce the plural marker as "s' if the Sound before the plural element is any of the Following Voiceless Consonants / p, t, k, f, q/ Eg Coughs. Sits ropes tops. Parks. Light Cots. Spots. Stuffs books. Rakes B. pronounce 's' as 'z' If the sound before the plural element is a vowel or any of the following voiced Consonants /b, d, g, v, l, m, n, q Eg. logs/Logz/ Lords/ld:dz/ hangs/hredz Films/filmz/ C. pronounce’s’ as 'iz' if the sound before the plural element is any of the following Consonant. /s, z, d, s, ts/ Eg. Is rages. buzzes matches fishes. church tosses. batchs. dances judge. teases /s/. /z/. /iz/ maps. cabs. catches

ropes. robes. fences mats. Card's. teases parks. tongues. ashes hoofs. wings. wages mobs. hears. bushes. ete. Theme: Structure Unit Topic: Types of sentences. Lesson Topic: The simple, compound, Complex an d Compound complex sentences A Sentence is a is a group of words expressing a statement, a question or an order usually Containing a subject and a verb. A Sentence Start with a capital letter and ends with a full-stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark Features of a sentence A sentence contains two necessary part Subject and predicate. The subject points to or names the person (s) thing(s) the sentence talks about ie who or what is being discussed. Eg. The boy dances well chioma died. The predicate indicates what is said on discussed about the person or thing. It includes the verb, auxiliary, adverb and adjective which say something about the subject. Eg: They suffered Babies eat. Subject may have marker like" my, the, a etc while the predicate may have auxiliary like "will, could has etc .

Eg the game must be going on now my Parents are Leaving . Types of sentence 1 . Simple sentence 2. Compound sentence 3. Complex senten ce 4. Compound complex sentence 1. Simple sentence: this contains one subject and one predicate or verb unit. It is made up of one main clause. Eg. a. the woman ran b. The thief has been caught. 2. Compound sentence: This contains two main clauses Linked by co-ordinating Conjunction Like "and, but or etc Eg a. the work stopped but the tools were kept inside. b. Ngozi found the goat and she took it to her mother 3. Complex sentence: This contains one main clause and one or more subordinate clauses. It is linked by the following who, which, as before, although, because, as If, unless, even though, when etc Eg: a. when it rains, he does not go to work. b. John did not do the assignment which the teacher gave him. 4. Compound complex sentence: This is made up of two or more main clauses and on or more Subordinate clauses. Eg: a. She Informed her parents that she was travelling to Lokoja to visit her uncle , tout she Changed her plans and went to kaduna where she stayed with some friends for a week. b. He came in (and) told us to leave the class, though he did not tell us the reason.

Such relationships exist between Singular and plural forms of regular nouns. pluraity is therefore Indicated with the suffix or Inflectional marker, ' s' or es which is also known as pulural markers. This letter’s’ has three forms of pronunciation which is realized as/s/, /z/ and /iz/. This however, depends on the sound that ends the Word (root word) before the plural’s’ is added. Sibilant is an’s’ sound or letter at the end of a word. It can be a letter or a group of letters added to the end of a Lexica / l root word to form plural or to change It into a new grammatical meaning. Types 1. 's suffix 2. es' suffix 3 ies' suffix 4. ves' suffix 1. Formation of plural using the’s’ suffice Examples: boy-boys day-day donkey-donkeys roof - roofs Key - keys Toy-toys. 2. Formation of plurals using the 'es' suffix Eg. Tomato- tomatoes class - classes

bush - bushes axis - axes basis - bases box- boxes fish- fishes match- matches Criss - Crises hypothesis - hypotheses- 3. Formation of plurals using the 'ies' suffix eg: Cuty - Cities Country - Countries. assembly - assemblies daily - dailies dairy dairies diary diaries 4 Formation of plurals using the 'ves' suffix Eg: thief -thieves. life - Lives self - selves Knife - Knives wife - wives Leaf - Leaves. 5. pluralization by either 's' suffix or res Suffix: scarf - scarfs/scarves

hoot-hoofs/hoves wharf - wharfs/ wharves. Plural marker's- S Z iz Ways of forming plural maker. Stuffs books. Is rages. buzzes matches fishes. church tosses. batchs. dances judge. teases /s/. /z/. /iz/ maps. cabs. catches

ropes. robes. fences mats. Card's. teases parks. tongues. ashes hoofs. wings. wages mobs. hears. bushes. ete. Theme: Structure Unit Topic: Types of sentences. Lesson Topic: The simple, compound, Complex an d Compound complex sentences A Sentence is a is a group of words expressing a statement, a question or an order usually Containing a subject and a verb. A Sentence Start with a capital letter and ends with a full-stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark Features of a sentence A sentence contains two necessary part Subject and predicate. The subject points to or names the person (s) thing(s) the sentence talks about ie who or what is being discussed. Eg. The boy dances well chioma died. The predicate indicates what is said on discussed about the person or thing. It includes the verb, auxiliary, adverb and adjective which say something about the subject. Eg: They suffered Babies eat. Subject may have marker like" my, the, a etc while the predicate may have auxiliary like "will, could has etc .

Eg the game must be going on now my Parents are Leaving . Types of sentence 1 . Simple sentence 2. Compound sentence 3. Complex senten ce 4. Compound complex sentence 1. Simple sentence: this contains one subject and one predicate or verb unit. It is made up of one main clause. Eg. a. the woman ran b. The thief has been caught. 2. Compound sentence: This contains two main clauses Linked by co-ordinating Conjunction Like "and, but or etc Eg a. the work stopped but the tools were kept inside. b. Ngozi found the goat and she took it to her mother 3. Complex sentence: This contains one main clause and one or more subordinate clauses. It is linked by the following who, which, as before, although, because, as If, unless, even though, when etc Eg: a. when it rains, he does not go to work. b. John did not do the assignment which the teacher gave him. 4. Compound complex sentence: This is made up of two or more main clauses and on or more Subordinate clauses. Eg: a. She Informed her parents that she was travelling to Lokoja to visit her uncle , tout she Changed her plans and went to kaduna where she stayed with some friends for a week. b. He came in (and) told us to leave the class, though he did not tell us the reason.

title: WORDS ASSOCIATED WITH COMMERCE
subject: English Language
rawText:
Week 2 Theme: speech (oral) Unit Topic: listening Comprehension Lesson Topic: listening to debates for main point and passing judgment. Debate is argument between two groups in which the speaker is expected to argue logically in supporter against a gives topic. It arms at convincing the reader or the audience to Share in the opinion or view points of The Speaker The debate is between girls and boys on the Topic Girls should be given equal educational opportunity as their male counterparts. Points for proposing 1. Before God, there is equality of all men 2. An educated girl makes a better wife. Men look out for good manners and Intelligence. women who will impact her knowledge to her Children. 3. If a girl is well educated, she will have good Job and be less dependent to the husband and relative 4. An educated girl will be a role model to her children. Opposing 1 God created man to be the head and not equal to a woman 2. If girl have equal educational opportunities as have male Counterparts, lack of respect for the man well thrive in families when they are married and this will surely lead to divorce. 3. Girls who are educated turn out to be working class mothers. Most working class are so occupied with office work that they hardly have time for their husbands and children. 4. The family tree is built on the male members. so the male should have an edge over the female. Theme: Register Unit Topic: Vocabulary Development Lesser Topic: Words associated with Commerce

Commerce can be defined as all the activities Involved in buying, selling and distribution of goods and services through the assistance of warehousing Insurance, advertising, Communication and how people buy sell and distribute goods and services. Words associated with commerce 1. Retailer: a person that sells goods to customers in a shop. 2. Exporter: a person or Company or Country that sells goods to another Country 3. Wholesaler: a person or Company who sells goods wholesale to retailers, that is in bulk quantity. 4. Imports: goods and services which we buy from other Countries. 5. Foreign trade: trade which takes place between two countries, it is also called external trade. 6 Partnership: a business organization formed by at least two persons to carry on business in Common with the aim of making profit. 7. Business transaction: a transfer of goods for services from one person to another in exchange, for cash or credit. 8. Ware housing: The business or practice of Storing Large quantities of goods especially in warehouses until they are demanded for 9. Advertising: The process & creating awareness about the existence of a product m order to promote demand or Sale. 10. Consumer: Someone who buys and uses products and services. 11. Capital: money or property especially when it is used to start a business or to Produce more wealth 12. Commercial Products: are those products produced and sold im Large quantities 13 production: The process of making or growing things to be sold especially m Large quantities. 14. manufacturing: The process or business of producing goods in factories 15 Banking: banks make funds available to business men for business transactions. Theme: Reading Comprehension Unit Topic: Reading to answer questions on a given Passage Lesson Topic: War on honest men..

Lesson will be on according to the passage no Page 11 war on honest men". The answers should be discussed by the teacher class.

Theme : speech Unit topic: Consonant sound Lesson topic: Revision on Consonant sound write five (5) words each on all the Consonant sound studed this term 1./P/ 2. /b/ 3/t/ 4./d/ 5. /k/ 6./g/ 7./n/ 8./m/ 9./g/ 10./s/ 11. /z/ 12. /ts/ 13./dz/ Theme: Structure Unit topic: Idioms Lesson topic: idiomatic Expression Am idiom is a fixed group of words or Phrase with a special meaning, which is different from the meaning of the individual words. It Is not easy to guess the meaning of an Idiom from the meaning of the separate words with which it is formed. For example" to kick the bucket" is an idiom meaning to die". This meaning has no Connection with either kicking or bucket. Also to spill the beans is not at all connected with beans. It means to tell something that a secret, ar to leak a Secret sometimes However, the meaning of an idiom can be guessed from the meaning of one of the Words. Eg the Idiom ‘to rack your brains meaning to think hard can be guessed from the word brains' in the Idiom. Similarly, to live in the Lap of Luxury meaning to live in a very luxurious way can also be guessed from the word 'Luxury" in the Idiom. Proverbs, some phrasal verbs, and wise sayings are also grouped under Idioms.

Idiomatic expressions and their Example 1. To be tied to the bottle - a drank 2. To pull one's legs - to know one's reactions. 3. To step on people's toes - to offend people. 4. To put round pegs in square holes - to do things wrongly 5. To do something at the nick of time - to do something at exactly on time. 6. To keep everyone on his toes: to keep everyone busy. 7. To experience a bitter pill-to have an unpleasant experience. 8. to have one's tongue on his cheek - not serious. 9. A bird at hand is worth two in the bush - what you already have worth more than those you are still capacity Theme: Comprehension Unit topic. WEEK 4 1. SPEECH : Unstressed vowel sounds / ə/. Schwa sound /ə/ vowel /Ձ/. Vowel sounds are sounds that are produced without any frication or obstruction in the flow of air in the vocal cord. /ə/ the central character is an upside-down and backward lower-case “e”= /əin English the vowel no 2/Ձ/ is used to represent the weak form of vowel in an unstressed (unaccepted) syllable of a given word, it is not stressed in any word. It is referred to as schwa sound. Schwa is a short vowel produced with the lips in neutral position, it is the mid central vowel or neutral vowel sound typically occurring in unstressed syllables in English. In articulation the sound, the tongue is in a central position and the lip in a neutral position. Note: the schwa sound /ə/ is represented by the letters “ a, ar,e, er, eo/ei, I, iou, o, or, oar, ou/our, ough, oir, re,u, ure, in some words. This means that the underline letters in the word below are pronounced as the schwa sound In English. Spelling symbols for /ə/ 1. letter “ɋ” as in əgo, chinə,məchete, orphən, moveəble, villə, womən, mirəcle, mədəm ete 2. letter “ɋr” as in collar, pərticular, monərchy, grəmmər, motər, forwərd, sugər, stew ərd etc. 3. letter “e” as in open, sharpen, deepen, ripen, cemetery, etc. 4. letter “er” as in starter, wonder, founder, perhaps, superman, latter, weather, etc. 5. letters “eou” as in righteous. 6. letters “eo/ei” as in luncheon, foreigner, surgeon, pigeon etc. 7. letter “I” as in possible, terrible, accessible, invisible, divisible, permissible etc. 8. letter “o” as in collate, photography, tomorrow, obey, polite, second, pilot, wisdom, etc 9. letters “oar” as in cupboard. 10.. letters “or” as in doctor, rector, supervisor, governor, minor, calculator, forget, etc. 11. letters “ou/our” as in famous, generous, glamour, colour, favour, rumour etc. 12. letters “ough” as in thorough 13. letters “oir” as in junior, senior etc. 14.letter “re” as in acre, metre, caliber, goiter, theatre, centra, meager, manouvre etc.

15. letter “u” as in litmus, suspect, minus, autumn, support, column, sustain, campus, etc 16. letter “ur“ as in augur, survive, surprise, surround, survey, surmount. Etc. 17. letters “ure” as in figure, furniture, injure, nature, culture, seizure, structure, etc The sound understudy can occur at the initial, medical and final position of a word thus: Initial position medical position final position 1. Again /əgen/ Commit /kəmit / Teacher /ti:tꭍə/ 2. Above /əbnv/ Success /səkses/ Mother /mΛðə/ 3. Offend /əfend/ Cupboard /kΛbə/ Plumber /plΛmə / 4. Among /əmΛg/ Vegetable /veʤtəbl/ Actor/ӕktə/ 5. Attack /ətӕk/ Method /meѳəd/ Sister/sist ə/ ii. STRUCTURE: Pronoun – Types of pronoun. Pronouns are words that are used to replace nouns in expressions, they are words that are used instead of a noun or in replacement of a noun to avoid the repetition of such nouns. The noun being replaced is referred to as the antecedent. E.g Ngozi and John are here. They are here. Pronouns unlike nouns, cannot be preceded by modifiers and they are not accompanied by the apostrophe like nouns. We cannot have your’s or their’s but we can have Tom’s as in Tom’s house. E.G Pronouns are used in sentences according to the number, gender, and case of the replaced noun or the function it performs. Consistency is required in the use of pronouns in sequence. She/he, it, mine, your, this, that, are quintessential examples of some pronouns. Types of pronoun The nine (9) types of pronouns in English includes personal, possessive, demonstrative, emphatic or intensive, interrogative, indefinite, relative, reciprocal and reflective or reflexive as earlier discussed in week one(1) or two (2), have more explanations of each below

1. personal pronouns: these refer to specific people or things, for example: I, me , you, she, he, they, us, it. They are used according to the number (singular or plural) of people or things. They also reflect gender and case thus: A.- number (singular and plural ) PERSON SINGULAR PLURAL First person i. me we, us Second person you you Third person he, she, it, her, him. They, them. B. Gender differentiates between male and female. Gender pronouns Masculine (male) he, him. Feminine (female) she, her Neuter (neutral) it, they, them. C. case Case indicates the role a pronoun is playing in an expression, whether subjective or objective. i. – subject pronoun performs the action of the verb or plays the role of the subject in a sentence. E. g He went home Subject He can be replaced with other subject pronouns; I, you, she, they. ii. Objective pronouns: these pronouns act as the receiver of the action of the verb thus; they occupy the object position in a sentence. Example mum gave me a pair of shoes subject object.

2. EMPHATIC OR INTENSIVE PRONOUN: Emphatic or intensive pronouns have the suffixes – self or selves like the reflective pronouns but they emphasize the noun (or pronoun) that precedes them. Example i. Ann herself went there . noun antecedent. Pronoun emphasizing Ann. The following expressions are wrong; himself, sheself, theirselves, themselves, weselves, ourself. 3. INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS: Interrogative pronouns are used to ask questions. We have who, whom, which, whose and what. Each of these examples can be formed with the suffix – ever to get whoever, whenever, whichever. Note that we use which to ask about a noun that is not a human being, it could be an animal or an object. Who are used for people and whom asks questions about the object (receiver) of the action. Whose expresses ownership E.g whose books are these? 4 .REFLECTIVE OR REFLEXIVE PRONOUNS : These pronouns refer back to the subject. The singular forms are myself, yourself, himself, herself, and their plural forms are ourselves, yourselves and themselves. E.G I took care of myself during the holiday. (“I” = subject and pronoun, “myself refer to it) 5 . RECIPROCAL PRONOUNS: These are pronouns used to join two or more subject. They are used to indicate a two-way relationship between two or more people. They are only two reciprocal pronoun in English language Viz , each other and one another. a. – each other: this is used to join two subjects, when talking about two people. E.g Tunde and Musa greeted each other. b. – one another: this is used to join three or more subjects when talking about an action involving more than two people. E.g

At the re-union, the old friends hugged one another. 6. DEMONSTRATIVE PRONOUNS: Demonstrative involves a supplementary gesture. (demonstration) is a special setting in order to determine reference. They point to specific items being referred to within a sentence. Basically, there are four demonstrative pronoun in English; this, these, that, those. I. This, these. - This (pronounced with /s/) is used for a singular item. While these(pronounced with/z/) refers to more than one item, it indicates plurality. This/these † noun are used to refer to things near to use (they refer to items that are not close to the speaker) or to things that we are mentioning now. ii. That, those That and those † noun are used to refer to things that are not so near (they refer to singular and plural but distance objects accordingly) or to things we mentioned before or to things that we are going to mention later. POSITION OF DEMONSTRATIVEPRONOUN Demonstrative pronouns can appear at the initial, medial, penultimate and final positions of a sentence. FUNCTIONS OF DEMONSTRACTIVE PRONOUNS Demonstrative pronoun perform the following functions in a sentences. 1. They point to specific items bring referred to within a sentences. 2.They indicate items that are nearby or far away in space/place or time. iii COMPREHENSION: Reading for critical evaluation. Reading for critical evaluation is the ability to make careful Judgements about how good or bad a text, a person, a situation, a law etc is, it is about readers ability to detect facts, opinions, logicality/ consistency, illogicality/ inconsistency in a written comprehension passage, it is the ability to access the

argument or proposition and to be able to determine its appropriateness and writes it on the board as the topic to be taught. One of the skills that are tested In comprehension questions is your ability to read the passage for critical evaluation. For example, as you read, you need to examine the three factors that are involved in a reading exercise the writer, the writing and reader. The writing is the topic, the subject matter, this will be judged on its own merits as the reader takes a look at the content, and context. Consider this short text for example: “in1984 when Nigeria had her independence, the Americans did not know that Nigeria would be a fertile nation economically. Otherwise, they would have delayed the independence in order to exploit and plunder our resources more”. The question is: did Nigeria gain independence in 1984? Or you ask what was America’s connection with Nigeria independence? Now, ponder more on the writers content and context. Thus, is the author able to convey the intended message in the text above? This is reading for critical evaluation. As the reader, you need to understand the purpose for which you are reading. What are your expectations in this writing? Can you find them? Are the facts or points satisfactory? You need to look closely at the writing to get what you want. The essence of reading for critical evaluation is to have questions in mind to probe the writer, the writing and yourself and to try to provide answers to all the questions asked below: i. are there understatements or exaggeration? ii. are the facts correct? iii. does the writers mix facts with opinions? Iv .are there illogicalities or inconsistencies? v. is any information left out? vi. are you able to grasp connections, transitions or implied meaning? vii. what are the purpose of the writer? What is he/she driving at or what does she / he want me to know? What message is she/ he passing across? viii. is the writer appealing, arguing, giving facts, expressing opinion, supporting a view, explaining a process, etc. ix. is the writer capable of treating the subject matter? Has he/she the knowledge or the facts?. x. is the writer biased? Does he/she tilt towards a particular view or factor?

The questions are good preparation for reading for critical evaluation. Your assessment, your analysis and your comprehension will improve if you have a questioning mind as you read. Referred to “uduefe the rubber thief” on page 103-104 and answer question number 1-3 Iv. CONTINUOUS WRITING- ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY Argumentative essay I a form of persuasive writing which is any written work that tries to convince or influence the reader of the writers opinion. Argumentative essay as the type of essay whose business is to argue. The writer makes attempt to prove with sound reasons, the validity of his/her point of view put differently, argumentative essay is a piece of writing that takes a stance on an issue. A writer attempts to persuade readers to understand and support their point of view about a disputable topic by stating their reason/s and providing evidence to break it up. In argumentative essay, the writer presents two sides of an issue. He makes known his own stand with convincing reasons and facts. Consider this argumentative essay topic “Democracy is better than military rule”. One can either support or oppose the topic. In supporting or opposing the topic, one must first reflect on the two sides, then take a definite position with good reasons that can convince ones readers. Features of argumentative essay Below are the salient features (format or style) of an argumentative essay. 1. TITLE/TOPIC/HEADING : controversial title(or disputable topic or polar position) from which you take a stance is presented. The topic for debate is known as Motion while in argumentative essay writing, it is known as topic or title. Examples of argumentative essay topics a- Teachers are more important than doctors. b- English is more beneficial to students than mathematics. c- Mathematics is an easy subject. d- Military rule is better than civil rule e- Child labour should be a punishable offence. f- corporal punishment should not be a disciplinary measure. g- female circumcision should be abolished.

h- boarding school is better than day school. 2. VOCATIVE : Salutation or greeting. Greet the audience, starting from the highest in rank of the dignitaries to the least personality present. Below are the formats of vocative in this essay type. Examples- Mr chairman (or the moderator), the organizers, panel of judges, accurate time keeper, my co-debators, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, good morning. 3. INTRODUCTION: The introduction should be interesting, captivating and stimulating, sustain the readers interest to want to read on. State the purpose and indicate the thesis(goal) of the essay then take a stance. Tell the audience what the motion is (all about), explain the polar position, the two faces or how side of a coin and indicate the side on which you stand. State what is boarding school, what is day school; add the background knowledge at this stage, if you are proposing the motion. Example: I am writing to oppose the motion which says that/ states, “Boarding school is better than day school” first of all, we all know that “Boarding school” is an educational institution where students live within premises while being given formal instructions during the school terms. Conversely, “day school” is an educational institution where students attend classes are given instruction during the day but return home in the evening on a daily basis. 4. BODY : at this stage, present some sound, solid and valid reasons to prove your claim with convincing points; why you believe a day school is better than boarding school as you have chosen. You should have at least, three to four good reasons to give in the body of the essay. If you are proposing the motion, the claims or arguments are presented at this level. Three to four valid ideas, reasons, evidences and facts could be presented in logical sequence or chronological order within paragraphs. Conversely, if you are opposing the motion, you could counter claim or counter the points raised by the opponent first then explain the motion an give or state at least three to four valid for opposing the motion. Pick on a point you think your opponent must have in support of the motive, e.g Boarding school……and try to counter it, by so doing, you are refuting earlier argument before presenting your points or lines of arguments in order to give weight to the actual position you are taking. Example The “chief proposer” has told you that students in boarding schools are more morally upright as teachers live with them in the compound to monitor their behavior. Do we not know that cultism,

homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. A day school goes home to his/her parents and siblings where all eyes are closely on him/her, he feels happy and none of these evil practices crosses his/her mind. A teacher does not give that close attention to boarders. The body of argumentative essay should be persuasive and devoid of waffing (avoid going off track/topic/theme or context), mal-propism, slang expression, contraction, dirty and abusive language. Employ the use of forceful and aggressive tone with rhetorical questions. Use moderate repetition and rhythmical pattern to spice up your writing, follow the rules of writing in English and properly apply the right punctuation marks, content, organization, expression and mechanical accuracy (C.O.E.M.A) should be apt in each content. 5. CONCLUSION : Have an effective and appealing conclusion. Summarize your ideas effectively and reaffirm your claim/s. sum up your points to remind your readers of the points you have raised. homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. A teacher does not give that close attention to boarders. CONCLUSION : Have an effective and appealing conclusion. Summarize your ideas effectively and reaffirm your claim/s. sum up your points to remind your readers of the points you have raised. Use strong appealing words to make the readers (or listeners/hearers/audience) see your points of view and agree with you. Your ability to conclude your writing well will undoubtly win the audience to your side. homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. pages.text: WEEK 4 1. SPEECH : Unstressed vowel sounds / ə/. Schwa sound /ə/ vowel /Ձ/. Vowel sounds are sounds that are produced without any frication or obstruction in the flow of air in the vocal cord. /ə/ the central character is an upside-down and backward lower-case “e”= /əin English the vowel no 2/Ձ/ is used to represent the weak form of vowel in an unstressed (unaccepted) syllable of a given word, it is not stressed in any word. It is referred to as schwa sound. Schwa is a short vowel produced with the lips in neutral position, it is the mid central vowel or neutral vowel sound typically occurring in unstressed syllables in English. In articulation the sound, the tongue is in a central position and the lip in a neutral position. Note: the schwa sound /ə/ is represented by the letters “ a, ar,e, er, eo/ei, I, iou, o, or, oar, ou/our, ough, oir, re,u, ure, in some words. This means that the underline letters in the word below are pronounced as the schwa sound In English. Spelling symbols for /ə/ 1. letter “ɋ” as in əgo, chinə,məchete, orphən, moveəble, villə, womən, mirəcle, mədəm ete 2. letter “ɋr” as in collar, pərticular, monərchy, grəmmər, motər, forwərd, sugər, stew ərd etc. 3. letter “e” as in open, sharpen, deepen, ripen, cemetery, etc. 4. letter “er” as in starter, wonder, founder, perhaps, superman, latter, weather, etc. 5. letters “eou” as in righteous. 6. letters “eo/ei” as in luncheon, foreigner, surgeon, pigeon etc. 7. letter “I” as in possible, terrible, accessible, invisible, divisible, permissible etc. 8. letter “o” as in collate, photography, tomorrow, obey, polite, second, pilot, wisdom, etc 9. letters “oar” as in cupboard. 10.. letters “or” as in doctor, rector, supervisor, governor, minor, calculator, forget, etc. 11. letters “ou/our” as in famous, generous, glamour, colour, favour, rumour etc. 12. letters “ough” as in thorough 13. letters “oir” as in junior, senior etc. 14.letter “re” as in acre, metre, caliber, goiter, theatre, centra, meager, manouvre etc.

15. letter “u” as in litmus, suspect, minus, autumn, support, column, sustain, campus, etc 16. letter “ur“ as in augur, survive, surprise, surround, survey, surmount. Etc. 17. letters “ure” as in figure, furniture, injure, nature, culture, seizure, structure, etc The sound understudy can occur at the initial, medical and final position of a word thus: Initial position medical position final position 1. Again /əgen/ Commit /kəmit / Teacher /ti:tꭍə/ 2. Above /əbnv/ Success /səkses/ Mother /mΛðə/ 3. Offend /əfend/ Cupboard /kΛbə/ Plumber /plΛmə / 4. Among /əmΛg/ Vegetable /veʤtəbl/ Actor/ӕktə/ 5. Attack /ətӕk/ Method /meѳəd/ Sister/sist ə/ ii. STRUCTURE: Pronoun – Types of pronoun. Pronouns are words that are used to replace nouns in expressions, they are words that are used instead of a noun or in replacement of a noun to avoid the repetition of such nouns. The noun being replaced is referred to as the antecedent. E.g Ngozi and John are here. They are here. Pronouns unlike nouns, cannot be preceded by modifiers and they are not accompanied by the apostrophe like nouns. We cannot have your’s or their’s but we can have Tom’s as in Tom’s house. E.G Pronouns are used in sentences according to the number, gender, and case of the replaced noun or the function it performs. Consistency is required in the use of pronouns in sequence. She/he, it, mine, your, this, that, are quintessential examples of some pronouns. Types of pronoun The nine (9) types of pronouns in English includes personal, possessive, demonstrative, emphatic or intensive, interrogative, indefinite, relative, reciprocal and reflective or reflexive as earlier discussed in week one(1) or two (2), have more explanations of each below

1. personal pronouns: these refer to specific people or things, for example: I, me , you, she, he, they, us, it. They are used according to the number (singular or plural) of people or things. They also reflect gender and case thus: A.- number (singular and plural ) PERSON SINGULAR PLURAL First person i. me we, us Second person you you Third person he, she, it, her, him. They, them. B. Gender differentiates between male and female. Gender pronouns Masculine (male) he, him. Feminine (female) she, her Neuter (neutral) it, they, them. C. case Case indicates the role a pronoun is playing in an expression, whether subjective or objective. i. – subject pronoun performs the action of the verb or plays the role of the subject in a sentence. E. g He went home Subject He can be replaced with other subject pronouns; I, you, she, they. ii. Objective pronouns: these pronouns act as the receiver of the action of the verb thus; they occupy the object position in a sentence. Example mum gave me a pair of shoes subject object.

2. EMPHATIC OR INTENSIVE PRONOUN: Emphatic or intensive pronouns have the suffixes – self or selves like the reflective pronouns but they emphasize the noun (or pronoun) that precedes them. Example i. Ann herself went there . noun antecedent. Pronoun emphasizing Ann. The following expressions are wrong; himself, sheself, theirselves, themselves, weselves, ourself. 3. INTERROGATIVE PRONOUNS: Interrogative pronouns are used to ask questions. We have who, whom, which, whose and what. Each of these examples can be formed with the suffix – ever to get whoever, whenever, whichever. Note that we use which to ask about a noun that is not a human being, it could be an animal or an object. Who are used for people and whom asks questions about the object (receiver) of the action. Whose expresses ownership E.g whose books are these? 4 .REFLECTIVE OR REFLEXIVE PRONOUNS : These pronouns refer back to the subject. The singular forms are myself, yourself, himself, herself, and their plural forms are ourselves, yourselves and themselves. E.G I took care of myself during the holiday. (“I” = subject and pronoun, “myself refer to it) 5 . RECIPROCAL PRONOUNS: These are pronouns used to join two or more subject. They are used to indicate a two-way relationship between two or more people. They are only two reciprocal pronoun in English language Viz , each other and one another. a. – each other: this is used to join two subjects, when talking about two people. E.g Tunde and Musa greeted each other. b. – one another: this is used to join three or more subjects when talking about an action involving more than two people. E.g

At the re-union, the old friends hugged one another. 6. DEMONSTRATIVE PRONOUNS: Demonstrative involves a supplementary gesture. (demonstration) is a special setting in order to determine reference. They point to specific items being referred to within a sentence. Basically, there are four demonstrative pronoun in English; this, these, that, those. I. This, these. - This (pronounced with /s/) is used for a singular item. While these(pronounced with/z/) refers to more than one item, it indicates plurality. This/these † noun are used to refer to things near to use (they refer to items that are not close to the speaker) or to things that we are mentioning now. ii. That, those That and those † noun are used to refer to things that are not so near (they refer to singular and plural but distance objects accordingly) or to things we mentioned before or to things that we are going to mention later. POSITION OF DEMONSTRATIVEPRONOUN Demonstrative pronouns can appear at the initial, medial, penultimate and final positions of a sentence. FUNCTIONS OF DEMONSTRACTIVE PRONOUNS Demonstrative pronoun perform the following functions in a sentences. 1. They point to specific items bring referred to within a sentences. 2.They indicate items that are nearby or far away in space/place or time. iii COMPREHENSION: Reading for critical evaluation. Reading for critical evaluation is the ability to make careful Judgements about how good or bad a text, a person, a situation, a law etc is, it is about readers ability to detect facts, opinions, logicality/ consistency, illogicality/ inconsistency in a written comprehension passage, it is the ability to access the

argument or proposition and to be able to determine its appropriateness and writes it on the board as the topic to be taught. One of the skills that are tested In comprehension questions is your ability to read the passage for critical evaluation. For example, as you read, you need to examine the three factors that are involved in a reading exercise the writer, the writing and reader. The writing is the topic, the subject matter, this will be judged on its own merits as the reader takes a look at the content, and context. Consider this short text for example: “in1984 when Nigeria had her independence, the Americans did not know that Nigeria would be a fertile nation economically. Otherwise, they would have delayed the independence in order to exploit and plunder our resources more”. The question is: did Nigeria gain independence in 1984? Or you ask what was America’s connection with Nigeria independence? Now, ponder more on the writers content and context. Thus, is the author able to convey the intended message in the text above? This is reading for critical evaluation. As the reader, you need to understand the purpose for which you are reading. What are your expectations in this writing? Can you find them? Are the facts or points satisfactory? You need to look closely at the writing to get what you want. The essence of reading for critical evaluation is to have questions in mind to probe the writer, the writing and yourself and to try to provide answers to all the questions asked below: i. are there understatements or exaggeration? ii. are the facts correct? iii. does the writers mix facts with opinions? Iv .are there illogicalities or inconsistencies? v. is any information left out? vi. are you able to grasp connections, transitions or implied meaning? vii. what are the purpose of the writer? What is he/she driving at or what does she / he want me to know? What message is she/ he passing across? viii. is the writer appealing, arguing, giving facts, expressing opinion, supporting a view, explaining a process, etc. ix. is the writer capable of treating the subject matter? Has he/she the knowledge or the facts?. x. is the writer biased? Does he/she tilt towards a particular view or factor?

The questions are good preparation for reading for critical evaluation. Your assessment, your analysis and your comprehension will improve if you have a questioning mind as you read. Referred to “uduefe the rubber thief” on page 103-104 and answer question number 1-3 Iv. CONTINUOUS WRITING- ARGUMENTATIVE ESSAY Argumentative essay I a form of persuasive writing which is any written work that tries to convince or influence the reader of the writers opinion. Argumentative essay as the type of essay whose business is to argue. The writer makes attempt to prove with sound reasons, the validity of his/her point of view put differently, argumentative essay is a piece of writing that takes a stance on an issue. A writer attempts to persuade readers to understand and support their point of view about a disputable topic by stating their reason/s and providing evidence to break it up. In argumentative essay, the writer presents two sides of an issue. He makes known his own stand with convincing reasons and facts. Consider this argumentative essay topic “Democracy is better than military rule”. One can either support or oppose the topic. In supporting or opposing the topic, one must first reflect on the two sides, then take a definite position with good reasons that can convince ones readers. Features of argumentative essay Below are the salient features (format or style) of an argumentative essay. 1. TITLE/TOPIC/HEADING : controversial title(or disputable topic or polar position) from which you take a stance is presented. The topic for debate is known as Motion while in argumentative essay writing, it is known as topic or title. Examples of argumentative essay topics a- Teachers are more important than doctors. b- English is more beneficial to students than mathematics. c- Mathematics is an easy subject. d- Military rule is better than civil rule e- Child labour should be a punishable offence. f- corporal punishment should not be a disciplinary measure. g- female circumcision should be abolished.

h- boarding school is better than day school. 2. VOCATIVE : Salutation or greeting. Greet the audience, starting from the highest in rank of the dignitaries to the least personality present. Below are the formats of vocative in this essay type. Examples- Mr chairman (or the moderator), the organizers, panel of judges, accurate time keeper, my co-debators, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, good morning. 3. INTRODUCTION: The introduction should be interesting, captivating and stimulating, sustain the readers interest to want to read on. State the purpose and indicate the thesis(goal) of the essay then take a stance. Tell the audience what the motion is (all about), explain the polar position, the two faces or how side of a coin and indicate the side on which you stand. State what is boarding school, what is day school; add the background knowledge at this stage, if you are proposing the motion. Example: I am writing to oppose the motion which says that/ states, “Boarding school is better than day school” first of all, we all know that “Boarding school” is an educational institution where students live within premises while being given formal instructions during the school terms. Conversely, “day school” is an educational institution where students attend classes are given instruction during the day but return home in the evening on a daily basis. 4. BODY : at this stage, present some sound, solid and valid reasons to prove your claim with convincing points; why you believe a day school is better than boarding school as you have chosen. You should have at least, three to four good reasons to give in the body of the essay. If you are proposing the motion, the claims or arguments are presented at this level. Three to four valid ideas, reasons, evidences and facts could be presented in logical sequence or chronological order within paragraphs. Conversely, if you are opposing the motion, you could counter claim or counter the points raised by the opponent first then explain the motion an give or state at least three to four valid for opposing the motion. Pick on a point you think your opponent must have in support of the motive, e.g Boarding school……and try to counter it, by so doing, you are refuting earlier argument before presenting your points or lines of arguments in order to give weight to the actual position you are taking. Example The “chief proposer” has told you that students in boarding schools are more morally upright as teachers live with them in the compound to monitor their behavior. Do we not know that cultism,

homosexuality and lesbianism started from boarding houses. A day school goes home to his/her parents and siblings where all eyes are closely on him/her, he feels happy and none of these evil practices crosses his/her mind. A teacher does not give that close attention to boarders. The body of argumentative essay should be persuasive and devoid of waffing (avoid going off track/topic/theme or context), mal-propism, slang expression, contraction, dirty and abusive language. Employ the use of forceful and aggressive tone with rhetorical questions. Use moderate repetition and rhythmical pattern to spice up your writing, follow the rules of writing in English and properly apply the right punctuation marks, content, organization, expression and mechanical accuracy (C.O.E.M.A) should be apt in each content. 5. CONCLUSION : Have an effective and appealing conclusion. Summarize your ideas effectively and reaffirm your claim/s. sum up your points to remind your readers of the points you have raised. Use strong appealing words to make the readers (or listeners/hearers/audience) see your points of view and agree with you. Your ability to conclude your writing well will undoubtly win the audience to your side. Examples - with the points I have raised above or before you, I am left in no doubt that you will agree with me that day school is better than boarding school. 6 . CLOSURE : thank you

Speech Word Stress (Monosyllabic and Polysyllabic Words) Word stress refers to the emphasis placed on a particular syllable in a word when it is spoken. Monosyllabic Words Monosyllabic words have one syllable , so the stress naturally falls on that syllable. Examples:  book  run  cat  man  house ➡ These words are pronounced with equal emphasis since they have only one syllable. Polysyllabic Words Polysyllabic words have two or more syllables . One syllable is stressed more than the others. Examples:  doc tor  hos pital  me di cine  a bout  pa tient Importance of Word Stress  Helps in correct pronunciation  Prevents misunderstanding  Makes speech clear and natural 2. Vocabulary Development

Words Associated with Medicine Medicine deals with the prevention and treatment of illness. Common Medical Vocabulary  Doctor – a medical professional  Nurse – assists in caring for patients  Patient – a person receiving treatment  Hospital – place for medical care  Clinic – smaller medical center  Medicine/Drug – substance used to treat illness  Injection – medicine given with a needle  Prescription – doctor’s written instruction for drugs  Diagnosis – identification of a disease  Treatment – care given to cure illness  Surgery – medical operation  Disease – illness  Symptoms – signs of illness  Vaccine – medicine that prevents disease 3. Structure Verb Forms – Active and Passive Verbs show action or state of being. Sentences can be in active or passive voice. Active Voice In the active voice , the subject performs the action . Structure: Subject + Verb + Object Example:  The doctor treated the patient . Passive Voice

In the passive voice , the action is done to the subject . Structure: Object + be + Past Participle (+ by subject) Example:  The patient was treated (by the doctor). When to Use Passive Voice  When the doer is unknown or unimportant  When focusing on the action or result 4. Reading Comprehension Reading for Specific Structural Patterns Structural patterns show how ideas in a passage are organized. Common Structural Patterns 1. Cause and Effect o Shows why something happens and its result Keywords: because, therefore, as a result 2. Problem and Solution o Presents a problem and how it is solved Keywords: problem, solution, resolve 3. Sequence / Chronological Order o Events arranged in time order Keywords: first, next, finally 4. Comparison and Contrast o Shows similarities and differences Keywords: however, unlike, similarly 5. Description o Gives details about a topic Keywords: for example, such as, characteristics Importance  Helps readers understand texts easily  Improves answering comprehension questions  Enhances summarizing skills

NOUN PHRASES A noun phrase is a group of two or more words that is headed by a noun (a person, place, or thing) that includes modifiers (e.g., ‘ the, ’ ‘ a, ’ ‘ of them, ’ ‘ with her ’). A noun phrase p lays the role of a noun. P ositons of N oun P hrases: Noun phrases can be found indifferent positions in a sentence. They can be the subject of the sentence, the object of the verb, the object of a preposition, or the complement of a verb. Functions of Noun phrases: The function of a noun phrase depends on its position in the sentence.  Noun phrase as subject of a verb e.g. “praising the teacher is the student’s delight”  Noun phrase as object of a verb e.g. “It gives me joy to teach the children”  Noun phrase as complement of a verb e.g. “He is the new chairman.”  Noun phrase as apposition to a noun e.g. “Mr. Ibe, a great teacher, writes and sings”. Noun phrase as object of a preposition e.g. “the senate agreed about the immunity clause”. Tips for Identifying Noun Phrases Noun phrases can be identified by a. Their function in the sentence; if a word or phrase functions as a noun, then it is a noun phrase. b. Their structure; they often contain noun, but they can also contain modifiers (adjectives, adverbs, e.t.c) and other phrases. Class-work  Hermoine Granger, a witch at Hogwarts School, is accomplished.  Jenny gave me a neatly packed gift box. Assignment a. A beautiful girl was crying S. b. She has many good friends O. c. The box is a big expensive present S.C. d. I will call you the red head O.C. e. Peter, Mark’s father is a handsome man. APP.

Positions/functions Subject: The subject of a sentence is the person or thing that the sentence is about. The subject of a sentence is always a noun phrase. E.G. The cat sat on the mat. Object: The object of a verb is the person or thing that the verb acts upon. The object of a verb can be a noun phrase, a pronoun, or a clause. E. G. I saw the cat on the fence. Object of a Preposition: The object of a preposition is the person or thing that the preposition refers to. The object of a preposition can be a noun phrase, a pronoun, or a clause. E.G. The cat is under the mat. Complement: a complement is a word or phrase that follows a verb and completes its meaning. The complement of a verb can be a noun phrase, an adjective, or an adverb. E.G. The cat is a furry creature.

The cat is under the mat. Complement: a complement is a word or phrase that follows a verb and completes its meaning. The complement of a verb can be a noun phrase, an adjective, or an adverb. E.G. The cat is a furry creature.

title: SPEECH:
subject: English Language
rawText:
1. Speech Listening Comprehension: Summarizing Speeches, Lectures, and Note-Making Listening comprehension is the ability to understand spoken information and extract important ideas. Skills Needed for Listening Comprehension  Listen attentively without distraction  Identify the main idea  Pick out supporting details  Notice keywords and repeated ideas  Understand the speaker’s purpose Summarizing Speeches and Lectures A summary is a short version of a speech or lecture that contains only the main points. Steps to Summarize: 1. Listen carefully to the entire speech 2. Identify the topic and main ideas 3. Ignore examples and unnecessary details 4. Write the ideas in your own words 5. Keep it brief and clear Note-Making Note-making involves writing down key points while listening. Effective Note-Making Tips:  Use short phrases, not full sentences  Use headings and subheadings  Use symbols and abbreviations  Number points logically  Write neatly and clearly 2. Structure Figures of Speech

Figures of speech are expressions used to make language more vivid and expressive. Common Figures of Speech  Simile – comparison using like or as Example: She runs like the wind.  Metaphor – direct comparison Example: The classroom was a zoo.  Personification – giving human qualities to non-living things Example: The sun smiled at us.  Hyperbole – exaggeration for emphasis Example: I waited forever.  Alliteration – repetition of initial sounds Example: Peter picked a peck of peppers.  Onomatopoeia – words that imitate sounds Example: bang, buzz, splash  Irony – saying the opposite of what is meant Example: A fire station burns down. 3. Reading Comprehension Reading for Specific Structural Patterns Reading comprehension means understanding written text. Reading for structure patterns means identifying how information is organized. Common Structural Patterns 1. Cause and Effect – Shows reasons and results Keywords: because, as a result, therefore 2. Problem and Solution – Presents a problem and how it is solved Keywords: problem, solution, resolve 3. Sequence/Chronological Order – Events arranged in time order Keywords: first, next, finally 4. Comparison and Contrast – Shows similarities and differences Keywords: however, similarly, unlike 5. Description – Gives detailed information about a subject Keywords: for example, such as

Importance  Helps readers understand texts faster  Makes it easier to answer comprehension questions  Improves study and exam skills 4. Continuous Writing Speech Writing – Features of a Good Speech Speech writing involves preparing a written text meant to be spoken to an audience. Features of a Good Speech 1. Clear Opening o Greeting o Introduction of topic 2. Clear Purpose o To inform, persuade, or entertain 3. Simple and Clear Language o Easy to understand o Short sentences 4. Logical Organization o Introduction o Body o Conclusion 5. Use of Rhetorical Devices o Questions o Repetition o Emotive language 6. Audience Awareness o Use appropriate tone o Address audience directly 7. Strong Conclusion o Summary of main points o Call to action or closing remark Example Opening of a Speech Ladies and gentlemen, today I stand before you to talk about the importance of education in our society.

Three consonant clusters at the medial position.

Endure /Indjuə/ Encumbrance /InkΛmbrəns/ Encrypt /lnkript/ Encroach /inkrəus/ Mixture /mikstꭍə/ Potentate /pəutnteit/ Poultry /pəultri/ Circumflex /s3:kəmfleks/ Electric /ilektrik/ Elementary /elimentri/ Disappointment /disəpϽintmðnt/ Certainly /s3:tnli/ Ancestry /ӕnsestri/ Askew /əskju:/ Back-ground /bӕkgraund/ Capsule /kӕpsju:/ Century /sentꭍəri/ Back-space /bӕkspeis/ Enthuse /intju:z/ Fulcrum /fulkrəm/ C. Prompt /prompt/ Lamps /lӕmps/ Pants /pӕnts/ Nests /nests/ Consonants /kϽnsənənts/ Camps /kӕmps/ Nymph /nimfs/ Text /tekst/ Pumps /pΛmps/ Depths /depѳs/ Sixth /siksѳ/ Adopts /ədopts/ Against /əgenst/ Thanks /ѳӕפks/ Sample /są:mpl/ Twelfth /twelfѳ/ iii . COMPREHENSION; Reading for main gist in a prose passage. The main gist of any prose passage is the essential contents. They are the main ideas or the main substance of what has been written. They do not contain unnecessary details. The main gist therefore is the significance, the summary or the aspect that is gripping and essential for the desired information. Referred to the passage on page 4 of the students English text (revolution without a will). iii. STRUCTURE: Adjectival phrases and functions. An adjectival phrase is a phrase that modifies a noun or a pronoun in a sentence. It performs the function of an adjective, prepositional phrase and participial phrase belong to this category. Prepositional phrase begins with preposition like (in, on, from, with etc) while participial phrase begins with the “-ing” form of a verb.

Examples; 1. The girl with dirty hands ate the food. 2. The money in the bag belongs to me. 3. The car with dark red colour is yours. 4. The coat made of cotton is very lovely. 5. The man working in the office came here. 6. The boy reading is my student. 7. The students forgot to bring back the book that I gave him. 8. I like the seat at the corner. 9. The man standing at the gate is my teacher. 10. The student to be suspended has stopped coming to school. FUNCTIONS 1. prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “girl”. 2. prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “money”. 3. prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “car”. 4. adjectival phrase modifying the noun “coat”. 5. participial phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “man”. 6. participial phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “boy”. 7. Adjectival phrase modifying the noun stu “dent”. 8. Prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “i”. 9. Participial phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “noun”. 10. Prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “student”. iv. CONTINUOUS WRITING: Creative writing – short story Creative writing is the skillful and imaginative literary work produced by someone without help from another. It can be short story, a drama piece, an essay or a poem. It is always created from the writer’s

imagination or factual knowledge of events that happened. It is the ability from the writer to express Himself in writing. It involves originality, skillful and imaginative use of language in writing. A short story is a narration created from the writers imagination or factual knowledge of events that happened, it is in most cases a narration. FEATURES OF A SHORT STORY 1. Theme: this means the main idea, the subject matter or the central point of view from which a story is developed. Example One good turn deserves another. A stitch in time saves another. 2. Plot: this is the sequential arrangement of events in a chronological order in which the events occurred. It is the story-line, the order that the story follows to develop the theme. 3. Setting: this refers to where the event’s happened(place) and when(time). It is the geographical location and the daily manner of living of the characters as well as the period during which the action occurs, it may be urban or rural area. 4. Tone/mood: This is the way or attitude that the author/writer delivers the message to his reader. It is the expression of the emotional attitude of the writer towards his subjects. It may be pleasant, apologetic, anger, sorrowful, humorous etc. 5. Characters: These are the people who participate in the action of the story. They could be human beings or inanimate objects of animals. The story will appear real if you give the characters names and interaction among them through dialogue. E.g “animal farm” by George Orwell. 6. Characterization: this is the manner of exposing the imaginary being created in your writing so that they appear to your readers if they exist. 7. Language/ Diction: this is the writer’s choice of words. It may be simple, straight forward, native language etc. the tense of the narration must be in the past, but when dialogue is brought In the tense can be present. 8. Style: this is simply writers method of expression which distinguishes his work from others. E.g Chinua Achebe combine English and Igbo 9. Figures of speech: these are the literary devices used in expressing ones thought in writing. E.g simile, personification, metaphor, Hyperbole etc

Three consonant clusters at the medial position.

Prompt /prompt/ Lamps /lӕmps/ Pants /pӕnts/ Nests /nests/ Consonants /kϽnsənənts/ Camps /kӕmps/ Nymph /nimfs/ Text /tekst/ Pumps /pΛmps/ Depths /depѳs/ Sixth /siksѳ/ Adopts /ədopts/ Against /əgenst/ Thanks /ѳӕפks/ Sample /są:mpl/ Twelfth /twelfѳ/ iii . COMPREHENSION; Reading for main gist in a prose passage. The main gist of any prose passage is the essential contents. They are the main ideas or the main substance of what has been written. They do not contain unnecessary details. The main gist therefore is the significance, the summary or the aspect that is gripping and essential for the desired information. Referred to the passage on page 4 of the students English text (revolution without a will). iii. STRUCTURE: Adjectival phrases and functions. An adjectival phrase is a phrase that modifies a noun or a pronoun in a sentence. It performs the function of an adjective, prepositional phrase and participial phrase belong to this category. Prepositional phrase begins with preposition like (in, on, from, with etc) while participial phrase begins with the “-ing” form of a verb.

Examples; 1. The girl with dirty hands ate the food. 2. The money in the bag belongs to me. 3. The car with dark red colour is yours. 4. The coat made of cotton is very lovely. 5. The man working in the office came here. 6. The boy reading is my student. 7. The students forgot to bring back the book that I gave him. 8. I like the seat at the corner. 9. The man standing at the gate is my teacher. 10. The student to be suspended has stopped coming to school. FUNCTIONS 1. prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “girl”. 2. prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “money”. 3. prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “car”. 4. adjectival phrase modifying the noun “coat”. 5. participial phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “man”. 6. participial phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “boy”. 7. Adjectival phrase modifying the noun stu “dent”. 8. Prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “i”. 9. Participial phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “noun”. 10. Prepositional phrase as adjectival phrase modifying the noun “student”. iv. CONTINUOUS WRITING: Creative writing – short story Creative writing is the skillful and imaginative literary work produced by someone without help from another. It can be short story, a drama piece, an essay or a poem. It is always created from the writer’s

imagination or factual knowledge of events that happened. It is the ability from the writer to express Himself in writing. It involves originality, skillful and imaginative use of language in writing. A short story is a narration created from the writers imagination or factual knowledge of events that happened, it is in most cases a narration. FEATURES OF A SHORT STORY 1. Theme: this means the main idea, the subject matter or the central point of view from which a story is developed. Example One good turn deserves another. A stitch in time saves another. 2. Plot: this is the sequential arrangement of events in a chronological order in which the events occurred. It is the story-line, the order that the story follows to develop the theme. 3. Setting: this refers to where the event’s happened(place) and when(time). It is the geographical location and the daily manner of living of the characters as well as the period during which the action occurs, it may be urban or rural area. 4. Tone/mood: This is the way or attitude that the author/writer delivers the message to his reader. It is the expression of the emotional attitude of the writer towards his subjects. It may be pleasant, apologetic, anger, sorrowful, humorous etc. 5. Characters: These are the people who participate in the action of the story. They could be human beings or inanimate objects of animals. The story will appear real if you give the characters names and interaction among them through dialogue. E.g “animal farm” by George Orwell. 6. Characterization: this is the manner of exposing the imaginary being created in your writing so that they appear to your readers if they exist. 7. Language/ Diction: this is the writer’s choice of words. It may be simple, straight forward, native language etc. the tense of the narration must be in the past, but when dialogue is brought In the tense can be present. 8. Style: this is simply writers method of expression which distinguishes his work from others. E.g Chinua Achebe combine English and Igbo 9. Figures of speech: these are the literary devices used in expressing ones thought in writing. E.g simile, personification, metaphor, Hyperbole etc

WEEK 5 I. SPEECH: Consonant clusters – two consonant in the initial position. Consonants clusters occurs when two or more consonants sounds appear together without a vowel sound in between them. Examples of consonant clusters at the initial medial and final position initial medial Final Slice /slӘis/sl Play /plei/ pl Bride /braid/ br Class / klą:s/ kl Pray /plei/ pl Boxer /bɒksz/ ks Cluster /klnstz/ kl Tablet /tӕblӘt/ bl Between /bitwiti:n/ tw Fumble /fΛmbl/ mb Structure /strnktsz/ st Fault / fdit/ lt Parts / pӘ:ts/ ʦ Proved /pru:vd/ vd Needs /ni:ds/ ds Rains /reinz/ nz ii. VOCABULARY DEVELOPMENT – MODIFIER: Word modifier (Adjective and adverb) Modifier is a word or group of words that changes, clarifies, qualifies or limits a particular word in a sebtences in ordwe to add emphasis, explanation or detail. Modifiers tend be descriptive words such as adjectives and adverbs Some modifiers affect nouns, while others affect other verbs, adjectives and adverbs. A modifier is an optional element in either a phrase or clause structure. The use of modifiers means using appropriate words to describe persons, places or things. Examples: smooth, skin, blind, a girl, an old man. Etc Forms of modifiers 1. Article as modifiers: eg A man of honour. An eye for an eye. The armed robber. 2. Adjective as a modifier: examples Dirty old man. Young rich fool.

Dark horse. Nigerian men. Note: many adjectives are found within phrases and thus acts as members of that group. They are called pre-modifiers or attributives adjectives. examples 1. My younger brother is in university. 2. The young and dynamic lecturer is around. C. Adverbs as modifiers: adverbs modify verbs, adjectives and other adverbs Examples 1. The sick man slept soundly. 2. The man was killed yesterday. 3. Serious students study regularly. The underlined above represent adverbs modifying verbs 4.Tthe politician is passionately concerned. 5. The killing was absolutely unnecessary. 6. Paul plays football very well. 7. The man is quite ambitious. 8. They moved rather sluggishly towards the scene.. 9. Joy does things extremely slowly. The underlined above represent adverbs modifying other adverbs. D. Adverbial phrase as modifiers: Examples 1- She learnt French some years ago.’ 2- He saw the do in the garden.

E. Adverbial clause as modifiers: examples; 1- Mike sold the old car because it was too small for the family. 2- While I was trying to sleep, sarah came in. 3- As he had no one to help him, the poor man started early to struggle. Note: an adverbial modifier is something the describes almost anything in the world that is not a noun. F. Adjective as a modifier. An adjective is a part of speech that modifies a noun or pronoun. Note: adjectives usually tell what kind, how many, or which about nouns or pronouns. iii. SUMMARY : Reading to summarize longer sentences into a specified number of sentences. title: READING FOR IMPLIED MEANING
subject: English Language
rawText:
Week 3 I. Speech: making a toast - meaning of toast and occasions for a toast. A toast can be a brief speech is congratulations, appreciation and remembrance for a person by a drink. However, the purpose for making a toast is, to thank someone, wishing someone good luck weeks celebrating an achievement. Occasions that require making a toast 1. Birthday party. 2. Wedding party. 3. Celebrating good health. 4. Celebrating an achievement. 5. Success in examination. 6. Celebrating admission into school. 7. Employment. 8. Celebrating survival of accident. Steps required in making a toast 1. To write a toast: it should be short, appealing and personal. The use of humerous language and quotation is required. The target is your toast is to make your friend is the person concerned as well as his guest happy. 2. Making notes: it is not ideal to write the entire speech on a book or read entirely from a note. This will look awkward. Rather, note some key words or phrases that will guide your thoughts and help you to remember what you want to say. Example: the first time you met your friend, how friendly you have been with each other, what you share in common etc. Short expressions like; first meeting, our friendship, our joy etc. The purpose of the note is to stimulate your memory. 3. When it is time, stand up to toast. 4. Raise your glass to the person to whom you are making the toast to. 5. Announce your relationship with the celebrant. 6. Propose your toast. As you do this, look at the person to whom you are toasting. 7. End your toast on a positive note. Example: let us now drink a toast to joy and many more happy years of celebration. When you say this, wave your glass to all. Then tip it towards the person you are

toasting. You may clink his glass if you are close enough with the people around you. Do this gently to avoid breaking a glass. It is rude to do so. 8. Get back to your seat. Note that your toast must be very short e.g. 5 minutes. Toast making is not an avenue for you to show off your skills in comedy. This avoid unnecessary jokes and your wine should be sip not gulp. II. Comprehension: Reading for Implied Meaning Reading for implied meaning means reading to fill in certain gaps in which some explanations are left out. The reader is expected to fill the gaps in order to get the full understanding of the passage. Tips needed while reading for implied meaning includes: 1. Keep asking questions at you read. Questions such as where, why, how will shed more light on the content is the passage. 2. You will note that subtle expression are laden with deeper meaning. 3. Keep linking ideas as you read on, to understand the writer's line is development. This will enable you notice when a gap in information occurs or is created. 4. Your background knowledge of a topic may assist you too decipher a hidden or implied meaning in the passage. 5. If something is amiss, you assume what has happened. This assumption will help you draw conclusion and subsequently help you locate the implied meaning. Page "80" the determined mother. III. STRUCTURE - NOMINALIZATION: Nominalism is the formation of noun from adjectives, verbs or other nouns using syllable. Suffixes are unstressed syllables added to a root-word which then changes the meaning or class of the word to another. Formation of Noun: common suffixes used for nouns : -ity, -ness, -ist, -ancy/ency, -ster, -ment, -age, - ance/ence, -ism, -hood. How best to form nouns using suffixes. Examples: a. Adjective: add -ity to form nouns and add -ant, -ment to adjective exchange for -ancy and ency to also form nouns. Example: Adjective + ity Noun i) Final + ity = finality II) Curious + ity = curiosity

III) Sensitive + ity = sensitivity Iv) Able + ity = ability V) Expectant + ity = expectancy Vi) Redundant + ancy = redundancy Vii) Fluent + ency = fluency Viii) Efficient + ency = efficiency Note: ity when added to adjective that ends with -al, -ble, -cal, -ous, -ive, turns to nouns. b. Verbs: add -ment, -age, -ance, or -ence to some verbs to form nouns. Example: Verb Noun I) Entertain + ment = Entertainment Ii) Retire + ment = Retirement III) Settle + ment = settlement Iv) Advance + ment = advancement V) Move + ment = movement Vi) Carry + age = carriage Vii) Spoil + age = spoilage Viii) Use + age = usage Ix) Def + ence = defence X) Repent + ance = repentance Xi) Adhere + ence = adherence Xii) Prefer + ence = preference c. Nouns can also be form from other nouns. Example: nouns can be formed by adding -ship, hood, -ish etc. Noun Noun II) Friend + ship = friendship II) Court + ship = courtship

III) Adult + hood = adulthood Iv) Brother + hood = brotherhood V) Boy + ish = boyish Vi) Girl + ish = girlish Vii) Child + ish = childish IV. CONTINUOUS WRITING - Writing speeches for specific purposes (Introduction, Purpose, Feature) A speech is a written material meant to be read to a group of listeners. Speeches are meant to entertain, educate and inform people. It is also to motivate people to action. Features of a Speech 1. The title: there must be a title for the speech you are meant to deliver. The title should indicate the mark of identification. Such as: The purpose. Name and title of speaker. Occasion. Place. Date and time. For example: 1. A farewell speech presentation by Gideon John, the head boy of Government secondary school, Kubwa on the welcoming party of our new principal, Mr Okechukwu Kunle Musa, at the assembly hall this day 20th January, 2024 at. 10:00am. 2. The introduction: this must be interesting and captivating so as to elicit the interest of the listeners. It must start with salutation. Example: Good morning the chairman, the principal, the school management, the PTA... Ladies and gentlemen. I feel highly honored to stand here today to deliver my speech on... You write your topic and say your topic. 3. The body of the speech: this is the stage that contains the actual message. Start by giving your main points and the support each points with relevant details, comparisons and contrast etc. explaining who, when, where, why and how. The ideas must be stated in good and clear sentences. 4. The conclusion: Here you summarize your points. It is important to end in a memorable way by: 1) making a forceful and shocking statement. 2) urging your audience to follow a certain line of action or thought etc. 3) Ending in an interesting and captivating manner

title: GIVING CLEAR, CONCISE AND CORRECT DIRECTIONS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Topic: Oral English Sub Topic : Giving Clear, Concise, and Correct Directions Class : JSS2 Subject : English Language 1. Meaning of Giving Directions Giving directions means telling someone how to get from one place to another using clear and correct words. Good directions help the person reach their destination without getting lost. 2. Features of Good Directions For directions to be useful, they must be: a. Clear* – Use simple words that the listener understands. Avoid confusing terms. b. Concise* – Be brief. Do not give too much unnecessary detail. c. Correct* – Give accurate information about roads, landmarks, and distances. d. Logical* – Give instructions in the order the person will follow them. 3. Useful Language for Giving Directions a. Starting a Direction - Excuse me, how do I get to…? - Can you tell me the way to…? - Where is the… located? b. Giving Instructions - Go straight ahead. - Turn left / Turn right. - Take the first/second road on the left/right. - Go past the school/church/market. - Cross the bridge/road. - It is next to / opposite / behind / in front of… c. Showing Distance and Time - It is about 5 minutes’ walk from here. - It is 2 kilometers away. - It is just around the corner.

d. Ending Directions - You can’t miss it. - It will be on your right/left. - That’s it. - Have a safe journey. 4. Things to Avoid When Giving Directions 1. Using vague words like _over there, somewhere near_. 2. Giving too many details at once. 3. Using difficult or local words the listener may not know. 4. Speaking too fast or unclearly. 5. Example of Clear Directions Question: Excuse me, how do I get to the school from here? Answer: Go straight ahead for about 200 meters. Turn right at the filling station. Walk past the market and cross the main road. The school is opposite the post office. It will take you about 10 minutes on foot. You can’t miss it. 6. Tips for Speaking Directions Clearly 1. Speak slowly and clearly. 2. Use your hand to show direction if possible. 3. Pause between each instruction so the listener can follow. 4. Check if the person understands by asking, _Do you understand? Good directions are like a map in words. If you speak clearly and step by step, anyone can follow you.

title: STRUCTURE:NOUN CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText:
*Noun Clause* — a clause that does the work of a noun in a sentence. _“Faith cometh by hearing”_ — *Romans 10:17*. Here, _“that Jesus is Lord”_ in _“I believe that Jesus is Lord”_ is a noun clause. It can’t stand alone, but it works like a noun. *1. What is a Noun Clause?* A *dependent clause* that functions as a noun. It has a subject + verb, but it cannot stand alone. *Signal words*: _that, what, whatever, who, whoever, whom, whose, when, where, why, how, whether, if_ *Examples*: 1. _What he said_ shocked everyone. 2. I know _that God answers prayer_. 3. _Whoever trusts in the Lord_ shall not be ashamed. *Romans 10:11* *2. Features of Noun Clauses* Feature Explanation Example **1. Has subject + verb** Like a sentence, but dependent *She believes* → in *She believes that God is good* **2. Starts with a connector***that, what, who, whether, if, how* *Whether he comes* is not sure **3. Cannot stand alone** Incomplete meaning by itself *“That he passed”* — what about it? **4. Can be replaced by ‘it’ or ‘something’** Test for noun clause *What you did* was kind → *It* was kind **5. No question mark** Even if it has *who/what*, it’s not a questionI know *what he wants*. Not: I know what he wants? *3. Functions of Noun Clauses* A noun clause can do anything a noun can do in a sentence.

Function Position Example Test with ‘it’ **1. Subject of verb** Starts the sentence *What the Lord has done* is marvelous. **Psalm 118:23** *It* is marvelous **2. Object of verb** After main verb I believe *that God is faithful*. I believe *it* **3. Subject complement** After linking verb: is, was, seems The truth is *that Jesus saves*. The truth is *it* **4. Object of preposition** After prep: to, for, about, in Give the prize to *whoever wins*. Give it to *him* **5. Appositive** Renames a noun The fact *that He rose again* gives us hope. **1 Cor 15:17** The fact, *it*, gives us hope **6. Object of infinitive/participle** After to + verb or -ing He loves to say *what is true*. He loves to say *it* *4. Quick Test: Noun Clause vs Other Clauses* 1. *Noun clause* → Replace with ‘it/something’ and sentence still makes sense. _I know where he lives_ → I know _it_. Noun clause ✅ 2. *Adjective clause* → Describes a noun. Answers “which one?” _The book that I read_ was good. → Describes “book”. Not noun clause ❌ 3. *Adverb clause* → Tells when/why/how. _I’ll pray when you call_ → Tells “when”. Not noun clause ❌ *Class Work: Identify the Function* Underline the noun clause and state its function. 1. _Why he left_ is a mystery. →

2. She told me _that she would come_. → 3. My hope is _that God will help me_. → 4. Listen to _what your teacher says_. → 5. The question _whether we should go_ remains. → _Answers: 1.Subject 2.Object of verb 3.Subject complement 4.Object of preposition 5.Appositive_ *Memory Trick*: *SOSA* — Noun clauses work as *S*ubject, *O*bject, *S*ubject complement, *A*ppositive. Want more practice sentences or a test on noun clauses vs adjective/adverb clauses?
