title: UNSTRESSED SYLLABLES
subject: English Language
rawText: UNSTRESSED SYLLABLES Meaning A syllable is a single, unbroken sound of a spoken (or written) word. It is a unit of pronunciation that usually contains one vowel sound. Examples: - ta-ble (2 syllables) - beau-ti-ful (3 syllables) - in-ter-est-ing (4 syllables) In English pronunciation, not all syllables in a word are given equal importance or emphasis. Some syllables are stressed, while others are unstressed. Definition of Unstressed Syllable An unstressed syllable is a syllable that is pronounced more softly and less forcefully than the stressed one. It receives less emphasis in speech. In other words, it is the weaker syllable in a word or sentence. Example: - In ta-ble, the first syllable TA is stressed, while ble is unstressed. - In beau-ti-ful, the first syllable BEAU is stressed, while ti and ful are unstressed. Characteristics of Unstressed Syllables 1. Reduced Loudness: They are pronounced with less volume than stressed syllables. 2. Shorter Duration: They are usually shorter in length (spoken quickly). 3. Weaker Pitch: The pitch or tone of voice is lower. 4. Reduced Vowel Sound: The vowel sound in unstressed syllables is often pronounced as the / n / sound (called schwa). Example: about → / nn ba n t/, the first syllable 'a' is unstressed and pronounced / n /. Examples of Words with Unstressed Syllables Word | Stressed Syllable | Unstressed Syllable(s) ta-ble | TA | ble com-put-er | PU | com, ter a-bout | BOUT | a to-day | DAY | to de-sert (noun) | DE | sert be-come | COME | be a-lone | LONE | a en-joy | JOY | en a-round | ROUND | a pre-sent (verb) | SENT | pre Unstressed Syllables in Sentences In connected speech (normal spoken English), many small words and syllables are unstressed. Examples: - I am going to the market. → “I’m gonna the market.” (am, to, and the become weak or unstressed) - He is a teacher. → “He’s a teacher.” (a is unstressed) The Schwa Sound (/ n /) The schwa is the most common vowel sound in unstressed syllables. It is pronounced softly like “uh.” Examples: - about → / nn ba n t/ - banana → /b nn n nn n n / - problem → / n pr n bl n m/ - teacher → / n ti n t nn / Importance of Recognizing Unstressed Syllables 1. Improves Pronunciation: Helps students speak more naturally like native English speakers. 2. Improves Listening Skills: Makes it easier to understand spoken English. 3. Enhances Reading Aloud: Helps in proper rhythm and stress pattern. 4. Aids Spelling and Word Stress Learning: Helps in dividing words correctly and placing stress properly. Tips to Identify Unstressed Syllables - Say the word slowly and listen for the part that is said softer or quicker. - Check dictionary pronunciation; unstressed syllables often contain / n / or short vowels like / n /. - Remember: function words (articles, prepositions, pronouns, etc.) are often unstressed in speech. Examples in Pairs Word | Pronunciation | Unstressed Syllable about | / nn ba n t/ | a banana | /b nn n nn n n / | ba, na photograph | / n f nn t nn r nn f/ | to, graph together | /t nnnn ð n / | to, er forget | /f nnn et/ | for Summary - Every word has at least one syllable. - Some syllables are stressed; others are unstressed. - Unstressed syllables are softer, shorter, and usually have the schwa sound / n /. - Recognizing them helps improve pronunciation, reading, and listening skills.

title: NARRATIVE ESSAY
subject: English Language
rawText: Comprehensive Note on Narrative Essay Writing Meaning of a Narrative Essay A narrative essay is a type of essay that tells a story. It gives an account of real or imagined events in a logical order. The main purpose of a narrative essay is to entertain, inform, or teach a moral lesson through storytelling. Features of a Narrative Essay 1. Plot (Storyline): A sequence of related events arranged logically (beginning, middle, and end). 2. Characters: The people or beings that take part in the story. 3. Setting: The time and place where the story occurs. 4. Conflict: The problem or challenge faced by the characters. 5. Climax: The most exciting or emotional part of the story. 6. Resolution: How the story ends or how the conflict is solved. 7. Theme: The main idea or lesson behind the story. 8. Point of View: The perspective from which the story is told. 9. Chronological Order: Events are presented in the order they happened. 10. Descriptive Language: Vivid and imaginative words that create pictures in the reader’s mind. Structure of a Narrative Essay 1. Introduction (Beginning): Introduces the story, main characters, and setting. 2. Body (Middle): Describes the main events in detail and in logical sequence. 3. Conclusion (End): Tells how the story ends or how the problem is solved. Language Features - Mostly written in past tense. - Uses time connectives (first, then, later, finally). - Uses adjectives, adverbs, and figurative expressions. - Dialogue may be included. Steps in Writing a Good Narrative Essay 1. Choose a suitable topic. 2. Plan your story – outline events in order. 3. Identify the characters. 4. Decide the setting. 5. Write the first draft. 6. Revise and edit. 7. Write the final copy neatly. Examples of Common Topics - A day I will never forget - The happiest day of my life - How I escaped an accident - My first time away from home - The day I lost my phone - An unforgettable experience Qualities of a Good Narrative Essay 1. Clear and interesting story with logical flow. 2. Well-developed characters and setting. 3. Strong emotional appeal. 4. Vivid descriptions. 5. Unity and coherence. 6. Lesson or moral at the end. Example (Short Narrative Paragraph) It was raining heavily when I left home that morning. The road was slippery, and the sky was dark. Suddenly, I heard a loud crash behind me. A car had lost control and hit a tree. I ran quickly to help the driver, my heart beating fast. Fortunately, he was not badly hurt. That day taught me how precious every moment of life can be. Summary - A narrative essay tells a story based on real or imaginary events. - It has a clear structure: beginning, middle, and end. - It includes characters, setting, plot, conflict, and resolution. - It should be descriptive, emotional, and written in chronological order. - The best narrative essays are both interesting and meaningful.

title: SUMM
subject: English Language
rawText:
NOTE ON SUMMARY WRITING Meaning of Summary Writing Summary writing is the process of condensing a long passage or text into a shorter form, while retaining only the main ideas and essential information. It involves expressing the key points clearly, briefly, and in your own words. A summary gives a reader the main message of the passage without unnecessary details, examples, or repetitions. Purpose of Summary Writing 1. To test one’s understanding of a passage. 2. To develop the ability to identify main ideas. 3. To test one’s ability to express ideas briefly and clearly. 4. To help improve writing and comprehension skills. Steps in Summary Writing 1. Read the passage carefully. 2. Identify the main ideas. 3. Underline or note down key points. 4. Write the points in your own words. 5. Ensure logical arrangement. 6. Check your work. Features of a Good Summary • It is brief and concise. • It is written in the writer’s own words. • It captures only the main ideas. • It is grammatically correct. • It is connected and coherent. • It avoids repetition and examples. Things to Avoid in Summary Writing • Copying sentences directly from the passage. • Including personal opinions or examples. • Writing long, complex sentences. • Exceeding the required word limit. • Omitting important points. Useful Tips • Use linking words like also, therefore, however, finally, etc. • Replace long phrases with short expressions.

• Write in the third person and past tense (if the passage is a narrative). • Count your words if there is a word limit. Example Original passage: Education is the key to national development. It provides individuals with knowledge and skills needed to improve their lives. A nation that neglects education will suffer from poverty and underdevelopment. Summary: Education promotes national growth by providing useful knowledge and skills.

Language Features - Mostly written in past tense. - Uses time connectives (first, then, later, finally). - Uses adjectives, adverbs, and figurative expressions. - Dialogue may be included. Steps in Writing a Good Narrative Essay 1. Choose a suitable topic. 2. Plan your story – outline events in order. 3. Identify the characters. 4. Decide the setting. 5. Write the first draft. 6. Revise and edit. 7. Write the final copy neatly. Examples of Common Topics - A day I will never forget - The happiest day of my life - How I escaped an accident - My first time away from home - The day I lost my phone - An unforgettable experience Qualities of a Good Narrative Essay 1. Clear and interesting story with logical flow. 2. Well-developed characters and setting. 3. Strong emotional appeal. 4. Vivid descriptions. 5. Unity and coherence. 6. Lesson or moral at the end. Example (Short Narrative Paragraph) It was raining heavily when I left home that morning. The road was slippery, and the sky was dark. Suddenly, I heard a loud crash behind me. A car had lost control and hit a tree. I ran quickly to help the driver, my heart beating fast. Fortunately, he was not badly hurt. That day taught me how precious every moment of life can be. title: NOUNS
subject: English Language
rawText:
Nouns a. What is a noun? b. What is a phrase? c. explain a noun phrase? Nouns: Nouns are the basic things we see around us such as the chairs we sit on, the food we eat, the books we write on et cetera. They are also some things we cannot see but feel such as love, air et cetera. They are words to identify and as such can be said to be words used to name a person, animal, place, thing and abstract idea. It is a part of speech that typically denotes a place, person, thing et cetera. Phrase: Phrase is a group of words which makes sense but not complete sense (for the given definitions, the teacher gives illustrative examples). The teacher goes further to give the definition of a noun phrase. Noun Phrase: A Noun Phrase is a group of words that functions in a sentence as subject and, or object. It is a phrase which has noun as its head word. It is also a word group with a noun or pronoun as its head and can also be called Nominal Phrase. A noun phrase is also defined as group of words that functions like a noun in a sentence. A noun phrase consists of a noun and its modifiers (adjectives, determiners, etc) Examples: The tall boy, A beautiful garden, A rotten Orange, The English Language teacher. The types of nouns include: a. Proper Noun, b. Common Noun, c. Abstract Noun, d. Collective Noun and e. Concrete Noun. Noun types and examples: Proper Noun: This identifies a particular person, place, thing or idea. Proper nouns are always capitalized. If a proper noun contains two or more words, each important word in the noun is capitalized. Examples: Abuja, Nigeria, River Benue, Dr James, Nigerian Museum of Natural History. Common Noun: This refers to any person, place, thing or idea. Common nouns are usually not capitalized. Examples include – city, ocean, people, individual, building etc. Abstract Noun: This is that noun which names an idea, a quality or a feeling. Examples include – belief, beauty, disappointment, love, hatred etc.

Collective Noun: This refers to a group of persons, animals or things. Examples – class, audience, committee, group, band, club, family, team, pride, flock, bunch etc. Examples in sentences: A crowd of students flocked into the auditorium. A swarm of reporters from the local newspapers gathered around the candidates. Concrete Nouns: These name something that can be seen, smelled, heard, tasted or touched. Examples are: vegetables, a village, table, sand etc. the plural formation of nouns as categorized into two (2): i. Regular plural formation: This is the plural formation where an ‘s’ or ‘es’ is added to singular nouns. Examples are: A. Nouns pluralized by adding an ‘s’ Singular Nouns Plural Nouns Book Books House Houses Table tables Cat Cats Apple Apples B. Nouns that end with the sounds ‘s’, ‘z’, ‘sh’, ‘ch’ and ‘j’ are pluralized by adding “es’ Singular Nouns Plural Nouns Box Boxes Match Matches Class Classes Sash Sashes Fox Foxes C. Nouns ending in z also double their ending consonant e.g – Quiz Quizzes D. Nouns ending in o also carry the surfix “es” to pluralize them. E.g Mango Mangoes Potato Potatoes Hero Heroes Mosquito Mosquitoes E. But words with foreign origin (Latin, Greek, Spanish) we just add an ‘s’ e.g Avocado Avocados Taco Tacos Maestro Maestros F. For nouns ending with y, we change the y to i then add es to pluralize them. Sky Skies Candy Candies Lady Ladies G. For nouns that end with y but preceded by o or a vowel we just add ‘s’

Toy Toy Day Days Donkey Donkeys H. For nouns that end with –f or –fe we change f to v and add “es” Leaf Leaves Life Lives Calf Calves If there are two terminal fs or if you still pluralize the f while pronouncing the noun then you just add “s” Cliff Cliffs Reef Reefs Chief Chiefs ii. Irregular Plural Formation: Unlike regular plurals, irregular plural formations don’t necessarily follow any particular pattern—instead; they follow a lot of different patterns. Because of this, irregular plurals require a lot of memorization; you need to remember which nouns belong to which type of pluralization. Examples are: A. No Change (Base Plurals) The first kind of irregular plural is the no-change or base plural . In these words, the singular noun has the exact same form as the plural. Most no-change plurals are types of animals: e.g i. sheep ii. fish iii. deer iv. moose B. Mid-Word Vowel Change In a few words, the mid-word vowels are changed to form the plural. These plurals are called the Mutant plurals. To pluralize the noun the vowels in the middle of the noun changes to other sounds. In English there are only seven (7) nouns or words that pluralized thus. They are: Singular noun Plural Noun Foot Feet Woman Women Man Men Tooth Teeth Goose Geese Mouse Mice Louse Lice C. Words or nouns pluralized by adding –en instead of ‘-s’ or ‘-es’ . E.g Singular Noun Plural Noun Child Children Ox Oxen Brother Brethren Sister Sistren

(Brethren and sistren are antiquated terms but included here because these are the four nouns that the rule applies to in English language) D. Borrowed words or nouns : These are the last of the irregular plural forms. These nouns are native to other languages (Latin, Greek) and have retained their plural forms from their original language. These nouns are pluralized by adding -i, -en, -a, -es, -ae. Examples are: 1. Singular Noun ending with -us Plural Noun ended with –i Cactus Cacti Fungus fungi Syllabus Syllabi (Cactuses and funguses are accepted informally. Octopuses is preferred to octopi, but octopi is an accepted noun formally) 2. Singular Noun ending with –a Plural Noun ended with –ae Formula Formulae Vertebra Vertebrae Larva Larvae 3. Singular noun ending with –ix,-ex Plural Noun ended with –ices, -es Appendix Appendices (Appendixes) Index indices 4. Singular Noun ending with –on, -um Plural Noun ended with –a Criterion Criteria Bacterium Bacteria Medium Media 5. Singular Noun ending with –is Plural Noun ended with –es Analysis Analyses Crisis Crises Thesis Theses E.g a. Ghana has just one crisis which is currency without value, while Nigeria has more crises. b. The print medium is more factual than the visual media. c. This year’s syllabus is different from the _______ of the past years. d. There is but just a criterion for eligibility to contest for prefectship in my school whereas other schools have a lot of____________ for the same exercise. a noun phrase can be identified in an expression by the question it answers. A noun phrase answers the question ‘what’? or ‘who’? This means that if a given expression is a phrase and answers to a question formed with the interrogative word ‘what’? or ‘who’? it is certainly a noun phrase. Example: He told us a story. Here the question would be .. i. What did he tell us? Or ii. He told us what? The answer to any of these questions obviously is .. ’a story’ . Since ‘a story’ is the answer to the any of the questions, the grammatical name given to it is a noun phrase . More examples of noun phrases in sentences The fat boy has come.

a) The girl in the class is sleeping. b) The principal bought a new car. Noun Phrases can be generic. Generic Nun Phrase is used to describe the entire classes of things. In other words, it is used when one wants to refer to things (living or non-living) in general. There are different ways of writing generic noun phrases. The commonest ways are: I. Removal or omission of articles and addition of plural markers /s/. If the noun is countable. e.g Vitamins are important to our health. II. A noun can be made generic if it is uncountable by the removal or mission of any article. e.g Water is essential. We need paper to write. functions of a noun phrase. Examples: I. Noun phrase performs the function as the subject of a sentence : A noun phrase is the subject of a sentence if it precedes the verb in a sentence. In this way, the noun phrase begins the sentence. E.g, a) The short slim boy has come again. b) Merely seeing him provoked the woman. II. Noun phrase as the object of a verb : A noun phrase is the object of a verb if it appears after the verb in the sentence. E.g, a) The policeman slapped the short slim boy. b) The rude girl begged all of us. III. Noun phrase as the complement of a subject : Whenever a noun phrase refers to or describes the subject of a sentence, it is said to function as the subject complement. E.g, a) Our principal is a hard-working woman. b) We were all once little children. IV. Noun phrase as the complement of an object : When a noun phrase is placed immediately after the object of a sentence, it serves as the complement of that object. However, the phrase is the same person or thing as the object. Examples: a) We made Musa our leader. b) The company appointed him as her representative in London. V. Noun phrase as the object/complement of a proposition : When a noun phrase is the object or complement of a preposition in a sentence, it is directly placed after the preposition. Example: a) The man died after a prolonged illness. b) The accused was arraigned before a Grade C Customary court.

title: ROAD TRAVEL
subject: English Language
rawText:
Road Travel Road travel means moving from one place to another using roads. It usually involves vehicles such as cars, buses, motorcycles, bicycles, or trucks. In simple terms: Road travel is the act of journeying on land by road instead of by air (plane) or water (ship). Example: Traveling from Lagos to Ibadan by car is an example of road travel. main features of road travel: 1. Use of Vehicles – Road travel is done using cars, buses, motorcycles, trucks, or bicycles. 🚗 2. Movement on Roads – It takes place on roads, highways, or streets that connect different 🛣 places. 3. ⏱ Flexible Time – Travellers can start their journey at any time they choose, unlike air or rail travel with fixed schedules. 4. Short and Medium Distance – It is mostly used for short or medium journeys within towns 🏞 or between nearby cities. 5. Low Cost – Road travel is usually cheaper than air or rail transport. 💰

6. Door-to-Door Service – Vehicles can pick up and drop off passengers or goods directly at 📦 their homes or destinations. 7. Comfort and Convenience – Passengers can stop along the way, rest, or enjoy the scenery. 🧳 8. Dependent on Road Condition – Smooth travel depends on the quality of the road and 🛠 weather conditions.

title: CONSONANTS
subject: English Language
rawText:
More on Consonant Sounds Consonants sounds are sounds produced under one obstruction or the other. In producing consonant sounds, the flow of air from the lungs is interrupted somewhere in the vocal cavity (mouth). It is therefore a sound that is produced with the obstruction of the air stream (passage). The Obstruction may be total or partial depending on the consonant sound being articulated. There are twenty four (24) Consonant Sounds in English language and they are: S/No Sounds Word Examples 1 /p/, Pan, happy, nap 2 /b/, Bud, rubber, rub 3 /t/, Tea, heater, seat 4 /d/, Deep, ridder, hide 5 /k/, Come, marking, pack 6 /g/, Get, target, rag 7 /f/, Fan, tougher, cough 8 /v/, Vim, cover, leave 9 /ð/, This, mother, breathe 10 /Ө/, Thank, anthem, both 11 /s/, Suck, facing, place 12 /z/, Zip, amazon, has 13 /ʃ/, Sheep, lashes, fish 14 /ӡ/, Genre, vision, garage 15 /h/, Hate, behead, 16 /ʧ/, Cheat, teacher, rich 17 /ʤ/, Joy, rejoice, page 18 /l/, Look, follow, sell 19 /r/, Rate, mirrow 20 /w/, Work, rewind 21 /j/, Yes, new 22 /m/, Me, remember, ram 23 /n/, Never, runner, rain 24 /ŋ/ . , singer, rang English sounds are classified. This classification is done based on three (3) factors which are: a) Manner of articulation:

Manner of articulation refers to the configuration and interaction of the articulators. The articulators are the speech organs such as the tongue , lips and palate when making a speech sound. So, by manner of articulation we are saying the way and manner the tongue, the lips and the palate are employed to produce the sound. b) State of the Glottis: The state of glottis is the amount of vibration in the vocal folds and closure in the glottis. This simply is voicing. c) Place of articulation: The place of articulation of a consonant is the point of contact where an obstruction/constriction occurs in the vocal tract in the course of sound production. That is the point at which the sound is produced. These points are seven in number namely: Bilabial, Labio-dental, Dental, Alveolar, Palato- alveolar, Velar and Glottal. Consonant sounds can be voiced or voiceless and this can be known through the state of the glottis in the process of producing the sound. Examples… Manner of Articulation State of Glottis Place of Articulation Number of Sounds in the Group. Voiceless Voiced STOP/PLOSIVES p t k b d g Bilabial Alveolar Velar 6 FRICATIVES f Ө s ʃ h v ð z ӡ Labio-dental Dental Alveolar Palato-alveolar Glottal 9 AFFRICATES ʧ ʤ Palato-alveolar 2 NASALS m n ŋ Bilabial Alveolar Velar 3 LATERALS l Alveolar 1 LIQUIDS OR ROLLS r Alveolar 1 SEMI-VOWELS j w Palatal Bilabial 2

every sound has already explained experience one form of obstruction or the other in the course of producing it as long as it is a consonant. However, this is called manner of articulation. Some of the obstructions can be total while some can be partial. Thus, in discussing Manner of Articulation, one thing comes to mind, ‘is the obstruction total or partial?’ there are seven (7) classification of the nature of obstructions, three (3) are total while four (4) are partial. These are PLOSSIVES, NASSALS AND AFFRICATES as total and FRICATIVES, LATERALS, LIQUIDS AND SEMI-VOWELS as partials.

title: ROAD TRAVEL
subject: English Language
rawText:
Road Travel Road travel means moving from one place to another using roads. It usually involves vehicles such as cars, buses, motorcycles, bicycles, or trucks. In simple terms: Road travel is the act of journeying on land by road instead of by air (plane) or water (ship). Example: Traveling from Lagos to Ibadan by car is an example of road travel. main features of road travel: 1. Use of Vehicles – Road travel is done using cars, buses, motorcycles, trucks, or bicycles. 🚗 2. Movement on Roads – It takes place on roads, highways, or streets that connect different 🛣 places. 3. ⏱ Flexible Time – Travellers can start their journey at any time they choose, unlike air or rail travel with fixed schedules. 4. Short and Medium Distance – It is mostly used for short or medium journeys within towns 🏞 or between nearby cities. 5. Low Cost – Road travel is usually cheaper than air or rail transport. 💰

6. Door-to-Door Service – Vehicles can pick up and drop off passengers or goods directly at 📦 their homes or destinations. 7. Comfort and Convenience – Passengers can stop along the way, rest, or enjoy the scenery. 🧳 8. Dependent on Road Condition – Smooth travel depends on the quality of the road and 🛠 weather conditions.

title: VOWEL SOUND
subject: English Language
rawText:
Vowel sounds are sounds made without blocking the air in your mouth. When you say them, your mouth is open and the sound flows freely. English vowel letters There are 5 vowel letters: A, E, I, O, U But vowel sounds are more than 5 because each vowel can sound different. 👉 Types of vowel sounds 1 ⃣ Short vowel sounds They are quick and soft. /æ/ → cat, man /e/ → bed, pen /ɪ/ → sit, pin /ɒ/ → hot, pot /ʌ/ → cup, sun 2 ⃣ Long vowel sounds They sound like the name of the letter. /eɪ/ → cake, name (A) /iː/ → see, tree (E) /aɪ/ → time, fine (I) /əʊ/ → go, home (O) /juː/ → use, music (U) 3 ⃣ Diphthongs (double vowel sounds) These glide from one sound to another. /aɪ/ → boy, coin /aʊ/ → cow, house /ɔɪ/ → boy, toy

Simple tip ✅ If the sound is short and sharp → short vowel If the sound is long and clear → long vowel

The purpose of comprehension is to test the students through the knowledge of any passage and his ability to answer questions very well. (A) BASIC GUIDELINES.. 1. Read the passage quickly to grasp the general idea. 2. Quickly look at the questions. 3. Read the passage again to understand the details. 4. While answering the questions, limit you answers only to the information provided. Do not include materials not found in the passage. 5. Letter and number your answer correctly. Eg. A,b,ci, cii, d, 1, 2, 3, etc. (B) Word substituted (synonym). The word substitute must express the meaning or nearly the same meaning of the word/phrase as used in the passage. This means that the word subtitue must mean and can perfectly replace the word as it is used in the passage.

Example: Singular – singular substitute Plural - Plural “ Past tense - past tense “ Present tense - present tense “ Verb - verb “ Noun - noun “ etc. (C) TEST ON GRAMMATICAL NAMES AND FUNCTIONS. The grammatical name and function of a phrase or a clause is always demanded. A good knowledge of this will help you to answer this section of the passage properly. We have six grammatical names and eleven grammatical functions. Example: GRAMMATICAL NAME GRAMMATICAL FUNCTIONS 1. Noun phrase 2.Noun clause 1.Subject of the verb, (2) Object of the verb. (3) subject complement. (4) Object complement. (5(. Object to a proposition. (6) in opposition. 3.. Aderbial phrase 4. Adverbial clause 7. Modifies a verb, (8). Modifies an adjectives. (9). To study at Night engages the reader 4. I love sleeping in the room 5. Called the former captain a typist. TOPIC: POINTS TO NOTE IN WRITING A SUMMARY WRITING. (LESSON 4) Summary is a shorter account of the point, reasons, causes, factors, etc, put forward by the writer, giving only the main points. It is the extraction of relevant materials or ideas from a large piece of writing or speech. A summary is the main gist, the exact points, reduction of a long story/passage/. In answering summary questions, you are expected to be precise and

direct to the point. You must leave out any material that would not add positively to the answer, TECHNIQUES AND PROCEDURES FOR SUMMARY WRITING. 1. Quickly read the question(s) 2. Quickly read the passage 3. Slowly and carefully read passage with demands of questions in mind. Study the question(s) thoroughly to be sure of the answers the examiner expects. 4. Write out answers to questions. Make a rough draft of the answers in complete sentence. Do(S) OF SUMMARY WRITING. 1. Use your own words as much as possible and only make use of the words or phrases from the passage if necessary. 2. The use of synonyms and paraphrasing is allowed. Apt lifting of few key words or phrases is allowed. HOW TO PARAPHRASE. 1. .Read the original text until you grasp its meaning. 2. Write down the main point or concepts. Do not copy original word. 3. Change the original words and create your own sentence structure 4. Try to modify the structure of the passage 5. Check your answers against the original to ensure you have not accidently plagiarized. 6. Answers should be numbered for clarity. Eg. I, ii, iii, or 1, 2, 3, do not mix up your answers. DON’T /S OF SUMMARY WRITING. In summary writing; do not . 1. Copy verbatim. Avoid mindless lifting repetition, examples, illustrations and comparison. 2. Be tempted to give your opinions, embellishment and additional meaning. 3. Start your answer with because’ 4. Jump up ideas’ sentences should be linked in one sentence using conjunctions such ‘and’, or, but, in order” etc. 5. Verbosity, brevity should be the watch word. Ensure that your final draft does not contain more words than necessary. 6. Ambiguous sentences/answers 7. Your answers should not be in phrases and clauses except if asked to do so. ASSIGNMENT. Read the passage on page 28 of your text book, and answer the summary questions. TOPIC; NOUN PHRASES AND THEIR FUNCTIONS. (LESSON 5). A noun phrase is a group of words without a finite verb and has a noun as its headward. FUNCTIONS OF NOUN PHRASE A noun phrase can function

a. Subject of a verb b. Object of a verb c. Subject of complement d. Object complement e. Object of a preposition f. In opposition to a noun. (A). SUBJECT OF A VERB: A noun phrase functions as subject of a verb if it starts a sentence and comes before a (the) verb in that sentence. Example: (i) Some broken plates are on the shelf. (subject of the verb “are”) (ii) The big brown bag on the table is heavy. (subject of the verb “is”). (B) OBJECT OF VERB: A noun phrase functions as object of the verb when it come after the verb in a sentence. Example: (i) I know that man standing at the gate. (it functions as object of the “verb” “know”) (ii) He received the insult of his life. (it functions as object of the verb “received” ©. SUBJECT COMPLEMENT: It functions as subject complement when it refers to the same person or thing as subject in the sentence. (i) Music is a healer of the soul. (it complement the subject “music”) (ii) The issue seems to be quite an interesting one. (it complements the subject “issue”.) (D) OBJECT COMPLEMENT: A noun phrase function as object complement when it refers to the same person of thing as the object in the sentence. Example: (i) we call him the leader of the gang. (it complements the object “him”) (ii) She made her husband a lovely humanitarian. (it complements the object “husband”) (E) OBJECT TO A PREPOSITION: A noun phrase functions preposition in the sentence. Examples: (i) Her success depends on her ability to study her books. (it functions as object to a preposition “on”) (ii) The prize will go to the most talented student. (It functions as object to the preposition “to”). (F) IN APPOSITION TO A NOUN: This happens when the noun phrase is an explanatory equivalent to a noun in the sentence. In other words, the noun phrase is placed side by side a noun which it refers to at the same time in the sentence. (G) Examples: (i) Nigeria, the giant of Africa is in west African. (it functions in apposition to the “Nigeria”). (ii) John, my one and only friend is here. (it functions in apposition to the noun “John”) ASSIGNMENT: Underline the noun phrase in the following sentences and state their functions. 1. This book is written for whoever wants it. 2. We believe that we shall win the match.

3. To study at night engages the reader. 4. I love sleeping in the room. 5. I called the former captain a typist. (LESSON 6). A. An expository essay is an explanatory essay where the writer aims to inform, instruct, explain, criticize or analyze some concepts or situation to the reader. It allows the writer to show his capability for logical thought and reasoning. It is a factual essay and most times makes judgment. B. LIKELY TOPICS UNDER EXPOSITORY ESSAY. 1. How my favourite food is prepared 2. Dangers of drug above 3. The dangers of premarital sex 4. The future of the Nigerian youth 5. Causes of indiscipline in Nigeria secondary school. 6. The consequences of dressing indecently 7. Why prostitution is a crime 8. Managing population explosion in Nigeria 9. My English teacher how I saw her/him 10. Controlling HIV/AIDS in Nigeria. C. GUIDELINE FOR WRITING AN EXPOSITORY ESSAY. 1. Think of the most logical way of presenting in order to avoid missing links- that could hinder full understanding. 2. Following a sequential order, organize your work carefully 3. Concentrate on one main point at a time. 4. Mention the particular movement when things should be done. 5. Develop your paragraphs. D. FEATURES OF AN EXPOSITORY ESSAY. 1. Title of the essay (unemployment) 2. Introduction: Define the concept – Unemployment. Talk on the alarming rate of unemployment in the country and the expression of worry and concern by the general public. E. Body of the essay – this includes the sequential presentation of ideas such as. I causes of unemployment- corruption, lack of infrastructures for development e.g poor access roads, electricity, lack of incentives for agriculture, lack of industries, shortfall in government revenue (finance) mono economy (much dependence only on oil. ii. Effects of unemployment on the society increase in robbery, burglary, car snatching, rape, kidnapping, ritual killing, etc. F. CONCLUSION: suggest way to solve the problem E.g Government should create conducive environment for factories and industries for both medium and small scale productions. Attention should be given to agriculture. More

factories should be opened, good roads should be constructed, electricity should be provided, low interest loans should be given to youth to short business. ASSIGNMENT: Write an expository essay on the topic: “The problem of unemployment in Nigeria – causes and effects.

Read the passage quickly to grasp the general idea. 2. Quickly look at the questions. 3. Read the passage again to understand the details. 4. While answering the questions, limit you answers only to the information provided. Do not include materials not found in the passage. 5. Letter and number your answer correctly. Eg. A,b,ci, cii, d, 1, 2, 3, etc. (B) Word substituted (synonym). The word substitute must express the meaning or nearly the same meaning of the word/phrase as used in the passage. This means that the word subtitue must mean and can perfectly replace the word as it is used in the passage.

Example: Singular – singular substitute Plural - Plural “ Past tense - past tense “ Present tense - present tense “ Verb - verb “ Noun - noun “ etc. (C) TEST ON GRAMMATICAL NAMES AND FUNCTIONS. The grammatical name and function of a phrase or a clause is always demanded. A good knowledge of this will help you to answer this section of the passage properly. We have six grammatical names and eleven grammatical functions. Example: GRAMMATICAL NAME GRAMMATICAL FUNCTIONS 1. Noun phrase 2.Noun clause 1.Subject of the verb, (2) Object of the verb. (3) subject complement. (4) Object complement. (5(. Object to a proposition. (6) in opposition. 3.. Aderbial phrase 4. Adverbial clause 7. Modifies a verb, (8). Modifies an adjectives. (9). Modifies another adverb. 5 Adjectival phrase 6 Adjectival clause (10) Qualifies/modifies a noun (11). “ “ “ pronoun (D. TEST ON FIGURE OF SPEECH A good knowledge of all the figure of speech and idiomatic expression are necessary in order to excel in this part. i. You will excel if you read the passage carefully and thoroughly. ii. Make sure your answer are as brief as possible this helps you to reduce mistakes in grammar and spelling. ASSIGNMENT: Read the comprehension passage in Q & A 2015 and answer the questions. 1. This book is written for whoever wants it 2. We believe that we shall win the match 3. To study at Night engages the reader 4. I love sleeping in the room 5. Called the former captain a typist. TOPIC: POINTS TO NOTE IN WRITING A SUMMARY WRITING. (LESSON 4) Summary is a shorter account of the point, reasons, causes, factors, etc, put forward by the writer, giving only the main points. It is the extraction of relevant materials or ideas from a large piece of writing or speech. A summary is the main gist, the exact points, reduction of a long story/passage/. In answering summary questions, you are expected to be precise and

direct to the point. You must leave out any material that would not add positively to the answer, TECHNIQUES AND PROCEDURES FOR SUMMARY WRITING. 1. Quickly read the question(s) 2. Quickly read the passage 3. Slowly and carefully read passage with demands of questions in mind. Study the question(s) thoroughly to be sure of the answers the examiner expects. 4. Write out answers to questions. Make a rough draft of the answers in complete sentence. Do(S) OF SUMMARY WRITING. 1. Use your own words as much as possible and only make use of the words or phrases from the passage if necessary. 2. The use of synonyms and paraphrasing is allowed. Apt lifting of few key words or phrases is allowed. HOW TO PARAPHRASE. 1. .Read the original text until you grasp its meaning. 2. Write down the main point or concepts. Do not copy original word. 3. Change the original words and create your own sentence structure 4. Try to modify the structure of the passage 5. Check your answers against the original to ensure you have not accidently plagiarized. 6. Answers should be numbered for clarity. Eg. I, ii, iii, or 1, 2, 3, do not mix up your answers. DON’T /S OF SUMMARY WRITING. In summary writing; do not . 1. Copy verbatim. Avoid mindless lifting repetition, examples, illustrations and comparison. 2. Be tempted to give your opinions, embellishment and additional meaning. 3. Start your answer with because’ 4. Jump up ideas’ sentences should be linked in one sentence using conjunctions such ‘and’, or, but, in order” etc. 5. Verbosity, brevity should be the watch word. Ensure that your final draft does not contain more words than necessary. 6. Ambiguous sentences/answers 7. Your answers should not be in phrases and clauses except if asked to do so. ASSIGNMENT. Read the passage on page 28 of your text book, and answer the summary questions. TOPIC; NOUN PHRASES AND THEIR FUNCTIONS. (LESSON 5). A noun phrase is a group of words without a finite verb and has a noun as its headward. FUNCTIONS OF NOUN PHRASE A noun phrase can function

a. Subject of a verb b. Object of a verb c. Subject of complement d. Object complement e. Object of a preposition f. In opposition to a noun. (A). SUBJECT OF A VERB: A noun phrase functions as subject of a verb if it starts a sentence and comes before a (the) verb in that sentence. Example: (i) Some broken plates are on the shelf. (subject of the verb “are”) (ii) The big brown bag on the table is heavy. (subject of the verb “is”). (B) OBJECT OF VERB: A noun phrase functions as object of the verb when it come after the verb in a sentence. Example: (i) I know that man standing at the gate. (it functions as object of the “verb” “know”) (ii) He received the insult of his life. (it functions as object of the verb “received” ©. SUBJECT COMPLEMENT: It functions as subject complement when it refers to the same person or thing as subject in the sentence. (i) Music is a healer of the soul. (it complement the subject “music”) (ii) The issue seems to be quite an interesting one. (it complements the subject “issue”.) (D) OBJECT COMPLEMENT: A noun phrase function as object complement when it refers to the same person of thing as the object in the sentence. Example: (i) we call him the leader of the gang. (it complements the object “him”) (ii) She made her husband a lovely humanitarian. (it complements the object “husband”) (E) OBJECT TO A PREPOSITION: A noun phrase functions preposition in the sentence. Examples: (i) Her success depends on her ability to study her books. (it functions as object to a preposition “on”) (ii) The prize will go to the most talented student. (It functions as object to the preposition “to”). (F) IN APPOSITION TO A NOUN: This happens when the noun phrase is an explanatory equivalent to a noun in the sentence. In other words, the noun phrase is placed side by side a noun which it refers to at the same time in the sentence. (G) Examples: (i) Nigeria, the giant of Africa is in west African. (it functions in apposition to the “Nigeria”). (ii) John, my one and only friend is here. (it functions in apposition to the noun “John”) ASSIGNMENT: Underline the noun phrase in the following sentences and state their functions. 1. This book is written for whoever wants it. 2. We believe that we shall win the match.

3. To study at night engages the reader. 4. I love sleeping in the room. 5. I called the former captain a typist. (LESSON 6). A. An expository essay is an explanatory essay where the writer aims to inform, instruct, explain, criticize or analyze some concepts or situation to the reader. It allows the writer to show his capability for logical thought and reasoning. It is a factual essay and most times makes judgment. B. LIKELY TOPICS UNDER EXPOSITORY ESSAY. 1. How my favourite food is prepared 2. Dangers of drug above 3. The dangers of premarital sex 4. The future of the Nigerian youth 5. Causes of indiscipline in Nigeria secondary school. 6. The consequences of dressing indecently 7. Why prostitution is a crime 8. Managing population explosion in Nigeria 9. My English teacher how I saw her/him 10. Controlling HIV/AIDS in Nigeria. C. GUIDELINE FOR WRITING AN EXPOSITORY ESSAY. 1. Think of the most logical way of presenting in order to avoid missing links- that could hinder full understanding. 2. Following a sequential order, organize your work carefully 3. Concentrate on one main point at a time. 4. Mention the particular movement when things should be done. 5. Develop your paragraphs. D. FEATURES OF AN EXPOSITORY ESSAY. 1. Title of the essay (unemployment) 2. Introduction: Define the concept – Unemployment. Talk on the alarming rate of unemployment in the country and the expression of worry and concern by the general public. E. Body of the essay – this includes the sequential presentation of ideas such as. I causes of unemployment- corruption, lack of infrastructures for development e.g poor access roads, electricity, lack of incentives for agriculture, lack of industries, shortfall in government revenue (finance) mono economy (much dependence only on oil. ii. Effects of unemployment on the society increase in robbery, burglary, car snatching, rape, kidnapping, ritual killing, etc. F. CONCLUSION: suggest way to solve the problem E.g Government should create conducive environment for factories and industries for both medium and small scale productions. Attention should be given to agriculture. More

factories should be opened, good roads should be constructed, electricity should be provided, low interest loans should be given to youth to short business. ASSIGNMENT: Write an expository essay on the topic: “The problem of unemployment in Nigeria – causes and effects.

title: CLAUSE
subject: English Language
rawText:
A clause is a group of words that has a subject and a verb. Example: 👉 She is reading. She → subject is reading → verb So, it is a clause. Types of Clauses 1 ⃣ Main (Independent) Clause This clause can stand alone and make complete meaning. Examples: I like rice. He went home. 2 ⃣ Subordinate (Dependent) Clause This clause cannot stand alone. It depends on a main clause. Examples: because I was tired when she arrived Used in sentences like: I slept because I was tired. Types of Subordinate Clauses a) Noun Clause It acts like a noun. Examples: What he said is true. I know that she will come.

b) Adjective (Relative) Clause It describes a noun. It usually starts with who, which, that, whose, whom. Examples: The boy who won the prize is my friend. This is the book that I bought. c) Adverbial Clause It shows time, reason, condition, purpose, etc. Examples: I will come when you call. (time) She cried because she failed. (reason) If it rains, we will stay inside. (condition)
