THEME: FIRST TERM LESSON NOTE FOR SS3 SUBJECT: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS STUDIES WEEK 1: SURATUN-NASR, LAHAB, IKHLAS, FALAQ AND NAS. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUN-NASR 1. Idha ja a nasrul-lahi wal-fatah. 2. Wara aytan-nasa yadkhuluna fidinil-lahi afwaja. 3. Fasabbih bihamdi Rabbika wastaghfirhu. Innahu kana tawwaba. TRANSLATION 1. When Allah’s help and victory come. 2. And you see people entering Allah’s religion (Islam) in crowds. 3. Glorify the praises of your lord, and seek His forgiveness. Certainly, He is ever ready to forgive. LESSONS 1. It is a Madinah- surah. 2. It was the last chapter that was revealed to prophet Muhammad as a whole. 3. Allah promised the prophet and his followers that He would help and give them victory over their enemies. 4. Help and victory come from Allah. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL-LAHAB 1. Tabbat yada abi lahabin watabb. 2. Ma aghna anhu maluhu wama kasab. 3. Sayasla naran dhata lahabin. 4. Wamra’atuhu hammalatal hatab. 5. Fijidiha hablun min masad. TRANSLATION 1. Perish the two hands of Abu lahab (the father of flame), and perish he. 2. Neither his wealth nor what he has gained shall be of benefit to him. 3. He will be burnt in a fire of blazing flame.

4. And his wife too, who carried wood (thorns which she used to put on the way of the prophet or used to slander him). 5. In her neck is a twisted rope of palm fibre. LESSONS 1. This is a Makkan surah. 2. It has two names, Al-lahan and Al-masad. Taken from the first and last verses to the surah respectively. 3. Abu labab’s real name is Abdul-uzza. 4. He was an uncle of the Holy prophet. He was a son of Abdul-muttalib, the grandfather of the prophet. 5. Abu lahab’s wife is called both Arwa and Umm Jameelah. 6. She was the sister of Abu sufyan bin herb. 7. Both Abu lahab and his wife hated the religion of Islam a lot. 8. Allah has promised to protect the religion of Islam despite all odds. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL-IKHLAS 1. Qul Huwal-lahu ahad. 2. Allahus-Samad. 3. Lam yalid walam yulas. 4. Walam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad. TRANSLATION 1. Say: He is Allah, the one 2. Allah, the Eternal, Absolute. 3. He begets not, nor is he begotten. 4. And there is none like unto him. LESSONS 1. The surah teaches monotheism and forbids polytheism. 2. It teaches the attribute of Allah (a) Ahad (the one) and (b) As-Samad (the Eternal). 3. The surah states that everybody depends on Allah but He does not depend on anybody or anything.

4. It teaches the uniqueness of Allah. 5. It condemns the doctrine of trinity. 6. Nobody is equivalent to Allah in any respect and no one resemble Him in any form. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL FALAQ 1. Qul’a’udhu birabbil falaq. 2. Min sharri ma khalaq. 3. Wamin sharri ghasiqin idha waqab. 4. Wamin sharrin-naffathati fil-uqad. 5. Wamin sharri hasidin idha hasad. TRANSLATION 1. Say: I seek refuge with the lord of the down. 2. Against the evil of what He created. 3. And against the evil of the darkness when it occurs. 4. And against the evil of witchcrafts when the blow in the knots. 5. And against the evil of the envious one when the practices envy. LESSON The theme of the surah is to seek Allah’s protection against all evils, example the evils that are associated with the night, envy, witchcraft e.t.c. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUN-NAS 1. Qul’a’udhu biRabbin-nas. 2. Malikin-nas. 3. Ilahin-nas. 4. Min-sharril-waswasil-khannas 5. Alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas. 6. Minal-jinnati wan-nas. TRANSLATION 1. Say: I seek refuge with (Allah) the lord of mankind. 2. The king of mankind.

3. The God of mankind. 4. From the mischief of the whisperer (of evil), who withdraws (after his whisper). 5. (the same) who whispers into the hearts of mankind. 6. Among Jinns and among men. WEEK 2: REVISION OF HADITH 23, 25 AND 26 OF AN-NAWAWI TRANSLITERATION 0F HADITH 23 Al-Hadithul-thalithu wal-ishirun Anil-Harithibni Asiminil Ash’ary, radiyallahu anhu qala: Qala rasulullahi Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: “At- tuhuru Shatrul-Iman, wal-hamdu lillahi tamla’ul-mizan, wasubhanallahi walhamdulillahi tamla’ani aw tamla’u ma baynas-sama’I wal-ard. Wa-salatu nur, was-sadaqatu-burhan, was-sabru diya, wal-Qur’anu hujjatun laka aw alayk. Kullunnasi yaghdu fa ba’I’un nafsahu fa mu tiquha aw mubiquha.” Rawahu Muslim. TRANSLATION On the authority of Harithu bn Asim al-Ash’ary (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “purification is half of faith, saying ‘peace be upon him’ fills the seal, saying, Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah (fills) the between the heavens and the earth, prayer is light, Sadaqah is proof (of sincere faith), endurance is shining glory, and the Quran is a proof for you or against you. All people go out early and sell themselves, thereby setting themselves free or destroying themselves.” Transmitted by Muslim- COMMENTS This tradition teaches that purification is half of faith because it is a pillar of worship for without purification there will be no acceptable worship and if there is no acceptable worship there would be no faith. Saying prayers is light because it guides to the right path because of the verses of Qur’an which are read and which give peace to mind. Giving out poor dues is a sign of strength of faith of the person who gives them out of his wealth. Patience is light because it gives strength of facing whatever may befall a person until he achieves success. The glorious Qur’an is an evidence for you if you carry out its teachings and it is an evidence against you if you do not carry out its teachings. TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 25

Al-Hadithul- khamisu wal-Ishirun An Abi dharrin radiyallahu anhu aydhan, anna nasan min ashabi rasulullahi (S.A.W): Ya rasulallah, dhahaba ahludduthuri bil-ujuri, yusalluna kama nusalli wa yasumuna kama nasuumu yatasaddaquna bi fuduli amwalihim. Qal: “Awalaysa qad ja’alallahu ma tasaddaquun? Inna bikulli tasbihatin sadaqah, wa kulli takhbiratin sadaqah, wa kulli tahmidatin sadaqah, wa amrin bil ma’arufi sadaqah, wa nahyun anil munkari sadaqah, wafi bud’i ahadikum sadaqah.” Qalu ya rasulullahi: Aya’ati ahaduna shahwatahu wa yakunu lahu fiha ajr? Qal: “Ara’aytum law wada aha fi haramin, akana alayhi wizr? Fa kadhalika idha wada’aha fil halali kana alihi ajr.” Rawahu Muslim. TRANSLATION On the authority of Abu Dharr (May Allah be pleased with him) who said: some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah said to the prophet (peace be upon him): “O messenger of Allah, the rich people have gone with the rewards; they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give alms with what they do not need out of their wealth”. The prophet said: “Has not Allah provide you with what you are able to give? In every ascription of glory to Allah, every declaration of His greatness, every utterance of praise to Him, every declaration that he is the only God, in enjoining what is reputable, in forbidding what is objectionable, and in a man’s sexual intercourse there is sadaqah.” They said: “O messenger of Allah would a reward be given for satisfying one’s passion?” He said: “Tell me; if he were to devote it to something forbidden, would it be a sin on his part? Similarly, if he were to devote it to something lawful, he would have a reward.” Transmitted by Muslim. TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 26 Al-Hadithul- Sadisu Wal-Ishirun

An Abhi Hurairata radiyallahu anhu Qaal: Qala Rasulullahi (S.A.W): “Kullu sulama muinan nasi alaihi sadaqah, kulla yaumin tadulu’u fihi shamsu: ta’adilu bainath naini sadaqah, wa tu’inur rajula fi dabbatihi fa tahmiluhu alaiha aw tarfa’u lahu alaiha mata’ahu sadaqah, wal kalimatu dayyibatu sadaqah, wabi kulli khadwatin tamshiha ilas salati sadaqah, wa tumidul adhaa anil dariq sadaqah.” Rawahul-Bukhari wa Muslim TRANSLATION On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: “The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Every bone of man’s fingers and toes must give sadaqah, every day the sun rises a man deals justly between two people it is sdaqah. If one helps a man with his beast, loading or lifting his goods on it, it is sadaqah. A good word is sadaqah, every step one takes towards prayer is sadaqah, any one remove anything injuries from the road it is sadaqah.” Transmitted by Al-Bukahari and Muslim. COMMENTS i. This tradition has much in common with the twenty-fifth tradition. It has given a wide range of deeds that can earn a Muslim excellent reward if he does them. This tradition shows typically how the generous the religion is to its follows. In whatever sphere of life, you happen to be it with you are wealthy or poor, Islam has not forgotten you. It has something for you only if you care to follow it. ii. This tradition has a lot of ethical teaching. If applied, it will contribute a lot in the betterment of human relationship. Its contribution to our society life is invaluable. WEEK 3: THE CONTRIBUTIONS MADE BY SELECTED MUSLIM PHILOSOPHERS/EDUCATIONIST IN WORLDMCIVILIZATIO CONTRIBUTIONS OF JABIR IBN HAYYAN AND AL-RAZI JABIR IBN HAYYAN (721-815 C.E)

Jabir ibn Hayyan was born in Tus in Iran. Shortly after he was born his father who was pharmacist, was political reasons. He was taught by the famous Imam Ja’afar al-Sadiq, studied medicine and became a court physician to the Abbasi caliph Harun ar-Rashid. He died in exile in Kufa, in modern Iraq in 815 A.C HIS CONTRIBUTIONS Jabir wrote more than 100 works, mainly on alchemy and chemistry with others on astronomy, of these books only 22 survive in Arabic. Some of his famous books on alchemy are the book of Mercy, the book of concentration, the book of the kingdom and the book of balances. Some of his works on chemistry were translated into European languages including Latin. He was known in Europe by the name of ‘Geber’. Jabir was acknowledged as the father of Modern Chemistry. AL -RAZI ALCHEMIST, PHILOSOPHER AND PHYSICIAN 865-925 A.C Abubakar Muhammad ibn Zakariya Al-razi was born in Rayy (in Persia) and studied mathematics, alchemy, philosophy, astronomy and Medicine in Baghdad. He served for a time as chief physician in a newly established hospital in Rayy, and later held a similar position in Baghdad. Many students attended his lectures that his voice could not be heard by those sitting far away, it was necessary for those sitting nearer to pass on his words to those at the back. He died in 925 A.C in his home town of Rayy. HIS GENERAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO LEARNING Razi was a prolific writer, and in accordance with the practice of his time he was knowledgeable in many of the sciences. Hence his writings include works on medical science, chemistry, physics, music, philosophy, mathematics, astronomy etc. He wrote about 200 books of which half are on medical subject. His most famous books were kitab ai-Mansur (composed for Mansur al-Ishaq the ruler of Rayy) and kitab al-Hawi, “the comprehensive book.” He was described as the greatest physician of the Ummah during his time.

His specific contributions were: a. On the disposition of the heart. b. He wrote a treatise on measles and small pox. c. His book kitab al-HAwi was the most comprehensive work on medicine by a Muslim scientist. IBN SINA PHILOSOPHER AND PHYSICIAN 370-428 A.H (980-1037 A.C) Ibn Sina (known as Avicenna in the west) was born near Bukhara in central Asia. His native language was Persian. He was well educated at Bukhara and soon showed his extraordinary intelligence and memory. By the age of 07-14 he had already overtaken his teachers, and by the time he was 16, famous physicians were working under his directions. At 18 he had mastered all the then-known sciences, and the progress he made thereafter was by the use of his own-brain and his own initiatives. He produced his first book on philosophy at the age of 21. Ibn Sina was invited by the ruler of Isfahan to his court where he worked until the time he died in Hamadan. THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF IBN SINA TO ISLAMIC PHILOSOPHY AND MEDICINE Meanwhile, he wrote books in the night and even while travelling on horseback or in prison. He was a very fast writer. He corrected arguments of Aristotle. He wrote altogether between 200-300 works in which he contributed to the advancement of all the sciences of his day: Natural history, history, physics, chemistry, astronomy, geology, medicine, mathematics, music, economics, politics, poetry, moral and religious affairs, Qur’anic commentary and philosophy in addition he wrote poetry as a vehicle for expressing his philosophy and also as medium of instruction for logic and medicine. His famous books were the kitab al-shifa (book of healing of the soul) a philosophical work and the Qanun fil tibb (canon of medicine). The latter book remained the authority on medicine both in Muslim lands and in Europe for 700 years until the modern age of experimental science began. Some of its teaching and treatments are still useful to doctors even today. Ibn sina’s greatest works were translated into latin, and he and Al-razi were recognized in Europe as the greatest masters of medicine, philosophy and natural sciences. Ibn sina’s(Canon of medicine) was

translated 87 times, all or in part, and formed the basis of medical teaching and practice in European Universities from 12 th to the 17 th century. AL-GHAZALI THEOLOGIAN, JURIST, ORIGINAL THINKER AND RELIGIOUS REFORMER 450-505 A.H (1058- 1111 A.C) Abu Hamid Muhammad known as al-Ghazali was born at Tus in Persia in 450 A.H equivalent to 1072 C.E. He joined marry scholars at the court of Nizam al-Mulk in Baghdad. Nizam al-Mulk sent him as chief professor to the Nizamiyya, a college he had established in Baghdad. WORKS More than 400 works are ascribed to Al-Ghazali, but some of these probably had other authors. Al-Ghazali wrote books on Fiqh (Jurisprudence), philosophy and logic, theology and Sufi theory and Sufi theology and practice. Al-Ghazali’s greatest work however was the” Ihya” Ulum al-din (Revival of the religious sciences). WEEK 4: AN-NIKAH. DEFINATION, IMPORTANCE, PURPOSE, RULES AND REGULATIONS GOVERNING ITS VALIDITY, RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF HUSBAND AND WIFE. AN-NIKAH Marriage is called An-nikah in Arabic. Marriage is encouraged in Islam. It has existed since the time of our earliest forefather Adam, when Allah created for him a mate, Hauwa, and they had children. Allah says: (24:32) “Marry single from among you and such that are fit of your male and female slaves. If they are poor Allah will enrich them of His bounty, surely Allah is sufficient and All-knowing. The prophet (P.B.U.H) said: There is no (monkhood) celibacy in Islam. The prophet also said: “Marriage is my Sunnah whoever Shuns it is not one of us”: PURPOSE AND IMPORTANCE OF MARRIAGE Allah refers to the purpose of marriage in verse of the Qur’an: “And among His signs is this, He has created mates for you from among yourselves so that you may fine tranquility with them and He has put love and tenderness between you. In this behold there are messages indeed for people who think.

This is a beautiful description of the Husband/Wife relationship. The marriage relationship is important because it fulfils a number of functions, among which are: a. The sense of security b. Sexual satisfaction c. Foundation of family life d. Security in old age RULES GOVERNING MARRIAGE Four conditions for the validity of marriage in Islam are these: 1. Mutual consent of the couple. proposal and acceptance (Ijab and Qabul in Arabic terms) any of the two can propose. The formular is ‘I marry you’ and ‘I accept’ 2. Waliyy: marriage guardianship. Approval by the parent or guardian of the bride. The Qur’an 4:25 states ‘Marry them with the permission of their people’ 3. Mandatory Gift from the groom to the bride: it has no limit. It is called Mahr or Sadaq. 4. Witness/publicity witnesses to the marriage contract. Marriage must not be conducted in secret. There must be at least two adult witnesses. LESSONS 1. A person must make a good choice of a spouse. 2. A girls parents’ consent must be obtained before marriage. 3. A bride gift is mandatory. 4. Witnesses are necessary. 5. Moderation should be applied to the amount of Mahr to be paid. RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF HUSBAND AND WIFE Allah says: “And men have rights over women as women have rights over men, and men are a degree above them”. The husband is fully responsible for the feeding, clothing, housing, satisfying her sexual desire and general welfare of the wife (and children). He is also expected to protect them from any external danger, and to

ensure their proper Islamic education which will protect them from doing wrong out of ignorance, mutual respect for her and her parents. The wife should take good care of the husband’s property. Whenever he is away, making the home comfortable and happy place for all the family. She should not allow into the house men of whom the husband does not approve. She should guard her chastity and keep a good reputation. She should also satisfy her husband (in sexual fulfilment), respect him and his parents. WEEK 5: HADITH 32 AND 34 OF AN-NAWAWI AND THEIR LESSONS TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 32 An Abi Said Sa’d ibn Malik ibn Sinanil-khudriyy, radiyallahu anhu, anna Rasulallahi sallallahu alayhi wa Sallama Qal: “La Dharara wala Dhirara”. Hadithun Hasanun, Rawahu ibn majah. TRANSLATION On the authority of Abu Said al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: “The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: There should be no damage nor should there be any damaging (to the others).” Transmitted by ibn majah. COMMENTS 1. This tradition teaches us that we should not oppress anyone and if we are oppressed, we should leave the matter with God, Most High or in the hands of justice. if we take revenge, we should not exceed the oppression done to us. 2. If is clear that peace is bound to prevail everywhere if the teaching of this tradition is put into practice. No one will harm you if you do not harm anybody else. TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 34 An Abu Saidinil Hhudriyyi, radiyallahu anhu Qal: Sami’tu rasullallahi Sallallahu alaiyhi wa Sallam Yaqul: “Man ra’a minkum munkaran falyugayirhu biyadih, fa in lam yastadi fabi lisanihi, fa in lam yastadi fabiqalbih, waq dhalika ad’aful-Iman”. TRANSLATION on the authority of Abu-Said Al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: “If anyone sees an abomination, he should change it with his hand,

if he cannot he should do it with his tongue, if he cannot he should do it in his heart, that being the weakest form of faith”. Transmitted by Muslim. COMMENT The tradition explains that it is a person whose faith is weak that cannot used either his hand or tongue to stop a wrong thing being done. He can then only hate such a thing in his mind only. WEEK 6: MORAL EDUCATION. KINDNESS TO PARENTS, HONESTY IN WORDS AND DEEDS, DIGNITY OF LABOUR KINDNESS TO PARENTS Islam teaches good morality. It wants Muslims to be good generally and to his parents in particular. This is imperative considering parent’s labour on the child. The Qur’an commands us to show kindness to parents in the following words: “Your Lord has decreed that you should worship nothing except him, and (show) kindness to your parents, whether one or both of them attain old age (while they are) still with you never say to them “Shame!” nor Scorn either of them, but speak to them in a generous way. Lower to them the wing of kindness out of mercy and say: “my Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little”. (Qur’an 17:23-24). NOTE: OBEDIENCE TO ALLAH COMES FIRST! If parents other their children to do something which Allah has forbidden, and to go against Islam, then the children should obey Allah and not their parents in a polite way. why they cannot obey them. They should, however, continue to show them respect and kindness. HONESTY IN WORDS AND DEEDS Allah says: “Shun every word that is untrue. (Q. 22:30). Verily, truth is goodness, and goodness leads to paradise, and verily lying is wickedness and wickedness leads to the fire (of hell). Hadith ibn Mas’ud (Musli). Truthfulness is a habit which lies at the root of all good habits, while lying is a habit which lies at the root of all bad habits. What are the ill effects of dishonesty on the other people and on society in general? Obviously the victim of someone’s lies on dishonesty will feel pain, anger, loss or disappointment.

DIGNITY OF LABOUR Islam encourages every Muslim to seek a lawful livelihood for himself and his family and not to beg, as he is capable of earning a living. One must not refuse any lawful occupation on account of its being low in dignity. While it is honourable to work to earn a living, it is dishonourable to depend on begging for a living. The prophet is reported to have e said: “Never has anyone eaten a better thing than what he eats from the work of his hand.” (Hadith from Bukhari) THE PROPHET’S ATTITUDE TO POVERTY AND BEGGING The prophet always cared for the poor. Even when he became the Head of state in Medina he lived as a poor Man. Sometimes he and his family did not have enough to eat. Whenever they had something, they used to share it with the poor, or give it away as Sadaqah to others who were in need. Every Muslim should care for the welfare of those around him. The prophet said: ‘He is not a Muslim who eats his fill while his neighbour goes hungry. Therefore, all Muslims, rich or poor, are urged to treat others with kindness and generosity. It this is done, there will be no cause to go and beg, and no excuse for those who wish to make begging a way of life. WEE 7: THE STATUS OF WOMEN IN ISLAM, POLYGAMY, RULES THAT GOVERN IT THE STATUS OF WOMEN IN ISLAM i. Women’s status in pre-Islamic societies. In some part of the world, women have been treated little better than a slave, forced to do heavy work for little reward. In some place’s women were regarded in law as chattels- the property of the husband or family to be inherited on his death along with his other possessions. Some societies have regarded women as play things, to be passed from man to man for his entertainment. Some have seen women ads not only without soul but as an agent of the devil. Consequently, the birth of a girl would be greeted with either a sigh or a curse. Some societies, such as that of Arabia before Islam, even sanctioned the burial alive of female infants. ii. Islam and Women: a revolutionary change. No other religion can compare with Islam in the revolutionary changes it introduced in the status of women. These changes required a major re- adjustment in the way women were to be evaluated and treated, both legally and morally.

Islam considered women and treated them very well in different status such as: a. Spiritual status b. Intellectual status c. Property-owning status d. Status in marriage e. The spirit of kindness towards women f. The status of the mother. POLYGAMY The word “Polygamy” is used to refer to marriage of a man with more than one wife at the same time while a woman who has more than two husbands at a time is practicing polyandry. Monogamy is having only one spouse. Islam prohibits polyandry and allows monogamy and polygamy. RULES THAT GOVERN IT LIMITS OF POLYGAMY IN ISLAM Islam allows a male Muslim to marry up to four wives concurrently if he is able to maintain justice and equity among the wives Allah says in Qur’an 4:3. “Then marry women of your choice, two, three, or four but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with them, then (Marry) only one…that is nearer to prevent you from doing injustice.” Equity and justice among wives are conditions for marrying more than one wife. The prophet said: ‘Whoever marries more than one wife and does not maintain justice among the wives shall be raised paralyzed on the last day. JUSTICE AND EQUAL TREATMENT OF WIVES MUST BE MAINTAINED In particular, equality should be maintained among wives in the following ways by providing: i. Food ii. Shelter iii. Clothing iv. Company

Or intimate relations/sharing of bed with the wife. The husband must share his time (day and night) equally among the wives in rotation. CIRCUMSTANCES WHICH MIGHT NECESSITATE POLYGAMY Polygamy has a role to play under some circumstances. For example, problems sometimes arise as the result of a disability in the first wife, such as: a. Infertility b. Serious illness, physical handicap, disablement or serious injuries due to accident etc. c. Mental illness. Another circumstance which may make polygamy preferable are: 1. In a situation where the husband is too virile for one wife. 2. In a wartime where marry men are killed, leaving thousands or even millions of widows, orphans, and unmarried young women. By allowing for polygamy the women can be protected, taken care of and enabled to enjoy the satisfactions of family life and children. WEEK 8: DIVORCE (AT-TALAQ) DEFINATION, ATTITUDE AND KINDS Talaq (Divorce) means the breaking of the marriage bond. In Islam marriage is intended to be a lifelong partnership wherein both partners find security and happiness, and are able to establish a family and bring up their children (see chapter 52). It occasionally happens however that a marriage runs into problems, and one or both of the partners want to separate. Sometimes these problems can be solved and the marriage continues, sometimes the problems are not solved and the marriage ends in divorce. TEACHING AGAINST DIVORCE Allah says: “If you fear a breach between them (Husband and Wife) appoint (two) arbitrators, one from his family and the other from her family, if they both wish to make peace, Allah will cause their reconciliation. Indeed, Allah is ever the All-know, well acquainted with all things.” Qur’an 4:35

DIVORCE AS LAST RESOR If all efforts to live harmoniously as husband and wife fails, Allah allows divorce through a laid down procedure. The Qur’an states: “But if they separate (divorce) Allah will provide abundance for everyone of them from his bounty, and Allah is ever All-sufficient, All-wise.” Qur’an 4:130 EVIL OF DIVORCE INCLUDE a. Enmity b. Poor upbringing of children c. Displeasure of Allah d. Sadness to one or both parties e. Weakening of family ties f. The wife’s beauty might have been reduced. KINDS OF DIVORCE There are basically four methods of divorce: a. Talaq: Divorce at the instance of the husband b. Khul: Divorce at the instance of the wife c. Faskh: Divorce by court order d. Mubarah: Divorce by mutual agreement of husband and wife REVOCABLE AND IRREVOCABLE DIVORCE Divorce may be revocable (i.e it can be recalled and cancelled) and it may be irrevocable (which cannot be reversed). i. Divorce which cannot be reversed is known as (Talaq bain) irrevocable divorce. ii. Talaq that may be reversed to resume marital life between the couple is called (Talaq raji) revocable divorce. OTHER MEANS OF DISSOLUTION OF MARRIAGE The laid down procedures for divorce have been explained as Talaq, khul, Mubarah, and Faskh. There are other practices which have the effect of dissolution of marriage. The practices are Li’an, ila and Zihar 1. Li’an (Mutual imprecation)

a. If the husband alleges that the wife commits adultery or he rejects the paternity of a child on the ground of an alleged infidelity on the part of the wife, then the process of li’an, self-cursing is adopted. Thereafter the marriage becomes irrevocable dissolved. b. The Qur’an 24:6-9 explains that if the husband alleges zina against his wife, he will swear four times in the name of Allah on it and on the fifth swearing he shall invoke Allah’s wrath on himself if his allegation is false. If he refuses to swear and he cannot produce four reliable male witnesses to the alleged committal of zina, he is to be punished with eighty lashes of the cane. If he makes the oath and the woman accepts, she is to be punished for zina and that ends the marriage but if she refutes it, then she shall swear four times and on the fifth time invoke the wrath of Allah on herself, if the husband’s allegation is true. This oath of innocence marks the end of the marriage snice trust is no longer existing in the marriage. The li’an terminates the marriage. 2. Al-Ila (Oath of conjugal suspension): It was the practice during the pre-Islamic period through which a husband vowed not to have sexual intercourse with the wife and she was thus left without divorce and without sexual intercourse. Qur’an 2:226-227 says: “in the case of those who swear not to be into their wives, the waiting period is four months, then if they go back, Allah is surely forgiving, merciful. And if they resolve on divorce, then Allah is surely Hearing, knowing.” Islam directs that he either resumes the conjugal relation without four months or she commences her ‘Iddah’ after the expiration of the four months at the end of the Iddah, the wife is free to marry someone else. 3. Zihar (husbands’ comparison of wife’s back with his mother’s) IDDAH (waiting period) AND KIND TREATMENT OF DIVORCED WOMEN, TYPES AND VARIATIONS WHAT IS IDDAH? Iddah is a waiting period pf a woman after divorce or death of the husband. She cannot re-marry another man while she is in Iddah. The uses of iddah including the following: a. In the case of Iddah of first or second divorce it allows time for reconsideration and reconciliation. b. It establishes whether the woman is pregnant by the divorced husband. This prevents any dispute over paternity of a child, which might arise if she were allowed to contract a new marriage at once. c. In case the wife is pregnant, it ensures her maintenance and care until she delivers.

d. In case of death of the husband it allows time for some recovery from the initial grief before deciding on any new marriage, since it is unlawful for a man to make a formal marriage proposal to a woman in Iddah, although he may hint at his intention. (Qur’an 2:235) DURATION OF IDDAH The duration of Iddah is generally speaking as follows: a. In the case of a woman who menstruates, it is the period of three quru (monthly cycles). That is she should observe three full gaps between 3 monthly periods before the Iddah expires. (Qur’an 2:228) b. In the case of a woman who is pregnant, her Iddah lasts until delivery (Qur’an 65:4) c. In the case of a woman who has stopped menstruation or a girl who has not started, the Iddah is three months (Qur’an 65:4) d. If a marriage was not yet consummated, there is no Iddah (Qur’an 33:49) e. In the case of death of the husband the iddah is four months and ten days (Qur’an 2:234). QUR’ANIC VERSES TOWARDS IDDAH I. Qur’an 65:1 state: “O prophet, when you divorce women divorce them through their Iddah and count their Iddah accurately and fear Allah your lord. And you Muslims must not turn them out if their (husband’s homes) or shall they leave except in case they are guilty of some obvious illicit deal. And those are the limits of Allah and whosoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then indeed has wronged himself. You know not, that Allah may thereafter bring some new things to pass. II. Qur’an 65:6 state: “Lodge them (divorce wives) where you dwell, according to your means, and do not ill treat them that they may be made to leave… CUSTODY OF CHILDREN AFTER DIVORCE In the event of divorce or death of the husband or wife Islam makes rules for the custody of the children (hadanah). The prophet responds to the enquiry of a divorced woman or whether she or the husband should have the right of custody of the children as follows: ‘You (the wife) have a better right to have him (son) as long as you do not re-marry’ ibn Majah. DURATION OF THE CUSTODY

The duration of the custody for a girl is until she is married and for a boy, it is until he attains puberty. Therefore, he or she can live anywhere, as dictated by circumstances. The order of priority for custody under the shari’ah are: 1. The mother of the children 2. Mother’s mother 3. Mother’s grandmother (maternal, then paternal) 4. Mother’s sister (full, then maternal, then paternal) 5. Grandmother’s sister 6. Mother’s aunt 7. Father’s mother or father’s grandmother (maternal, then paternal) 8. Father 9. Child’s sister 10. Father’s sister (Hashiyat al-Dasuqi vol.2: p-527) WEEK 9 AND 10: MODESTY IN DRESSING AND BEHAVIOUR, PERSEVERANCE (sabr) AND ALLAH’S CONSCIOUSNESS (taqwa) MODESTY IN DRESSING AND BEHAVIOUR The difference in the sexuality and attraction of males and females to the exposure of sensitive and sexually arousing parts of the body of the opposite sex accounts for the emphasis which Islam places on covering of almost all parts of a female body. A woman, except when she is with her husband or close relation is expected to cover her body except the face and the hands. She is not to wear any dress that is tight or transparent except when she is alone, with her close relatives, her Husband or other females. Men too must not expose their nudity except when they are with their wives or close relatives. Men’s nudity is what lies between their navel and knee. For men and women, even if they are in privacy, should not be naked. Both men and women are expected to be modest in dressing and behavior by lowering their gaze and guarding their modesty. They should not stare at or intimately gaze at people of the opposite sex who are no their spouse or close relation. QUR’ANIC VERSES ON MODESTY ON DRERSSING AND BEHAVIOUR

Allah says: “Tell the believing men to lower their gaze (from looking at forbidden things), and protect their private parts (from illegal sexual acts etc.) that is purer for them. Verily, Allah is All aware of what they do. And tell the believing women to lower their gaze (from looking at forbidden things), and protect their private parts (from illegal sexuality) … PERSEVERANCE (SABR) Sabr is an Arabic word denoting endurance, perseverance and patience. Because of its importance in shaping the life of man, Allah in several places in the Qur’an enjoins His creatures to cultivate Sabr even when things go wrong. Qur’an 2:153-157 enjoins Muslims to demonstrate Sabr in the face of danger, loss and hardship. Prophet Muhammad also counselled his followers to exercise patience and perseverance and described those who uphold this as being grateful to Allah. Prophet Muhammad demonstrated sabr through his life. He was persecuted by the idol worshippers, betrayed by the hypocrites and was even stoned out of Taif when preaching, yet he did not abandon practice patience is necessary for doing good and resisting evil. ALLAH’S CONSCIOUSNESS (TAQWA) Taqwa is often translated to mean God consciousness. It also means piety of fear of Allah. The Glorious Qur’an describes a person who is conscious of Allah as one who sincerely practices Islam both outwardly and inwardly. It is he whose moral probity is not in doubt. Taqwa should obviously improve the attitude and behavior of the person who possess it. TRUST (AMANAH) Trust (Amanah) is a very importance aspect of man’s responsibity. A good Muslim must keep trust not betray it. If one is the head of a place, those under him are to put in him trust, he should therefore treat them well for Allah shall ask how he has treated them. The same applies to one’s wife and children, they are put in one’s care and must be taken care of. If a teacher keeps some money in care of a student, the student should not say that the money is lost, it is amanah. Allah says: “verily, Allah commands you to render back the trusts to those entitled to them…”

LEADERSHIP, FOLLOWSHIP AND JUSTICE Leadership is a form of guardianship over those under one’s care or supervision. A leader has been given some responsibilities to which he is accountable to Allah. Leadership therefore imposes on one that care for the welfare of those under one and doing what is best for them. Justice on the other hand implies that matters are decided by the leader and he leads on the basis of truth and facts. No one is to be given what is not his due or denied of his/her due. The leader should not abuse his privilege position to misrule or commit injustice against those under his care. A leader should uphold the truth and shun favouritism. An unjust leader cannot command the required respect from the subjects and therefore cannot have peace. Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) is the best example worthy of emulation, he led by example because he was just and responsible. His leadership qualities are on record for all generations. WEEK 11: UNITY AND BROTHERHOOD, RELIGIOUS TOLERANCE AND PEACEFUL CO-EXISTANCE UNITY AND BROTHERHOOD (Importance and meaning of brotherhood) Islam is a religion that governs all aspects of human lives. Muslims are considered as brothers of the same family in that whatever happens to one (good or bad) others are also affected. In whatever part of the world Muslims meet one another, they should be at home and demonstrate the unifying spirit of Islam to the world. The unity which salat provides through coming together five times daily and the annual Ramadan fast and pilgrimage should be extended to other aspects of our lives. Unity and brotherhood were demonstrated by the Muslims in the early days of Islam. The Muslims of Madinah (Ansar) accommodated the emigrants (Muhajirun) in the spirit of Islamic brotherhood. It was with this spirit that the Muslim Ummah was able to subdue the large Makkan army. The modern-day Muslims should embrace the brotherhood of Islam to promote their course rather than allow factionalism based on ethnic and sectarian inclinations to divide them. INJUNCTIONS ON UNITY AND BROTHERHOOD. QUR’ANIC VERSES i. “And hold fast, all together into the bond with Allah, and do not be disunited. And remember the blessings which Allah has bestowed on you, for you were enemies one to another but he

joined your hearts together, so that through His blessings you become brethren…” (Qur’an 3:103) ii. “All believers are brothers. Hence, (make peace between your two brothers, and remain conscious of Allah, so that you might be graced with His mercy” (Qur’an 49:10).

pages.text: THEME: FIRST TERM LESSON NOTE FOR SS3 SUBJECT: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS STUDIES WEEK 1: SURATUN-NASR, LAHAB, IKHLAS, FALAQ AND NAS. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUN-NASR 1. Idha ja a nasrul-lahi wal-fatah. 2. Wara aytan-nasa yadkhuluna fidinil-lahi afwaja. 3. Fasabbih bihamdi Rabbika wastaghfirhu. Innahu kana tawwaba. TRANSLATION 1. When Allah’s help and victory come. 2. And you see people entering Allah’s religion (Islam) in crowds. 3. Glorify the praises of your lord, and seek His forgiveness. Certainly, He is ever ready to forgive. LESSONS 1. It is a Madinah- surah. 2. It was the last chapter that was revealed to prophet Muhammad as a whole. 3. Allah promised the prophet and his followers that He would help and give them victory over their enemies. 4. Help and victory come from Allah. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL-LAHAB 1. Tabbat yada abi lahabin watabb. 2. Ma aghna anhu maluhu wama kasab. 3. Sayasla naran dhata lahabin. 4. Wamra’atuhu hammalatal hatab. 5. Fijidiha hablun min masad. TRANSLATION 1. Perish the two hands of Abu lahab (the father of flame), and perish he. 2. Neither his wealth nor what he has gained shall be of benefit to him. 3. He will be burnt in a fire of blazing flame.

4. And his wife too, who carried wood (thorns which she used to put on the way of the prophet or used to slander him). 5. In her neck is a twisted rope of palm fibre. LESSONS 1. This is a Makkan surah. 2. It has two names, Al-lahan and Al-masad. Taken from the first and last verses to the surah respectively. 3. Abu labab’s real name is Abdul-uzza. 4. He was an uncle of the Holy prophet. He was a son of Abdul-muttalib, the grandfather of the prophet. 5. Abu lahab’s wife is called both Arwa and Umm Jameelah. 6. She was the sister of Abu sufyan bin herb. 7. Both Abu lahab and his wife hated the religion of Islam a lot. 8. Allah has promised to protect the religion of Islam despite all odds. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL-IKHLAS 1. Qul Huwal-lahu ahad. 2. Allahus-Samad. 3. Lam yalid walam yulas. 4. Walam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad. TRANSLATION 1. Say: He is Allah, the one 2. Allah, the Eternal, Absolute. 3. He begets not, nor is he begotten. 4. And there is none like unto him. LESSONS 1. The surah teaches monotheism and forbids polytheism. 2. It teaches the attribute of Allah (a) Ahad (the one) and (b) As-Samad (the Eternal). 3. The surah states that everybody depends on Allah but He does not depend on anybody or anything.

4. It teaches the uniqueness of Allah. 5. It condemns the doctrine of trinity. 6. Nobody is equivalent to Allah in any respect and no one resemble Him in any form. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL FALAQ 1. Qul’a’udhu birabbil falaq. 2. Min sharri ma khalaq. 3. Wamin sharri ghasiqin idha waqab. 4. Wamin sharrin-naffathati fil-uqad. 5. Wamin sharri hasidin idha hasad. TRANSLATION 1. Say: I seek refuge with the lord of the down. 2. Against the evil of what He created. 3. And against the evil of the darkness when it occurs. 4. And against the evil of witchcrafts when the blow in the knots. 5. And against the evil of the envious one when the practices envy. LESSON The theme of the surah is to seek Allah’s protection against all evils, example the evils that are associated with the night, envy, witchcraft e.t.c. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUN-NAS 1. Qul’a’udhu biRabbin-nas. 2. Malikin-nas. 3. Ilahin-nas. 4. Min-sharril-waswasil-khannas 5. Alladhi yuwaswisu fi sudurin-nas. 6. Minal-jinnati wan-nas. TRANSLATION 1. Say: I seek refuge with (Allah) the lord of mankind. 2. The king of mankind.

3. The God of mankind. 4. From the mischief of the whisperer (of evil), who withdraws (after his whisper). 5. (the same) who whispers into the hearts of mankind. 6. Among Jinns and among men. WEEK 2: REVISION OF HADITH 23, 25 AND 26 OF AN-NAWAWI TRANSLITERATION 0F HADITH 23 Al-Hadithul-thalithu wal-ishirun Anil-Harithibni Asiminil Ash’ary, radiyallahu anhu qala: Qala rasulullahi Sallallahu alayhi wa sallam: “At- tuhuru Shatrul-Iman, wal-hamdu lillahi tamla’ul-mizan, wasubhanallahi walhamdulillahi tamla’ani aw tamla’u ma baynas-sama’I wal-ard. Wa-salatu nur, was-sadaqatu-burhan, was-sabru diya, wal-Qur’anu hujjatun laka aw alayk. Kullunnasi yaghdu fa ba’I’un nafsahu fa mu tiquha aw mubiquha.” Rawahu Muslim. TRANSLATION On the authority of Harithu bn Asim al-Ash’ary (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “purification is half of faith, saying ‘peace be upon him’ fills the seal, saying, Glory be to Allah and praise be to Allah (fills) the between the heavens and the earth, prayer is light, Sadaqah is proof (of sincere faith), endurance is shining glory, and the Quran is a proof for you or against you. All people go out early and sell themselves, thereby setting themselves free or destroying themselves.” Transmitted by Muslim- COMMENTS This tradition teaches that purification is half of faith because it is a pillar of worship for without purification there will be no acceptable worship and if there is no acceptable worship there would be no faith. Saying prayers is light because it guides to the right path because of the verses of Qur’an which are read and which give peace to mind. Giving out poor dues is a sign of strength of faith of the person who gives them out of his wealth. Patience is light because it gives strength of facing whatever may befall a person until he achieves success. The glorious Qur’an is an evidence for you if you carry out its teachings and it is an evidence against you if you do not carry out its teachings. TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 25

Al-Hadithul- khamisu wal-Ishirun An Abi dharrin radiyallahu anhu aydhan, anna nasan min ashabi rasulullahi (S.A.W): Ya rasulallah, dhahaba ahludduthuri bil-ujuri, yusalluna kama nusalli wa yasumuna kama nasuumu yatasaddaquna bi fuduli amwalihim. Qal: “Awalaysa qad ja’alallahu ma tasaddaquun? Inna bikulli tasbihatin sadaqah, wa kulli takhbiratin sadaqah, wa kulli tahmidatin sadaqah, wa amrin bil ma’arufi sadaqah, wa nahyun anil munkari sadaqah, wafi bud’i ahadikum sadaqah.” Qalu ya rasulullahi: Aya’ati ahaduna shahwatahu wa yakunu lahu fiha ajr? Qal: “Ara’aytum law wada aha fi haramin, akana alayhi wizr? Fa kadhalika idha wada’aha fil halali kana alihi ajr.” Rawahu Muslim. TRANSLATION On the authority of Abu Dharr (May Allah be pleased with him) who said: some of the companions of the Messenger of Allah said to the prophet (peace be upon him): “O messenger of Allah, the rich people have gone with the rewards; they pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, and they give alms with what they do not need out of their wealth”. The prophet said: “Has not Allah provide you with what you are able to give? In every ascription of glory to Allah, every declaration of His greatness, every utterance of praise to Him, every declaration that he is the only God, in enjoining what is reputable, in forbidding what is objectionable, and in a man’s sexual intercourse there is sadaqah.” They said: “O messenger of Allah would a reward be given for satisfying one’s passion?” He said: “Tell me; if he were to devote it to something forbidden, would it be a sin on his part? Similarly, if he were to devote it to something lawful, he would have a reward.” Transmitted by Muslim. TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 26 Al-Hadithul- Sadisu Wal-Ishirun

An Abhi Hurairata radiyallahu anhu Qaal: Qala Rasulullahi (S.A.W): “Kullu sulama muinan nasi alaihi sadaqah, kulla yaumin tadulu’u fihi shamsu: ta’adilu bainath naini sadaqah, wa tu’inur rajula fi dabbatihi fa tahmiluhu alaiha aw tarfa’u lahu alaiha mata’ahu sadaqah, wal kalimatu dayyibatu sadaqah, wabi kulli khadwatin tamshiha ilas salati sadaqah, wa tumidul adhaa anil dariq sadaqah.” Rawahul-Bukhari wa Muslim TRANSLATION On the authority of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: “The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: “Every bone of man’s fingers and toes must give sadaqah, every day the sun rises a man deals justly between two people it is sdaqah. If one helps a man with his beast, loading or lifting his goods on it, it is sadaqah. A good word is sadaqah, every step one takes towards prayer is sadaqah, any one remove anything injuries from the road it is sadaqah.” Transmitted by Al-Bukahari and Muslim. COMMENTS i. This tradition has much in common with the twenty-fifth tradition. It has given a wide range of deeds that can earn a Muslim excellent reward if he does them. This tradition shows typically how the generous the religion is to its follows. In whatever sphere of life, you happen to be it with you are wealthy or poor, Islam has not forgotten you. It has something for you only if you care to follow it. ii. This tradition has a lot of ethical teaching. If applied, it will contribute a lot in the betterment of human relationship. Its contribution to our society life is invaluable. WEEK 3: THE CONTRIBUTIONS MADE BY SELECTED MUSLIM PHILOSOPHERS/EDUCATIONIST IN WORLDMCIVILIZATIO CONTRIBUTIONS OF JABIR IBN HAYYAN AND AL-RAZI JABIR IBN HAYYAN (721-815 C.E)

Jabir ibn Hayyan was born in Tus in Iran. Shortly after he was born his father who was pharmacist, was political reasons. He was taught by the famous Imam Ja’afar al-Sadiq, studied medicine and became a court physician to the Abbasi caliph Harun ar-Rashid. He died in exile in Kufa, in modern Iraq in 815 A.C HIS CONTRIBUTIONS Jabir wrote more than 100 works, mainly on alchemy and chemistry with others on astronomy, of these books only 22 survive in Arabic. Some of his famous books on alchemy are the book of Mercy, the book of concentration, the book of the kingdom and the book of balances. Some of his works on chemistry were translated into European languages including Latin. He was known in Europe by the name of ‘Geber’. Jabir was acknowledged as the father of Modern Chemistry. AL -RAZI ALCHEMIST, PHILOSOPHER AND PHYSICIAN 865-925 A.C Abubakar Muhammad ibn Zakariya Al-razi was born in Rayy (in Persia) and studied mathematics, alchemy, philosophy, astronomy and Medicine in Baghdad. He served for a time as chief physician in a newly established hospital in Rayy, and later held a similar position in Baghdad. Many students attended his lectures that his voice could not be heard by those sitting far away, it was necessary for those sitting nearer to pass on his words to those at the back. He died in 925 A.C in his home town of Rayy. HIS GENERAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO LEARNING Razi was a prolific writer, and in accordance with the practice of his time he was knowledgeable in many of the sciences. Hence his writings include works on medical science, chemistry, physics, music, philosophy, mathematics, astronomy etc. He wrote about 200 books of which half are on medical subject. His most famous books were kitab ai-Mansur (composed for Mansur al-Ishaq the ruler of Rayy) and kitab al-Hawi, “the comprehensive book.” He was described as the greatest physician of the Ummah during his time.

His specific contributions were: a. On the disposition of the heart. b. He wrote a treatise on measles and small pox. c. His book kitab al-HAwi was the most comprehensive work on medicine by a Muslim scientist. IBN SINA PHILOSOPHER AND PHYSICIAN 370-428 A.H (980-1037 A.C) Ibn Sina (known as Avicenna in the west) was born near Bukhara in central Asia. His native language was Persian. He was well educated at Bukhara and soon showed his extraordinary intelligence and memory. By the age of 07-14 he had already overtaken his teachers, and by the time he was 16, famous physicians were working under his directions. At 18 he had mastered all the then-known sciences, and the progress he made thereafter was by the use of his own-brain and his own initiatives. He produced his first book on philosophy at the age of 21. Ibn Sina was invited by the ruler of Isfahan to his court where he worked until the time he died in Hamadan. THE CONTRIBUTIONS OF IBN SINA TO ISLAMIC PHILOSOPHY AND MEDICINE Meanwhile, he wrote books in the night and even while travelling on horseback or in prison. He was a very fast writer. He corrected arguments of Aristotle. He wrote altogether between 200-300 works in which he contributed to the advancement of all the sciences of his day: Natural history, history, physics, chemistry, astronomy, geology, medicine, mathematics, music, economics, politics, poetry, moral and religious affairs, Qur’anic commentary and philosophy in addition he wrote poetry as a vehicle for expressing his philosophy and also as medium of instruction for logic and medicine. His famous books were the kitab al-shifa (book of healing of the soul) a philosophical work and the Qanun fil tibb (canon of medicine). The latter book remained the authority on medicine both in Muslim lands and in Europe for 700 years until the modern age of experimental science began. Some of its teaching and treatments are still useful to doctors even today. Ibn sina’s greatest works were translated into latin, and he and Al-razi were recognized in Europe as the greatest masters of medicine, philosophy and natural sciences. Ibn sina’s(Canon of medicine) was

translated 87 times, all or in part, and formed the basis of medical teaching and practice in European Universities from 12 th to the 17 th century. AL-GHAZALI THEOLOGIAN, JURIST, ORIGINAL THINKER AND RELIGIOUS REFORMER 450-505 A.H (1058- 1111 A.C) Abu Hamid Muhammad known as al-Ghazali was born at Tus in Persia in 450 A.H equivalent to 1072 C.E. He joined marry scholars at the court of Nizam al-Mulk in Baghdad. Nizam al-Mulk sent him as chief professor to the Nizamiyya, a college he had established in Baghdad. WORKS More than 400 works are ascribed to Al-Ghazali, but some of these probably had other authors. Al-Ghazali wrote books on Fiqh (Jurisprudence), philosophy and logic, theology and Sufi theory and Sufi theology and practice. Al-Ghazali’s greatest work however was the” Ihya” Ulum al-din (Revival of the religious sciences). WEEK 4: AN-NIKAH. DEFINATION, IMPORTANCE, PURPOSE, RULES AND REGULATIONS GOVERNING ITS VALIDITY, RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF HUSBAND AND WIFE. AN-NIKAH Marriage is called An-nikah in Arabic. Marriage is encouraged in Islam. It has existed since the time of our earliest forefather Adam, when Allah created for him a mate, Hauwa, and they had children. Allah says: (24:32) “Marry single from among you and such that are fit of your male and female slaves. If they are poor Allah will enrich them of His bounty, surely Allah is sufficient and All-knowing. The prophet (P.B.U.H) said: There is no (monkhood) celibacy in Islam. The prophet also said: “Marriage is my Sunnah whoever Shuns it is not one of us”: PURPOSE AND IMPORTANCE OF MARRIAGE Allah refers to the purpose of marriage in verse of the Qur’an: “And among His signs is this, He has created mates for you from among yourselves so that you may fine tranquility with them and He has put love and tenderness between you. In this behold there are messages indeed for people who think.

This is a beautiful description of the Husband/Wife relationship. The marriage relationship is important because it fulfils a number of functions, among which are: a. The sense of security b. Sexual satisfaction c. Foundation of family life d. Security in old age RULES GOVERNING MARRIAGE Four conditions for the validity of marriage in Islam are these: 1. Mutual consent of the couple. proposal and acceptance (Ijab and Qabul in Arabic terms) any of the two can propose. The formular is ‘I marry you’ and ‘I accept’ 2. Waliyy: marriage guardianship. Approval by the parent or guardian of the bride. The Qur’an 4:25 states ‘Marry them with the permission of their people’ 3. Mandatory Gift from the groom to the bride: it has no limit. It is called Mahr or Sadaq. 4. Witness/publicity witnesses to the marriage contract. Marriage must not be conducted in secret. There must be at least two adult witnesses. LESSONS 1. A person must make a good choice of a spouse. 2. A girls parents’ consent must be obtained before marriage. 3. A bride gift is mandatory. 4. Witnesses are necessary. 5. Moderation should be applied to the amount of Mahr to be paid. RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF HUSBAND AND WIFE Allah says: “And men have rights over women as women have rights over men, and men are a degree above them”. The husband is fully responsible for the feeding, clothing, housing, satisfying her sexual desire and general welfare of the wife (and children). He is also expected to protect them from any external danger, and to

ensure their proper Islamic education which will protect them from doing wrong out of ignorance, mutual respect for her and her parents. The wife should take good care of the husband’s property. Whenever he is away, making the home comfortable and happy place for all the family. She should not allow into the house men of whom the husband does not approve. She should guard her chastity and keep a good reputation. She should also satisfy her husband (in sexual fulfilment), respect him and his parents. WEEK 5: HADITH 32 AND 34 OF AN-NAWAWI AND THEIR LESSONS TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 32 An Abi Said Sa’d ibn Malik ibn Sinanil-khudriyy, radiyallahu anhu, anna Rasulallahi sallallahu alayhi wa Sallama Qal: “La Dharara wala Dhirara”. Hadithun Hasanun, Rawahu ibn majah. TRANSLATION On the authority of Abu Said al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: “The messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: There should be no damage nor should there be any damaging (to the others).” Transmitted by ibn majah. COMMENTS 1. This tradition teaches us that we should not oppress anyone and if we are oppressed, we should leave the matter with God, Most High or in the hands of justice. if we take revenge, we should not exceed the oppression done to us. 2. If is clear that peace is bound to prevail everywhere if the teaching of this tradition is put into practice. No one will harm you if you do not harm anybody else. TRANSLITERATION OF HADITH 34 An Abu Saidinil Hhudriyyi, radiyallahu anhu Qal: Sami’tu rasullallahi Sallallahu alaiyhi wa Sallam Yaqul: “Man ra’a minkum munkaran falyugayirhu biyadih, fa in lam yastadi fabi lisanihi, fa in lam yastadi fabiqalbih, waq dhalika ad’aful-Iman”. TRANSLATION on the authority of Abu-Said Al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: “I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) saying: “If anyone sees an abomination, he should change it with his hand,

if he cannot he should do it with his tongue, if he cannot he should do it in his heart, that being the weakest form of faith”. Transmitted by Muslim. COMMENT The tradition explains that it is a person whose faith is weak that cannot used either his hand or tongue to stop a wrong thing being done. He can then only hate such a thing in his mind only. WEEK 6: MORAL EDUCATION. KINDNESS TO PARENTS, HONESTY IN WORDS AND DEEDS, DIGNITY OF LABOUR KINDNESS TO PARENTS Islam teaches good morality. It wants Muslims to be good generally and to his parents in particular. This is imperative considering parent’s labour on the child. The Qur’an commands us to show kindness to parents in the following words: “Your Lord has decreed that you should worship nothing except him, and (show) kindness to your parents, whether one or both of them attain old age (while they are) still with you never say to them “Shame!” nor Scorn either of them, but speak to them in a generous way. Lower to them the wing of kindness out of mercy and say: “my Lord! Have mercy on them both as they did care for me when I was little”. (Qur’an 17:23-24). NOTE: OBEDIENCE TO ALLAH COMES FIRST! If parents other their children to do something which Allah has forbidden, and to go against Islam, then the children should obey Allah and not their parents in a polite way. why they cannot obey them. They should, however, continue to show them respect and kindness. HONESTY IN WORDS AND DEEDS Allah says: “Shun every word that is untrue. (Q. 22:30). Verily, truth is goodness, and goodness leads to paradise, and verily lying is wickedness and wickedness leads to the fire (of hell). Hadith ibn Mas’ud (Musli). Truthfulness is a habit which lies at the root of all good habits, while lying is a habit which lies at the root of all bad habits. What are the ill effects of dishonesty on the other people and on society in general? Obviously the victim of someone’s lies on dishonesty will feel pain, anger, loss or disappointment.

DIGNITY OF LABOUR Islam encourages every Muslim to seek a lawful livelihood for himself and his family and not to beg, as he is capable of earning a living. One must not refuse any lawful occupation on account of its being low in dignity. While it is honourable to work to earn a living, it is dishonourable to depend on begging for a living. The prophet is reported to have e said: “Never has anyone eaten a better thing than what he eats from the work of his hand.” (Hadith from Bukhari) THE PROPHET’S ATTITUDE TO POVERTY AND BEGGING The prophet always cared for the poor. Even when he became the Head of state in Medina he lived as a poor Man. Sometimes he and his family did not have enough to eat. Whenever they had something, they used to share it with the poor, or give it away as Sadaqah to others who were in need. Every Muslim should care for the welfare of those around him. The prophet said: ‘He is not a Muslim who eats his fill while his neighbour goes hungry. Therefore, all Muslims, rich or poor, are urged to treat others with kindness and generosity. It this is done, there will be no cause to go and beg, and no excuse for those who wish to make begging a way of life. WEE 7: THE STATUS OF WOMEN IN ISLAM, POLYGAMY, RULES THAT GOVERN IT THE STATUS OF WOMEN IN ISLAM i. Women’s status in pre-Islamic societies. In some part of the world, women have been treated little better than a slave, forced to do heavy work for little reward. In some place’s women were regarded in law as chattels- the property of the husband or family to be inherited on his death along with his other possessions. Some societies have regarded women as play things, to be passed from man to man for his entertainment. Some have seen women ads not only without soul but as an agent of the devil. Consequently, the birth of a girl would be greeted with either a sigh or a curse. Some societies, such as that of Arabia before Islam, even sanctioned the burial alive of female infants. ii. Islam and Women: a revolutionary change. No other religion can compare with Islam in the revolutionary changes it introduced in the status of women. These changes required a major re- adjustment in the way women were to be evaluated and treated, both legally and morally.

Islam considered women and treated them very well in different status such as: a. Spiritual status b. Intellectual status c. Property-owning status d. Status in marriage e. The spirit of kindness towards women f. The status of the mother. POLYGAMY The word “Polygamy” is used to refer to marriage of a man with more than one wife at the same time while a woman who has more than two husbands at a time is practicing polyandry. Monogamy is having only one spouse. Islam prohibits polyandry and allows monogamy and polygamy. RULES THAT GOVERN IT LIMITS OF POLYGAMY IN ISLAM Islam allows a male Muslim to marry up to four wives concurrently if he is able to maintain justice and equity among the wives Allah says in Qur’an 4:3. “Then marry women of your choice, two, three, or four but if you fear that you shall not be able to deal justly with them, then (Marry) only one…that is nearer to prevent you from doing injustice.” Equity and justice among wives are conditions for marrying more than one wife. The prophet said: ‘Whoever marries more than one wife and does not maintain justice among the wives shall be raised paralyzed on the last day. JUSTICE AND EQUAL TREATMENT OF WIVES MUST BE MAINTAINED In particular, equality should be maintained among wives in the following ways by providing: i. Food ii. Shelter iii. Clothing iv. Company

Or intimate relations/sharing of bed with the wife. The husband must share his time (day and night) equally among the wives in rotation. CIRCUMSTANCES WHICH MIGHT NECESSITATE POLYGAMY Polygamy has a role to play under some circumstances. For example, problems sometimes arise as the result of a disability in the first wife, such as: a. Infertility b. Serious illness, physical handicap, disablement or serious injuries due to accident etc. c. Mental illness. Another circumstance which may make polygamy preferable are: 1. In a situation where the husband is too virile for one wife. 2. In a wartime where marry men are killed, leaving thousands or even millions of widows, orphans, and unmarried young women. By allowing for polygamy the women can be protected, taken care of and enabled to enjoy the satisfactions of family life and children. WEEK 8: DIVORCE (AT-TALAQ) DEFINATION, ATTITUDE AND KINDS Talaq (Divorce) means the breaking of the marriage bond. In Islam marriage is intended to be a lifelong partnership wherein both partners find security and happiness, and are able to establish a family and bring up their children (see chapter 52). It occasionally happens however that a marriage runs into problems, and one or both of the partners want to separate. Sometimes these problems can be solved and the marriage continues, sometimes the problems are not solved and the marriage ends in divorce. TEACHING AGAINST DIVORCE Allah says: “If you fear a breach between them (Husband and Wife) appoint (two) arbitrators, one from his family and the other from her family, if they both wish to make peace, Allah will cause their reconciliation. Indeed, Allah is ever the All-know, well acquainted with all things.” Qur’an 4:35

DIVORCE AS LAST RESOR If all efforts to live harmoniously as husband and wife fails, Allah allows divorce through a laid down procedure. The Qur’an states: “But if they separate (divorce) Allah will provide abundance for everyone of them from his bounty, and Allah is ever All-sufficient, All-wise.” Qur’an 4:130 EVIL OF DIVORCE INCLUDE a. Enmity b. Poor upbringing of children c. Displeasure of Allah d. Sadness to one or both parties e. Weakening of family ties f. The wife’s beauty might have been reduced. KINDS OF DIVORCE There are basically four methods of divorce: a. Talaq: Divorce at the instance of the husband b. Khul: Divorce at the instance of the wife c. Faskh: Divorce by court order d. Mubarah: Divorce by mutual agreement of husband and wife REVOCABLE AND IRREVOCABLE DIVORCE Divorce may be revocable (i.e it can be recalled and cancelled) and it may be irrevocable (which cannot be reversed). i. Divorce which cannot be reversed is known as (Talaq bain) irrevocable divorce. ii. Talaq that may be reversed to resume marital life between the couple is called (Talaq raji) revocable divorce. OTHER MEANS OF DISSOLUTION OF MARRIAGE The laid down procedures for divorce have been explained as Talaq, khul, Mubarah, and Faskh. There are other practices which have the effect of dissolution of marriage. The practices are Li’an, ila and Zihar 1. Li’an (Mutual imprecation)

a. If the husband alleges that the wife commits adultery or he rejects the paternity of a child on the ground of an alleged infidelity on the part of the wife, then the process of li’an, self-cursing is adopted. Thereafter the marriage becomes irrevocable dissolved. b. The Qur’an 24:6-9 explains that if the husband alleges zina against his wife, he will swear four times in the name of Allah on it and on the fifth swearing he shall invoke Allah’s wrath on himself if his allegation is false. If he refuses to swear and he cannot produce four reliable male witnesses to the alleged committal of zina, he is to be punished with eighty lashes of the cane. If he makes the oath and the woman accepts, she is to be punished for zina and that ends the marriage but if she refutes it, then she shall swear four times and on the fifth time invoke the wrath of Allah on herself, if the husband’s allegation is true. This oath of innocence marks the end of the marriage snice trust is no longer existing in the marriage. The li’an terminates the marriage. 2. Al-Ila (Oath of conjugal suspension): It was the practice during the pre-Islamic period through which a husband vowed not to have sexual intercourse with the wife and she was thus left without divorce and without sexual intercourse. Qur’an 2:226-227 says: “in the case of those who swear not to be into their wives, the waiting period is four months, then if they go back, Allah is surely forgiving, merciful. And if they resolve on divorce, then Allah is surely Hearing, knowing.” Islam directs that he either resumes the conjugal relation without four months or she commences her ‘Iddah’ after the expiration of the four months at the end of the Iddah, the wife is free to marry someone else. 3. Zihar (husbands’ comparison of wife’s back with his mother’s) IDDAH (waiting period) AND KIND TREATMENT OF DIVORCED WOMEN, TYPES AND VARIATIONS WHAT IS IDDAH? Iddah is a waiting period pf a woman after divorce or death of the husband. She cannot re-marry another man while she is in Iddah. The uses of iddah including the following: a. In the case of Iddah of first or second divorce it allows time for reconsideration and reconciliation. b. It establishes whether the woman is pregnant by the divorced husband. This prevents any dispute over paternity of a child, which might arise if she were allowed to contract a new marriage at once. c. In case the wife is pregnant, it ensures her maintenance and care until she delivers.

d. In case of death of the husband it allows time for some recovery from the initial grief before deciding on any new marriage, since it is unlawful for a man to make a formal marriage proposal to a woman in Iddah, although he may hint at his intention. (Qur’an 2:235) DURATION OF IDDAH The duration of Iddah is generally speaking as follows: a. In the case of a woman who menstruates, it is the period of three quru (monthly cycles). That is she should observe three full gaps between 3 monthly periods before the Iddah expires. (Qur’an 2:228) b. In the case of a woman who is pregnant, her Iddah lasts until delivery (Qur’an 65:4) c. In the case of a woman who has stopped menstruation or a girl who has not started, the Iddah is three months (Qur’an 65:4) d. If a marriage was not yet consummated, there is no Iddah (Qur’an 33:49) e. In the case of death of the husband the iddah is four months and ten days (Qur’an 2:234). QUR’ANIC VERSES TOWARDS IDDAH I. Qur’an 65:1 state: “O prophet, when you divorce women divorce them through their Iddah and count their Iddah accurately and fear Allah your lord. And you Muslims must not turn them out if their (husband’s homes) or shall they leave except in case they are guilty of some obvious illicit deal. And those are the limits of Allah and whosoever transgresses the limits of Allah, then indeed has wronged himself. You know not, that Allah may thereafter bring some new things to pass. II. Qur’an 65:6 state: “Lodge them (divorce wives) where you dwell, according to your means, and do not ill treat them that they may be made to leave… CUSTODY OF CHILDREN AFTER DIVORCE In the event of divorce or death of the husband or wife Islam makes rules for the custody of the children (hadanah). The prophet responds to the enquiry of a divorced woman or whether she or the husband should have the right of custody of the children as follows: ‘You (the wife) have a better right to have him (son) as long as you do not re-marry’ ibn Majah. DURATION OF THE CUSTODY

The duration of the custody for a girl is until she is married and for a boy, it is until he attains puberty. Therefore, he or she can live anywhere, as dictated by circumstances. The order of priority for custody under the shari’ah are: 1. The mother of the children 2. Mother’s mother 3. Mother’s grandmother (maternal, then paternal) 4. Mother’s sister (full, then maternal, then paternal) 5. Grandmother’s sister 6. Mother’s aunt 7. Father’s mother or father’s grandmother (maternal, then paternal) 8. Father 9. Child’s sister 10. Father’s sister (Hashiyat al-Dasuqi vol.2: p-527) WEEK 9 AND 10: MODESTY IN DRESSING AND BEHAVIOUR, PERSEVERANCE (sabr) AND ALLAH’S CONSCIOUSNESS (taqwa) MODESTY IN DRESSING AND BEHAVIOUR The difference in the sexuality and attraction of males and females to the exposure of sensitive and sexually arousing parts of the body of the opposite sex accounts for the emphasis which Islam places on covering of almost all parts of a female body. A woman, except when she is with her husband or close relation is expected to cover her body except the face and the hands. She is not to wear any dress that is tight or transparent except when she is alone, with her close relatives, her Husband or other females. Men too must not expose their nudity except when they are with their wives or close relatives. Men’s nudity is what lies between their navel and knee. For men and women, even if they are in privacy, should not be naked. Both men and women are expected to be modest in dressing and behavior by lowering their gaze and guarding their modesty. They should not stare at or intimately gaze at people of the opposite sex who are no their spouse or close relation. QUR’ANIC VERSES ON MODESTY ON DRERSSING AND BEHAVIOUR

Allah says: “Tell the believing men to lower their gaze (from looking at forbidden things), and protect their private parts (from illegal sexual acts etc.) that is purer for them. Verily, Allah is All aware of what they do. And tell the believing women to lower their gaze (from looking at forbidden things), and protect their private parts (from illegal sexuality) … PERSEVERANCE (SABR) Sabr is an Arabic word denoting endurance, perseverance and patience. Because of its importance in shaping the life of man, Allah in several places in the Qur’an enjoins His creatures to cultivate Sabr even when things go wrong. Qur’an 2:153-157 enjoins Muslims to demonstrate Sabr in the face of danger, loss and hardship. Prophet Muhammad also counselled his followers to exercise patience and perseverance and described those who uphold this as being grateful to Allah. Prophet Muhammad demonstrated sabr through his life. He was persecuted by the idol worshippers, betrayed by the hypocrites and was even stoned out of Taif when preaching, yet he did not abandon practice patience is necessary for doing good and resisting evil. ALLAH’S CONSCIOUSNESS (TAQWA) Taqwa is often translated to mean God consciousness. It also means piety of fear of Allah. The Glorious Qur’an describes a person who is conscious of Allah as one who sincerely practices Islam both outwardly and inwardly. It is he whose moral probity is not in doubt. Taqwa should obviously improve the attitude and behavior of the person who possess it. TRUST (AMANAH) Trust (Amanah) is a very importance aspect of man’s responsibity. A good Muslim must keep trust not betray it. If one is the head of a place, those under him are to put in him trust, he should therefore treat them well for Allah shall ask how he has treated them. The same applies to one’s wife and children, they are put in one’s care and must be taken care of. If a teacher keeps some money in care of a student, the student should not say that the money is lost, it is amanah. Allah says: “verily, Allah commands you to render back the trusts to those entitled to them…”

LEADERSHIP, FOLLOWSHIP AND JUSTICE Leadership is a form of guardianship over those under one’s care or supervision. A leader has been given some responsibilities to which he is accountable to Allah. Leadership therefore imposes on one that care for the welfare of those under one and doing what is best for them. Justice on the other hand implies that matters are decided by the leader and he leads on the basis of truth and facts. No one is to be given what is not his due or denied of his/her due. The leader should not abuse his privilege position to misrule or commit injustice against those under his care. A leader should uphold the truth and shun favouritism. An unjust leader cannot command the required respect from the subjects and therefore cannot have peace. Prophet Muhammad (S.A.W) is the best example worthy of emulation, he led by example because he was just and responsible. His leadership qualities are on record for all generations. WEEK 11: UNITY AND BROTHERHOOD, RELIGIOUS TOLERANCE AND PEACEFUL CO-EXISTANCE UNITY AND BROTHERHOOD (Importance and meaning of brotherhood) Islam is a religion that governs all aspects of human lives. Muslims are considered as brothers of the same family in that whatever happens to one (good or bad) others are also affected. In whatever part of the world Muslims meet one another, they should be at home and demonstrate the unifying spirit of Islam to the world. The unity which salat provides through coming together five times daily and the annual Ramadan fast and pilgrimage should be extended to other aspects of our lives. Unity and brotherhood were demonstrated by the Muslims in the early days of Islam. The Muslims of Madinah (Ansar) accommodated the emigrants (Muhajirun) in the spirit of Islamic brotherhood. It was with this spirit that the Muslim Ummah was able to subdue the large Makkan army. The modern-day Muslims should embrace the brotherhood of Islam to promote their course rather than allow factionalism based on ethnic and sectarian inclinations to divide them. INJUNCTIONS ON UNITY AND BROTHERHOOD. QUR’ANIC VERSES i. “And hold fast, all together into the bond with Allah, and do not be disunited. And remember the blessings which Allah has bestowed on you, for you were enemies one to another but he

joined your hearts together, so that through His blessings you become brethren…” (Qur’an 3:103) ii. “All believers are brothers. Hence, (make peace between your two brothers, and remain conscious of Allah, so that you might be graced with His mercy” (Qur’an 49:10).

title: FORMAL LETTER
subject: English Language
rawText:
THEME: FIRST TERM LESSON NOTE FOR SS3 SUBJECT: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS STUDIES WEEK 1: SURATUN-NASR, LAHAB, IKHLAS, FALAQ AND NAS. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUN-NASR 1. Idha ja a nasrul-lahi wal-fatah. 2. Wara aytan-nasa yadkhuluna fidinil-lahi afwaja. 3. Fasabbih bihamdi Rabbika wastaghfirhu. Innahu kana tawwaba. TRANSLATION 1. When Allah’s help and victory come. 2. And you see people entering Allah’s religion (Islam) in crowds. 3. Glorify the praises of your lord, and seek His forgiveness. Certainly, He is ever ready to forgive. LESSONS 1. It is a Madinah- surah. 2. It was the last chapter that was revealed to prophet Muhammad as a whole. 3. Allah promised the prophet and his followers that He would help and give them victory over their enemies. 4. Help and victory come from Allah. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL-LAHAB 1. Tabbat yada abi lahabin watabb. 2. Ma aghna anhu maluhu wama kasab. 3. Sayasla naran dhata lahabin. 4. Wamra’atuhu hammalatal hatab. 5. Fijidiha hablun min masad. TRANSLATION 1. Perish the two hands of Abu lahab (the father of flame), and perish he. 2. Neither his wealth nor what he has gained shall be of benefit to him. 3. He will be burnt in a fire of blazing flame.

4. And his wife too, who carried wood (thorns which she used to put on the way of the prophet or used to slander him). 5. In her neck is a twisted rope of palm fibre. LESSONS 1. This is a Makkan surah. 2. It has two names, Al-lahan and Al-masad. Taken from the first and last verses to the surah respectively. 3. Abu labab’s real name is Abdul-uzza. 4. He was an uncle of the Holy prophet. He was a son of Abdul-muttalib, the grandfather of the prophet. 5. Abu lahab’s wife is called both Arwa and Umm Jameelah. 6. She was the sister of Abu sufyan bin herb. 7. Both Abu lahab and his wife hated the religion of Islam a lot. 8. Allah has promised to protect the religion of Islam despite all odds. TRANSLITERATION OF SURATUL-IKHLAS 1. Qul Huwal-lahu ahad. 2. Allahus-Samad. 3. Lam yalid walam yulas. 4. Walam yakun lahu kufuwan ahad. TRANSLATION 1. Say: He is Allah, the one 2. Allah, the Eternal, Absolute. 3. He begets not, nor is he begotten. 4. And there is none like unto him. LESSONS 1. The surah teaches monotheism and forbids polytheism. 2.
